on behalf of the gue/ngl group. – mr president, some colleagues took the initiative of putting an urgency resolution on the agenda on brazil’s refusal to extradite cesare battisti to italy. i understand their motives, but as i shall demonstrate, this is not at present a human rights case. it is not an urgent case and it is not even a ‘breach of the rule of law’ case. furthermore, it comes at a terrible moment when brazil is facing the worst natural disaster in its history. cesare battisti is in prison. he is awaiting the decision of the brazilian supreme court and the supreme court is currently not in session during the southern hemisphere’s summer holiday. there is no reason to believe that there will not be an independent decision. i expressed my solidarity with the families of the victims in this case, and rest assured i have no sympathy with political violence either from the right or the left, but we should use the urgencies to debate southern sudan, the case of buchtar tabuni in indonesia, or the palestinian man shot dead in his bed. is the parliament going to allocate to president dilma rousseff, just after her groundbreaking election and for no sound formal reason, the kind of debate that we usually reserve for people like mugabe? i would ask you to remove brazil from the urgencies on the agenda.
madam president, it is never too much to say that europe has higher standards than anywhere else in the world for the quality of food products and that image cannot be called into question. it is demanded by our consumers, by the markets to which we export and by our producers, who put a great deal of work and investment into complying with them. if the contamination that recently occurred in germany had happened in many other parts of the world, we would probably never have even known about it. but no, i'm not. it happened in the european union. and what happened in germany is unacceptable and must not only be fully clarified but also the perpetrators of what appears to be a crime and not an accident must be held accountable. the source of the contamination does not seem to be fully understood and this causes me great uneasiness. the responsibility of the german authorities for any failure to control is not clearly defined. it seems that the knowledge was due to a communication from the company and not to a control by the authorities. the people responsible are not known and the seriousness of this situation requires an objective clarification by the commission.
madam president, commissioner, the discovery of products contaminated with dioxins and their dissemination through various marketing channels is a matter of the utmost seriousness. without prejudice to fully identifying the responsibilities and consequences of this and tracing the fate of the contaminated products, this incident calls for a deeper reflection on the failure of the entire existing regulatory framework. here is an example of the consequences of a market-oriented common agricultural policy which promotes intensive export-oriented production models, favours large agro-industry and destroys small and mediumsized farming and family farming. it makes it impossible, rather than possible, to promote local production and consumption which would be much more traceable. here is another example of how, also for reasons of public health and food safety and quality, a profound change in the current common agricultural policy is necessary.
the ec should urge germany and all countries involved in this matter to take appropriate measures to address this situation, impose sanctions and ensure that all those involved in this dioxin crisis bear full responsibility for the vast damage caused to the agro-livestock, processing and consumer sectors. the fact that some feed producers have been aware of this dioxin contamination since march 2010 without reporting it to the public authorities is totally unacceptable. it is therefore urgent to inform all member states and third countries with great transparency about all details of potentially contaminated food. all foodstuffs that do not comply with eu legislation must be identified and withdrawn from the market. it is necessary to ensure that all measures are taken to protect public health, to have timely and detailed information on developments in the situation and to report on them as closely and transparently as possible, so that we can return to normalcy and consumer confidence in the food chain as quickly as possible.
madam president, illegal logging in central african countries such as cameroon and the congo is a threat to the integrity of resources on which the existence and livelihoods of local communities and indigenous peoples depend. a threat to an ecosystem which is a repository of enormous biodiversity and of great importance in the regulation of biogeochemical cycles. in view of the progress of the destruction of the tropical forest in this region - fuelled, let us not forget, by the demand of operators and importers from the industrialized countries, particularly the european union - the solution cannot be to legalize what is now illegal, namely the unsustainable exploitation of the forest, in some way legitimizing the usurpation of land from local communities and the occupation of large areas of forest by logging companies, as is happening. the european union's development cooperation and aid policy plays a very important role here, supporting the diversification of the economies of these countries and reversing a model based on the high dependence on the exploitation and export of a small number of raw materials to the industrialized countries.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i congratulate mrs angelilli on the opportunity to put this oral question. i am of the opinion that we must develop more effective child protection policies aimed at preventing situations of poverty, abuse and abandonment of children and, at the same time, alternatives to their placement in institutions, where adoption should play a crucial role. unicef recognizes that the number of children in institutions has not decreased and that the increase in adoptions has fallen far short of the increase in the number of children in institutions, so we have to do a little soul-searching. it is important to make a general assessment of the law and administrative and judicial practice in relation to adoption procedures in the various member states in order to identify any obstacles to their proper functioning. and in relation to third countries, we must keep an eye on the problem of irregular or illegal adoptions, which mainly affects the poorest regions. this is the case, for example, in guinea-bissau, where more than 50% of children are not registered, which facilitates the development of criminal activity by child trafficking networks. i therefore believe that a european strategy is needed to protect the interests of children in the context of intercountry adoption procedures, in order to prevent and prevent the abduction, sale or trafficking of human beings.

mr president, the recognition of agriculture as a strategic sector in the context of food security, which this report is talking about, is inseparable from the recognition and promotion of the concept of food sovereignty. the greater a country's food dependence, the greater its food insecurity, the greater the difficulty in ensuring that its population is supplied with food in sufficient quantity and quality. food sovereignty is the best insurance against the volatility of food prices, a subject which is dramatically coming back on the agenda. this volatility has been caused mainly by financial speculation in food products, an area where speculators, investment funds, hedge funds, pension funds, large banks, have been concentrating as other speculative bubbles have been drying up or bursting. the only way to stop this speculation is to stop the instruments that enable it, in particular some financial products such as otc derivatives. unfortunately, the measures taken by the european union in this area are far from being able to stop this sinister speculative machine and its inhuman consequences, as a recent un report by the special rapporteur on the right to food acknowledges.

in writing. recommendation on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european community and the economic and monetary union of west africa on certain aspects of air services. i voted in favour of the resolution on a draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european community and the west african economic and monetary union on certain aspects of air services. the community currently has exclusive competence in respect of several aspects of external aviation. the council authorized the commission to open negotiations with third countries to replace certain provisions in existing bilateral agreements with community agreements. the commission has negotiated an agreement with the west african economic and monetary union which avoids discrimination between eu air carriers; allows the taxation of aviation fuel for operations within the european union; and brings clearly anti-competitive provisions in bilateral agreements (compulsory commercial agreements between airlines) into line with community competition law.
in writing. − the transfer of competence from the member states to the communities has justified the replacement of bilateral agreements on external aviation by new agreements to which the european community is a party. the resolution adopted deals with precisely such issues and aims to harmonize the existing international legal instruments with the present reality of european integration and to adapt them to the additional requirements arising from community law. the matter in question is eminently technical, involving the replacement of previously existing agreements by new ones, and not involving any contentious or ideological differences of any kind. the unanimous vote in favour of the report in committee confirms this interpretation. it was therefore for the plenary to ratify a consensus decision. i voted for it.
in writing. the report by mr dieter-lebrecht koch suggests the conclusion of an agreement between the european community and the economic and monetary union of west africa on certain aspects of air services. the spirit of the european union in the treaties is to standardise procedures throughout the eu. it therefore makes no sense as the court of justice of the european union has ruled that in matters such as this there are bilateral air service agreements between eu member states and member states of the west african economic and monetary union. i therefore welcome the adoption of this agreement, which will strengthen the bonds of european territorial cohesion and encourage respect for community competition law.
in writing. - in the current concrete framework in which civil aviation activity is developing, this proposed agreement raises serious doubts as to its scope and possible consequences. if until now the member states have been sovereign in deciding on the organisation and scope of the agreements to be drawn up in this field, with obvious impacts on airlines, in a sector which is, for various reasons, strategic for safeguarding national interests, from now on the market is to prevail here too. in particular, we cannot underestimate the fact that the alleged creation of a level playing field for the various european airlines can compete for the facilitation of monopolistic concentration in the sector (a process already under way) and for the reduction of the capacity of member states to defend their flag carriers. the free competition, which is always mentioned and which must be defended at all costs, is once again the cornerstone on which this initiative is based. the consequences in this and other sectors are not substantially different: it is the monopolistic concentration that always ends up imposing itself in these scenarios. for these reasons, we did not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - the existence of 47 bilateral agreements between eu member states and member states of the west african economic and monetary union is manifestly inadequate to frame the various aspects of air services. the agreement is therefore welcome in order to replace certain existing provisions in bilateral agreements with community agreements. the agreement highlights the issues of non-discrimination between european air carriers and the taxation of aviation fuel in accordance with the respective directive on the taxation of energy products and electricity. the agreement also complies with community competition law.
in writing. - the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european community and the economic and monetary union of west africa on certain aspects of air services. on the basis of the current exclusive competence of the european union in this field, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with third countries to replace the traditional bilateral air service agreements between member states and third countries. the draft agreement was examined by the committee on transport and tourism, which delivered a favourable opinion, highlighting, among other points, the creation of a community designation clause to avoid discrimination between eu air carriers and the taxation of aviation fuel in operations carried out in the territory of the european union. these two points, which i emphasize in the favourable opinion of the committee on transport, are the reasons why i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the conclusion of this agreement, which, within the framework of the exclusive competence granted to the eu in respect of various aspects of external aviation, is intended to replace certain provisions of the current 47 bilateral air services agreements between eu member states and member states of the economic and monetary union of west africa, in order to bring them into line with community law.
in writing. − the exclusive competence in certain areas of external aviation, established in 2003 in the open skies judgment, allows the european commission to negotiate agreements with third countries in order to bring the european aviation market into line with community rules and, at the same time, to make it competitive and transparent. i welcome the approval of this agreement with the member states of the west african economic and monetary union, and consider it essential that the european union should present a policy of coherence in this sector of external aviation, gradually reducing the various provisions of the existing bilateral air services agreements between the two parties. i would stress the non-discrimination clause in the agreement between european airlines, the taxation of aviation fuel in accordance with the directive on the taxation of energy products and electricity, the conformity of the provisions of the bilateral agreements with community competition law and regulatory control, measures which will allow the opening up of markets and, consequently, the creation of investment opportunities for both parties. these agreements should be seen as a way of strengthening strategic cooperation between the two organisations.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which seeks to improve the effectiveness of eu humanitarian aid. the eu humanitarian consensus is a great step forward. however, the evaluation of its action plan should be more consistent, with more measurable objectives and more reliable indicators. only then can we help more effectively. in view of the increasing number and intensity of natural disasters caused by climate change, i agree with the position that not only timely aid is important, but also support for the communities' own capacities to prepare better for disasters, and that the hyogo action plan needs to be strengthened. it is also necessary to focus efforts on human rights issues arising from internal conflicts and complex crises, by improving the capacity of actors to reach out to populations, which can only be achieved through a clear distinction of roles between political, military and humanitarian decision-makers. i also agree with the effective implementation of a european rapid response capacity.

in writing. − in the mid-term evaluation of the european consensus on humanitarian aid, i cannot but regret that its public awareness has not been as desirable as it should have been and that the role of the member states in its implementation has been limited. but more than pointing out shortcomings, we need to promote and define the way forward in humanitarian aid. the humanitarian context has changed considerably in recent years (natural disasters, increased displacement, the multiplication of various internal conflicts, food crises, etc.). a balanced and effective global response based on concrete needs, results-oriented and guided by the principle that saving livelihoods is saving lives, taking into account the self-development and self-sufficiency of the areas concerned, is more urgent than ever. the promotion of these humanitarian values by the consensus and the optimisation of resources by the various actors is crucial in this regard. once again, i am in favour of the urgent establishment of a european civil protection force, following the barnier report of may 2006. i congratulate mrs michèle striffler on the positive content of the proposals she has put forward and i reiterate my view that the consensus is a fundamental instrument, with all its relevance in the present situation.
in writing. − the european consensus on humanitarian aid, reached on 18 december 2007 by the parliament, the council and the commission, represented an important step forward in the definition, scope and range of european humanitarian aid. we are proceeding with this report, whose conclusions i strongly support, to its mid-term review as provided for in the action plan of may 2008, and i would like to congratulate my colleague, mrs michèle striffler, for her excellent work. as regards the ideas expressed in the report, i would stress the focus on genuine and continuous participation of beneficiaries in the management of aid, a principle which i have been advocating, and which should lead the eu to focus its action increasingly on civil society and local authorities, to the detriment of eu-state relations, which should continue to play a role, but not in an exclusive relationship, as has often happened here. i would also stress the need to put forward proposals aimed at establishing a european civil protection force, based on the optimisation of the existing community civil protection mechanism and the mutualisation of existing national resources, which would imply an increase in the marginal cost of the synergies achieved through the use of the capacity already installed in the member states.

in writing. - the multiplication of catastrophic and humanitarian emergencies is evident throughout the world today. the european union has been playing an important role in combating these scourges and i hope it will maintain it and even strengthen it to the extent of its possibilities. it is not enough, however, to give the fish to the hungry, we must teach them to fish. i believe that almost as important as dealing with emergencies that are occurring is helping to empower the less resourceful countries with the human and material resources that are likely to deal with future crises. the european consensus on humanitarian aid deserves my support and my hope that the commitment of the european institutions will result in an ever better operationalisation of the means at the disposal of the union, always bearing in mind the priority to be given to those who have the least and those who suffer the most and the total exemption from political or ideological agendas.
in writing. - in recent years, the globalised world has seen a significant increase in disasters, both in terms of the geographical area affected and the number of victims. although this is a very important issue, the impact of climate change on these disasters should not be addressed in this context. on 18 december 2007, a significant step forward in humanitarian aid was taken with the signing of the humanitarian consensus (council of the european union, european parliament and european commission), notably by adopting a five-year action plan, which provided for an interim review. that is the aim of this report. the whole world knows and recognises the eu's priority role in humanitarian aid. this parliament has addressed this question at several sittings, including our intervention. indeed, recent events in brazil, haiti, pakistan, madeira and many other places have given us pause to reflect on the effectiveness of civil protection and humanitarian aid support. as this report shows (despite the limited information available), there has been a positive development at european level, as evidenced by the creation of the working group on humanitarian aid and food aid (cohafa). but there is still much to be done!
in writing. - the eu's so-called humanitarian aid plays a significant role in what has come to be known as its foreign policy. often taking advantage of genuine needs for support and cooperation to be met, particularly in emergency situations, the objectives in practice are quite different. the actions and methods employed, including military intervention and occupation, seek to reproduce and deepen forms of political and economic domination, to compete for markets and natural resources in the third world countries. in the present context of the deepening crisis of capitalism, these guidelines are also aimed at containing the struggles of peoples for more justice and social progress, taking on slightly different forms and forms throughout the world. under the guise of a supposed humanitarian interest, various ngos, logistics companies and others are beneficiaries and accomplices of these policies, promoting their own interests or those of their funders, whether public or private, political, profit-making, religious or other. we are in principle in favour of expressions of concrete solidarity with the peoples who are victims of any kind of disaster or conflict. but they must be based on the interests of these peoples, on respect for international law, on the independence and sovereignty of these countries.
in writing. - there is no doubt that natural disasters have become more and more frequent in recent times. it is also true that the eu is one of the world's leading actors in humanitarian aid and, despite the crisis, it is important that this role be maintained. i am of the opinion, however, that, in addition to helping the most disadvantaged and all those affected by such disasters, it is also necessary to provide the poorest countries, and therefore the most vulnerable to such situations, with the human and financial means to prevent external aid from becoming so urgent, and this can only be achieved through development policies and aid to these countries in the medium and long term.
in writing. − the european union, together with the european commission and the member states, is the world's largest donor of humanitarian aid. its contribution represents more than 40% of official international humanitarian assistance. a thorough mid-term evaluation of the implementation of the european consensus on humanitarian aid can only conclude that it is necessary to contribute to a greater dissemination of this mechanism and to greater coordination and effectiveness among all the entities involved. the economic contribution alone can be sterile if it is not accompanied by close and effective coordination at all stages and forms of community aid. we are living in a crucial moment in which the humanitarian context has been profoundly changing in recent years, which makes it all the more relevant to strictly and strongly implement the humanitarian consensus. i am voting in favour of this report and i call for a policy of systematic dialogue, greater cooperation on the ground, better management and a focus on crisis prevention. i support the creation of a european civil protection force, following the barnier report of may 2006.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which takes stock of the implementation of the european consensus on humanitarian aid and makes important proposals to help increase its visibility and make it more effective in pursuing its objectives. in the current humanitarian context, marked by a significant increase in the number and intensity of natural disasters, this instrument is of the greatest relevance, and it is curious that efforts are being made to fully implement the commitments arising from it and to involve member states more closely in its implementation.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because food security is a human right, achieved when all people have access to enough, safe and nutritious food to meet their needs for an active and healthy life. in europe, 16% of citizens still live below the poverty line and food accessibility remains a key unresolved issue. food security therefore continues to require a strong common agricultural policy. the new cap, which is due to come into force after 2013, must respond to food security and other challenges, including climate change, the economic crisis and maintaining the territorial balance in the eu. on the other hand, the eu's ambitious energy targets have encouraged the large-scale cultivation of biofuels, but their production competes with food production in terms of land use, which has a potentially negative impact on food security.
in writing. - food security is a fundamental human right! today, it is estimated that some 900 million people suffer from chronic hunger, and many more do not have a healthy and sufficient diet because of varying degrees of poverty. achieving the desired food security implies that all people have permanent access (physical and economic) to adequate and safe food that meets their nutritional needs. food security through agricultural policy a strong but coherent common with social concerns: consistent in not allowing production surpluses that distort the market and raise environmental problems; social by ensuring that all social strata have access to food and with quality. i also welcome the approach to the issue of diversity in european agriculture; competitiveness and innovation can and must go hand in hand with traditional, small-scale, organic and local distribution agriculture. financial investment in these sectors will be key to effective land use in certain regions, as will energy investment that reduces the dependence between food and energy security.
in writing. - this is an own-initiative report by the european parliament's committee on agriculture and incorporates ideas and suggestions from all the political groups. in this sense, and with a view to obtaining workable commitments, a very comprehensive text has been produced, linked by a minimum common denominator, with which i generally agree. i consider the right to food security to be a fundamental human right and i consider agriculture to be a strategic sector and absolutely indispensable to the future of our continent. that is, as an inalienable element of our sovereignty as a union of peoples and countries. i would like to say that the right to safe food, which is fundamental, must be guaranteed by our own internal production. a cap is therefore essential to ensure this objective. i would reiterate, however, that the fundamental objective of the cap should be to maintain the competitiveness of european agriculture and to support agricultural activity in the eu in order to ensure food production, especially at local level, and balanced territorial development. i also believe that fair incomes in the agricultural sector should be ensured, because it is only possible to stimulate sustainable and ethical production systems if farmers are properly compensated for the investments they make and the commitments they make.

in writing. − the food and agriculture organisation (fao) recently warned of a possible increase in food prices in 2011, after food prices reached new all-time highs in 2010, following the rise during the 2008 food crisis. the fao index of 55 food commodities rose for the sixth consecutive month to 214.7 points, up from the previous all-time high of 213.5 points reached in june 2008. the price of sugar and meat are at new all-time highs and unless there is an increase of at least 2% in cereal production, cereal prices will continue to rise. it is therefore welcome and, as i said in a question to the european commission last week, given that price volatility affects all market players, i believe that concrete measures must be taken within the cap to increase production, to supply markets better and to ensure greater price stability, as well as to ensure production that meets european consumer needs. as i have said, agriculture must be seen, especially in times of crisis, as a strategic sector.

mr president, the intention of this directive is clear from the outset: to include health services in the objective of liberalising services and thus to satisfy the interests of economic and financial groups by expanding their business areas in the field of health in all the countries of the european union, treating health as if it were a market good and the users of health services as mere consumers. this proposal will increase inequalities between citizens, harming those who cannot afford to use private health services or health care in another eu member state. the adoption of this directive, even with the amendments that have been made to it, would have serious consequences for some countries, in particular for portugal and its national health service, given the very high costs that it may entail. in practice, the same european union that imposes heavy constraints on national budgets when it comes to financing public services such as health care, does not mind overburdening those budgets when it comes to channelling public money to private economic and financial groups that are engaged in the business of health and to feed health tourism. in addition, this proposal, in its desire to promote business, did not adequately safeguard the safety of users or the quality of health care, particularly in relation to non-hospital care. contrary to what some have said, the prior authorisation system does not adequately address these cases. it is therefore necessary, as in 2007 with the exclusion of health services from the infamous bolkestein directive, that these intentions be defeated again.
mr president, this text is the result of a lot of work and negotiation and i would like to thank my colleagues mr bowis, mr grossetête and mr roth-behrendt for this. it is right to acknowledge the progress made because this new version gives more guarantees as regards safety and quality of services. although the wording of articles 7 and 8 has been improved, i think that more could have been done to ensure greater fairness. most patients, especially those from weaker socioeconomic groups, do not want to be treated abroad because of language barriers and lack of family support. higher-income citizens do not have these obstacles. so i fear that in countries with universal and tendingly free health care systems, the new legislation may act as an incentive to divest from national systems and help create a health market for the rich. i hope, however, that the implementation of the directive will help to reduce health inequalities.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this directive allows all patients in the european union to benefit from health care, given the rights they now have in this area, rights which have already been recognised by the court of justice of the european union. this proposal clarifies and facilitates access to crossborder healthcare and the exercise of the right to reimbursement by the member state of affiliation. it is a step forward in the process of european integration and construction, in the strengthening of solidarity and in the europe of the citizens. we will have shorter waiting lists, better health care, competition and more incentives for scientific research. rare diseases are a priority, and diagnosis and treatment in the member state can be made more appropriate for this purpose. this directive is for all european citizens who need health care. it is therefore absurd for the portuguese minister for health to say that this is an option for the most educated and the most economically powerful. that is what is happening now without this directive. portugal has excellent health care, excellent professionals and cannot be left out of this important project, and it must take advantage of this directive to modernise itself further and compete in order to be able to provide services in this area to all european citizens who need them. i would like to congratulate the great rapporteur, mrs françoise grossetête, who has done an excellent job.
mr president, commissioner, madam minister, this directive lays down rules to facilitate access to safe and quality crossborder healthcare and promotes cooperation between member states in full respect of national competences. it contains core values of universal access to high-quality health care, equity and solidarity. the benefits for patients, especially those suffering from rare and complex diseases, are clear, as they will be able to access centres of excellence in the area of their disease. this directive is another example of europe at the service of the citizen. we all congratulate you, especially the commission, the council and our colleague, mrs françoise grossetête, on the excellent work you have done and on helping to make this directive a reality. in writing. after a long process, we have today adopted the text of the directive on the exercise of patients' rights in crossborder healthcare. it is a success for parliament, but above all a victory for consumers. the new legislative framework will allow citizens of any member state to receive healthcare in another member state under the same conditions as in their own state. this mobility of patients will make it possible to bypass national waiting lists in completely legitimate conditions and to take advantage of the availability of medical services in other european countries. it also opens up the possibility of specialisation (especially in rare diseases), by moving from providing healthcare in the vicinity to the place where you specialise in your treatment. we are not here to promote medical tourism, but to ensure full mobility of citizens within the eu on equal terms, so that from now on everyone can choose to seek treatment where it is faster, more effective and of higher quality, with reimbursement of the costs by the home country, in the exact terms in which they would have been if health care had been provided there.

member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, i again thank parliament and the members who have taken the floor for their engagement with the important cause of alzheimer’s and other forms of dementia. the commission welcomes parliament’s report and its recommendations. let me take this opportunity to stress that the commission is fully committed to doing its share to address alzheimer’s and other forms of dementia. these conditions are unfortunately part of the ageing process for many european citizens. i believe it is our collective responsibility to work together to minimise their burden and to invest in innovation to prevent, diagnose, treat and manage these conditions. i look forward to supporting member states in their efforts to work closely with parliament in addressing alzheimer’s disease and other forms of dementia. on the ‘effecto’ klein petition, i must state first of all – referring to mrs manzoni’s statement that the commission’s job is to stand by the citizens – that i can assure you my job is to stand by the patient. it is very important for me, as commissioner responsible for health, not to compromise on patient safety, not to take any shortcuts and short-circuit the processes and procedures that we have in place to ensure that any device to be used in any medical way is properly tested and its safety assured. the issue here is not how to deliver a medicine with a piece of plastic, as has been said. the issue is that we need clinical evidence that the product is safe and to do this the petitioner, in this case mr klein, was requested to conduct clinical studies on 24 patients. that is the extent of the clinical tests that were requested. why is there a resistance to providing these clinical tests? what is causing this resistance? this is something that i am asking myself. we need to know, for example, is this product universal in application, is it to be used with one specific medicine, is it to be used with different types of medicines? if it is, do these medicines require different dosages? is there an adjustment system in the device to adjust the dosage? as a layman, if i had to use a device like this, these are the questions that i would ask myself. this is the kind of thing the authorities have been asking themselves. they have been asking for proof that this device would be safe in the hands of patients at large. there is, as i said, a proper safety assurance procedure, and i will be not short-circuiting that. it has been said that i promised to look into the case. i promised to look into the case, and i did look into the case. i have had a lot of details about the case. naturally, these are details that i had to learn from others who have been here in the commission since 1987. when mr klein asked for a meeting with me or my cabinet, i immediately agreed. my ‘chef de cabinet’ informed him that we were prepared to have a meeting to explain it. he sent an e-mail back setting a lot of conditions, amongst which he stated that as a basis for this meeting, the eu commission should completely take over the expenses. this included the flights and overnight stays in brussels for him and his staff, and i could not accommodate this.
