hungary takes over the eu presidency at a time when the economic and financial crisis is still ongoing. the last country in the tripartite presidency, shared by spain and belgium, has as its main agenda the economic recovery, the integration of the roma people, an energy strategy, the enlargement process and the involvement of citizens in the european project. the programme considers that the institutionalisation of the financial stabilisation mechanism and the european semester is essential for economic recovery. i consider it extremely important to strengthen cooperation and coordination at economic level as a means of promoting european competitiveness and innovation and thus preventing and/or anticipating future crises. in the area of transport, the new strategy 2011-2020 will be adopted, as will the amendments to the transport network directive which are essential for the completion of the internal market and for social, economic and territorial cohesion. the road, navigation on eu rivers and the implementation of the galileo system are other topics that will be discussed. regional policy is once again seen as the horizontal pillar of the whole hungarian programme strategy, capable of providing integrated responses to the economic crisis and regional disparities. the allocation of the post-2014 multiannual financial framework appears to be the key debate of the hungarian presidency.
in writing. − the directive on patients' rights in crossborder healthcare represents an essential step for patient mobility within the european union. the aim is to clarify and facilitate access to safe and quality cross-border healthcare and the exercise of the right to reimbursement by the member state of affiliation, and to promote cooperation between member states. the advantages for patients are clear, especially for those suffering from rare and complex diseases who will thus be able to make diagnosis and treatment in the member state more appropriate for that purpose. on the other hand, this mobility will make it possible to legitimately bypass national waiting lists by taking advantage of the availability of medical services in other countries of the european union. this directive will enable all patients to benefit from a number of rights already recognised by the court of justice of the european union. it is undoubtedly a step forward in the process of european integration and construction, in the strengthening of solidarity and in the europe of the citizens. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − this directive lays down rules to facilitate access to safe and high-quality crossborder healthcare and promotes cooperation on healthcare between member states, in full respect of national competences. it contains the common core values of universality, access to high quality health care, equity and solidarity. the benefits for patients, especially those suffering from rare or chronic diseases, are clear, as they will be able to benefit from and have access to centres of excellence in the area of their disease. this directive is another example of europe at the service of its citizens, since it allows the choice of the institution which will provide the appropriate health care, regardless of the european country in which it is located.
in writing. − member states are responsible for providing safe, high-quality, effective and necessary healthcare to their citizens. this directive should therefore not affect the freedom of the member state to decide on the most appropriate type of health care. we live in an area of freedom, security and justice where european citizens enjoy freedom of movement, which makes it urgent to establish clear rules on the provision of cross-border healthcare, in particular the issue of reimbursement of costs relating to healthcare provided in another member state. following the case law of the court of justice, this directive allows european citizens to be more confident that they will be able to receive the medical care they need in another member state and be reimbursed up to the amount provided for by their national system. it is important to create a system of prior authorisation for hospital care that is simplified and does not hinder patients from obtaining safe and quality medical care. this directive is an essential first step towards ensuring patient mobility within the eu, and uniform minimum rules are preferable to the case-by-case recourse to judicial decisions.
in writing. − this proposal clarifies and facilitates access to crossborder healthcare and the exercise of the right to reimbursement by the member state of affiliation, allowing all eu patients to benefit from healthcare in another member state, rights which were already recognised by the court of justice of the european union. it is a step forward in the process of european integration and construction and in the strengthening of solidarity, with a reduction in waiting lists, a higher quality of health care and the encouragement of scientific research. rare diseases are a priority and diagnosis and treatment can be carried out in the member state most appropriate for this purpose. this directive is for all european citizens who need health care. that is why it is absurd for the portuguese minister of health to say that this option is for the most enlightened people and those with the greatest economic power. that is what is happening now, without this directive. portugal has excellent health care and cannot be left out of this important project, and should take advantage of this directive to modernise itself further and compete to be able to provide services in this area to all european citizens who need them.
in writing. - we voted against the directive on the application of patients' rights in crossborder healthcare, although it contains some changes compared to the original text. this final text is the result of a compromise reached by a majority in the council, which provides for 30 months for its transposition by the member states. our vote against is the result of applying the principle of free movement to health services, without taking into account their specific features, including the need for a national public health service that responds first and foremost, in each country, to the needs of its citizens. it is recalled that this proposal of the european commission came after the refusal by the european parliament to include health services in the directive on the liberalisation of services in 2007, in the face of the important struggle of workers and populations, defeating this part of the infamous bolkestein proposal for a directive. however, the final decision of the european parliament, which we have always fought against, includes some back-up measures which allow member states who so wish to use some of the mechanisms for protecting their public services. although it may increase the difficulties of access to health services, especially for citizens who cannot afford to use private health services or have the money to pay for trips abroad, the practical consequences of its application will still depend on the decision of the assembly of the republic and the portuguese government.
in writing. - the question of access to healthcare, reimbursement or responsibility for clinical follow-up of crossborder healthcare is currently unclear to the vast majority of citizens. the aim of this directive is to ensure that all patients, not just those who are best informed, benefit from a number of rights in health care, which have now been recognised by the court of justice of the european union. however, this directive does not remove responsibilities from the member states as regards the health care of their citizens. it only concerns patients and their mobility within the eu, not the free movement of service providers.
in writing. − each member state is responsible for providing healthcare to its citizens. this directive lays down rules to facilitate access to safe and high-quality cross-border healthcare and promotes cooperation on healthcare between member states, in full respect of national competences. the evolution of highly specialised healthcare is asymmetrical, with centres of excellence developing in certain countries for rare or chronic diseases which, in that particular place, have an unusual incidence and require specialisation. this is certainly one of the conditions for promoting free movement in this chapter. we are faced with a directive which is an example of europe at the service of its citizens, promoting solidarity between peoples and creating advantages for patients, especially those suffering from rare or chronic diseases, who will be able to benefit from and have access to centres of excellence in the field of their disease. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − this directive aims, in line with the case law of the court of justice of the european union, to clarify and strengthen the rights of users in terms of access to safe and high-quality crossborder healthcare, by promoting patient mobility within the eu and enhancing cooperation and solidarity between member states in this field. it therefore represents an important step forward in the construction of europe, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the objective of building an internal market based on free movement between member states requires measures to achieve it. the free movement of persons and services requires particular attention in the form of health care that nationals of one member state may receive in another eu state. the court of justice has recognised rights for patients, in particular with regard to access to healthcare, its high quality and safety and reimbursement. the need for greater legal certainty in this area implies a commitment by the states to cooperate with each other, in particular by recognising medical prescriptions issued in other states, and to guarantee a quality service in their own territory. i would stress that the commission will be obliged to take measures to make information easier to understand, with regard to prescription and instructions for use of medicinal products, the indication of the active substance and dosage, which will be of clear benefit to patients. the specific nature of the subject makes a separate directive from the services directive necessary. i think it is important to affirm the rights of patients in terms of crossborder healthcare, and i therefore voted in favour of the report by mrs grossetête.
in writing. - i welcome the voluntary partnership agreements (vpas) for what they represent in terms of combating the trade in illegal timber in the eu. i would stress its importance in combating deforestation and forest degradation, and the resulting carbon emissions and loss of biodiversity worldwide. those agreements promote economic growth, human development and sustainable food sources at the same time. i call on the commission to ensure a coherent eu policy with a view to making an effective contribution to the international commitments of all parties involved in the vpas.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on flegt voluntary partnership agreements (vpas), as the negotiation of these vpas should allow the definition of good practices for future negotiations with timber-producing countries with a view to eradicating illegal logging and the conservation and sustainable use of forest resources at global level.
in writing. - illegal logging is a real plunder of the natural resources of producing countries, usually developing countries, and a clear attack on biodiversity and the quality of life of the population and its prospects for the future. agreements such as those concluded with the congo and cameroon, if they prove effective in combating this scourge, could provide a good basis for future agreements of the same kind. i welcome the european concern to protect the natural resources of other countries, but i cannot help stressing that, despite the legal framework resulting from the agreements, any success in the fight against illegal timber trafficking depends overwhelmingly on the governments and institutions of the producing states. without their effective involvement and commitment, any instruments that are agreed will be nothing more than dead letters. this model is therefore also a call for accountability from eu counterparts so that they understand the need to safeguard the interests of their future generations and can resist the appeal of immediate profit for the benefit of all.
in writing. − the european union has been fighting against illegal logging, seeking to conserve and promote the sustainable use of forest resources globally. i therefore welcome the conclusion of the voluntary partnership agreements (vpas) with cameroon and the republic of congo to improve forest governance and reform existing legislation where necessary to ensure that forestry activities are transparent, respect the rights of indigenous peoples and do not contribute to adverse environmental effects. these agreements are key to eradicating illegal logging, halting deforestation, forest degradation and the resulting carbon emissions and loss of biodiversity worldwide. i would stress in this connection the request to the commission to draw up and regularly submit to parliament a report on the progress made in implementing the various provisions of the current and future agreements.
in writing. the resolution rightly points out that large-scale industrial exploitation of tropical forests is unsustainable, leading to the degradation and destruction of ecosystems of great importance, both from the functional point of view and from the point of view of the natural values they house. it also points out the limitations and even contradictions of the voluntary flegt partnership agreements, which we believe is right and timely. but it falls short of what would be needed in addressing the root causes of the problem of illegal or unsustainable logging. in particular, it would be important to point out that this problem is inseparable from the enormous weakness of the economies of these countries and the significant levels of poverty among their populations, this activity being sometimes the only source of income for many families. this would necessarily lead to the conclusion - contained in the amendment we tabled and which was unfortunately rejected - that it is only possible to put an end to illegal or unsustainable logging if the terrible social and economic situation prevailing in these countries is properly addressed and resolved; if an economic model based on the high dependence on the exploitation and export of a limited number of raw materials to the industrialized countries is reversed, sustaining neo-colonial relations of dependence, subjugation and plunder of resources of the third world countries.
in writing. - logging in african countries is often carried out illegally, which is very bad for the protection of the natural resources of the producing countries and is also a threat to biodiversity and the quality of life of the population and its prospects for the future. the agreements concluded with the congo and cameroon could help to reverse this trend if they are effective and clearly end the scourge of illegal logging in these african countries. the eu's defence of foreign natural resources through such agreements is noteworthy. however, for these initiatives to succeed, it is very important that the governments and institutions of the producing states help in this fight.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the voluntary partnership agreements on the enforcement of legislation, governance and trade in the forestry sector in respect of timber products imported into the european union (flegt). i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe that the negotiation of these ppas will provide guidance on good practice which can serve as a precedent for the negotiations currently under way on other ppas with timber-producing countries. in this context, i welcome the eu's assumption of its share of responsibility in eradicating illegal logging, as well as the related trade and enforcement efforts towards the conservation and sustainable use of forest resources globally. i welcome the fact that the commitments made by the parties involved to improve forest governance are transparent and respect the rights of indigenous peoples, ensuring forest biodiversity, climate and sustainable human development.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which, in line with the voluntary partnership agreements (vpas) concluded with cameroon and the republic of congo, stresses the need to provide, in the framework of the negotiations for future agreements of this type, for measures to meet the objectives of eradicating illegal logging, conserving and using forest resources sustainably and respecting the rights of local populations.
in writing. − i agree with the aim of providing a legislative framework to identify and ensure the traceability of timber products, to establish governmental and independent verification procedures to certify that all timber products exported by cameroon to european markets have been legally harvested, cut, transported and exported, to establish the basis for legal management and exploitation in the cameroonian timber sector and to strengthen the enforcement of forestry regulation and governance. i also believe that this agreement is of the utmost importance as this country is the main african exporter of timber to europe and has serious problems at various levels of governance, such as environmental degradation and corruption. it is also necessary to ensure compliance with the international commitments made by the eu and cameroon in environmental terms, the adoption of civil society oversight and greater involvement of local and indigenous communities, ensuring that they enjoy their fundamental rights.
in writing. − i welcome the commitments made between the eu and the republic of cameroon to improve forest governance and reform existing legislation where necessary to ensure that forestry activities are transparent, respect the rights of indigenous peoples and do not contribute to adverse environmental effects. the forest environment is a common heritage of humanity and must be protected, preserved and, if possible, restored with the ultimate aim of maintaining global biodiversity and ecosystem functions, protecting the climate. it is essential that partner governments in africa and third countries develop resource management and land-use planning plans to achieve these objectives. at the same time, they should identify the support that will be needed from foreign partners and international organisations to advance these objectives.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation on the eu-cameroon voluntary partnership agreement, because it provides for political and legislative reforms that will enable the cameroonian timber sector to promote good governance and transparency with a view to combating fraud and illegal timber trade.
in writing. − the conclusion of a voluntary partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of cameroon on forest law enforcement, governance and trade in timber products imported into the european union (flegt) is of the utmost importance given the negative impact that illegal timber trafficking necessarily entails. this agreement should allow the tracing of the origin of the wood and encourage the application of independent verification procedures to prove this. i hope that the linking of cameroon to flegt will effectively reduce the means at the disposal of traffickers and thus establish an effective and transparent system for monitoring the legality of timber.
in writing. − the european union has been fighting against illegal logging, seeking to conserve and promote the sustainable use of forest resources globally. i therefore welcome the conclusion of the voluntary partnership agreements (vpas) with cameroon to improve forest governance and reform existing legislation where necessary to ensure that forestry activities are transparent, respect the rights of indigenous peoples and do not contribute to adverse environmental effects. these agreements are key to eradicating illegal logging, halting deforestation, forest degradation and the resulting carbon emissions and loss of biodiversity worldwide. i would stress in this connection the request to the commission to draw up and regularly submit to parliament a report on the progress made in implementing the various provisions of the current and future agreements.
in writing. - the objectives set out in this agreement, aimed at the traceability and certification of wood products originating in the republic of cameroon, while apparently meritorious, do not respond in the way we believe would be necessary to the problem of the destruction of forests and, with it, the threat to the integrity of resources of extreme ecological and conservation value, on which the existence and the way of life of local communities and indigenous peoples depend. the rapporteur himself is aware of the weaknesses of the agreement, as he lists a wide range of concerns not explicitly addressed in it. in particular, the agreement does not exclude the possibility that large-scale industrial exploitation may encourage forest degradation and deforestation, including in intact forest areas of high biodiversity. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat climate change, and for the eu to take action to combat climate change. it is recognised that there is no direct involvement of local communities and indigenous peoples in the discussion of the agreement. it is also acknowledged that there is no specific funding and no technical or human support necessary for its implementation. these are some of the reasons why we abstained.
in writing. - logging in african countries is often carried out illegally, which is very bad for the protection of the natural resources of the producing countries and is also a threat to biodiversity and the quality of life of the population and its prospects for the future. i hope that the agreement negotiated with cameroon will combat the illegal exploitation of that country's timber resources effectively, thereby contributing to the improvement of the living conditions of the people who live off the income of this economic sector, and also contributing to the improvement of biodiversity and the protection of cameroon's natural resources.
in writing. - i am in favour of the conclusion of a voluntary partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of cameroon, which aims to strengthen forest governance, promote cameroonian wood products and improve the country's competitiveness on the international market. these objectives should respect the objectives and commitments of the flegt agreement (strengthening rights of occupation and access to community land, ensuring the effective participation of civil society, with particular attention to indigenous peoples, in political decisions on forest governance matters, improving transparency and reducing corruption). the effective and efficient involvement of the authorities of the republic of cameroon is necessary to ensure that these objectives are not rendered fruitless. i agree with the rapporteur when he stresses the need for the european parliament, in the light of the new powers conferred by the treaty of lisbon, to monitor the different stages of negotiation and implementation of the vpas, requesting the commission, among other documents for the analysis of the implementation of the agreement, to carry out studies on the social, economic and environmental impacts of this agreement.
in writing. − the eu-cameroon voluntary partnership agreement provides for a series of political and legislative reforms that will enable the cameroonian timber sector to establish good governance practices and greater transparency. it is important to ensure that timber and timber products from cameroon entering european markets do so in full compliance with the law and that the reforms implemented ensure respect for the rights of local and indigenous communities and have an effective impact in terms of fighting corruption and strengthening the role of local civil society. i therefore supported the conclusion of this agreement and expressed my hope that the commitments and objectives of flegt would be fully respected in its implementation.
in writing. − i agree with the aim of providing a legislative framework to identify and ensure the traceability of timber products by establishing governmental and independent verification procedures that certify that all timber products exported from the congo to european markets have been legally harvested, logged, transported and exported, in order to lay the foundations for legal management and exploitation in the congolese timber sector and to strengthen the enforcement of forest regulation and governance. this agreement is important as the country exports over eur 250 million a year in wood and wood products, more than half of which is destined for the eu. i also agree with the need to ensure that the congo fulfils its international commitments in terms of human rights and the environment.
in writing. - i welcome the commitments made through the voluntary partnership agreements (vpas) between the eu and the republic of congo to improve forest governance and reform existing legislation in this field. it is necessary to ensure that forestry activities are transparent, respect the rights of the people and do not contribute to adverse environmental effects. i would stress the role of independent national civil society organisations and independent external observers in monitoring the proper implementation of the vpas by all parties involved.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation on the eu-congo voluntary partnership agreement, because it provides for political and legislative reforms that will enable the congolese timber sector to promote good governance and transparency with a view to combating fraud and illegal timber trade.
in writing. - the illegal trade in timber is a problem that seriously affects producing countries, including the congo, and threatens the ecosystems, livelihoods and economies of developing countries themselves. unfortunately, the european union continues to receive illegal timber, and all measures to make it more difficult for it to enter the community are welcome. in this sense, a partnership agreement to safeguard the origin and legality of timber entering the european union is obviously a positive measure. as with other consumer goods, the consumer should be able to trace the wood to its origin and ensure that it complies with the legal requirements applicable to it.
in writing. − the european union has been fighting against illegal logging, seeking to conserve and promote the sustainable use of forest resources globally. i therefore welcome the conclusion of the voluntary partnership agreements (vpas) with the republic of congo to improve forest governance and reform existing legislation where necessary to ensure that forestry sector activities are transparent, respect the rights of indigenous peoples and do not contribute to adverse environmental effects. these agreements are key to eradicating illegal logging, halting deforestation, forest degradation and the resulting carbon emissions and loss of biodiversity worldwide. i would stress in this connection the request to the commission to draw up and regularly submit to parliament a report on the progress made in implementing the various provisions of the current and future agreements.
in writing. - this agreement aims to ensure the traceability and certification of wood products originating in the republic of congo, objectives which, while seemingly meritorious, do not respond to the way we understand that would be necessary to the problem of the destruction of forests of high ecological and conservation value, on which local communities and indigenous peoples depend. the concerns expressed by the rapporteur himself are sufficient to show the weaknesses of the agreement, which justified our abstention. in particular, the agreement does not, by itself, ensure the fight against deforestation and the large-scale degradation of intact forests, and may even, in the absence of additional and complementary measures, promote them, since it favours the import of wood products from the congo into the eu area. this could result in clear contradictions with the eu's stated objectives of combating climate change and protecting biodiversity. the report also stresses the lack of specific funding and of the technical and human resources needed to implement the agreement.
in writing. - logging in african countries is often carried out illegally, which is very bad for the protection of the natural resources of the producing countries and is also a threat to biodiversity and the quality of life of the population and its prospects for the future. i hope that the agreement negotiated with the congo will effectively combat illegal logging in that country, thereby contributing to the improvement of the living conditions of the people who live off the income from this economic sector, and also contributing to the improvement of biodiversity and the protection of the congolese natural resources.
in writing. - the voluntary partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of congo on the enforcement of the law, governance and trade in forestry products imported into the eu (flegt) also received my vote in favour. i welcome the objective of creating a legislative framework to, among other things, identify and ensure the traceability of timber products, to establish governmental and independent verification procedures to certify that all timber products exported from the congo to european markets have been legally harvested, logged, transported and exported, in order to lay the foundations for legal management and exploitation in the congolese timber sector, and to strengthen the enforcement of forestry regulation and governance. the highlight of the congo-eu fta, concluded on 9 may 2009, was the fulfilment of the criteria resulting from the fta definitions, in particular at the level of the negotiation process, which resulted in an innovative agreement aimed at effectively combating the practices of poor governance that underpin the illegal timber trade and corruption, and the establishment of an effective and transparent system for monitoring the legality of the timber and timber products sector.
in writing. − the eu-congo voluntary partnership agreement provides for a series of political and legislative reforms that will enable the congolese timber sector to establish good governance practices and greater transparency. it is important to ensure that timber and timber products from the congo enter european markets lawfully and that the reforms implemented ensure respect for the rights of local and indigenous communities, contribute to improving the living conditions of the population and to preserving the environment, and have an effective impact on the fight against corruption and on the capacity building of local civil society. i therefore supported the conclusion of this agreement and expressed my hope that the commitments and objectives of flegt would be fully respected in its implementation.
in writing. - i welcome the efforts being made to strengthen trade relations between the pacific and the eu with a view to supporting regional integration and promoting the progressive integration of the acp economies into the world economy. the eu has an important role to play in promoting sustainable social and economic development in the acp countries and in contributing to the overall effort to eradicate poverty in these countries. trade relations between this region and the eu should therefore foster and increase trade, sustainable development and regional integration, while contributing to economic diversification and poverty reduction. the current economic and financial crisis makes trade policy more important than ever for the developing world, and i call for the swift negotiation of a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (epa) with all 14 pacific acp states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the partnership agreement will support regional integration and promote the progressive integration of the acp economies into the world economy, while at the same time promoting the sustainable social and economic development of these countries and also contributing to the eradication of poverty.
in writing. - although only papua new guinea and fiji have signed the interim partnership agreement with the european community, i believe it may be worth supporting because it allows the opening of european markets to local products and, in return, a phased opening of their markets to european products. i hope that trade relations between the pacific states and the european union will increase and strengthen, while respecting local specificities and taking into account the special needs of those who have the least. this trade mechanism should therefore be used in the light of the development needs of the signatory states and as a tool for their promotion. the global agreement to be concluded should not ignore the key issues listed in the resolution: (a) negotiations on intellectual property rights; (b) transparency of public procurement; and (c) the granting of work visas.
in writing. − the partnership agreements between the ec and the pacific states should aim at increasing trade, sustainable development and regional integration, while promoting economic diversification and poverty reduction. although only papua new guinea and the republic of the fiji islands have signed the agreement at present, it is an important step for the future economic development of this region of 14 states and a key factor in the development of international trade.
in writing. − it is clear from this european parliament resolution on the ec-pacific provisional partnership agreement that there is a widespread belief that promoting trade relations between the ec and the pacific states and the eu should foster and increase trade, sustainable development and regional integration, while promoting economic diversification and poverty reduction, and that this interim agreement should fulfil the millennium development goals. this, together with the creation of a genuine regional market, is a crucial basis for the successful implementation of the interim epa and, by analogy, of a possible global epa in the future. regional integration and cooperation are essential for the social and economic development of the pacific states. i voted in favour because i am convinced that this epa can contribute to the economic development of these regions and i share the concerns expressed in the resolution that this development must be accompanied by policies of environmental sustainability and inclusion. the european parliament shall be responsible for monitoring the implementation of this agreement within the framework of the powers conferred on it by the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution on the interim partnership agreement between the ec and the pacific states, hoping that this agreement, now limited to two countries papua new guinea and the fiji islands , can pave the way for the conclusion of a broader agreement, which constitutes an instrument for promoting sustainable social and economic development in the pacific region, as well as for poverty reduction and the strengthening of regional integration and cooperation, in line with the millennium development goals.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it contributes to the establishment of new trade arrangements compatible with wto rules with the countries of fiji and papua new guinea. provisional economic partnership agreements (epas) are agreements on trade in goods which are intended to prevent a break in acp trade with europe. although the interim agreements may be considered as a first step in the process, legally they are fully independent international agreements which may not necessarily lead to a full epa. i welcome the recommendations on the conclusion of final agreements, on the origin of eu funds to finance these agreements (not to come from the edf), the need for a parliamentary committee to monitor implementation and a global impact review clause within three to five years.
in writing. − despite the limited number of countries that have accepted the interim partnership agreement, it demonstrates europe's commitment to supporting the development of the pacific countries through the use of a mechanism that goes beyond mere assistance procedures and seeks to mobilise local economies, the desirable effect of which will be the creation of businesses and jobs and greater movement of people and goods. despite my agreement in principle to such an instrument, i am not unaware of the doubts about the impact the partnership agreement may have on the industrial sector related to fisheries. i would therefore like the european commission to follow this matter with particular care and i believe it is justified for that institution to submit a report to the european parliament on fisheries in the pacific and the management of fishery resources in the region as requested by the rapporteur.
in the light of the recent developments in the region, the commission has decided to extend the period of validity of the provisional partnership agreement to the period from 1 january 1997 to 31 december 1999. 1. these countries represent the largest economies in the region and have concluded economic partnership agreements with the eu in the past; 2. notwithstanding the interest in extending this partnership to other states in the region, this has not been possible; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. 4. the republic of fiji has undertaken commitments to the eu with regard to human rights, democratic principles and the rule of law; 5.despite criticism from civil society and political elements in the region, this partnership can contribute to the strategic development of these countries.
in writing. - we have long been critical of the conclusion of these epas with the acp countries. these agreements, whatever their designation and whatever rhetorical phrases they use, are aimed primarily at the objective of free trade, with all the profoundly negative consequences that follow from this. recently, and again at the last acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly in december 2010, the acp council expressed concern that the european commission did not respect its objections on matters relating to the defence of their economies, even considering that there is a contradiction between the commission's claimed flexibility and the inflexible stance it has taken in the technical negotiations. in this (provisional) epa with fiji and papua new guinea, too, the eu has been heavily criticised by social and political organisations in the pacific region for putting pressure on these two countries to sign the provisional agreement, with the threat of losing preferential access to european markets. there is also criticism that there has been a significant decline in solidarity between the pacific states since the signing of this agreement, and that this has created feelings of division, leading to the disintegration of some regional groups due to the pressures they have felt to conclude the interim agreements.
in writing. − the partnership agreements between the ec and the pacific states should aim at increasing trade, sustainable development and regional integration, while promoting economic diversification and poverty reduction. although only papua new guinea and the republic of the fiji islands have signed the agreement at present, it is an important step for the future economic development of this region of 14 states and a key factor in the development of international trade. this is the first step towards extending the agreement to other countries in the region and thus giving a major boost to their economies and the well-being of their populations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation on the interim eu-pacific partnership agreement for the following reasons. fiji and papua new guinea decided to enter into the agreement mainly in the hope of protecting their sugar and tuna industries. the interim agreement covers rules of origin for fisheries, textiles and agriculture, but provides for derogations which may affect the competitiveness of certain community industries. as regards the canned tuna sector, the derogation granted allows countries such as papua new guinea to act as hubs for the processing of huge quantities of tuna of all origins (philippines, thailand, china, usa, australia, etc.) landed in their ports to be processed in factories set up hastily by operators from the countries concerned for the sole purpose of benefiting from the full exemption from customs duties granted by the eu under this interim agreement. this has hurt the european canning sector, which has complained of unfair competition. i therefore join the rapporteur in calling for a report to be submitted to parliament on the specific aspects of the fisheries sector in the pacific states to assess the real impact that these measures may have on the community market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, as i believe that promoting trade relations between the pacific states and the eu can contribute to promoting the sustainable social and economic development of the region, as well as to reducing poverty and strengthening regional integration and cooperation, in line with the millennium development goals. i share, however, the concerns expressed by the rapporteur regarding the derogating system of origin rules and its negative impact on the eu fish processing and canning industry, which should be properly assessed by the commission.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on intercountry adoption in the european union. although this is a matter for the member states, i believe that the protection of children's rights should be an objective of the european union. in this context, i believe that it is necessary to consider the possibility of coordinating strategies at european level on the instrument of intercountry adoption and on post-adoption services, taking into account that all international conventions on the protection of the rights of the child recognize the right of abandoned or orphaned children to have a family and to receive protection.
in writing. - adoption of children is a particularly sensitive matter. the dignity of the person and, in the present case, the special care which the best interests of the child require, call for compliance with the international conventions relating to the child, the study of best practices and the exchange of experience between member states. the european union can accompany these efforts and contribute to tackling the scourge of child trafficking, which affects above all the poorest countries and the most vulnerable people.
in writing. − the european union has always fought for the protection of children's rights and for the defence of their best interests. this resolution calls for consideration to be given to the possibility of coordinating at european level strategies relating to the instrument of intercountry adoption, in accordance with international conventions, in order to improve assistance in the fields of information services, intercountry adoption preparation, processing of applications for intercountry adoption and post-adoption services, taking into account that all international conventions on the protection of the rights of the child recognize the right of abandoned or orphaned children to have a family and to receive protection. i voted in favour because i believe that although the matter of adoption is a matter for the member states, a minimum of european convergence is necessary, provided that the best interests of the child are always respected.
in writing. - we all agree with the defence of the welfare of children and the guarantee of their rights, as stated in the european parliament's resolution. but it is not enough to make these general statements. it is also necessary to look at the causes that lead to the exploitation of children in situations of intercountry adoption. the main causes of child abandonment are poverty, inadequate social security systems, lack of adequate social infrastructure networks, lack of adequate public services, and conflict and military interventions.
in writing. − adoption of children is a matter of concern to the eu and should be treated with the utmost care. children are the future of any society and, in this sense, they must be treated with all dignity, taking into account their best interests, which require and recommend compliance with the international conventions concerning them. it is therefore the eu's duty to do everything in its power to tackle the scourge of child trafficking, which affects children in particular in the poorest and most deprived countries.
in writing. the european parliament has voted in favour of this resolution on international adoption in the eu. this is an initiative which meets the objective of the union, as defined in article 3 of the lisbon treaty, namely the protection of the rights of the child. the economic development of eu countries does not prevent serious shortcomings in children's rights. in particular, the problems of childhood poverty, in particular abandoned and institutionalized children, violence against them and trafficking of children for adoption, prostitution, clandestine labour, forced marriage, begging and other illegal purposes, remain a serious problem in the eu. this is the framework which defines the importance of this initiative which asks the commission to consider the possibility of coordinating strategies at european level concerning the instrument of intercountry adoption. a strategy in line with international conventions to improve assistance in the areas of information services, preparation and processing of applications and post-adoption services. to have in mind the protection of the rights of the child and to recognise the right of abandoned or orphaned minors to have a family and to be protected.
in writing. adoption is a particularly sensitive issue which should be given full attention by the member states and the eu. despite considerable progress made under the hague convention on the protection of the rights of the child, childhood poverty, violations of children's rights, violence against children and trafficking in children for adoption, prostitution, illegal labour and other illegal purposes remain a problem in the eu. every effort should therefore be made to protect the child's right to family life, and in this regard it is important to consider the possibility of coordinating strategies at european level on the instrument of intercountry adoption, in accordance with international conventions, in order to improve assistance in the areas of information services, preparation and processing of applications and post-adoption services.
in writing. - the right of a child to grow up in a healthy family environment, conducive to his or her harmonious development, is the key concept behind this resolution. the growing number of children living in orphanages, as well as the violation of their rights, namely human trafficking, adoption and illegal labour and prostitution, which persists in the european union, leads to a position to reverse these developments. at the same time, there is a growing number of illegal international adoptions from third countries which do not comply with the requirements of the hague convention. the institutionalisation of children's rights in the eu, in article 3 tfeu as one of the eu's objectives, and in the charter of fundamental rights, article 24, opens up the opportunity to coordinate member states' policies and strategies, in line with existing international instruments. i believe that the creation of a mechanism at european level to show how the different national systems in this field work is urgent. a transparent and effective mechanism to monitor the adoption of children, pre- and post-adoption, and the involvement of international organisations, not only promotes children's rights but also opens the door to their harmonious development.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this own-initiative report which aims to further a set of measures, in particular with regard to promoting early diagnosis and quality of life, improving epidemiological knowledge of the disease and the coordination of existing research, promoting the sharing of good practice between member states and respect for people living with dementia, because in the current situation, where every year some 14 million european citizens develop some form of dementia, alzheimer's disease accounts for half of these cases. the different existing policies need to be articulated in order to address this situation in a coordinated, objective and more effective way, supporting carers and families in areas such as strengthening different health systems and in training and counselling. i think it is important that the european dementia strategy places more emphasis on the social dimension of people living with dementia, with an increasing emphasis on research and early prevention and diagnosis.
in writing. − dementia is a disease characterised by a slow and progressive loss of memory, concentration and the ability to learn, usually in people over 65 years of age. dementias are a group of neurodegenerative diseases that should not be considered as a normal part of the aging process. estimates suggest that more than 8 million europeans aged 30 to 99 suffer from neurodegenerative diseases (12.5 per 1 000 inhabitants), with women more affected than men. scientific media admit that this number may double in the next 20 years. the most common type of dementia in europe is alzheimer's disease (representing 50-70% of cases). i voted in favour of this report, which aims to improve the quality of life and well-being of patients, encourage research and prevention and improve coordination between member states in order to provide a more effective and supportive response to the prevention and treatment of people living with dementia, in particular alzheimer's disease, and those around them. equally important is the proposal for the creation of a european year of mental health.

in writing. − the eu institutions and the member states have an obligation to ensure that human rights are respected, protected and promoted, in accordance with the european convention on human rights, the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and article 6 of the treaty on european union, without any distinction on grounds of sexual orientation. it is therefore necessary to urge the lithuanian authorities to refrain from adopting any legislation which would infringe the principle of equality and non-discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation.
religious freedom statistics show that in recent years, most acts of religious violence have been committed against christians. in 2010, the number of attacks against christian communities increased alarmingly. unfortunately, there are many innocent lives to be lost as a result of the bloody attacks on the christian community in nigeria and pakistan, the terrorist attacks on coptic christians in alexandria and the philippines, acts of terrorist jihad against assyrian christian families and the coordinated bombings of christian homes in baghdad. we also deplore and condemn the persecution of christians in the islamic republic by the iranian government and the repression of the activities of the catholic church and other religious communities in vietnam. the european union must strengthen its longstanding commitment to the pursuit of freedom of religion, freedom of conscience and freedom of thought, which are fundamental principles of the european acquis. governments have a duty to guarantee these freedoms. i therefore call on the council, the commission and the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy to act swiftly, firmly and forcefully to ensure the protection of religious freedom in the world.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. but development, being essential and long-term, is no longer enough on its own. the eu needs, as high representative ashton said today, a coherent strategy with the use of all instruments, including those aimed at reforming the security sectors of the countries in the region and at democratic and institutional capacity building. because that is not how the european union has acted. we look closely at guinea-bissau, which has now become a narco-state and from which the european union has recently withdrawn a mission under the esdp. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european union is able to take part in the negotiations on the future of the european union. another example of what the european union is not doing as it should in the sahel is the way it has washed its hands of the search for a solution to the conflict in western sahara. if we continue to look at the - even now - over the top fuse of what is happening in tunisia and the consequences for the whole region, we will only worsen the security conditions in the sahel, providing yet another cornered and desperate generation for the criminal and terrorist organizations like al-qaeda in the maghreb, which are already at large in the region. we cannot continue to be without that coherent strategy in action that mrs ashton spoke of.
the rapporteur. - mr president, i am not going to go into the details of the situation in libya, but i would like to say that i am very pleased that the commission has taken the initiative to make a statement on the situation in libya. some member states have strong relations with libya and are keen to ensure that they are properly anchored in the union's core values and interests. we therefore support the development of relations with libya through the establishment of a framework agreement covering various areas of cooperation with a view to stimulating substantive political dialogue. but we must not forget that libya is ruled by a dictatorial regime with a history of serious human rights violations and terrorist attacks and meddling in other countries, although it has shown signs in recent years of wanting to make headway. the framework agreement with libya can therefore only be approved by this parliament if certain conditions are met. it is a sine qua non condition that libya allows the united nations high commissioner for refugees to resume operations in the country with an extended mandate. i dare say it clearly: without unhcr there is no deal. the european union is also calling for the immediate release of all political prisoners, including those who have been held in custody for more than two years. any readmission agreement between the european union and libya should exclude all those who declare themselves to be asylum seekers, refugees or persons in need of international protection and should be implemented in full compliance with the principle of non-refoulement. the very serious situation of the 400 eritreans who were on the verge of being expelled en masse from libya last summer must not happen again. the european union must encourage libya to adopt legal and social solutions that will improve the inhumane living conditions of the approximately 2 million migrant workers in libya, about a quarter of the population. these immigrants deserve legal protection and cannot be treated any longer as abid, slaves. the european union must invest in joint programmes to combat the growing trafficking in human beings, which has devastating consequences, especially for women and children. the european union's support for iom and all organisations working to support migrants in transit in libya must be stepped up to improve the conditions of migrants held in detention centres which are beginning to fill up again, despite having been suddenly emptied in the middle of last year. the union cannot afford to fail to persuade libya to commit itself to a moratorium on the death penalty and it is essential that it requires the libyan authorities to make public the identities of executed nationals and foreigners. the union should insist that libya ratify the rome statute of the international criminal court. in the framework of cooperation, the union should encourage reforms that modernise social, political and judicial structures, that open up the country to the outside world, that expose society to free information, that promote the independence of the media and that invest in the institutional capacity building of business, labour and other representative civil society organisations. the bouazizi revolution in tunisia cannot but have repercussions in neighbouring libya and this even the gaddafi regime can understand. we need to strengthen the support we provide to the libyan health sector through the benghazi action plan, extending it to other medical facilities and other public health needs. we are aware that the negotiations between the european commission and libya are at an advanced stage, although they are facing difficulties in the area of trade and energy cooperation. we would be well advised to establish a european union delegation in tripoli as soon as possible to facilitate the negotiations and to monitor developments in libya. in these recommendations, commissioner, we asked the commission for detailed information on the financial lines used and planned for cooperation with libya. i hope you can provide us with that data soon. finally, i would point out that parliament has only recently had the opportunity to accede to the council's mandate for negotiations. this is unacceptable and cannot continue. finally, i would like to thank all the shadow rapporteurs for their collaboration, which was essential to the broad consensus that was reached on this potentially divisive issue.
rapporteur. − mr president, i would like to thank all my colleagues who have participated in this debate. i think this debate highlights the dilemmas we face. from my own visit to libya, as part of the delegation led by our colleague mr panzeri in november 2010, i came to the conclusion that we have to pursue the line of engagement. we recognise that we have to deal with a difficult interlocutor, but it would be unconscionable not to pursue that line because there are humanitarian obligations towards the people who are suffering so much in libya, in particular the migrants who are going through libya and enduring the situation there. i believe that many of the difficulties are due to the fact that this regime is isolated. despite the difficulties, and despite having no illusions that we will achieve an agreement soon or that all the conditions that we put forward will be met, we need to pursue that line. in my opinion this is clear. indeed in that sense having the eu delegation established in tripoli is extremely important because i think that – as many have said here – what is happening in tunisia now is bound to have repercussions in libya, despite the differences. in libya we are not dealing with a similar situation in many respects because of the total dependency on the people of income from oil. nevertheless i think that the message is that, despite our different perceptions at this stage, we are committed to following closely the negotiations by the commission. i am grateful for the briefings we have had and which have been useful. we will follow them very closely and will be able to make recommendations at any time. i think that through the very wide consensus achieved with the collaboration of my shadow rapporteurs and everybody, we are conveying a very clear message to the council and to the commission, which has the task of negotiation, but also to our libyan interlocutors, on what points we believe are absolutely essential to be met if we are to achieve the improvements that we want to see in the bilateral relations, and also on the crucial question of respect for human rights in libya. that message is very clear.
for the gue/ngl group mr president, i believe that in these discussions there is always an implicit assumption that humanitarian action is expensive, and we do not do humanitarian action because it is expensive, but there is also a correspondence in this implicit assumption: if it wasn't expensive, we'd do the humanitarian. it turns out that there are cases where a humanitarian policy is a cheaper policy. and a recent study by the house of commons of the british parliament proves exactly that. that a rapid response system for asylum seekers is much cheaper and that, even more costly, is delay and forced removal of families. we are only talking about administrative costs, not including the costs for asylum seekers themselves, both those who are entitled to asylum and those who are then ultimately denied their claims for the right or wrong reasons. and so what's the problem: if we can have humanitarian action, fulfill our moral duties and do it cheaper, why don't we do it? the eu has no concerted action, no common action, and i would like to take the liberty of disagreeing with my colleague mr busuttil here, not because the implementation of the current legislation is costing the member states, but because it is partial, incomplete. we have a policy which is at the moment only repressive and which ends up being unfair to asylum seekers, to administrations and, as we are now discovering, ultimately to the european taxpayers. i ask the council to give us updated information and to answer these questions so that we can finally move towards a consistent and concerted policy.
mr president, i would first of all like to congratulate the authors of this question, and in particular my colleague monika hohlmeier, and i am very much in line with what mr díaz de mera has just said. we know that this is only one of the five instruments which have to do with the foundations of the european asylum system. this is about the minimum standards for asylum procedures. but the report the commission presented to us last year recognises that member states have adopted divergent practices and that there is considerable variation between the procedural safeguards enshrined in each member state. there are significant disparities between member states, ranging from provisions on fast-track procedures to provisions on personal interviews, assistance and access to an effective remedy. let 's be clear: some member states have incorrectly or incompletely transposed this directive and others simply apply it loosely. either we give up on having a european asylum system, or we have to eliminate these procedural differences. we have to make improvements. the improvements that appear necessary, in particular the improvement of the quality of the examination of applications, the so-called front loading. the evaluation we are asking the commission to make is therefore the one that is needed. we need to identify where we can improve and put an end to these differences. we know that the commission needs the cooperation of the member states, in particular by providing the necessary training, including but not limited to cost. let's get this straight. the european institutions and the member states must cooperate to this end. our aim must remain the same: that in 2012 the common asylum system can be a reality.
in writing. − given libya's geographical situation and the economic interdependence between the eu and libya, it is in the common interest to pursue an eu-libya strategic partnership. however, we cannot forget the dictatorial regime that reigns in this country, with no respect for human rights and basic freedoms. despite the clear interest of many member states in pursuing a framework agreement with libya, the eu cannot forget the core values it defends and subordinate itself to economic interests alone. a partnership is needed to implement legal reforms in the field of human rights in this country and at the same time to enable the diversification of the national economy, recalling some progress already made, such as the abandonment of its nuclear programme or even international obligations that the state has in relation to human rights, despite the sanctions applied by the un.
in writing. - i welcome the commitments made through the framework agreement currently under negotiation, which covers a wide range of issues, from strengthening political dialogue to managing migration, developing trade and economic relations, energy security and improving cooperation in various sectors. i believe that the framework agreement could be an opportunity to strengthen the political dialogue between libya and the eu. i emphasise the role of the framework agreement, which provides for actions to assist in the development of institutional capacity, as a means of strengthening civil society, supporting modernisation, encouraging the introduction of democratic reforms and the establishment of an independent media and judiciary, and supporting other efforts to open up space for libyan businesses, academic institutions, ngos and other actors.
in writing. - the economic partnership between europe and libya is already a de facto reality. libya has the largest proven oil reserves in africa and is the third largest supplier of energy (oil and gas) to europe. in addition, the eu is libya's largest trading partner (70% of its total trade in 2009). europe continues to recognise that libya has an important role to play in the field of regional and global security, in the context of the containment of islamic extremism and also in the context of regional stabilisation. it is therefore welcome that a framework partnership agreement is being negotiated, which, as the report makes clear, should not leave out certain issues which i consider to be fundamental: the progressive democratization of the regime; greater respect for human rights, particularly freedom, in all its aspects; a progressive change in the penal system towards the abolition of the death penalty; acceptance of the jurisdiction of the international criminal court and accession to the 1951 geneva convention.
in writing. − the opening of negotiations by the european union with libya is an opportunity to secure better conditions for the economic development of both parties and, at the same time, to promote serious developments in the mediterranean region and in africa in terms of respect for human rights and its contribution to global peace and stability and to the fight against climate change. libya has a population of 6 million, of which 2 million are foreigners. it has the largest proven oil reserves in africa and is the third largest supplier of energy (in oil and gas) in europe. the eu is its largest trading partner: transactions between the two parties accounted for almost 70% of libya's total trade in 2009. the framework partnership agreement with the eu should be seen as an opportunity to highlight the advantages of humanist values and democracy for sustainable and diversified development. as the report warns, this process cannot be dissociated from the eu's core values, such as the fight against the death penalty and discrimination against minorities, immigrants and refugees, the promotion of public health and the need for political democratisation.
in writing. - we are all aware that libya remains a dictatorial regime and systematically violates international conventions on fundamental rights and freedoms. despite these facts, libya has been expanding its trade and political relations with several eu member states. this role of libya as a partner in the mediterranean region and in africa in many areas has proven to have a major impact on the security and stability of the region, including migration, public health, development, trade and economic relations, climate change, energy and cultural heritage. in this context, the framework agreement now being negotiated is important, but we must not leave unanswered a number of fundamental questions, including: a progressive democratisation of the regime, respect for human rights, changes in the penal system, with the abolition of the death penalty as a first priority, and accession to the geneva convention.
in writing. - i congratulate the european union for having repeatedly expressed its commitment to religious freedom, freedom of conscience and freedom of thought. governments have a duty to guarantee these freedoms worldwide, considering that the development of human rights, democracy and civil liberties is the common basis on which the european union builds its relations with third countries and is provided for in the democracy clause in agreements concluded between the eu and third countries.
in writing. - i was one of the first to sign this motion for a resolution, which i believe describes quite accurately and appropriately the situation faced by christian minorities in some countries of the middle east. one of the noblest tasks of the european parliament, as far as its external action is concerned, is to defend and promote the values in which we believe, and in this case we are referring specifically to freedom of thought, conscience, expression and religion, freedoms which have clearly been put at risk by cowardly attacks by religious fanatics who have murdered innocent people, sometimes en masse, in a way which i consider inhuman and incomprehensible. i hope that this resolution, which has been endorsed by all the groups in this parliament, will help to raise awareness among the public and among the government and public administration officials of the countries concerned of the importance of the full exercise of fundamental freedoms in their countries and of the need to hold murderers and agitators accountable, and to promote interreligious and intercultural dialogue within and between our societies, which, although living on different continents, share many common values and visions.
in writing. - attacks on christians are increasing all over the world. this disturbing and deplorable fact cannot but be deeply regretted, all the more so since christianity preaches peace and harmony among men, regardless of whether they are jews or greeks, as st. paul would say. what is at stake is the religious freedom and peace of communities that have existed for many centuries and have coexisted peacefully with other religions in the territories where they are found and that are the target of indiscriminate violence just because they believe in christ. but the question is broader. in addition to the attacks, the christian faith and its manifestations have also been attacked in europe itself, often under the cover of misrepresentations of concepts such as secularism and the neutrality of states and institutions. in this connection, i cannot but deplore the recent attacks on the celebration of catholic masses in barcelona and call on the spanish state and the european institutions to condemn and combat the atmosphere of christophobia which seems to be on the increase. a man who denies his own roots deserves little respect from others.
in writing. - everyone has the right to freedom of religion, conscience and thought. this right confers the freedom to manifest one's religion or belief, individually or in association with others, both in public and in private, through worship, observance of rites, practice and teaching. religious freedom statistics show that most acts of religious violence are committed against christians. indeed, it is noted that innocent lives have recently been taken in bloody attacks on the christian community in nigeria, alexandria, the philippines, iraq and syria. in addition, the iranian government has intensified its campaign against christians in the islamic republic. in vietnam, the activities of the catholic church and other religious communities are also severely repressed. in addition to condemning these attacks and urging governments to guarantee freedom of religion, conscience and thought, the council, the commission and the high representative of the union for foreign affairs are called upon to devote greater attention to the issue of freedom of religion and to take concrete action as a matter of urgency, including action against states which deliberately fail to protect religious denominations.

in writing. - i am very concerned, but i must also say with great hope, that i look at the political and social situation in belarus. that is why i wholeheartedly support this joint resolution, which has been endorsed by five parliamentary groups (minus the gue/ngl confederal group of the european united left/nordic green left). but rather than deplore what is happening, which is well described in the resolution, i would like to stress the concrete measures which this resolution points to and which i believe both the council and the commission should put into effect immediately: the application of economic sanctions; the freezing of all financial aid granted through the imf as well as through the eib and the ebrd; support by all possible means of the efforts of belarusian civil society towards a freer and more democratic society; the reinstatement of the visa ban on belarusian senior leaders, extending it to senior officials; the suspension of belarus' participation in the eastern partnership activities at the eastern partnership summit to be held in budapest; and finally, the intensification of work on the negotiation of visa facilitation agreements and direct contacts with the population, with a view to strengthening contacts between the populations.
