in writing. - the situation in belarus should concern all those who believe in democracy and the rule of law. the citizens of this country live under a regime which does not respect human rights and which maintains a very castrating political police. the eu must support all efforts to democratize this regime, which means improving the lives of its people. the repressive measures still in force in belarus must be brought to an end.
in writing. - i welcome this report, since the commission has responded to the crisis and, at the same time, applied the competition policy measures. i support a role for the ep as co-legislator on competition policy and, as long as this is not possible, for the commission to inform parliament in detail about the follow-up to its recommendations and to justify deviations from them. i am disappointed that it has not yet been possible to improve the competitive environment within the single market in a way that is more favourable to smes.
in writing. − eu competition policy is not only a fundamental and truly structural policy of the european legal framework, but also the foundation of a successful internal market and a sustainable and competitive economy. that is why i think it is important that the commission informs parliament of its development and implementation. the year 2009, as we all know, was an extraordinary year in many ways. it was indeed the year after the collapse of lehman brothers (september 2008), which led to the introduction of several exceptional competition measures, notably as regards state aid, the four communications on the financial sector and the temporary framework for the other sectors. i therefore consider it essential that a thorough analysis be made of the impact of these measures on the economy and finances of the various states and that their effectiveness be properly studied so that the appropriate consequences can be drawn.
in writing. − this resolution deals with competition policy 2009 and provides a comprehensive overview of all state aid to the transport sector within the eu, which is essential for the existence of a market without frontiers and with free movement of people, goods and services. the economic crisis of recent years has led to the bankruptcy of many companies and regulatory measures are needed to prevent distortions in this sector, in particular by regulating support for the sector. on the other hand, the eu's peripheral countries have increased costs in this area and financial means are needed to minimise this situation. i therefore welcome the adoption of this resolution, welcoming the creation of a set of market monitoring measures, the environmental concern with co2 emissions and the encouragement of research to improve competitiveness in europe, in particular by recommending that the commission and the member states ensure 3% investment in this area.
in writing. - it is unacceptable that, at a time of deepening financial and economic crisis, a 2009 report on competition policy, which advocates competition and insists on further liberalisation, particularly in the railway sector, should be adopted by the european parliament, when it states that the internal rail market must be completed by opening up national passenger transport markets. the same applies to the pharmaceutical sector, where it calls on the commission to speed up the completion of the internal market in medicines, telecommunications, etc. what we have is a report which calls for further liberalization in basic sectors which are essential for the improvement of the people's living conditions, without regard to the consequences for employment, prices and people's lives. it is only interested in the profits of economic and financial groups, even if in one case or another reference is made to the smes that the neoliberal policy of the european union is putting in question. it is always forgotten that so-called free competition only gives the big companies the freedom to crush the small ones, and then the workers, consumers and small businessmen suffer the consequences. for all these reasons, we voted against the report.
in writing. − analysis of the 2009 competition policy report reveals that the economic crisis, which started in 2008, may have had some effect on competition policy itself, in particular because member states have provided support to their economies in various forms. it is time to analyse the consequences of such aid in the internal market and to interpret whether it has distorted free competition. we cannot forget that the eu's competition policy is based on the principles of open markets and a level playing field in all sectors, which is the foundation of a successful internal market and a precondition for the creation of sustainable and knowledge-based jobs.
in writing. − analysis of the european commission's competition policy report for 2009 allows us to draw conclusions on the benefits of this european policy. european competition policy is one of the key policies of european integration. the underlying idea is to achieve an internal market in which economic operators can freely take up and pursue their activities. i believe that, as the document aims, we need clear competition rules if the creation of smes is to be a possible reality. the european union is currently experiencing one of the most serious periods of economic and financial crisis in its history and the activity of smes is central to the recovery of the economy. i welcome the development of greater synergies between competition policy and consumer protection policy. i regret, however, that there are still distortions of competition in the energy market and i support the invitation to the european commission in the document put to the vote today to monitor closely the implementation of the third energy liberalisation package by the member states.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that three eu member states are members of the arctic council, while iceland is in accession negotiations. the eu has an important role to play in this region, with shared competences in several areas and exclusive competences, such as fisheries. in addition, the eu is at the forefront of certain policies, such as environmental research and climate change. in addition to this, it is necessary to take into account that some arctic partners are already major contributors to the supply of energy, raw materials and fish to europe. its variety of resources and its potential for alternative energies can only be developed through an ecosystem approach and integrated management plans. in addition, the development of new trade routes could benefit the european economy, given europe's privileged position in providing services such as gps coverage through the galileo system.

in writing. − in the current priority framework for combating climate change, the defence and promotion of the arctic is of crucial importance, not only in environmental terms, but also in terms of economic development and global stability and security. the potential of the region to supply renewable energy and raw fish is highlighted, and the sustainable exploitation of the natural resources of this region is therefore key. the interests of the indigenous peoples of this region must not be underestimated in the process. in this respect, the european union can and must play a leading role in defending the culture, language, customs and living conditions of these indigenous communities. without this, any intervention strategy for safeguarding a capital region of importance for the future of the world's population and the planet will be at risk. i would stress the importance of ensuring the best conditions for scientific research.
in writing. - the relationship between the eu and the arctic is unquestionable, not least because denmark, finland and sweden are arctic countries and both finland and sweden are partly located in the arctic circle. given the contribution of the eu and its member states to research and funding, its impact through eu legislation on the environment, climate, fisheries and similar issues, as well as the possibilities for future cooperation on issues such as the development of mapping and maritime security, economic development and similar issues, it can be concluded that the eu has a major contribution to make to the sustainable development of the arctic. this region will be crucial to a world that is adapting to face climate change, population growth and resource scarcity.

in writing. − the conflict involving russia and georgia demonstrates the potential for instability in the black sea region and fully justifies the european union adopting a strategy to address the specific challenges facing this part of the world. despite the tension that has not yet ceased, this is also a region that can have a more stable and balanced future, and the union can play an important role in this stabilisation. in this connection, it is necessary not only to set objectives but above all to provide those implementing the european strategy with the human, technical and financial resources to enable them to achieve them in the best possible way. given their own geographical situation, their history and their practical knowledge of the region, romania, bulgaria and greece can make valuable contributions to the strategy to be designed to be appropriate to the objectives of promoting peace, security, democracy, good governance and economic, social and human development.
in writing. - the importance of the black sea for the european union is recognised, as are the problems of instability surrounding this region. in a context encompassing eu member states bulgaria, greece and romania , together with turkey and several states of the former soviet bloc, including russia, the black sea is seen as a key to energy supply and diversification of gas distribution. it is a strategic bridge linking europe to the caspian sea area, central asia and the middle east, as well as southeast asia and china. among many of the differences and rivalries, close historical and cultural ties stand out, as does the importance of intercultural and interfaith dialogue. in this context, the eu needs to be more committed and more effective in implementing measures to help stabilise and revitalise the region, in a process which should involve all the countries concerned.
in writing. - nothing new emerges from this report. the recipes and objectives are the same as those which have long been the focus of the eu's so-called external policy: controlling the region's natural resources, notably oil and natural gas, on which the eu depends, ensuring its uninterrupted supply, and seeking to guarantee access to its markets and the exploitation of workers. the mechanisms for achieving this are also the same: interference and repeated attempts to limit the national sovereignty of these countries through international campaigns run by the major news agencies and ngos funded by eu funds; the push for militarism and the arms race, as in the case of the ongoing rearmament of georgia. and looking for those countries who, in exchange for their own interests or those of the interests they serve, would defend those of the eu, the us and their economic groups, accepting nato's eastward enlargement and allowing the installation of us military bases in the region, which have been used as a supply platform for nato troops in afghanistan. of course, this path is not without its bumps: the european parliament has been a very active participant in the debate on the future of the european union, and it is not surprising that the european parliament has been a very active participant in the debate on the future of the european union.
in writing. − the black sea region is strategically crucial for the european union because of its geographical location, which encompasses three eu member states, greece, romania and bulgaria, and several important partners, including russia and turkey. on the other hand, concerns about security and energy supply lead to the need for greater involvement between the european union and the states of the region. i therefore agree that the main concerns expressed in the report are to ensure peace, democracy and stability in the black sea region and to ensure the energy security of the european union. the increase in relations between the european union and the black sea region will undoubtedly be important, and the parties can take greater advantage of this and more effective cooperation.
in writing. − the black sea region is of great strategic importance to the european union. this is due to its geographical location, encompassing three eu member states, greece, romania and bulgaria, one candidate country, turkey, and six partners, including russia. in addition, the challenges of energy security and supply require the european union to be more involved and focused in relations with the member states of this region. i therefore subscribe to the concerns expressed in the document voted on today, which must be of two kinds: ensuring peace, democracy and stability in the black sea region and ensuring the energy security of the european union. i believe that from a regional point of view it is necessary to create synergies and develop greater cooperation in order to achieve a more effective partnership in the field of transport and energy, with a view to a greater diversification of supply routes and sources. the deepening of the dialogue between the european union and the black sea region will undoubtedly be beneficial, and the different parties can benefit from more effective cooperation.

the president of the council. - ladies and gentlemen of the house, commissioner. it is a great pleasure to address you before the next european council, despite the fact that the role of the rotating presidency is defined by the lisbon treaty as the primary responsibility for preparing the european council rests with the permanent president. at the same time, it worked very closely with the permanent president in preparing the european council meeting, for example in the context of the general affairs council held on monday under the hungarian presidency. we also naturally monitor the implementation of the european council conclusions, both in the general affairs council and in the other council formations. first, let me outline the main issues on the agenda for the february meeting, which will focus primarily on energy and innovation. in the context of defining the europe 2020 strategy, the european council decided in march 2010 to hold a thematic debate on energy and innovation. i think it goes without saying that these two sectors are crucial for european growth and jobs. the european council's task is not only to respond to immediate crises but also to formulate strategic guidelines for the future. let's start with the energy issue. energy security is a priority for all of us. this requires greater integration and interconnection of the energy market. we need to increase our r&d spending, make our economy more competitive and sustainable, and strengthen our cooperation with the main transit, energy producing and energy consuming countries. the first element is therefore an integrated and interconnected energy market. we need to have a complete internal energy market. to this end, the european council will have to decide on a number of important steps. firstly, the legislation on the internal energy market needs to be implemented. we have to do more on the regulatory level. for example, we need to simplify the procedures for authorising the construction of new infrastructure. in addition, we need to make a serious effort to modernise and expand europe's energy infrastructure and to link markets through cross-border cooperation. no country, no region of the union can remain isolated. all this must be financed primarily by the private sector. in addition, appropriate cost-sharing principles should be established for cross-border investments. thirdly, there will be projects which, although of great importance for energy security, are not attractive enough for private capital to finance in full. in such cases, it may be appropriate to provide limited public funding for projects from member states or union sources. the current negotiations are not, however, intended to prejudge the debate on the multiannual financial framework, which is due to start at the end of june. the second big energy issue is energy efficiency and renewable energy. these - needless to say - increase competitiveness and promote security of energy supply and sustainability at lower costs. the council will examine in 2011 the proposal that the commission will present for a new energy efficiency plan. the proposal will take account of the progress made towards the eu's energy efficiency target for 2013 and will include further measures. external relations are also of paramount importance in energy policy. there is a need to coordinate more systematically union and member state activities in relation to key producer, transit and consumer countries. for example, it would be appropriate for member states to share information on contracts concluded not only for natural gas, as they currently do, but also for other types of energy. concrete work should be initiated to develop partnerships with key actors on regulatory approaches on all issues of common interest. this applies, of course, to russia, but also to all the union's partners and neighbours. let's move on to the topic of innovation. innovation is what can help address the most critical societal challenges of our time, such as health, food security, energy security, sustainable development, climate change and an ageing population, and also offer opportunities for new markets. innovation can also help to resolve the dilemma between fiscal austerity and growth-friendly policies. how can we finance growth before it becomes self-sustaining? we can't do it on credit, because we don't want to. we want to stop the debt. so innovation is about unlocking the resources of creativity to provide the right answers. so, within the innovation theme, we need to focus on addressing major societal challenges, moving towards the european research area. we need to create free mobility for researchers, improve the framework conditions for innovative enterprises and the european council should also address the prioritisation of state aid. energy and innovation: investing for the future. the european council must also deal with current economic and financial issues, since we all know that the crisis is not yet completely behind us. the situation is fragile. we must do everything we can to protect the single currency, the euro, and we must calm the markets. the european financial stability facility should therefore be strengthened, and stress tests on banks should be mentioned. the hungarian presidency is particularly committed to the six-pack of economic governance legislation. we would like to inform the heads of state and government of our position in the consultations in both the council and the parliament. finally, the heads of state or government will also be discussing the need for further joint measures to ensure competitiveness, and of course, in the current acute situation, they will also be talking about tunisia and egypt. ladies and gentlemen of the house of representatives, i hope that we will have a european council on very difficult subjects, where you can formulate specific questions which will also define the work of the council for the coming months, and president herman van rompuy will report to you after the meeting.
president of the commission. − mr president, this european council takes place at a very important moment for our neighbourhood, namely egypt, tunisia and belarus. while respecting the different specific situations in these countries, i expect this european council to state in very clear terms that the principles of the rule of law and respect for fundamental rights and pluralist democracy must be enacted and respected. democracy is indeed the best way to achieve stability and prosperity in those countries, just like anywhere else. this friday, the european council will discuss two areas which are also very important for the future of europe and its economy: energy and innovation. both of them are core elements of the europe 2020 strategy and central to our aim of restoring sustainable growth and increasing the european union’s competitiveness. and let us not forget that energy and innovation are also two fields where the community approach and european dimension can offer a lot of value added. this is an important point to make in the current context. through the europe 2020 strategy we have already agreed on a set of ambitious goals and targets on energy innovation. i could mention the innovation union flagship initiative, adopted last october, or the resource efficient europe flagship initiative, adopted just last week and in which energy features prominently. so this week’s european council should identify clear, concrete deliverables. the discussion and outcome should be as operational and productive as possible. i have described energy policy as the next great european integration project and it is not hard to see why a safe, secure, sustainable, affordable energy supply is key to our economic and strategic interests as a global player. we have already done a lot in the past with our climate and energy package and with internal market legislation. we must build on that by exploiting the opportunities provided by the lisbon treaty, deepening our existing cooperation and launching initiatives in new areas like energy security. therefore the first credibility test of our energy policy is delivering what we have already agreed upon. the commission has outlined the measures we think are urgently needed in our energy 2020 and energy infrastructure communications. i want the european council to endorse these priorities and, in particular, make a clear commitment to completing our internal energy market by 2014. a common technical standard should also be fixed for electric vehicle charging systems this year, as well as for smart grids and meters by the end of 2012. a truly integrated internal market on energy is key to delivering more growth and jobs, promoting technological progress, modernising our infrastructure and reducing our exposure to import and price volatility. we must also ensure that, when it comes to energy, no member state is isolated from the rest of europe. i want member states to agree on a 2015 deadline to put an end to energy islands in europe. we have done good work in connecting the baltic countries to the continental system. now i will turn to central and eastern europe to move forward the north-south energy interconnections. i want a plan to be agreed in the autumn on the projects needed to link the baltic to the adriatic. while we are on track to achieve our renewables targets, on present performance we will only meet half of our energy efficiency targets. more efficient energy use is the key to unlocking massive environmental and economic benefits – and reducing europe’s annual energy bill by around eur 200 billion. it could also create two million jobs by 2020. so i will ask the european council to give new impetus to our pursuit of energy efficiency. we could use the scale of public procurement across the eu to give a real boost to energy efficiency and this means local jobs, jobs that cannot be outsourced, jobs for smes and real savings for both industry and households. the commission will adopt in the coming weeks an energy efficiency plan proposing specific measures to boost energy efficiency; for instance, that by 1 january 2012 all member states should include energy efficiency standards in public procurement. the commission will then review the progress achieved with these measures by 2013 and will consider further measures, including proposing legally binding targets if necessary. member states should agree a deadline for including energy efficiency standards in all public procurement for public buildings and services. for its part, the commission stands ready to explore new measures in the fields of energy saving for cities, sustainable biofuels, smart grids and energy storage. we also need to focus on the external dimension of european energy policy. just a fortnight ago i had encouraging discussions with the presidents of azerbaijan and turkmenistan on europe’s access to the caspian gas fields, which would enable the realisation of the southern corridor. an important breakthrough was achieved with the signature of a joint declaration with azerbaijan and a concrete commitment from turkmenistan to supply gas to europe. the message i took from that visit is this: when we take key decisions on energy jointly in europe, we are a strong player in the global race for energy resources. underlining the importance of the external dimension of the european union energy policy should be a key message from the european council, so i am looking forward to a very important discussion on energy at this european council and – i am happy to say this – here in the european parliament. i know this parliament is very supportive of a strong european policy on energy and the president of parliament has been a champion of a stronger commitment by europe in terms of energy policy. moving now to innovation, i think there is already broad agreement about what should come out of the european council. perhaps less evident is a sense of how urgent, how desperately urgent, action is; why boosting research and innovation is needed now, when member states are all making difficult choices about where to cut their budgets. fiscal consideration and public support for innovation are not irreconcilable policies. several member states have shown that you can cut your overall budget while maintaining growth-friendly expenditure, in particular on research and innovation. this is important because delivering the innovation economy is the key deep structural change. our competitors know this, they are already betting on innovation. to avoid being left behind, we need the european council’s endorsement of our strategic and integrated approach to innovation. innovation needs to be part of our economic policy, not simply a research instrument, as some people think. at european level we can add real value by improving the framework conditions for research and innovation in the european union. europe must become the natural home of innovation, through effective standardisation, better use of intellectual property rights, innovation-friendly public procurement and measures to help small innovative companies to secure financing. much of this does not cost money, but it does need political will. and the political will to take measures using a european approach and a european dimension. we can also squeeze much more out of the european research area, making full use of the single market by improving the mobility of researchers, for example. and as well as maintaining spending, we need to spend better. with the budget review we have launched a debate on how to simplify the way european union money is spent, and to work towards a common strategic framework for research and innovation funding. in other words, getting better value for money also means cutting red tape, so that eu-funded scientists can spend more time in the lab or on their work, and not on red tape and bureaucracy. we will never attract the most brilliant scientists and most innovative companies with an incoherent set of funding instruments based on complex and bureaucratic rules. so this month’s european council will discuss energy and innovation. but it will not avoid discussing the economy. the economy, the problems of the unemployed, these remain the most important concerns for our citizens. we have just launched the first european semester – putting economic governance into action. the annual growth survey was well received. the messages were focused and clear. it provides the necessary guidance at european union level so that member states can take our interdependence into account when making their national policy decisions. good progress has already been made on the legislative proposals that will underpin our new system of economic governance. i would like to thank the hungarian presidency. the hungarian presidency has my full support in accelerating work to ensure adoption by june. in addition, as part of this comprehensive response, we will need to resolve the outstanding issues surrounding the european financial stability facility (efsf) and the european stability mechanism. regarding the efsf, other than widening its scope, what is at stake now is how to increase its effective lending capacity – as stated by the commission in the annual growth survey. of course, this issue should be put in the context of the comprehensive response. the discussions in the european council of friday next will most likely cover the need for reinforced coordination of economic policies in the european union and the euro area. i welcome such a discussion, which fits very well with the commission’s annual growth survey. in fact, the european semester is not just about coordinating budgetary policies, but addressing wider issues like macroeconomic imbalances and competitiveness gaps. in addition, we have recently heard some authoritative voices arguing in favour of deepening economic governance, but at the same time stating that it can only be done through the intergovernmental method. we have to be clear about this: the commission welcomes the deepening and acceleration of economic governance and policy coordination, including within the euro area. but we are firmly convinced that the treaty provides the right framework and instruments to achieve this. in fact, we would not further our cause if parallel structures were to work in an ultimately incoherent manner. establishing a system of reinforced economic governance for the eu, and in particular the euro area outside the union framework, raises important, and politically very sensitive, questions. in fact, member states should adopt measures which are fully compatible with the community method and the framework provided by the treaty. insofar as measures fall under national competence – and of course some of them are under national responsibility –this competence should be exercised in coherence with the overall union framework. i really believe this matter is extremely important because we can, in fact, make great progress in matters of economic governance. we need – and we have been arguing in favour of this – more policy coordination and better economic governance, but we have to do it in a way that is coherent and compatible with the treaties and with a community approach. the commission will be particularly attentive to these issues. the treaty, with the ensuing ‘community method’, implies full respect for the role of all the european institutions.
as we know, energy is a vital sector for creating new jobs and opportunity should therefore be the keyword of this council which we are now preparing. but unfortunately, it is not. when we need concrete investment to address the energy efficiency of our cities, and particularly in countries that are being subjected to the greatest speculative attacks and, above all, in countries that have the highest levels of unemployment, what we get from governments are answers that are the old recipes and it is on them that we continue to insist. what we need in this council is an energy revolution. we don't just need more public-private partnerships, that's insisting on failure. we are still very much stuck with the old energy, fossil fuels, nuclear energy and very unambitious about the new energy, which is the only one that can guarantee equal access and which is the only one that can guarantee that a large project is as important as a local project. only by putting everything together could we have an integrated policy, and that is why a council which should be a breakthrough is a council of continuity. and i ask you, mr president, for permission to make just one final appeal: because emergency situations require emergency appeals, and the appeal i ask you to make is to ask european leaders, in relation to what is happening in egypt, to show at least as much solidarity with the people on the street as they have shown with the authoritarian regimes, while these have governed on the basis of the economy and not on the basis of respect for democracy.
we know that the deepening of the single market means more liberalization and then greater concentration of monopolies in favour of the largest economic groups in the most developed countries of the european union. we want to make clear here our opposition to this path in areas which are strategic for economic and social development, particularly in the peripheral countries, such as energy issues. but the most serious thing is that all that has been said here by the council and the commission, particularly on the strengthening of economic governance, ignores the reality of social problems, the worsening of inequalities, unemployment, social exclusion and energy poverty, which is growing exponentially in some countries with the increase in electricity and fuel prices. economic and energy policies should have a central objective: social progress, the improvement of the living conditions of our peoples, but the opposite is happening. so here is the indignation we see growing in the streets in many of our countries and now also in tunisia, in egypt, to whose people we send our solidarity and also want their rights to be respected, in particular by the council, which should take a clear position on all this.
i have no doubt that this council will be very important, particularly in relation to the relaunch of european economies, particularly in the areas of energy and innovation. and so i would like to stress that this council is, at bottom, part of the implementation of this 2020 strategy for europe and is therefore part of that half, or that side of the coin which is the side of growth, competitiveness, the revival of economies. but because it is so important, i wanted to leave it here, and that is the meaning of my speech, an appeal. i would like to ask the council to discuss, among other important issues, energy and innovation, and to prepare a solution to the financial crisis in the european union. i don't think we have time to waste. and if we cannot expect the council to come to a decision on this problem next friday, if we cannot expect the council to come to a decision on this problem next friday, although we expect it in march, it is essential that the heads of government and the heads of state of the european union prepare, as from 4 february, for the flexibilization of the stabilisation fund and also, at the same time, for the relaunching of the european economic govern ment. i think this is an essential matter and cannot be left out of this council. and now, if i may, i would like to make another note to this council: that this council should also prepare a european union strategy for the mediterranean. that it should prepare a response to the situation in tunisia and egypt today. it is therefore, despite the importance of energy and innovation, that the financial and political crisis in the north african countries should be dealt with by this council.
mr president, energy and innovation are two very important subjects, which are at the heart of the europe 2020 strategy and which can contribute to sustainable and smart growth and to the creation of more and better jobs. in fact, energy and innovation are areas in which my country, portugal, has made major investments with good results. in recent years portugal has doubled its investment in r&d and has reached the top 5 for renewable energy, so that 31% of electricity consumed is already from renewable sources and is expected to be 60% by 2020. but this council cannot ignore, as has already been said here, what is happening in egypt, a popular revolution. and you cannot ignore the financial and economic crisis. the euro area member states with the most difficulty are doing the right thing by adopting the austerity measures needed to contain the deficit and calm the markets, measures that require great sacrifices from households and businesses. and is the european union doing the right thing? i don't think he is! in the face of speculators' attacks on the euro - because it is through sovereign debts that speculators attack the single currency - the european response has been casuistic, delayed and ineffective. the diagnosis is made and the recipe is known. the european union must improve economic coordination and strengthen and make the financial stability facility more flexible so that it can buy up the public debt of the countries most under pressure from the markets. so we are facing global problems that require a global response. this is also what the citizens expect from the next european council.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have said this before in this house and i will say it again today. the outermost regions, and in particular madeira, the region from which i come, have no objection whatsoever to the conclusion of the geneva agreement or to the conclusion of the bilateral agreements which have been concluded since then. we all recognize not only its importance but also its inevitability. but we also know that in these agreements there are winners and losers. and in these agreements, in particular, the outermost regions are clearly defeated and harmed. what i cannot accept is that, as the commission has done again today, it insists on the argument that the 2006 revision of the posei already foresaw this situation and that therefore, in this measure, it has already compensated the producers in the case in question, when we know that what was taken into account in 2006 was a tariff of 176 euros per tonne and now we are dealing with a tariff of 148, 114 or even 75 euros per tonne. what we are asking for is compensatory measures.
by opening, or rather opening the doors of the european market to american multinationals, which already control more than 80% of the world banana trade, this agreement will have serious consequences that even those who are going to approve it here will not hide. european producers in portugal, spain, greece, cyprus and france, which in 2008 were responsible for supplying almost 600,000 tonnes to the european market, will be hit hard. the rapporteur herself admits that the agreement threatens her future existence. in this context, beyond the substance of the agreement, it is very serious that the commission, while acknowledging the impacts, does not envisage any specific support measures for european producers, in particular through amendments to the posei regulation and budget adopted in 2006. the acp producers, who were not included in the discussions on this agreement, will also be severely affected by its consequences and the measures announced will not prevent these consequences. whoever approves this agreement must take responsibility for its consequences and it is no use coming here to express petty and inconsequential concerns in the form of questions or requests to the commission and the council.

on behalf of the ppe group. madam president, commissioner, the incidence of tuberculosis worldwide continues to be a major concern despite the progress made. due to the rise of resistance to this disease and insufficient scientific research, about two million people die each year today. in this resolution we welcome the eu's initiatives to combat tuberculosis, but we call for the development of further scientific research to develop new forms of vaccine against this disease. vaccines are the most effective public health measure to protect citizens from infectious diseases, but it is important that healthcare reaches developing countries too, in order to contribute to increasing life expectancy and fighting poverty. as i said, there has been some progress and we are on the right track, but there is a need for renewed eu commitment and for greater concerted action and integration of european research to combat poverty-related diseases. only in this way will we be able to reduce the dramatic situation in many developing countries. i would like to ask the commission how it intends to follow up scientific research efforts in this area, step up these efforts and translate the results of this research to the benefit of the populations in the light of the europe 2020 strategy?
with four years to go before the deadline for achieving the millennium development goals, tuberculosis is claiming two million lives a year. tuberculosis is a striking example of the inequalities that are rampant in this world. let us not forget that this is a disease of very low prevalence in industrialized countries. the problem of tuberculosis, like other diseases, cannot be solved without quality public health services accessible to the whole population, including primary health care. the development cooperation and aid policy has a key role to play here, which of course must involve support for vaccination programmes, but more is needed. it is necessary to break with mechanisms such as debt and debt service, which drain the resources of the third world and allow the maintenance of situations of backwardness, dependence, subjugation and misery.

in writing. the proposal for a regulation amending the development cooperation instrument aims to support the main african, caribbean and pacific (acp) banana exporting countries through accompanying measures for the banana sector. the initiative follows the reduction in preferential tariffs for acp banana exports agreed by the european union. the world trade organisation framework makes it necessary to reduce the tariffs on products imported into the european union. the plan is to run for four years, from 2010 to 2013, and according to the document, the measures should be guided by the objectives of development and poverty eradication, taking into account environmental, health and labour standards, and the specific criteria for the allocation of funds should be formulated. i support the initiative based on the concern to contribute and cooperate to the development of the acp countries by adding a programme of accompanying measures for the banana sector. i look forward to seeing how the situation of the outermost regions producing in this sector will be affected and taken into account subsequently as a result of the change in the trading conditions between the two parties.

in writing. − the agreement reached on 15 december 2009 between the union, a group of latin american countries and the united states on customs duties on bananas appears to have advantages, but does not fully reconcile the legitimate interests of all parties. it is therefore important to take certain actions aimed at better implementation of the agreements at various levels, in particular through an impact assessment for the banana-producing developing countries and the outermost regions of europe, to carry out an assessment of the mab 18 months before the end of the programme, to propose measures jointly with the acp countries to help the states heavily dependent on banana cultivation to diversify their economies, and to review and adjust the support package for eu domestic producers provided for in the posei budget, in particular the french overseas departments of guadeloupe and martinique, the azores, madeira and the canary islands. these and other measures of equal importance are highlighted in this resolution.
in writing. − the geneva agreement initialled on 15 december 2009 between the eu and the latin american banana producing countries has ended a long-standing dispute within the world trade organisation (wto). these negotiations, which are being conducted under the doha round, involve not only latin american countries but also african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries and the united states (which has committed to ending the wto dispute over the eu's banana import regime), with whom the eu has trade relations. the aim of this agreement is to introduce a gradual reduction in eu customs duties over seven years. i therefore welcome the negotiations conducted by the commission and hope that these agreements on banana trade - the geneva agreement and the eu/us agreement - will be signed as soon as possible. finally, i hope that these agreements will help to improve competitiveness and promote policies of economic diversification and help to raise the social, economic and environmental level of these developing countries, not forgetting, of course, the measures to support the eu's outermost banana-producing regions under posei.
in writing. - the amendments which we tabled and which the majority of parliament rejected summarise the reasons for our final vote against this resolution. the settlement of a dispute, in this case a commercial one, is not in itself a cause for rejoicing. it all depends, of course, on how the dispute was resolved, who won and who lost with the final solution, whether it was fair or not. that is what most of this parliament seems to ignore. the end of this dispute benefits the american multinationals in the sector, but hurts european and acp producers, especially small and medium-sized producers. the resolution acknowledges this, not without some hypocrisy, since those who propose it are the same people who approved the agreement that produces the negative effects that have been pointed out; the same people who now express petty concerns about these effects, but who made them viable by voting for them; the same people who demand an impact assessment of the agreement, but who do not wait for the results of this assessment to give it their endorsement; the same people who now call for respect for the ilo's decent work agenda, but who blindly tune in to the pace of the wto and turn a blind eye to complaints of human rights violations by american multinationals in latin american countries.
in writing. - i must welcome the end of one of the most technically complex, politically sensitive and commercially important disputes the wto has ever faced. i also believe that this agreement is not perfect and that it may cause some problems in the future. it therefore urges the commission to present as soon as possible an assessment of the impact of the bananas trade agreements on banana-producing developing countries and the outermost regions of europe in the period up to 2020, so that we can take stock of the difficulties of these countries and act accordingly, and if necessary adjust and strengthen the posei programme.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution because i consider that it contains important recommendations to the commission and the council in the context of fair compensation for the negative externalities of the agreements concluded, especially as regards the outermost regions of europe. the agreement reached does not fully reconcile the legitimate interests of all the parties and it is therefore important to take certain actions aimed at a better implementation of the agreements at various levels, in particular through an impact assessment for developing banana producing countries and for the outermost regions of europe. it would therefore be important to review and adjust the support package for internal eu producers provided for in the posei budget, namely the french overseas departments of guadeloupe and martinique, the azores, madeira and the canary islands.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution which, following the agreement reached on 15 december 2009 between the eu, a group of latin american countries and the us on customs duties on imported bananas, draws attention to the need to assess the impact of these duties on developing producer countries and the outermost regions of europe and to provide adequate support to acp and eu producers so that they can adapt to the new reality of the international market.
in writing. − under the agreement with latin american countries, the eu will gradually reduce the banana export duties from the current 176eur/tonne to a final value of 114eur/tonne by 2017. the aim is a more predictable and stable global banana market, with more investment and growth in the sector, ending a decades-long conflict based on complaints against the eu when it introduced changes to banana customs duties in 2006. the question of eu relations with third countries in the banana sector also includes the treatment of acp countries through new accompanying measures. it remains to be seen what measures will be taken to take due account of the interests of producers in the outermost regions, which are allegedly already compensated in the posei budget. given that the last revision of posei was made in 2006, it is not acceptable to argue that these changes in the framework of trade relations in the sector have already been taken into account. compensatory measures are urgently needed in the forthcoming revision of the regulation to ensure that european banana producers in the outermost regions have the means to minimise the impact of the liberalisation of the sector.
in writing. - while agreeing with the rapporteur's position on the need for the commission and the council to commit themselves to an impact assessment of the consequences of the agreements for the outermost regions and developing countries, i disagree with the way in which the process was carried out without impact assessments having been carried out beforehand, when it was known that production relevant to some territories of the european union, such as the outermost regions, was at stake. i therefore protest and abstain from voting.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation on the banana trade agreements because i believe that the conclusion of these agreements will put an end to disputes within the wto and contribute to the stability of the world banana market. i do, however, believe that it is necessary to ensure that the interests and specificities of banana producers in the outermost regions are respected, in particular by increasing posei funds.
in writing. - the banana sector is the fourth largest market in the world and only a limited number of producing countries are involved. only 20% of total production is destined for international trade. on 15 december 2009, the union, a group of latin american countries and the united states reached an agreement on customs duties on imports of bananas. it closed a wto dispute centred on european discrimination against latin american producer countries vis-à-vis acps, and required a review of union policies and a gradual reduction from the current eur 176 per tonne to the final value of eur 114 per tonne by 2017. there will therefore be a loss of competitiveness of the acp countries which, despite the exemption from customs duties they enjoy, could lead to a negative economic and social impact. the agreement appears to have some advantages, but it is important to present an impact assessment of the acp countries' ability to react to market changes.
in writing. - the conclusion of a geneva agreement on trade in bananas between the eu and certain latin american countries and another agreement on trade in bananas between the eu and the united states of america. i voted in favour of this resolution not only because it asks the commission to clarify whether the financing agreement provides for an increase in the current amounts for development, but above all because it gives special attention to european producers in this agricultural sector which is located in the outermost regions of europe, such as madeira, where unemployment rates are quite high, thus contributing to the increase in social and economic cohesion. i therefore hope that the amounts allocated to posei will be increased so that european banana farmers can withstand the competition created by the increasing liberalization of this sector as a result of the new agreements.

in writing. − on 15 december 2009, the eu, a group of latin american countries and the us reached an agreement on customs duties for banana imports, ending a long-running dispute over the preferential treatment given by the eu to acp bananas over bananas from latin america. under this agreement, the eu will have to gradually reduce customs duties on imports of bananas from latin america from the current 176 eur/tonne to 114 eur/tonne by 2017, which will naturally have a negative impact on the banana-producing acp countries and the eu's outermost regions. the impact of the agreement should therefore be carefully assessed and appropriate measures adopted to support producers in the acp countries and the eu's outermost regions. in this respect, in addition to the additional aid provided for the main acp banana exporting countries - the so-called banana sector accompanying measures (bams) - it is essential that adjustments are made to the package of support for eu domestic producers provided for in the posei budget in order to help them adapt to the effects of changes in the world banana market.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on customs duties on bananas, which aims to implement the new duties provided for in the geneva agreement, the conclusion of which should contribute to the stability and predictability of the world banana market.
in writing. − on 15 december 2009, the union, a group of latin american countries and the united states reached an agreement on customs duties on bananas. it closed a wto dispute centred on european discrimination against latin american producer countries vis-à-vis acps, and required a review of union policies and a gradual reduction from the current eur 176 per tonne to the final value of eur 114 per tonne by 2017. following the adoption of the geneva agreement on trade in bananas, it will be essential to make the necessary legislative amendments and corrections to ensure its effective implementation. in this regard, the current council regulation (ec) no 1964/2005 on the customs duties applicable to bananas, which provides for a duty of eur 176 per tonne, should be repealed.
in writing. − the customs duties applicable to trade in bananas were provided for in council regulation (ec) no 1964/2005. following the recent negotiations between the eu and banana-producing countries, which have given rise to new agreements - notably the geneva agreement - and ended with long-running conflicts within the wto, it is imperative to abolish the said regulation. so, although it was not possible to reach a full consensus, i welcome this further progress in order for the eu's final commitment on this matter to be included in the next round of negotiations and i express my full agreement with the repeal of the customs duty provided for in council regulation (ec) no 1964/2005 of 29 november.
in writing. - this agreement illustrates the power of multinationals and the role of the wto as a forum for defending their interests. it also reveals to us, once again, how the european union is also acting as an instrument serving the interests of transnational monopolies. the agreement will further increase the market share of american multinationals, which already control more than 80% of the world banana trade - interests which the commission has taken it upon itself to reassure with this agreement. it is these multinationals that are facing accusations and denunciations of human rights violations, of expropriation of land from indigenous populations and of the promotion of conditions of work close to slavery. all to promote environmentally unsustainable models of intensive production. on the other hand, the agreement - as the rapporteur herself admits - will put the survival of thousands of small and mediumsized producers, both in the acp countries and in european countries, at risk. the small and mediumsized producers, social and labour rights and environmental protection continue to be sacrificed on the altar of free trade, reduced to mere verbs in official discourse, trampled on in practice every day, as we have seen once again.
in writing. - i must welcome the end of one of the most technically complex, politically sensitive and commercially important disputes the wto has ever faced. with the approval of this new agreement we have to adapt council regulation (ec) no 1964/2005. it has to be repealed in order to comply with the agreement leading to the reduction of customs duties and providing for a reduction from the current eur 176/tonne to eur 114/tonne by the end of 2017.
in writing. - i voted in favour of report a7-0003/2011, but i believe that an impact assessment should be presented on the consequences for the outermost regions, given that in many of these regions banana production is essential for the local economy. as the posei regulation is currently being revised, the commission should examine the possibilities of mitigating the negative externalities produced by this agreement in the regions mentioned. the geneva agreement on trade in bananas between the eu and latin american countries such as brazil, colombia, costa rica, ecuador, guatemala, honduras, mexico, nicaragua, panama, peru and venezuela resulted in a reduction of customs duties on imported bananas until 2017. european internal legislation will have to be adapted as a result of the repeal of regulation (ec) no 1964/2005 on the customs duties applicable to bananas. the final outcome of the agreement, namely the gradual liberalisation of the sector and the opening of the european market to banana imports, will inevitably have negative consequences for european domestic production in the sector, which must be taken into account.
in writing. − on 31 may 2010, the geneva agreement on trade in bananas was signed between the european union and brazil, colombia, costa rica, ecuador, guatemala, honduras, mexico, nicaragua, panama, peru and venezuela, providing for the gradual reduction of customs duties on imports of bananas from these countries. a first cut, applied retroactively from 15 december 2009, the date of entry into force of the agreement, reduced the duty to eur 148 per tonne. subsequent cuts will be applied over seven years, with a possible maximum delay of two years if the wto doha round agreement on agricultural product modalities is delayed. the final customs duty of eur 114/tonne should be reached by 1 january 2019 at the latest. therefore, following the conclusion of this agreement, it is now necessary to repeal council regulation (ec) no 1964/2005 of 29 november 2005 fixing the mfn customs duty applied by the eu to imports of bananas at eur 176 per tonne.
in writing. − the conclusion at international level of a geneva agreement on trade in bananas between the eu and latin american countries such as brazil, colombia, costa rica, ecuador, guatemala, honduras, mexico, nicaragua, panama, peru and venezuela aims to progressively reduce customs duties on imported bananas by 2017. it is therefore necessary to adapt european internal legislation to the terms of this agreement. this means that we are voting today to repeal regulation (ec) no 1964/2005 on the customs duties applicable to bananas. the conditions of this agreement, in particular the progressive liberalization of the sector and the opening of the european market to banana imports, will inevitably have consequences for european domestic production in the sector. it is urgent that the european commission should present an impact assessment on the consequences for the outermost regions, such as madeira, where i come from. the banana production is essential to the economy of several of the outermost regions, whose status, enshrined in the lisbon treaty, requires, in my view, that future adjustments be made to the posei programme.
in writing. - i approve this report as it takes account of the current need to integrate and increase the functionality and effectiveness of the disposal of waste electrical and electronic equipment. despite the positive figures, which show that about 85% of this type of waste is collected, it is nevertheless found that, if we compare the quantity collected with the number of equipment placed on the market, we find that 65% of the equipment sold is collected again and that a large part of this data is not reported to the authorities or treated appropriately. i also support the idea that the implementation of the directive could increase the rate of waste treated and released, particularly as regards the collection rate, responsibility for achieving the collection objective and consumer responsibility. the implementation of the directive will provide clearer rules on collection, treatment and recycling standards, with clearer indications on the costs resulting from collection and treatment.
in writing. − prevention of waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee), and its reuse and recycling are fundamental to sustainable production and consumption. it is essential to reduce the amount of waste to be disposed of and to contribute to the efficient use of resources. i call for better environmental performance by all operators involved in the life cycle of electrical and electronic equipment, namely producers, distributors and consumers, and in particular by operators directly involved in the collection and treatment of waste electrical and electronic equipment. in order to achieve the desired level of protection of human health and the environment, separate collection is a precondition for ensuring specific treatment and recycling of weee. i call on consumers to contribute actively to the success of this collection. to this end, appropriate facilities for the delivery of weee, including public collection centres, where individuals can deliver such waste at least free of charge, should be established.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on waste electrical and electronic equipment because it contains proposals which should help to reduce administrative burdens and strengthen the protection of the environment and human health by preventing or reducing the adverse impacts of the management of waste electrical and electronic equipment, with benefits for society.
in writing. − waste electrical and electronic equipment has grown exponentially across the union and its treatment and conversion is now a particularly important problem in the european context. in addition to the environmental and public health issues, which are in themselves of concern, the non-reuse of raw materials leads to inefficiency and an additional cost to the production system, which could be offset by improving the use of the materials in the equipment in question. i hope that the european union will make increasingly rational use of electronic and electrical machinery and equipment and that it will be able to reuse them in an environmentally safe and socially responsible way.
in writing. − the establishment of clear rules and objectives for the management of waste electrical and electronic equipment is absolutely key to the sustainable consolidation of the internal market and to better environmental quality in the european union, as well as to the recovery of strategic raw materials. it is essential that we know how to make better use of the resources available, especially in the face of the recognized scarcity of raw materials, and to value the wealth or added value that waste represents for our economy. given the discrepancies within the eu in the collection of weee from 16 kg per capita per year to 1 kg , i stress the need to ensure a greater effort of harmonisation, with a minimum of 4 kg per capita already in 2012 being perfectly reasonable. in a developed europe, it is important to meet the target of 85% of electrical and electronic equipment being collected by 2016 (as proposed by me in the committee on the environment, which was approved) and recycled between 50 and 75% of this equipment. i would also like to recall the proposal i made, which was approved in committee, for member states to submit data on the amount of resps generated each year.
in writing. - waste streams of electrical and electronic equipment have been increasing in the european union. in view of this, an amendment to the 2002 directive, which is still in force, is proposed. the collection and treatment of waste electrical and electronic equipment is important and necessary, taking into account not only the potential consequences for the environment and public health of this waste, but also the loss of secondary raw materials if not carried out, which is a serious problem. some 85% of waste electrical and electronic equipment produced is already collected in the eu. however, there are illegal shipments of this waste outside the eu, which reinforces the important role of member states in the control and supervision of collection and treatment. the proposal for a directive provides for a number of possible approaches for member states, ranging from restricting the circle of those who are authorised to collect waste equipment, to increasing the number of collection points, to requiring producers to set up incentive schemes for the delivery of waste equipment by consumers. in any case, the aim is greater recycling and greater reuse. for these reasons we have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - economic growth and the constant technological evolution of electrical and electronic equipment have brought a major problem, namely the treatment of its waste. this situation raises a number of problems, including environmental, public health and economic problems, which are now aggravated by the crisis the world is going through and which is reflected in the cost of treating this waste. we must therefore find ways of dealing with waste that do not, at the same time, impede the necessary sustained growth of the eu economies.
in writing. - i voted in favour, bearing in mind that the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission concluded in its opinion that the proposal in question does not contain substantive amendments other than those identified as such and that, as regards the codification of the unchanged provisions of the previous acts together with the amendments introduced, the proposal is limited to the mere codification of existing acts without any substantive changes. i support the european parliament's request to the commission to submit this proposal again to the european parliament if it intends to substantially amend it or replace it with another text.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a directive recasting directive 2002/96/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 27 january 2003 on waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee). weee is the fastest growing waste stream in the eu and it is essential to promote increased collection and proper treatment of waste. the serious consequences of inappropriate disposal of weee in terms of damage to the environment and public health and loss of raw materials should be avoided. the amendments now proposed are therefore welcome, and they aim precisely to create a higher separate collection rate, reduce the loss of waste equipment in the weee system, prevent illegal shipments and ensure a high level of treatment of waste electrical and electronic equipment.

in writing. − we welcome the eu's initiatives to combat tuberculosis in the poorest countries, but call for more scientific research to develop new drugs and vaccines against this disease. vaccines are the most efficient and cheapest public health measure to protect citizens from infectious diseases, but it is important that health care reaches developing countries too, in order to contribute to increasing life expectancy and fighting poverty. as i said, progress has been made and we are on the right track, but there is a need for renewed eu commitment and for greater concerted action and integration of european research in the fight against poverty-related diseases. only in this way can we reduce the dramatic health situation in many developing countries. i would like to ask the commission how it intends to follow up scientific research efforts in this area, step up efforts and translate the results of this research to the benefit of the populations in the light of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the tuberculosis vaccination initiative because only a broad vaccination campaign can contribute to the achievement of the millennium development goal, which aims to halt the increase and reverse the trend in the incidence of tuberculosis by 2015 and to eliminate tuberculosis by 2050. it is urgent to explore innovative funding pathways that can strengthen health systems and tackle inequalities, in particular in maternal health and infant mortality.
in writing. − although tuberculosis is one of the diseases that has practically disappeared from the focus of health concerns in developed countries, the truth is that it remains today one of the leading causes of death in the world, as it kills close to 2 million people a year. especially in developing countries, this disease continues to be fatal in many cases, especially when associated with hiv/aids. it is therefore an example of the health inequalities between the industrialized world and the developing world. moreover, although tuberculosis continues to kill, research is being abandoned for the sake of commercial profitability. it is therefore important that europe invests in scientific research and supports the tbvii (tuberculosis vaccine initiative) as large-scale vaccination could have a positive effect on the elimination of tuberculosis by 2050. as we know, vaccines are an essential instrument, together with better, reliable and inexpensive infection tests, more effective diagnostics and treatments, which implies a major reorientation of research and increased and sustained funding, in which i believe the eu can play a key role.
in writing. the european parliament, the council and the commission have adopted a joint resolution on the situation in the democratic republic of congo (drc) and the situation in the democratic republic of congo (drc). improving the health of the world's population is one of the eu's major concerns. although at european level we can say that tb is under control, in developing countries, in association with other infectious diseases, it continues to be the cause of death for millions of people. a concerted effort, political and financial, is essential to bring this world scourge to a speedy end. i therefore welcome the adoption of this initiative to eradicate a contagious disease which, in the 21st century, continues to claim many lives, especially in developing countries.
in writing. - efforts in the field of research and development of new drugs and effective vaccines against diseases such as tuberculosis, which continue to claim millions of lives worldwide every year, should be encouraged and positive results strongly welcomed. once these results have been obtained, it is important to make the new achievements of science and technology available to those who need them, without exclusion of any kind. the only criterion for access should therefore be that of necessity. in the third world, the payment of external debt and debt service to rich countries represents a major drain on resources which are not going to health and education budgets - reduced to almost insignificance. the so-called structural adjustment programmes imposed from outside also contribute to this. for this reason, the fight against diseases such as tuberculosis, which increase poverty, also involves combating these mechanisms which generate and sustain dependency and poverty. in this context, it is regrettable that the provision of the new tuberculosis vaccine to the least developed countries - which we obviously support - can be defended in the name of strengthening the eu's role and leadership in these countries, as is done in the question which gave rise to this resolution.
in writing. − although tb is virtually extinct in developed countries, it remains a threat in poor and underdeveloped countries, particularly in africa, where it continues to kill millions of people every year. only a global vaccination plan can end this scourge and achieve the total elimination of this disease by 2050 as part of the millennium development goals (mdgs).
in writing. - tuberculosis is one of the examples of the way in which inequality between peoples affects health, given that this disease is almost eliminated in industrialized countries, and is still prevalent in other parts of the world. it is also important to bear in mind that tuberculosis is one of the opportunistic infections in the case of hiv or aids, and is therefore particularly serious. these considerations have prompted this resolution, which advocates the need for a large-scale vaccination programme to boost the achievement of mdg6 beyond 2015 and, above all, to eliminate tuberculosis by 2050. it was also these meritorious objectives which determined my vote in favour. to achieve these objectives and decisively combat tuberculosis, vaccines are an essential tool, coupled with better, reliable and inexpensive infection detection tests, more effective diagnostics and treatments, which implies a major reorientation of research and increased and lasting funding. the eu, through the european commission, should explore innovative funding avenues, such as the application of a member state and/or eu financial guarantee to mobilise resources for the tbvi initiative from the eib and thus secure funding and research in this area.
in writing. − despite progress, the global incidence of tuberculosis remains a major concern, with tb remaining one of the leading causes of death worldwide, especially in developing countries. research and funding in this area should therefore be strengthened by mobilising resources for the tb vaccination initiative (tbvi), as only a large-scale vaccination campaign can contribute to halting the increase and reversing the trend of tb incidence by 2015 and to eliminating tb by 2050, as envisaged in the united nations millennium development goals and the who stop tb programme.

in writing. − a first trade, development and cooperation agreement between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of south africa, of the other part, was signed in pretoria on 11 october 1999 and entered into force on 1 may 2004 for an indefinite period. this agreement had a review clause for 5 years after its entry into force. the entry into force of the lisbon treaty also requires the adoption of a new agreement, with the eu exercising all the rights and obligations previously exercised by the european community. the revised agreement signed in kleinmond in 2009 introduces a number of significant changes to the original agreement, including the following development-related changes: disarmament, alongside democratic principles, human rights and the rule of law, cooperation on disarmament issues and non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. hence my vote.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of south africa, of the other part, amending the agreement on trade, development and cooperation. since the entry into force of the cbca, eu trade in goods with south africa has been steadily increasing. the european union is south africa's main trading partner: in 2009, the eu was the destination of about 34% of south africa's total exports and the source of about 35% of south africa's total imports. the balance between imports and exports is striking, and i am concerned only with the production methods in south africa for products exported to the eu, which must comply with the same standards as european producers in the same industry. these indicators point to a path where the results of the first agreement signed in 1999 are already evident. i share the rapporteur's wish that the union's development cooperation objectives be respected, the main one being the reduction and, in the long term, the eradication of poverty.

in writing. − 1999 marks the signing of the first trade, development and cooperation agreement between the european community and its member states and the republic of south africa, which entered into force in 2004. this first agreement was purely economic in nature, liberalizing trade and leaving little room for development cooperation. the revision of the agreement, signed in 2009, introduces important changes to development policy, including cooperation on disarmament and non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, the incorporation of the rule of law and human rights, aid effectiveness, particularly in the fight against poverty, and the achievement of the millennium development goals. new areas of cooperation were added: combating terrorism and organised crime, preventing mercenary activities, combating the manufacture, trade and accumulation of small arms and light weapons, and cooperation on migration. i welcome the approval of this agreement with a strategic partner of the european union, and the institutionalisation of non-state actors as cooperation partners, and thus eligible for financial aid.
