in writing. − the aim of this resolution is to vote in favour of four agreements between the european union and iceland, liechtenstein and norway, which are designed to establish the contributions of these countries to reducing economic and social disparities within the european economic area and to strengthen them compared to the previous period. this proposal strengthens the contribution of the states concerned and does not substantially alter the fishing concessions. in this respect, the period 2009-2014 is essentially a renewal of the previously agreed period 2004-2009. the unanimous vote in the committees on international trade and fisheries is a clear indication of the uncontroversial nature of this question.
in writing. the european commission is presenting to parliament a proposal for four agreements. two of these agreements, on financial mechanisms for the period 2009-14, have a total financial allocation of eur 1.8 billion and concern an agreement between the eu, iceland, liechtenstein and norway (european economic area/eea financial mechanism, with an increase of 31%) and another between the eu and norway (norway financial mechanism, with an increase of 22%). the other two agreements relate to fishing concessions for iceland and norway between the years 2009 and 2014 and provide for their renewal. for iceland, the concessions are the same; as regards norway, as they have increased slightly, there will be a renewal of the transit agreement which expired on 30 april 2009. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the european union, including the countries of the former soviet union, the former soviet union and the former soviet union.
in writing. the conclusion of this agreement, which was approved here today, follows on from the agreement on the european economic area (eea) which has been in force since 1994 and involves the eea-efta states. at that time, five-yearly contributions were agreed by these states to reduce economic and social disparities in the eea, an objective which we naturally value. the appropriations for this five-year period (2009-2014) have increased to more than double the amount made available in the previous period. these eea financial resources will be made available to the 12 newest member states, as well as to greece, portugal and spain, and can be used in a wide range of areas, including environmental protection, social and human development and the safeguarding of cultural heritage. in view of the enlargements of the eu and the worsening social and economic situation in many of its countries, such as portugal, we consider it important to increase these appropriations.
in writing. - these agreements provide for an overall package of eur 1.8 billion, consisting of a 31% increase in the eea financial mechanism and a 22% increase in the norwegian financial mechanism. it should be noted that these eea financial resources should be channelled to finance, as a matter of priority, environmental protection, climate change and renewable energy, civil society, human and social development and the safeguarding of cultural heritage. norway's financial resources will be channelled into the priority sectors of carbon capture and storage, eco-industrial innovation, research and scholarship, human and social development, justice and home affairs, and the promotion of decent work and tripartite dialogue. as regards the two protocols on certain fishing concessions for iceland and norway for the period 2009-2014, they provide for the renewal of the previous protocols for 2004-2009, with the concessions for iceland remaining unchanged and those for norway being slightly increased, which will serve as a basis for the renewal of the fisheries transit agreement by norway.
in writing. − this report gives the green light to the renewal of the eea agreements. since the entry into force of the eea agreement in 1994, the eea-efta states (now iceland, liechtenstein and norway) have contributed to reducing economic and social disparities in the eea. these contributions have always been agreed for five-year periods and it is now intended to renew the agreements for the period 2009-2014. in parallel, but independently of these negotiations, negotiations were also initiated and then concluded on 18.12.2009 on the basis of the revision clause of the two bilateral fish protocols with iceland and norway. the outcome of the above negotiations should include the significant increase in the financial mechanism, although iceland's position remained unchanged in view of the severe crisis it is going through. as regards the agreements on certain fishing concessions for iceland and norway for the period 2009-2014, i support the favourable opinion of the fisheries committee which highlights the slight increase in concessions to norway, which will serve as a basis for the renewal of the fisheries transit agreement by norway, which expired on 30.04.2009. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − since the entry into force of the agreement on the european economic area (eea) in 1994, the eea-efta states (now iceland, liechtenstein and norway) have contributed to reducing economic and social disparities in the eea. these contributions have always been agreed for five-year periods, and this is now the case with regard to the agreements reached on the financial mechanisms for the period 2009-2014 and the renewal of two bilateral protocols with iceland and norway concerning fishing concessions. no major changes were made to these protocols compared with the previous period, with the concessions for iceland remaining unchanged and those for norway only slightly increased. as regards the agreements on financial mechanisms, they have led to a significant increase in the contribution of the eea efta states compared to the period 2004-09, with an overall package of eur 1800 million being made available to the 12 newest member states, as well as greece, portugal and spain, to finance priority important sectors, including environmental protection, climate change, renewable energy, human and social development and the safeguarding of cultural heritage. i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. - i approve this report in view of the fact that the schengen area already allows free movement across 42 673 km of external maritime borders and 7 721 km of land borders, covering 25 countries and 400 million citizens. the gradual enlargement of this area has enabled third countries with special relations with the eu to participate in schengen cooperation and the swiss confederation to also accede to the schengen acquis on 1 march 2008. given the policy of openness between switzerland and the principality of liechtenstein, a micro-state which has been gradually integrating into the european trading area since its accession to the european economic area in 1995, the fact that it has already transposed 98.4% of eu directives into its internal law and that this state is part of the single market, there is no reason for me to oppose its accession to the schengen area.
in writing. - five member states decided 25 years ago to abolish internal borders between them and create a single external border. at present, all member states are full schengen members, with the exception of the united kingdom, ireland, cyprus, bulgaria and romania. three associated states are also involved: norway, iceland and switzerland, with liechtenstein set to become the fourth. liechtenstein's association with schengen was expected to take place at the same time as switzerland 2008. however, the procedure did not proceed as planned, in particular because of reservations raised by two member states (germany and sweden) on issues related to tax evasion. the isolated accession of switzerland has made it necessary to introduce controls in areas where, for over a hundred years, there was no real border, and the 41 km that separates switzerland from liechtenstein has become an external border. in view of the new rules in the lisbon treaty, which allow the ep to be associated much more closely with the conclusion of international agreements, and the fact that the reservations that existed in the council have been lifted, i propose that the ep give its consent to the conclusion of this protocol, hoping that liechtenstein can join schengen as soon as possible.
in writing. − given the open border policy between the principality of liechtenstein and the swiss confederation, it would be expected that the two countries would have joined schengen at the same time. however, that is not what happened. switzerland joined the schengen area on its own on 12 december 2008. however, the swiss accession agreement already provided for the possibility of accession by liechtenstein, by means of a protocol, which this parliament now approves. with this accession, it was for the first time necessary to carry out border controls between liechtenstein and switzerland, in places where, for a century, no real border existed.
in writing. − this recommendation advises parliament to give its consent to the establishment of a protocol between the european union, the european community, the swiss confederation and the principality of liechtenstein on the accession of the principality of liechtenstein to the agreement between the european union, the european community and the swiss confederation on the swiss confederation's association with the implementation, application and development of the schengen acquis, which was signed on 28 february 2008. the schengen treaty aims to create an area where there is free movement of persons and goods, without controls at the internal borders between states, and where there is only one external border. with the treaty of amsterdam (1999), schengen cooperation was taken over by the european union within the framework of its legal competences. for decades, the principality of liechtenstein and the swiss confederation have practised a policy of open borders with free movement of persons. with switzerland's accession to the schengen area in 2008, a problem of movement between the two states was created by turning this border into an external border, which is now being addressed. in view of the advantages of the entry into force of this protocol, nothing prevents its adoption.
in writing. the schengen agreement dates back to 1985 and was concluded between germany, belgium, france, luxembourg and the netherlands. the agreement, and the subsequent convention adopted in 1990, aims to abolish systematic checks at the common borders and to establish a regime of free movement of persons. the convention implementing the schengen agreement abolished internal border controls between the signatory states and created a single external border with common visa rules, police and judicial cooperation, and the schengen information system. the schengen area currently comprises 25 schengen member states: the member states of the european union austria, belgium, denmark, france, finland, germany, greece, italy, luxembourg, the netherlands, portugal, spain, sweden, slovenia, the czech republic, estonia, hungary, latvia, lithuania, malta, poland, slovakia, and the three associated countries which are not members of the eu norway, iceland and switzerland. at present, bulgaria, romania and cyprus only partially apply the schengen acquis and therefore controls continue to be carried out at their borders.
in writing. − the accession of new countries to the schengen information system is essential to achieve a europe without borders. liechtenstein has been part of the european economic area (eea) since 1995 and has been gradually integrating into the european trading area. it has been subject to a number of evaluation procedures, in particular with regard to data protection, the schengen information system, air, land and sea borders, police cooperation and visa policy. the accession of liechtenstein to the agreement will make it part of the schengen acquis.
in writing. the schengen agreement was signed on 14 june 1985 between germany, belgium, france, luxembourg and the netherlands. at present, schengen cooperation is part of the eu's legal and institutional framework and comprises 25 schengen member states, including the three countries associated with the eea - norway, iceland and switzerland. switzerland joined the schengen area on its own on 12 december 2008 with the abolition of checks at land borders, followed by the abolition of border checks on intra-schengen flights at airports on 29 march 2009. since liechtenstein has not joined and there is an intense free movement policy between the two countries, it has been necessary for the first time to carry out checks in places where, for a century, there has been no real border. the 41 km that separates the two countries has become an external border of schengen. this agreement removes this barrier by the accession of the principality of liechtenstein to schengen. i welcome the new rules introduced by the treaty of lisbon which allow the european parliament to play an active role in the adoption of these agreements. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the agreement on the accession of the swiss confederation to the schengen acquis, in force since 1 march 2008, already explicitly provided for the possible association of liechtenstein by means of a protocol. in fact, given the decades-old policy of open borders between the principality of liechtenstein and the swiss confederation, it was expected that both countries would join the schengen area at the same time. the truth is that this did not happen, and switzerland alone acceded to the schengen acquis on 12 december 2008, which eventually determined the need to carry out controls in places where, for a century, there was no real border. in order to overcome this obstacle, and also in view of the fact that liechtenstein is part of the european economic area and the single market, i have given my support to the conclusion of this protocol, in the hope that liechtenstein's accession to the schengen acquis can finally be achieved.

in writing. − the agreement concluded on 26 october 2004 with the swiss confederation on the criteria and mechanisms for determining the state responsible for examining an asylum application lodged in a member state or in switzerland, the so-called dublin agreement with switzerland, provides for the possibility of liechtenstein's accession to the dublin acquis by means of a protocol. in fact, the existence of a policy of opening the borders to the movement of persons between liechtenstein and switzerland that has been in place for several decades led liechtenstein to express again in 2005 its interest in acceding to the dublin agreement with switzerland. the final conclusion of the agreement has not yet been achieved for a number of reasons: firstly, because no other agreements have been concluded with liechtenstein; secondly, because of a disagreement over the legal basis; and finally, because of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. finally, the european parliament sees its objectives achieved when it is heard to give a favourable opinion rather than merely being consulted. i welcome this and i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. − the agreement concluded on 26 october 2004 with the swiss confederation on the criteria and mechanisms for determining the state responsible for examining an asylum application lodged in a member state or in switzerland (the dublin agreement) provides for the possibility for liechtenstein to join the dublin acquis by means of a protocol. as a result of a decades-long policy of opening the borders to the movement of persons between switzerland and liechtenstein, liechtenstein expressed interest as early as 2001 in joining the dublin agreement with switzerland, but was not involved in the negotiations because it had not concluded an agreement on the taxation of savings with the european community. with the subsequent conclusion and entry into force of that agreement between the european community and liechtenstein, liechtenstein confirmed on 10 june 2005 its wish to become a party to the dublin acquis. having overcome the differences with the council as regards the legal basis and having assumed the need for the approval of the european parliament, i believe that all the conditions are met for consent to the conclusion of this protocol with liechtenstein.

in writing. − while brazilian citizens can travel to all eu member states without a visa for short stays, there are still four eu member states (estonia, cyprus, malta and latvia) whose citizens require a visa to enter brazilian territory. while all other member states have negotiated bilateral agreements with brazil to ensure the exemption from the visa requirement for short stays, at present there is no longer any possibility for member states to conclude such agreements on an individual basis. the union thus has exclusive external competence in the field of the common visa policy. an agreement between the eu and brazil was thus concluded on 8 november 2010 granting reciprocal visa-free travel for tourist and business purposes to all eu and brazilian citizens. i support this agreement, which thus guarantees equal treatment for all eu citizens, while ensuring that it can only be suspended or terminated by either brazil or the eu if it applies to all its member states.

in writing. - under the last portuguese presidency, the european union established a special strategic partnership with brazil. in the spirit of such an agreement, all measures to remove obstacles to contacts between european citizens and those of the portuguese-speaking country are obviously to be welcomed. since four european countries do not yet enjoy such an exemption, i think it would be very useful to extend the same system to them and, consequently, to assess positively the agreement which is now being proposed to us. as regards eu-brazil relations, i would remind you that the strategic importance of this country has long justified the establishment of a specific delegation, as is already the case with the other members of the bric group and with countries that are objectively less relevant on the international scene.
in writing. − brazilian citizens, in accordance with regulation (ec) no 539/2001, can travel to all eu member states without a visa and provided that the stays are short. however, not all people from the european union enjoy the same privileges. this situation concerns nationals of the following countries: estonia, cyprus, malta and latvia, and therefore the principle of reciprocity is not respected. in order to ensure that these citizens are on an equal footing with the rest of the inhabitants of the european union and brazil, an agreement between the eu and brazil is necessary. because we cannot have a two-speed european union, i welcome the approval of this agreement, not only because it seems to be entirely fair, but also because it ends one of the few negative discriminations that still exists between citizens of the european union.
in writing. - it is intended to extend to the european union (eu) countries still subject to its abolition short-term stays for holders of a common passport. the report supports the conclusion as soon as possible of this visa-free agreement so that all eu citizens, including the citizens of estonia, latvia, malta and cyprus, can travel without a visa to brazil for tourism and business purposes, just as brazilian citizens can already travel without a visa to all eu member states. this is the application of the reciprocity policy on visas. the european parliament believes that visa reciprocity should be extended until all its citizens from all member states can enter without a visa all the countries whose citizens can already travel without a visa to the eu, including the united states and canada. which we think is fair.
in writing. − all eu citizens who want to travel to brazil for tourism and business purposes will not need a visa for stays of up to three months, just as brazilian citizens can already travel visa-free to all eu countries, according to the agreement now approved by the european parliament. this agreement will mainly benefit the citizens of estonia, latvia, malta and cyprus, who still needed a visa to enter brazil. this agreement concerns holders of a common passport. with the approval of this agreement, all eu citizens - including citizens of estonia, latvia, malta and cyprus, who were still required to have a visa by brazil - will be able to enter the country without a visa for tourism and business purposes, just as brazilian citizens can now travel without a visa to all eu member states. the duration of the stay is limited to three months, and for a period of six months in the schengen area. this agreement will cover about 90 to 95% of all travellers.
in writing. − brazilian citizens can travel to all eu member states without a visa for short stays, in accordance with council regulation (ec) no 539/2001. however, brazil continues to require a visa for entry into its territory from citizens of four member states: estonia, cyprus, malta and latvia. the other member states have concluded bilateral agreements directly with brazil. to address this and in the light of the european union's exclusive external competence in this area, the council adopted a decision authorising the commission to open negotiations for the conclusion of a visa waiver agreement between the european union and brazil for short stays. the current eu-brazil agreement, which i vote for, grants reciprocal visa-free travel for tourist and business purposes to all brazilian and eu citizens, including nationals of the four member states who do not currently enjoy visa-free travel to brazil. the agreement does not replace, but complements, the existing agreements in force between several member states and brazil, which cover travel for purposes other than tourism and professional travel (e.g. students and researchers).
in writing. - i voted in favour of the conclusion of the eu-brazil agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of a common passport, in order to ensure that, in accordance with the requirements of the principle of reciprocity and the principle of equal treatment, all eu citizens - including the citizens of estonia, latvia, malta and cyprus, who until now still required a visa to enter brazilian territory - can travel without a visa to brazil for tourist and professional purposes, just as brazilian citizens can now travel without a visa to all eu member states.
in writing. - the lisbon treaty has institutionalised the exclusive competence of the european union to conclude agreements on the common visa policy with third countries. council regulation (ec) no 539/2001 already allowed brazilian citizens to travel to all member states without the need for a visa. however, brazil continued to require visas for entry into its territory from citizens of estonia, cyprus, malta and latvia, member states of the european union. the object of this reciprocal visa-free agreement is for tourist and business purposes, which will bring economic advantages to both parties. the duration of the stay is three months for a period of six months in the schengen area. i think it is important to stress that this agreement takes account of the member states which do not yet fully apply the schengen acquis, namely cyprus, bulgaria and romania, by granting visa-free access to brazilian nationals for a period of three months in the territory of each of the member states, irrespective of the duration of the entire schengen area. i am voting in favour of this agreement because i consider it essential to avoid discrimination between citizens of different member states and to implement the principle of reciprocity, which is a fundamental principle of the european community.
in writing. - i approve this recommendation in view of the fact that brazil is included in the list of countries whose citizens are exempt from the visa requirement when crossing the external borders of the union under regulation (ec) no 539/2001, but that four member states of the european union do not yet enjoy the benefits of reciprocity. since the changes introduced by the lisbon treaty mean that the common visa policy towards foreign countries will become the exclusive competence of the eu, all member states will benefit from visa-free travel with brazil. in addition, the safeguard of existing bilateral agreements between the ms and brazil is maintained, as they include some categories of passengers not covered by the eu-brazil agreement. i also agree with the rapporteur when she says that this agreement should serve as an example for reciprocity with other countries, in particular the usa and canada.
in writing. − although brazil is on the so-called positive list of countries whose citizens are exempt from a visa when crossing the eu's external borders, there are still nationals of 4 eu countries (estonia, latvia, malta and cyprus) who cannot enjoy a similar right when travelling to brazil. under the lisbon treaty, the eu has exclusive competence for the common visa policy towards third countries, so it is up to the eu to negotiate this agreement, which ensures equal treatment for all eu citizens. it was decided to conclude two separate agreements: one for holders of a common passport and the other for holders of a diplomatic, service or official passport. i support this decision, which allows at least the agreement on diplomatic, service or official passports to enter into force more quickly, since unlike the agreement on common passports, it does not require ratification by the brazilian congress. the bilateral agreements concluded previously remain valid as they provide for a visa-free short-stay visa for certain categories of passengers not covered by any of the eu-brazil agreements.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation as it represents progress in establishing a full and reciprocal visa waiver for short stays for holders of diplomatic, service or official passports between the eu and brazil. the conclusion of this agreement should serve as an example for other countries, notably the usa and canada, which continue to maintain visa requirements for certain eu member states.
in writing. as regards the resolution we voted on today on the agreement to be concluded between the european union and the federative republic of brazil on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of a common passport, the majority of us believe that the same should apply to holders of diplomatic, service or official passports. reciprocity in this type of agreement is fundamental and important if we are to ensure that such exemptions are not restricted by administrative or bureaucratic requirements which may jeopardize the legitimate expectations of citizens. brazil is an increasingly important partner of the european union, with which it shares a common history and language. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect, and i am sure that the commission will be able to support them.
in writing. − brazilian citizens, in accordance with regulation (ec) no 539/2001, can travel to all eu member states without a visa and provided that the stays are short. however, not all people from the european union enjoy the same privileges. this situation concerns nationals of the following countries: estonia, cyprus, malta and latvia, and therefore the principle of reciprocity is not respected. in 2008, the council adopted a decision authorising the commission to negotiate an agreement between the eu and brazil to end the breaches of the principle of reciprocity. in order to speed up procedures and not delay its entry into force, the contracting parties decided to establish two agreements: one for holders of a common passport and the other for holders of a diplomatic passport (this does not require ratification by the brazilian congress). i therefore welcome this initiative which seeks to guarantee equal treatment for all citizens of the european union, in full respect of the principle of reciprocity.
in writing. - brazil is on the so-called positive list of countries whose citizens are exempt from having to apply for a visa when crossing the external borders of the european union. in accordance with the principle of reciprocity underlying this regulation, all eu citizens should enjoy a similar right when travelling to brazil. until now, the principle of reciprocity has been put into practice through bilateral visa waiver agreements concluded between brazil and individual member states. however, four eu countries - estonia, latvia, malta and cyprus - have not signed such agreements. therefore, its citizens are still required to hold a visa to travel to brazil, which violates the principle of reciprocity. the eu-brazil visa waiver agreement, which does not replace other bilateral agreements signed with several member states, now covers travel for tourist and business purposes by holders of diplomatic, service or official passports.
in writing. − all eu citizens who want to travel to brazil for tourism and business purposes will not need a visa for stays of up to three months, just as brazilian citizens can already travel visa-free to all eu countries, according to the agreement now approved by the european parliament. this agreement will mainly benefit the citizens of estonia, latvia, malta and cyprus, who still needed a visa to enter brazil. this agreement concerns holders of diplomatic, service and official passports. with the approval of this agreement, all eu citizens - including citizens of estonia, latvia, malta and cyprus, who were still required to have a visa by brazil - will be able to enter the country without a visa for tourism and business purposes, just as brazilian citizens can now travel without a visa to all eu member states. the duration of the stay is limited to three months, and for a period of six months in the schengen area.
in writing. − in accordance with the lisbon treaty, the common visa policy towards third countries is the exclusive competence of the eu. only the eu, and not individual member states, may negotiate and conclude a visa waiver agreement with brazil. this was not the case until the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. this report analyses the eu-brazil agreement on visa waiver for holders of diplomatic, service or official passports. the agreement was formally signed on behalf of the union and brazil in brussels on 8 november 2010. this visa waiver agreement does not replace other bilateral agreements signed with several member states, but complements them. however, the agreement concluded by the union shall prevail over bilateral agreements in the areas covered by them, in particular travel for tourism and business purposes. i welcome the reciprocity clauses between brazilian nationals and eu citizens and the guarantee of equal treatment for all eu citizens. it is envisaged that brazil and the eu may only suspend or terminate the agreement in respect of all member states. i voted in favour of all of this.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the conclusion of the eu-brazil agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic, service or official passports, in order to ensure that, in accordance with the requirements of the principle of reciprocity and the principle of equal treatment, all eu citizens holding diplomatic, service or official passports - including citizens of estonia, latvia, malta and cyprus, who until now still required a visa to enter brazilian territory - can travel without a visa to brazil for tourist and professional purposes, just as brazilian citizens can now travel without a visa to all eu member states.
in writing. - brazil is on the positive list of countries whose citizens are exempt from the visa requirement when entering the external borders of the european union. so far, this policy of reciprocity has been carried out by bilateral agreements between brazil and the member states. however, estonia, latvia, malta and cyprus have not concluded any agreements and their citizens are not exempt from visas. this agreement aims at visa-free travel for holders of diplomatic, service or official passports and has the same object and scope as the agreement on common passport holders. however, due to brazilian legislation, the agreement on diplomatic passport holders does not require ratification by the brazilian congress and will therefore enter into force more quickly. the two agreements do not replace the bilateral agreements concluded between the member states and brazil, but only complement them. i think it is important that this reciprocity in visa waiver agreements should be applied to other third countries in order to eliminate the existing discrimination, particularly with regard to the united states of america and canada.
in writing. - i approve this report as i recognise the potential of the internal market services directive for better integration of the economy, and also consider that the implementation of the directive can consolidate the mutually reinforcing relationship between the internal market and cohesion policy. to achieve this, greater transparency in the provision of information to citizens and businesses is needed. the conditions for non-application of the country of origin principle in certain matters or activities should be specified, in particular as regards different legislation under other community instruments and the set of guarantees which the sending state must grant to posted workers. this matter provoked a long debate and prevented the directive from being applied in advance. i am afraid that the implementation of this directive at regional and local level may be counter to the measures of deregulation and prevent attempts to simplify administrative procedures, especially since the implementation of this directive may involve additional resources, and the contribution of the structural funds and other instruments to compensate for this is essential during the transitional period. i would therefore call for greater coherence and coordination between all policies.
in writing. − the services directive in the internal market, adopted in december 2006, is a response to the principle of free movement, aiming to create a common market for services within the european union. although adopted in 2006, this evaluation of its implementation revealed some delays in its implementation in some member states, both for legislative and technical reasons, as different legislative instruments were needed for its proper implementation. a fully functioning single market in services is essential to europe's economic recovery, accounting for over 70% of jobs and net job creation in the single market. the eu-wide gains could total between eur 60 and 140 billion, representing a potential growth of between 0.6% and 1.4% of gdp. i therefore support this report on the application of the services directive because i consider it important to evaluate the application of the directives, taking into account that these evaluations may reveal some existing shortcomings in the application of the directives and thus make it possible to correct them.
in writing. − the services directive is a key instrument for the growth of the european union, allowing selfemployed people and small and medium-sized enterprises in particular to carry out their activities in other member states much more easily, and to develop new sectors of activity and recruit staff there. these activities account for 40% of gdp and employment in the european union and are a key sector for economic growth and the fight against unemployment. it is important to strengthen the enormous potential for economic development and job creation that the european internal market in services holds, as it is an essential step towards a genuine internal market in services, which should enable businesses, in particular smes, to provide citizens with better quality services at competitive prices throughout the internal market. i hope that the objectives of the directive can begin to be achieved in the near future and that the whole of the eu and its regions can benefit from this, thus contributing to genuine economic, social and territorial cohesion through the creation of decent, lasting and quality jobs, as well as in terms of improving the quality and safety of the services provided.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider that the implementation of the services directive by the member states has been partial and limited so far. although this directive is one of the most important european laws aimed at opening up the services sector to free movement in the european union, there is still a long way to go. it is necessary to ensure that this legislation, adopted more than three years ago, is properly applied, in particular by the effective creation of contact points to which any citizen wishing to sell services in another country can turn to obtain the necessary information.
in writing. − directive 2006/123/ec on services in the internal market aims to open the market to service providers in the european union, to remove protectionist restrictions on the exercise of the activity of providing services, and to comply with the principle of free movement, with a view to achieving a genuine internal market for the sector. the services sector accounts for 40% of gdp and employment in the union and has enormous potential for growth and job creation, particularly in smes. the deadline for implementation of the directive expired at the end of 2009, but some deviations from its correct and effective implementation by some member states still remain. only 22 states have the online portal with all the necessary administrative information in operation, and of these 22 only 14 states have the necessary procedures available electronically. it is necessary to ensure and monitor the correct application of this directive by the member states, with a view to eliminating arbitrary obstacles and/or making the rules which continue to exist in the member states proportionate and non-discriminatory in nature.
in writing. - the proposal for a resolution on the implementation of directive 2006/123/ec on services in the internal market. the principle of free movement of persons and goods throughout the european union is enshrined in all the treaties and is intended to underpin the creation of the common market. with the aim of breaking down the bureaucracy that restricted the activity of providing services in the member states, directive 2006/123/ec was adopted. however, it is noted that not all member states are implementing this directive because of certain aspects which they consider to be not sufficiently clarified. that is why this resolution is so important. i welcome the creation of a rapid and effective means of responding to requests from employers and workers' representatives, such as one-stop shops, and i hope that they will not be limited to the electronic format but will also include a personal service, as we know how important this is when we are in a foreign country.
in writing. we voted against this report in line with all our previous positions on the infamous bolkestein directive and its unacceptable aims of facilitating the liberalisation of services, including public services, in order to promote the interests of the economic and financial groups in the european union at the expense of worsening unemployment and poorer services for their users, as is already clearly visible today in sectors which have embarked on this path. the report aims to put pressure on the member states which have not made as rapid progress as most meps would like, by protecting the interests of european economic groups, in transposing the directive on services in the internal market (2006/123/ec), which entered into force on 28 december 2006, with the aim, as stated in the report itself, of opening up the market to service providers in the european union, removing protectionist restrictions on the exercise of the activity of providing services in the member states and complying with the principle of free movement, which is the basis of the common market. what was needed was an objective assessment of the consequences of the implementation of liberalization and subsequent privatisation of services, in some cases of essential public services, in order to resume the uncompromising defence of the rights of the population and workers.
in writing. − directive 2006/123/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 12 december 2006 on services in the internal market aims to remove the remaining obstacles to the crossborder provision of services. after some difficulties in transposing the directive due to doubts in some member states, the guidelines for this procedure, which are designed to simplify coordination between member states in the areas of consumer protection, environmental protection, safety and public health, will finally be put into practice in all member states, and this report will contribute to an even more effective implementation and better operability of the measures presented. hence my vote.
in writing. the services directive aims to contribute to the completion of the internal market in services, while ensuring high levels of quality and social cohesion. it is an instrument to serve the eu's growth purpose and its implementation is part of the strategy 2020 framework and the single market act. the transposition of the services directive is a major challenge for member states, public administrations and local authorities, both in terms of the rules on the right of establishment and the provision of services and in terms of the creation of one-stop shops for service providers, especially smes. this directive makes it much easier for selfemployed people and smes in particular to carry on their activities in other member states, to develop new sectors of activity and to recruit staff. i voted in favour because i am convinced that the internal market information system and the single points of sale, by requiring a great deal of administrative cooperation between all the authorities involved, will lead to greater interoperability and the creation of networks at national, regional and local level throughout the eu, thus bringing the outermost regions closer to a genuine internal market.
in writing. − directive 2006/123/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 12 december 2006 on services in the internal market (the 'services' directive) aims to open up the market to service providers in the european union, to remove protectionist restrictions on the exercise of the activity of providing services in the member states and to comply with the principle of free movement, which forms the basis of the common market. it is an important instrument towards a genuine internal market in services, which aims to enable businesses, in particular smes, to provide better quality services at competitive prices throughout the eu, contributing to the promotion of prosperity and competitiveness as well as to job creation. the rapporteur rightly points out that it is therefore essential to ensure that they are properly transposed and applied by the member states, which must ensure that bureaucratic obstacles are removed and that employers have access to the relevant information, in particular by promoting the creation of one-stop shops.

in writing. - this report concerns a joint draft adopted by the conciliation committee of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the fundamental rights of passengers using bus and coach transport. first of all, i would like to congratulate the conciliation committee on the work it has done and on the consensus it has reached. in fact, out of the three rights initially identified by the council, it was possible to reach twelve, among which i would highlight the rules on liability, compensation, assistance, alternative transport and special attention to passengers with disabilities or reduced mobility. i therefore welcome this step by the european union which i am sure will increase the number of passengers travelling by bus because of the sense of safety and comfort it brings, which will contribute significantly to reducing co2 emissions.
in writing. − the agreement on passenger rights in bus and coach transport, reached by the european parliament and the council in the conciliation committee, redefines the scope of the regulation established during the second reading, restricting it to passengers using so-called long-distance road services defining them as those involving a journey of 250 km or more. at the same time, it sets out 12 fundamental rights for short-distance passengers, focusing on the needs of people with disabilities and reduced mobility, such as compensation for loss of or damage to wheelchairs and other mobility equipment, non-discriminatory tickets and contractual conditions and rights of information. these are proposals which we naturally value. we cannot, however, fail to express some doubts about the amendments introduced in the conciliation committee and the criteria used for the application of the regulation. the different sizes and characteristics of eu countries may make the regulation difficult to apply in some of them, especially the smaller ones, with many trips hardly falling within the accepted concept of long-distance travel and consequently their passengers being deprived of the rights in question without satisfactory justification.
in writing. - so far, only air, rail and sea passengers are covered by specific legislation. from now on, passengers on buses will also have their rights protected. passengers travelling by bus will thus have rights comparable to those of passengers using other modes of transport. the regulation we have adopted today provides for assistance and compensation to passengers in the event of accidents, cancellations or delays and non-discriminatory access for disabled persons. the new rules apply to all scheduled services, whether national or crossborder, with a route of at least 250 km. this is therefore an important step forward in the defence of citizens' rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on passenger rights in bus transport. i welcome the fact that the final text is a good and balanced compromise, since it succeeds in guaranteeing the rights of passengers without at the same time imposing a heavy burden on the carriers, many of whom are small and mediumsized enterprises. the commission's proposal to introduce at european union level passenger protection rights comparable to those applicable to other modes of transport and to ensure a level playing field between transport companies in the different member states and between the various modes of transport is a measure which can benefit everyone. the negotiations were long and ended in a conciliation process, the main deadlock being the national implementing bodies and the scope of the directive. finally, the certificate will apply to all scheduled, national or cross-border services, provided that the distance covered by the service is equal to or greater than 250 km ('long distance'). the certificate also covers compensation and assistance in the event of an accident; passenger rights in the event of cancellation or delay; and rights of disabled persons and/or persons with reduced mobility.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i considered that the final text of the regulation, adopted in the conciliation committee, represents a balanced compromise which ensures adequate protection for passengers transported by bus, by recognising an important set of rights, in particular in the event of an accident, cancellation or delay, in terms of access to information and the submission and handling of complaints, as well as in terms of the needs of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility.
in writing. the european commission's proposal is aimed primarily at giving bus passengers the same rights as other modes of transport and ensuring a level playing field between transport companies in the different member states and the different modes of transport. despite the differences in the procedure, i welcome the adoption of this regulation, which will safeguard the rights of bus passengers without, however, creating too much burden for small and mediumsized enterprises operating in this sector. this regulation lays down a set of essential rights, of which i would highlight the special attention paid to persons with reduced mobility and persons with disabilities, the right to compensation and assistance in the event of an accident, cancellation or delay. these duties apply to all regular, national and cross-border transport provided that the distance covered is equal to or greater than 250 km. however, passengers who undertake part of these long-distance journeys are also covered. a number of rights for passengers on short-haul scheduled services have also been established, including non-discriminatory access to transport and the right to information during the journey.

in writing. − the road transport sector is the second largest emitter of greenhouse gases in the european union and its emissions are continuing to increase. the commission has already taken a number of measures to reduce the emissions of co2 from road transport. the greenhouse gas reduction target will be more easily achieved if there is community-wide legislation rather than national legislation with different objectives. in addition, we will have greater security and legal certainty for the car manufacturing sector. however, we must combine ambition with realism and common sense. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the european union's transport policy. i therefore agree with the target of 147 g co2/km emissions for new light commercial vehicles registered in the union, and provided that the feasibility of this option is confirmed. i am also pleased that no single european speed limit has been introduced for this type of vehicle.
in writing. − we are in favour of the development and application of technologies that reduce the consumption of fossil fuels and, consequently, the levels of emissions of gases into the atmosphere from the combustion of these fuels. for reasons of environmental quality, public health and welfare, and for reasons connected with the progressive and inexorable shortage of fossil fuel reserves worldwide, which requires great wisdom and thrift in their management. this is also inseparable from the need to invest in means of transport which do not depend on this form of energy, such as rail transport, and which must be developed. in this particular case, we believe that the emission performance standards for new light commercial vehicles should not ignore either the diversity of car manufacturers or the legitimate interests and needs of small and mediumsized enterprises in the different member states. the discussion of this dossier has shown that there are various possibilities for limiting vehicle emissions, with inherent investment costs and also different application horizons, which should be carefully evaluated; these different possibilities include the introduction of speed limiters in vehicles, which in addition to reducing emissions can also have positive implications for road safety.
in writing. - two years ago, legislation was passed on passenger car emissions. it is now time for the european parliament to approve the introduction of co2 emission limits for new light commercial vehicles. these vehicles are mainly used by businesses, including small and medium-sized enterprises, and currently account for about 12% of the car fleet. in addition to contributing to better air quality and to the achievement of eu climate objectives, vehicles should provide greater energy savings for the small businesses that depend on them. the objectives set are designed to encourage innovation in industry. the regulation sets a target of 175 g co2/km to be applied in 2014, which should be progressively reduced to 147 g co2/km by 2020. the penalties applicable to trade marks which fail to comply with this regulation shall be strictly observed.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on new legislation to set emission performance standards for new light commercial vehicles as part of the community's integrated approach to reducing co2 emissions from light commercial vehicles. i based my decision on the various data presented in the various documents which informed the proceedings, in particular the fact that these vehicles currently account for about 12% of the car fleet. it is necessary to set co2 emission standards for new light commercial vehicles to avoid regulatory loopholes and it is important to encourage the automotive sector to invest in new technologies. i agree with the rapporteur when he stresses the need for the light commercial vehicle sector to follow the example of the passenger car sector which is striving to reduce co2 emissions. however, changes in these vehicles are not in their shape or weight but in the engine and mechanics, unlike passenger cars, which makes the process more time consuming and costly. however, it is important to encourage this technological advance for the benefit of all.
in writing. − the conclusion of the sustainable development strategy, initiated by the commission, emphasises the most urgent problems of sustainable development, in particular energy efficiency measures in transport. with a view to combating climate change in terms of co2 emissions and increasing the competitiveness of the european automotive industry, this regulation aims to establish incentive schemes, in particular the granting of supercredits and compensation for eco-innovations, as well as fewer criminal penalties. the agreement reached by the european parliament on this subject is ambitious but at the same time achievable. the community's short-term and phased target is 175 g co2/km to be achieved in 2017 and the long-term target is 147 g co2/km by 2020. at the same time, it provides super credits for vehicles that meet the efficiency criteria and imposes reasonable penalties when co2 emission ceilings are exceeded. i believe that the adoption of this regulation is part of the european union's environmental sustainability policies and, at the same time, protects producers, mostly small and mediumsized enterprises, users and promotes innovation in the sector.

in writing. − the existence of legislation within the eu protecting patents is essential for the protection of intellectual property rights. we will be able to have uniform protection in the territories of the participating member states, as well as reducing costs and simplifying administrative procedures. i would remind you that the cost of registering a patent in europe is currently about ten times that of a japanese or american patent. this is a way of encouraging innovation and scientific research and at the same time improving the internal market. according to commissioner barnier, only spain and italy have not expressed an interest in such enhanced cooperation. however, there are some legal doubts about the applicability of the enhanced cooperation procedure to the specific case. in fact, under article 328 (1) tfeu, when enhanced cooperation is established, it is open to all member states, provided that the conditions for participation, if any, laid down in the authorisation decision are respected. they shall also be open at any other time, provided that, in addition to the conditions referred to above, the acts already adopted in this context are complied with. i would remind you that in this enhanced cooperation there will be only one language regime for three languages: english, french and german.

in writing. - i am in favour of a european patent system, but for linguistic reasons and after reflection i abstained from voting on this report. i would have voted in favour if only the english language had been provided for, which today functions as a lingua franca. and i did so for three main reasons: first, because creating a patent system with mandatory translation of each application into the 23 official languages would be a costly, time-consuming process and would create a serious competitive deficit; second, because english is in fact now commonly used as a lingua franca; and third, because 90% of patent applications are filed in english. i cannot agree that french and german should be included in this procedure to the detriment of more widely spoken languages such as portuguese or spanish (as if there were languages with different statuses in the eu, which i reject) and so i abstained, thinking that it is urgent to move forward with a european patent system but the best solution would be a single language, english.

in writing. − the absence of unitary patent protection throughout europe places european companies in a clear competitive disadvantage vis-à-vis their american and japanese counterparts. in fact, patent costs in europe are about 10 times higher than patent costs in the us and japan, which is mainly due to the burden of translating patents into the languages of the various eu countries. in this context, i consider it essential that, in the name of strengthening the competitiveness of portuguese and european industry, rapid progress be made towards the creation of a unitary patent protection system, which is less onerous and complex, and which can act as a stimulus to innovation and scientific and technological development in portugal and the eu. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution. i cannot, however, fail to regret the choice made as regards the language arrangements. in fact, there are strong arguments against the current three-language solution - english, german and french - and i think it would have been preferable to have opted for the english-only system.

in writing. - the proposal consists essentially of a codification of the unchanged provisions of three regulations adopted between 1987 and 1990 which set the levels of radioactive contamination tolerated in the event of a radiological emergency. however, the insertion of a new recital explaining the need for an existing article, reserving the exercise of implementing powers to the council, implies a substantial change which justifies the use of the recasting technique. the content of the regulation consists of a two-tiered intervention mechanism in the event of a radiological emergency or nuclear accident which the commission proposes: immediate adoption by the commission of an ad hoc regulation to apply to a specific case, in a specific area and for a limited period of validity, the maximum tolerated levels of radioactive contamination specified in annexes i and iii to the proposal; set a deadline of one month after its adoption for a commission proposal to the council to adapt or confirm this ad hoc regulation. as the debate in the committee itself and in the alternative proposals it has put forward have shown, there is a certain guerrilla war of competence between the commission and the council. but what should be at the forefront should be serving the interests of citizens by better managing the situation after accidents, while respecting the competences of the member states concerned. hence our final vote of abstention.

in writing. - the present report concerns a legislative proposal which consists essentially of a codification of the unchanged provisions of three regulations adopted between 1987 and 1990 following the chernobyl disaster (1986), at which time the question of radioactive contamination of the environment gained importance. these regulations set the levels of radioactive contamination that are tolerated in the event of a radiological emergency. the content of the regulation consists of a two-tiered intervention mechanism in the event of a radiological emergency or nuclear accident which the commission proposes: (a) immediate adoption by the commission of an ad hoc regulation to apply to a specific case, in a specific area and for a limited period of validity, the maximum tolerated levels of radioactive contamination specified in annexes i and iii to the proposal; (b) set a deadline of one month after its adoption for a proposal from the commission to the council to adapt or confirm this ad hoc regulation. i am voting in favour of this report because i consider the amendments proposed by the european parliament to be positive and to give the text a modern logic. since the main objective of the regulation is the protection of public health, i consider that the legal basis should be article 168 tfeu.

changes that have been made along the way. we started in the market, we ended up in health (i welcome this shift towards health), we started in the physical space, we included the internet, we could not leave out the main gateway for counterfeit medicines in europe, we had only one control system, we associated it with sanctions and penalties. if we consider counterfeiting to be a crime, it in writing. - a reaction is urgently needed to the alarming increase in medicines that are falsified as to their identity, history or origin. these products usually contain low-quality or falsified substances, posing a serious threat to human and public health and leading to a lack of trust of patients also in the legal supply chain. these risks should be avoided by strengthening the verification requirements for manufacturers of medicinal products. the safety devices for medicinal products should also be harmonised in the union, allowing the authenticity and identification of each package to be verified and any falsifications to be proved, while ensuring the functioning of the internal market for medicinal products. the risk assessment should take into account aspects such as the price of medicinal products and the history of falsifications in the union and in third countries, as well as the consequences of falsifications for public health, depending on the specific characteristics of the products concerned and the severity of the disease to be treated. the security devices shall allow the verification of each pack of medicinal products supplied, irrespective of the mode of distribution used, including distance sales.
in writing. − the counterfeiting of medicines is an organised criminal activity which, like drug trafficking, endangers human lives. however, this type of criminal activity is not regulated in the same way, nor subject to the same level of sanctions as those normally applied to illicit acts associated with narcotics. the illegal production of medicines by copying their active products, or by simply omitting to do so, does not require large facilities or large investments. the profits are big and easy. the proceeds from the sale of counterfeit medicines in 2010 are estimated at eur 50.6 million, an increase of 95% compared to estimates made five years ago. this expansion is largely due to the lack of specific legislation in some countries, or the lack of the means or the will to implement it, and the fact that the level of sanctions envisaged does not have a genuine deterrent effect. i support the compromise reached by the rapporteur. it is balanced and puts the protection of patients first. this is a first step, although it leaves out important issues such as the fact that generic and non-prescription medicines are not covered by the application of safety devices.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on falsified medicines, because it includes measures to combat the alarming increase in falsified medicines in the eu, such as safety devices to verify the authenticity of the product throughout the distribution chain, with a view to patient safety and the protection of public health. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the eu, including the eu's maritime borders. i also welcome the fact that the ep is advocating the need for medicines to be controlled on entry and exit from the eu and for the application of heavy sanctions, since these are criminal acts that endanger human lives.
in writing. - consumer safety is a matter of vital importance to me, especially when these consumers are also patients who look to the medicines used for a cure or at least a significant improvement in their health. such security is even more important when seeking to ensure the authenticity of medicinal products placed on the market, whether in the traditional market or in products marketed on the internet. that is why i think it is essential to adopt very clear rules on the counterfeiting of medicines, a growing phenomenon in europe (and the world), with dire consequences for consumer confidence, for businesses and, most importantly, for the health of those who use counterfeit medicines. i therefore support this report and congratulate mrs marisa matias on the work she has done and on all the commitments negotiated.
in writing. - the illegal trade in medicines has been compared to the illegal trade in weapons of war and drug trafficking. this is a scourge that affects millions of people worldwide, and it is a nightmare for anyone who has a duty to protect public health: someone who is sick, often with chronic or terminal illnesses, is taking something that is harmless or even harmful! we know that there are more and more counterfeit or falsified medicines in circulation, and their number is in the millions. it is imperative to combat organised crime and cross-border traffickers, and to put an end to the existence of parallel marketing channels, in particular on the internet. i therefore welcome the adoption of tamper-proof packaging and the creation of an early warning mechanism. i welcome the adoption of this directive by parliament and the council which, by tracing its entire path, will prevent the introduction of falsified and/or counterfeit medicines into the european union and will strengthen the protection of public health by improving the quality and safety of medicines consumed. finally, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, marisa matias, my fellow citizen, on her work.
in writing. − this is a problem with serious effects on public health and the economies of the member states. the falsification of medicines and the alarming numbers of medicines entering the legal supply chain are concerns that need to be properly addressed and combated. without forgetting that medicines are only counterfeited and sold illegally because there are economic reasons that encourage this phenomenon, and the existence of generic medicines that are accessible to the populations at lower cost makes counterfeits less profitable. the report addresses the relevant issue of internet sales, part of the illegal supply chain. he refers to the importance of raising public awareness of the risks associated with the purchase of medicines through this channel. we stress the importance of enhancing cooperation and coordination between the competent national authorities, the european medicines agency (ema) and other international bodies with a view to exchanging information, increasing knowledge and understanding of the phenomenon and thereby improving the fight against it. we recall that this cooperation must also work in other areas, such as pharmacovigilance. there is a need for greater transparency in existing european structures such as the eea, with regard to the studies they carry out and their operation. we believe that the compromise reached is a positive step in the necessary fight against the problem.
in writing. − as this is a very serious problem affecting the public health of eu citizens, i consider it essential that new rules are put in place to protect patients from falsified medicines. on 23 april 2010, the european commission was therefore asked about a joint operation involving the 27 eu countries, called medi-fake, which at the time confiscated 34 million counterfeit tablets in just two months. that is why i have always advocated strong measures to combat this reality, in order to put an end to a business that represents 45 billion euros a year of profit for some criminal networks. hence my vote.
in writing. − this report is based on a commission proposal to prevent the introduction of counterfeit medicines into the supply chain by drawing attention to an issue of growing concern to european citizens: the quality and safety of the medicines they consume. the positive effect of this proposal is to encourage debate on a fundamental subject, with the ultimate aim of fighting against counterfeit medicines. in fact, counterfeiting medicines is a crime that deprives patients of the medical treatment they need and harms their health, possibly even leading to death. the main objective of the directive, as the rapporteur has said, should be to protect public health. this objective should be reflected in the legal basis of the directive. on the other hand, i think it is essential to safeguard the distribution network for medicinal products by establishing clear and precise definitions, not only of the scope of the directive but also of the different actors in the supply chain: traders, distributors, brokers; by defining roles and responsibilities. i voted in favour of this because i consider it essential that legislative action be taken in this area to deal with this growing threat to health and to better ensure patient safety.
in writing. − i support this resolution only because of the strong commitment by the commission to strengthen the financing instruments currently used to ensure that smes have more access to capital to finance their growth and innovation policies. one case that is relevant in the current economic crisis is the removal of the 'red tape' from existing eu support schemes. while approving the measures proposed in this resolution, i draw the commission's attention to moving forward with a more ambitious 'small business act' for the programming period after 2013. i would remind you that in the current economic climate, strong institutional and financial support for smes is more important than ever, since they are the backbone of the european economy and can only grow with adequate and sustainable financing tools.

in writing. - there are some 23 million smes in the european union, and their weight in national economies and their growth potential for the labour market is undeniable. portugal is an example of this. some 300 000 smes represent more than 99% of all enterprises and are directly responsible for more than 2 million jobs and around €170 billion in turnover. with the recent economic crisis, its already limited financing capacity has been significantly aggravated, in particular by the increasingly restrictive credit conditions imposed by the banking sector. the operation of the sme financing arrangements is thus made permanent, in particular through an increased union budget allocation to the competitiveness and innovation programme of the structural funds and fp7. on the other hand, it is important to correct market inefficiencies and to gradually remove administrative barriers. the right measures must be taken in good time so that the national economies of the member states can achieve their growth potential and contribute to the growth of the labour market, enabling the development of the states and the consequent social cohesion.
in writing. − this european parliament resolution deals with practical issues on the review of eu instruments to support financing for small and medium-sized enterprises in the next programming period. at european level, the number of small enterprises has been increasing significantly in recent years. they already represent 99% of all businesses, are responsible for some 100 million jobs and make a crucial contribution to economic growth and social cohesion. despite this, their access to finance has been very difficult and has been aggravated by the current financial crisis in which the banking sector has introduced high levels of demand into its financing mechanisms. i therefore welcome the adoption of this resolution and hope that there will be a significant strengthening of the sme financing arrangements and a simplification of administrative procedures, in particular by reducing the number of programmes and improving the complementarity between national and eu programmes.
in writing. - this resolution is very contradictory in that, while it has some positive references to necessary measures to support smes, it covers and insists on the same kind of policies that are at the root of the problems affecting smes, namely the stability pact, financial market liberalisation and so-called free competition, which only serve to protect economic and financial groups that charge high prices in order to obtain ever-increasing profits, either in the granting of credit or in the cost of energy and other raw materials. what was needed was an effective change in community policies. it is time to put an end to the stability pact and its irrational criteria and to replace it with a genuine pact for employment and social progress, which encourages small-scale investment, gives micro-enterprises the opportunity to grow and, in particular, supports groups - for example, young entrepreneurs - who are having difficulty finding credit opportunities for their business ideas, and promotes employment with rights and the improvement of living conditions so that there is more purchasing power of the population.
in writing. - there are 23 million small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in the eu, representing 99% of all businesses and more than 100 million jobs, making a key contribution to economic growth, social cohesion and job creation, being an important source of innovation and vital for maintaining and expanding employment. however, they have a poor access to finance, which is a major obstacle to their creation and growth, and the current financial and economic crisis aggravates the problem. a significant increase in funding for innovative financial instruments in the eu budget is therefore essential to meet the financial needs of smes in the light of the europe 2020 strategy.
