in writing. − smes in the european union are an essential element for economic growth and job creation, providing more than 100 million jobs and playing a crucial role in contributing to social cohesion. however, these companies have limited access to financial credit and loans, a situation which has been aggravated by the economic crisis and which is often complicated by administrative burdens. i am very much in favour of an attempt to improve the functioning of sme financing systems. in my view, this should be achieved by strengthening the importance of the eib's role in the lending scheme and also by implementing the instruments already in place within the competitiveness and innovation programme, the jeremie programme and the jasmine programme. i also support simplifying access to the structural funds for smes, particularly as regards guarantee schemes, avoiding duplication of effort. it will also be advisable to reflect on new effective financial instruments for the next multiannual financial framework, such as joint instruments with the european investment bank.
in writing. − the future of european citizens' pensions is one of the key challenges for the future of europe and i recognise the difficulties facing pension systems in the member states. however, i do not agree that the only way to solve the problem is to pay more, work more and retire less. i would also stress that the member states are primarily responsible for pensions, although the eu can add value by coordinating the various pension schemes and sharing best practices, as it also has competence in the area of pension portability and the supervision of institutions for occupational retirement provision (iorp directive). i only approve this report on the basis of the compromise based on more than 450 amendments, which include some of the main concerns for the white paper. i would also point out that a decent and sustainable pension system can only be achieved by tackling the precarious economy, low pay and low quality jobs. funded pensions should be based on solidarity and this should be reflected in eu standards.
in writing. − the issue of the sustainability of social security systems has been an inescapable topic on the european political agenda. increasing life expectancy, an ageing population, weak levels of economic growth, rising unemployment are factors which have contributed to the imbalance of social security systems. in the light of the current situation, decisions are needed to ensure the sustainability of social security schemes. i support this report because it advocates the need to build together a sustainable, secure system that provides adequate pensions at member state level. it recognises that free movement in europe cannot be limited to the benefits of the first pillar alone, but that mobility is indispensable for an operational and effective labour market. it advocates the creation of a european pension platform including representatives of the eu institutions, social partners and stakeholders, with a view to exchanging information on best practice and preparing policy initiatives, always respecting the principle of subsidiarity. it calls on the european commission to set up a specific working group on pensions.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis has significantly aggravated the demographic challenge facing the eu, leading to an increase in unemployment, poverty and social exclusion. the 75% employment rate target set in the eu 2020 strategy should help ensure the sustainability of pension schemes as it is linked to higher levels of employment, higher productivity and economic growth the holistic approach adopted in the green paper aims to give new impetus, both at national and eu level, to the establishment of sound, long-term adequate, sustainable and secure pension systems. smes are one of the main sources of employment and growth in the eu and make a significant contribution to the sustainability and adequacy of member states' pension systems. call for the development of sectoral, inter-sectoral and/or territorial funds that increase the membership of sme workers in pension schemes.
in writing. − while the member states are responsible for the provision of pensions, it is nevertheless important that there is coordination at european level for certain aspects. i am aware of the disparities between pension systems in europe. however, the need to develop a strategy to increase cohesion and consistency in the field of retirement pensions is clear, with full respect for the principles of subsidiarity and solidarity. this strategy must take account of the current economic and demographic situation, but also of the completion of the single market, since we must not forget that free movement in europe is a fundamental right of european citizens, which implies mobility of people and in particular of workers who should be able to benefit from an operational and effective labour market and from the guarantee that they will have access to a sustainable, secure and adequate income after retirement. it is also important to provide citizens with adequate and continuous information on their pension rights, especially in relation to schemes relating to cross-border activities and mobility.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it advocates the need for the eu and the member states to coordinate their different pension policies more appropriately and to ensure adequate, secure and sustainable pension schemes for women and men. it is essential to individualise pension rights according to gender and to define specific criteria for the calculation of pensions for women in order to ensure economic independence for both men and women.
in writing. − the increase in average life expectancy, coupled with the reversal of the age pyramid in europe, poses important challenges to an ageing society which will have to ensure that its elderly have adequate living conditions and a role which, in many cases, can (and should) be active. however, faced with the real threat of the bankruptcy of traditional pension systems, states must take the necessary measures - not just raising the retirement age - to safeguard social security schemes in a bold and forward-looking manner. the emphasis should be placed on modernisation, with the possibility of mixed models, ensuring that those who now enter the system can freely choose the model they want for their old age protection.
in writing. - the current crisis has highlighted a problem that was once widely recognised as a serious one: the failure of social security systems. indeed, the imminent reversal of the age pyramid following demographic changes resulting from a longer life expectancy of the population is calling into question the financial sustainability of pension schemes. on the one hand, the number of unemployed is increasing; on the other hand, more resources are being consumed in paying for pensions. in addition, young people are entering the labour market increasingly late, not cooperating with the contribution system. because we do not want old age to be synonymous with poverty, we must create a guaranteed minimum pension that gives the elderly a quality of life. a measure that will help eradicate poverty and ensure that the elderly live in dignity. all these problems are reflected in the european commission's green paper on pensions. a set of coordinated policies at eu level is now required. i therefore fully agree with the conclusions of this report and welcome initiatives aimed at achieving intergenerational solidarity that will enable all pensioners to have a sustainable and dignified income.
in writing. we regret that the motion for an alternative resolution which we tabled was not adopted. in this way, the majority of members of the european parliament, including the socialist group, have taken the side of the anti-social policies which the commission and the council are pursuing, giving cover to the neoliberal path which they are pursuing and want to deepen. they have thus forgotten the struggles which workers have waged in various countries of the european union against the raising of the legal retirement age, in defence of a public, solidarity-based and universal social security system which values the lowest pensions and pensions, which respects the elderly and allows them to live in dignity, and which contributes to the eradication of poverty. as stated in the alternative resolution we tabled, it is possible to improve pensions and pensions without raising the legal age, provided there is more employment with rights, especially for young people, better wages, higher taxation on financial transactions. for example, recent studies show that a general financial transaction tax of 0.1% at eu level could provide an increase in annual revenues of around 2.1% of gdp, or around eur 262 billion.
in writing. - the serious problem of demographic change, i.e. the reversal of the age pyramid which we will soon be witnessing, together with the increasing life expectancy, thanks to which the elderly enjoy good health, remain active and participate longer in our society, force us to reflect on a strategy which will increase cohesion and coherence in the field of retirement pensions. in the face of the new reality, initiatives are needed to redefine the future of young and old, as well as solidarity between generations and individuals, thus contributing to a sustainable, secure and adequate income after retirement.
in writing. − this report on adequate, sustainable and secure european pension schemes represents an important step in the implementation of a policy of coordination at european union level. although it is a matter for the member states, the pension system is directly linked to the financial market and is also one of the items in the stability and growth pact. for demographic reasons, which are well known, it is necessary to consider a strategy to increase cohesion and consistency in the field of retirement pensions. there is a need to create initiatives that redefine the future of young and old, as well as solidarity between generations and people, thus contributing to a sustainable, secure and adequate income after retirement. there are marked differences in europe between the various pension schemes, but it is important to create a common platform clearly defining the responsibilities of each. in this way, we can build together a sustainable, safe, modern system which recognises the freedom of movement in europe, which is part of the premise that mobility is indispensable, especially for the younger generations and, of course, for an operational and effective labour market. for all these reasons i voted in favour.

madam president, it is always better to prevent a catastrophe than to remedy it. there is a real risk of a world food crisis. it's not my line. it came from a government of one of the founding member states of the european union. the signs are disturbing. the rise in the prices of some basic food commodities, such as cereals, is continuing and, according to the fao, they even reached historic levels in january. the problem is obviously not european, and the weight of each of the hypothetical causes justifying the phenomenon is, as has already been emphasized here today, far from being known. we know that the commission is not inattentive, and its communication of the 2nd of this month is a document that deserves careful consideration. however, the specific nature of agricultural production deserves special attention in the cap, by enshrining genuine risk management instruments in development cooperation policy, by supporting food production at the expense of other forms of support and at international level. and here i welcome france's position within the g20, influencing the regulation of financial markets and the fight against price manipulation and also establishing rules to prevent abrupt disruption of trade flows, as has recently happened with russia, for example.
madam president, three years after the 2008 crisis, the world is on the verge of another food crisis. to stop it, we have to look at its causes and attack them. look at agricultural and trade policies that destroy small and mediumsized farming, that encourage intensive export-oriented production models and thereby threaten food security and food sovereignty, as is the case with the cap. the trend in oil prices and the high dependence of agricultural activity on this raw material, which must be reduced, must be taken into account. look at the enormous power of agribusiness multinationals who hold the monopoly of key production factors, at the increasing use of fertile land for purposes other than food production, at the usurpation of land from the local communities who live and work on it. above all, we must look at and attack the irrationality of an inhuman system that allows speculation on food. the financial instruments that enable speculation must be abolished, and the eu must accept this necessity, or it will be complicit - as it already is - in its consequences.
in writing. we are dealing with a problem which is above all a political issue requiring foresight. more than short-term remedies, what is needed is the courage to establish a new architecture that reconciles the need to increase food production by 70% over the next 40 years with the increasing limitations of natural resources. so what is done or not done in africa, asia, america or europe affects everyone everywhere with consequences on food availability, access and prices. this is seriously affecting poor populations and the beef and dairy farmers. that is why the response must be global and go far beyond the field of agricultural policy, and it is essential to call for a set of other policies, without which we will not really be reaching the necessary solutions. solutions that on a global scale involve defending food as a right, supporting countries' ability to feed themselves, supporting agricultural producers and ensuring their fair access to value in the food chain, limiting financial speculation, protecting access to land, creating food reserves.
food prices have risen sharply in recent years not so much as a result of the laws of supply and demand but mainly as a result of speculative behaviour. it turns out that these increases are mostly affecting the less well-off, who have to spend more than half their income on food. we cannot tolerate the exploitation of the hunger of others, either in europe or in the developing countries. food security is a citizen's right, which presupposes that everyone has access to healthy food. food shortages have a number of causes: wrong land-use planning policies and support for agriculture, for example, but also climate change. it is therefore crucial that the eu supports farmers to cultivate the land and produce the food they need. it is not acceptable that consumers pay too much and producers make too little, leaving the profits to the speculators. and also because of food security, the fight against climate change must be a priority for the eu.

mr president, we are facing the ultimate exponent of a trade vision which, instead of being oriented towards complementarity and reciprocity, is oriented solely towards competition. competition between countries, between products, between workers. the expected balance sheet of this free trade agreement is presented, as always, in millions of euros of profits for the large economic groups and transnational corporations. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. this agreement will mainly affect countries such as portugal and the regions most dependent on the sectors covered: textiles, automobiles and components, and electronics. it is significant that the rapporteur himself foresees the inevitable redundancies in europe, but we know that trade unions and farmers' organisations in korea are also against this agreement. it's clear who wins and who loses with your signature.

we must be very clear about this, because the second point that has been made is that the european external action service has a very broad mandate, which includes military operations. and the question i ask is: do these two aspects intersect, and how is it that the european investment bank cannot be easily diverted from its own objectives, from the mandate for which it was set up?

in writing. − on 23 april 2007, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with the republic of korea for the conclusion of an eu-korea free trade agreement. the agreement was initialled on 15 october 2009. the bilateral safeguard clause in this agreement, which provides for the possibility to reinstate the duty applied to parties benefiting from most-favoured-nation treatment (mfn) where, as a result of trade liberalisation, imports increase in such a way, in absolute terms or relative to domestic production, and under such conditions as to cause or threaten to cause serious injury to the union industry manufacturing like or directly competing products, is very important in order to maintain healthy competition which does not harm any of the parties. however, in order to achieve practical effects, the safeguard clause should be incorporated into the legislation of the european union, since it is necessary to specify not only the procedural aspects of the application of safeguard measures, but also the rights of the parties concerned. the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation under consideration constitutes the legal instrument for the application of the safeguard clause of the eu-korea fta.

in writing. − the european council in 2009 called on the commission to develop a european strategy for the danube region, taking into account that the danube region, comprising 115 million inhabitants and 14 european member states and non-eu member states - germany, austria, slovakia, the czech republic, slovenia, hungary, romania, bulgaria, croatia, serbia, bosnia and herzegovina, montenegro, moldova and ukraine - is a space where greater synergies between various eu policies can be developed. i cannot but welcome the adoption of the danube region strategy by the european commission and support the accompanying action plan, which is based on four pillars (namely connecting the danube region, protecting the environment, creating prosperity and strengthening the danube region), meeting the need to improve mobility, energy security, environmental protection, social and economic development, cultural exchanges, security and civil protection in the danube region. i hope that the eu strategy for the danube region will be adopted by the european council and that it will be implemented as soon as possible.
in writing. the danube region is made up of 14 eu member states and a total of 115 million people. it is a very heterogeneous region, with high mobility and strong interconnectivity, and has proved to be the right terrain for strengthening synergies between various policies, such as cohesion policy, transport policy, economic, energy, environmental policy, and also enlargement and neighbourhood policy itself. it is a rich region with strong economic capacities, but it requires coordinated efforts to develop a coherent, integrated and sustainable plan. an integrated and coordinated strategy aimed at cooperation between member states and between regions is an appropriate way to achieve the objective of territorial cohesion. to this end, i believe it is essential to involve all institutional and civil actors, in particular through the participation of local and regional authorities. the strategy should also be implemented through more efficient use of the structural funds and, above all, the possibility of using unused financial resources for macro-regional projects. i am voting in favour of this resolution for the danube, and i look forward to similar strategies being developed for other european macro-regions.

in writing. the european council welcomes the commission's proposal to establish a european energy charter for the period 2000-2006. i agree that the energy strategy should address and facilitate the transition to an environmentally sustainable energy development pathway and that the world bank should adopt a private sector development approach that maximises the benefits for the poor while also tackling climate change. i regret that a large part of the loans for fossil fuels continue to play a predominant role, despite the strategic objective of phasing out financing for such projects. i also note the concern that much of the multilateral financing granted to financial intermediaries is still poorly controlled and that these should have clear development objectives. i call on the world bank to reorient its current strategy towards a large-scale export-oriented energy model, towards decentralised and small-scale energy projects that more clearly respond to the basic needs of rural areas. finally, i fully agree with the need for the world bank to clearly identify and publicly disseminate the benefits of development before funding is allocated.

in writing. - according to the data in the proposal, 1.5 billion people currently lack access to electricity, of whom 4 out of 5 live in sub-saharan africa and south asia, and almost 2.4 billion people still use traditional biofuels for cooking and heating, which represents an unsustainable use of natural resources. it is therefore essential that the world bank adopts a new strategy for financing energy projects, focusing on the provision of efficient, affordable and clean energy as a way to reduce poverty and promote economic growth. in this context, and as the world bank finalizes its energy strategy, taking into account that it has in the past committed to making half of its investments in low-carbon energy, parliament called for priority to be given to clean energy projects, and in particular a clear focus on renewable energy, as a way of promoting sustainable development in the most disadvantaged regions.
in writing. the european parliament resolution on the world bank's energy strategy for developing countries. if we consider that today more than 1.5 billion people do not have access to electricity, a fundamental right of every citizen, we will understand the importance of this matter. at a time when the world bank is finalising a new energy strategy, a detailed approach is relevant. in fact, although this subject has been debated for more than twenty years, the results are far from satisfactory. we continue to rely too heavily on fossil fuels rather than exploring alternative energy sources. we are accelerating climate change and hurting people who live in extreme poverty. i therefore believe that the world bank should review its policy of supporting the exploitation of energy from fossil fuels by making support for this sector more transparent and by encouraging green energy in order to reduce not only environmental pollution but above all the external energy dependence of developing countries.
in writing. − there is no doubt that access to modern energy services is a prerequisite for poverty eradication and economic development, and that this requires energy services to be reliable, affordable - especially for the poor - and distributed in a balanced way, so that the gap between urban and rural areas can be bridged. in the 21st century, some 1.5 billion people still lack access to electricity, with 4 out of 5 living in sub-saharan africa and south asia, mostly in rural areas, and almost 2.4 billion people still using traditional biofuels for cooking and heating, causing serious health problems and 1.9 billion deaths a year from indoor pollution, as well as ecological damage from unsustainable use of natural resources. the world bank should therefore give priority to local and small-scale access to energy, particularly in the least developed countries of africa and asia.
in writing. - i support the concerns and suggestions expressed by the european parliament in this resolution, which i voted in favour of, on the world bank's energy strategy. given that access to modern energy services is a prerequisite for poverty eradication and economic development, and that the right to energy implies that energy services are reliable, affordable and distributed in a balanced way so as to bridge the gap between urban and rural areas, it seems to me essential that an investment policy based on the sustainable use of natural resources be promoted. i therefore support the european parliament's recommendations to the world bank in this area.
in writing. - i approve this proposal, taking into account that the current crisis raises the concern that the current mechanisms will not allow the crisis to be overcome, and the lack of coherence in achieving the five major objectives, particularly as regards employment rates, is aggravating. the annual growth review and the european semester framework are crucial instruments, but they should not replace or diminish the broad guidelines for economic and employment policies. the commission has already taken a number of measures to make the unity of economic efforts visible, including a system of eurobonds, a public bond market with high liquidity, lower interest rates and the creation of a european tax on financial transactions to curb speculation. the development and job creation should not be compromised, and a stronger role for the eib and the ebrd should be proposed in support of infrastructure, technology and especially smes. i would also point out that the strategy for growth and employment cannot be jeopardised by the current short-term view of fiscal consolidation and must take due account of public investment in its objectives.
in writing. - the economic and financial crisis we are currently experiencing has led to significant job losses in europe. the creation of more and better jobs in europe is a priority of the 2020 strategy and the european employment strategy. the aim is to transform europe into a smart, sustainable and inclusive economy, delivering high levels of employment, productivity and social cohesion. europe must act collectively to overcome the present situation. this resolution goes in that direction, calling on the commission and the council to involve, alongside the european parliament, national parliaments, the social partners and regional and local authorities in policies aimed at restoring jobs and growth. this requires the strengthening of the community method and the adoption of the european semester in the legislative governance framework. the emphasis on the role of smes and the single market act in job creation is commendable. finally, we would like to highlight the role of the agenda for new skills and jobs in achieving these objectives. that is why i support this resolution.

in writing. - the world in general and the european union in particular have been living through turbulent times, as exemplified by the current economic and financial crisis. in order to put an end to this situation, the european council adopted on 17 june 2010 the europe 2020 strategy for jobs and smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. it is a growth strategy for the next decade that will boost the european economy to high standards of employment, productivity and social cohesion. the objectives to be achieved by 2020 are ambitious: at the educational level, to reduce school drop-out to below 10% and to raise the percentage of graduates to 40% among the population aged 30 to 34; at the social level, to lift 20 million people out of situations at risk of poverty and exclusion. it also wants 3% of gdp to be invested in scientific research. i welcome the selection of flagship initiatives focusing on education, employment, youth, innovation, the digital agenda, the environment, globalisation, resource use and tackling exclusion, which will boost europe 2020's growth and competitiveness. i welcome the adoption of this strategy and urge the eu institutions and member state governments to spare no effort in achieving the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. - the reality is that it is not enough to put forward proposals, even if they are very modest in the social field, to achieve these objectives, especially if the policies they propose are exactly the same as those adopted so far and which are at the root of the social crisis we are experiencing. this is the case with strategy 2020, which is now associated with so-called economic governance. the leap forward they are seeking to make in economic governance, with the creation of the european semester, the deepening of sanctions in the context of compliance with the sgp, the economic policy guidelines and indicators that will be adopted, is not accompanied by a significant increase in the community budget, which would always be an essential condition for moving towards economic and social cohesion and preventing the worsening of the current divergences. what they want is to create a genuine straitjacket for the member states to put the so-called austerity measures into practice, which are the deepening of the neoliberal cartel with all its serious anti-social consequences. if there is any doubt about this, there is the german and french draft of the so-called competitiveness pact which seeks to raise the retirement age, to call into question collective bargaining and to deal yet another blow to labour and social rights, just to guarantee greater profits for economic and financial groups. that is why we voted against this resolution.

in writing. - i support this proposal as necessary in the face of the growing volatility of food prices, with an increase of around 90% in 2010, and of commodity prices, which have caused problems in the functioning of food supply chains, making the measures proposed in this resolution necessary. these include internal action with a strong cap to compensate farmers for increased costs, a greater focus on small organic farms for local consumption, the submission of appropriate proposals on the mifds and the market abuse directive, the enhancement of the effectiveness of the emea in the supervision of commodity markets, and even the mandate for regulators and supervisory bodies to restrict speculation. the eu also needs a global strategy to combat speculation, which involves international coordination of a mechanism to prevent excessive price fluctuations and the creation of specific regulations to be applied in as many countries as possible.
in writing. − the food and agriculture organisation (fao) warned in january of a possible increase in food prices in 2011, after food prices reached new all-time highs in 2010, following the rise during the 2008 food crisis. the fao 55 food raw materials index rose for the sixth consecutive month to 214.7 points, up from the previous all-time high of 213.5 points reached in june 2008. right now, food prices have reached record highs for the seventh consecutive month between 2010 and 2011, the highest since fao began tracking food prices in 1990. as i have said in the past, i believe that concrete measures must be taken within the framework of the cap to increase production, to supply markets better and to ensure greater price stability, as well as to ensure production that meets european consumer needs. as i have said, agriculture must be seen, especially in times of crisis such as the one we are going through, as a strategic sector, which is essential to guaranteeing the food security of the population.
in writing. − the right to food is a fundamental right, which is achieved when all people have, at all times, physical and economic access to adequate, safe and nutritious food that meets their needs to lead an active and healthy life. i consider the existence of hunger in the eu and in the world to be an unacceptable failure. in fact, according to estimates by the food and agriculture organization of the united nations (fao), the number of undernourished people worldwide stood at 925 million in 2010. this situation may be aggravated by the increase in food prices associated with unforeseeable food supply shortages. i therefore advocate a strong and sustainable agricultural sector in the eu where the countryside is prosperous and sustainable. the cap must ensure this. i also draw attention to the decline in agricultural incomes in the eu, caused by rising production costs and price volatility, which have a negative impact on farmers' ability to maintain production. in addition, european farmers have to meet the world's most stringent standards for food safety, the environment, animal welfare and labour.
in writing. - the resolution contains important positive aspects, such as the need to give priority to agriculture in development aid and the recognition of the disinvestment which has occurred in this area; the need for strategic and intervention stocks; the need for market intervention instruments to become a key part of the future cap (even if these instruments are not specified later, it is true that many advocate only the so-called emergency mechanisms, compatible with the market liberalization which has been pursued). however, the resolution omits key points and contains other negatives, even unacceptable ones. it does not say that the food crisis is the result of the agricultural and trade policies in force (such as the cap and free trade), does not make the just and necessary criticism of these policies or call for the change that is needed. it welcomes the integration of agriculture into the wto, although it proposes measures to mitigate this inclusion. we, for our part, maintain that agriculture should remain outside the wto. the fundamental concept of food sovereignty, which is inseparable from food security, is not addressed. the problem of speculation is not adequately addressed. the proposed measures go little beyond the calls for greater transparency in the market, which is clearly insufficient.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this motion for a resolution because i agree with all the principles it sets out. i am in favour of producing healthy food in sufficient quantities to contribute effectively to the world food demand. it is essential to ensure farmers' incomes and to create mechanisms to avoid huge volatility in prices and markets. to ensure that, on a global scale, we have enough food to feed the entire world's population, it is essential to support farmers in developing countries. at the global level, we must ensure that all available means are put in place to combat climate change, so that it does not diminish natural resources and agricultural production incomes. it is essential to strengthen the position of farmers in the food chain. the question of price increases linked to other external costs and speculation in agricultural commodities is essential for the productive sector to thrive.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the 'price of foodstuffs', because in six months the price of the fao food basket, including 55 basic necessities, has increased by 34%. in portugal we have an unsustainable reality for farmers with agricultural diesel approaching the record price of 1 euro per litre in 2008; electricity increased by almost 4% and agricultural electricity is expected to run out this year; feed, fertilizer and pesticide prices have also skyrocketed; the interest rates for crop loans are in the order of 6%, just to give a few examples. i also think it is unacceptable that, at a time when the general crisis is worsening, consumers should pay inflated prices without an improvement in farmer incomes. i believe that the european commission should take up its responsibilities and look at these serious problems in the agricultural sector from a holistic perspective and not, as it is doing with the milk package, leaving out one of the main players in the milk package, the large retailers.
in writing. − the right to food, enshrined in the universal declaration of human rights and article 39 tfeu, has been severely affected by the current economic and financial crisis. the projected population growth, particularly in emerging economies, and the increasing levels of poverty and hunger worldwide demonstrate that there must be at least a 70% increase in food production to meet the needs of the population. in parallel, financial speculation in food commodities is added to this scenario, which consequently leads to volatility in food prices, climatic phenomena and the steady increase in bioethanol production to the detriment of foodstuffs. i believe that concrete measures are urgently needed to combat the destabilisation of agricultural markets, and in this way support farmers and boost innovation in the sector, reinforcing the role of the cap as a key eu objective. this cross-cutting issue should be discussed multilaterally, as it affects the world's population and the multiplier effects are indisputable. an example of this is the riots in developing countries. support for countries at risk must be strengthened to prevent future food crises.
mr president, the introduction of taxes on financial transactions has long been necessary at world level and therefore also in the european union, as has the abolition of tax havens and speculative financial products. the need for effective control and regulation of the capital market has long been felt, preventing speculation on a wide range of products, from raw materials to real estate transactions, pensions, pensions, insurance, with a whole range of derivative products, including sovereign debt itself. unfortunately the european commission has not moved forward with these proposals, but it is known that the financial damage caused by tax evasion and fraud in europe is estimated at eur 250 billion a year, which alone would be enough to reduce public deficits without the need for tax increases. according to current revenue generation estimates, a financial transaction tax, even at the reduced rate, would generate about €200 billion a year at the eu level and $650 billion globally. and it is in this context that we ask: how can we accept that a clear position on the creation of a financial transaction tax at european union level is being postponed on the pretext of another study, new studies, new assessments? it is time to take clear decisions on capital control and taxation and not to continue to make workers and micro and small enterprises pay for the economic and social crisis.
mr president, the subject of innovative finance at global and european level is not only important but extremely topical. i regret that it has come down to the question of whether or not there is a new financial transaction tax, but i will not shy away from the debate. there are a number of questions i want to put to you. firstly, do you know of any crisis in this house which has been solved by the existence of new taxation? do you know of any studies on the administrative costs of this new taxation? do you know of any studies that determine the effects that this new taxation will have on the economy? i, in all honesty, do not know. moreover, do you know of any form of regulation that could be done by setting new taxes? or is regulation done through supervision and control over the market? it seems obvious to me that it is. i would like to make one final appeal: that this speech and this debate be conducted with the serenity that is due and not on the ideological basis of someone who cares little about economic growth, the growth of companies and the well-being of citizens.
mr president, it is not worth repeating that the present moment is the most serious test for the survival of the euro and therefore of europe. the podimata report opens up constructive solutions, and i would also like to congratulate our colleague on the ideas she has put forward. the gravity of the moment is not due to the fact that the euro area as a whole has an excessive deficit or external debt, but rather to the fact that the economies within it are persistently and severely diverging under the impact of common policy. we are also lacking the instruments which will enable these economies to converge, which will enable europe to regain its equilibrium, which will enable europe to grow. let's get this straight. the euro area and the european union cannot survive with the current degree of integration and diversity of its economies, with a budget of 1% of collective wealth. in practice, after the crisis, the only solution we were able to build was the austerity recipe, and it is the workers and the companies who are now paying for the deficits generated by the speculative crisis in the financial sector, in the salvation of which 26% of the wealth of the european union has been committed. the financial transaction tax, charged at a very low rate, for example 0.05% on transactions in high-risk, highly speculative products, is true to be paid by its consumers. but why should they not pay, when ordinary citizens pay vat on bread, milk and the most basic products? the tax burden must be redistributed in such a way as to harm workers and businesses less and to be shared more equitably by the financial sectors, in particular the speculative ones. and, commissioner, i do not think it is the commission's place at this time to refuse or to evade the clear political message that this parliament is sending to it. the public consultation cannot exclude the analysis of the financial transaction tax, on the contrary, it must be analysed with the highest priority.
mr president, this proposal for a regulation is intended to consolidate into a single document the recommendations adopted by the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean, which are intended to promote sound management of the mediterranean basin with the participation and accountability of all those who have an influence on it. i congratulate the rapporteur on his work. the good ecological status of this important sea basin is the main objective of the gfcm, and the promotion and sustainable development of this basin presupposes a range of measures for the conservation and management of marine biological resources, which are the gfcm's aim and which should govern fishing in this region. in this conservation strategy, the fight against illegal fishing is one of the greatest challenges facing us today. the general outlook for the council and parliament's proposals for a regulation is positive, but it is also necessary to monitor the implementation of all measures for control, cooperation, information and communication, not only for vessels flying the flag of the community but also for all vessels flying the flag of member states which are contracting parties to the gfcm, which should ensure that good fishing practices are applied. the correct implementation of the recommendations which will come into force with the adoption of this diploma will make it possible to achieve the objectives mentioned above, ensuring equal treatment for all fleets involved in these fisheries.
mr president, we would like to draw attention to one aspect of this proposal for a regulation which we consider to be of the utmost importance and which, unfortunately, we cannot accept. the importance of multilateral cooperation in the field of the good conservation of living marine resources is not in question, quite the contrary. but this proposal is intended to give the commission the power to adopt delegated acts in areas which conflict with the sovereignty of a member state, in this case the republic of cyprus, over its exclusive economic zone. this is all the more serious because sovereignty over this area is currently being threatened, as we know, illegally by a third country which is applying for membership. for this reason, this is also a very sensitive political issue. this proposal, as it stands, interferes with the legitimate right of a member state to exploit the natural resources under the seabed of its exclusive economic zone, a right which is recognised by the united nations convention on the law of the sea. we therefore call on you to support our proposal to restrict the scope of delegated acts by voting against the paragraph for which we are asking for a separate roll-call vote.
the european union has had fisheries agreements with mauritania for more than two decades. for 15 years, these agreements have included explicit objectives in the field of cooperation for the sustainable development of the fisheries sector in mauritania. the question now is: what are the practical results of these agreements? the fisheries sector in mauritania is still at a very early stage of development. the modernisation and development of small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing and related industries, the development of port infrastructure and the improvement of conditions for landing fish, the development of aquaculture projects, the improvement of control and surveillance at sea - all these were objectives that have either not been achieved or have made little progress over the last two decades. all or almost all of it is simply transferring sums of money in exchange for the right to exploit the resources of the country, which is thus deprived of the surpluses it would obtain if it were itself to exploit these resources, from the outset, at the level of processing and selling fish. the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force. the lack of adequate landing facilities for fish along more than 600 km of the central and southern coast of the country is particularly incomprehensible, which means that a substantial part of the fish caught in mauritania's waters is landed in ports of other countries. the failure of the european union's cooperation policy in this area must be acknowledged and profound changes must be made by involving the mauritanian authorities in the discussion of whether we want genuine and fruitful development cooperation.
mr president, fisheries agreements with third countries must strike the right balance between economic interests and the promotion of sustainable fisheries. this requires that the european union also transfers the good fishing practices it has applied in its waters, thus contributing to the balance of marine ecosystems at a global level. the fisheries agreement with mauritania is particularly important in this context. the creation of jobs, the reduction of poverty levels, the development of support structures for the sector are important objectives to safeguard. the key, however, is to promote sustainable fishing by combating illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and ensuring that the community market is supplied with quality fish. it is not enough, then, for community fishing vessels to adopt practices which respect the environment and the codes of conduct established by the fao. it is essential that the same position be adopted by all those cooperating in the area of the agreement. in this connection, it is urgent to ensure that mauritania requires third countries, with which it also has partnership agreements, to respect the same rules as those applied to community-flagged vessels; otherwise our shipowners will be placed in an unfair competitive disadvantage and the objectives of conservation and sustainable management of fisheries resources will be seriously compromised.
the treaty of lisbon enshrines the objective of territorial cohesion within the european union. this dimension, as well as the economic and social dimension of regional policy, depends on the development of renewed strategies for europe's regions if it is to be effective. for it to succeed, it is necessary to take account of the reality of the regions on the basis of their common specific characteristics and their particular problems. the atlantic region is an area with strong key characteristics for an ambitious strategy. it is, of course, a remote area, with regions where accessibility and connectivity problems are of concern. it has a fragile environment, increasingly weakened by climate change, and a dynamic maritime activity, resulting from the importance of shipping, but also from fishing and energy-related activities. it should be remembered that it is thanks to the atlantic region, and in particular its outermost regions, that the european union has the largest exclusive economic zone in the world. the creation of an integrated strategy for the atlantic region should be supported, provided that it takes due account not only of the important maritime dimension but also of the land dimension. synergies between the various sectoral policies should be created and promoted, thus seeking to achieve added value for the region. the strategy should obviously include all the regions of the atlantic coast, including the outermost regions of macaronesia, i.e. madeira, the azores and the canary islands. there is a need to improve the connectivity of these regions, which, due to their specific geographical and structural characteristics, require optimisation in terms of accessibility and mobility. this will not only help to boost the dynamism and growth of the regions, but also to achieve the objectives of the internal market more effectively. a further word to highlight the need for multi-level governance within this strategy, where it is desirable that the regional and local authorities are called upon to intervene, from the stage of diagnosing the regional reality to the stage of implementing the concrete measures.
it is essential for the european union, as a global player, to have a strategic atlantic orientation which will enable it to develop the full potential of this privileged frontier which links it to such important areas of the world as north america, south america or the whole of western africa. it is in this strategic framework that the creation of a strategy for the atlantic region can really develop its full potential for added value, not only for this region but for the whole european union. only within the framework of a strategic orientation which gives the atlantic a central role can we have an approach to this region which is much less peripheral and much more geocentric in the global context. a strategy for the atlantic region involving member states and their regions should also prioritise new areas of innovation in the economy and science, with a focus on new products and services linked to the environment and renewable and ocean energy, marine biotechnology related to food, health or smart high-tech products and services.
mr president, commissioner, the european union's atlantic strategy achieves a fundamental objective: to deal with europe's oceans and seas in an integrated and articulated way, in a way adapted to their specificities. the atlantic's intercontinental dimension, the diversity of its sea basins and the fact that it is an ultra-deep ocean are distinctive features of the atlantic. these, together with the historical links between the countries and regions bordering the atlantic, are arguments that justify their differentiated approach. its geostrategic position on the border between europe, africa and america creates challenges and opportunities for various levels of maritime activities, such as the protection and safeguarding of ecosystems, maritime safety, the study of climate change, food and energy security and supply, etc. however, it is at deep ocean level that the great wealth of the atlantic in natural, genetic and mineral resources will be rooted. in this context, i believe that, under the european union's atlantic strategy, research, development and technological innovation measures should be implemented to ensure the sustainable exploitation and management of these resources, and that it is necessary to set up a european deep sea observatory in a privileged area such as the azores.

in writing. - the offence of tax evasion is only punishable if the taxpayer knows that it is tax evasion and intends to do so (german penal code and general tax code). in this case, there was clearly no intention to evade tax, since the amount in question was paid in a transparent manner, to the credit of a current account of the member, after having invoiced it to the company speaker's agency. moreover, it is quite common for accidental omissions of declaration of small amounts, such as in this case, to be dealt with in a purely administrative procedure. the fact that this omission was dealt with in such a way that elmar brok was not even directly informed of what he was accused of is completely exceptional. the fact that the public prosecutor has not even quantified the exact amount of the amount due - including interest on late payment - is a reason to justify the existence of a fumus persecutionis even more obvious. in these circumstances, it is inappropriate to waive the member's immunity.

in writing. i shall vote in favour of this report. the proper functioning of the internal market requires safe products and confident consumers. i note that the main concern is to make it safer, but that does not prevent its extension. after a common approach to defining product specifications has been adopted, with progress reflected in the enhancement of general product safety in the internal market, improvements can nevertheless be made, as too many accidents with tragic consequences, particularly with children, still occur in this area. the general product safety directive 2001/95/ec, which sets general product safety requirements, was adopted some 10 years ago and needs to be revised to end the existence of two overlapping levels of divergent market surveillance rules that apply to harmonised goods, whether consumer products or non-consumer products. the relevant legislative framework therefore consists of three elements: new legislative framework, gsp and sectoral harmonisation directives. it is therefore important to harmonize this complexity.
in writing. − the review of directive 2001/95/ec aims to ensure a high level of protection of the health and safety of consumers, with particular attention to the most vulnerable consumers, in particular children and the elderly. the aim is to ensure greater transparency and more active market surveillance and to provide more rapid means of action to remove products considered dangerous from the market. the proper functioning of the internal market requires safe products and informed consumers with the ability to make choices. for these reasons i have supported this report.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential to ensure that all products placed on the community market are safe, ensuring a high level of consumer protection. it is necessary for member states, in collaboration with the european commission, to introduce, in a coordinated manner, fines, including heavy fines, for economic operators who deliberately place dangerous or non-compliant products on the internal market.
in writing. - to ensure consumer confidence, it is essential to have strict rules on the quality of products that are placed on the market and this is where the community rules have been going, and well. but these rules, in my view, must necessarily have two beacons which are nothing more than two sides of the same coin: (i) on the one hand, they must not be more restrictive for european producers than for their international competitors, who, by not complying with the same rules, place their products on the same market; (ii) they must not be so demanding as to compromise economic competitiveness. in taking account of these two barriers, the commission should therefore review the directive on general product safety and market surveillance, paying particular attention to the most vulnerable consumers and, in particular, children. we know that many of the accidents that occur because of unsafe products placed on the market are in large part with children, which requires concrete measures concerning not only the safety of the final product but also its suitability for the intended public.
in writing. - this report deals with the need to revise the directive on general product safety and market surveillance adopted some ten years ago. over the last decade, there has been significant progress in this area in the european union, and everyone recognizes that improvements are possible and desirable within a legislative framework that ensures product safety and at the same time benefits consumers and businesses. first of all, the directive must be brought into line with the new legislative framework. secondly, it is urgent to put an end to the overlapping of certain areas and the exclusion of others from the scope of the general product safety directive (gspd) and the nqf. i agree with the rapporteur that the product safety rules should be updated and harmonized with the nql, so that we can optimise consumer protection - by providing a quality product - and ensure full transparency for producers.
in writing. the report sets out a set of guidelines for the future revision of the directive on general product safety and market surveillance. the aim of achieving a higher level of product safety is underlined, with the need for increased supervision, for which sufficient resources should be allocated to the supervisory authorities to ensure, inter alia, traceability throughout the supply chain. the important issue of the country of origin of the product and the responsible manufacturer - which, in addition to defending the right of consumer information, also defends the industries of the eu countries - is also addressed. we have criticised and denounced the consequences of the development and deepening of the single market for economic and social divergence in the eu. but the concrete proposals put forward in this report - which focus on the interests of consumers - deserve our agreement.
in writing. - despite our opposition to the development of the european internal market, on which the premise of this report is based, the concrete proposals it presents and the central issue it analyses are the improvement of conditions and safety for consumers. the specific objective is to provide guidance for the future revision of the directive on general product safety and market surveillance. the rapporteur attaches great importance to the need for greater supervision in order to achieve a higher level of product safety. it also stresses that sufficient resources should be allocated to the supervisory authorities to ensure traceability throughout the supply chain, given their importance in determining the country of origin of the product and the responsible manufacturer, which in the case of imported products also defends eu industries. that is why we voted in favour.
in writing. − the consolidation of the internal market is essential for the good economic development of the eu. however, this is only possible if safe products are available on the market and consumers have confidence in them. the objective of achieving free movement and the expansion of the variety of products available on the market cannot be dissociated from the corresponding safety of consumers. in recent years, great progress has been made in product safety. however, further progress is needed to improve products, especially those intended for children, who are most likely to be affected when safety rules are not met.
in writing. − this report concerns the revision of the directive on general product safety and market surveillance. in a context of free movement and the constant expansion of the variety of products available on the market, it is essential that we do not lose sight of consumer safety. it is not only the duty of governments but also of companies to ensure that products are safer. legislation at european level has already been successful in strengthening the overall safety of products in the internal market. but improvements can be made, as there are gaps in this area which compromise consumer safety and which could have dire consequences. i voted in favour of this report because i cannot help but agree with the rapporteur's aim of highlighting the importance of revising the current european legislation on product safety so that dangerous products can be identified and withdrawn from the market, for the benefit of the final consumer. i would particularly like to highlight the changes to product safety standards for the most vulnerable consumers in the single market, namely children, the elderly and the disabled.
in writing. − i am voting in favour of this report as i agree that better cooperation is needed in response to pandemics and i agree that a review of the prevention plans established by the eu and by its member states is needed. it is urgent that the who reassess its definition of a pandemic, taking into account not only its geographical spread but also its severity. i think that better management of this case must be achieved by evaluating the recommended vaccination strategies and that this can only work with a better application of the competences of the european centre for disease prevention and control as an independent agent, with the appropriate means at its disposal.
in writing. − influenza a (h1n1) caused by influenza a virus h1n1 was first detected in mexico in late march 2009 and has since spread to several countries. in may 2009, who classified influenza a (h1n1) as moderately severe, and in june 2009 who declared it at alert level 6 corresponding to the pandemic phase. the who's high alert has triggered a series of measures in europe. in some cases very expensive measures (this refers to the estimated costs for the uk of €1.3 billion, in france €990 million, compared with €87 million against seasonal influenza). the response was disproportionate. each member state has reacted on its own, without much coherence or even solidarity. the present report, which i supported, takes the necessary steps by calling for greater coordination between the member states and the european health institutions, as well as clarification and review of the roles and responsibilities of key actors and of the management structures and threats to health at european level. finally, it recognises the need for independent studies by the pharmaceutical industry on vaccines and antiviral medicines, including the monitoring of vaccination coverage.
in writing. − given the response of several eu countries to the possible h1n1 pandemic, i agree that improvements are needed in the formulation of responses based on the scientific information available in this type of situation. i therefore support a review of the action and prevention plans in the event of a pandemic risk. these reviews should aim at enhanced cooperation and coordination between the health authorities of the member states and the european institutions. another aspect which i consider extremely important is the transparency required both in the medical products used and in the scientific reports provided by the health authorities, in order to prevent conflicts of interest and to ensure the safety and information of citizens.
in writing. − the eu was the region in the world with the best preparedness and capacity to respond to this outbreak, although considerable differences in member states' preparedness and the lack of genuine cooperation between them led to a weakening. preparedness and response to health risks in the eu is a responsibility of member states, but it is essential to improve cooperation and coordination between them and international and regional institutions and organisations, in particular in the early stages of a viral outbreak, in order to assess its severity and to be able to take the relevant management decisions and a coherent approach. the divergent recommendations made in the eu and in the member states regarding the priority target groups for vaccination highlight the enormous uncertainty and divergent views that have persisted around the appropriate response. the costs, which are quite significant, could also have been reduced by increased cooperation between member states and between them and the ecdc/cepcd. i support the need to create a european code of conduct for the exercise of the scientific expert function in any european authority responsible for safety, risk management and anticipation, in order to prevent further cases of corruption.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'management of h1n1 influenza' because it stresses the importance of enhancing cooperation, independence and transparency in the management of future pandemic crises, in particular through better application of the competences of the european centre for disease prevention and control as an independent agency.
in writing. − in 2009, the world was gripped by fear of a virus with great pandemic potential and possibly lethal: "gripe a". fortunately, the greatest fears about the morbidity and mortality associated with the h1n1 virus were not confirmed. in europe, this virus was responsible for 2,900 deaths, far fewer than the number of deaths caused by seasonal influenza. however, following the warnings of the who and fear, exceptional measures were taken by the states, such as mass vaccination, which represented a substantial expense for health systems. it is important to draw conclusions from the management of influenza a, rather than pointing out errors. the first of these, in my view, is that it is still better to sin in excess than in absence. second, we must learn lessons for managing future pandemics, which may prove to be more aggressive, and understand how and when to act and what measures to take.
in writing. − fortunately, according to data provided by the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc), the h1n1 influenza virus has caused fewer deaths than initially expected and is now considered a disease of low severity in the eu. at the beginning of its spread, a certain alarm was created, which led several member states to make huge investments in vaccination programmes that proved to be excessive, since in countries such as poland, which did not take any exceptional measures, the mortality rate remained at the level of countries that carried out national vaccination campaigns with costs estimated at many millions of euros. according to this report, the vaccine procurement policies adopted were the direct consequence of latent contracts concluded since 2007 with pharmaceutical companies. there is a lack of transparency in this process because of the unacceptable dependence of the member states on pharmaceutical companies. i cannot therefore agree with the rapporteur but hope that her recommendations, particularly on information security and the precautionary principle - which must benefit patients and not companies - will be taken into account by the commission and all the member states.
in writing. - in the face of the difficult management of the declared pandemic of influenza a (h1n1) and the known numbers (2900 deaths as a result of h1n1 influenza when the seasonal flu originated in the same year 40 000), the report continues its efforts to demand transparency, which we find commendable. both in terms of what has happened - with full clarification of the procedures adopted and responsibilities - and in terms of how to deal with future situations. this includes: the issue of the procurement of vaccines and antiviral treatments; information on recorded cases and their severity; the granting of access to clinical trial documents, research protocols and adverse drug reactions (by the european medicines agency); and conflicts of interest among experts advising european public health authorities. the report calls for the prevention plans established in the eu and the member states to be reviewed in order to gain effectiveness and coherence, autonomy and flexibility. it also recommended that cooperation between member states in this area be strengthened, both in the definition of the severity of viral outbreaks and in decision-making. we consider it to be a positive overall approach and have therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. − in this phase of evaluating the management of the h1n1 influenza outbreak, lessons must be learned and the need for countries to have public health systems and public health outreach services that can intervene in a number of areas, including:- the development and evaluation of scientific studies, independent of the pharmaceutical industry, on the efficacy, safety and risk-benefit ratio of vaccines and antiviral medicines and on recommended target groups;- the evaluation of information on recommended medication in case of health emergencies, especially in pandemic situations;- the strengthening of capacity in terms of risk management and anticipation and the level of r&d in these areas, as well as in matters of preventive public health measures. cooperation between the different national services and between them and the relevant international and regional institutions and organisations also needs to be strengthened.
in writing. − the management of h1n1 in the eu has revealed a number of difficulties, including its actual severity and scale, the response by states, disproportionate size and very high costs when compared to the annual deaths from normal influenza and the amounts spent by member states to combat it. the analysis of the management of h1n1 influenza in europe highlights a fundamental problem: a lack of independent assessment by national and/or european health authorities and the consequent inability to adapt public health measures as closely as possible and in real time to the actual clinical and epidemiological statistics available. therefore, changes in the management of future pandemics are needed to avoid widespread public panic and unnecessary costs.
in writing. − the report on the management of h1n1 influenza in 2009-2010 in the eu highlights the low statistical severity of the disease in the european area (at the human level, each person who dies is an irreplaceable loss). the european centre for disease prevention and control reports 2,900 deaths in europe from h1n1 infection in 2009. this figure is lower than the official estimates of the european commission for the number of deaths due exclusively to seasonal influenza. the number of deaths is also well below the most optimistic forecasts of the health services of the eu member states. the costs to member states and the european institutions of accepting the maximum alert level as proposed by the who have resulted in a costly set of measures that are disproportionate to the severity of h1n1 influenza. but in view of the who recommendation, i do not think that any other course of action could have been taken. however, this case needs to be reflected on and i agree with the rapporteur when she points out that the eu needs greater cooperation between its member states, more independence and more transparency, particularly in assessing the cost-benefit of these measures of great financial impact.

in writing. the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) was established in 1949 by an international agreement. its area of competence covers the mediterranean, the black sea and adjacent waters, the promotion of the development, conservation and management of marine biological resources, the formulation and recommendation of conservation measures and the promotion of cooperation projects in the field of training. the aim of this proposal for a regulation is simply to transpose some recommendations adopted by the gfcm and already operational in the gfcm countries into a single community legislative act, to which future recommendations may be added by amendment.
in writing. - i am in favour of this report because it is intended to trigger a new taxation process in the financial sector, which is an urgent measure in itself and also a complement to the recently adopted regulatory and supervisory instruments. in this area, i would stress that 'the taxable base for the financial transaction tax should be as broad as possible', as the document suggests, so as to include all types of transaction. among other benefits, an itf makes the market fairer and more transparent, reduces speculation and tax evasion levels, and distributes the burden of the crisis among financial actors. the additional resources from this measure should help to fight poverty, promote job creation, finance the welfare state, achieve climate and environmental objectives and finance others stemming from the europe 2020 strategy. i, for my part, support the need for the commission to study a future system of eurobonds and the issuing of common european project bonds as measures to stimulate investment. i also support the polluter pays principle. finally, we cannot neglect development aid, and it is important to keep the commitment to allocate 0.7% of each member state's gnp to oda.
