in writing. - at the time of the vote on this resolution it is not yet clear what will be the outcome of the revolutions throughout the mediterranean which have sought to overthrow long-standing authoritarian regimes. in the libyan case, there are conflicting reports about the successes and failures of the rebels and the forces still supporting the dictatorial regime of gaddafi, and it seems that we are facing a case of real civil war. however, there are multiple sources denouncing the brutal violence and unprecedented repression by the libyan regime and the very high number of victims it has caused. the united nations itself has rightly condemned the atrocities committed. it is now clear that the people who are in revolt do not want to live under regimes which do not respect their rights and which do not ensure respect for the rules of democracy and the rule of law. the european union cannot remain indifferent to what is happening. it must demand an end to violence, persevere in condemning and sanctioning those responsible for it, support those who fight for our common values and seek to show solidarity, to follow and better understand the aspirations, desires and trends of movements that are seeking change.
in writing. - this resolution is worrying and unacceptable. in particular, in the context of the latest events in libya, the need for a peaceful and political solution to the conflict, without external interference, is more urgent than ever. in the face of the dangerous and serious accumulation of actions which, instead of contributing to the reduction of tension, are aimed at the preparation of acts of aggression by the usa and nato against libya, the majority of the european parliament is condoning acts of interference, aggression or occupation of libya. any aggression against this country, whatever the pretext and mandate, would have grave consequences for a people already living in a situation of deep tension and insecurity. it would be deeply damaging to all those in libya who are continuing to fight for their rights, democracy, sovereignty and peace and would introduce serious factors of instability and conflict into the region. any military aggression against libya - inseparable from the objectives of controlling libya's natural resources - will be directed not only against the libyan people but against all the peoples of the region who have risen up and continue to fight for their social and political rights, for freedom, for democracy and for the real sovereignty and independence of their countries.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which describes the serious situation in iran, denounces the repressive practices and systematic violations of human rights perpetrated by the iranian authorities and stresses the need to pursue a diplomatic solution to the nuclear issue. i join in particular in expressing solidarity with the iranian people who, following the 2009 presidential elections, have legitimately called for democratic change in their country.
in writing. - i unconditionally support this joint resolution, stressing the importance of the issues discussed with regard to the rights of persons belonging to minorities, the promotion of the defence of human rights and fundamental freedoms, as well as the rights of children, while combating terrorism. i draw attention to the conclusions agreeing that the eu should strengthen its practice of speaking with one voice as it would increase its visibility and influence as a global actor, and that delegations in geneva and new york should increase the coherence, visibility and credibility of eu action at the unhrc. i agree with the resolution that calls on member states to encourage the unhrc to give equal attention to discrimination based on all principles, including gender, race, age, sexual orientation, religion or belief. i also agree with the reform which stresses the need for the unhrc to be more active as a warning and preventive mechanism, by maintaining the special procedures and preserving the independence of the office of the high commissioner for human rights, as well as the funding needed to maintain its regional offices.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i consider that the agenda of the 16th regular session of the human rights council contains important topics of particular urgency. the importance of the agenda, which includes reports on the rights of persons belonging to national or ethnic, religious and linguistic minorities, on the promotion and protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the fight against terrorism, and numerous meetings on the rights of the child, should be underlined.
in writing. − the 16th session of the united nations human rights council will take place at a particularly troubled historical period which calls into question its own composition, since some of its members are far from fulfilling the precept of the universal declaration of human rights and promoting and protecting human rights as their mission should be. the european union must actively participate in this session and do everything possible to ensure that its universalist vision of human rights based on the dignity of the human person is increasingly widely outlined and effectively applied in all countries of the world. the appointment of a european high level representative for human rights could contribute to the increased visibility of the union's positions and the persistence of the strategy of one message with several voices by the member states in the council and has the potential to continue to build support for european positions.
in writing. - the european parliament has long accustomed us to a policy of double standards in human rights matters. the restrictive and instrumental view they have of the declaration adopted by the united nations general assembly in 1948: the universal declaration of human rights, is also well known. once again, the selective way in which various states are referred to is evident in this report. the countries with which the eu has economic and diplomatic relations and which it attaches strategic importance to because they serve its strategic interests, despite the fact that they are experiencing serious human rights violations, are omitted. these are the examples of israel, colombia or morocco, just to name three, on different continents. we do not have a restrictive view of human rights. we take seriously all the contents of the declaration, which we consider to be the inspiration for our political intervention. finally, we do not accept the european union's claim to a permanent seat in the un general assembly for the simple reason that this would not make sense in the light of the spirit and principles of the organization, as contained in the charter of the united nations. the un is and must remain an organization of independent and sovereign states.
in writing. - the selective nature of the states criticised in this report and the instrumental nature of this debate are clear. the hypocritical use of this report is evident in that it does not criticise countries with which the eu has good economic and diplomatic relations and which are of strategic importance, despite the fact that human rights violations are taking place in them, such as colombia and honduras. nor is there any demand for an end to morocco's occupation of western sahara or of palestine by israel. another point which we cannot support is the claim of the european union for a permanent seat in the un general assembly, because the un is an organization of sovereign and independent states, whereas the european union is not a state within the meaning of the united nations charter. the defence of human rights - including their indivisibility and non-hierarchization - and their consideration as an indispensable condition for respect for the rights of peoples and for true social justice, peace, freedom and democracy, are a cornerstone of our political action. they count on us to defend human rights, not to exercise hypocrisy.
in writing. - in the troubled times we are facing today, particularly in the regions of north africa, this 16th session of the human rights council is of paramount importance. the european union will therefore have to play a very active part in this session and make every effort to ensure that its universalist approach to human rights, based on respect for the dignity of the human person, is followed by all countries in the world. it is also important for the eu to appoint a high-level european human rights representative so that its vision of the defence of human rights is increasingly widely spread.
in writing. − respect for, promotion of and safeguarding the universality of human rights are part of the eu's legal and ethical acquis and constitute one of the foundations of european unity and integrity. every effort should therefore be made to make the eu and its member states' action in this area more visible and effective, and it is important to ensure their active and committed participation in this important 16th session of the human rights council (unhrc) as well as in the unhrc review process to be held in 2011.

in writing. - i approve this report because the european council's proposal for the creation of a permanent stability mechanism would create an intergovernmental procedure outside the eu sphere, which would be a dangerous precedent. the european institutions, in particular the european commission and the parliament, should be an integral part of this council (the commission as a member and not an observer). the european parliament is an important democratic watchdog and the council should consider the s&d group's proposal for a possible commitment to involve the ep in the operational components of the mechanism. in this connection, i would stress the idea in the report that 'the mechanism must not give rise to a new model of european governance which does not meet the democratic standards achieved in the union'. moreover, the stability mechanism should be seen as only one part of the framework of solutions for european economic governance. for example, the commission should investigate the potential of a future eurobond system.

in writing. - i support the report by mr brok and mr gualtieri, who acknowledge the need to make it possible, within the institutional framework of the union, to create a stability mechanism for the member states whose currency is the euro. practice has shown that more economic governance is needed in the eu, with consequences for economic and financial policies and allowing for greater budgetary discipline. the report rightly stresses that temporary measures are insufficient and that any attempt to create a system outside the eu's institutional framework is a threat to the community project and, for this reason too, rightly calls for a more relevant role for the european commission. i also agree with the invitation to the commission to present the legislative initiatives that may prove necessary to strengthen financial stability and sustainable economic growth.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the amendment of the treaty on the functioning of the european union as regards the stability mechanism for member states whose currency is the euro, as this is essential to stabilise the euro area in the long term, limit speculation against european countries and protect citizens. despite the intergovernmental nature of this mechanism, i welcome the strengthening of the community method and the role of the european institutions, in particular the commission and the european parliament, in the economic governance of the eu.
in writing. - in exceptional moments in the life of states and organisations, such as the one we are now experiencing, it is the duty of all of us to find adequate and ambitious answers to the challenges facing us. the debt crisis facing europe requires exceptional measures and the maturity needed to find in our institutional structure the way to mechanisms that will give the euro the necessary stability and robustness, firmly anchored in budgetary discipline, coordination of macroeconomic policies and the existence of sustainable growth policies. while i support regulatory stability, it is because we are living in an exceptional moment that i support the amendment to article 136 tfeu now proposed, insofar as it allows the creation of a permanent mechanism for safeguarding the stability of the eurozone, as proposed in report a7-0282/2010, approved by this plenary on 20 october 2010.
in writing. − the european union must strengthen its economic governance, which can only be achieved through the community method, with the commission taking the lead, rather than the intergovernmental method. i hope that the strengthening of the jcp, the european semester, the europe 2020 strategy and the amendment of article 136 tfeu on a stability mechanism will lead to sustainable economic growth. the functioning of this mechanism should respect the essential principles of democratic decision-making such as transparency, parliamentary control and democratic accountability. this mechanism is an important element of an overall package of measures designed to define a new framework to strengthen budgetary discipline and the coordination of the economic and financial policies of the member states, which should include promoting a joint european response to the challenges posed by growth and at the same time overcoming economic and social imbalances and improving competitiveness. i voted in favour of the creation of this mechanism in the hope that it will make a valuable contribution to bringing greater stability to financial markets and to sustainable economic growth.

in writing. the european council in brussels on 14 and 15 december called on the commission to take all necessary steps to ensure that the euro is not used as a bargaining chip in the world economy. in a less serious situation, i would not agree with the proposed amendment to the treaty of lisbon, which has only recently come into force. at this point, it is essential to go beyond temporary measures to stabilise the euro area and the eu must undoubtedly strengthen the means of combating the sovereign debt crisis. in this sense, the amendment of article 136 tfeu is essential for the creation of a permanent european stability mechanism that is effective in helping member states in difficulty.
in writing. − strengthening economic governance in the eu has become a priority, especially in the current international economic context. indeed, when the treaty of lisbon entered into force on 1 december 2009, there was no expectation that it would be amended in the near future. however, the exceptional circumstances of a financial, economic and social nature, which are already well known, have led to this amendment, which has the support of a majority of the political groups. i cannot, however, fail to stress that this simplified revision process should not set precedents for future constitutional revisions in which there are no truly exceptional circumstances such as those we are currently experiencing. in agreeing with the need for a concerted and coherent economic and financial policy among the euro area member states, which can ensure the cohesion and stability of the euro area, i voted in favour of this report which seeks to amend article 136 tfeu and thereby institutionalize a permanent european financial stability mechanism with the aim of ensuring stability and financial assistance under certain conditions, in particular a rigorous analysis and the implementation of an economic and financial recovery programme.
in writing. the sovereignty crisis affecting the member states is forcing the european union to rethink its economic strategy. the economic governance of the union is gradually becoming a reality. there is a need for a concerted and coherent economic and financial policy among the euro-zone member states, a genuine 'euro pact'. in this way, and in order to ensure the cohesion and stability of the euro area, this report seeks to amend article 136 tfeu and thus institutionalize a permanent european financial stability mechanism with the aim of ensuring stability and financial assistance, subject to certain conditions, including rigorous analysis and the implementation of an economic and financial recovery programme. i am voting in favour of this amendment because i believe it is essential to institutionalize and at the same time make the european mechanism more flexible. i would like to stress, however, that the commission must take account of the powers of the european institutions and that an institutional framework should not be created apart from them. the current situation requires that serious and real action be taken by the member states, and in particular by the euro-zone countries. however, i would stress that this simplified revision process should not set precedents for future constitutional revisions.

in writing. other the european union has in the recent past negotiated and concluded several agreements with other states in the field of air transport. the court of justice held that the traditional designation clauses in existing bilateral agreements infringed european law by discriminating against eu air carriers established in one member state but owned and controlled by nationals of other member states. since such agreements violate the principle of freedom of establishment, as laid down in article 49 tfeu, the european commission has initiated and has been developing a practice of negotiating and concluding agreements between the european union, on the one hand, and third states, on the other, in the field of air transport. the main elements of these agreements are safety concerns, passenger rights, mutual recognition of certificates and regulatory cooperation. in this context, i would like to recall the limited role that parliament has in these matters. with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, its opinion is binding, but only on the final text already signed, and this house cannot make suggestions or amendments to its content.

in writing. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a regulation on the application of the principle of equal treatment for men and women in matters of social security. although the community executive says that the level of increase does not destabilise the eu wine industry, in doubt, and in defence of the interests of portuguese agriculture, we abstained from voting. moldova has requested the european commission to increase the duty-free tariff quota for wine under the autonomous trade preferences granted to the country in a 2008 regulation. in order to support moldova's economic recovery and provide a positive outlook for those working in the wine industry in the country (a quarter of the working population), they propose to increase the duty-free tariff quota for wine from 100 000 to 150 000 hectolitres in 2011; from 120 000 to 180 000 hectolitres in 2012; and from 2013 onwards to 240 000 hectolitres per year. the commission states the following: 'as overall moldovan imports represent only 0.04% of all eu imports, further market opening should not create any negative effects for the eu. at present, about 90% of all imports from moldova... (parliament adopted the legislative resolution)
in writing. − moldova has been making efforts over the past few years to increasingly converge with european benchmarks of freedom, democracy and good governance. the efforts outlined here have been consistent and have demonstrated that moldova is concerned about continuing its path towards possible enlargement. thus, in order to support the economic recovery of moldova and to provide a positive outlook for the people working in the wine industry in the country (a quarter of the working population), it is proposed to increase the duty-free tariff quota for wine from 100000 hectolitres (hl) in 2011 to 150000 hl in 2012, from 120000 hl to 180000 hl and from 2013 onwards to 240000 hl per year. the amendments to this regulation are designed to do just that and can help the moldovan economy and its development.
in writing. - as i have already had the opportunity to mention earlier, it is essential for the eu to have a coherent and effective european neighbourhood policy. as part of that neighbourhood policy, regulation (ec) no 55/2008 introduces a specific autonomous trade preference regime for the republic of moldova, under which free access to the eu market is granted to all products originating in moldova, with the exception of certain agricultural products listed in its annex, for which limited concessions have been granted, either in the form of exemption from customs duties within the limits of tariff quotas or in the form of reduction of customs duties. one of the exceptions to free movement concerns the wine sector, and a tariff quota has been established which, according to the available data, has been fully used months before the end of the year. as the moldovan economy is being strongly affected by the negative effects of the global financial and economic crises and as the wine sector employs some 300 000 workers, this report, which i voted for, proposes to increase the current tariff quota for wine in order to support moldova's efforts and to provide an attractive and reliable market for its wine exports, which, incidentally, do not compete with portuguese production.
in writing. − in order to support moldova's economic recovery efforts and to encourage the momentum towards convergence with eu legislation and standards, the commission has put forward a proposal to increase the tariff quota for moldovan wine. the commission believes that this measure will not have a negative impact on the european wine industry, which is why i have supported the granting of this aid to moldova.
in writing. − i approve this report given the changes that have been introduced to extend the validity of the current system - generalised system of preferences (gsp) - until december 2013, taking into account the uncertainties as to the time needed to complete the current legislative process. the adoption of this report thus avoids a break in the legal coverage of the gsp and avoids disparities in treatment between nations.
in writing. the current regulation establishing the generalised system of preferences (gsp) expires at the end of this year. however, as the european commission is still awaiting the completion of a study on the subject in order to submit a new proposal for the gsp, in order to avoid a legal vacuum, it was decided to extend the current regulation and its current provisions for another two years. however, the commission should present a legislative initiative on this very soon, as there is an urgent need to review the current system and make it more effective. i therefore subscribe to the main points, which the rapporteur has made, that need to be reviewed in this legislative proposal to be put forward by the commission. these are an effective system which better meets the interests of the beneficiary countries and economic operators, rules which provide for a reform process in which the participation of the beneficiaries is guaranteed and also that the democratic control task which parliament is called upon to perform is ensured.
in writing. the united nations conference on trade and development (unctad) recommended in 1968 the creation of a generalised system of preferences (gsp) with the aim of the more developed countries supporting the developing countries by granting trade facilities. in 1971 the european community pioneered the implementation of a gsp which has become one of the main methods of cooperation with developing countries in international trade to combat poverty. the current regulation needs updating, due to its obsolescence and lack of a framework in the lisbon treaty, and substantial reform. although this proposal is not yet a new regulation (which needs to be drawn up) and given the urgency of its adoption, i agree with the report under discussion and hope that the commission will come forward as soon as possible with a new proposal so that the eu can continue to support developing countries.
in writing. − the generalised system of preferences is a trade mechanism through which the eu grants developing countries non-reciprocal preferential access to its market through tariff reductions. the mechanism is defined as a development aid instrument and is not without contradictions, in particular between some of its declared aims and the practical results achieved. indeed, many developing countries have been increasing their economic dependence and shaping their economies on a model of low diversification based on a narrow range of export products, to the detriment of the development of their internal market. an international division of labour has been consolidated, which is unfavourable to these countries, and the big multinationals, some of them european, are often the ones who benefit most from this system. a comprehensive review of this mechanism is therefore required, accompanied by an in-depth debate on its various aspects and complexities and on its impacts, not only in developing countries but also in eu member states, especially the most fragile ones. however, given the delay in the commission's submission of a new proposal for a regulation, which makes it impossible for it to enter into force immediately after the expiry of the current regulation, an extension of the current regulation is necessary. (parliament adopted the legislative resolution)
in writing. the current gsp expires at the end of this year, so at this stage it is only a matter of voting on the extension needed to ensure legal certainty and to guarantee the mutual interests of the 150 or so countries involved. however, the importance of this subject, both for developing countries and for the member states of the european union with weaker economies whose industrial, agricultural or social interests are not always safeguarded in the international trade agreements promoted by the european commission, requires that a thorough debate be held on the new regulation, the proposal for which should be sent as soon as possible by the european commission, so that the various aspects and the whole complexity of the gsp can be properly analysed, as well as its impact on the various areas and countries.
in writing. the current regulation on generalised tariff preferences expires at the end of this year. in the absence of a new regulation in due time, due to the delay in the delivery of the study requested by the commission, we are obliged to extend the current regulation for another two years. however, given the importance of this regulation for the regulation of trade between developing countries and the eu, it is necessary for the commission to present a new updated version of it quickly.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 732/2008 establishes a scheme of generalised preferences (gsp) which is valid until 31 december 2011. the gsp has been one of the eu's main trade and development policy instruments to help developing countries reduce poverty by generating revenues through international trade. the ep consultation process on the last gsp was very limited and did not allow for a broad negotiation. parliament has pointed out in due course that it will need more time in the future to carry out its duties. on 26 may 2010, the commission, citing a lack of time to present a new regulation, only proposed to extend the validity of the current regulation. this proposal for an extension did not take into account the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. the ep noted this shortcoming and proposed amendments to the commission proposal to ensure that the rights and powers which the ep acquired under the lisbon treaty are respected. in this connection, i voted in favour of this report, which approves the extension of the regulation and which amends the elements necessary to respect the new powers acquired by the ep after the treaty of lisbon, in particular to ensure the new powers on delegated acts.
in writing. since 1971, the european union has been granting trade preferences to developing countries under its generalised system of preferences (gsp). the gsp is implemented through successive regulations applying a system of generalised tariff preferences for a period, generally three years at a time. the current system was established by regulation (ec) no 732/2008 and applies until 31 december 2011 and its replacement by a new regulation is being prepared. the period of application of regulation (ec) no 732/2008 is insufficient to allow for the preparation of a commission proposal and the subsequent adoption of a new regulation by the ordinary legislative procedure and, therefore, in order to ensure the continuity of the system, it is necessary to extend the period of application of that regulation until 31 december 2013. i voted in favour, in the expectation that the commission will soon present a new proposal which will help to make the gsp a clearer, more transparent and more effective system.

in writing. − following the 2002 judgment of the court of justice of the european union which found that the traditional designation clauses included in bilateral air service agreements concluded by member states infringe union law, it became necessary to negotiate an agreement aimed at replacing certain provisions of the current 17 bilateral air service agreements between member states and vietnam. those clauses infringed article 49 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which guarantees nationals of member states exercising their freedom of establishment the same treatment in the host member state as that accorded to nationals of that member state. in this context, in order to avoid such discrimination between eu air carriers, the traditional designation clauses for air carriers of the member state party to the bilateral agreement are replaced by an eu designation clause applicable to all eu carriers. the aim is to grant all eu air carriers non-discriminatory access to routes between the eu and vietnam. in view of all this, i voted in favour of this report, which also received the favourable opinion of the tran committee.

in writing. - negotiations between the european union and the gulf cooperation council have been going on for more than two decades in an attempt to negotiate a free trade agreement. they are thus one of the oldest trade negotiations launched by the union, which so far have remained inconclusive. in the last 20 years, the context of these negotiations has changed profoundly. the gcc states have a significant financial leverage in sovereign wealth funds, which reached over usd 1 380 billion in 2009, or over 35% of the world's volume. the gcc member states have become the economic engine of the entire middle east/north africa region, accounting for more than 40% of the national wealth produced in this area and holding 50% of official foreign exchange reserves, i.e. usd 1 070 billion. in view of the great financial and economic potential of these countries, we must take advantage of the present situation if the negotiations are to be successful.

in writing. − this proposal aims to address the concerns expressed in the stockholm programme to create flexible immigration policies to support the eu's economic development and performance. it aims to simplify and harmonise the rules currently in force in the member states by creating a single application procedure leading to a combined residence and work permit. it should contribute to improving the effectiveness of this procedure and bring clear benefits both for employers and for third-country nationals wishing to immigrate to the territory of the member states. it will ensure that these migrants have rights and obligations comparable to those of eu citizens in terms of working conditions, education and training, recognition of qualifications, social benefits, etc. at the same time it allows for easier control of the legality of their residence and employment. i therefore voted in favour of the excellent report presented to us by my colleague, mrs véronique mathieu.

in writing. - this report addresses a subject which is increasingly urgent for discussion. in fact, the expected reduction in europeans with an active contributory status requires europe to open its borders to the entry of third country nationals to reside and work here, or else the current social security systems will fail. in 2004, the 'hague programme', alongside the need to combat illegal migration, recognised that legal migration would play a key role in the economic development of the european union. the stockholm programme, adopted by the european council on 10 and 11 december 2009, provides that labour migration can increase the competitiveness and vitality of the economy. i therefore agree with the position expressed in this report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the regulatory amendment to implement a single procedure for the granting of authorization to third-country nationals legally resident in a member state, taking into account the demographic challenges that europe is beginning to face. it is also a more efficient and economical simplification process.
in writing. - the proposal for a directive on the single application procedure for the granting of a single authorization for third-country nationals to reside and work in the territory of a member state, while claiming to improve the situation of workers from these countries, may in fact represent an attack on workers' rights in general. we must not forget that the proposal has its origins in the principle of the country of origin, established by the infamous bolkestein directive, which has increased inequalities between workers, particularly in terms of pay, and has ended up being harmful to all workers by the pressure it introduces towards a lower level of working conditions. by seeking to introduce disparities and differences in treatment between european workers and workers from third countries, the proposed directive increases the segregation of immigrant workers and further weakens the situation of all workers, forcing greater precariousness. we are faced with an attempt to promote social dumping. we believe that the rights of all workers, including immigrants, seasonal workers and posted workers, must be strengthened. we therefore regret that after the lead of the first version of this report, heavy measures are being insisted upon... in writing. - the adoption of the directive on the single application procedure for the granting of a single authorisation for third-country nationals to reside and work in the territory of a member state may represent an attack on workers' rights in general. the proposal has its genesis in the bolkestein directive, which introduced the principle of country of origin, encouraging the increase of differences between workers, particularly in terms of pay, and causing a penalising effect for all workers. by seeking to create disparities between european workers and workers from third countries, it increases segregation vis-à-vis immigrant workers, accentuating differences in treatment and further undermining their living conditions through the weakness and precariousness of their working conditions. this proposal for a directive may be promoting social dumping and increasing precariousness in industrial relations. what is needed is to strengthen the rights of all workers, including immigrants, seasonal workers and posted workers. however, the struggle of workers in various european countries (notably in portugal) made it possible for the proposal for a directive to be rejected at the last plenary session of 2010. we regret the insistence on heavy measures... (parliament adopted the legislative resolution)
in writing. - with the adoption of this proposal for a directive, immigrant workers will have the same rights as national workers as regards at least pay and dismissal, health and safety at work, working time and holidays. the proposal aims to establish a 'single residence and work permit' procedure for legal immigrants and to give them a common set of rights throughout the eu. this simplifies the procedures for national authorities to issue a 'single residence and work permit' to legal immigrants, so that they enjoy a set of rights equivalent to those of workers in the member state in which they reside. however, the admission of immigrants for the purpose of work, including the volume of admissions, should remain a matter for each member state.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this legislative resolution of the european parliament on a proposal for a european parliament and council directive on a single application procedure for the granting of a single authorisation for third-country nationals to reside and work in the territory of a member state and on a common set of rights for third-country workers legally resident in a member state. this is a subject which is becoming increasingly relevant in the current economic and social context. indeed, one of the best ways to combat irregular immigration and illegal work is to develop balanced legal migration channels, which respond to the needs of our labour markets as well as to the social requirements of good integration into the host society.

in writing. − the aim of this report is to create a single residence and work document for third-country nationals in a member state, thus making the admission process faster and more uniform, while reducing the bureaucratic and financial burden of the process. economic migration is now a reality which must be analysed with a view to developing legal and balanced immigration channels which can meet the needs of european labour markets. the economic and demographic challenges facing europe require a common immigration policy to be devised among the 27 member states. the entry into force of the lisbon treaty has established a new legal basis in this area, the codecision procedure, and i therefore consider it essential to establish a common and harmonised approach in order to reduce the differences between national legislation. in addition to the above, the proposal also provides for equal treatment of national workers, creating a secure and protective legal status, since immigrants participate in the economic activity of the host country. decisions not to grant aid shall be duly justified and transparent and the costs incurred shall be proportionate to the services actually provided.
in writing. − in october 2008, the european commission presented a proposal for a directive which aims to bring together in a single text the consumer protection acquis, which covers four directives (on unfair contract terms, on certain aspects of the sale and guarantee of consumer goods, on consumer protection in distance sales and on consumer protection in out-of-commerce contracts). it should be noted that these revised directives contained minimum harmonisation clauses, which led many member states to maintain or adopt stricter consumer protection rules, creating a fragmented regulatory framework throughout the community with consequences for the internal market, in particular for businesses and consumers in cross-border transactions. i believe that this legislative text, which was voted on today, strengthens consumer protection while taking account of the specificities of sectors where full harmonization would not always be feasible. i welcome the proposal to set up a system of mutual evaluation, which would require member states to indicate in detail why different national provisions are necessary and to what extent they respect the principles of proportionality and effectiveness.
in writing. - consumer law is one of the main pillars of the internal market. their protection and security are fundamental to greater security in the conduct of the day-to-day procurement of goods for cross-border trade and, consequently, for the competitiveness of businesses. in this respect, a balance between consumer rights and the cost to businesses is essential. furthermore, it is necessary to take account of the various national particularities and the protection offered, with due regard for the principle of subsidiarity. i therefore believe that this is an area where, on the one hand, maximum harmonization may be useful, but on the other hand, minimum harmonization may also be adopted depending on the type of contract, because it is more appropriate.
in writing. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of consumers in respect of the use of certain dangerous substances. it aims to ensure that consumers in all 27 member states have confidence in a high level of consumer protection and that businesses, large and small, can supply goods and services to consumers in all 27 member states of the union without unnecessary legal obstacles. the proposal aims to ensure that consumers, wherever they shop in the eu, have clear information on prices and surcharges before they sign a contract. it strengthens consumer protection against late or non-delivered goods by giving them rights in respect of cooling-off periods, returns, refunds, reparations, guarantees and unfair contractual terms. the trader is obliged, in relation to all contracts concluded with consumers, to provide clear information enabling an informed choice to be made. i welcome the exemption from the information requirements for contracts which involve 'daily transactions and in which the trader has to supply the good or service immediately after the conclusion of the contract', which avoids an unnecessary administrative burden.
in writing. - another commission proposal in which the promotion of crossborder trade appears as the central motivation for the exercise of the power of legislative initiative. in this case, and because we are faced with an unoriginal proposal for 'consumer protection', the argument is again made that free competition is the alpha and omega of consumer protection, and once again and forever a profession of faith in the virtues of the free market is made. in fact, it is more about the rights (and interests) of companies than about the rights of consumers. the european commission advocates full harmonisation of the rules laid down for consumers. this harmonization, if not made by progress and taking into account the legislation already in place in each country, could in practice lead to the loss of consumer rights in some member states where legislation in this area is more advanced. as this is a first reading, and as it has already been possible, in the course of the debate so far in the committee, to improve the commission's initial proposal, we hope that it will be possible to go even further in defending the rights of consumers.
in writing. - we are at the first reading stage of the european commission's proposal for a directive on consumer rights, which focuses on promoting crossborder trade, always starting from the principle that free competition is what best serves consumer rights, but in fact paying more attention to business rights than consumer rights. the european commission also advocates full harmonisation of consumer rules, without taking into account existing legislation in each country, which could lead to the loss of consumer rights in some member states. however, in the parliament's committee on internal trade there was an intense debate and a broad consensus was reached which made it possible to significantly amend the initial proposal submitted by the european commission. however, there seems to be room to go further in defending consumer rights and to try to influence the negotiations with the council in a positive way. we have therefore agreed to the rapporteur's request to refer this report back to the committee on the internal market of the european parliament.
in writing. the proposal aims to replace four directives currently in force on out-of-commerce contracts, unfair terms, distance contracts and the sale and guarantee of consumer goods by merging them into a single legislative act. the purpose of this proposal for a directive is to increase consumer confidence and protection when shopping in stores or on the internet and to reduce the reluctance of companies to sell in other countries. the proposal for a directive on consumer rights aims to ensure that, wherever they shop in the eu, consumers have clear information on prices and surcharges before they sign a contract. in general, all contracts are covered, i.e. whether purchases are made in a shop, at a distance or outside commercial establishments. this directive is intended to strengthen the internal market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the idea of codifying consumer rights in a single act. the reduction of barriers to crossborder trade is to be noted and the attempt to make the internal market more efficient and to promote crossborder trade by combining the four directives now consolidated into one is to be commended. the proposed directive still contains aspects which can and should be improved, but it is still a very positive step forward in this area.
in writing. − the european commission wants to simplify and complete the regulatory framework on consumer rights and therefore proposes to merge the four existing directives into a single legislative instrument. this proposal requires, on the one hand, that consumers in the 27 member states be given a high level of confidence in the protection of their rights and, on the other hand, that suppliers of goods and services reduce legal and administrative obstacles when selling across borders. the adoption of this report is another step towards the full completion of the internal market, as the existing legal fragmentation is a deterrent for both consumers and businesses when they wish to carry out cross-border trade. the content of the proposal allows for full harmonisation aimed at out-of-business and distance contracts, in particular online transactions. at the same time, the rapporteur includes flexibility clauses which allow member states to maintain a high level of consumer protection. the application of a set of rights and duties to consumers and businesses in a single legal framework will allow for a simplified network for the growth of transactions in the internal market.
in writing. - i approve this report as electronic communications, infrastructure and services are essential for today's society and as the european network and information security agency has done important work and has ongoing issues, including cyber security, it makes sense to extend its mandate and its functions.
in writing. − network and information security is a growing concern not only for policy-makers but for all citizens who increasingly interact with each other and with state authorities through them. the same zeal and attention that once guided public efforts to crack down on mail fraud must now be required for the security of new forms of communication which, being more sophisticated, require constant monitoring and updating. i agree with the extension of the mandate of the european agency by 18 months, as proposed by the european commission and supported by a parliamentary committee, in order to allow a rich and fruitful debate between the european institutions, involving citizens, on the challenges, priorities and competences of the agency and at the same time to avoid the legal vacuum that would result from the lack of extension.
in writing. - this report is based on a proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending regulation (ec) no 460/2004 establishing the european network and information security agency (enisa). enisa was set up in 2004 for an initial period of five years to support the functioning of the internal market by monitoring the security of networks and ensuring the flow of information within the european union. with the widespread availability of information technology and the speeding up and flexibility of networks, the first attacks by so-called hackers have emerged, putting network and information security at risk. recently, the world was stunned by the revelations made on the wikileaks website. in march 2009, the commission asked enisa to support member states in their protection against 'cyberattacks and cyberbullying'. in july of the same year, member states supported the extension of the mandate of enisa. considering that network security and information flows issues play a key role in the digital agenda for europe7 (europe 2020), i agree to extend the mandate of enisa for a further 18 months.
in writing. −we recognise the importance of network and information security in the multiple fields of activity where it has relevant social applications today. but the mechanisms by which this security is guaranteed cannot be dissociated from the political and social context in which they are developed and applied. in particular, we cannot ignore the fact that the prevailing logic of valuing security and the logics of surveillance of cyberspace have not always ensured due respect for the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens. we think it is particularly significant that the eu is funding research programmes by large multinationals that have mastered the technologies that allow governments to spy on internet users, while creating or developing agencies, such as enisa, that will pay for the use of these same technologies. the internet is recognised as one of the most important public spaces of the 21st century, and it is important to value this feature of the internet, rather than opening the way for the appropriation of this space by economic power, thus using it for the benefit of a few, a few, to the detriment of the vast majority and using it for social progress.
in writing. − the extension of the mandate of enisa and the strengthening of its resources in the name of an alleged 'increase in the level of network and information security within the european union' is part of a logic of valuing security, which does not always ensure due respect for the rights, freedoms and guarantees of all citizens. we must be careful that the name of greater supervision of cyberspace does not become a tool for oppressing and repressing people. the internet and its various tools are not oppressive in themselves. the question is the political and social context in which it is used. in this regard, it is particularly significant that the eu is funding research programmes by large multinationals (who dominate the technologies that allow governments to spy on internet users) while creating or developing agencies, such as enisa, that will pay for the use of these same technologies. the internet is recognised as one of the most important public spaces of the 21st century. the commission has already taken the necessary steps to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, violence against women is a serious violation of human rights, we have all said that. it is an old and global problem that affects culturally and geographically distinct more and less developed countries. this reality is often associated with disorganized families, families from weaker social and economic strata, but it is actually a phenomenon that exists in many families regardless of educational level, economic level or social position. it is estimated that in europe about one in five women has been the victim of physical violence at least once in her adult life. the priority is therefore to ensure support for women victims of violence and this report has a set of initiatives to this end: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment from harmful substances. the damage to the physical and mental health of the women victims is incalculable, but society also bears high costs. the fight against this phenomenon therefore requires political and social mobilization. it is, after all, about ensuring equality and development. the organization of a european year to combat violence against women is therefore welcome, as it will have the virtuality of raising awareness among european citizens against this terrible scourge.
in lampedusa, commissioner, the refugees were received in terrible conditions, without food, without toilets, in truly inhumane conditions. the detention centre is currently closed, with no access for ngos, journalists or even, possibly, mps. the italian refugee council is calling for temporary protection permits to be granted to these refugees, in accordance with directive 2001/55/ec, the implementation of which the commissioner has approved. and i thank you for your intervention, because that application was comprehensive and global. there are things we agree on, there are things we disagree on. however, what blocks such global action also has a name: the hypocrisy of the member states. the commissioner spoke about the closure of the codecision procedure for resettlement. as rapporteur, i can say that parliament is ready to see any idea that the council brings to the table. but we've been waiting for a year and a half and we don't have a single idea about resettlement. it is this hypocrisy of the member states that is at issue when, for years, they have allowed mr gaddafi to sweep refugees and immigrants under the carpet while selling them arms. that's why all the talk about the current lack of resources is absolutely hypocritical as well. in 2009 alone, european union countries earned 343 million from arms sales to mr. gaddafi and the first amount they made available to take in refugees from the arab revolutions was 3 million euros, a hundred times less. i think this difference says it all.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner malmström, we have all said that we are faced with an increase in migration flows in terms of scale and complexity. the chronic conflict situations in afghanistan, somalia and the democratic republic of congo have now been joined by an alarming increase in new situations, such as those in egypt, tunisia and libya, which have led to a dramatic worsening of the situation. member states that, for geographical reasons, have been most affected by these migratory pressures have also lost considerable capacity to respond. the chaotic situation on the island of lampedusa, which has been mentioned by several speakers, is an example where the number of refugees has exceeded the number of residents. it is therefore urgent to ensure the necessary support to the member states most particularly affected by providing the financial, human and technical means to ensure an effective response capacity to massive migratory flows and to be able to respond with humanity to the human pressure we are facing. i therefore support the request made by my colleagues that the european union's solidarity mechanism be activated immediately. it is also important to take advantage of existing infrastructures and bodies such as frontex, the asylum support office and probably to reassess and adapt operation hermes. i also support what commissioner rui tavares has already said about the process of resettling refugees. it is important that the council, which is missing in this debate, does not continue to close itself off on legal pretexts and is able to successfully close this dossier of the resettlement of refugees. finally, commissioner, i believe that we need more solidarity between the member states of the union, better coordination of efforts and a sharing of responsibilities and burdens.

mr president, about half the states of the european union have nuclear power stations on their territory. the age of many of the reactors in operation is relatively high, which makes it urgent to dismantle some of these reactors for reasons of safety and defence and to safeguard the health of the population and the environment. in the case of the new member states, which have been faced with the requirement to dismantle several units, it seems to us that it is right that they can count on community support to carry out the dismantling processes in an appropriate and safe manner. those processes should not neglect the necessary maintenance and monitoring after closure, waste treatment, storage and decontamination, environmental requalification of installations and support for the replacement of the energy capacity of decommissioned power plants, with particular attention to environmental sustainability and energy efficiency. as the report says, the social consequences of this process must be fully taken into account, and workers must be guaranteed, in addition to all the safety conditions before, during and after dismantling, the safeguarding of their jobs.
