in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the egf was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of economic, financial and social crises. at a time when we are faced with this serious crisis, with rising unemployment as one of its main consequences, the eu should use all the means at its disposal to respond, particularly in terms of the support to be given to people who have been confronted, overnight, with the reality of unemployment. i have therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of the egf for the czech republic to support workers made redundant in three enterprises in division 28 manufacture of machinery and equipment and nace rev. 2.
in writing. - i welcome the work carried out on the basis of the european globalisation adjustment fund, in particular in support of workers affected by changes in world trade. i also support the decision to mobilise the egf for poland in favour of workers in the machinery and equipment manufacturing sector who have been made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. this is a very pertinent measure given the large drop in exports in this sector, which has consequently been accompanied by an equally worrying rate of unemployment.
in writing. - the request concerns 594 redundancies in three enterprises operating in the podkarpackie region of poland (machinery and equipment manufacturing). this is the first request to be examined under the 2011 budget. it is based on the intervention criterion in article 2 (b) of the egf regulation, which requires at least 500 redundancies in a nine-month period in enterprises operating in one or two nuts ii contiguous regions. the empl committee has assessed favourably their eligibility conditions. the fund was established in 2006 with the aim of providing additional support to workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns in order to assist them with their reintegration into the labour market. following a review of its regulation in 2009, the scope of the egf was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the global economic and financial crisis. the annual budget available for the egf is eur 500 million. i believe that it would be a good thing if the necessary efforts were made to speed up the mobilisation of this instrument, so that aid can reach the workers in need more quickly.
in writing. − this report is based on a proposal for a decision of the european parliament (ep) and of the council on the mobilisation of eur 453 570 from the european globalisation adjustment fund to support the reintegration of polish workers made redundant as a result of the current economic and financial crisis. this application, the first to be approved under the eu budget for 2011, was submitted by poland on 27 april and concerns 594 workers from the podkarpackie region working in the manufacture of machinery and equipment. given that this is a specific budgetary instrument, that the amount requested has a legal framework and that it complies with the provisions of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the european parliament, the council and the european commission, in particular point 28, i am voting in favour of this proposal and hope that it will help to alleviate the economic difficulties of the inhabitants of that region and to revive the local economy.
in writing. - the situation of agriculture and the difficulties facing the rural world are inseparable from the deep systemic crisis and the policies in force, such as the cap, which is mainly responsible for the continuing degradation of agricultural activity in some member states, all of which is geared to the interests of large farmers and agro-industry in northern europe, destroying family farming and compromising the viability of small and medium-sized farms. the role of women in agriculture and rural development is of paramount importance, representing some 42% of agricultural workers, and is a cornerstone in maintaining activity and ensuring effective combating of rural desertification. the report adopted, although lacking a realistic critique of the cap, is generally positive in its approach and in the way it values the role of women. it refers to the promotion of gender equality as a fundamental objective of the eu and its member states, as well as the creation of better living conditions in rural areas, countering the phenomenon of desertification, for which it is essential to defend quality transport infrastructure and improve access to transport for all in order to combat social exclusion and inequality in society that primarily affects women.
in writing. - this report allows the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund - podkarpackie machinery, located in poland. it is noted that poland has requested assistance in respect of 594 redundancies in three enterprises of the machinery and equipment manufacturing division in the nuts ii region of podkarpackie. the european commission proposed to mobilise the amount of eur 453.570, taking into account that the companies meet the eligibility criteria provided for in the egf regulation, linking the redundancies with the impact of the economic and financial crisis, which resulted in the decline of exports of the companies huta stalowa wola sa, hsw - zzn and dezamet sa by 47%, 34% and 58% respectively. the result, they claim, was a considerable decrease in the production of machinery and equipment, thus demonstrating the effect of the crisis on the companies concerned in this country. the 594 redundancies have a serious impact on living conditions, employment and the local economy, and the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund is therefore of the utmost importance in supporting the workers affected. we therefore voted in favour, although we think that the most important thing is to avoid closures and unemployment.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid should now be granted to poland which has submitted a request for assistance in respect of 594 redundancies (200 of which are potential beneficiaries of assistance) in 3 enterprises in nace rev. 2 division 28 (manufacture of machinery and equipment) in the nuts ii region of podkarpackie, poland.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. on 15 february 2011, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the fund for poland to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. this concerns the dismissal of 594 workers (of whom 200 are potential recipients of assistance) from three enterprises operating in the area of machinery and equipment manufacturing in the podkarpackie region of poland during the nine-month reference period from 1 june 2009 to 1 march 2010. this is the first application to be examined under the 2011 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of € 453 570. the commission's assessment concluded that the redundancies were linked to major structural changes in world trade patterns or the financial and economic crisis and that the redundancies were unforeseen. the application meets the eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation and i therefore voted in favour of the mobilisation of the egf.
in writing. − the application submitted by poland for egf assistance concerns 594 redundancies (of which 200 are eligible for assistance) in 3 enterprises operating in nace rev.2 division 28 (manufacture of machinery and equipment) in the nuts ii region of podkarpackie. according to the commission's assessment, this application fulfils all the eligibility criteria defined by law. regulation (ec) no 546/2009 of the european parliament and of the council of 18 june 2009 amending regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 establishing the european globalisation adjustment fund temporarily extended the scope of the egf to cover situations such as this one where, as a direct consequence of the global economic and financial crisis, 'at least 500 redundancies occur in a nine-month period, in particular in small and medium-sized enterprises, in a division at nace level 2, in one or two regions adjacent to nuts ii'. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, hoping that the mobilisation of the egf will help to ensure the effective reintegration of these workers into the labour market.
in writing. − europe is facing an increase in migration flows due to instability in many countries, which is a challenge for the eu. these migratory phenomena can cause tensions between countries of origin and destination, as well as between countries of origin and countries of transit. combining development cooperation measures with a broader political vision that includes security, regional cooperation and bilateral agreements should be the eu's strategy. in this regard, this report identifies the following possible areas for action: encouraging countries of transit and countries of origin to achieve greater institutional economic stability; strengthening eu mediation and conflict prevention efforts in cooperation with regional organisations; negotiating bilateral immigration agreements with transit countries; and developing an economic agenda that includes specific measures to increase employment levels in eu partner countries. in developing new instruments for external action for the period after 2013, the commission should seek to enhance synergies between the development and the stability and security pillars. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - i welcome the community's efforts to respond to the challenges created by instability and migratory flows, which affect not only the countries of origin but also the countries of transit in various aspects related to violence, violation of human rights, etc. i therefore support an active policy in this area, which seeks to address the initial destabilising factors in the countries of origin, such as the lack of economic and democratic structures. only in this way can the negative consequences of migration be eliminated, since migration must be positive and productive, not a means of escape. this policy should be based on cooperation between the countries of origin and transit, based on dialogue, in order to achieve solid, effective and lasting results.
in writing. - this is a very relevant topic and should be analysed in the light of its complexity. the report in question reflects the importance of pursuing cooperation treaties in the european neighbourhood policy (enp). this phenomenon of emigration motivated by crises and instability has negative implications for the country of origin, for the country of destination, and for the displaced populations themselves. it is necessary to reverse this phenomenon so that emigration, in these circumstances, is no longer a last resort, a flight to a context of insecurity, low economic development, instability or fear. i repeat in this declaration of vote the need to take measures to ensure and promote stability and security in the countries of origin. the prospect of reducing these migration flows, motivated by instability and crisis, should be prevention. i believe that european foreign policy, and very specifically the enp, should include aid to these regions of the world, promoting security, stability, the protection of human rights in a process of broader development, as i stated in my report on the revision of the enp-south, which will also be voted on this week.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on migration flows due to instability: scope and role of eu foreign policy. political, social and economic instability, insecurity and political repression, but also climate change, are pushing communities to migrate, and the eu needs to develop a common immigration policy, including, inter alia, the promotion of the economic and social progress of the countries of reception, transit and origin, and the strengthening of social cohesion and integration of migrants.
in writing. - the link between the hotspots of social, economic or political instability and the flows of migration into the european union is now clear. the union's foreign policy cannot be indifferent to this phenomenon, but must seek to understand and monitor it as widely as possible. indeed, the eu must take steps to optimise the use of its own financial resources and institutional structures to effectively manage the migratory flows resulting from the instability that exists today in various parts of the globe. a prevention policy using the most appropriate foreign policy instruments to address and tackle the causes of instability could help to turn the current desperate need for emigration into an opportunity for emigration. the rule of law must be promoted, human rights protected and the development of democracy and sound economies fostered. without such joint efforts in the respective countries and in collaboration with the respective peoples and social structures, it will not be possible to contribute effectively to the reduction of instability.
in writing. - this report focuses on migration flows resulting from political instability in certain regions of the world, notably north africa and the southern mediterranean. this situation has affected the countries of southern europe, particularly italy. we are all aware of the situation on the island of lampedusa, where more than 20 000 people have arrived, and the island of malta, which has brought over 400 000 000 refugees to europe! in order to minimise this situation, it is essential that the eu, in addition to the mobilisation of the european refugee fund, implement, as soon as possible, a more sustained plan aimed at humanitarian assistance and ensuring the basic needs of these populations. in addition, a regional programme for refugees from egypt, tunisia and libya should be drawn up, both in terms of asylum and refugee protection, in order to prevent trafficking in human beings and to prepare for their return to their countries of origin. i welcome the adoption of this report, which is a move by the eu, through its external policy of cooperation, to tackle the problems arising from migration flows in their structural causes and without prejudice of any kind.
in writing. - migration flows have causes. these include such factors as wars and armed conflicts, systematic violations of human rights, conflicts and ethnic and religious repression. but natural disasters and poverty resulting from the lack of adequate economic and democratic structures are also among the most frequent causes of migration flows. the effects of the crisis of capitalism on a world scale and the consequences of its irregular and asymmetrical development are aggravating the economic and social situation in many countries. the revolts in the arab world are also an expression of this phenomenon, which tends to give greater weight to migratory flows. the european union is often hypocritical in this respect, pursuing a policy of double standards. on the one hand, it claims to defend human rights in third countries, even taking an instrumental view of them when it comes to attacking some of these countries. it is also consistent with the persistence of serious situations, such as that in lampedusa, italy. we need measures to prevent these migratory flows, based on a genuine policy of cooperation and development aid, solidarity and the promotion of peace, including the peaceful resolution of conflicts, which is not happening today.
in writing. - we know that wars and armed conflicts, ethnic tensions, systematic violations of human rights - such as the refusal to allow people to practice their religion - natural disasters, poverty resulting from the lack of adequate economic and democratic structures are the main causes of migration flows. in the present situation, the situation is likely to worsen with the crisis that capitalism is suffering and its social consequences, including the uprisings in the arab countries. the european union cannot therefore continue its hypocritical policy of double standards, claiming to defend human rights in third countries, while allowing serious situations such as that in lampedusa to persist. we need a policy of prevention, of development cooperation measures with a broader political vision that includes above all solidarity and the safeguarding of human rights, which is not happening today. the european commission and the european parliament itself usually give priority to their economic and geo-strategic interests and forget about solidarity and the millennium development goals themselves, passing shameful directives such as the return directive. that is why we voted against this report, despite some positive references.
in writing. − migration flows resulting from instability are a challenge for the european union. wars and armed conflicts, ethnic tensions, systematic human rights violations such as refusal to allow people to practice their religion, natural disasters and lack of adequate economic and democratic structures are the main causes of this type of migration flow. this phenomenon is particularly worrying because it can cause or exacerbate tensions not only between countries of origin and countries of destination but also between countries of origin and countries of transit. in order to respond effectively to this challenge, the european union must implement a policy of prevention, using the most appropriate foreign policy instruments to directly address the causes of instability, turning migration into an opportunity rather than a desperate need.
in writing. − migration flows resulting from instability are currently a major challenge for the eu. they stem from wars, armed conflicts, ethnic tensions, human rights violations such as the refusal to allow people to practice their religion , natural disasters and the lack of adequate economic and democratic structures. this is a growing phenomenon which creates tensions not only between countries of origin and countries of destination but also between countries of origin and countries of transit. this report sets out a set of recommendations to enable the eu to respond effectively to this challenge. i would stress, among other measures, the adoption of a prevention policy to tackle directly the causes of instability, turning migration into an opportunity rather than a desperate need, and development cooperation as a broader political vision that includes security, regional cooperation, bilateral agreements with countries of origin and transit. these objectives must be pursued in parallel with the millennium development goals, which are closely linked to political stability and must frame the whole process.
in writing. the role of women in agriculture and the countryside is becoming increasingly important. in recent years, it has been found that support for women and their projects has made it possible to make important progress, resulting in greater development of rural society as a whole. women have contributed to the advancement of traditional economic models and lifestyles in rural areas, while also contributing to the stabilisation and modernisation of these business models and, consequently, to the sustainable development of rural areas. in rural areas too, women aspire to realise their life projects, to secure their economic independence and to face family challenges. in this connection, this report, which i have supported, argues for the need to pay more attention to the multiple interests of women, their skills and the objectives they have achieved, if women are to continue to be attracted to farming. providing rural men and women with success and good life prospects must be the main objective of european rural policy.
in writing. - i welcome the importance given by the commission to the role of women in rural development. the multifunctional role of women in recent years is a reality to which we cannot remain indifferent, both economically and socially. this applies in particular to agriculture, a sector in which women have made a significant contribution in recent years, particularly in diversifying and adapting farms to the market. in this way, and in line with the objectives of the common agricultural policy for a more sustainable use of rural areas, action should be taken to meet the needs and aspirations of women in these areas. to this end, particular attention should be paid to the maintenance and development of the necessary support infrastructure, with particular emphasis on education.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the promotion of gender equality is a fundamental objective of the eu and that this principle should be included in the cap. it is essential that women's access to farming land and agricultural credit be facilitated. this report also contributes to the promotion of sustainable economic growth and rural development itself.
in writing. - if we want to make a serious commitment to the agricultural sector - as i do - and if we want to make the development of activity in rural areas a real option for families, it is imperative to ensure that those who make this choice have access to conditions - in terms of health, education or family support infrastructures - similar to those existing in urban areas. development and social cohesion imply that there is harmony between rural and urban areas, not that the former are forgotten, but that they are systematically considered less attractive. this paradigm shift can, of course, be achieved through the active role of women in farming communities. i don't have a romantic, bucolic vision of running away to the country. on the contrary, i know that such a lifestyle choice comes with costs and often means giving up easy access to infrastructure essential to modern life. that is why i welcome the concerns expressed in this report to enable quality infrastructure to be developed in rural areas too, in support of families, education, health and transport.
in writing. − the promotion of gender equality is a key objective of the eu and its member states. this principle should be included in the cap to promote sustainable economic growth and rural development; farms, rural tourism, direct marketing, social services are cornerstones of a rural supply structure and must be supported in a sustainable way through the common agricultural policy. these services should be promoted through the cap in order to provide women with new prospects and opportunities for paid employment, but also to make it significantly easier to reconcile family and working life. the ageing of the rural population must be combated and the conditions for population fixation must be created to this end, emphasising the importance of living, dynamic rural areas with a diverse population. i would stress in this context the importance of appropriate development opportunities and challenges for young women. it is necessary to support and revitalize the rural environment as a diverse and inclusive economic and living space, taking advantage in particular of the key role, expertise and skills of women.
in writing. the resolution opposes the adoption of the draft regulation proposed by the commission on 'the authorisation and refusal of authorisation of certain health claims made on foods and referring to the reduction of disease risk or to children's development and health', as it is not compatible with the aim and content of the regulation on nutrition and health claims made on foods. docosahexaenoic acid (dha) is present in breast milk and contributes to normal visual development in children up to 12 months of age. in a context where there is no clear scientific consensus on the effect of dha-enriched formulas on infants (whether from milk powder or other infant foods) in a biological environment other than breast milk, we believe that a precautionary and preventive stance should be adopted. we are therefore concerned about the adoption of the proposal for the regulation in question, as it is contrary to the requirements of regulation (ec) no 1924/2006 which states, inter alia, 'that claims must be scientifically substantiated, taking into account all available scientific data'.
in writing. − all policies of the european union and the member states must take into account the promotion of equality and women's rights, as well as the fight against discrimination on grounds of sex. the situation of women in agriculture and the rural world, whose lives are affected by the deep crisis into which current policies such as the cap and others have plunged the rural world, must therefore be given particular attention. women, who account for some 42% of the 26.7 million people working in agriculture, are particularly affected by the closure of hundreds of thousands of small and medium-sized farms and the process of destruction of family farming, which have resulted from successive reforms of the cap. they are also, as in other areas of activity, victims of unemployment, precarious employment, low wages and poverty, which is aggravated by the anti-social policies imposed under the pretext of the crisis. so, more than empty words of substance, we need a break with the policies that have generated the current situation. the role of women, their rights, equality, public services in rural areas, health, education, cultural and leisure facilities, social facilities, etc. must be given priority. (parliament adopted the legislative resolution)
in writing. - the increasing importance of women in agriculture and rural areas requires that the new cap takes this into account in order to promote gender equality. only in this way can we promote sustainable economic growth and rural development. as in urban areas, we must create good living conditions in rural areas so that women and their families have an incentive to stay.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the general thrust of its proposals, in particular the promotion of multi-functionality in rural areas, which is a vital and economic space for the establishment and dynamisation of rural populations. it is important to recognise that rural areas are particularly affected by the ageing of the population, low population density and, in some regions, depopulation, and the cap must therefore be geared to responding to these challenges. it is a fact that women's work in agriculture has historically and systematically been devalued, often unpaid or subject to remuneration equal to that of work done by men. it is important to reflect on this issue and, above all, to establish equal working conditions for equal work. in any case, i believe that the key point is that this issue should lose its relevance for the establishment of gender equality in agriculture as well.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on eu funding for the decommissioning of nuclear power stations in the new member states. i believe that the eu should support the closure of these plants and investment in alternative energy projects in order to ensure the safety and health protection of european citizens, reduce energy dependence and minimise any social costs.
in writing. − the rules in force in the central and eastern european countries before accession were less stringent than the rules applied in the eu at the time. in addition, some of these countries had old soviet-made reactors in operation which could not be adapted to the minimum safety standards required at an economically acceptable cost. for this reason, lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria undertook upon accession to dismantle reactors found to be non-compliant. this required eu intervention and financial assistance, which is expected to continue in 2013. in the wake of the tragic events in japan, i consider it urgent to complete all the programmes for the closure and dismantling of nuclear power stations in central and eastern europe whose operation does not comply with european safety rules.
in writing. − lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria have fulfilled their obligations regarding the timely closure of their units at the three nuclear power plants: unit 1 of the ignalina unit was closed on 31 december 2004 and unit 2 on 31 december 2009; unit 1 of the bohunice v1 nuclear power plant was closed on 31 december 2006 and unit 2 on 31 december 2008. units 1 and 2 of the kozloduy nuclear power plant were closed on 31 december 2002 and units 3 and 4 on 31 december 2006. there is a legal basis for granting financial assistance; the amounts are fixed annually by a commission decision on the basis of individual combined annual programming documents which allow monitoring of the development and financing of approved projects. the aim of community assistance is to help these three member states cope with the financial and economic burden of early closure dates and to cover the costs of many major decommissioning activities, to invest in energy projects with the aim of reducing energy dependence and to help mitigate the social impact of nuclear decommissioning.
in writing. - we know that the average age of the reactors in operation at nuclear power stations, which exist in about half of the member states of the european union, is relatively high, which puts us before the need to dismantle some of these reactors for reasons of safety and defence and to safeguard the health of the population and the environment. in the case of the new member states, which have been faced with the requirement to dismantle several plants, it seems to us that it is right that they can count on community support to carry out the dismantling processes in an appropriate and safe manner. those processes should not neglect the necessary maintenance and monitoring after closure, waste treatment, storage and decontamination, environmental requalification of installations and support for the replacement of the energy production capacity of decommissioned power plants, with particular attention to environmental sustainability and energy efficiency. finally, it is noted that the social consequences of these processes must also be taken into account, guaranteeing not only all the safety conditions for workers before, during and after dismantling, but also the safeguarding of employment and other workers' rights.
in writing. − this report deals with eu funding for the decommissioning of old nuclear power stations in the new member states. these plants pose a danger to public health and the ecosystem not only of their country of origin but also of the whole of europe and the whole planet. in the light of the report's subject matter, i voted in favour of helping to dismantle these old power stations. however, i believe that the eu's nuclear policy must go further. in view of the serious risks of nuclear energy, which have been known for a long time, and the current nuclear disaster in japan, i call for the immediate establishment of a european plan to abandon this type of energy. i also believe that the eu should immediately suspend funding and support for new nuclear power stations.
in writing. - nuclear safety is a concern for everyone in europe. the recent accident in japan has highlighted the risks inherent in nuclear power stations. the countries of eastern europe which are seeking to join the eu have nuclear power stations of soviet technology which have been in operation for many years and are therefore at the end of their life. in view of the high costs of dismantling these structures, it is only natural that the eu should support these countries in their efforts to dismantle them so that no nuclear accident with the consequences that we all unfortunately know will occur in europe.
in writing. − in the context of eu accession negotiations, lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria negotiated support for the decommissioning of old soviet-designed nuclear reactors which, in the view of the international community and in line with the 1992 g7 munich summit, could not be adapted to the required minimum safety standards at an economically acceptable cost. in the context of the accession negotiations, the three countries undertook to close and subsequently dismantle these nuclear reactors by fixed dates. recognising that early closure represented an exceptional financial burden, the european union, out of solidarity, committed itself to providing adequate additional financial assistance for the decommissioning of these reactors by the end of 2013. the assistance programme has been subject to regular audits and evaluations. the eca is currently conducting outcome audits of the three programmes and a report is expected in autumn 2011. it can be concluded at this stage that synergies could have been created between the three projects to make eu action more efficient and effective. i voted in favour of this report, in particular the recommendation to the commission for the harmonization of the rules on the financing of the decommissioning of nuclear reactors.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the egf was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of economic, financial and social crises. at a time when we are faced with this serious crisis, with rising unemployment as one of its main consequences, the eu should use all the means at its disposal to respond, particularly in terms of the support to be given to people who have been confronted, overnight, with the reality of unemployment. i have therefore supported the present report on the mobilisation of the egf in the czech republic to support workers made redundant by unilever čr spol. s r.o.

in writing. − this report is based on a proposal for a decision of the european parliament (ep) and of the council on the mobilisation of eur 323 820 from the european globalisation adjustment fund to support the reintegration of workers in the czech republic made redundant as a result of the current economic and financial crisis. this application, the second to be approved under the eu budget 2011, was submitted to the commission on 24 march 2010 and concerns 634 employees of unilever čr from the střední čechy region, who worked in the retail sector. given that this is a specific budgetary instrument, that the amount requested has a legal framework and that it complies with the provisions of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the european parliament, the council and the european commission, in particular point 28, i am voting in favour of this proposal and hope that it will help to alleviate the economic difficulties of the inhabitants of that region and to revive the local economy.
in writing. - another mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) has been launched. this time to support the workers laid off at the multinational unilever factory in the czech republic. as on other occasions, we voted in favour. but beyond the reservations we always make in these situations, there are particularities in this process that deserve to be highlighted: the european commission merely stated that unilever did not receive any state aid or aid from community funds for the opening of the plant in the czech republic, before or after accession to the eu. but the commission did not inform, as it should have and was asked to, about what is happening in other factories of the group, arguing that it was not mandatory under the egf regulation. more than what happened in the specific case of the unit in the czech republic, it is important to know and assess the behaviour of the unilever group at the level of the european union. we therefore regret the absence of this information on public aid granted to this group and, in general, to multinational companies whose restructuring justifies intervention by the egf.
in writing. - this is another mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf), which in this case aims to benefit workers who have been made redundant at the czech plant of the multinational unilever. the european commission's position in this area has been very controversial, as it merely stated that unilever did not receive any state aid or financial support from european funds for the opening of the plant in the czech republic, before or after accession to the eu, but did not provide information on what is happening in other plants of the group, arguing that it is not mandatory under the egf regulation. in the debate in the committee on employment and social affairs, therefore, it drew attention to the fact that no information was available on what was happening with the unilever group at european union level and proposed that this issue be taken into account in the revision of the regulation so that the financial situation, including public aid for multinational companies whose restructuring justifies intervention by the egf, could be examined without jeopardising access to the fund for workers made redundant. that is why we are voting in favour of these proposals.

in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. on 15 february 2011, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in the czech republic to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. this was the second application to be examined under the 2011 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of € 323 820. the case concerns the dismissal of 634 workers (all potential beneficiaries of the intervention) from the company unilever čr, spol. sr., operating in the retail sector in the střední region, during the four-month reference period from 16.09.2009 to 16.01.2010. the commission's assessment concluded that there was a causal link between those redundancies and the significant structural changes in world trade patterns resulting from the financial crisis, as well as the unforeseen nature of the redundancies in question. since the application meets the eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation, i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the egf.
in writing. − the application submitted by the czech republic for egf assistance in respect of 634 redundancies in the period from 16 september 2009 to 16 january 2010 in the company unilever čr, spol. sr.o, operating in the retail sector in the nuts ii region of střední čechy, meets all the eligibility criteria defined by law. regulation (ec) no 546/2009 of the european parliament and of the council of 18 june 2009 amending regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 establishing the european globalisation adjustment fund temporarily extended the scope of the egf to cover situations such as this one where, as a direct consequence of the global economic and financial crisis, 'at least 500 redundancies occur in a company in a member state in a four-month period'. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, hoping that the mobilisation of the egf will help to ensure the effective reintegration of these workers into the labour market.
in writing. − dual-use technological products are all products (including software and technologies) which can be used for civilian or military purposes in parallel, and therefore require special care when exported to prevent the proliferation of weapons and, in particular, weapons of mass destruction. as is clear to any analyst, it is essential for international security that these products are controlled and that the regulations establishing such control mechanisms are continually updated in line with technological developments. it is also clear that in a state governed by the rule of law such controls must be transparent and democratic, as the commission intends. finally, i believe, as is clear from the afet opinion, that the commission should be sensitive to the fact that there are states within the eu which have more restrictive and more demanding rules on the control of exports of dual-use items. that is natural and, in my view, should be maintained.
in writing. - this report deals with the need to control the export and circulation of so-called dual-use goods, i.e. those which have a use not only for civilian purposes but also for military purposes. the european union (eu) has taken a number of measures over the past few years to prevent these materials from being used in the manufacture of weapons, including weapons of mass destruction. the main eu control instrument is regulation (ec) no 428/2009 of 5 may, which covers brokerage activities and the transit of these materials, but needs to be amended to avoid differential treatment between member states. i therefore support the proposals in this report, as they are intended to reassure european citizens about the production and circulation of dual-use items and make the current system more transparent and more democratic.
in writing. − export controls on dual-use goods have been subject to eu-wide measures. the main export control instrument is regulation (ec) no 428/2009 of 2009. this regulation introduced the extension of the scope of controls on brokerage and transit activities. although the report attempts to introduce greater democratic control and transparency, there are some key points which prevent us from voting in favour. with the establishment of the dual-use coordination group, chaired by the commission, the list of exporters, brokers and interested parties consulted from exporters is the responsibility of the commission. it is this group that decides which countries can be traded with, removing this competence from the member states and thus undermining their sovereignty. another aspect is the inclusion of israel in the list of countries of destination for dual-use goods. for example, joint research projects funded by the 7th framework programme for research, in particular those involving the israeli aerospace industries - the manufacturer of the drones used in the 2008/2009 attack on the gaza strip, which killed dozens of people.
in writing. - we voted in favour of returning this report to the respective parliamentary committee to allow negotiations with the council to continue, on the basis of the legislative proposal with the amendments introduced by the european parliament today. we know that the use of civilian products and technologies for military purposes lacks an approach that does not stop at the control of exports of so-called dual-use goods and related services. while this export control is important and must be carried out in a judicious manner, without jeopardizing developing countries' access to products and technologies necessary for their development, it is necessary to increase the transparency of processes and to enable democratic scrutiny. but we stress that consistency with other eu policies and the objectives of this regulation is also required in this area. joint research projects funded under the 7th framework programme for research are well known, in particular those involving the israeli aerospace industries, the manufacturer of the drones used in the attack on the gaza strip in 2008/2009 that killed dozens of people.
in writing. − the treaty of lisbon clarifies the eu's competences in the field of international trade, and is thus a good opportunity to reaffirm the eu's role in this area and the role, competence and responsibility of the european parliament within the eu's institutional framework for decision-making. the community's dual-use regime should be organised in a more transparent and democratic way; the full participation of the european parliament, through the implementation of the obligations arising from the treaty of lisbon and the adoption of a joint interpretation by the european parliament and the european commission under the new framework agreement, will be crucial to achieving this objective.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider that the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon and the consequent clarification of the eu's powers in the field of international trade is a good opportunity to reaffirm the eu's role in this area and the role, competence and responsibility of the european parliament in the eu's institutional framework for decision-making. the community's dual-use regime should be organised in a more transparent and democratic way; the full participation of the european parliament, through the implementation of the obligations arising from the treaty of lisbon and the adoption of a joint interpretation by the european parliament and the european commission, in the framework of the new framework agreement, will be crucial to achieving this objective. this is a recast of regulation (ec) no 1334/2000 in the light of the current international framework. indeed, the extension of the scope of export controls on dual-use items is essential to cover controls on transit and brokering and the application of sanctions to the illegal brokering of dual-use items related, for example, to a weapons of mass destruction programme.
in writing. export credit agencies (eca) are the world's largest source of public funding for private sector projects. these are government agencies or financial institutions segmented by governments that provide export credits, loans, insurance and investment guarantees to companies operating in high-risk regions abroad, including many developing countries. it should be noted that the financing of these major projects in developing countries amounts to several times the combined annual amount of all the multilateral development banks. in this sense, the aces are a well-placed instrument to contribute to the eu's external policy objectives, namely poverty alleviation and climate change. i welcome the improvements in the agreement in question, particularly in terms of greater transparency, and i consider it essential that it be explicitly stated that export aecs must take account of and respect the objectives and policies of the union, in particular the values associated with the consolidation of democracy, respect for human rights and policy coherence for development. while aces facilitate trade, in the absence of clear and transparent criteria and rules, they can distort trade.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on officially supported export credits because i believe that it is necessary for officially supported export credit institutions to demonstrate greater transparency and provide more information on their activities. full consistency with the objectives of article 208 of the treaty establishing the reduction and eradication of poverty as the main objectives of the union's development cooperation policy should also be ensured.
in writing. − the commission and the council are currently reviewing the legislative framework (the 'official supported export credit agreement') with a view to its transposition into eu law. the aim is to give the export credit agencies (eca) of the member states more legal certainty. export credits are effective instruments to support union enterprises, capable of helping to create jobs and develop projects that might otherwise face financing difficulties. the fact that more and more applications are being received would suggest a rapid introduction of the oecd convention by member states. i agree with the econ committee's opinion that 'european supervision of export credits should be introduced as an exception when there is any distortion of competition in the internal market. the principle of subsidiarity should be maintained.'
in writing. the report is concerned with a proposal for a european parliament and council decision on the application of certain rules to the obtaining of export credits by companies which are recipients of official support. in fact, most member states have export credit agencies (eca) which play a key role in supporting european trade and business investment, reaching €468 billion in the period 2004-09. these supports are part of the agreement on subsidies and countervailing measures (asmc), also known as the arrangement, negotiated within the framework of the organisation for economic cooperation and development (oecd) countries and represent public financing instruments to which the european union is committed. given that these agencies mainly support industrial activities with negative effects on the environment, in particular due to the production of co2, and that, according to the world bank, the effects on poverty reduction are negligible, i agree with the rapporteur's position that the aces should contribute to the achievement of eu policies and objectives, and there is therefore no need to revise the oecd convention.
in writing. − we believe that export credit agencies (eca) need to have greater supervision and control of both exports and investments and financing, as their lack of transparency causes immense damage and is conducive to bribery and corruption. the eca are public instruments which are often used by the eu to help finance its international objectives and its economic and geostrategic interests, which are inseparable from the objectives of domination and control of regions and countries, leading to the establishment of genuine relations of a neo-colonial nature. investments financed by the eca often do not bring any benefit to the countries that would supposedly benefit. the establishment of export credit guidelines is intended to circumvent the announced end of direct aid under wto agreements, which is opposed by developing countries, by putting pressure on these countries to accept the signing of the doha round. with direct aid or credit, the main objective remains control over markets, natural resources, exploitation of workers and the conditioning of the national sovereignty of the countries receiving the products or investments made possible by the financing of the aces.
in writing. − public export credit agencies (pecas) need to be more closely monitored and controlled, both in terms of exports and in terms of investment and financing, as their lack of transparency causes immense damage and is conducive to bribery and corruption. but the aces are public instruments often used by the eu to help finance its international objectives, notably in relation to climate change and poverty alleviation. sometimes this is used as a way of financing genuine eu neo-colonialism in so-called developing countries. the establishment of export credit guidelines is intended to circumvent the announced end of direct aid under wto agreements, which is opposed by developing countries, by putting pressure on these countries to accept the signing of the doha round. with direct aid or credit, the main objective remains control over markets, natural resources, exploitation of workers and the conditioning of the national sovereignty of the countries receiving the products or investments made possible by the financing of the aces.
in writing. − export credit agencies have been playing an increasingly important role in supporting all types of investment, thereby helping to reduce the impact of the current economic and financial crisis by creating jobs, helping trade and investment for companies that otherwise would not be able to obtain credit in the private sector. export credit agencies have become the largest source of public financing in developing countries. a significant proportion of export credit financing projects in developing countries are concentrated in sectors such as transport, oil and gas and extractive industries, as well as in large infrastructure projects such as large dams. it is important, however, that there be close supervision of the activities of these agencies to avoid problems in the future.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the rapporteur that export credit is a powerful instrument to support eu businesses. in view of the growing momentum of official export credit applications, it is of the utmost importance that the latest oecd export credit facility agreement is introduced as soon as possible by member states. medium- and long-term export credit support is a valuable instrument which is not yet fully exploited in all member states and which needs to be encouraged, especially in a weak economy such as portugal. export credit is certainly a driver of job creation by guaranteeing the financing of projects that would otherwise have no access to capital. any legislation in this area should avoid any new form of administrative red tape which could increase existing costs. european export credit supervision should only be introduced as an exception where any distortion of competition in the internal market could occur. the principle of subsidiarity must be strictly observed in this area.

the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all, a special thanks to all those who have taken part in the preparation of this report and, in particular, a special thanks to the shadow rapporteurs from all the political groups. this is a report which allows the 2012 budget of the european parliament to be an austerity budget, a budget of restraint, a strict budget. in fact, we have actually cut some 49 million euros from the initial proposal. we have gone further than we had promised in the position we have taken, which was voted and supported here in plenary by a large majority. we said the update would be around inflation. well, we are far from inflation, which means that the 2012 budget is a real decrease, a budget that is also below 20% of heading 5 which is the one that has the money for the institutions of the european union. we have not been able to achieve this target for some years now and we were already over 20%. i would also remind you that the committee of presidents set the target for parliament's budget at 20 to 22%, and this year it is below that figure. but also in the implementation of the budget in 2012, we will want savings using the principles of good management, the principle of economy, the principle of efficiency and also the principle of effectiveness. we want all expenditure to be justified, we want variable expenditure to be subject to a cost-benefit analysis. in this way we will also achieve additional savings in execution. the effort must be on the part of all the institutions in terms of saving and the margin of heading 5, which covers the administrative expenditure of all the institutions, is expected to have a surplus of around eur 380 million in 2012. well, we propose that 100 million euros for administrative expenditure be transferred to the youth area. and why youth? because it is the generation that has the greatest difficulty in terms of access to employment, it is the one whose unemployment rate is twice that of other generations. but there are additional objectives and reasons for choosing the priority 'youth' also for 2012. it was already in 2011 and, in addition, in the european union 2020 strategy which guides the next financial perspective, but which also guides mrs balzani's budget for 2012, youth is present in all five objectives. and furthermore, with regard to school drop-out and education for the generation between 30 and 34 years old, 40 per cent of this generation has university degrees, which makes two of the exclusive objectives. i hope that amendments which are contrary to this proposal will be reconsidered, because we believe that the priority 'youth' should be a priority to be maintained by this parliament.
we meps have the power to decide on our own salary. we also decided on the money to hire people. between 2010 and 2011, we allocated an additional 3,000 euros to each of us per month. we are still the ones who vote on the cost ceilings for our offices, the cost subsidies, the subsidies and even the way we travel. in these matters our power is absolute and that is why i ask myself and i ask you: have we used or abused this power of ours, have we been wise and thoughtful or, on the contrary, have we not known how to resist the power that this power has over us? unfortunately, we have not known, and that is why this debate is not about numbers, this debate is about ethics and politics, it is a debate that qualifies or disqualifies us in the eyes of those who hold us accountable. i am not, by any means, an anti-party populist or one who thinks that members of parliament should work by candlelight. but it is precisely because this demagogy exists in our countries that we have to be extremely demanding when it comes to deciding on the money and the perks that affect us. i am sorry, but it is not normal for members who have always travelled in economy class to have to do so in executive once flights have started to be reimbursed by ticket and not by kilometre. and the same kind of criteria apply to our salaries and expenses. i think they are excessive, in some cases even extravagant, but that is not what is at issue here, what is at issue is whether we have the courage to vote at least for a freeze on these expenditure. i do not understand how there can be members here who do not hesitate to defend in their countries austerity policies and reductions in wages and pensions, but who, when it comes to deciding on their own money, have austerity on their doorstep. this is not serious my friends, this is indecent and very sad.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the external aspect of the common fisheries policy is of particular importance, since it is not possible to meet our needs in fishery products on the basis of our fisheries resources alone. the european fishing industry only provides 40% of our self-sufficiency. in 2009, we imported eur 15.5 billion and exported only eur 2.5 billion in fishery products, which means that without the bilateral agreements with third countries, 3,000 vessels would have been paralysed and 40,000 jobs would have been lost, but the external dimension of the common fisheries policy also has positive aspects for our partners. the european union, unlike many of our international competitors, does not simply trade fish for money. the agreements we conclude are based on the values we defend, both in terms of human rights and respect for the sustainability of resources. under the treaty, the union's exclusive competence for the conservation of biological resources applies to the management of the fishing activities of community fleets in non-community waters. the activities under the external dimension of the common fisheries policy are primarily aimed at extending the principles of sustainable and responsible fishing at international level. the other objectives which currently govern the external dimension of the common fisheries policy, as i have already said, namely maintaining the presence of a community fleet at international level and ensuring that it supplies the community market, are therefore becoming less and less relevant. it is in this context that the report i have drawn up and which we are discussing here today on the fisheries agreement with the union of the comoros should be understood. the agreement provides for the right of access to comorian waters for 70 european vessels in return for a financial contribution of some eur 600 000 per year, about half of which is to be used to develop the fisheries sector in this country, which, as we know, has virtually no other resources and on which some 30 000 of its 800 000 000 inhabitants depend. the agreement includes mechanisms for monitoring catches, hiring local crew and a clause relating to suspension or review in the event of human rights violations. this small country, independent of france since 1975, has already experienced a number of coups d'état. i therefore propose that this agreement be approved and draw attention to the various recommendations i make, in particular those which refer to the need to significantly improve the evaluation of results. i take this opportunity to use the minute i have left to refer to another aspect of another report, the report by mrs grelier, which does not merit my agreement and which, together with other members, is the reason for the amendment. i am referring to the amendment which aims to allow the continuation of fishing for hake and plaice with gillnets in areas 8, 9 and 10 off the portuguese coast, which was prohibited by a commission decision from 1 october 2010 on the grounds that it is affecting certain bycatch shark populations without any scientific study having been carried out to support it. the amendment proposes that this decision be repealed by 2012 so that the portuguese authorities can complete scientific studies that may or may not support this decision. this position is also supported by the economic and social committee, and i therefore call on parliament to approve it, because it is fair.
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, this regulation, regulation (ec) no 861/2006, establishes community financial measures relating to the implementation of the common fisheries policy and the law of the sea. it is an important financial instrument of the european union in the fisheries sector. together with the european fisheries fund, they are the two main instruments for implementing the common fisheries policy. since the adoption of that regulation in 2006, several elements of related ancillary legislation have been amended, which now justifies that regulation to be amended in order to ensure consistency between all elements of the legislative framework. the commission also considers that in some cases experience has shown the need to ensure that the provisions of the regulation are slightly adapted to better meet the needs. i therefore propose to them a limited scope for this revision, maintaining essentially the objectives and structure of the original regulation. while maintaining this limited scope, we nevertheless considered it appropriate to propose some additional amendments which, although they are specific, could help to bring this legislation into better alignment with recent developments in the sector and its future prospects. the debate before and during the preparation of the report, as well as the opinions and proposals of the shadow rapporteurs and other colleagues, which i would like to highlight and take to heart, and thank everyone for their participation, have contributed greatly to the final result. among the proposed amendments contained in the report, i would stress the reference to the safeguarding of coastal fishing activities, the possibility of financing, in addition to the purchase, also the development by the member states of various technologies affecting the fisheries sector, such as equipment and logical support, computer networks enabling the compilation, management, validation, analysis and development of sampling methods and the exchange of data on fisheries, among others. in the field of aquaculture, i note the possibility of introducing funding for the collection, management and use of environmental data in addition to the socioeconomic data previously provided, thus promoting environmental and health monitoring and monitoring of this sector, in order to contribute to its sustainability. i would like to draw attention to the three additional amendments we are proposing to this report. there is now widespread and growing recognition of the importance of fisheries management based on up-to-date and rigorous scientific knowledge of the state of resources. this is an essential condition for the sustainable development of the activity. for this reason, we propose that the community co-financing rates for the collection, management and use of basic and supplementary scientific data on the state of fisheries resources be increased. it is proposed to raise this ceiling from 50% to 60%. similarly, with regard to control activities, we propose an equal increase in the maximum possible rate of community co-financing, while maintaining the commission's prerogatives, which already exist at present, as regards the possibility of financing certain actions at higher rates, in a framework in which the member states and their control authorities have and should continue to have a central role in the conduct and implementation of control measures in their waters. these changes are the result of an attempt to reach a compromise, taking into account the objections raised by various groups to the maximum of 75% originally envisaged. they are supported by our group, the gue/ngl, and a number of colleagues from other political mr president, commissioner, in congratulating the four rapporteurs, let me focus on just two of the reports under discussion. in 2008, the lack of agreement on a draft regulation to simplify and clarify the community regulation on the conservation of fishery resources led to the adoption of the current regulation establishing a set of transitional measures initially foreseen for the period from 1 january 2010 to 30 june 2011. this legislative proposal extends this transitional regime for an additional period of 18 months, i.e. until 1 january 2013, pending a new technical measures regulation to frame the reformed cfp. in this transitional period, it is important to maintain a regulatory framework for fisheries, to safeguard the interests of fishermen, while keeping in mind the fundamental objective of protecting sustainable fisheries. the current intention not to extend the use of gillnets and to ban them from 1 october 2010 at depths between 200 and 600 metres, without a sound scientific basis, is not a good example of the above. the current ban on this fishing technique, which for decades has been used by a segment of the portuguese artisanal fleet for the sustainable exploitation of species such as drumsticks and cod, is a severe economic and social blow to the sector and fishing communities most dependent on the exploitation of these resources. i therefore ask for your support in getting a proposal passed which my colleagues capoulas santos and joão ferreira and i have tabled in the house and which is intended to guarantee, by 2013, what was law before 1 october 2010. i am also referring to the proposal for a regulation laying down community financial measures for the implementation of the common fisheries policy and the law of the sea - the ferreira report. it is the most important financial instrument for fisheries support, alongside the eff, providing funding in the fields of international relations, governance, data collection and scientific advice, and monitoring the implementation of the cfp. in this context, i express my full support for the proposals put forward by the rapporteur in the plenary to increase the possibility of community co-financing, up to 60%, in the field of the collection, management and use of basic data, as well as in the field of the collection, management and use of supplementary data. the general and growing recognition of the importance of fisheries management, supported by up-to-date and rigorous scientific knowledge of the state of resources, fully justifies the approval of the rapporteur's proposals and his report as a whole.

the common fisheries policy is a set of measures designed by the european union to ensure the sustainability and competitiveness of the european fisheries sector. the main priorities for the reform of the common fisheries policy are to make it more effective in ensuring the economic viability of european fleets, the conservation of fish stocks, the link with maritime policy and the supply of quality food to consumers. it is in this context that the measures adopted today by the european parliament, such as the revision of technical measures and the adaptation of existing legislation in terms of the collection of scientific data, fit in. the sustainability of the sector and its competitiveness must exist in a balanced way. fisheries are essential for the economic and social development of coastal communities by contributing to the dynamism of the regions and by encouraging activities in related sectors. for example, in the outermost regions of the union, which make up the european union's largest exclusive economic zone, the fisheries sector plays a key role in the region's economic activity and it is therefore a priority to ensure the sustainability and development of this sector.
the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner barnier, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, parliament has responded to the commission's request for action to relaunch the single market by the report under debate and vote today. in the group of 19 proposals for which i was rapporteur, on the single market act for europeans, we identified five priorities, using the criteria of tangible and short-term feasibility. first, to increase the mobility of citizens through the mutual recognition of professional qualifications, professional identity cards, the european skills passport and the regular measurement of mobility within the union. secondly, border controls on goods imported from third countries and a multiannual action plan for market surveillance and product safety. thirdly, the application of the regulation on roaming until june 2015, limiting its prices in order to reduce the burden on the public and businesses. fourthly, guaranteeing access to traditional banking services by improving transparency and comparability. fifthly, to remove the obstacles to mobile workers in order to ensure the full portability of their pension rights. if this was an easy and consensual exercise, it was more difficult to agree on measures to combat the fatigue of the single market referred to in the mario monti report and the holistic and concerted approach to respond to the needs and concerns of the citizens so well identified in the grech report, approved by the european parliament in may last year. we certainly recognize that the division of parliament's work into three separate reports is artificial, despite the efforts of the imco committee to give it unity of analysis and action. the three components - business, citizens and government - must move forward simultaneously to achieve a competitive single market with smart, inclusive and sustainable growth that puts europeans at the heart of that market. we also recognise that the proliferation of commission initiatives in this area and europe 2020, industrial policy, innovation europe, risk blurring the core issue of the relaunch, which is to make the idea of the single market not only more friendly but more attractive to europeans. the consensus, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, was more difficult on two points. firstly, in respect of social values and rights, we have been confronted with the reluctance of our colleagues on the right and the liberals to accept the need for permanent safeguards of the social rights of europeans so that they can never be submerged by the logic of the market in all future legislation. we particularly regret that a reference to the revision of the directive on the posting of workers was not accepted as a priority. secondly, in safeguarding social services of general economic interest, the aim was to remove the content of the activities of these services from the pure logic of the market or, at least, to eliminate the possibility of transforming public services of social responsibility into private monopolies or oligopolies in matters such as water supply, urban transport, education, health and social support services. if the introduction of competitive management and internal market mechanisms in such services seems useful, the social values associated with universal access, where the principles of solidarity prevail over the mere logic of the market, must be safeguarded. we are faced here with the reluctance of the parliamentary groups on our right to accept european legislation on this subject, only agreeing to use all the available options which are consensual and based on article 14 and protocol 26 of the treaty. my group abstained in the final vote on the three reports in committee because there was no progress on the social dimension of the single market. however, after the vote in committee, many positive aspects were included which greatly improved the report. consensus was reached through successive rapprochements, with final amendments signed by the main parliamentary groups without victory or defeat. the final result, which honours the imco committee and those who worked on the report, was contributed to by all the parliamentary groups through 266 amendments as well as opinion reports from five committees. all the contributions were helpful. i thank the shadow rapporteurs róża gräfin von thun, jürgen creutzmann, malcolm harbour, emile turunem, kyriacos triantaphyllides and the group coordinators for the productive criticism and the spirit of cooperation which made it possible to bring the negotiations to a successful conclusion. i am particularly grateful to malcolm harbour for the generous and far-sighted approach he has given to the work of the committee over the past four months.
