in writing. − this protocol to the fisheries agreement between the european community and the union of the comoros, one of the many fisheries partnership agreements to which the union is a co-signatory, expires on 31 december 2010. the new protocol will be concluded for a period of three years (2011-2013) from the entry into force of the council decision on the provisional application of the said protocol and after the expiry of the current protocol. the aim of the proposal is to define the fishing opportunities for eu vessels on the basis of the available surplus and the financial contribution due, separately, for access rights and sectoral support. the new protocol is in line with the interests of both parties and aims to strengthen cooperation in the fisheries sector using the available financial instruments. the need to create a favourable environment for the development of investments in this sector and to optimise the production of small-scale fisheries has been felt. like the rapporteur, i believe that parliament should be allowed to monitor closely the way in which the agreement is being developed and implemented, and that it is for the commission to ensure that this is the case.
in writing. − this report is based on a proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of a protocol setting out the conditions under which european union (eu) fishing vessels may engage in fishing activities in the maritime waters of the union of the comoros. the eu has established 'fisheries partnership agreements' with a number of countries over the years, in return for which it provides a certain amount of money, which is mainly used to support national fisheries policies, in particular the protection of resources. with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the european parliament has assumed increased responsibilities in this sector, and we now need to approve the new fisheries agreements. the eu/union of the comoros protocol expired on 31 december 2010 and it is therefore urgently necessary to renew it. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. − this report supports the new protocol to the eu-comoros fisheries partnership agreement, which will be in force for three years and whose main objective is to define the fishing opportunities allocated to eu vessels and the financial contribution due under access rights and sectoral support. the agreement provides for the right of access to comorian waters for 70 european vessels in exchange for a financial contribution of some eur 600 000 per year, about half of which is to be used to develop the fisheries sector in the country, which has virtually no other resources and on which some 30 000 of its 800 000 inhabitants depend. it is in this area that the implementation of the so-called partnership agreements in this area has most visibly failed, which should be a reason for reflection and policy change. the commission has also proposed that the fishing opportunities for bluefin tuna be increased to 25 000 tonnes by the end of the year. portugal will continue with the five longliners it already had. the main beneficiaries remain france and spain.
in writing. − this new agreement replaces the previous one, which expired on 31 december 2010. this type of agreement allows eu fishing vessels access to the comoros' fishing stocks with the appropriate financial compensation. the great advantage of these types of protocols is that the eu can help these countries develop, in this case with a greater focus on the fisheries sector, which absorbs about 50% of the funds earmarked for counterpart measures. we must bear in mind that in the comoros some 30 000 people depend directly on the fisheries sector, hence the importance of this support.
in writing. − the conclusion of bilateral fisheries agreements between the european community and third countries, known as 'fisheries partnership agreements', has been a common practice under the common fisheries policy/cfp and is central to its external dimension. this proposal for a new protocol to the eu-comoros fisheries partnership agreement is an integral part of the external policy of the cfp and serves the interests of both parties. the report makes the following recommendations which are considered relevant: (ii) the commission shall forward to parliament the conclusions of the meetings and proceedings of the joint committee provided for in article 9 of the agreement, as well as the multiannual sectoral programme referred to in article 7 (c) of the protocol and the results of the annual evaluations thereof; • representatives of the european parliament should be allowed to participate as observers in the meetings and proceedings of the joint committee; • the commission shall present to the european parliament and the council, prior to the renegotiation of the agreement, an analysis of its implementation; • the european parliament and the council should be treated equally as regards the right to be informed promptly and fully, as well as the monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of international fisheries agreements and the negotiation of their revision. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − this protocol is intended to replace the protocol annexed to the eu-comoros fisheries partnership agreement, which expired on 31 december 2010. the main objective of the new protocol is to define the fishing opportunities available to eu vessels under access rights and sectoral support and to continue cooperation between the european union and the union of the comoros in order to promote the establishment of a partnership framework for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and responsible exploitation of fisheries resources in the comorian fishing zone. under the new protocol, the eu's overall annual financial contribution is eur 1 845 750 over the entire three-year period. the development of investments in the fisheries sector is also planned to optimise small-scale fishing. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal for a new protocol to the eu-comoros fisheries partnership agreement, as it serves the interests of both parties.
in writing. − all the improvements made to the euro-mediterranean agreements have a major impact on the economic and political stability of the countries, contributing to the numerous social and democratic gains that result. i therefore welcome any effort to do so. in view of the incomplete resolution of certain disputes concerning the trade provisions of the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european communities and the hashemite kingdom of jordan, i acknowledge the demonstrated ineffectiveness of the system operated through diplomatic channels in this matter. i therefore accept the need for a mechanism to enable resources to be applied in a simple and effective way and therefore support the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of an agreement in the form of a protocol between the european union and the hashemite kingdom of jordan. the aim of this protocol is to establish a dispute settlement mechanism for the trade provisions of the euro-mediterranean agreement.
in writing. - the euro-mediterranean agreements contain provisions for the liberalisation of trade in goods, but the rules for settling disputes arising from them have been dependent mainly on diplomacy and have been easily blocked by the claimant. in 2006, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with its mediterranean partners to establish trade-related dispute settlement mechanisms based on the dispute settlement mechanisms of the most recent agreements concluded by the european union in the wto. a draft agreement with jordan was initialled on 9 december 2009. i support the establishment of the dispute settlement mechanism, hoping that it will have a deterrent rather than a repressive function and that jordan will be able to resist the instability that has been plaguing the region, while remaining the moderate and responsible partner it has been under the reigns of hussein and abdullah ii.
in writing. − this recommendation is based on a proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of a protocol between the european union (eu) and jordan aimed at implementing a dispute settlement mechanism under the euro-mediterranean agreement. resolving trade disputes between countries, usually by diplomatic means, has not always had the desired effect. in the euro-mediterranean context, negotiations were therefore opened between the eu and the mediterranean partners, in particular jordan, and the draft agreement was signed on 9 december 2009 at the euro-mediterranean ministerial conference on trade in brussels. i agree with this draft legislative resolution of the european parliament, aware that it will bring about significant improvements in relations between the states in the area of free trade and contribute to the political and economic stability of this region. i therefore welcome the new agreement and hope that, once it has entered into force, there will be no conflict between the eu or its member states and jordan.
in writing. - as stated in the explanatory memorandum to this report, the settlement of disputes arising from euro-mediterranean agreements has always been achieved through diplomatic channels. the 'alternative' model proposed to us is part of the logic promoted within the wto, which, in the name of supposed effectiveness, seeks to override national sovereignty, the resolution of disputes by respecting the specificity of each country, its right to defend its interests and the interests of its peoples. the settlement of disputes through diplomatic channels guaranteed equal treatment between countries. this mechanism, on the contrary, subverts this principle by favouring the circulation of capital and by placing economic power above political power, the interest of capital above the interest of countries and their peoples. our opposition to this mechanism and its implications is all the more justified as it stems from the signing of an agreement between the eu, whose legitimacy under the lisbon treaty is questionable (and, in any case, deplorable), and the king abdullah regime which continues to violently repress the emerging peaceful youth movement demanding democratic reforms and freedoms.

in writing. − the european neighbourhood policy (enp) provides for the gradual opening up of certain european union (eu) programmes to the participation of neighbouring countries with the aim of promoting reforms, modernisation and often democratisation. to this end, on 5 march 2007 the council adopted a 'general approach to allowing the participation of partner countries covered by the european neighbourhood policy in community agencies and programmes'. following this 'approach', the commission has started negotiations on framework agreements with several neighbouring countries, including ukraine, the text of which is now completed and ready for submission to the european parliament for approval, in accordance with the treaty on the functioning of the european union. as this is another step in the pursuit of the objectives which led to the creation of the common market, i approve and welcome the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and ukraine, of the other part, on the general principles governing ukraine's participation in union programmes.

in writing. - i support this report because it is in the interest of the regions concerned to establish a legal basis for trade between the eu and greenland, in this case under the rules of the eu internal market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'imports of fishery products from greenland', which aims to apply the rules of the internal market to these imports, provided that greenland undertakes to transpose european legislation, in particular on food safety and animal health. i do, however, think that the legal basis of the proposal should be adapted so that the act takes the form of a regulation rather than a council decision.
in writing. − this proposal lays down the general rules for trade between the eu and greenland in fishery products, live bivalve molluscs, echinoderms, tunicates, marine gastropods and by-products thereof, among others. member states shall authorise the import of products from greenland in accordance with union legislation on internal trade. the import of products into the union will be subject to a number of conditions, including the effective transposition and application of the applicable rules laid down in union legislation on animal health and food safety. like the rapporteur, i believe that the proposed act should have been adopted in a codecision procedure and that parliament should exercise its legislative rights in similar cases in the future.
in writing. − greenland's exports of fishery products represent about 82% of total exports, amounting to eur 255 million in 2007. the majority (87%) went to the eu, notably denmark (97%). the committee on legal affairs unanimously adopted an opinion supporting the request that the legal basis for the proposed legislative act be articles 43 (2) and 204 tfeu as well as the sole article of the protocol (no 34) on the special arrangements for greenland instead of the legal basis chosen by the commission - i.e. article 203 tfeu. i therefore agree with the adoption of the resolution, given that the subject is not the content of the draft legislative resolution but a legal question and given the consensus reached.
in writing. the major debate on this report is incidental to the subject which motivates it. in particular, the european parliament's committee on fisheries expressed its disagreement with the legal basis chosen by the commission for the presentation of this proposal - article 203 tfeu, which provides that the council, after consulting the european parliament, is to decide on 'the provisions relating to the modalities and the procedure for the association of the countries and territories with the union'. the committee on fisheries considered that article 43 (2) on the ordinary legislative procedure (co-legislation) and article 204 tfeu, as well as the sole article of the protocol (no 34) on the special arrangements for greenland, should be adopted as the legal basis. this position was supported by the committee on legal affairs in an opinion. on the sidelines of this discussion, there remains the relevant issue which should be the substance of the report: the definition of the rules applicable to imports into the eu of fishery products from greenland. the main exports of fishery products from greenland include shrimp (59%), greenland halibut (23%), cod (9,5%), shoe-fish (1,9%), molluscs (1,4%) and fry (1,3%).
in writing. − with the establishment of the rules on trade between the eu and greenland for fishery products, live bivalve molluscs, echinoderms, tunicates, marine gastropods and their by-products, imports from greenland are now in line with eu legislation. imports of products into the union have to be subject to the applicable rules laid down in union legislation as regards matters of animal health and food safety. that is why it is important that this report be adopted.
in writing. − on 26 april 2010, the european parliament was consulted by the council on this proposal under the consultation procedure provided for in article 203 tfeu. the committee on fisheries and the legal service of the ep expressed serious doubts about the choice of legal basis by the commission - i.e. article 203 tfeu - and instead suggested as the relevant legal basis articles 43 (2) and 204 tfeu as well as the single article of the protocol (no 34) on the special arrangements for greenland. the commission proposal has been amended in accordance with the report which is now being put to the vote, following the recommendations of the committee on legal affairs. i shall vote in favour of this report and i hope that it will be adopted at first reading.

in writing. - the progress made over the last ten years towards the creation of a common european asylum system has been enormous. however, there are still important differences between national provisions and in their implementation, which must be overcome if we are to establish by 2012 a common area of protection and solidarity based, inter alia, on a common asylum procedure. the main objective is that, irrespective of the member state in which people lodge their asylum application, they should be able to benefit from a high and equivalent level of treatment throughout the union. this is why this thorough revision of the procedures directive is so important, as it should allow for an accessible, fair and effective procedure. the commission's initiative is generally positive, allowing for greater coherence and harmonisation, improved protection standards and improved quality and efficiency of procedures. i commend the rapporteur for her work and commitment, but i am sorry that in some of her proposals she has gone a little too far, which makes it impossible to reach agreement with the council on this initiative which is so urgent and necessary to make the asylum process more efficient and to prevent abuse.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that these measures contribute to the creation of a fair and effective common european asylum system. these measures have a direct impact on the lives of people seeking protection, but they also help to strengthen the european union's capacity to create a genuine area of freedom, security and justice.
in writing. - the european union and its member states have long been working towards a common european asylum system (ceas). it is easy to understand the complexity and the complexity of attempts to do so, since this matter touches the very heart of state powers in relation to foreigners. the commission has been submitting proposals to parliament and the council to provide appropriate solutions to the problems identified in the meantime. the 'procedures' directive, the recast of which was proposed by the commission on 21 october 2009, is part of this improvement effort. despite the progress made, we are still far from the harmonization that many people want. the strengthening of the harmonization of procedures and guarantees could contribute positively to the clarification of the procedure and the proposal for a revision of the directive is therefore appropriate.
in writing. - after the entry into force of the amsterdam treaty in 1999, the creation of a common european asylum system (ceas) was initiated. in december 2005, with the aim of harmonising the legal procedures of the member states, council directive 2005/85/ec was adopted, laying down the rules for granting and withdrawing 'refugee status'. recent social and political upheavals in several countries, notably in north africa and the middle east, have put issues related to asylum applications in the european union (eu) on the agenda. indeed, refugees, when they cross a border, should not be persecuted or received with suspicion. i therefore welcome the adoption of this proposal which ends the manichean view of this problem by recognising that the right to asylum is a fundamental right and must be treated fairly and equitably by the member states. i welcome the rapporteur's recommendations to increase the number of legal aid services, since these are vulnerable people who lack effective guarantees, to improve procedures and to provide greater guarantees for applicants, especially minors.
in writing. the proposal for a directive on the rules applicable to the granting and withdrawal of international protection in the member states follows the approach for the establishment of a common asylum system (cas). however, it should be understood that this 'harmonisation' at the legal level is moving in parallel with the whole of the european union's foreign policy and the hypocritical positions on immigration and support for refugees. the situation in lampedusa, where thousands of refugees are without adequate protection, is a clear example of this, in addition to the hundreds or thousands who are dying on the boats crossing the mediterranean, as is unfortunately happening once again. we are deeply concerned about the scale of the present problem, particularly in view of what is happening in the serious conflicts of war, with particular emphasis on the situation in libya. we also stress that this proposal for a directive contains aspects which ultimately restrict and condition the right to asylum, in particular by limiting the sovereign right of each member state to decide on its own options and procedures in the field of asylum.
in writing. the proposal for a directive voted today in the european parliament on the rules applicable to the granting and withdrawal of international protection in the member states follows the approach for the establishment of a common asylum system (cas). however, it should be understood that this 'harmonisation' is not legally separate from the whole of the european union's foreign policy, nor from the hypocritical positions on immigration and support for refugees, as in the case of lampedusa, where thousands of refugees are without adequate protection, in addition to the hundreds or thousands who are dying on the boats crossing the mediterranean. we are deeply concerned about the scale of the present problem, particularly in view of what is happening in the serious conflicts of war, with particular emphasis on the situation in libya. we also stress that this proposal for a directive contains aspects which ultimately restrict and condition access to and the right to asylum, particularly as regards the sovereign right of each member state to decide on its own options and procedures in the field of asylum. that is why we are critical of this report.
in writing. - more than 10 years have passed since work began on the creation of a common european asylum system (ceas) following the entry into force of the treaty of amsterdam in may 1999, on the basis of the principles adopted at the tampere european council. in a first phase of the esaw (1999-2005), the objective was set to harmonise the legal frameworks of the member states on the basis of common minimum standards. there is still a long way to go before genuine harmonization can take place, but we must be aware that only the strengthening and harmonization of procedures and the guarantees that they provide will make it possible to build a common system. in this context, a thorough review of the procedures directive is absolutely necessary to ensure an accessible, fair and effective procedure in the interest of both asylum seekers and member states.
in writing. - since may 1999, following the entry into force of the treaty of amsterdam, work has begun on the establishment of a common european asylum system (ceas), based on the principles adopted by the tampere european council. the path has seen significant advances. the proposal now put forward for a thorough review and recast of the procedures directive is another step forward. the differences which still exist between national provisions and their application are the reason for the present amendments, which were totally incompatible with a common european asylum system. the common european asylum system is intended to ensure that, in whatever member state the application for asylum is lodged, that person enjoys a high level of treatment equivalent to that of the union as a whole. to this end, i agree with the need to establish a sound european legal framework to create an adequate and effective common european asylum system. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that only the strengthening and harmonization of procedures and the guarantees that they provide will make it possible to build a common system.
in writing. - tourism has become increasingly important to european businesses and citizens in recent times. in this respect, it is important that statistics for the development of more effective tourism policies at european, national, regional and local level are as reliable as possible, as they are useful tools to support the decision-making process in companies and the private sector. i should also stress that it is important that the commission takes these suggestions as they are proposed.
in writing. - tourism is an important sector of the european economy, with some 1.8 million businesses, mainly smes, employing some 9.7 million workers. the tourism industry is estimated to produce more than 5% of the eu's gdp. with the presentation of communication com ((2010) 352), the commission intends to define a new policy framework for tourism in europe, seeking to strengthen this sector through coordinated action at eu level that complements member states' initiatives. thus, for the new policy framework to be successful, sound decisions must be taken based on reliable and comparable statistical data. this report, which has been supported by me, recognises the important role of statistics in developing more effective tourism policies at european, national, regional and local level, and is a useful tool to support the decision-making process. it also supports the establishment of a common regulatory framework for the systematic production of european statistics on tourism, through the collection, compilation, processing and transmission of harmonised european statistics on tourism supply and demand by the member states.
in writing. − in several member states, such as my own, portugal, the tourism industry is an important part of the economy and has an intrinsic potential to generate new sources of employment and economic growth. tourism is the third largest european socioeconomic activity, producing over 5% of the eu's gdp. it continues to be the world's most popular tourist destination, accounting for about 40% of global arrivals in 2008. the eu intends to define a new policy framework for tourism with the aim of strengthening this sector so that it can meet the major challenges of climate change, demographic trends, globalisation, etc. through coordinated action that complements member states' initiatives. the compilation of data on tourism allows for a better knowledge of the volume of this sector, its characteristics, the profile of tourists, the various patterns of travel, which contributes not only to the correct formulation of sector policies and business strategies, but also to a better understanding of the socioeconomic implications of this sector. i therefore support the updating and optimisation of the current statistical system so that we can have reliable and comparable statistical data.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that statistics on tourism contribute to the development of more effective policies and are a useful tool to support decision-making in business and the private sector. this new regulation will undoubtedly improve the timeliness, comparability and completeness of tourism statistics as well as the efficiency of data processing.
in writing. − according to the report, europe remains the world's number one tourist destination, with tourism being the third largest socioeconomic activity in the eu, with some 1.8 million businesses, mainly smes, 9.7 million jobs and a production equivalent to 5% of gdp. it is therefore an activity which must be properly monitored, regulated and promoted, especially in the specific context of economic recovery and the need to increase the production of tradable goods. this is true for the eu as a whole, but it is particularly important for portugal, which has long been committed to tourism as a particularly dynamic economic activity with a lot of potential for growth. in this context, and in view of the importance of a thorough and realistic knowledge of the reality of tourism in the development of appropriate policies, the commission's proposal to update and optimise the legal framework for european tourism statistics which we are voting on today is important.
in writing. − this report focuses on an area that is crucial for the future of the european union (eu): tourism. despite the global crisis in 2010, according to the world tourism organization (unwto), the sector grew by 2%, despite political upheavals in various parts of the world. at european level, in addition to growing at a steady pace, tourism comprises 1.8 million businesses - the vast majority smes - and provides 9.7 million jobs, being the third largest socioeconomic activity in the eu, producing more than 5% of gross domestic product (gdp). in addition, europe is the world's leading tourist destination with 40% of tourist arrivals. this is an essential activity for the achievement of the objectives set out in the europa2020 strategy. this regulation updates the existing legislation, especially as regards the collection and processing of data on accommodation and accessibility for people with reduced mobility - which are essential in preparing the new european tourism strategy. i welcome the adoption of this proposal, which, in addition to creating a pilot study programme to be carried out by the member states, will include data on rural tourism and agro-tourism (more than 50 000 accommodation facilities are available) managed mainly by smes.
in writing. the usefulness of statistical information depends on its comparability in time and space, which implies the adoption of a set of common definitions and nomenclatures. in the case of tourism, the sector involves concepts and definitions which have long remained unclear, making it difficult to obtain reliable and credible information. it is therefore necessary to clarify and harmonise criteria and definitions to obtain comparable data. the existence of these statistics is of great importance in determining the direct and indirect impacts of tourism on the economy, supporting the planning and development of new tourism options or the readaptation of existing ones. the proposal in the report aims to improve the timeliness, comparability and completeness of the statistics transmitted, as well as the efficiency of data processing, including better data validation. it also aims to adapt the legal framework to reflect the latest trends in the sector by introducing new variables, for example on day trips. for these reasons we voted in favour.

in writing. − regulation (ec) no 861/2006 establishes community financial measures relating to the implementation of the common fisheries policy and the law of the sea and is an important financial instrument of the european union in the fisheries sector. since the adoption of this regulation, several elements of the legislation have evolved. the commission proposes to amend it in order to ensure consistency between all the elements of the legislative framework and also to clarify the scope of some of the actions financed. i supported this report because it proposes some amendments to the commission proposal which will help to clarify the legislation, taking into account the recent developments in the fisheries sector and its future prospects, in particular: the possibility of increasing community co-financing (from 50% to 60%), which is an added value for the development of the fisheries sector in portugal; the increasing importance attached to aquaculture, which justifies the introduction of the possibility of collecting, managing and using environmental data, in addition to socioeconomic data, also in this field.

in writing. the report is based on a proposal for a european parliament and council regulation amending regulation (ec) no 861/2006 of 22 may 2006 laying down financial measures for the implementation of the common fisheries policy (cfp) and the law of the sea. since 2006, several aspects of the abovementioned regulation have evolved and are outdated, and therefore it is necessary to amend it. this proposal is based on the existing regulation and aims to safeguard coastal activities by financing the modernisation of the sector, in particular equipment and computerisation. the amendments tabled by the commission have been taken into account, as have other contributions which significantly improve the previous regulation, in particular the financing of investment, which is essential to have scientific, accurate and up-to-date data to enable us to take the measures required in each situation on the basis of sound evidence, and the increase in co-financing rates. i therefore support this proposal for a regulation.

in writing. − in 2008, the commission presented a proposal for a council regulation on the conservation of fishery resources through technical measures which was intended to replace an earlier regulation. such a proposal was not approved and regulation (ec) no 1288/2009 was adopted for reasons of legal certainty in order to maintain the proper conservation and management of marine resources, which established transitional measures from 1 january until the end of june 2011. in the light of the obligations arising from the lisbon treaty, in 2010 the commission withdrew its proposal for a council regulation on the conservation of fishery resources through technical measures. the basic principles on technical measures should now be incorporated into a new basic regulation on the reform of the common fisheries policy, with a proposal to this effect expected in 2011. as there is currently no other legislation in force, it is proposed that the validity of that regulation be extended for a further period of 18 months, i.e. until 1 january 2013. in view of the arguments of legal certainty and protection which have been put forward, i believe that this extension deserves support. i hope that this additional time will allow us to assess the impact of the measures in force.
in writing. - the fisheries sector is fundamental to the european union, not only for food reasons but also for environmental reasons, as aquatic ecosystems are at stake. the european parliament, aware of the importance of this sector, has often debated this matter. in 2009, it adopted resolution a&-0206/2009 on the need to conserve fisheries resources in the atlantic ocean and the north sea. the current regulation, adopted in 2008, establishes a set of transitional measures which were intended to apply until june 2011, the date foreseen for the entry into force of a new legal framework under the common fisheries policy. however, the commission was not able to submit a proposal for a regulation. the commission therefore requests an extension of the current regulation until 1 january 2013, by which time it expects the eu to have legislation in place, to be adopted in accordance with the co-decision procedure laid down by the lisbon treaty, by the council and by the parliament and to be supported by up-to-date scientific studies, so that it does not jeopardise the planet's marine resources. in this respect, i agree that the current regulation should remain in force until 1 january 2013.

in writing. − the 2012 budget is being discussed at a time when member states, many of them, are facing extreme budgetary restraint and austerity needs, which is why the budget for the functioning of this parliament, as the rapporteur mentions, should 'respond with the required quality and efficiency and use rigorous budgetary management processes in order to achieve savings'. the citizens of europe would not understand if, when they are asked to make sacrifices in their own countries, the european union failed to show restraint and efficiency in the management of its own resources. the citizens are asking us to manage the resources allocated to us properly and to save wherever possible. the report by my colleague josé manuel fernandes gives some good hints in this regard. for reasons of ethics, especially when we are asking european citizens, and in particular the portuguese, to make sacrifices, i have decided not to vote for any amendment affecting my remuneration or the exercise of my duties as a member of parliament.
in writing. - despite the fact that the crisis of capitalism is hitting hard at workers and the general population and that austerity measures are geared towards those who have the least, the community budgets have not reflected the need to change the direction of the policies in the eu which are responsible for this crisis. this report does not concern the guidelines for the general budget of the eu. however, it cannot be disconnected from the context in which we live. in addition to the considerations we made during the debate in plenary, we are concerned that the framework proposed will facilitate job insecurity, worsening the situation of workers who after decades of service are still without a permanent employment contract, as well as the 'transfer' of many workers to temporary work companies, so we do not see any amendment proposals which, by advocating savings in parliament, open up space for insecurity.
in writing. - this report on the european parliament's budget reflects the contradictions affecting most of the political forces represented here. although they are not the guidelines for the budget of the european union, they are not detached from the basic policies that drive their destinies. section i - parliament - of the 2012 estimate, although containing adjustments to parliament's expenditure by reducing the external provision of services and other minor expenditure, but also increasing the subsidy and travel items, reflects an increase of 2,3% compared to the same section of the 2011 budget. we are concerned that the proposed framework will facilitate job insecurity, worsening the situation of workers who, after decades of service, are still without a permanent employment contract, in addition to the transfer of workers to temporary work companies, so we do not see ourselves in amendment proposals which, by advocating savings in parliament, make room for insecurity and seek to favour the financing of european parties and european political foundations, although we think that members should set an example by changing their financial statute, a statute against which we voted by substantially increasing their salaries. for all these reasons we voted against this report.
in writing. − the crisis that has struck the world and the difficult economic and budgetary conditions in the member states have led parliament to show responsibility and budgetary restraint in the 2012 financial year, without calling into question the ambitious objectives it has set itself, including that of legislative excellence. this budget of the european parliament for next year will have an increase below the rate of inflation. the budget is expected to amount to eur 1.725 billion, an increase of 2.3% in 2012, below the eu-27 inflation rate of 2.8%. it is this kind of concern that must always be present when discussing community budgets so that all the citizens of the member states can see themselves in european policies and have their contributions properly implemented.
in writing. - i would first of all like to congratulate the rapporteur on the work he has done. it is always a demanding subject, but in the times of containment we live in it is becoming especially demanding. the economic and budgetary conditions in which all member states are now found are not unknown to this parliament, which should show responsibility and budgetary restraint in the 2012 financial year while maintaining the quality of its work. the budget was cut in real terms by 2,3% compared to the 2011 budget and by a total cut of eur 48,9 million compared to the draft estimates. this is due in particular to cuts in expenditure on buildings. i would like to stress the concern of the rapporteur, who follows the concern of the group, to focus on young people. to this end, the rapporteur proposes a reduction of the ceiling of heading 5 of the 2012 multiannual financial framework by eur 100 million and a corresponding increase of other headings in favour of youth. this is a balanced report which takes due account of the budgetary constraints needed in times of crisis and the maintenance of the conditions for profitable and quality work. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, because i believe that in the current crisis context, the european parliament and the other eu institutions must act with responsibility and restraint, using rigorous budgetary management processes to promote the optimisation of resources and to achieve savings. i would also like to publicly express my appreciation for the excellent work done by the rapporteur, my colleague mr josé manuel fernandes.
in writing. − in the face of difficult economic and budgetary conditions in the member states, parliament should show responsibility and budgetary restraint in the 2012 financial year, without, however, undermining the objective of legislative excellence. the budget in question was cut in real terms by 2,3% compared to the 2011 budget and by a total cut of eur 48,9 million compared to the draft estimates. this is due in particular to cuts in expenditure on buildings and in costs for the 18 new meps and the enlargement to croatia. these last two items will be the subject of an amending budget at a later date. the epp group believes that the focus on young people is a key priority at the moment. the rapporteur therefore proposes a reduction of the ceiling of heading 5 of the 2012 multiannual financial framework by eur 100 million and a corresponding increase of other headings in favour of youth. finally, i would like to emphasize that the elimination of the budget line for the house of european history will not affect its viability, since the amount will be transferred to another heading, in accordance with a transparent procedure approved by the budgetary authority.
in writing. − i approve this resolution which aims to amend regulation no 1924/2006 of the european parliament and of the council on nutrition and health complaints made about food which were only authorised by the commission under that regulation. i agree with this resolution because it concerns a health complaint on the permitted list of complaints for the use of infant milk from 6 months of age and above, since dha has detected a type of acid added to milk formula.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on 'authorisation and refusal of authorisation of certain health claims made on foods for children's development and health', as there is no recognised scientific evidence to show that synthesised dha added to milk powder and other infant foods, and which is different from the dha found in breast milk, contributes to the visual development of children. i therefore consider that until conclusive studies are available the nutrition claim should not be authorised.
in writing. - the issue of possible acceptable claims in food labelling (or even advertising) is of the utmost importance because it can lead to the creation of false expectations or to the adoption of behaviour that has no scientific support. in this regard, any claim to be added to the list of permitted claims should be weighted according to the latest scientific state of the art so that it is duly substantiated, as the commission maintains that this is the case here, where it is considered proven that docosahexaenoic acid ('dha') contributes to normal visual development in children up to 12 months of age.
in writing. the european parliament resolution concerns the draft regulation submitted by the commission on the authorisation and refusal of authorisation of certain health claims made on foods and referring to the reduction of disease risk or to children's development and health. the food of citizens in general and of children in particular must be given special attention by all european bodies, because it is a question of healthy growth and quality of life for people. the promotion of foods through claims may mislead consumers and violate scientifically advised claims. i therefore vote against this draft regulation, given the arguments put forward by the rapporteur on a matter as sensitive as it is important, because i believe that it does not fully protect the health of citizens, especially children.
in writing. the document opposes the adoption of the draft regulation proposed by the commission on 'the authorisation and refusal of authorisation of certain health claims made on foods and referring to the reduction of disease risk or to children's development and health', as it is not compatible with the aim and content of the regulation on nutrition and health claims made on foods. this is mainly due to problems resulting from the addition of dha to media other than breast milk, where it contributes to normal visual development in children up to 12 months of age. but the generally accepted scientific evidence demonstrates that the same synthesized dha added to formula and other infant foods is unclear. this means that there is no clear scientific consensus on the effect of dha-enriched formulas on infants, as they are used in formula and other infant foods in a biological environment other than breast milk. that is why we are opposed to the adoption of the draft commission regulation.
in writing. - i approve of this report as the increasingly globalised world requires the eu as a whole to make reproductive investment choices, agreeing with the position set out in this report that the commission and the council should start negotiating to start investments with third countries such as canada, india and china. i therefore consider it crucial that the ep ensures responsible behaviour by european investors abroad, while protecting the eu's rights to regulate in accordance with our public interest.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the proposed investment policy will meet the expectations of both investors and the states concerned, contributing to the strengthening of the competitiveness of the eu and its businesses. a coordinated european policy on international investment could have a major impact on job creation, not only in the eu but also in developing countries.
in writing. − according to articles 206 and 207 tfeu, foreign direct investment (fdi) is an exclusive competence of the eu. in addition to the management of bilateral investment treaties concluded, the union is required to define a future european investment policy that meets the expectations of investors and beneficiary countries and at the same time respects its external action objectives. the protection of investors should remain the first priority of investment agreements, but the commission is asked to present a clear definition of the investments to be protected. future agreements should be based on best practices drawn from member states' experience and take into account the needs of smes.
in writing. - this report addresses the issue of the future european policy on international investment. since the founding of the european union (eu), many bilateral investment treaties (bits) have been signed by member states (about 3,000 since 1959!). with the entry into force of the treaty on the financing of the european union, this matter has passed into the exclusive domain of the eu and is now part of the preparation of the future european investment policy, which needs to be discussed very carefully. this is a very important issue, because we are at a turning point and facing two challenges: to equip the eu with the tools to enable companies abroad to fulfil their investment programmes, and at the same time to keep europe as a leader in global investment. we live in a time of aggressive business activity and we need to be careful in choosing our business partners. i therefore agree with the rapporteur on this document that the prerogatives of the ep should be respected and that the negotiating procedures should be sent in time to avoid unnecessary delays and serious disruptions in the eu's relationship with these countries.
in writing. − foreign direct investment (fdi) is defined as 'long-term investments which allow the acquisition of at least 10% of the capital/shares of a company and give the investor control over the management of that company'. with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, fdi became the exclusive competence of the eu, whose main tasks are to manage the existing bilateral investment treaties (bits) and to define a european investment policy 'that meets the expectations of investors and beneficiary states'. it is on the basis of these new powers that the implementation of a common investment policy is advocated. it is very questionable, to say the least, whether fdi brings the advertised value-adds to the 'beneficiary' countries. in particular, if it is conducted under the responsibility of the eu, in defence of the interests which it defends. the example of portugal is illustrative. while one of the serious problems facing the portuguese economy is the continued decline in investment - reflected in low rates of economic growth and rising unemployment - foreign direct investment has been a major feature of the portuguese economy over the years. the reality is, however, that increasing shares of the wealth produced in portugal are being transferred abroad.
in writing. − according to the definition of the eu court of justice, fdi is a long-term investment, which allows the acquisition of at least 10% of the capital/shares of a company and gives the investor control over the management of that company. with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, fdi has become the exclusive competence of the eu, whose main tasks are the management of the existing bits (bilateral investment treaties) and the definition of a european investment policy that meets the expectations of investors and beneficiary states. the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of national authorities responsible for the protection of the environment. but our position is different. in most cases, fdi does not solve the development problem of the countries where it is processed. we know what the multinationals are doing. they sustain themselves while making fabulous profits and endorsements. then, at the slightest failure, they look elsewhere and do not take into account the unemployment and the blockage to development that they create. portugal is unfortunately well aware of this situation.
in writing. − the eu has exclusive competence when it comes to foreign direct investment (fdi) as defined in articles 206 and 207 tfeu the bilateral investment treaties concluded must be managed and the union must define a future european investment policy that meets the expectations of investors and beneficiary countries. it is important that investors are protected, but the commission is asked to present a clear definition of the investments that should be protected. in future, agreements should build on past good practice and also take account of the needs of smes.
in writing. − under articles 206 and 207 tfeu, foreign direct investment (fdi) is an exclusive competence of the european union. this highly consequential development poses a dual challenge, both for the management of the more than 1200 bilateral investment treaties (bits) already concluded by the member states and for the definition of a future european investment policy that meets the expectations of investors and beneficiary states, while respecting the objectives of the eu's external action. a coherent, sound and effective investment policy requires an unequivocal definition of foreign direct investment and a clear definition of its scope. i voted in favour of this report and highlighted the ep's call on the commission to establish a clear definition of investments to be protected, including both fdi and portfolio investments, stating that investments of a speculative nature, as defined by the commission, should not be protected.
in writing. - under the lisbon treaty, foreign direct investment is now the exclusive competence of the european union. this presents a twofold challenge: firstly, to manage the existing bilateral investment treaties between member states and, secondly, to define a european investment policy that meets the expectations of investors, beneficiary states and the interests of the eu. an integrated and coherent policy that promotes high-quality investment and contributes positively to economic progress and sustainable development worldwide is essential. to this end, a clear definition of the investments to be protected should be made, with the exception of those of a speculative nature which should not be protected. it would be useful to introduce the term 'eu investor' and to define strictly 'foreign investor'. the identification of good practices arising from the experience of the member states and the observance of basic standards such as non-discrimination, fair and equitable treatment and protection against direct and indirect expropriation will lay the foundations for a coherent european policy in this field. these measures and a definition of the sharing of responsibilities between the eu and the states will help to create conditions for smes to invest abroad.

in writing. - fraud, as the rapporteur very well defines it, is voluntary irregular behaviour which constitutes a criminal offence and an irregularity means the breach of a rule. this is the defining framework that should make us zero tolerance for fraud and set as our objective, as i said in relation to the 2008 report, to achieve a zero level of financial irregularities in the eu. as i pointed out in a question at the end of last year, following an investigation by the financial times, there are serious doubts about the purpose and effectiveness of the cohesion fund. these doubts cannot die in the pages of the newspapers. at the same time, this report also regrets that a large amount of eu funds continues to be misused and calls on the commission to take appropriate action to ensure the swift recovery of these funds. this misuse of community funds requires better administration and control in the use of funds and provision should be made for effective application of sanctions to member states which do not make good use of the funds received. only then can we move towards the desirable zero fraud framework in the eu.
in writing. − this report focuses on the commission's report to the european parliament (ep) and the council on the protection of the european union's financial interests fight against fraud annual report 2009 (com (2010) 382) and aims to comply with article 325 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) which obliges the commission and all member states to safeguard the eu's financial interests and obliges the commission, in accordance with paragraph 2 of that article, to submit a detailed report to the ep and the council on an annual basis. despite the improvements made in recent years, it is essential to continue to work to prevent any kind of fraud, although this is also combated by member states' bodies. i agree with the proposals put forward by the rapporteur, which should be complemented by the recommendations suggested during the debate, in particular the need to clarify the concepts of 'fraud' and 'irregularities', as this represents behaviour which is deliberately detrimental to the eu's interests, while these should be the subject of a better management system. i hope that the 2010 report, incorporating the suggestions made, will be of a higher quality than the one of 2009.
in writing. − the report summarises the available statistics on irregularities reported by member states in a number of areas, including agricultural policy, cohesion policy, pre-accession funds and the collection of the eu's traditional own resources. during 2009, numerous irregularities were detected in the above areas in different member states. many of these irregularities are detected and/or reported late, jeopardising the protection and sound use of public financial resources. we welcome the criticisms and comments made by the rapporteur on the need to put in place an effective recovery system. the overall recovery rate is frankly low. we stress, however, that the fight against fraud and corruption must, for various reasons and, above all, for reasons of efficiency, be carried out at a level as close as possible to that at which these phenomena occur. the fight against fraud and corruption in each member state must therefore be strengthened, and common eu legislation alone is not a panacea for the phenomenon.
in writing. − it is a report on financial interests which summarises the statistics on irregularities reported by the member states in various fields, including agricultural policy, cohesion policy, pre-accession funds and the collection of the eu's traditional own resources. during the period 2009 numerous irregularities were detected in these areas and in different member states. many of these irregularities are detected and/or reported late, jeopardising the protection of taxpayers' money. we support the criticism raised by the rapporteur regarding the need to put in place an effective recovery system. the overall rate of recovery of the amounts recovered is currently well below what would be desirable. however, we stress that more important than common eu legislation in the fight against corruption and fraud, it is necessary that the fight against fraud and corruption be put into practice in each member state. in any case, we would point out that monitoring cannot be confused with excessive bureaucracy which jeopardises the rights of those who use the aid, especially small social organisations and smes.
in writing. − this report highlights the level of irregularities and fraud in each member state in the use of european union funds. the increase in the number of reported cases was caused by the introduction of new communication technologies. i believe that everything must be done to hold member states accountable and to discipline them in respect of fraud and irregularities. the necessary information on each member state should be available in order to increase the effectiveness of the control and supervision systems and to ensure a true picture of the situation. member states should introduce the irregularity management system to improve their compliance with their reporting obligations to the european institutions. agriculture, cohesion policy and pre-accession funds are areas where irregularity and fraud rates are high. measures are therefore needed to increase monitoring, detection and correction. we must be concerned about creating a transparent and efficient system for the management and application of community funds.

in writing. − strengthening european economic governance, coordinating the implementation of the eu 2020 strategy and relaunching the single market are key elements for the revitalisation of the european economy. the single market must be competitive, making a positive contribution to the daily lives of workers, students, pensioners and citizens in general, as well as to businesses, in particular smes; one of the main challenges for relaunching the single market is to ensure leadership, commitment and coordination at political level. i believe that good governance of the single market can only be achieved by good quality and up-to-date information on its functioning. this should be done by using appropriate tools for monitoring and evaluating single market policies to link the different phases of the policy cycle from design to implementation. it is also important that member states should engage in the evaluation and monitoring of single market rules.
in writing. the commission's communication on the single market act followed up the report by mario monti on a new strategy for the single market. this is the context in which this report is to be put. the objectives are clear: to strengthen free competition and to accelerate the process of liberalization and privatization in various sectors of economic activity and social life. the rhetoric of the report tends to obscure its real intentions, with the symptomatic statement that it seeks to 'strengthen development based on a highly competitive social market economy, aiming at full employment and social progress', coupled with a 'high level of environmental protection and improvement'. it is a contradictory and demagogic speech, which goes on to say that 'businesses, especially smes, and europeans' will be 'at the centre of the single market'. they will certainly be at the centre of its negative consequences - which have become so evident over the last decades of the single market. the council conclusions of 25 march and the 'pact for the euro plus' adopted there illustrate the war waged against workers, young people and pensioners, and in the end against the general population.
in writing. this report is part of the package of the commission's communication on the single market act, whose proposal follows up the report by mario monti entitled 'a new strategy for the single market'. the aim is to strengthen free competition and to speed up the process of liberalisation and privatisation, although the whole document is covered with language that seeks to hide its real intentions, writing, for example, that it is intended to 'strengthen development based on a highly competitive social market economy, aiming at full employment and social progress, with a high level of protection and improvement of the quality of the environment', adding that it is thus intended to put companies, especially smes, and europeans at the centre of the single market. but in fact, it is enough to read the conclusions of the council of 25 march and above all the euro plus pact, which launches a war against the world of work, collective bargaining, trade unions, pensioners and their right to pensions and pensions, to see what is being sought. the central objectives are to accelerate the process of capitalist concentration and accumulation in favour of monopoly groups, and to put an end to any attempt to protect smes, workers and public services. that is why we are voting against.

in writing. - i approve this report amending directive 2000/75/ec. both the council and the ep agreed to change the legal basis because the commission proposal was submitted before the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. these changes are justified, in my view, by the spread of the disease and the scientific discovery of a vaccine which does not pose the risks posed by the previous one.
in writing. - i welcome the amendments to this directive which make the rules on vaccination more flexible. new technologies have made available 'inactivated vaccines' against bluetongue, which do not pose risks to unvaccinated animals. it is now agreed that vaccination with inactivated vaccines is the best tool for the control of bluetongue and for the prevention of clinical disease in the union. the widespread use of these vaccines during the vaccination campaign in 2008 and 2009 resulted in a significant improvement in the health situation. i call for the current vaccination rules laid down in directive 2000/75/ec to be amended to take account of recent technological developments in vaccine production, in order to ensure better control of the spread of the bluetongue virus and to reduce the burden on the agricultural sector due to this disease.
in writing. − traditionally, vaccination against bluetongue was carried out with live attenuated virus vaccines, which entailed a number of restrictions on vaccination in order to prevent the spread of the virus to unvaccinated animals. however, scientific developments have allowed the creation of new inactivated vaccines. unlike ' live attenuated vaccines', these can be used safely and without restrictions, as there is no longer a risk of circulating any active virus. in view of the serious consequences of bluetongue for livestock farming, all measures to make vaccination easier and more effective should be taken in order to protect livestock breeders from animal losses and ultimately food safety.
in writing. − bluetongue, also known as blue tongue, is a disease that mainly affects ruminant animals such as sheep, goats and cattle and can become epidemic when environmental and climatic conditions are favourable, particularly in late summer and early autumn. although there is no record of any human infection, it is essential to know about it and seek to implement measures that lead to its eradication. at european level, the disease has been manifested first in southern, and then in central and northern europe. thanks to successive vaccination campaigns co-financed by the european union. the use of certain vaccines may not eradicate the disease but allow it to continue to circulate. a vaccine has been developed to control and prevent the disease in the eu, but its use is limited by current rules. the current directive therefore needs to be amended. whereas this proposal for a directive amending directive 2000/75/ec of the european parliament and of the council is in line with the animal health strategy (2007-2013) and aims at a more flexible approach to the vaccination system thus contributing to the improvement of the control of the most serious animal diseases, i am voting in favour of this amendment;
in writing. - the main objective of this report is to update directive 2000/75/ec, which adopts specific provisions on measures to control and eradicate bluetongue. over the past few years, advances have been made in the area of animal vaccination. the risk posed by so-called 'live attenuated vaccines' has now been removed, as new inactivated vaccines are now available. these inactivated vaccines, unlike ' live attenuated vaccines' do not pose a risk of undesirable circulation of the vaccine virus and can be used safely outside restricted areas. that is what the report says. we believe that greater flexibility in the vaccination of bluetongue, taking into account technological developments in the production of vaccines, will contribute to better control of the disease and to reducing the burden it imposes on the agricultural sector. we also believe that the amendments to this directive should be implemented as soon as possible, for the benefit of the agricultural sector.
in writing. − vaccination against bluetongue was carried out with live attenuated virus vaccines, which entailed a number of restrictions on vaccination in order to prevent the spread of the virus to unvaccinated animals. however, recent technological developments have led to the emergence of new vaccines with the absence of live viruses. these new vaccines can be used with a higher level of safety and without any restrictions, as there is no longer any risk in the circulation of any active virus. in view of the serious consequences of bluetongue for livestock holdings, all measures facilitating good vaccination practices should be adopted in order to protect breeders from the loss of animals, which often leads to fatal losses for those holdings.
in writing. - the commission proposal on vaccination against bluetongue, now improved by this report, aims to make the rules on vaccination against bluetongue more flexible, in particular by allowing inactivated vaccines to be used outside areas subject to animal movement restrictions. the new rules will help member states to make the use of vaccines to control bluetongue more effective and reduce the burden of bluetongue on the agricultural sector. in fact, since 2004, the measures restricting mobility and marketing have imposed significant constraints on the producers concerned, compromising normal trade flows within a restricted zone and always with increased costs for the producers. i therefore voted in favour of the report on vaccination against blue tongue.

in writing. - i regret that the european parliament has not been able to draw the lessons from what has happened in japan. persisting in denying the great risks of using nuclear energy is not the best way of serving our citizens. the ep plenary was unable to pass a resolution in the face of the unenlightening spectacle of groups canceling each other out, rejecting each other's proposals without being able to pass anything in common. the transnational nature of the risks and consequences of accidents and the safety of the population should have been more pronounced. strengthening nuclear safety, testing for vulnerabilities, freezing nuclear expansion projects in europe and investing more effectively in clean energy and energy conservation should have been obvious conclusions. to close our eyes to what happened in japan and pretend that nothing happened is foolish and dangerous. calling for greater transparency and information on risks and accidents is something that chernobyl and fukushima have only made more evident.
in writing. - on 11 march, japan was struck by a very serious earthquake followed by a tsunami, which triggered the largest nuclear crisis in its history. the fukushima nuclear power station suffered severe structural damage and has since been at imminent risk of a major nuclear disaster. these events have led to a wave of reactions in europe, with commissioner oettinger calling for an extraordinary meeting of the international atomic energy agency; the german chancellor suspending for three months the decision to extend the life of the country's nuclear power stations; and the austrian environment minister, nikolaus berlakivich, demanding tests be carried out on european power stations. it is essential that the full consequences of the fukushima disaster be removed, particularly as regards the safety rules imposed on european nuclear power stations, in order to ensure their safety and ultimately the safety of europeans. once again, i take this opportunity to convey to all those affected by the disaster in japan my sincere condolences and my solidarity at this difficult time.
in writing. the problems with the fukushima nuclear power plant have put the discussion on the energy from nuclear fusion on the agenda, since 30% of the energy consumed in the european union comes from this source, with countries producing around 80%, such as france, and countries without nuclear power plants such as portugal and austria. it is therefore imperative that the eu promote a safety verification programme for its nuclear power plants, including through the performance of so-called 'strength tests'. these assessments should be based on a rigorous and harmonised assessment model, covering all types of possible risks in a realistic european scenario, and be carried out by the end of the current year in an independent and coordinated manner, covering all existing and planned nuclear installations in the eu; nuclear energy is now indispensable to ensuring europe's low-carbon energy supply. however, we must move towards greater energy efficiency and increased renewable energy. the commission and the member states should focus on modernising and expanding european energy infrastructure and on interconnecting networks to ensure a reliable energy supply.
in writing. − ensuring the safety of nuclear installations and avoiding accident risks in every possible way are important issues addressed in this resolution, which also calls on member states to impose a 'moratorium on the development and entry into service of new nuclear reactors, at least during the period of endurance testing'. we must, however, bear in mind that the tragedy in japan must not be an opportunity for lobbyists to advance or to retreat today to advance tomorrow. lessons must be learned seriously and from experience, and design and operational failures and deficiencies in other plants which may lead to accidents must be diagnosed. and also to take this experience into account in future energy developments. it is necessary that experts from the specialised bodies of the member states and also from the international atomic energy agency (iaea) be involved in this evaluation, while preserving their function, authority, autonomy and independence. recommendations at this level should be made by the eea as a technical, autonomous and independent body with the appropriate support of the eu and not the other way around. it is regrettable that this resolution is used as a pretext to support the so-called common energy policy and its objectives of liberalizing the energy sector.
in writing. - this motion for a resolution was not the best. so it was rejected, although it had some positive aspects, and so we abstained. ensuring the safety of nuclear installations and avoiding or minimising any risk of accident are important issues addressed in this resolution, which also calls on member states to impose a 'moratorium on the development and entry into service of new nuclear reactors, at least during the period of stress testing'. we must, however, bear in mind that the tragedy in japan must not be used as a catapult for economic interests to gain ground, to the detriment of the interests of the security of the people. instead, it is important to diagnose the design and operational failures and deficiencies of the plant which made the accident possible. it is necessary that experts from the member states' specialised agencies and also from the international atomic energy agency (iaea) be part of this evaluation, preserving their function, authority, autonomy and independence, and above all that the lessons be learned seriously and that the result of the analysis of this experience be incorporated into future developments in energy matters. we do not agree with interference in the energy policies of member states and third countries, and recommendations at this level should be made by the eea as a technical, autonomous and independent body, with the appropriate support of the eu.
in writing. the fukushima disaster reminded the planet that there is no zero risk for nuclear. the danger posed to mankind by nuclear energy is absolutely unsustainable, as are the risks added by the waste produced. we must therefore go beyond ensuring safety and improving safety testing. these two criteria would be a minimum condition for us to reach an agreement. the commission has not yet been able to secure an exit plan for the effective change in european energy policy, which will necessarily involve defining alternatives and phasing out the nuclear industry in europe. i voted against this resolution because i consider that none of the above assumptions have been guaranteed.
in writing. - in voting the resolution on nuclear safety after the fukushima accident i voted against the proposed amendment on co2 reduction targets for three reasons: (b) the objectives listed raise the eu's unilateral co2 reduction bar disproportionately; (c) such an ambitious - and in fact unrealistic - co2 reduction would only be acceptable if coupled with the introduction of a co2 tax on imports, otherwise it would seriously affect the competitiveness of european industry and lead european companies to relocate their production to countries without co2 restrictions, with serious effects on the eu economy and employment.
in writing. - the recent protests in several arab countries demonstrate that undemocratic and authoritarian regimes cannot guarantee credible stability and that democratic values are central to economic and political partnerships. i call on the authorities of bahrain, syria and yemen to respect the norms of international law on human rights and fundamental freedoms. it is necessary to start as soon as possible the process of open and meaningful political dialogue, with the participation of all democratic political forces and civil society, with a view to paving the way for genuine democracy, the lifting of the state of emergency and the implementation of genuine, ambitious and meaningful political, economic and social reforms, which are essential for long-term stability and development.

in writing. - the european union, by the example it has set throughout its existence, has a historic duty to denounce all violations of human rights and to fight for the right of peoples to self-determination, whether through denunciation or through development support programmes. the situation in bahrain - which has a strategic position for the balance of the gulf - where, beneath an apparent normality, there is a very tense situation with continuous detentions of people who are only accused of violating the right to freedom of expression; in syria, with protests in several cities being brutally suppressed despite eu calls for the rights to freedom of expression, assembly and association to be respected; and finally, in yemen, where the situation is deeply worrying, having already been condemned by the eu for the repression of protesters, it cannot leave us indifferent. i therefore support the measures proposed in this resolution, in particular the condemnation of those responsible for the massacres in these countries, and i hope that they will take effect as soon as possible so that these peoples will no longer be trampled underfoot. i also welcome the initiative to ask the un commission on human rights to condemn these violations of fundamental rights.
