in writing. − despite the technical and financial assistance provided over the years to the least developed countries, it must be recognised that most of them have not been able to rise above this status and maintain permanent weaknesses and needs. it is right to mention here, as the resolution adopted does, the exceptional circumstances of cape verde, which, despite its scarcity of resources, has managed to overcome some of the difficulties it was facing and to raise the living conditions of its population. i therefore congratulate the people of cape verde, their government and their parties, who have been able to conduct their work in a responsible and respectable manner, and today that portuguese-speaking country is an example for the less developed countries to follow. despite the limitations on trade and the problems of training and access to information and the means and units of production, it cannot be overstated that the backwardness of the least developed countries lies mainly in the incapacity of their policy-makers and the inefficiency of their institutions because their people are as capable as others.
in writing. the fourth united nations conference on the least developed countries (ldcs) will be held in istanbul, turkey, from 9 to 13 may. the eu, which has always been a leader in supporting developing countries through programmes to eradicate poverty - and whose financial allocation has tripled in recent years - is very committed to hosting this meeting. this parliament will also be represented by a delegation with well-founded proposals, although its observer status does not allow for much visibility, and i hope that it will be a strong impetus for us to win the 'battle' of sustainable development and equitable growth in these countries. given that all countries have responsibilities in supporting the least developed countries in order to meet the millennium development goals, i agree with the proposals contained in this joint motion for a resolution and i wish the target of halving the least developed countries by 2020 to be achieved. mdg-iv should support concrete measures that help address the development needs of the least developed countries, combat poverty and ensure decent income and livelihoods.
in writing. − in the context of the 4th united nations development conference, it is appropriate to consider the millennium development goals (mdgs) adopted by the united nations general assembly in 2000 and to assess their achievement, namely: eradicating poverty and hunger; promoting equality between men and women; increasing and improving maternal and child health care; combating hiv/aids; developing environmental sustainability; achieving universal primary education. as far as development policy is concerned, the dissonance between the words and the action of the eu is evident. the means at our disposal to eradicate poverty exist. as a result of scientific and technological development, they are actually expanding. but what we are seeing is the increase in poverty worldwide. they are the consequences of a system that is dominant on a global scale - capitalism, inherently unjust and unequal. we stress the importance of the alternative resolution tabled by the gue/ngl and the amendments tabled to the joint resolution (and unfortunately rejected by the majority), focusing, among other things, on issues such as food sovereignty and agricultural development and the need to put an end to the blackmail exercised by the eu on a number of developing countries on the basis of the so-called economic partnership agreements.
in writing. − it is essential to support the poorest and most fragile countries on the planet, which includes almost half a hundred countries whose people are suffering the consequences of successive failures to implement the conclusions of successive united nations conferences. this is largely due to colonialism and the exploitation of their resources and populations. it is not fate, nor are it inevitable limitations or natural constraints that make these countries poor. quite the contrary: many of them are rich, very rich, in natural resources. in other cases, it is the continuation of capitalist exploitation, with the injustice and inhumanity of a system - a mode of economic and social organization that is dominant on a world scale - that is based on asymmetrical relations, generating and reproducing inequalities. it is the result of free trade, financial deregulation, illicit capital flight allowed by tax havens, but also of war and conflict fuelled by the competition for natural resources. it is in breaking with the foundations of this system and in a genuine and solidary policy of cooperation and development aid that lies the possibility of the emancipation of these peoples and the development of their countries.

in writing. − the european neighbourhood policy (enp) has proven to be a key instrument of european foreign policy, providing closer relations with partner countries and mutually beneficial outcomes. the changes brought about by the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon were intended to make the european external dimension more coherent, more efficient and more legitimate. however, it is imperative to review and point out the mistakes of the past. the review of the enp and the eastern partnership (eap) should set out specific priorities for action for each partner, benchmarks and differentiation based on performance and results achieved. a bottom-up approach, with support for civil society and democratisation processes, is a prerequisite for long-term stability and sustainable growth. a strong focus on training, education, research and mobility is essential to tackle the region's socioeconomic problems. finally, i underline the eu's support for belarusian civil society in strengthening democratic and social reforms to enable its participation in the enp and other sectoral policies.

the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fisheries sector is not left behind. the current sales dynamics do not allow the fluctuations in the cost of production factors, including fuel, to be reflected in fish prices, which is also due to the current import policy. average first sale prices have been stagnating or declining for several years without this being reflected in a decrease in prices to the final consumer. the current common organisation of the market in fishery products has not contributed sufficiently to improving prices at first sale or to a better distribution of value added in the value chain of the sector. the economic situation of a large number of companies has deteriorated in recent years, leading to the disappearance of many of them, and there is a real risk that thousands of fishing businesses will disappear and thousands of jobs will be destroyed due to the increase in fuel prices. the small-scale coastal and artisanal fisheries are particularly vulnerable, accounting for more than 90% of the fleet in some member states (such as portugal). in this context, the commission's attitude of inertia and refusal to take the necessary measures, which the commissioner has confirmed here today, is absolutely reprehensible. the commission only conceives of one solution to the problems facing the fisheries sector: the indiscriminate slaughter of the fleet, that is, to cure the disease by killing the sick. it is important to say that this past culling, without taking into account the specificities of the fleets, the state of the fishery resources in each case and the consumption needs of each country, has not solved any of the problems facing the sector. it has merely concentrated ownership and activity in the sector at eu level. emergency measures must therefore be adopted to provide an immediate and adequate response to the socioeconomic needs of the sector, such as the creation of a guarantee fund, shared at community level, to guarantee the stability of fuel prices and the use of all the possibilities and financial margins of the community budget to finance extraordinary measures to support the sector. but in view of the structural trend towards higher oil prices and also the requirements of environmental sustainability, measures are also required to ensure the viability of the sector in the medium/long term. mechanisms are needed to improve the first sale price and promote a fair and appropriate distribution of value added across the value chain of the sector. the eff needs to provide effective and substantial support for the renewal and modernisation of fishing fleets, in particular in terms of improving gear selectivity, replacing engines for safety, environmental protection and fuel economy reasons. in addition to the tax measures that can be adopted at member state level, community responses are needed in order not to aggravate the inequalities that already exist between member states and are increasing in the face of the serious economic and social crisis that particularly affects the most vulnerable economies.
i would also like to add my voice to those who have expressed concern here about the low incomes of fishermen, aggravated by the historic fuel prices, particularly in recent months. as has been well said here, fuel costs have a very high impact on the survival of our small and medium-sized shipowners and are aggravating, with particular gravity, the already fragile incomes of fishermen. this rapid rise in prices is also having profound negative effects: fewer trips to sea, poverty incomes for fishermen, aggravated by the low prices paid at first sale, increased imports of aquaculture and fishery products from third countries to the european market and a consequent abandonment of the activity, due to financial difficulties, with more job losses. in this context, to avoid a further worsening of the crisis, action is needed, and action must be taken quickly and in depth on the problems of fisheries. the commission must therefore respond positively, with short- and long-term measures, to the difficulties facing the sector and the serious loss of income suffered by our fishermen.
, in writing. other european fishermen, and especially those living in member states facing greater financial difficulties such as portugal, are in a difficult economic situation, which has been aggravated by the increase in fuel prices. to deal with this situation, the commission needs to adopt emergency measures to help fishermen. the commission should therefore allow for a transitional period of three years for the aid that member states can grant to fishermen to be increased from eur 30 000 to eur 60 000. in addition, the european fisheries fund (eff) should provide aid to fishermen, in particular for improving the selectivity of fishing gear and for replacing engines, for reasons of safety, environmental protection and/or fuel economy. in the context of these measures, special attention shall be given to small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing. finally, it is crucial that there are regulatory mechanisms to improve the first sale price and to promote a fair and appropriate distribution of value added through the fisheries value chain in a way that values the prices paid to producers.
the rapporteur. - actually, this report wasn't done by me. i am an accidental and supervenient rapporteur, since the original rapporteur left this report and i, as chairman of the committee and in accordance with the rules, took it over. in addition to being the accidental rapporteur, i am also an embarrassed rapporteur because i did not actually vote for it and i have the most serious objections to its content. but things are as they are, and i have no choice but to assume, with gallantry, this charge that has been given to me. as we know, this report on the granting of exceptional trade preferences to pakistan has its origins in a decision of the council of the union, which instructed the commission to make a proposal to parliament and the council. in the case of exceptional preferences which are not compatible with the wto rule of non-discrimination, either positive or negative, a waiver, a derogation from the wto, must be obtained in advance before these trade preferences can be granted. the commission nevertheless submitted the proposal to parliament and the inta committee, which i chair and for which i am the incidental rapporteur, decided to proceed with the discussion and vote on the report. that is the result of that vote which we are bringing to the house. the subject, madam president, ladies and gentlemen, has proved to be a contentious one in the committee on international trade of this parliament, both as to whether we should use trade preferences as a means of emergency aid to a particular country, and that was the pretext which justified this proposal from the commission, and as to the duration of these trade preferences, as to their extension, and finally as to the conditions to be imposed on the beneficiary country, namely pakistan. although the committee voted by a majority on the commission's proposal to grant these exceptional preferences to pakistan, the fact is that the international trade committee also voted on several amendments to limit the impact of these trade advantages granted to pakistan, including, among others, amendments and approval of a safeguard clause in case imports from pakistan increase too much due to the reduction or elimination of import trade tariffs. other amendments relate, for example, to requiring pakistan not to create or remove existing restrictions on exports of raw materials. in conclusion, it should be borne in mind that our efforts here may prove to be totally in vain, for we may lose them if we do not obtain the waiver from the world trade organization, which we do not know at this moment when or if it will be granted. in any case, even if this effort of ours proves to be futile, it will at least be an excellent opportunity to discuss the meaning, if any, and the limits of using exceptional commercial advantages as a means of emergency aid or as a means of political gratification of a particular country as in this case. we are in danger of setting dangerous precedents, or worse, of making commercial preferences a political instrument which may have to be guided by much more objective criteria, much less discretionary and short-term than in this case.

the rapporteur. mr president, welcome to commissioner de gucht, although with a little delay which we understand, but i think there is still time to express the commission's final positions. as an incidental rapporteur and, once again, malgré moi, of this report, i would like to make only two comments. the first is that this discussion has shown as much or more division on this matter than in the committee on international trade itself, and the second is that the merits of the proposals adopted in the committee on international trade, some of which the european commission considers inconclusive - the plenary tomorrow will decide on the merits of these proposals and the commission's objections. let me make just two final remarks. there are two things that parliament and the international trade commission cannot be accused of. firstly, that we have tried to block this matter, despite the fact that it is dependent on a waiver from the world trade organisation and that we are actually voting on a matter which may be rendered useless by the absence of this waiver. the truth is that the international trade commission decided to go ahead despite this. secondly, we have taken into account all the amendments which have been tabled by the commission, because the commission - which is the body and institution with the right of legislative initiative - has put forward its proposal, but then the terms of the request for a waiver submitted to the world trade organisation do not coincide with the proposal which the commission has put forward to parliament. and then there was the council's commitment, which also differs from the commission's initial proposal. the committee on international trade has not regarded any of these things as an obstacle to taking the discussion and voting on this matter into its own hands and has taken account of all these amendments which have been tabled by both the commission and the council.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. the question is simple. this is an initiative of the committee on international trade, of which i am chairman, and it is in my capacity as chairman that i put the question on which the political groups have reached consensus. i am pleased to put this question, which has been approved by the political group coordinators in my committee, and which seeks to obtain from the european commission an answer to a set of concerns about the state of play of the free trade agreement negotiations between the european union and india which have been ongoing since 2007. the importance of this initiative goes without saying. indeed, one of the great innovations of the lisbon treaty was to give the european parliament not only the right to give its final assent to international trade and other agreements after they have been negotiated, but also the right to be informed of all the steps of the negotiations from the very beginning. this means that the european parliament has the power and the duty to follow the negotiations - in this case, trade negotiations - and to intervene politically through the parliamentary means at its disposal (hearing, resolutions and also oral questions) to learn about the progress of these negotiations. that is why the committee on international trade wishes to hear from the commission, which, we must say, has given us a great deal of information on this subject, but i think that publicly there needs to be an answer to a set of questions, seven of which are in this oral question about, in particular, the progress that has been made on a set of sensitive issues, such as public procurement, on the negotiations on intellectual property rights in connection with generic medicines, on the request that the commission has made to the council of the union for a mandate to negotiate overseas investment, on something in negotiation on culture and cultural services, on whether there is already a concrete assessment of the effects of a possible free trade agreement with india on the main european industries, whether there is a quantitative assessment of the foreseeable benefits and losses to the european union from this trade agreement and finally whether the commission will take parliament's views into account in this matter. the questions are written, they are in the document we have tabled and i think they are clear enough to get us to make progress on public information on this important trade negotiation between the european union and one of our major trading partners.
madam president, the deep weakening of the productive apparatus of the weakest economies in the european union, such as portugal, which is the result of an integration based on competition between the strong and the weak, between the rich and the poor, and conducted in accordance with the interests of the major economic groups of the european powers, is aggravated by the liberalization and deregulation of world trade, conducted by the same groups in their own interests. in the face of the visible disaster caused by this path, the european union, instead of grabbing its way, continues to give signs of wanting to force a breakthrough. it is in this context that we must look at this agreement, the most comprehensive ever negotiated. a fundamental change in the current trade policies is urgently needed, with international trade being oriented towards complementarity rather than competition, towards the establishment of fair and equitable economic relations, mutually beneficial, serving the development of peoples and countries, and not just some economic and financial groups. the multifaceted crisis we face calls for a new economic, social, energy and environmental rationality, which free trade, one of the pillars of neoliberalism, clearly makes impossible.
i am the parliament's rapporteur on refugees and i have to say that this mission has become, in recent times, a depressing, if not sometimes macabre, mission. last month i reported to the house the death of more than a hundred refugees off the coast of lampedusa, and now, barely recovered from the news of the disappearance of 600 refugees leaving libya, we know that more than 60 have died at the sight of nato ships and european navies. let us not think that there is nothing to be done in the face of these tragedies. there is much to be done and much we have to do, and we are obliged to do so by the international conventions we have signed. i'll give you three examples in the 20 seconds i have left. the council must end the codecision on the resettlement of refugees which this parliament voted for and which provided for emergency mechanisms to be used on such occasions. the proposal for a humanitarian corridor to remove refugees from libya on the back of unhcr must be put on the table and nato must fulfil its mandate in the 1973 resolution to protect civilians, which means to carry out rescues at sea. the failure to help, let us not forget, is a crime, and it should not be done in our name.
madam president, on a subject which is necessarily broad, i would like to make only two brief remarks. the first is to draw attention to the threats facing many forest ecosystems today. among others, i highlight the spread of invasive alien species, pests and forest fires. some of these factors have shown some recurrence, particularly in convergence regions. a rigorous study of their impacts is required, as well as the best ways to increase the resilience of the forest to this set of biotic and abiotic threats. to this end, sufficient financial resources should be channelled through community support programmes and measures to assess the ecological and phytosanitary status of forests and their restoration, including reforestation, giving preference to native species and mixed forests for the sake of their resilience and biodiversity. a second note to draw attention to the enormous diversity of natural conditions and consequently of forest ecosystems that occur in europe. it must be recognised and valued, valuing its multifunctionality and its potential to generate employment and development in the rural world.
mr president, commissioner, mr president-in-office of the council, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to congratulate all the rapporteurs on their excellent work. i would like to turn this speech mainly to heading 5, the administrative and operating expenditure of the various institutions, and to recall that the volume of administrative and operating expenditure represents less than 6% of the annual budget of the european union. despite this number, i consider it essential that the principles of economy, the principles of efficiency and the principles of effectiveness be applied. and, moreover, budget implementation must promote and encourage savings, and at the same time we cannot in any way encourage and promote the use of all the money from each heading. it is important to advocate rigor, austerity and, at the same time, the minimum means for the european parliament to achieve the objective of legislative excellence. and as far as interpretation and translation are concerned, i think it is essential and crucial that members can express themselves and work in their mother tongue. it's basically to give shape to the motto: united in diversity. i believe that instead of purely incremental budgets, we should have zero-based budgets at the beginning of each parliamentary term and, moreover, the budgets of the institutions should be multiannual budgets. control cannot mean bureaucracy, because this is always an unnecessary cost. the principle of trust in the institutions must prevail. finally, discharge cannot be an exercise in discussing fundamental policies which require broad consensus and, in particular, the revision of the treaties. i therefore consider it inappropriate, for example, to discuss workplace issues in discharge reports.

in writing. − eurojust is a european union body that helps investigators and prosecutors across the eu work together in the fight against crossborder crime. it plays a key role in information exchange and extradition processes. the particular importance and sensitivity of these matters justify the agency being provided with the means to pursue them effectively, although, as is obvious, in matters of justice and the suppression of crime, all the means available are always insufficient. the effective management of human resources seems to be the agency's main problem. the fact that 24% of the agency's posts remain vacant and that several senior posts are occupied by non-staff raises fears for the continuity and efficient pursuit of the agency's activities.
in writing. − the tasks of frontex are to coordinate operational cooperation between member states in the field of external border management; to support member states in the training of national border guards, including the definition of common training standards; to carry out risk analyses; to monitor the development of relevant research on external border control and surveillance; to support member states in circumstances requiring enhanced operational and technical assistance at the external borders; to provide member states with the necessary support in the organisation of joint return operations. the increasing migratory pressure on the union's borders and the need for coordination between member states justify to a large extent that the agency should be equipped with the appropriate means to fulfil the tasks entrusted to it. however, i share the rapporteur's concern that the court of auditors has found that the cost of prefinancing for border authorities is overestimated by 27%, and that there are excess advances.
in writing. − the supervisory authority is responsible for ensuring the management of the public interest in european gnss programmes and acts as the regulator of these programmes. the competences of the galileo joint undertaking, which expired on 31 december 2006, were transferred to it as from 1 january 2007. the regulation provides for the commission to be provisionally based in brussels and to carry out, among other things, the following tasks, which are currently under review: management, inherited from the galileo joint undertaking, of the contract with the operator responsible for operating the egnos system; coordination of the actions of the member states with regard to the frequencies necessary for the operation of the system; cooperation with the commission in the preparation of proposals for the programme; modernisation of the system; management of all aspects relating to the protection and security of the system; action as the european gnss security approval authority; management of the research activities necessary for the development and promotion of the european gnss programmes. such a role of competence indicates the importance attached to the agency and reinforces the requirement that the agency should align its activities and expenditure with the budget allocated to it and that it should comply with the rules for its implementation.
in writing. − the artemis joint undertaking is implementing the joint technology initiative (jti) in the field of embedded computing systems. this public-private partnership is mainly intended to support the co-financing of research initiatives at european level and to improve cooperation between the different players in the sector. the rapporteur also stresses that the commission's proposal is to set up a european network of information centres to provide information on the use of the internet and the internet for the purposes of the protection of personal data. the initial stage in which the company is still situated makes it possible to have high expectations of its future achievements and to hope that it will justify the investment which is being made in it.
in writing. − the clean sky joint undertaking was set up in response to the perceived need to promote the development, validation and demonstration of clean air transport technologies in the european union with a view to putting them into practice as soon as possible. like the artemis joint undertaking, it is still in the early stages of its activity. this does not mean that there are no longer any procedures and practices to correct, particularly as regards the budgetary structure, as the rapporteur rightly points out.
in writing. − the joint undertaking aims to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of the drug development process so that the pharmaceutical sector produces innovative medicines that are more effective and safer. the joint undertaking thus aims to contribute to the implementation of the seventh framework programme and to support pharmaceutical research and development in the member states and countries associated to the seventh framework programme. it encourages the participation of small and medium-sized enterprises in its activities and cooperation between the private sector and academia. the embryonic stage in which it is still situated does not allow for a clear view of its future budgetary executions. however, it should in particular continue to complete its internal control and information systems.
in writing. the aim of this joint venture is to modernise the european air traffic management system and to pool the community's research and development efforts under the sesar (european new generation air traffic management system) project. the safety of citizens who increasingly use the services of airlines, as well as of their employees, justifies a particular effort to find the best solutions for managing this type of traffic, as well as the monitoring and comparison of the methodologies already applied in the various member states with a view to the joint adoption of best practices and safe, cost-effective and innovative solutions. like other joint ventures in the start-up phase, sesar has not yet fully put its internal controls and financial information system into operation. you should do so as soon as possible.
in writing. - this report deals with the request for the defence of the privileges and immunities of mr luigi de magistris, mep, made pursuant to articles 8 and 9 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union and article 68 of the constitution of the italian republic, as amended by constitutional law no 3 of 29 october 1993, following a request by the tribunal de benevento for his presence and following an action brought by mr clemente mario mastella, mep, following an interview with an italian media outlet. in view of the established practice in this parliament, considering that judicial proceedings are of a civil or administrative nature and taking into account the opinion of the committee on legal affairs, i am voting in favour of the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr luigi de magistris.
in writing. - the european parliament was asked to lift the parliamentary immunity of luigi de magistris mep following a summons against him at the benevento court on behalf of clemente mario mastella, member of the european parliament, in relation to an interview luigi de magistris gave to an italian newspaper on 31 october 2009. the committee on legal affairs has taken a position on the matter and adopted a report in which it decided not to waive parliamentary immunity. in fact, it was considered that luigi de magistris was in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament when he made the statements. according to the report, he was acting in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament, engaging in political activity and expressing his opinion on a matter of public interest to his constituents. i voted in favour of defending the freedom of expression of members in the exercise of their duties and defending the interest of the european parliament as an institution. i would add, however, that i believe that political leaders in general, including members of parliament, should always speak truthfully and use language that is respectful of those they are speaking to, which is not always the case.
in writing. - this report deals with the request for the defence of the privileges and immunities of bruno gollnisch, mep, made following an attempt to arrest him by the french police for questioning by the french judicial authorities in a case concerning the expression of political opinions. the case concerns an accusation of incitement to racial hatred brought by the international league against racism and anti-semitism (licra) following a statement published on the website of the national front of the rhône-alpes council, of which bruno gollnisch was president. in view of the established practice in this parliament and the opinion of the committee on legal affairs, i agree with the rapporteur's position and i am voting in favour of the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr bruno gollnisch.
in writing. - bruno gollnisch asked the ep to defend his parliamentary immunity in the context of measures he considers to be inhibiting his freedom, applied by the french authorities in the context of the judicial investigation of a criminal complaint (plainte avec constitution de partie civile) lodged by the international league against racism and anti-semitism on 26 january 2009 against an unidentified third party for incitement to racial hatred. it is concluded that the case does not fall within the scope of bruno gollnisch's political activities as an mep but rather concerns his activities as a member of the regional council of the rhône-alpes region, a mandate for which he was elected by direct universal suffrage and which is distinct from that of an mep. the investigation carried out has found no evidence of fumus persecutionis, i.e. intent to harm the member's political activity. i voted in favour of this report, which decides not to defend the privileges and immunities of bruno gollnisch, leaving it to the competent judicial authorities to decide, in compliance with all democratic guarantees, to what extent the french law on incitement to racial hatred has been violated and what the legal consequences may be.

in writing. the prespa river basin (prespa park) is shared between greece, the fry and albania. the first is a member state of the european union, the second is a candidate country for eu membership and the third is a potential candidate country for eu membership. albania and the jra have signed a stabilisation and association agreement with the eu, and there is significant employment potential associated with the development of a sustainable economy and green infrastructure which by their nature lead to the creation of local jobs, thus contributing significantly to the europe 2020 strategy. moreover, resource efficiency, sustainable economic development and nature conservation can and should be inseparable and should at the same time strengthen cooperation with neighbouring countries for their integration into the european area. for all the reasons explained above, i approve this proposal for an agreement.

in writing. - i welcome the conclusion of the stabilisation and association agreement between the european union, albania and the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, which aims to establish cooperation between all those sharing the prespa river basin, in order to ensure integrated protection of the ecosystem and the sustainable development of the park. this agreement demonstrates the successful implementation of the eu water framework directive, for the protection of the environment, for the improvement of the living standards of the inhabitants of the region, as well as for cooperation between the three countries (greece, albania and the fry), reinforcing the good neighbourly relations between the parties in the particularly sensitive region of the balkans.
in writing. − this recommendation concerns the draft european council decision on the conclusion of an agreement on the protection and sustainable development of the area of the prespa national park (classified as such since 1977) and designated as a transfrontier protected area under the declaration of 2 february 2000 by the prespa countries (greece, albania and the republic of macedonia). since the 1970s, the european union (eu), aware of the urgent need to protect and safeguard natural resources, has adopted a legislative package, the most prominent of which is the water framework directive 2000 (wfd). the aim of the agreement is to establish cooperation between the eu and the abovementioned countries in order to promote the sustainable development of the region, in particular through integrated management plans for the prespa river basin and the protection of the ecosystem. at a time when the number of disasters caused by climate change is increasing, i congratulate the council on this project and hope that it will be signed as soon as possible.
in writing. the prespa river basin (prespa park) is shared by greece, the former yugoslav republic of macedonia and albania. it is of extreme importance as a vital habitat for the conservation of many rare and/or endemic species of fauna and flora, as a nesting place for globally endangered birds, and as a repository of significant cultural heritage. the aim of the agreement is to establish cooperation in order to ensure integrated protection of the ecosystem and sustainable development of the prespa park area, including the development of integrated river basin management plans. in this regard, the countries involved in the agreement undertake to take the necessary measures, individually or in cooperation, respecting the principles of sovereign equality, territorial integrity, mutual benefit and good faith, with a view to the management of the waters of prespa, the prevention, control and reduction of pollution, the protection and conservation of biodiversity, soil protection, the prudent use of natural resources and sustainable development. we therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the prespa park, i.e. the prespa watershed, shared by greece, the former yugoslav republic of macedonia and albania, is of extreme ecological importance as a vital habitat for the conservation of many rare and/or endemic species of fauna and flora, as a nesting place for globally endangered birds and as a repository of significant cultural heritage. the aim of this agreement is to establish cooperation to ensure integrated protection of the ecosystem and sustainable development of the prespa park area, including the development of integrated river basin management plans. in this regard, the countries involved in the agreement undertake to take the necessary measures, individually or in cooperation, respecting the principles of sovereign equality, territorial integrity, mutual benefit and good faith, with a view to the management of the waters of prespa, the prevention, control and reduction of pollution, the protection and conservation of biodiversity, soil protection, the prudent use of natural resources and sustainable development. we therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - this report is based on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement on the protection and sustainable development of the prespa park area of the prespa river basin. the european union has long had legislative instruments to protect its waters, notably the water framework directive of 2000, which sets the objective of protecting all waters (rivers, lakes, groundwater and coastal waters) and provides for the coordination of efforts in the case of shared river basins across administrative and political borders to achieve this objective. the prespa water catchment area is shared by greece, the former yugoslav republic of macedonia and albania. the jra is a candidate country for eu membership and albania is a potential candidate country for eu membership. in this context, the need arises to establish an international agreement for the pursuit of the objectives of the water framework directive, namely the protection of biodiversity and ecosystem services in this area. i voted in favour of this report, which was previously unanimously approved by the committee on the environment, public health and food safety.
in writing. the prespa river basin is spread between greece, albania and the former yugoslav republic of macedonia. as a focus of biodiversity of undeniable ecological interest, which also translates into a natural climate regulator, its protection is worthy of the efforts of the european union, in accordance with the provisions of the water directive (2000/60/ec). according to this directive, when a river basin is concerned that extends beyond the territorial limits of the union, coordination efforts should be undertaken between the states concerned, and to this end an agreement on the protection and sustainable development of the prespa park area was concluded on 2 february 2010, in which the commission, on behalf of the eu, also participated. however, its final adoption by the council requires the approval of the european parliament. for the reasons stated above, i voted in favour of approving this agreement.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'port state' to cover all ports. a resolution on port state measures, presented by the eu, was adopted at the iotc (indian ocean tuna commission) plenary meeting in busan, south korea, in march 2010 (resolution 2010/11). the eu has also put forward similar proposals in other rfmos with a view to strengthening and aligning its port state measures currently in force with the requirements of the agreement. unfortunately, in many cases they could not be adopted because of the opposition of a number of countries, such as some latin american countries and small pacific island countries. like the rapporteur, i also urge the european commission to continue to press for the adoption of these proposals, since the measures provided for in the agreement will only be truly effective in combating iuu fishing if and when they are applied in a comprehensive, uniform and transparent manner, so as to avoid loopholes that can easily be exploited by iuu fishermen.
in writing. - i agree with the proposal for a council decision on the approval, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement on port state measures to prevent and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. i believe that the effectiveness of such measures is essential to ensure the conservation and sustainability of marine ecosystems and, therefore, of the marine exploitation and industry. in order to ensure the efficiency sought, it is necessary that these measures are applied harmoniously by the member states in the control of landings, transhipments and other operations carried out in their ports. i would therefore like to stress the relevance of the proposed point concerning the information-sharing mechanism which should underlie the agreement.
in writing. - illegal fishing is a phenomenon that threatens all the efforts made by the international community and the european union in particular to balance a strong and dynamic fishing industry with the necessary replenishment of fisheries resources. in 2007, the fao fisheries committee agreed on the development of a legally binding international instrument on measures to be taken by port states to prevent, deter and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. then, in 2009, in rome, an agreement was adopted which is now intended to be approved on behalf of the eu. i am aware of the importance of this subject, particularly for a maritime country such as portugal, and i am voting in favour of the approval of this agreement.
in writing. − the food and agriculture organisation of the united nations (fao) established in 2001 an international action plan to prevent, deter and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (ipoa-inn). in 2005, the fao adopted a set of measures that states whose ports are used by fishing or fish transport vessels should adopt to combat illegal fishing. the preservation of natural resources, including marine resources, is a constant concern of the european union (eu), which seeks to prevent illegal fishing by all means at its disposal. it has therefore closely followed all fao measures and played an active and constructive role, in particular in the preparation of the agreement adopted at the 36th fao conference held in rome from 18 to 23 november 2009. i agree with the rapporteur's position that the european commission should not only sign this agreement but also continue to put pressure on international bodies, including the fao, to adopt the measures envisaged.
in writing. − this agreement was adopted at the 36th session of the fao conference in rome in november 2009, culminating in a process of discussion that was preceded by a set of other agreements and codes of conduct adopted over the past two decades within the fao framework. illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing is a global threat to the sustainable exploitation of living aquatic resources. for this reason, the fight against iuu fishing should be a central concern of any fisheries policy and an essential element of international fisheries management in the forums concerned. the objective of this agreement is to prevent, deter and eliminate iuu fishing through the application of effective port state measures and thus ensure the long-term conservation and sustainable exploitation of living marine resources and marine ecosystems. experience shows us the good cost-effectiveness and the central role played by port state measures in combating iuu fishing, in conjunction with other instruments. the agreement also supports a broad definition of iuu fishing to include a wide range of unregulated fishing operations. we therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − the prevention, deterrence and elimination of illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing is a key priority for the success of the common fisheries policy. the objective of the agreement is to prevent, deter and eliminate iuu fishing through the application of effective port state measures and thereby ensure the long-term conservation and sustainable exploitation of living marine resources and marine ecosystems. iuu fishing continues to constitute one of the most serious global threats to the sustainable exploitation of living aquatic resources and the eu has played an active and constructive role in the elaboration of this draft agreement. the parties shall, through the possibility provided for in the international instrument on port state measures, refuse entry into their ports if they have sufficient evidence that the vessel seeking entry has been engaged in iuu fishing or related activities. on the basis of these considerations, i consider the agreement to be an important contribution to the ongoing global fight against iuu fishing and i am voting in favour of its approval.
in writing. - millions of citizens use the right to trade in the eu's internal market, to live, work and move throughout the eu. the eu has legislation that allows crossborder complaints and mutual recognition of national court decisions. but getting a court decision is only part of the process; citizens and businesses must have the right to have those decisions effectively enforced. a necessary component of effective enforcement is that courts can, as an interim measure, act quickly to order the disclosure and freezing of debtors' assets. without such a measure, rogue traders and other debtors may escape their liability by simply transferring their assets to another jurisdiction, thereby denying the creditor effective enforcement of the judgment in the single market. the citizen or small business will have spent money and resources to secure a judicial decision and will end up having to go to the courts of another member state, with no guarantee of success or justice. this report thus indicates the need for an effective regime for the freezing and disclosure of debtors' assets and as such i approve it.
in writing. − there needs to be an effective system to prevent and punish situations of default of payments when they occur between persons whose assets are in different countries, otherwise the free movement of persons, goods, services and capital within the eu will be jeopardising the legal security of european citizens. i therefore welcome and agree with the recommendations to the commission on the proposed measures on the freezing and declaration of debtors' assets in crossborder cases.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it sets out a series of measures to help prevent dishonest traders and other debtors from evading their responsibilities by transferring their assets to other jurisdictions, thereby denying the creditor effective enforcement of the court decision in the single market.

in writing. − opportunism and greed of citizens and certain businessmen lead them to take advantage of the free movement of people and goods throughout the european union (eu) to the detriment of others. despite existing rules such as the brussels i regulation, the european enforcement order, the european small claims procedure and the injunction procedure, it is not always possible - let alone quick - to obtain the effective enforcement of a court judgment in the single market. this report, which contains a set of recommendations to the european commission on the proposals put forward on the freezing and declaration of debtors' assets in crossborder cases, deserves my full support and i hope that by next june we will have a concrete proposal with the measures to be taken in this area.

in writing. − the most important instrument the union has at its disposal to promote growth in the aftermath of the financial crisis is its internal market. at present, union law, in particular in the field of civil justice, is not effectively applied. in fact, the current level of crossborder debt recovery is markedly low, both in terms of the assets of individuals and of companies. this in itself discourages cross-border trade, sending a message of impunity to debtors, and undermines the union's economic performance. in fact, the cost of crossborder debt collection is currently prohibitive for creditors in cases where the debtor has assets in several member states. this is an obstacle to the full functioning of the internal market. it is essential that the european union put an end to this situation and that eu citizens are given effective remedies, if they have a complaint against another citizen or company, measures that simplify and speed up this recovery process. in this context, i voted in favour of this report, in which the european parliament calls on the commission to submit legislative proposals on measures to freeze and declare the assets of debtors and alleged debtors in crossborder cases.
in writing. - the construction of a single market requires that the parties have at their disposal mechanisms enabling them to satisfy their claims throughout the community. this is the reason for the brussels i regulation, which aims to establish a uniform system for the recognition of judgments in the eu. however, it remains extremely burdensome for a creditor to enforce a claim when the debtor's assets are spread over several member states, which, needless to say, poses serious difficulties for the implementation of a genuine single market. the european heritage preservation order (ehpo) and the european heritage declaration order (ehdo) can be good instruments for this purpose. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − the purpose of the agency is to provide the institutions and authorities of the european union and its member states, in the context of the application of community law, with assistance and expertise in the field of fundamental rights, and to support them in adopting measures and defining appropriate actions. the main tasks of the agency are to collect, analyse and disseminate objective, reliable and comparable information on the situation of fundamental rights in the eu; to improve the comparability and reliability of data through new methods and rules; to carry out and/or promote research and studies in the field of fundamental rights; to formulate and publish conclusions and opinions on specific issues, either on its own initiative or at the request of the european parliament, the council or the commission; and to promote dialogue with civil society in order to raise awareness of fundamental rights among the general public. i welcome the fact that, having opened an investigation against the agency in 2008, the european anti-fraud office (olaf) closed it without any further action being taken.

in writing. - i welcome the assistance provided by the european union to this country, as the largest donor of humanitarian aid to the rest of the world, following natural disasters devastating its economy and its people. however, the use of the union's trade policy as a form of humanitarian aid and development aid is deeply wrong. in my view, the commission should never propose such a measure without first quantifying the economic and social impacts in the various regions of the eu. one of the most serious consequences of this measure is precisely in portugal, where the textile and clothing industry represents 11% of exports and 160 000 jobs, and would be profoundly affected by the competition from pakistan.
in writing. the commission has also adopted a communication on the implementation of the european union strategy for the environment (2007-2013) and a communication on the implementation of the european union strategy for the environment (2008-2013). the european union (eu) is always at the forefront of humanitarian aid. this was the case last summer when floods ravaged large parts of pakistan with enormous human and material losses. in addition to humanitarian aid in the first hours of the disaster, the eu has sought other ways of supporting the economic recovery of that country, which are set out in this proposal for a regulation. however, we must ensure that aspects which could be detrimental to some european trade sectors (in particular in the textile sector) are safeguarded. i also believe that trade preferences are not the right way to help a country in the event of a disaster. these preferences may even set a dangerous precedent. we must not forget that the current economic and financial crisis has placed the companies most exposed to globalisation in a vulnerable position and it is unacceptable that trade preferences should be able to harm them.
in writing. - as we have said on more than one occasion, the tragedy that has befallen pakistan calls for european solidarity. but it cannot be a pretext for calling into question the textile industry in several member states, as is the case in portugal. there are other ways to show solidarity. more effective forms of aid; aimed at the rehabilitation of the affected areas and the improvement of the living conditions of the affected populations; based on an effective and lasting development cooperation and aid policy, which supports the integrated and sustainable development of local communities. but also fairer forms of aid. these trade concessions benefit mainly the large european importers, who are thus satisfied with longstanding claims. but they harm the textile industry and the countries and regions most dependent on it. all this in a context of deep crisis and high unemployment. the commission's proposals are not, of course, a pretext for further redundancies and increased exploitation in european industry, but we cannot ignore the objective difficulties they create, which the report itself acknowledges as an attempt to sugarcoat the situation by introducing safeguards which do not change the essential facts.
in writing. - it is yet another example of the defence of the interests of the economic and financial groups of the european union at the expense of the industry of the countries with the weakest economies. by introducing autonomous emergency trade preferences for pakistan, the european commission is bringing into the scope of humanitarian aid what is strictly within the scope of the commercial interests of some, pure and simple business. it is an exercise in hypocrisy which uses the natural disaster that has struck pakistan to avenge the claims of some of the major economic groups of the european union powers, which will harm the eu textile industry and the countries and regions most dependent on it. this is a serious impact in a sector that has been deeply affected by the liberalisation of world trade, which is concentrated in regions with high levels of unemployment, poverty and low economic diversification, such as several regions in the north and centre of portugal. we therefore supported the proposal to reject the agreement and regret that it was not adopted. but we also supported his return to the commission, hoping that it would still be possible to take account of the position of the assembly of the republic in portugal, which passed a resolution against these trade concessions. the necessary solidarity with pakistan must be genuine aid in cooperation and development aid policies.
in writing. - i voted against granting trade preferences to pakistan by exempting imports from duties on the pretext of last year's floods. i think it is illogical to use exceptional trade preferences, contrary to the rules of international trade law, as a means of emergency aid, which has its own instruments. never before has the european union done this, or for other countries. no other developed country has followed suit (nor have the united states, japan, australia, new zealand, canada). even if the advantages given to pakistan were a kind of prize for its role in afghanistan, i believe that the political instrumentalization of trade preferences sets a dangerous precedent. on the other hand, the trade advantages granted to pakistan will be paid for by the european industries most affected, namely the textile industry in southern europe, and also by the poor countries which export the same products to europe and which will suffer the diversion of european imports to pakistan (such as bangladesh or the north african countries). however, i voted in favour of the amendments tabled, which substantially mitigate the negative impact of the proposal (safeguard clause, one-year time limit and human rights clause).
in writing. - following the floods which devastated large parts of pakistan last summer, the commission has put forward a proposal to extend to pakistan, in the form of tariff exemptions, autonomous trade preferences for 75 products of interest to pakistan (mainly textiles and clothing). this measure, which is presented as a transitional measure but for a period of three years, would have a strong impact on portuguese textiles, which is why i voted against this report. however, since the report has been adopted and in order to minimise the impact on portuguese textiles, i have successfully argued that the duration of the trade preferences should be limited to one year from the date of entry into force of these measures. the duration may be extended, if necessary, following a serious study on the impact assessment on european textiles to be presented by the commission. finally, i also supported, with reference to portuguese textiles, the introduction of a safeguard clause providing that if a product originating in pakistan is imported under conditions which cause, or threaten to cause, serious difficulties to an eu producer of similar or directly competing products, the common customs tariff duties on that product may be re-established at any time.
in writing. the natural disaster that struck the people of pakistan last august has raised our awareness and deserves the solidarity of the european union. the european union must show its support for pakistan and help to minimise the devastating effects of the floods, as it has done in the past, on the basis of its policy of international cooperation and humanitarian aid, in the event of other tragic events. however, attempts to use the common commercial policy to express this solidarity may have undesirable repercussions for the future, in this particular case and in others that may arise. the effects on the internal market are negative for the production of european countries such as portugal. but the international effects are also worrying, as they are creating an exception within the wto and in a key sector for many developing countries. for these reasons, and also because i believe that an impact study should be carried out to assess the intra-community impact of the agreement, i voted in favour of amendment no 43, which rejects the european commission's proposal to grant preferences to pakistan.
in writing. − the current system of foreign direct investment is governed by a myriad of redundant and sometimes contradictory bilateral investment treaties (bits) between member states, and must be replaced within a reasonable period of time by a new framework of modern eu investment treaties, consistent with its cross-cutting policy objectives. i also support the rapporteur's position that he strongly supports the coexistence approach in the commission's draft regulation. it is undoubtedly essential that, through an authorisation process, existing bits of member states continue to be in force and that, under clear conditions, member states are allowed to renegotiate existing bits, conclude those that are pending and negotiate new ones. however, legal certainty will remain relative as long as the transition of the investment protection regime is not completed and the bits in force in the member states are not validated in the light of public international law. i welcome the report, but i would stress the need to continue the debate on this subject in order to improve its legal framework.
in writing. − in view of the harmonisation of the eu's external policy, i agree to change the current system of bilateral investment treaties between member states and third countries. i also share the concern expressed by the rapporteur to ensure legal certainty during the transition process, and this requires the introduction of a time limit for this and the clarification of the conditions for withdrawal of authorization.
in writing. − with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, in accordance with articles 206 and 207 tfeu, foreign direct investment becomes an exclusive competence of the union. the commission has already adopted a number of proposals for the creation of a european investment bank, including a european investment fund for smes. the aim is to find fair and effective transitional measures which safeguard the existing bilateral agreements and do not ignore the expectations of investors. we must therefore avoid legal loopholes and ensure a well-balanced transition. i therefore call on all parties to strike a fair balance during the trilogues between the need to protect legitimate expectations and the correct application of the lisbon treaty, with particular attention to the articles on review and withdrawal of authorisation. i congratulate the rapporteur on all the work he has done, but i call for greater thought and commitment.
in writing. - this report concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down transitional provisions for bilateral investment agreements between member states and third countries, which are within the exclusive competence of the european union under article 207 (1) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) as regards foreign direct investment. without prejudice to the need for existing bilateral treaties in the member states to remain in force, i agree with the rapporteur's position that a high degree of legal certainty should be ensured during the transition period, as well as with the three grounds for withdrawing the authorisation for the existence of a bilateral treaty: conflict with eu legislation, partial or total redundancy in relation to an existing union agreement with the same third country, and whether such redundancy is not specifically mentioned in the latter and what may constitute an obstacle to the development and implementation of the union's investment policies.
in writing. − trade policy is another area where member states have been removed from competence and the eu has become solely responsible. this is the basis of this proposal for a regulation, namely the application of article 207 (1) tfeu, which provides for the exclusive competence of the eu in the field of foreign direct investment, within the framework of the common commercial policy. the importance of trade policy and investment policy as instruments for promoting the interests of a country and its people, in view of their specific characteristics and conditions, is therefore all too evident. the damage caused by trade and investment policies which do not take due account of the interests, circumstances and constraints of the country, and which are basically decided by the major eu powers (who have gained decisive weight as the eu has been strengthening its powers), in defence of the interest of its major economic groups, is also all too evident. the regulation, among other important aspects, is intended to give the commission the power to withdraw authorisations, to ask member states to negotiate or to denounce bilateral investment treaties (bits) and to approve new bits. these are reasons for our vote against.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation laying down transitional provisions for bilateral investment agreements between member states and third countries. this is in line with article 207 (1) tfeu, which provides for the exclusive competence of the eu in the field of foreign direct investment, within the framework of the common commercial policy. in a world of globalised transfers of goods and capital, and as a logical consequence of the union's common commercial policy, the investment policy of the member states must also be coordinated and decided at union level. this means that the current system, which is a myriad of redundant and sometimes contradictory bilateral investment treaties (bits) between member states, must be replaced within a reasonable time by a new framework of modern eu investment treaties, consistent with its cross-cutting policy objectives. the transition to a union investment policy, given the risky and far-reaching nature of foreign direct investment, is a long and complicated process. it is of the utmost importance to ensure a high degree of legal certainty during the transitional period.
in writing. − since the eu has exclusive competence under the tfeu in the field of foreign direct investment, it is necessary to provide the union with the means to move from a diffuse perspective to a harmonised approach. in this connection, solutions must be found to avoid legal uncertainty during the transitional period, without, however, jeopardizing the objectives which guide community action.
in writing. − according to article 207 (1) tfeu, the eu has competences in the field of fdi, and this type of investment is directly related to the new common commercial policy. the treaty of lisbon entered into force at a time when many bilateral investment agreements with third countries had expired and no transitional provisions had been defined to ensure the evolution in an integrated manner towards future agreements with exclusive competence for the union. i welcome the fact that a thorough analysis of all the bilateral agreements currently in force with third countries has been carried out and that a common strategy has been adopted by all the member states. as stated in this report, it is essential that the rules established are transparent, known to the main political actors and evaluated over a period of up to 10 years. at a time when transactions in goods and capital are increasingly globalised, it is important that the european union adopts a common investment policy, in line with the strategy defined by all member states.
