in writing. − the proposal for a regulation adopted by the commission on 30 january 2010 aims to simplify the existing regulatory framework by bringing together in a single regulation the three existing directives on the designation and labelling of textile products. at first reading on 18 may 2010, the european parliament adopted by a large majority 63 amendments, mainly technical amendments, aimed at aligning the text with the treaty on the functioning of the european union. it also approved substantive amendments, including rules on marking of origin, the indication of materials derived from animals, multi-fibre textile products, etc. the council rejected all the substantive amendments proposed by parliament. the report, which is a recommendation for second reading, has my support because it incorporates the vast majority of the amendments tabled by the ep at first reading (marking of origin, indication of materials derived from animals, multi-fibre textile products, amongst others). these changes will contribute to the promotion and innovation of european industry and will increase the level of information provided to consumers. equally important will be the study to be presented by the commission by september 2013 to determine whether there is a causal link between allergic reactions and chemical substances or mixtures used in textile products.
in writing. - i believe in the positive impact of simplifying and improving the existing regulatory framework for the labelling of textile products, in particular by encouraging the development and use of new fibres. i therefore agree with the adoption of the regulation presented by the european parliament and the commission. i do, however, consider the amendments tabled by the rapporteur to be relevant.
in writing. - the aim of this regulation is to lay down rules on the use of textile names and the corresponding labelling of textile products and on the quantitative analysis of binary and ternary mixtures of textile fibres. this means that directive 96/74/ec is to be transformed into a regulation and that directives 96/73/ec and 73/44/eec are to be repealed. the aim is to make the process of adding new fibres to the list of harmonised names more transparent and to adapt the legislation to technological developments in the textile industry. the amendments reintroduced by the rapporteur cover the issues of identification of the origin of materials, non-textile parts of animal origin, a review clause, a request for a study on dangerous substances, language-independent symbols or codes for fibres, requirements for the technical file to be attached to the application for authorisation of the name of textile fibres, multi-fibre textile products, self-employed tailors, laboratories responsible for testing textile mixtures and the mandatory indication of the composition of felt fibres and felt hats. i voted yes.
in writing. − this recommendation for second reading concerns the council position on the adoption of the european parliament and council regulation on textile fibre names and related labelling and fibre composition marking of textile products. the textile sector is very complex and represents a significant share of economic activity in the member states. the rapporteur has reached agreement on such controversial matters as origin marking, non-textile parts of animal origin, dangerous substances, etc. in addition, it was possible to include a review clause to remove obstacles to the smooth functioning of the internal market. despite some initial difficulties, an understanding was reached between the three european institutions, which is a very satisfactory result. the council will therefore be able to adopt this legislation quickly, with a view to its entry into force as from january 2012, which would greatly benefit consumers. i therefore welcome the consensus reached and vote in favour of this regulation, which repeals council directive 73/44/eec, directive 96/73/ec of the european parliament and of the council and directive 2008/121/ec of the european parliament and of the council.
in writing. the aim of the proposed regulation is to simplify and improve the existing regulatory framework for the labelling of textile products, with a view to protecting and encouraging the development and use of new fibres. the proposal facilitates the process of adapting legislation to technical progress by converting three existing directives into a single regulation, avoiding the transposition of purely technical updates and reducing the time between the submission of an application and the adoption of a new fibre name. the rules on naming and labelling are the focus of long-standing aspirations of producers. simplifying the existing regulatory framework can encourage innovation in the textiles and clothing sector, while also allowing consumers to benefit more quickly from innovative products. in the first reading vote in 2010, parliament approved amendments to the rules on origin marking, the indication of materials derived from animals, the use of language-independent symbols and a revision clause, but the council did not accept all of them. it is important that you accept the various proposals now, particularly on origin marking. for these reasons, we have supported most of the positions adopted here.
in writing. the initial aim of this proposal was to simplify and improve the existing regulatory framework for the labelling of textile products. the ep also welcomed the commission's proposal to introduce a new directive on the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. the presence of materials derived from animals should be clearly indicated in order to avoid the risk of consumers or persons suffering from allergies inadvertently buying products made of genuine hides and skins when they would prefer not to do so. by 30 september 2013, the commission shall prepare a study to determine whether there is a causal link between allergic reactions and chemical substances or mixtures used in textile products. on the basis of that study, the commission shall, where appropriate, submit legislative proposals. this regulation is expected to be adopted shortly by the eu council of ministers and will enter into force on the 20th day following its publication. for rules on labelling requirements, such as those on the indication of non-textile parts of animal origin, there will be a transitional period of two and a half years.
in writing. the new rules for the labelling of textile products are very important to avoid problems for the less informed consumers. the presence of materials derived from animals must be clearly indicated in order to avoid the risk of consumers or people suffering from allergies inadvertently buying products made of genuine hides and skins when they would prefer not to. the initial objective of this proposal is to simplify and improve the existing regulatory framework for the labelling of textile products. it was very important during the negotiations with the eu council of ministers to introduce new provisions in the regulation, such as requiring the indication of animal-derived materials in textile products and the carrying out of a study to determine whether there is a causal link between allergic reactions and chemicals used in textile products.
in writing. − this report includes a recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on textile fibre names and related labelling and marking of the fibre composition of textile products. the council rejected at first reading all the substantive amendments proposed by the european parliament, considering that they went beyond the simplification envisaged. the main amendments proposed by the european parliament and reintroduced in this report, which i voted for, concern matters which i consider of the greatest importance for the european market. among others, i would like to highlight the marking of origin, i.e. the introduction of a requirement to indicate the country of origin of textile products imported from third countries. the current lack of harmonised rules on origin marking places the eu at a disadvantage compared to its main trading partners, such as canada, china, japan and the usa, which require origin marking for imported goods. marking of origin would facilitate consumer choice and contribute to the reduction of fraudulent, inaccurate or misleading indications of origin.
in writing. the european parliament adopted 63 amendments to the commission proposal for a regulation on textile fibre names and related labelling of textile products, some of technical and some of substantive nature, including rules on marking of origin, indication of animal-derived materials, use of language-independent symbols and a revision clause. the technical amendments were accepted by the council in the main, but it rejected all the substantive amendments proposed by the ep. many of these amendments have now been taken up again and it is important that the council can recognise their importance and give them due consideration.
in writing. - i approve this proposal as it amends certain elements of regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 to allow for its extension until 31 december 2015 and to make certain adjustments following the entry into force of the bilateral agreements with bosnia and herzegovina and serbia. in so far as the interim/stabilisation and association agreements (saas) provide for trade concessions in favour of bosnia and herzegovina in respect of the products identified in the autonomous trade preferences, those concessions should be deleted from council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009. we are talking about the preferential tariff quotas for baby beef, sugar and sugar products, certain wines and certain fishery products. the end of the trade preferences would deprive the beneficiaries of an objective economic advantage in their trade with the eu. this could have very adverse consequences on the overall economic performance of the entire western balkan region, with the consequent negative repercussions on its internal reform and transition processes. moreover, their economic recovery could be seriously jeopardised.
in writing. - we voted today to extend exceptional trade measures such as tariff exemptions and trade preferences for bosnia and herzegovina, serbia and kosovo until 2015. under council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009, preferential tariff quotas apply to baby beef, sugar and sugar products, certain wines and certain fishery products. this extension is intended to address the situation of widespread economic crisis, as the end of trade preferences would jeopardise the economic recovery of these states and would have consequences for the entire stabilisation and transition process in the western balkans.
in writing. − this report is based on a proposal for a regulation of the european parliament (ep) and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 adopting exceptional trade measures in favour of countries and territories participating in or linked to the european union's (eu) stabilisation and association process. this is the situation of the western balkan countries, whose indigenous products enjoy duty-free and unlimited exceptional access to the eu market. these measures are intended to alleviate the crisis and to revitalize the economies of these countries. these exceptional measures expired on 31 december 2010 and their non-extension would have serious consequences for wealth creation, jeopardising their economic recovery and internal reform and transition processes. i therefore agree with the amendments proposed by the rapporteur and with the extension of these measures until 31 december 2015 and with the safeguarding of the necessary adjustments under the new bilateral agreements with bosnia and herzegovina and serbia.
in writing. − the aim of this report is to extend unlimited exceptional duty-free access to the eu market for almost all products originating in the countries and territories benefiting from the so-called stabilisation and association process. the pretext is to revitalise the economies of the western balkans through privileged access to the eu market, on the assumption that the resulting economic development will promote political stability throughout the region. these measures are therefore inseparable from the current situation in the balkan region - in particular in bosnia and herzegovina, serbia and kosovo - of severe economic and social crisis. the crisis in this region, which is obviously part of the general crisis of capitalism and is suffering its effects, is nevertheless rooted in a long process of interference, aggression and military occupation of the region, promoted by the eu, its major powers and the usa, with the aim of imposing their economic and political dominance in the region. the secession of kosovo and the role played by the eu in that process are illustrative of this, and the internal processes of reform and transition are the current stage in this process of imposing imperial rule on the region. it is in this context that the proposals now being made should be inserted, analysed and understood.
in writing. - this report aims to extend unlimited exceptional duty-free access to the eu market for almost all products originating in the countries and territories benefiting from the so-called stabilisation and association process. the pretext is to revitalise the economies of the western balkans through privileged access to the eu market, on the assumption that the resulting economic development will promote political stability throughout the region. these measures are therefore inseparable from the current situation in the balkan region - in particular in bosnia and herzegovina, serbia and kosovo - of severe economic and social crisis. the crisis in this region, which is part of the general crisis of capitalism and is suffering its effects, is nevertheless rooted in a long process of interference, aggression and military occupation of the region, promoted by the eu, its major powers and the usa, with the aim of imposing their economic and political dominance. the secession of kosovo and the role played by the eu in that process are illustrative of this, and the internal processes of reform and transition are the current stage in this process of imposing imperial rule on the region.
in writing. − with regulation (ec) no 2007/2000, the european union granted exceptional unlimited duty-free access to the eu market to almost all products originating in the countries and territories benefiting from the stabilisation and association process. the main objective of this measure is to revitalise the economies of the western balkans through privileged access to the eu market. the resulting economic development will promote political stability throughout the region. the benefits of this regulation shall end on 31 december 2010. in view of the ongoing financial and economic crisis, it is necessary to extend these conditions until 31 december 2015 in order to ensure that the end of these privileged conditions does not lead to stagnation of the economies of these regions, which need good economic conditions to maintain stability and peace in this troubled region of the balkans.
in writing. − the purpose of this report is to extend the scope of council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 adopting exceptional trade measures in favour of countries and territories participating in or linked to the eu's stabilisation and association process. the european union has granted unlimited exceptional duty-free access to the eu market for almost all products originating in the countries and territories benefiting from the stabilisation and association process. the main objective of this measure is to revitalise the economies of the western balkans through privileged access to the eu market. i believe that this exceptional access should have included an impact study on the internal market. these trade preferences were granted for a period ending on 31 december 2010. the end of trade preferences could deprive beneficiaries of an objective economic advantage in their trade with the eu and could have serious consequences for the overall economic performance of all the western balkans, with negative repercussions on their internal reform and transition processes and even jeopardising their economic recovery. the present proposal, which i voted in favour of, aims to extend the validity of these measures until 31 december 2015.
in writing. − through regulation (ec) no 2007/2000, the european union granted exceptional unlimited duty-free access to the eu market to almost all products originating in the countries and territories benefiting from the stabilisation and association process. the main objective of this measure is to revitalise the economies of the western balkans through privileged access to the eu market. these trade preferences, which currently apply to bosnia and herzegovina, serbia and kosovo, were granted for a period that was to end on 31 december 2010, but in order not to jeopardise their recovery process, it is now necessary to extend their validity until 31 december 2015.

in writing. − transparency of political institutions is a prerequisite for their legitimacy and an ethical imperative. the parliament was the first european institution to deal with the phenomenon of the growing number of interest groups at european level and, in particular, with the consequences of this development for the legislative process. after several reports and in-depth discussions, parliament launched its register for interest representatives in 1996. in 2006, the commission published a european transparency initiative in which it proposed the creation of a single common register of interest representatives in the commission and parliament. parliament's response to this commission initiative was the report of the committee on constitutional affairs on the development of a framework for the activities of interest representatives in the european institutions, adopted by the plenary on 8 may 2008. subsequently, the high-level joint working group set up to create a common system approved a draft agreement for the establishment of a transparency register in november 2010, and parliament has achieved its essential objectives. i voted in favour of this report because i consider that the common register is a step forward towards greater transparency in the european institutions.

in writing. − the smooth functioning of the internal market depends on the stability of the financial system and the trust placed in financial institutions and transactions by european citizens and consumers. in the wake of the financial crisis, it has become clear that the quality of consumer protection and safeguards in the financial services sector requires tangible and significant improvement, in particular in the areas of control and supervision. an effective and appropriate governance system is required in terms of risk management, compliance, internal audit functions, strategies and policies, as well as processes and procedures. to meet this challenge, which is both important and complex, a set of measures with immediate or medium-term effects is needed. the organisation of the responsibility of the members of the management boards should be clearly defined and carried out in a reasonable manner so as not to compromise the desirable exploitation of business opportunities by financial institutions or the quality of the human resources at their disposal. this report sets out solutions to this problem and i therefore approve it.

in writing. − the proper functioning of the internal market depends on the stability of the financial system and, consequently, on the confidence of european citizens and consumers in financial institutions and transactions. this implies the need to strengthen and review the current systems which have proved inadequate, with particular emphasis on control and supervision mechanisms. i therefore welcome the conclusions and observations set out in the green paper and the opportunity to improve the governance of financial institutions through the union, and i support the rapporteur in his call for a cost-benefit impact assessment of the commission's proposals, focusing on the need to preserve competitiveness and contribute to economic growth. it is therefore urgent to find mechanisms and solutions that allow for risk reduction and to create a permanent dialogue between supervisory authorities, auditors and institutions.
in writing. − the financial crisis, which began with the collapse of lehmann brothers in 2008 and the subprime lending (abusive securitisation of mortgage debt), has cast very serious doubts on the soundness of financial institutions, forcing governments in both europe and the united states to inject public funds (around 25% of gdp) into the financial sector. this situation led the european commission, through its communication of 4 march 2009, to present a genuine programme of reforms of the regulatory framework and the financial market supervision regime. in view of the economic and financial crisis we are experiencing, it is never too late to redouble our attention to the financial sector, starting with the governance of financial companies, which most of the time do not take into account their customers (borrowers, depositors, etc.). i therefore welcome the commission's green paper and welcome its proposals, which can and should accompany and complement the rules adopted to strengthen the financial system and in the context of the new european supervision. i therefore vote in favour of this report on corporate governance in financial institutions, hoping that it will make a decisive contribution to the soundness of these institutions.
in writing. − the report acknowledges some important aspects and some evidence, such as the fact that the financial sector must respond to the needs of the economy, contribute to sustainable growth and demonstrate social responsibility, and that during the recent financial crisis many institutions around the world have been a heavy burden on the taxpayer. however, having made these statements, it is unable to draw all the consequences of the facts it sets out, leaving it with some inconsequential considerations. the report also calls for the commission to take a more active role in the fight against fraud, and calls for the commission to be able to take a more active role in the fight against fraud. we are not ignorant of the contribution that some of these guidelines can make to significantly (and temporarily) improving the functioning of the financial system. but of course they do not change the essential thing, the unsustainability of the system and its predatory nature, the speculative drive, aimed at the central objective of multiplying profits. the report completely fails to address the central issue: the recovery of the role of the state in this area and the rescue of the financial sector back to its social function, with its public and democratic control.
in writing. − the only important aspect the report presents is the recognition that the financial sector must respond to the needs of the real economy, contribute to sustainable growth and demonstrate greater social responsibility, adding further that during the recent financial crisis many institutions around the world have been a heavy burden on the taxpayer. it goes so far as to claim that some financial institutions and supervisory authorities did not fully understand the nature, scale and complexity of the risks they were exposed to. but then the report does not make the necessary corrections, limiting itself to questions of ethics in the behaviour of some players in financial institutions and markets and the creation of an effective and adequate governance system in terms of risk management, compliance with standards, etc. of course these proposals may slightly improve the functioning of the banks for a while, but they do not change the exploitative nature of the system, its central objective of multiplying profits and attempts at speculation. the report therefore misses the central issue: public and democratic control of the entire financial sector. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. − the recent financial crisis has reinforced the need to look at ethical issues related to management in financial institutions in a more responsible way. aspects related to the remuneration structure and governance of the remuneration of directors and managers of financial institutions must be governed by ethical and deontological principles, which do not allow situations such as those experienced in the recent past, with the distribution of management bonuses in companies that soon afterwards went bankrupt or revealed tremendous difficulties. the eu must have a long-term productive, social and environmental model that respects the interests of all, companies, shareholders and workers.
in writing. − this report on corporate governance in financial institutions sets out a set of measures to be implemented in the corporations that govern financial institutions. in short, the aim is to draw lessons from the global financial crisis triggered by the collapse of lehman brothers in the autumn of 2008, coupled with the abusive securitisation of us mortgage debt. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the euro against counterfeiting is based on the principle of the protection of the euro against counterfeiting. the commission has also proposed that the new rules on the application of the principle of proportionality be amended to take account of the new rules on the application of the principle of proportionality. it is a package of measures to which i attach my vote, in the hope that the measures presented by the commission, and now by the european parliament, will be sufficient to prevent situations such as those we experienced in the autumn of 2008, and which are still reflected in the daily lives of the portuguese.
in writing. - i vote against for the following reasons. the report does not assume that the financial crisis of 2007-2008 was systemic in nature. in other words, a nature that arises from the way the financial system is organised, which implies recognising that the organisation of the system strongly influences the decisions of the directors of financial companies, whatever the levels of transparency required of the directors. for example, the report fails to recognise that a very important factor in the crisis was the possibility for commercial banks to exploit financial investments of a speculative nature. this is an organisational issue that remains untouched in this report, and there are no risk assessment committees or professional competence requirements for administrators to prevent the harmful consequences of using household savings for speculative profit. herd behaviour in financial markets is an inevitable phenomenon which inevitably leads to the formation of speculative bubbles and their bursting.
in writing. − no market in which financial institutions take on a central dimension can operate without the confidence of the various economic operators in its proper functioning. to do this, a balance must be struck between the freedom of enterprise of the institutions in what is essentially a private matter and the economic impact that a (new) crisis in the financial system could have on the real economy, on the lives of all as members of a community. in view of the causes of the recent financial crisis, it is necessary to find mechanisms to control investment risk, the composition of the boards of directors and the remuneration of directors, and thus to promote the strengthening of cooperation between public and private supervisory bodies, while ensuring their independence. because this resolution makes proposals in the areas mentioned, i voted in favour.
in writing. - i support this motion for a resolution, considering that the multilateral trading system remains by far the most effective framework for achieving fair and equitable trade worldwide. for that reason, achieving a balanced outcome in the wto doha agenda negotiations should be a priority for the union negotiators. the importance of this agreement lies in the fact that india is the seventh largest economy in the world, but it is important to note that despite sustained economic growth, huge inequalities persist. i stress the need to ensure that the acl does not limit the powers that the indian government needs to solve the problems of poverty and inequality. the final acl should include a binding inter-state dispute settlement mechanism, provisions on mediation on non-tariff barriers, anti-dumping measures and countervailing duties, as well as a general waiver clause based on articles xx and xxi of the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt). however, i would point out the need for the commission to include strong and effective safeguard clauses in the acl and to insist during the negotiations that india ratify the npt.
in writing. the world's largest democracy today is a reflection of paradoxes and asymmetries which a history often spanning thousands of years seems to have integrated without difficulty. while the most severe poverty has not disappeared, it is no less certain that the surges and flows of prosperity have propelled india to a more prominent role internationally and revealed that its economy and society are thriving and innovating with speed and efficiency. a free trade agreement between the european union and india could be a happy conclusion to a process of deepening trade interaction. i hope that, beyond the sharing of values, the eu and india will continue to seek to know each other better and to benefit from that knowledge and the gains that come from that contact.
in writing. the european parliament's resolution on the situation in the middle east calls for the eu to take action to help the people of the region. trade relations between the eu and india are significant, with india being india's largest trading partner and largest foreign investor. the eu, in turn, is the main recipient of indian investment abroad and should continue to give priority to a multilateral trading system that favours developing countries. in fact, india is the largest beneficiary of the generalized system of preferences. given the importance of the eu-india strategic relationship and the fact that issues relating to agriculture, respect for human rights (in particular the issue of child labour), environmental protection, compliance with the recommendations of the international labour organisation on social issues and respect for copyright are safeguarded, the conditions are right for us to vote in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. - this free trade agreement the most comprehensive to date negotiated by the eu , beyond its concrete content, necessarily leads to a wider discussion on free trade, its role, its objectives and its consequences. free trade is one of the pillars of neoliberalism, emerging in the 1970s, in the context of the so-called washington consensus, as one of the axes of the capitalist system's response to the structural crisis that then (as now) was once again showing signs of itself. it has meant a way for powers with imperialist ambitions to extend their domination of markets and force new and more intense forms of exploitation of workers by competing with labour from very different countries and regions of the world, and thereby forcing a lower leveling of living and working conditions. with this they sought to gain renewed conditions for the continuation of the process of capitalist accumulation. and so it remains. the consequences are obvious: in addition to the pressure on workers and their rights, competition between production systems with very different levels of development tends to accentuate differences, i.e. to strengthen the strong and weaken the weak. this deal won't be any different.
in writing. - the liberalization and deregulation of world trade has caused a profound weakening of the productive apparatus of the weakest eu economies, such as portugal, which are run in accordance with the interests of the major economic groups of the european powers. in the face of the visible disaster caused by this path, the eu, instead of grabbing its way, continues to give signs of wanting to force a breakthrough. it is therefore in this context that we must look at this agreement - the most comprehensive to date negotiated by the european union. what is needed is an urgent and profound change in the current trade policies to take account of the specificities of each member state of the european union, by orienting international trade towards complementarity rather than competition; towards the establishment of fair and equitable economic relations, mutually beneficial, serving the development of peoples and countries and not just some economic and financial groups. the multifaceted crisis we face calls for a new economic, social, energy and environmental rationality and the defence of each country's right to produce in a sustainable way - something that free trade, one of the pillars of neoliberalism, clearly makes impossible.
in writing. − the eu is india's main trading partner, with trade in goods and services in 2009-2010 accounting for approximately eur 84 billion and the eu accounting for 20.15% of india's total exports and 13.32% of its total imports, but india accounting for 2.6% of the eu's total exports and 2.2% of its total imports. we cannot therefore fail to take into account that the objectives of the common commercial policy must be fully coordinated with the overall objectives of the european union and that, according to the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the union's common commercial policy must be conducted in accordance with the principles and objectives of the union's external action, and must contribute, in particular, to sustainable development, poverty eradication and the protection of human rights. it is therefore very important that the use of child labour and the failure to comply with international social and environmental standards, which is a form of dumping harmful to european companies and workers, should not be forgotten in these negotiations. it is therefore essential that the commission clarifies these points before concluding a trade agreement.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution on the state of play of the negotiations on the conclusion of the eu-india free trade agreement. the negotiations between the european union and india for a free trade agreement have made significant progress. india is taking a new position in the international geopolitical context, having gone from a recipient country of development aid to a donor country. this agreement is of particular importance. indeed, if the cooperation between the eu and india, which is now being negotiated, is based on a system of shared universal values, it could serve as a model for cooperation with other countries. i would highlight from the context of these negotiations the emphasis placed on the protection of the sme sector in india, suggesting that all eu-india development cooperation programmes aim to strengthen smes with measures to help finance local market-oriented projects. in india, as in the countries of the union, smes are a motor of economic growth and, consequently, of job creation.
in writing. − given the significant benefits that both sides can achieve, i hope that the negotiations between the eu and india can continue with a view to the swift conclusion of an ambitious, balanced and comprehensive free trade agreement.
in writing. the european parliament has also called for the establishment of a european union-wide network of information and communication networks. in particular, japan is the third largest economy in the world in terms of gdp. in this regard, it is important to raise investment and trade in services in all trade discussions with japan, ensuring that greater market opening does not compromise the ability of either the eu or japan to take measures in the general interest and does not undermine their provisions on the protection of public services and cultural diversity. i believe that the multilateral trading system, as represented by the wto, remains by far the most effective framework for achieving fair and equitable trade worldwide; i reiterate my strong support for a successful conclusion of the doha agenda negotiations, and am concerned that the bilateral negotiations are disrupting the achievement of this objective. finally, i would stress that effective safeguard mechanisms must be in place if, as a result of the possible liberalisation of trade between the eu and japan, imports increase to the point of causing or threatening to cause damage to european industry.
in writing. − trade relations between european countries and japan go back several centuries and have intensified since the end of the second world war. japan has been the subject of one of the most remarkable success stories and economic and social recovery in world history, and today it is a respected and admirable state. the tragic events that have befallen the country call for our solidarity with our partners. the tenacity and courage that its people have shown in the face of difficulties should be an inspiration to a europe that seems to be too settled and not always sufficiently attentive to what is happening outside its borders. i believe that both sides could benefit from a free trade agreement which would further strengthen their trade relationship and remove the barriers which unjustifiably hindered that relationship. i regret that such a goal still seems to be a long way off and i hope that europe and japan will persevere in their efforts to achieve it.
in writing. the european parliament resolution on the situation in the middle east and the situation in the middle east calls for the eu to take action to prevent the spread of the virus. trade relations between the eu and japan are not only important but also fundamental to their respective economies (in 2009, they accounted for more than a quarter of world gdp and more than 20% of world trade). in addition, the eu is japan's third largest trading partner. i therefore support this report, although i agree with the rapporteur that the eu should require japan, among other things, to remove non-tariff barriers and obstacles to access to public procurement before negotiations are opened. the european parliament should also send a positive signal in the wake of the tsunami that devastated part of the japanese coast with enormous loss of life and property (not to mention the fukushima nuclear power plant).
in writing. - the resolution is very clear about the view it takes in the opening recitals. the committee welcomes the progress made in the implementation of the wto's multilateral trading system, which is the most appropriate framework for regulating and promoting open and fair trade, while ensuring that the doha round is completed. it is a view of trade, so-called free, as a class instrument in the service of the big economic and financial groups, promoting an increasing exploitation of workers and peoples, with social dumping, which is associated with the destruction of productive forces and environmental degradation, with environmental dumping. this trade policy and the agreements which give it concrete expression are increasingly lacking in democratic legitimacy. in almost all cases, they are negotiated in the utmost secrecy, behind the backs of the citizens, seeking to conceal their economic, social and environmental impacts, avoiding informed debate and clarification. the choice of profit by the big economic groups, at the expense of meeting the needs of the population and workers, and even of industry in the eu's weaker economies, can only be condemned and deserves our strong opposition.
in writing. - negotiations with japan to deepen trade relations cannot be used as a class tool in the service of the big economic and financial groups, promoting the growing exploitation of workers and peoples, the destruction of productive forces and the destruction of the environment. the eu is increasingly lacking in democratic legitimacy, being pushed by the right and social democracy, negotiating trade agreements in secret and turning its back on the sovereignty of the peoples and the member states, trying to hide the enormous economic and social impacts that these will have, without informing, clarifying, debating and taking into account the opinion of the peoples. the choice of profit by the large economic groups, at the expense of meeting the needs of workers and the working classes and even of industry in the countries with the weakest economies in the european union, continues to generate loss of rights, unemployment and poverty and also affects small and medium-sized farmers, fishermen and smes, all of whom are its victims. this blind profit-seeking option limits democracy and sovereignty, creates greater dependence in countries like portugal, which need to create jobs, produce and create wealth to generate better living conditions and not more deindustrialization, less agricultural production and less fisheries.
in writing. − in 2010, the total amount of bilateral trade between the eu and japan, the world's third largest economy in terms of gdp, amounted to €120 billion, with japan being the eu's sixth largest trading partner and the eu japan's third largest trading partner. however, there is a large untapped trade potential and a strong determination is needed to strengthen eu-japan trade relations by focusing on the removal of non-tariff barriers to trade and investment, including numerous restrictive rules and regulatory measures for european companies to access the japanese market. in this sense, the eu-japan fta has great potential to be beneficial for both economies.
in writing. − the rules-based multilateral trading system established by the world trade organisation (wto) is the most appropriate framework for regulating and promoting open and fair trade, and the eu is in favour of integrating developing countries into the international trading system. bilateral agreements, such as the one under consideration, are specific mechanisms which can, in parallel, contribute to the pursuit of the above objectives. i voted in favour of this resolution on eu-japan trade relations because i am convinced that the eu-japan free trade agreement has the potential to be beneficial for both economies. in fact, the existence of open and fair trade is a powerful tool for generating more growth and social well-being, taking advantage of the comparative advantages of each economy and the potential synergies of greater economic integration and new contributions to a knowledge-based economy. it is about boosting a market, the eu-japan, which already represents, as a whole, more than a quarter of world gdp and more than 20% of world trade.

in writing. − forests and wooded areas cover 42% of the eu's surface. although some 500 000 hectares of forest are lost annually as a result of forest fires and illegal logging, the trend towards increased forest cover in the eu appears to be stable in the long term. as forestry policy is the primary competence of the member states, it is nevertheless the eu's responsibility to coordinate and complement member states' forestry initiatives and programmes, adding value to them by defining a common eu strategy and action plan. enhanced forest protection should be part of eu and member states' strategies, especially in view of the proliferation of climate-related extreme events such as fires, floods, landslides and desertification. i therefore support the creation of new instruments and increased funding for eu forest protection measures, in particular to meet the new challenges posed by climate change. information on forest resources, the state of forests and the impact of climate change is also essential to ensure that decisions taken in relation to forests deliver the greatest possible socio-economic and ecological benefits.

in writing. − this report concerns the annual report from the council to the european parliament (ep) on the main aspects and key options of the common foreign and security policy (cfsp) in 2009, submitted to the european parliament in accordance with point 43 of part ii-g of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006. this report is based on the institutional framework established by the treaty of lisbon and, as a result of its restructuring, is more transparent in its presentation of the common foreign and security policies. it addresses the situation in various parts of the world where countries and regions are in crisis, such as the western balkans, neighbouring countries in eastern europe, central asia, russia, turkey, the middle east, the mediterranean region, asia, africa and latin america. while recognising the possibility of improvements, in particular in the detail of events by country, in the description of the means needed to achieve the objectives of the eu's external policy, and in a more qualitative assessment of this policy with the inclusion of strategic and organisational recommendations for the future, i welcome the preparation of this report and i hope that the eu will continue to develop effective multilateralism, which is one of the hallmarks of the eu's geostrategic concern.

in writing. - some of the contents of this report are disturbing in several ways. in essence, they confirm many of the warnings and warnings we made when the treaty of lisbon was discussed and came into force: the european union is in the midst of an unmistakable process of militarization, which we are now seeking to accelerate and intensify. the militarization of the eu obviously does not serve peace, it does not serve the interests of the peoples. the transformation of the eu into the european pillar of nato, as called for in the treaty of lisbon, is part of the process of disputing zones of influence on a world scale, in the framework of (still) concertation with the usa, which takes the lead in this process of asserting an imperial hegemony, which guarantees them control of markets and resources, some of them progressively scarcer. as the gue/ngl amendments stated, military interventions designed to allegedly stabilise certain countries or regions are the wrong way to go. instead of stabilizing, they destabilize. instead of solving them, they deepen the problems. the situation in libya is one more example, which is added to afghanistan and iraq. the development of the common security and defence policy serves the interests of the eu's military-industrial complex, but not the interests of the peoples or peace.
in writing. - as we have been warning, and this report consolidates this path, with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the militarisation of the european union will be accelerated even more sharply and at a faster pace. as our group's amendments have pointed out, military interventions or a military approach to resolving conflicts in order to allegedly stabilise certain countries or regions are the wrong way forward, which, instead of resolving them, actually exacerbates them, as the current situation in libya, afghanistan and iraq shows. the militarization of the eu serves no people. the ongoing transformation of the eu into the european pillar of nato is part of a process of international division of zones of influence, led by the us, in the quest to secure greater exploitation of the labour force and access to and control over increasingly scarce natural resources, notably hydrocarbons, and control over markets. the development of the common security and defence policy is a threat to peace, an element of deepening the policy of interference, a contribution to the arms race, including nuclear arms, to promote fabulous profits for the eu military-industrial complex.
in writing. - the lisbon treaty has given the european parliament increased responsibilities in the field of foreign and security policy. we must therefore make every effort to ensure that it promotes its values and interests on a global scale, with the overall aim of contributing to peace, security, solidarity, conflict prevention, the promotion of democracy, the protection of human rights, gender equality, respect for international law, support for international institutions, effective multilateralism and mutual respect between nations, sustainable development, free and fair trade and poverty eradication. only then will we be able to achieve the objectives we have set ourselves.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the development of the common security and defence policy following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. the common security and defence policy is an integral part of the common foreign and security policy. both dimensions have been integrated into the institutional, legally binding framework of the eu's principles (democracy, the rule of law, the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms, respect for human dignity, the principles of equality and solidarity, respect for the principles of the united nations charter and the principles of international law, including the responsibility to protect), and their objectives have been merged with the general objectives of the eu's external action. in this area i support the rapporteur's proposal to step up cooperation with the eu's national parliaments in the democratic control of the cfsp and the csdp, with a view to strengthening mutual influence on the political choices made by the other european institutions and the member states, while fully respecting the prerogatives of national parliaments in defence matters. within the framework of the eu's values and principles, it is essential that its common security and defence policy be conducted through a transparent and democratic process.
in writing. − the european union can only achieve its international standing through concerted action by the member states and the union's institutions. in this context, a common security and defence policy capable of meeting the challenges facing it is a priority objective. the union's active voice at international level can only be ensured by its own adequate defence instruments. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i support this proposal as it suggests strengthening the eu's role in the multilateral system. it is entirely right that the eu should have a more effective representation in international organisations and that this representation should be valued, as the eu is the organisation that contributes the most to development aid. the eu's principles and values promoting better and more preventive multilateral action should position the eu as a major international player in the emerging interpolar world. in particular, the eu must make efforts to move beyond being a mere observer at various un programmes and conferences. it should also strengthen its position in international bodies in the field of economics and monetary and financial stability, in line with its role as one of the world's major economic powers. i also welcome the report's suggestions to seek to strengthen the eu's role in multilateral security organisations, the g8, the g20 and others.
in writing. − i welcome the efforts made to improve europe's multilateral action, stressing the importance of an active and leading role for the eu in the reform of world governance. this is a good opportunity for the european union to use its foreign policy instruments and to take the lead in the most effective approach to current and future international crises. i therefore welcome the focus on the eu's position in the united nations system, in the international financial institutions and in the other multilateral institutions, and i agree with the proposals for reform and strengthening of the various positions we have taken.
in writing. − the oft-repeated phrase 'not a political dwarf but an economic giant' takes on new meaning when we look at the eu's presence in the international/other regional organisations to which it belongs. we must change this reality! i therefore consider this own-initiative report to be timely and i support it in general. this report examines the eu's role as a global actor in international bodies. in this respect, i agree with the rapporteur that there is still a lot to be done to ensure the credibility, coherence and visibility of the eu's external action, since there is no european strategy for each organisation to which the member states or the eu belong. the increasing complexity of the international system requires that relations between member states and between member states and the eu be objectively coordinated at the various stages where we interact. that is why we adopted the treaty of lisbon! and there is already an example of good practice, our presence in the wto! it is therefore urgent that the eu should be represented with one voice in the various international bodies. and i think that the drawing up of a white paper on this subject, as proposed in the report, could be a good start to the end of this very bizarre reality!

in writing. − in this resolution, parliament addresses the role of the european union in the united nations system, international financial institutions, multilateral security organisations, summit diplomacy and other multilateral organisations and calls for a strengthened role for the union at multilateral level. the need for better coordination of the union's action as such with that of the member states is clear. i believe that the union should play an active and leading role in reforming global governance so as to make international institutions and organisations more legitimate, effective and conducive to shared responsibility. i am not unaware of the many difficulties that a radical overhaul of the current institutional representation of the union in multilateral bodies would entail, particularly with regard to a possible strengthening of the eu's position within the un. the house's insistence on the need for a comprehensive reform of the un security council and the need to strengthen its legitimacy, regional representativeness and effectiveness by granting the union a permanent seat remains therefore a goal that is difficult to achieve in the short term.

in writing. − i support this proposal as it aims to achieve the europe 2020 strategy's major objectives of reducing the rate of early school leaving from 15% to 10% and increasing the percentage of people with tertiary education from 31% to 40% by 2020. the youth on the move initiative also focuses on promoting learning mobility, and it is also essential to ensure that the education they receive is compatible with labour market needs in order to equip them with the skills and knowledge they need. mobility is important for getting to know other cultures, but also for getting to know yourself. less than a third of the eu population has a tertiary education, compared with 40% in the us and over 50% in japan, and europe needs to increase these numbers if it is to become more competitive in a growing world economy.
in writing. − the youth on the move initiative is part of the europe 2020 strategy and contains 28 measures to better adapt education and training systems to the needs of young people by encouraging them to take advantage of eu support to study or undertake training in another country. this initiative aims to increase the mobility of young people by ensuring that by 2020 all young people in the european union have the opportunity to study abroad. the present report, which has my support, draws attention to a number of situations which deserve special attention. in order to prevent this initiative from being a mere concept, it is necessary that member states commit themselves both in terms of financial support and implementation, and that an eu budget be adopted for this purpose. practical barriers and obstacles to mobility need to be overcome, as well as additional mechanisms need to be put in place to ensure that people with disabilities enjoy the same opportunities as everyone else. the mobility of secondary school students is equally important and programmes such as comenius should be further promoted in the member states.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the directive. in addition to improving the chances of european students finding their first job, learning mobility promotes greater european awareness and citizenship, and therefore greater involvement of young people in the democratic processes of the union. that said, i support the efforts made to ensure the quality and accessibility of educational mobility and i stress the importance of the rapporteur's call for more member states to sign the commission's european charter on quality mobility.
in writing. - today, young people are one of the social groups most affected by the global economic and financial crisis. the eu and the member states have an obligation to support concrete and effective measures to enable people to make the transition to the labour market through better education, training and mobility. the youth on the move initiative responds precisely to this desire by addressing the challenges faced by young people and helping them to succeed in the knowledge economy. in the face of unacceptable youth unemployment, i believe that quality education and training, proper integration into the labour market and a strong focus on youth mobility are crucial to unlocking the potential of all young people and achieving the europe 2020 objectives. on the other hand, although this initiative focuses on employment as the end result, it does not dissociate aspects related to education, youth participation, active citizenship, mobility, language learning and a whole range of skills which are now fundamental in the context of non-formal education. i support the report presented and call for strong funding for the initiative, which is essential for sustainable growth.
in writing. - young people are largely characterised by their dynamism, their enormous generosity and their immense capacity for learning and assimilation. a europe with a future and which wants to become increasingly competitive and dynamic needs this important capital. the youth on the move programme, which is part of strategy 2020, is therefore an important systematization of programmes to support young people, with ambitious but very clear objectives, which i look back on and which i hope will be the target of strong participation by those to whom it is addressed. this initiative advocates the need to improve access to the labour market for young people - a very relevant objective at the moment, given the value of youth unemployment in several member states. the importance of the mobility of young europeans, both during their training and during their professional experience, is also of note. this multicultural and pluri-geographical training will provide a more complete and richer education, contributing to the building of an effective sense of european belonging which will help to cement the concept of european citizenship enshrined in the treaties. in supporting and strengthening these measures, i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. − the focus on education and training to achieve a higher level of qualification for young europeans is a key objective of the eu 2020 strategy and an instrument which i consider essential to combat unemployment and encourage entrepreneurship. the youth on the move initiative is therefore to be welcomed, particularly in its support and encouragement of student mobility and the recognition of qualifications, and in the importance it attaches to non-formal and informal training, which is often as important as or more important than formal learning. if europe is to succeed in meeting the ambitious objectives of the eu 2020 strategy with a strong focus on innovation, research and training , it will have to invest in better qualifying its young people, opting for education models that are more geared towards future integration into the labour market, paying particular attention to the skills that really prepare young people for the future.
in writing. - this report deals with the youth on the move initiative, which is expected to be a framework for improving education and training systems. it is one of the seven flagship initiatives of the europe 2020 strategy, which has as interlinked priorities smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. this initiative consists of 28 key actions and concrete measures aimed at promoting education and training for young people through mobility and employability, meeting the eu 2020 strategy objectives of reducing school drop-out to below 10%, increasing the level of tertiary education from 31% to 40% by 2020 and reducing unemployment, especially among young people, which currently stands at around 21%. that is why, as the proponent of the preparatory action for young people your first eures job, i could not agree more with the proposals contained in the report and voted in favour of it, aware that the eu must continue and strengthen all measures to support our young people. only then will we achieve a stronger, more united and more inclusive europe.

in writing. − the youth on the move initiative, one of the seven eu 2020 initiatives, is made up of 28 key actions to improve education and training for young people through mobility and the integration of young people into the labour market. the relevance of this report in times of european austerity is evidenced by the increasing percentage of young people unemployed in the different member states, concluding that this age group is one of the most affected by the global financial crisis. i therefore consider it essential that measures be taken to reduce early school leaving, to increase the number of graduates and to make vocational education and training more attractive. the commitment to education and training should not be seen as an expense but as an investment in the future. as such, i believe it is important to reinvest in existing mobility and education/training programmes and to establish minimum conditions at european level for traineeships, as they should not be seen as employment but rather as the acquisition of practical knowledge. finally, i would stress the need to coordinate these measures with national, regional and local authorities in the form of partnerships in order to make the youth on the move initiative a success.

in writing. − early childhood care and education is provided in different ways across the european union, with different definitions of quality depending strongly on the cultural values of the states and regions and their interpretation of childhood. early childhood learning is the foundation for successful lifelong learning, which is central to achieving the europe 2020 objectives. in this context, i voted in favour of this report on early childhood learning which sets common objectives for the european union to pursue the objectives of the barcelona european council, namely to ensure that by 2010 at least 90% of children between the age of three and the age of compulsory schooling and at least 33% of children up to the age of three are enrolled. i join the rapporteur in calling for these objectives to be made even more ambitious. it is a child-centred approach and recognises that the early years of childhood are crucial for cognitive, sensory and physical development, for emotional and personal development, and for language acquisition, and also form the basis for lifelong learning.
in writing. − early childhood is the prime time for children to develop a set of cognitive and social skills whose repercussions will be felt throughout life. for example, consider the ability to speak several languages. however, studies of this stage of learning and its importance in the general context of education are residual, with negative repercussions, for example, for those who grow up in the most disadvantaged families, where children's cognitive development is often less stimulated. there is therefore an urgent need to increase early childhood care and education (ecce). i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. - the proposal for a european parliament joint resolution on the renewal of the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the islamic republic of mauritania, which expires on 31 july 2012. the european commission, aware of the importance of renewing this partnership and in accordance with the council's mandate, has initiated a process aimed at renewing this protocol, in full respect of article 218 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the current agreement with mauritania has contributed to the economic development of mauritania, where the fisheries sector is one of the key pillars of the economy, accounting for about 10% of gdp, 29% of national budget revenue and almost 50% of exports. but it is also essential for the european union (eu), and in particular for its fishing fleets. i agree with this proposal, which i voted for, but i think that scientific monitoring of the control of catches, the modernisation of the navigation control systems and the cleaning up of wreckage is necessary. in addition, surveillance and the seizure of illegal vessels must be strengthened.
in writing. - this resolution raises important questions, in line with the questions, criticisms and suggestions we have been making for a long time about the fisheries partnership agreements, and especially about the very insufficient achievement of their cooperation objectives. we welcome the fact that several of the points in our resolution have been incorporated in this joint resolution. among the most relevant aspects, we highlight: the need to make an exhaustive and detailed assessment of the causes of the insufficient achievement of the objectives of development cooperation and the various lines of support for the fisheries sector in mauritania; the advocacy of support for the construction, as soon as possible, of suitable landing facilities along the central and southern coast of mauritania (including nouakchott), so that fish caught in mauritanian waters can be landed in national ports and not outside the country, as is often the case today; that fisheries agreements between the eu and third countries should be preceded by a broad debate in the countries concerned that allows the participation of the public, civil society organisations and national parliaments, thus promoting greater democracy and transparency.
in writing. - the fisheries partnership agreements, as they are currently undertaken and implemented by the eu, give rise to a number of reservations. it is a special one, it is clear that its objectives in the field of cooperation are not sufficiently achieved. we support the principle, enshrined in the united nations convention on the law of the sea, that access granted to the eu must cover the quantities that the mauritanian fleet is not able to catch. in addition, this resolution contains a number of positive aspects, such as: - that fisheries agreements between the eu and third countries should be preceded by a broad debate in the countries concerned, which allows for the participation of the public, civil society organisations and national parliaments, thus promoting greater democracy and transparency; - the financial support granted to the multiannual fisheries programme of mauritania must be adjusted to the country's needs for the sustainable development of fisheries; - the need to carry out a thorough and detailed assessment of the causes of the insufficient achievement of the objectives of development cooperation and of the various lines of support for the fisheries sector in mauritania. for these reasons, we voted in favour.
in writing. − the current protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement with mauritania expires on 31 july 2012 and has to be renegotiated so that eu-flagged vessels can continue to fish in mauritanian waters. it is therefore a good opportunity to add improvements to the existing agreement. infrastructure improvements and the construction of adequate landing facilities along the central and southern coast of mauritania should be promoted to allow the eu fleet to operate more effectively, facilitating investment flows and increasing the impact of this agreement on the local economy. as regards the stocks caught, the surplus stocks and those which cannot be caught by the mauritanian fishing fleet should be used, so that the environmental balance is maintained and the activity is sustainable over the years.
in writing. − fisheries agreements with third countries should ensure a fair balance between economic interests and the promotion of sustainable fisheries. in this respect, it is important that the eu, under the partnership agreements it establishes, ensures good cross-border fishing practices, in full respect of the fundamental principles of the cfp. the fight against illegal fishing, the creation of jobs, the reduction of poverty levels in third countries and the supply of quality consumer products to the community market are fundamental objectives to be ensured under this agreement with mauritania. it is also urgent to ensure that mauritania requires third countries with which it has other agreements to respect the same rules as those applied to community-flagged vessels, thus avoiding competitive inequalities which are to the detriment of the community fleet.
in writing. − i support this proposal, considering that it will benefit the eu, as a well-functioning public procurement market is essential to promote the single market, stimulate innovation, promote a high level of environmental and climate protection, and social inclusion across the eu. particularly in view of the need to overcome the financial and economic crisis and to protect against possible future crises, public procurement is of crucial relevance as a catalyst for the revitalisation of the eu economy and, consequently, for employment and welfare. i share the conviction that a sound and properly considered process of optimising the legal framework for public procurement is of vital importance for the well-being of eu citizens, eu consumers and businesses, national, regional and local authorities and thus for the acceptance of the eu as a whole.
in writing. − public procurement represents important economic opportunities for businesses, is of significant importance in promoting the single market, stimulates innovation, promotes environmental and climate protection, and social inclusion. public procurement policy should ensure the most efficient use of public money and keep public procurement markets open, contributing to the revitalization of the european union's economy, job creation and welfare. public procurement also plays a key role in the europe 2020 strategy and is one of the instruments to be used to achieve the proposed objectives. this motion for a resolution calls on the commission to address the issue of balanced access to public sector markets and to review public procurement and concessions, thus allowing for the involvement of the european parliament, the member states and citizens and businesses. it also called on the commission to give priority to modernising the rules on public procurement. equally important is the request it makes to the commission to assess the problems associated with the abnormally low tenders and to propose appropriate solutions. i therefore support this motion for a resolution.
in writing. - given that public procurement represents millions of euros annually, its economic importance cannot be called into question. for this reason, although there is a long tradition of community legislation on these same contracts, it is never too much to ask for better and more effective laws, which ensure full transparency of procedures; which prevent all forms of corruption or manipulation of tenders for the benefit of a competitor; which limit to the maximum the number and value of contracts awarded without a competition or without negotiation; and which ensure effective competition in the internal market between competing undertakings, regardless of their country of origin.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive on the protection of the environment. the eu has adopted a number of documents on this subject, including directives (2004/18/ec, 2004/17/ec, 93/13/ec and 2007/66/ec), resolutions (ep, 18 may 2010), reports (mario monti, a new strategy for the single market at the service of the european economy and society), the european commission communication an act for the single market towards a highly competitive social market economy and the european commission green paper on the modernisation of eu public procurement policy. a well-functioning public procurement market is essential to overcome the current financial and economic crisis in order to revitalise the economy and safeguard equal treatment. i declare that i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that it goes against the principle of better lawmaking and gives priority to the modernisation of the rules on public procurement and concessions, which is a significant improvement in eu law.
in writing. - we are facing another attempt to force the liberalization of public procurement. the eu is pursuing this aim both at home and in third countries through free trade agreements. in both cases, the intention is the same: to prevent countries from protecting their companies in public procurement, to make life easier for the economic groups of the powers that want to dominate the awarding of public contracts, through sacrosanct competition. we do not agree with this approach, but we do recognize that there are important changes to be made in this area. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the european communities' financial interests against fraud and other irregularities is based on the principle of proportionality. the committee on budgets has also called for a balanced composition, including trade unions and representatives of enterprises, particularly smes, and for greater transparency both in the committee on budgets and in the advisory committee which the commission intends to set up to deal with public-private partnerships.
in writing. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu's security is not compromised. while in one case or another this may be true, in most cases it is not. what they want to do is to prevent any country from trying to protect its companies in public procurement, just to make life easier for the economic groups of the powers that want to dominate the awarding of public contracts as well. that is why we are voting against it. however, there are some aspects of the resolution with which we agree, in particular the criticism of the lack of transparency in the composition and work of the commission's internal services' consultative group on public procurement procedures (acpp) and the role and powers of the advisory committee on public procurement (acpp), calling on the commission to ensure a balanced composition, including trade unions and representatives of companies, particularly smes, and greater transparency, both of that committee and of the advisory committee which the commission intends to set up to deal with public-private partnerships. similarly, it seems appropriate to stress in the context of the european union's commitments to public procurement at international level the importance of strengthening anti-corruption mechanisms in the field of public procurement and draws attention to the need to focus efforts on ensuring transparency and fairness in the use of public funds; calls for the european parliament to be duly informed and to be provided with all available information at all stages and at the end of the procedure.
in writing. − a well-functioning public procurement market is of key importance for promoting a single market, stimulating innovation, boosting employment, growth and competitiveness, promoting a high level of environmental and climate protection and the protection of social rights across the eu, and for delivering the highest value for public authorities, citizens and taxpayers. with the aim of overcoming the financial and economic crisis and protecting against possible future crises, public procurement is of crucial relevance as a catalyst for the revitalisation of the eu economy and, consequently, for employment and welfare in the eu. a sound and well-balanced process for optimising the legal framework for public procurement is therefore of vital importance for the well-being of eu citizens, eu consumers and businesses, and national, regional and local authorities.
in writing. − a well-functioning public procurement market is of key importance to promote the single market, stimulate innovation, promote a high level of environmental and climate protection as well as social inclusion across the eu, and to deliver the highest value for public authorities, citizens and taxpayers. for these reasons i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution on equal access to public sector markets in the eu and in third countries and on the review of the legal framework for public procurement, including concessions. in this respect, i join the proponents of this resolution in calling on the commission to give priority to modernising the rules on public procurement and to deal with service concessions in order to avoid further fragmentation of eu public procurement law, in line with the principles of better regulation.
in writing. − a well-functioning public procurement market is of key importance to promote the european single market and stimulate innovation and investment. in order to overcome the current economic and financial crisis, public procurement is proving to be of enormous importance as a driver of the european economy, contributing to job creation. the european union rejects the possibility of protectionist measures and aims at equal access to public sector markets in the european union and in third countries. in this respect, the eu strongly believes in the principle of reciprocity, mutual benefit and proportionality in this area. to this end, i advocate better coherence between the common commercial policy and the practices of states that accept exceptionally low bids from companies from countries not party to the agreement on government procurement, putting companies from eu member states at a disadvantage. i therefore reiterate the call of this house for priority to be given to modernising the rules on public procurement in order to avoid their fragmentation and to encourage companies to use this route.
