in writing. - i express my deep solidarity with the european fishermen whose wages have been directly affected by the increase in the price of oil, which has seriously aggravated their economic fragility linked to the irregular nature of activity in this sector. i think it is essential to introduce mechanisms to promote the appreciation of prices paid at production, and to this end to keep prices paid at final consumption as low as possible. i therefore support the motion for a resolution tabled by the ppe group, which duly emphasizes the points mentioned.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the crisis in the european fisheries sector due to the increase in the price of oil, which has affected the economic viability of the fisheries sector, with direct impacts on the income of fishermen. emergency measures of a temporary nature are needed to deal with the difficult economic situation facing european fishermen, but the commission should develop a medium- and long-term plan to improve fuel efficiency in the fisheries sector, including aquaculture.
in writing. - fishing is an essential economic activity for european countries, especially for maritime countries such as the one i come from, and as such this parliament must pay particular attention to the conditions affecting the fishing population. the increase in the price of fuel - an essential cost for the continuation of fishing - has had a huge impact on fishermen's income. at a time of severe economic and financial crisis, when all possible support to maintain businesses and jobs is scarce, i welcome the proposal made in this resolution by my colleagues from the epp to support eu fishermen and to raise the de minimis aid threshold from eur 30 000 to eur 60 000 per company over the three-year period. this will help the fishing industry to cope with the increase in operating costs linked to the price of oil.
in writing. the commission is also proposing that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer. this increase is felt above all at the level of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) often family-level whose workers begin to see their jobs as being at stake. i therefore welcome the adoption of this proposal and hope that the member states will soon be able to increase support for fishermen and that the european union, through the european fisheries fund (eff), will increase the rates of participation for the improvement and modernisation of vessels and equipment and will set up a fund to which smes can turn in case of difficulty. support for small-scale fishermen is particularly important.
in writing. - it was good that the ep adopted this resolution. the significant increase in fuel prices has seriously aggravated the crisis facing the fisheries sector, its economic viability and has reduced the already meagre incomes of fishermen. the current sales dynamics do not allow the fluctuations in the cost of production factors, including fuel, to be reflected in fish prices, which is also due to the current import policy. average first selling prices have in many cases been stagnating or declining for several years without this being reflected in a decrease in prices to the final consumer of fresh fish. the current common market organisation (cmo) for fishery products has not been able to contribute sufficiently to improving prices at first sale and to a better distribution of value added in the value chain of the sector. the economic situation of a large number of companies has deteriorated in recent years, leading to the disappearance of many of them, and there is a real risk that thousands of fishing companies will disappear and thousands of jobs will be destroyed due to the increase in fuel prices. small-scale coastal fishing is particularly vulnerable. these measures must be implemented.
in writing. - the recent increase in oil prices has affected the economic viability of the fisheries sector and is causing concern among many fishermen who do not know how to cope with these additional costs. we must not forget that the increase in the price of oil directly affects the income of fishermen. the uncertainty of the incomes and wages of fishermen, due to various factors such as the irregular nature of the activity, the marketing approaches used and the way in which prices are formed at first sale, makes it necessary to maintain certain national and community public aids. the financial and economic crisis is having a particular impact on industrial sectors and small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) and is affecting activity and employment in the primary and secondary sectors. as in the past, we now have to adopt emergency measures of a temporary nature to overcome the difficulties facing the fisheries sector in the context of rising fuel prices.
in writing. the world economic crisis, aggravated by the political crisis in the maghreb and the middle east, has led to a further increase in fuel prices, with the price of a barrel rising above $100. in the face of the political instability that has plagued the arab world, this figure could still soar. the energy bill represents the largest share of the operating costs for the fisheries sector and, unlike other activities, the sector cannot counteract the increase in this cost by increasing production, due to the catch ceiling established by the tacs and quotas. despite the diversity of opinions on how the fisheries sector should be managed, there is a consensus point that should be highlighted: fishing is a very important activity for the food supply of the european population and a source of employment for many of the eu's coastal communities where there are no alternative occupations. to ensure the continuity of fishing activity and to avoid supply disruptions and increased unemployment in the sector, the eu should raise the ceiling set by the de minimis regulation to values close to eur 60 000, as well as adopt other measures capable of mitigating the recent increase in fuel prices.
in writing. - the cost of fishing activity is highly dependent on the price of oil. in this respect, and since the recent increase in oil prices has affected the economic viability of the sector, it is important that emergency measures be taken to deal with the difficult economic situation facing european fishermen.

in writing. − the small business act (sba) is the strategic framework for more effective exploitation of the growth and innovation potential of smes, to be implemented in the eu and the member states. there are some 23 million smes in the eu, representing some 99% of all businesses and creating over 100 million jobs, playing an important role in economic growth, social cohesion and job creation. this resolution, which i supported, acknowledges that several of the sba initiatives have been initiated. however, much more can be done to help european smes, including: the swift transposition by member states of the late payment directive; the need for the commission to have more effective mechanisms to encourage member states to apply the principles of the sba; the adoption by member states of the latest pending proposal on the statute of the european private company as soon as possible; the importance of the commission and the member states ensuring that the sme test is regularly carried out in impact assessments; the imperative of reducing the bureaucratic and administrative burden on smes; the permanent institutionalisation of the erasmus programme for young entrepreneurs with an appropriate budget.
in writing. - i welcome the creation and development of the small business act, which in my view provides timely solutions to the main obstacles smes face in expanding their activities and entering the market. many of these obstacles are due to excessive bureaucracy and difficulties in obtaining funding. the small business act encourages member states to improve the business environment for the benefit of smes and therefore its principles should be properly worked out and adopted.
in writing. - small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) alone account for about 99% of all businesses and create more than 100 million jobs in the european union. it is therefore vital for economic growth, social cohesion and job creation. the small business act (sba) is based on fundamental principles such as access to finance and markets and better regulation. however, it is undeniable that smes continue to face a number of problems, such as the difficulty of expanding their activities, difficult access to markets or the numerous difficulties in obtaining financing. in this respect, i welcome the conclusions of the commission's analysis and i welcome these new proposals, which aim to improve access to finance and markets and to move forward with the process of de-bureaucratisation.
in writing. − this european parliament resolution examines the small business act (sba), a set of policy principles aimed at supporting small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in terms of access to finance and markets, and improving legislation. the role of smes in the european union (eu) at social, economic and financial levels is unquestionable. in the eu, there are some 23 million of them, representing 99% of the business sector and creating over 100 million jobs. the current financial crisis has had a negative impact on these companies. hence the need to review existing legislation in order to facilitate access to finance, reduce administrative costs and all the red tape, encourage energy saving (currently only 24% of companies value this issue), improve business technology through eco-innovation, encourage the improvement of the level of qualifications, education and vocational training, and promote internationalisation and good governance. i therefore welcome the adoption of this resolution. i hope that all smes will benefit from these measures and become prosperous, because all european citizens will benefit.
in writing. - we are faced with another resolution full of contradictions. on the one hand, it welcomes the commission's appointment of the new sme representative and supports his mandate to monitor progress made by the member states in implementing the sba and to defend the interests of smes in all commission services, in particular by ensuring the effective application of the 'think small first' principle. a positive recommendation is made: member states are asked to appoint national representatives for smes to coordinate policies relating to smes and to monitor the application of the sba in the different administrations. we also welcome the fact that the commission points out that the smaller the enterprise, the higher the administrative burden, and therefore calls for a distinction to be made between micro, small and medium-sized enterprises. but on the other hand, the resolution does not address (or does not address enough) many of the constraints, direct and indirect, which today weigh on smes - many of them stemming from the dominant policies at eu level.
in writing. - welcomes the commission's appointment of the new sme representative and supports his mandate to monitor progress made by the member states in implementing the sba and to defend the interests of smes in all commission services, in particular by ensuring the effective application of the 'think small first' principle; calls on the member states to appoint national representatives for smes to coordinate policies relating to smes and to monitor the implementation of the sba across administrations.' but on the other hand, it does not criticize or propose alternatives to the neoliberal and restrictive policies of the stability pact, which are causing so many problems for smes and the general population. welcomes, however, the fact that administrative burdens are relatively higher the smaller the enterprise and therefore calls for a distinction to be made between micro, small and medium-sized enterprises; the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european company register is based on the principle of equal treatment of men and women in the labour market. we will be keeping an eye on the development of its application.

in writing. the report highlights the importance of innovation, in its many dimensions, for the development of societies. it does so by making important contributions in a number of areas and by making proposals - for example, on increasing the spread and uptake of innovation in a number of sectors - which we consider relevant. in the opinion i was responsible for in the committee on the environment, public health and food safety on this same subject, i tried to summarise the essence of our vision and concerns in this field. the commission's proposal for an opinion will make it clear that there are clear discrepancies with the commission's communication. they focus mainly on aspects which are also incorporated in this report and which are the source of some of the contradictions which make it sick: the view of innovation as essentially a business opportunity, the predominance given to the market, competition, the instrumentalisation and commercialisation of innovation, the defence of the internal market, community patents. these are the aspects that deserve our disagreement. another issue that was not sufficiently addressed was the risk of a division in innovation between the most innovative countries and regions and the others, as we expressed in the debate, a risk that was clearly evident in the results of the 2009 innovation panel.
in writing. - the report gives sufficient emphasis to innovation as a necessary means of helping to respond to many of the problems and challenges facing humanity today. it should be a key element of public policies in areas such as the environment, water, energy, transport, telecommunications, health and education and help to solve problems such as scarcity and resource efficiency, waste recovery and treatment, food quality and safety, demographic change, emerging epidemics, nature conservation and biodiversity. but the report contains some contradictions, considering that the context of some of it is neoliberalism, with the defence of the internal market and community patents, which we disagree with. the current constraints on member states may result in further restrictions on investment in ct&i, in particular in the most vulnerable countries. the result could be, instead of the so-called innovation union, a genuine division in innovation between the most innovative countries and regions and the others. where the public interest, development, cohesion, progress and social welfare should have been, what ended up prevailing were the so-called business opportunities, the market, competition, competition, the instrumentalisation and commodification of innovation.

in writing. - the adoption of the ilo convention, supplemented by a recommendation on domestic workers, is an important step forward which we welcome. in the various countries, as was clear during the debate, these workers are mostly women, with an increasing proportion of undocumented immigrants. these are among the most vulnerable groups and are more exposed to phenomena such as violence or sexual abuse. it would be important that action be taken in this respect at the next international labour conference. the serious conditions of exploitation and discrimination in which they work are well known. many of these domestic workers work in undignified conditions, subject to intense exploitation, without guaranteed rights such as the right to social security, health and safety protection and maternity protection, limits on working time, rest, freedom of association and representation. the need for regulation of domestic work is thus evident. effective policies to combat precarious work, false green certificates, undeclared work and illegal work are therefore urgently needed.

in writing. − it is positive that there has been a decrease in the use of antibiotics, which has been helped by the publication in several member states of guidelines on the prudent use of antibiotics. any decision leading to the administration of antimicrobials, whether to humans or animals, should be carefully considered and take into account the potential threat of antimicrobial resistance. in fact, this resistance affects both humans and animals and can be transmitted from humans to animals and vice versa. while antimicrobial resistance in humans is often caused by inadequate doses of antibiotic drugs and improper treatment... however, it may also be caused by the transmission via animals of pathogenic bacteria carrying antimicrobial resistance genes, with serious consequences for public and animal health. we are therefore faced with a truly cross-cutting issue which requires a coordinated approach at community level, which should seek to ensure that antimicrobials can remain an effective tool in the fight against disease in both humans and animals, encourage prudent and responsible use and limit any recourse to them to what is strictly necessary.

in writing. - antibiotic resistance is a serious problem affecting the livestock industry, which is why i support the committee on agriculture in its concerns on this subject and in its proposals not only to reduce animal resistance to antibiotic treatment but also to encourage other ways of combating animal diseases, which do not necessarily involve the use of antibiotics. as regards the use of antimicrobials as growth promoters in animal feed, i would point out that this poses risks not only to animals, which become resistant to antibiotics, but also to populations, as products of animal origin enter the food chain, thereby affecting humans. it is therefore urgent to study the possibilities of a ban on the use of antimicrobials in animal feed, and to promote further measures to reduce antibiotic resistance and thereby ensure better animal health and food safety.

in writing. - in addition to being an economic power, the european union is also a cultural power whose influence extends far beyond its borders. the fact that several states have traditional historical relations with several european states strengthens europe's capacity to penetrate other cultures and to make itself understood in other parts of the world. it is never too late to stress the importance of the language factor as a vehicle for maintaining and deepening these direct contacts. i regret that, despite all the declarations of intent, the european union still does not understand the extent to which it should promote the teaching of european languages with particular communicative abilities in its institutions. on the contrary, the eu has opted for an inward-looking language policy. i wish i could turn that trend around. the cultural dimension cannot be overlooked in the foreign policy that the union is planning to develop, but must be seen as an asset, not always tangible but particularly important in a world increasingly sensitive to the soft power of states and international organizations. the european external action service will have an important role to play in this respect. i hope you're up to the challenge.
in writing. - this report, drawn up by marietje schaake, mep, deals with the cultural dimensions of the european union's (eu) external action. although it may seem a little strange to talk about culture, a non-essential good, when many european citizens are confronted daily with difficulties in obtaining the goods essential to their survival, we cannot sit idly by and think that, in addition to being fundamental in improving our quality of life, culture can and should be an opportunity for economic development and job creation for young people, and, of course, a factor of union and cohesion between peoples. the eu must be a community of cultural values where diversity is an asset and a factor of unity and cohesion, or, as the rapporteur says, an instrument of peace and global stability. it is therefore urgent to review the absence of a foreign policy in the cultural field. i am voting in favour of this report because i agree with its proposals and i hope that culture will help to find solutions to the crisis and will be an asset to the well-being of european citizens.
in writing. - this report confirms the current approach to culture in the european union: an instrumental view of culture, considering it to be at the service of foreign policy, through the concept of cultural diplomacy. in other words, culture is seen as a kind of vanguard for promoting and disseminating the interests of the european union and its member states in the world (point 22 of the report) and look how far this vision goes for promoting international trade (point 23 of the report). how often is this not synonymous with policies and practices that nullify or disrespect the identity and cultures of each country? the report also underlies a fallacy, which is repeatedly mentioned in the eu's discourse on culture: the existence of a unique european identity and culture, based on values such as freedom, democracy, tolerance and solidarity. culture, like all historical phenomena, is not made up of any homogeneous and common identity. on the contrary, it is an expression of antagonisms, conflicts and contexts of cultural domination. european culture is indebted, as we know, to many cultures in various parts of the world (such as those of the peoples subject to european colonialism). we are faced with a report which distorts and exploits the notion of culture.

in writing. - the repeal of council regulation no 1541/98 is intended to relieve importers of the burden of providing proof of origin for certain products. since products can be freely imported, it appears that proof of origin is unnecessary, but doubts remain about the goodness of this facilitating measure. i cannot but stress the need to ensure the quality of products sold in the european union and to guarantee the safety of their users. more than knowing the origin of textile products from outside the union, it is essential to ensure european standards and not to allow raw materials and processed products to enter and be sold in the union without having minimum conditions that allow it. i also believe that it is more important than the type of products used in the manufacture of textiles to assess whether they are produced in compliance with the rules of competition and with respect for the dignity and rights of workers, since there are more and more cases of violation of both, with unacceptable consequences for the owners and for the viability of the european textile sector, particularly the portuguese sector, which is forced to compete with those who systematically violate these rules and rights.
in writing. - the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation repealing council regulation (ec) no 1541/98 as regards proof of origin for certain textile products and the conditions for admissibility of proof, and amending council regulation (eec) no 3030/93 on the common rules for imports of certain textile products from third countries. the amendments now introduced in the regulatory framework make it possible to improve trade policy measures, especially following the increase in imports from the people's republic of china, by introducing control instruments for imports of textile products from third countries. i voted in favour of this report because, by significantly improving consumer information, it will allow all citizens of the member states to make an informed and responsible choice and to opt for products made in the eu.
in writing. the commission proposal, which the report approves, aims to simplify the formalities for importers of certain textile products released for free circulation in the community. to this end, it is proposed to repeal the conditions for accepting proofs of origin for certain textiles and related products originating in third countries. the range of products covered is extensive: silk; wool, cotton; other vegetable textile fibres; synthetic or artificial filaments; felt and false fabrics; carpets and other floor coverings; special fabrics, lace, tapestries, embroidery; knitted or crocheted fabrics; clothing and accessories; among many others. the consequences of the liberalization of international trade in textiles, with the elimination of quantitative restrictions on imports and special safeguard provisions, are well known in countries such as portugal. this proposal, in line with previous measures, is intended to make life even easier for the major european importers their main beneficiaries, who thus have access to low-cost raw materials and final products, at the expense of national industries and thousands of jobs. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be able to provide the member states with the information they need to ensure that the information provided is accurate and that the information is not misused.

in writing. - regulation (ec) no 1541/98 was concerned with the requirements for proof of origin for textile products originating in third countries subject to quantitative restrictions on imports. in view of the changes that have occurred since then, in particular as a result of the wto agreement on textiles and clothing of 2005, it seems justified to remove that first proof of origin of the products and therefore supported the repeal of that regulation. the overall aim is to reduce the burden on products entering the european area without sacrificing the interests of purchasers at the last moment. to this end, it is important to maintain alternative mechanisms for controlling imports of such products into the eu.
in writing. − in 1998, the european union introduced the obligation for importing companies to provide proof of origin for products listed in section xi of the combined nomenclature, referred to in annex 1 to council regulation (eec) no 3030/93, which have been produced in third countries. it should be noted that in 2005 the quantitative restrictions on imports of textile and clothing products from wto member countries were removed and at the end of 2008 the provisions on the same type of products from the prc also expired. i therefore vote in favour of this report because i believe that it is a good thing to define a clearer and simpler legislative framework for european companies importing textile and footwear products from third countries, where quantitative restrictions still exist because they are not members of the wto. i also believe that import authorisations effectively help to monitor the import of this type of product in an efficient manner, effectively safeguarding its impact on the economic fabric of the eu and, consequently, of each member state.

in writing. - drugs are one of the biggest scourges facing our society today. it is a socially and culturally complex and dynamic problem, which is constantly changing, presenting new contours, the use of new substances and new groups of consumers. the european monitoring centre for drugs and drug addiction (emcdda), set up in 1993, has as its main tasks the collection of data on drugs and drug addiction and the production and publication of objective, reliable and comparable information at european level. this information is very important because it provides a basis for analysing drug demand and ways of reducing it, as well as phenomena associated with the drug market in general. croatia is a transit route for illicit drugs, which are smuggled on their way from producing countries to consuming countries. it is therefore very important for europe that croatia provides objective information on drugs, drug addiction and their consequences, while also being able to obtain information on best practice. i therefore support this recommendation.

in writing. − the emcdda plays a key role in collecting data on drugs and drug addiction, contributing to the availability of objective, reliable and comparable information at european level which serves as a basis for analysing the level of drug demand, ways of reducing it and, in general, the phenomena associated with the drug market. third countries which share the interests of the union and the member states in the objectives and work of the emcdda may participate in the work of the emcdda. croatia submitted its request in 2005 and the negotiations were successfully concluded in 2009. the approval of this agreement is important as croatia is one of the main routes for illicit drug trafficking into the eu and it is therefore essential that this country is associated with the work of the emcdda as soon as possible, especially as croatia's accession to the eu is planned for the end of 2012 or the beginning of 2013. croatia should have a link to the european reitox network and share data with the emcdda, in full compliance with the data protection rules provided for in union law as well as in national legislation.

in writing. − this report, by sílvia-adriana ţicău, focuses on the application of satellite navigation systems in transport in the european union (eu), following the publication by the commission on 14 june 2010 of the action plan on global navigation satellite system (gnss) applications. since 2000, the year gps became available, this sector has grown exponentially (€124 billion in 2008), and is expected to have a global market value of around €230 billion by 2025. the eu could not afford to fall behind in this cutting-edge technology of satellite navigation, so it developed a european geostationary navigation system called egnos (european geostationary navigation overlay service), the precursor to the galileo system, which is expected to be operational by 2013 with a level of accuracy ten times that of gps. in the near future, it is expected to be accurate to within 18 inches. i welcome the rapporteur and welcome the adoption of this report, which i voted in favour of, which will allow the eu to increase its market share and provide the industry with competitive conditions in a strategic and fast-growing market.

in writing. − on 14 june 2010, the commission published its action plan on global navigation satellite system applications, containing 24 specific recommendations for further action. this sector as a whole has experienced a huge expansion since the first availability of gps services from us satellite facilities in 2000. in fact, the estimated value of the global market was eur 124 billion in 2008 and is projected to reach eur 230 billion by 2025. of this, 20% comes from intelligent transport systems and 5% from security applications, including transport security applications. the aim of this project is to provide secure signals for civilian use and to ensure that european industry at all levels is able to compete in this strategic and growing market. the current european market share of 25% is below expectations. egnos is compatible with the gps system, but will offer more possibilities when galileo becomes operational in 2013, with a level of accuracy now ten times that of gps. these facts, together with the immediate and important implications for the transport sector, which has included advanced driver assistance systems, among other things, justify my vote in favour.

in writing. − the international air agreements provided for by the lisbon treaty are supranational agreements which aim to supersede existing bilateral agreements concluded by member states. our position against this principle has been reiterated in the successive agreements on which parliament has been speaking, and has been duly accompanied by criticism of the overall meaning of these agreements, which aim, without exception, at the liberalisation and privatisation of the sector. the rapporteur (significantly from the socialist group) says that air transport agreements with neighbouring countries or important global partners can bring substantial benefits to passengers, freight transport operators and airlines. however, the reality in this and other sectors where liberalisation has advanced (see the case of rail transport) belies these promises of benefits. if there are indeed winners in the process of monopolistic concentration in the air transport sector - which inevitably follows liberalisation and free competition - it is not the passengers, not the workers, not many of the so-called flag carriers, but the large european groups in the sector. these are reasons for our vote against.
in writing. - this report refers to the international air agreements provided for in the lisbon treaty. these are supranational agreements aimed at harmonising and superimposing existing bilateral agreements concluded by the member states. the rapporteur notes that air transport agreements with neighbouring countries or important global partners can provide substantial benefits to passengers, freight transport operators and airlines through market access. however, the reality is that the practice of these agreements at eu level has already shown us that such promises of benefits are nothing but a lie both for workers and for passengers. most of these agreements have as their implicit objective the opening up of the market and the liberalisation of the sector, arguing for free competition or avoiding distortions of competition, the benefits that the most powerful companies can derive from it and the false environmental solution to reducing carbon emissions, namely the inclusion of aviation in the emissions trading system.
in writing. - the adoption of the lisbon treaty has increased the number of cases where parliament's approval is required for the conclusion of international agreements. air service agreements now belong to this category because they cover an area to which the ordinary legislative procedure applies. the committee on transport and tourism has therefore decided to propose this own-initiative report with the aim of laying down some general principles on how air transport agreements should be assessed in terms of substance and the procedures that the committee can adopt to keep itself properly informed throughout the negotiations and to have the opportunity to express its priorities well before it is faced with the final decision of approval or rejection. the new parliamentary powers provided for in the lisbon treaty create a new responsibility to ensure that parliament and its committee responsible are duly informed about the preparation of the agreements which they will later be called upon to approve. this obligation is matched by a responsibility to monitor the conduct of the negotiations more closely. these assumptions must therefore be taken into account in the future negotiations for international agreements.
in writing. − the treaty of lisbon, in force after 1 december 2009, increased the number of cases where parliament's consent is required for the conclusion of international agreements. air service agreements now belong to this category because they cover an area to which the ordinary legislative procedure applies. previously, only parliament had to be consulted on such agreements. in view of this amendment, the committee on transport and tourism has decided to draw up an own-initiative report which aims to define some general principles on how air transport agreements should be assessed by the european parliament in terms of their substance before it is confronted with the final decision and can only approve or reject them. the new parliamentary powers provided for in the lisbon treaty create a new responsibility to ensure that parliament and its committee responsible are duly informed about the preparation of the agreements which they will later be called upon to approve. this obligation is matched by a responsibility to monitor the conduct of the negotiations more closely. the possibilities identified in this report, which i vote for, can be understood as a list of elements to be adopted according to the particular circumstances of each agreement.
in writing. - the treaty of lisbon has increased the european parliament's powers to conclude international agreements, and the process of redefining its statute requires new forms of legal framework for its action. this is the spirit in which this report emerges. as the european parliament is now (also) competent for air service agreements, it is important to ensure that it is provided with means of information throughout the negotiation process. in fact, its intervention cannot be limited to the final stage of the procedure, when its action is limited to approving or rejecting the final solution, without it having at its disposal a range of relevant indicators for taking a weighted position. the need to involve the european parliament in the process is well-founded, but attention must also be drawn, albeit in general terms, to such matters as the terms under which information is provided and the times at which it should be made available.
in writing. − the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon has institutionalised new areas where the european parliament's consent is required for the conclusion of international agreements. air transport agreements fall into this category, as they form part of the ordinary legislative procedure. this requires that the ep be regularly informed, so that a concerted assessment of the whole negotiating process can be made, and that it can at the same time express its views and priorities. this report provides guidance on how air agreements should be analysed in terms of content and procedures to be adopted. three types of agreements are presented, covering different objectives, namely horizontal agreements, global agreements and security agreements. i am voting in favour of this agreement because i think it is essential that the position taken by the european commission, and underlined in this report, should state that the ep should regularly monitor the whole process by sharing information and that, at least every three years, the commission should present an analysis of the advantages and disadvantages of existing agreements. the approval of the agreements must be achieved through a fruitful interinstitutional relationship, which allows the european institutions to participate actively in it.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account the new elements introduced by the council, in particular as regards earmarking, more transparency and initiatives for fleet renewal, vehicle capacity and the possibilities for more efficient variation of infrastructure. eurovignette iii will allow member states to tax road users for external costs (pollution, air, noise) so that polluters-payers are introduced into road transport. in anticipation of the white paper, the legislation now envisaged obliges member states and the commission to take the next steps towards a more sustainable and interoperable transport system, a harmonised charging system and more internalisation of external costs.
in writing. - the imposition of a tax on heavy vehicles is a measure which penalises the peripheral countries of the european union, such as greece, italy, spain and portugal, which in turn are largely the most affected by the context of the financial crisis (which has become a budgetary and economic crisis in these countries). in view of the above, i am voting against the document presented, because i consider it unfair that these taxes should be levied unequally, since the peripheral countries would receive the bulk of the revenue, to the benefit of the countries of central europe.
in writing. - i voted against the report on 'taxation of heavy goods vehicles' because i believe that the application of infrastructure charges could have a negative impact on the european economy, particularly in peripheral countries. given that various taxes and charges, including excise duties on fuel, are already applied in the road transport sector, and given the current economic situation, i think that the internalisation of costs in the sector should be considered in order to merit a wider consensus among the various actors covered by these measures.
in writing. − the revision of the eurovignette directive requires heavy goods vehicles travelling on european motorways to be subject to the polluter pays principle, allowing member states to include the costs of noise and air pollution in national tolls. the average additional cost should be between three and four cents per vehicle/kilometre. this principle, at a time when the european economy is weak and competitiveness is more necessary than ever, can serve to make the transport of goods even more expensive, especially for the peripheral countries, for which the price of the good is added to the transport costs, which are not only already forced to internalize the costs of fuel but will now have to do the same with the additional costs at the toll, thus losing competitiveness. without wanting to minimize the environmental issue, i do not think that now is the time to burden european companies with another tax.
in writing. - the imposition of a tax on heavy vehicles is a measure which penalises the peripheral countries of the european union and at the same time constitutes an additional revenue in the countries of central europe. the text resulting from the trilogue is less negative for portugal than the proposal from the committee on transport and tourism (tran), as it reduces the rate of variation to 175%, and the hourly peak of taxation to five hours, extending the exemption of the least polluting vehicles for another 1 year (now for 4 years). however, the imposition of this tax will remain a reality and will bring an increase in the existing costs for the peripheral countries of the european union. these new provisions of the euro-vignette directive will allow member states to include in the tolls charged to heavy goods vehicles, in addition to the cost of using the infrastructure, an amount corresponding to the cost of noise and air pollution caused by traffic. this average additional cost should be three to four cents per vehicle/kilometre. the least polluting vehicles will be exempt. i voted against the proposal for this report because i believe that the peripheral member states are being harmed.
in writing. - the heavy reliance on road transport is a real problem (in portugal, the reliance on this mode of transport is even higher than the eu average). the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not distorted by the effects of the oil crisis. it is therefore essential to promote the diversification of freight transport modes, particularly by focusing heavily on rail transport. unfortunately, this commitment has not only not been made, but in some countries - as in the case of portugal - what we have seen is the divestment of this type of transport. the trend towards greater divestment is the result of liberalization and privatization. the report in question, in addressing some of these issues, is simply seeking to impose a new tax on heavy goods vehicles (in addition to those already in existence, some of which have recently been increased in portugal), which is doubtful as to its effectiveness in achieving the stated objectives and represents an additional burden whose effects, in the face of the current economic and social crisis, may lead to liquidation situations for many companies.
in writing. - we know that the heavy reliance on road transport is a real problem (in portugal, the reliance on this mode of transport is even higher than the eu average). this situation must be changed, both for reasons of environmental and public health, due to the high levels of pollution associated with it, and also for reasons of an energy nature, linked to the progressive shortage of oil and the increased difficulty of access to this raw material. it is therefore essential to promote the diversification of freight transport modes, particularly by focusing heavily on rail transport. however, this commitment has not only not been made, but in some countries - as in the case of portugal - what we have seen is a disinvestment in this type of transport, which tends to be accentuated following liberalization and privatization processes. this report addresses some of these issues, but then confines itself to seeking to impose a new tax on heavy goods vehicles (to be added to those already in existence) - some recently increased in portugal, such as tolls on scuts - whose effectiveness is doubtful as regards the effective pursuit of the stated objectives, and which represents an additional burden, the effects of which, in the face of the current economic and social crisis, may generate liquidation situations for many companies.
in writing. - this directive provides that member states are to include in the tolls charged to heavy goods vehicles, in addition to the cost of using the infrastructure, an amount corresponding to the cost of noise and air pollution caused by traffic. i believe that the polluter pays principle is not a solution which simply leaves the decision to the market. authorizing and legitimizing pollution if it's economically viable for the company is not a path to sustainability. i believe that the european union's priority must be to impose stricter measures on the pollution caused by heavy road transport and to make a decisive move towards rail freight transport. this directive, without solving the problem of pollution, aggravates inequality between member states by placing a greater burden on peripheral countries such as portugal, which are exporters but not transit countries. for these reasons i voted against.
in writing. - environmental concerns can never be called into question. however, they cannot be dissociated from economic questions, especially at a time of crisis which we are still experiencing and which continues to plague the countries of southern europe, and in particular my country, portugal. i cannot therefore agree with the adoption of the polluter-pays principle, because this situation will greatly harm the industrialists in the freight transport sector in the peripheral countries, particularly portugal, to the detriment of the wealthier countries of central and northern europe.
in writing. - this report presents a pragmatic approach to waste no more time with the adoption of the so-called eurovignette iii directive on the charging of heavy goods vehicles for the use of certain infrastructures. the aim is to achieve the best possible compromise within parliament and with the council. the proposed amendments are the result of consultations with the political groups. in this context, i voted in favour of this report, which will allow member states - if they so wish - to also charge road users some (limited) external costs in order to introduce the polluter-pays principle in road transport. it will also give member states additional opportunities to make their national road charging systems more efficient, which means a better tool for managing transport demand. these objectives were confirmed by the council's position. the proposal to reserve revenue for external costs and infrastructure to be used in particular for sustainable transport and transeuropean networks should be emphasised. an effective revenue reserve (increasing accountability and transparency) will not only increase public acceptance but also ensure the reduction of the external costs of road transport.
in writing. - this directive provides that member states are to include in the tolls charged to heavy goods vehicles, in addition to the cost of using the infrastructure, an amount corresponding to the cost of noise and air pollution caused by traffic. i believe that the polluter pays principle is not a solution which simply leaves the decision to the market. authorizing and legitimizing pollution if it's economically viable for the company is not a path to sustainability. i believe that the european union's priority must be to impose stricter measures on the pollution caused by heavy road transport and to make a decisive move towards rail freight transport. this directive, without solving the problem of pollution, aggravates inequality between member states by placing a greater burden on peripheral countries such as portugal, which are exporters but not transit countries. for these reasons i voted against.
in writing. - the proposal to revise the eurovignette directive in question aims to introduce the polluter-pays principle in road transport, allowing member states to include the costs of noise and air pollution in national tolls, which translates into the imposition of an additional charge on heavy vehicles. this is a penalising measure for the peripheral countries of the european union, which is particularly serious in the context of the current financial crisis. for these reasons i voted against this report.
in writing. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. the eurovignette is a measure which penalizes the peripheral countries of the european union and at the same time constitutes an additional revenue in the countries of central europe at a time when those countries are going through a period of economic and financial difficulties. the revision of the directive in line with the european parliament's position will have a considerable negative impact on the competitiveness and development of the economy of several member states, such as portugal. although i recognize that the final text adopted today in strasbourg is less negative than the previous text agreed in committee, the imposition of this tax will remain a reality and will bring an increase in the existing costs for the peripheral countries of the european union. for the reasons stated, in the national interest and as a member of the transport committee in the european parliament, i voted against the document presented in plenary.
in writing. - the report is approved, taking into account that, with the necessary negotiations, the rapporteur had the opportunity to ensure the inclusion of a revision clause for the regulation in question for the possible introduction, following an implementation report by the commission, of new models covering a variety of environmental goods. this review should take place before the year 2013. in addition, the possibility of estimates has been introduced, which makes it possible to fill in gaps in case member states do not provide data in time.
in writing. - for sustainable development, it is essential to make sound environmental policy decisions based on reliable data. i therefore support and welcome the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the economic accounts for the environment of the european union, as i believe it will help to evaluate policies, in particular by providing data on the environmental impact of economic activities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the economic accounts of the european union for the environment, as i considered it necessary to have indicators relating to sustainable development and the well-being of citizens, in addition to gdp, which would also allow the evaluation of european environmental policies.
in writing. the report also calls for the commission to take action to ensure that the environmental impact of the eu's activities is taken into account in the environmental assessment of the eu's policies. this is an important idea and is, in fact, the only way to obtain concrete data on the real impact of environmental policies. while economic growth cannot ignore the environment, environmental policies cannot ignore (or turn their backs on) economic activities and the competitiveness of european firms and industries. it is always in this light that i see the problem of sustainable development, which necessarily implies economic growth with respect for the environment, two sides of the same coin that europe, especially at the present time, cannot (and must not) forget.
in writing. − on 28 september 2009, the commission presented a communication entitled gdp and beyond: measuring progress in a changing world, proposing measures to create a database on eu environmental accounts with a view to better public debate and better informed decision-making. the commission should, by the end of 2013, present a report answering questions such as: what is the state of our forests? how much are our fisheries resources depleted? to this end, we need a credible and up-to-date statistical base to be created by this regulation. the legal framework created by this proposal will enable the eu to assess environmental accounts in the light of sustainable development. it's never been more important to pay attention to the environmental/economic bipolarity. i voted in favour of this report because, in addition to enabling more comprehensive and informed political decisions to be taken, it meets the maxim that we do not own this world, we have inherited it from our grandchildren. it is essential that we leave a healthy environment for future generations.
in writing. − the development and provision of indicators and descriptive statistics to monitor the evolution of economic and environmental factors and their possible interactions is undoubtedly a useful tool to support strategic planning, the definition of public policies and the delineation of sustainable development pathways. the report also calls for the commission to take a more active role in the fight against fraud and for the commission to be able to take a more active role in the fight against fraud. the information obtained can provide an important basis for environmental policy decisions. the proposal for a regulation only provides for the collection and compilation of data in the field of emissions into the atmosphere, environmental taxes by economic activity and the accounts of material flows to the economy. other data could be acquired in other areas. the rapporteur also suggests that pilot studies should be carried out to ascertain its practical applicability. however, account should be taken of the necessary adaptation of national statistical systems and their costs. the commission seems to take this into account in its proposal, albeit only partially, by providing for derogations for member states when large-scale adaptations are necessary.
in writing. - the proposal for a regulation under discussion only provides for the collection and compilation of data in the field of emissions into the atmosphere, environmental taxes per economic activity and material flow accounts for the economy. other data could be acquired in other areas. the rapporteur also suggests that pilot studies should be carried out to ascertain its practical applicability. but the development and provision of indicators and descriptive statistics to monitor the evolution of economic and environmental factors and possible interactions between them is undoubtedly a useful tool to support strategic planning, policy-making and the development of sustainable development pathways. the data obtained can and should contribute to policy evaluation by allowing the environmental impact of economic activities to be measured. the information obtained can provide an important basis for environmental policy decisions. however, account should be taken of the necessary adaptation of national statistical systems and their costs. the commission seems to take this into account in its proposal, albeit only partially, by providing for derogations for member states when large-scale adaptations are necessary.
in writing. − i believe that a better range of statistics on the environmental consequences of member states' and eu policies, as well as on the accounting of certain taxes that underpin environmental policies, is needed. it is regrettable that statistics and taxes are indiscriminately included in environmental accounting. the aim of this assimilation is the implementation of the climate market and its pollution stock exchange rights. the delegation of powers to the commission is also moving in that direction. i voted in favour, because i support the idea of statistical instruments being needed, even if i reject the policies they serve.
in writing. − it is very important that environmental economic accounts contribute to policy evaluation by providing data on the environmental impact of economic activities. this information can provide an important basis for environmental policy decisions. we must be able to define the object, the purpose and the contribution of the proposal in this regulation to the overall strategy of gdp and beyond. this regulation provides only for the collection and compilation of data in the field of emissions to air, environmental taxes per economic activity and material flow accounts for the economy. it is a first step towards the development of more complete economic accounts of the environment, since, according to information from the competent european and national statistical services, only data at european level are currently available for these areas. further progress is therefore needed to make environmental statistics more reliable and more frequent.
in writing. − in 2006, the european council invited the eu and its member states to extend national accounts to the main aspects of sustainable development, proposing measures to be taken in the short and medium term to develop global indicators that would provide a better public debate and help decision-making based on the economic impacts of the environmental measures to be implemented. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with this first step towards the development of more complete environmental economic accounts, since at present, according to the relevant european and national statistical services, only data at european level are available. other priority modules already under work should be identified in a work plan and for which corresponding data, in particular data on the environmental impact of economic activities, may also be submitted in the near future. recycling and waste prevention, air emissions and climate change, along with sustainable consumption and production, could be better monitored if quality data were available that combined the environment with the economy. this data can provide important support for decision-making on environmental measures.
in writing. - a sustainable development policy requires, in order to achieve the desired effects, that information is included in decision-making processes to enable sound solutions to be adopted. it is therefore necessary for the member states to compile a broad set of indicators which, in aggregate terms, provide a global picture of the community environment. this is the subject of the commission's proposal to the european parliament and the council, which is now before the european parliament. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.

madam president, the eu must keep up pressure on the government of sudan to withdraw troops from the border town of abyei. a solution to the abyei problem is needed urgently to prevent the escalation of armed conflict between sudan and south sudan. this conflict is jeopardising the peace process that should have followed the referendum of january 2011. the firing of shots by militia men at a un helicopter at the end of may was an outrageous and cowardly act; as outrageous as the call by the khartoum government for un peacekeepers to withdraw after 9 july. the un presence is more necessary than ever to help observe the parties and stabilise the region, thus preventing the conflict from expanding. ensuring a peaceful transition to independence in south sudan also requires that the fight against impunity remains at the top of the eu agenda for both countries and for their unhelpfully meddling neighbours. the eu should not be tempted to make any potentially ‘convenient deals’ with president al-bashir in exchange for forgetting that he and his henchmen must be brought before the international criminal court (icc) to answer for the war crimes and the crimes against humanity committed against the sudanese people in darfur.
the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, mr president-in-office of the council, ladies and gentlemen, six short notes. the first is to strengthen schengen. the free movement of persons is one of the european union's greatest successes and achievements. schengen is one of the great pillars of the union. we are therefore among those who believe that it should not be weakened, but rather preserved and strengthened. i support the views expressed by commissioner malmström in this connection a short while ago. the five founding member states gave rise to the present 25 - 22 states in the union and three outside the union. the free movement of persons is thus guaranteed in a territory with almost 43 000 kilometres of external maritime borders, more than 7 700 kilometres of land borders, covering 25 countries, as i said, and 400 million citizens. second note: mutual trust. the abolition of internal border controls requires a high level of mutual trust between member states. there is a need for a rapid and adequate exchange of information through the schengen information system, good police cooperation and the existence of effective external border controls. the security of the schengen area depends on the rigour and efficiency with which each member state carries out its controls at its external borders. when this is not done, the schengen area is weakened, the union's credibility is undermined and mutual trust is destroyed. third note: equal rules. there must also be trust in procedures, which must be clear and fair. the applicant countries must be able to implement and apply effectively and correctly all the schengen criteria, the same criteria that were required of all previous applicants for accession, no more and no less. fourth note: transparency. in the name of freedom, but also of security, greater transparency must be ensured. i regret that once again the council has not behaved in the best possible way towards the european parliament by refusing members of parliament access to the evaluation reports. the problem was only overcome thanks to the diligence of the romanian and bulgarian ambassadors who requested that these reports be declassified and sent to the european parliament, thus allowing members of this house to have access to the content of the final assessments, recommendations and conclusions. the council has unfortunately once again failed to respect this parliament. the same transparency is required for the outstanding problems identified which, although not constituting an obstacle to the full accession of the two countries to schengen, should be monitored by the evaluation committee in order to verify the follow-up given to these recommendations as well as any changes still in progress. the european parliament demands access to this information. the fifth point is european citizenship. how often do we invoke the value of european citizenship in our speeches? since their accession to the union in 2007, both bulgaria and romania had a legitimate expectation that their citizens would become full eu citizens and be able to enjoy the same rights as other eu citizens, including freedom of movement within the schengen area. it is therefore european citizenship that we are strengthening by extending the schengen area. sixth and final note: you did a good job. it is clear that both countries are to be congratulated on the effort they have made to meet all the requirements of schengen. this is clear from the evaluation reports and subsequent follow-up of the expert missions that carried out the evaluation and it is clear from the mission we carried out in bulgaria and romania, for which i thank the collaboration of our romanian colleagues marian-jean marinescu, ioan enciu, renate weber and our bulgarian colleagues andrey kovatchev and mariya nedelcheva. we are therefore in a position to welcome bulgaria and romania into the schengen area and i hope that the council will adopt the same position as soon as it receives our positive opinion.
the rapporteur. - during the debate a colleague said that allowing romania and bulgaria to enter would be a childish decision. i don't agree with that. i think that when we reach adulthood we appreciate rational arguments, and if we're well-educated adults, we appreciate rational judgments that are fair. and to be fair, we can't go around with double standards. what we have to ask is whether bulgaria and romania fulfil the conditions for joining schengen or not. and if they do, they should come in. it is legitimate that its citizens should be considered full-fledged european citizens. and the citizens of bulgaria and romania must not be held hostage to populist speeches. we know that everything is not going well with schengen. we are therefore advocating a new schengen evaluation system, so that we can identify problems, respond accordingly and take decisions if problems persist. but the debate on the new schengen evaluation system must not make the citizens of bulgaria and romania hostages to this legislative process either. they're different processes, each with its own rhythm. finally, mrs gyõri, thank you very much for the kind reference to portugal and the one-sis-for-all which has facilitated the entry of several countries, including your own, into the schengen area. i am very grateful to you for that kind reference and reminder. i would like you to take to the council the picture of this debate and, above all, as i hope, the picture of the vote we will be having tomorrow, which i believe will be very expressive, that the council will understand that when the assembly which represents the citizens of europe by such a large majority, as i hope, says yes to bulgaria and romania, i hope the council will do so in the shortest possible time.
for the gue/ngl group i have been listening to this debate and i shall therefore be speaking against the tide. and the first question is this: is a sound currency sustainable without a strong european budget? the answer, in my opinion, is no, it's not possible. and the sovereign debt crisis proves exactly that. it proves that if we had a strong budget today, there would have been no speculative attack on the sovereign debts of greece or portugal. and this is exactly what we have to answer to, and i think this is the main problem which mr garriga's report fails to address. this report lacks ambition. the possibility of a marginal increase of 5% in european budgets only seems too great in the light of the views of her majesty the queen of england. actually, the problem is something else. it is not possible to set priorities for growth and job creation with a european budget that is essentially frozen. it is not possible to meet the new obligations arising from the treaties with a budget that is essentially frozen. it is not possible to think that cohesion policy is enough, because it is not enough when europe returns to social divisions within its own territory. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
mr president, it is unacceptable that at this time of serious crisis in the eurozone, due to neo-liberal policies and the lack of solidarity and economic and social cohesion, there should be no call for a break and a change in the european union's policies and its financial resources. when we are experiencing an economic and social crisis, one of the greatest challenges is to find a new multiannual financial framework in which there is a significant increase in the community budget to support economic and social cohesion, accompanied by a reduction in the obligation of national co-financing, reducing it to a maximum of 10% of the project submitted, especially in the countries with the greatest financial difficulties, which focuses on investment, public services, support for production, the creation of jobs with rights, the eradication of poverty, social inequalities and all types of discrimination, including gender. the promotion of peace, cooperation and development aid, and a sharp reduction in military and foreign representation expenditure are also essential. we therefore consider that the report falls far short of what is needed for a better and fairer future for europe and its citizens.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on the excellent work he has done, which has resulted in a report that is a good start to the construction of the next multiannual financial framework and a challenge for the commission and the council. this is an ambitious report and at the same time a realistic one. i hope that all the institutions have taken the necessary steps to deal with the financial, economic and social crisis which is not going to let us down. one thing is clear to me: only a united, united europe with a strong, concerted and convergent economic governance will be able to successfully meet the political challenges ahead. we need more and better europe. we need to give priority to the community method over the intergovernmental method. we need to tighten the budget. the european union 2020 strategy is consensual, its priorities are clear and its objectives are measurable. it will be the guide to the next financial outlook. however, this strategy will only succeed if there is a budget that corresponds to its actions, to its objectives. in this respect, the amounts of the multiannual financial framework must be commensurate with the ambition, the commitment, of the european union 2020 strategy. cohesion policy is also based on the principle of solidarity. it is important that this cohesion be economic, social and territorial and that it involves the poorest regions. i therefore consider it essential that the funds for cohesion policy should at least be kept at the same level as the funds for the common agricultural policy. it is also important to move towards a multiannual financial framework whose revenue does not depend on more than 80% of national budgets.
mr president, commissioner, i would first like to congratulate the rapporteur on his excellent work. i welcome the fact that the priorities set out in this report are in line with the europe 2020 strategy and put growth at the heart of european policies. we need more and better europe. in this sense we must give priority to those areas which contribute most to competitiveness, such as scientific research, innovation and energy. there is therefore a need to substantially increase funding for science and innovation in order to promote scientific excellence across europe. it is also important to strengthen the european system of science funding in order to achieve the investment target of 3% of gdp. the new budget should also promote energy efficiency and support the construction of future infrastructure, in particular energy infrastructure, creating the conditions necessary for the competitiveness of european industry. the role of industry, and in particular of smes, needs to be strengthened, helping to strengthen european leadership in a globalised world.
in writing. let us look at the current multiannual financial framework. the enlargement of the eu to 12 new countries, generally with levels of development below the average of the 15 countries that formerly made up the eu, brought with it undeniable challenges and requirements for the implementation of the principle of economic and social cohesion. what we have seen, however, is the relative reduction of the structural funds from 0.42 to 0.37 per cent of community gni. that is, the moment they were most needed was when they were relatively diminished. the results are in sight: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a good example of the need to ensure that the safety of workers is not compromised by the introduction of a new type of product. this is the mff which now serves as the reference for the discussion of the financial perspective 2013-2020 and it is proposed, in principle, to maintain it. the proposed 5% increase will not raise the community budget substantially above 1% of community gni. once again, the proclaimed principle of cohesion is called into question. the problem is aggravated by the fact that the available resources are now channelled to other purposes (which are now included in the treaties - militarism, external interventionism, among others) which further subordinate this principle.

in writing. - since the signing of the schengen agreement in 1985, the five founding states have been enlarged to 25, 22 of which are member states of the european union. schengen has made it possible to abolish internal border controls between the signatory states and to create a single external border where access controls to the schengen area are carried out. bulgaria and romania adopted the schengen acquis upon their accession to the european union in 2007. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the directive will also provide for the possibility of extending the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment. this is an important step forward for these countries and also a strengthening of european citizenship. i therefore support this report and congratulate the rapporteur.

in writing. the rapporteur, who has been following these matters for several legislatures, believes that although there are still outstanding issues which warrant regular monitoring, they do not constitute an obstacle to the accession of bulgaria and romania to the schengen area. given his experience in this field, i think i can safely subscribe to his assessment and his requirements for the security of the external borders. the decision to open the borders to these member states will improve freedom of movement and, in practical terms, will enable bulgarians and romanians to feel more integrated into a union of which they are a full part. i hope that the symbolism of the moment will also translate into more fluid trade between countries and more integrated management of immigration and security issues. the rapporteur warns of the sensitivity of the bulgaria-turkey-greece region in terms of illegal immigration. i agree with the need he points out for bulgaria to adopt additional measures, including a special plan including measures to be applied upon entry into the schengen area and a common approach (between greece, turkey and bulgaria) to deal with a possible sharp increase in migratory pressure.

in writing. − bulgaria and romania have been subject to an assessment of the proper application of all parts of the schengen acquis land, sea and air border control, police cooperation, visa issuance, connection to the schengen information system (sis) and data protection as a precondition for the adoption of a decision by the eu council of ministers to abolish internal border controls with these countries after consulting the european parliament. following the positive results of the evaluations and follow-up visits carried out by teams of experts, it can be concluded that although there are still some outstanding issues which may require regular reports and follow-up in the future, these do not constitute an obstacle to the full accession of bulgaria and romania to the schengen area. however, we cannot ignore the bulgaria-turkey-greece region, which is one of the most sensitive of the eu's external borders in terms of illegal immigration. the measures already taken need to be strengthened and we need to be prepared to deal with a possible sharp increase in migratory pressure, and bulgaria should adopt additional measures, including a special plan including measures to be applied upon entry into the schengen area.

in writing. − accession to the schengen acquis involves the need to comply with a number of evaluation procedures, and candidate countries must meet a number of conditions in order to be admitted to the area of free movement, an area which currently covers 25 countries and 400 million citizens. this report assesses the positions of bulgaria and romania, highlighting on the one hand the best practices followed by bulgaria in several activities and on the other hand the efforts made by romania in relation to the identified gaps. in conclusion, and without wishing to put a number of points to the test, the overall assessment of the behaviour of these two states is positive.
in writing. the schengen area was created in 1985 and now covers a territory with 42,673 km of external maritime borders and 7,721 km of land borders, covering 400 million citizens. the schengen agreement currently includes 25 member states with a common area of free movement of persons, through the abolition of systematic internal border controls and the creation of a single external border. common rules have been established for the full implementation of this agreement, in particular on checks at the external border, the common visa policy, police and judicial cooperation, and the schengen information system has been set up. this report concerns the accession of bulgaria and romania to the schengen acquis and concludes, through evaluation visits and a final report, that both countries are ready for full accession. however, there are still outstanding issues, in particular the need to establish a plan to deal with possible illegal migration pressure. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that the member states concerned should inform parliament and the council within six months of the entry into force of this decision of the implementation of the additional measures and the development of the gaps identified.

in writing. the european union continues to build its trade policy with consequences that affect the different member states profoundly but differently. the agreements which give concrete expression to this policy are based fundamentally on free trade, the aims and effects of which are well illustrated by the rhetoric associated with it: that of so-called offensive interests, as if it were a war. in general, these agreements are increasingly lacking in democratic legitimacy, since they are negotiated almost always in the utmost secrecy, behind the backs of the citizens, seeking to conceal their economic, social and environmental impacts, avoiding informed debate and clarification. with the negotiations said to be well advanced and due to be concluded in 2011, their full sectoral and country-specific impacts are yet to be discussed. but the content of this agreement is not new: the opening up of markets, the liberalisation of services, including public services, which are increasingly commodified, at the mercy of the interests of multinationals and with difficulties for the people. the consequences are well known: domination of markets by some, destruction of the weakest productive systems and increased pretexts for attacks on rights and living and working conditions.
