in writing. - i welcome this own-initiative report as it addresses the current issues of debate in the rating industry, namely the lack of competition, oligopolistic structures and the lack of accountability and transparency, particularly in the rating of sovereign debt.
in writing. − the rating agencies carry out assessments of countries, institutions and companies, assigning risk ratings on the ability to pay their debts on the agreed date. regulation no 1060 on credit rating agencies was adopted in 2009 as a first reaction to the financial crisis. that regulation addressed the most pressing issues and subjected credit rating agencies to supervision and regulation. however, it did not solve all the problems. in fact, the financial crisis has highlighted three fundamental problems in the functioning of these agencies: lack of competition, over-reliance on external ratings and lack of accountability. this report, which i supported, calls on the european commission to identify the shortcomings and provide an impact assessment on possible alternatives, including new legislative proposals. the european commission is also asked to assess the costs and benefits of setting up a fully independent european credit rating foundation.
in writing. − given the consequences that sovereign risk ratings can have on the market, on fiscal balances and on the well-being of the general public, it is imperative that they are based on reliable facts and data. in order to preserve the veracity and fairness of such ratings, it is necessary to improve the transparency underlying such decisions as well as the accountability of such agencies. i therefore support and welcome the setting of priorities for the regulation of credit agencies proposed today, which i consider to be essential to overcome the problems of this industry.
in writing. the role of credit rating agencies is undoubtedly important in today's market economy. these agencies are, by their very nature, information intermediaries, facilitating market access for dividend issuers and investors, allowing a reduction in information costs and consequently greater liquidity and transparency. however, as in many other areas of the sector, the crisis has brought to light three fundamental problems: lack of competition, over-reliance on external ratings in the regulatory framework and lack of accountability for the ratings of credit rating agencies. the role of these agencies in the regulation of the global financial market needs to be reviewed and effective solutions to their lack of competition found, and it is imperative to assess conflicts of interest in the business model.
in writing. − ncas rate three different sectors - the public sector, corporates and structured finance - and have played a significant role in the path to the financial crisis, by assigning incorrect ratings to structured finance instruments that had to be downgraded by an average of three to four notches during the crisis. regulation (ec) no 1060/2009 was the first response to the financial crisis and already addresses the most pressing issues by subjecting ncas to supervision and regulation. however, i hope that the ancs will be obliged to be more transparent in their actions. the lack of certainty about the applicable regulation in this sector is putting at risk the smooth functioning of eu financial markets and it is therefore necessary that the commission, before submitting further amendments to regulation no 1060/2009, correctly identify the gaps in the new framework and provide an impact assessment for the range of alternatives available to fill this gap, including the possibility of new legislative proposals. the credit rating industry has several problems, some of the most important being lack of competition, oligopoly structures and lack of accountability and transparency.
in writing. - the reality of recent years has amply demonstrated the lack of credibility of credit rating agencies. however, they remain at a loss and their action is extremely damaging, especially for the countries with the weakest economies. as entities that are dependent on the financial system, a very interested party in the valuations they make, they live above all from the disproportionate stimulus to credit and capitalist financial speculation. these agencies are a clear expression of the financialization of the economy without any translation or correspondence in real increase in productive activity and constitute a central part of the strategy of development of neoliberalism, always in search of profit rates that real production cannot ensure, due to the well-known tendency of the low profit rate. although the report does contain some criticisms of the functioning of these agencies, it never really goes to the heart of the matter and does not propose public control of the financial sector, because it does not want to compromise the interests of the large economic and financial groups. this is a key issue. we therefore insist on effective regulation of the financial sector, putting an end to the liberalization of capital movements, tax havens, derivatives and the operation of these credit rating agencies.
in writing. - we know, as has been shown by experience, that credit rating agencies are not credible, but their activities continue to be very harmful, particularly for the countries with the weakest economies, which live mainly on the disproportionate encouragement of credit and capitalist financial speculation. they are mainly the result of the financialization of the economy without any translation or correspondence in real increase in productive activity and constitute a central part of the development strategy of neoliberalism, always in search of profit rates that real production cannot ensure. the report, while it does contain some criticisms of the way these agencies operate, never really goes to the heart of the matter, nor does it propose public control of the financial sector, because it does not want to compromise the interests of the major economic and financial groups. we therefore insist on effective regulation of the financial sector, including the liberalization of capital movements, tax havens, derivatives and the operation of these credit rating agencies. we need another tax policy that contributes to economic development, social justice and balanced public accounts, which can be helped by the end of tax benefits in tax havens, the taxation of capital gains on the stock exchange and the introduction of a supplementary tax on the profits of large economic and financial groups.
in writing. − credit rating agencies serve a number of useful purposes, producing information on the credit quality of issuers, enabling issuers to access global and domestic markets, reducing information costs and widening the number of potential investors, making markets more liquid. however, the recent financial crisis has brought to light three major problems in this industry: lack of competition, over-reliance on external ratings in the regulatory framework and lack of accountability for the ratings of ncas. we have to be mindful of the potential actions to be taken. these should be subject to the necessary assessments and impact checks to avoid hasty decision-making that could be counterproductive, increasing barriers to entry and the risk of more prudent ratings with their effects on the real economy and lending. we must look at this industry in a global perspective, as it is a truly global industry with an underlying global capital market. so it's important to keep up with developments in the us.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this parliament resolution on credit rating agencies, because i agree that it is essential to reduce unfair competition caused by the common practice of credit rating agencies to assess market participants at the same time as they receive rating requests from them. i believe that the commission should carefully consider the potential use of alternative instruments to measure credit risk. it is essential that the european securities and markets authority effectively exercises its supervisory powers and has the right to carry out unannounced investigations and on-site inspections and that, in exercising its supervisory powers, it provides persons subject to proceedings with the opportunity to be heard in order to respect the rights of the defence. i also agree with the request to the commission to undertake a detailed impact study on the costs, benefits and potential governance structure of a fully independent european credit rating foundation, which would extend its remit to the three rating sectors.
in writing. - while there are some positive aspects to this report, it was not able to propose the creation of a public and independent european credit rating foundation. on the contrary, the ambiguity of the written text allows for public funding of a new private agency. the report also omits the withdrawal of government bonds from the agency's banknotes - the main measure that could be taken in this area to combat speculation against the euro. finally, the report should have suggested to the commission to consider the possibility of a prior approval by esma of all 'structured finance products'. for these reasons, i vote against.
in writing. − the recent financial crisis has demonstrated the need to regulate credit rating agencies (cras). in fact, recent events have made it possible to identify the shortcomings of their action and to reframe their status as certifying bodies for the object of their analysis: enterprises, the public sector and structured financial instruments. in this respect, it became clear that they play an important role in reducing the information asymmetries that could be felt among investors, but on the other hand, it was noted an excess of confidence in the rating assigned by these agencies, which will have contributed to a large extent to the sharpening of the financial crisis. it is therefore urgent to find a new regulatory model to reduce the dependency on ratings of ncas. the solution is to limit the ecb's reliance on data from external agencies, to strengthen the powers of regulators and supervisors, to open up the debate on the creation of a european credit rating foundation, to increase the range of information available to investors (thus reducing the power of ncas) and, for example, to strengthen the mechanisms for civil liability.
in writing. − credit rating agencies are information intermediaries which, by reducing information asymmetries in capital markets and facilitating access to the global market, by reducing information costs and by harnessing the potential of creditors and investors, promote liquidity and transparency in markets. however, these agencies have some problems, notably the lack of competition, oligopolistic structures and over-reliance, and lack of transparency and accountability. such issues are more relevant in the present day, particularly for member states which, due to their economic and financial difficulties, see the rating of various national institutions fluctuate in an inconsistent and cyclical manner. in the future, it is appropriate to define the role of these agencies, whose importance cannot, however, be denied. i therefore support the proposal put forward by this parliament to ask the commission to carry out an impact assessment and a study on the costs, benefits and governance structure of a european credit rating agency competent in the various rating sectors: the public sector, companies and financial instruments.

in writing. - our globalised world, in which countries are interconnected in economic, social, cultural and political relations, is an undeniable reality. however, in the context of trade relations between the european union and third countries, profound differences remain in social protection systems and working conditions. the european union, as a trading partner and a major negotiating voice on a global scale, must help to promote higher labour and social standards in third countries. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which underlines the essential role that the eu can play in respecting human rights, in particular through the right to decent work.

in writing. − the ilo has a key role in the international system, as it contributes to building consensus around labour standards. a large part of this important acquis is recognised by all eu member states. however, differences in labour law between developed and developing countries persist. it is, in my view, imperative for the eu to agree these standards with third countries, in particular with key trading partners, in order to preserve a minimum of fairness in international trade. this report goes against this view by outlining some strategies for these countries to respect the same eu principles at work. the creation of a standard of fair working conditions is an essential prerequisite for sustainable and sustainable development, and also allows us to meet the millennium development goals. i therefore believe that this report is a very valuable contribution to the development of the international trading system, which is based on such disparate labour relations between different countries/trade blocs. i believe that the promotion of this policy of responsibility for working conditions is a sign of a vigilant and rigorous europe which is guided by the defence of the universal values in which it believes.

in writing. - this report by richard falbr on social responsibility deals with the external dimension of social policy, the promotion of labour and social standards and the social responsibility of european enterprises. the european union has been a stronghold in defending the social rights of workers, whose respect is a sine qua non for negotiations with third countries. despite the eight conventions of the international labour organisation, according to the same organisation, more than 50% of workers do not enjoy social rights, including immigrants, women and children. it is in the eu's interest to promote human dignity and respect for social rights in all member states by creating a mechanism to monitor and penalise those who do not give these rights to their workers. i welcome and support this report, which calls for the importance of values in a globalising and increasingly economistic society, defends the dignity of the human being, does not allow its exploitation, promotes well-being and its integrated development and calls on the eu to ensure that ilo standards are met.
in writing. - we are again faced with a statement of legitimate concerns and complaints, which unfortunately does not go to the bottom of the issues and which, for that very reason, ends up being largely inconsequential. the ilo's 2010 world report on social security states that more than 50% of workers lack social protection. it is in this context that the european union is developing a trade policy based on the vigorous defence of free trade, achieved through the negotiation and signature of numerous bilateral and regional agreements. agreements which, far from encouraging the (in practice) non-existent social responsibility of enterprises, only protect the profits of economic and financial groups and do not give due attention to labour rights, the importance of collective bargaining and free association of workers, the effective elimination of discrimination in employment, the elimination of forced labour, precarious and low-paid work and child labour. this is just one example of an area where the report could and should have gone much further. it was important to hold the european commission to account, requiring it to be consistent in its policies and action and to take a series of effective measures to promote social and labour standards.
in writing. - this report contains some positive aspects of the continuing disregard for workers' rights and decent work by multinationals, the need to integrate social policy horizontally into all the external policies of the european union, including the so-called corporate social responsibility (csr). however, these positive aspects are diluted by the lack of demand for the implementation of alternative policies that effectively require the implementation of corporate social responsibility. we therefore regret that the amendment calling for the deletion of paragraph 31, which stresses that no directive regulating csr and its implementation should be adopted at eu level, has been rejected. rather than inviting or encouraging the commission to take a position, parliament should demand the creation of a csr legislative framework with minimum standards that promote, in multinational companies and in the european union itself, respect for the core labour standards advocated by the ilo, including decent work and social clauses, both in the bilateral trade agreements that the european union negotiates and in the wto itself. we therefore voted against the report.
in writing. − the globalisation of the economy and the relocation of european companies have raised concerns about the external dimension of social policy. it includes eu activities and initiatives aimed at promoting labour and social standards in third countries. the eight ilo conventions on freedom of association and collective bargaining, the elimination of forced and compulsory labour, the elimination of discrimination in employment and occupation and the abolition of child labour contain the essential labour standards. in order to negotiate with the eu, third countries must respect the above-mentioned rules. this is a condition without which no negotiations with third countries are possible. trade policy cannot ignore the disregard for workers' rights, and society can only continue to develop if these obstacles are removed. it is essential that international labour standards are used to ensure that economic development remains very much focused on improving human life and dignity rather than on determining the conditions and rights of workers.

in writing. − in an increasingly globalised world, the eu must use its influence at international level to ensure that workers' rights are protected in a model of respect for the dignity of the person. in this context, a number of questions arise, such as the choice of the appropriate instrument for the eu to print its guiding principle. the eu's negotiating power is also important when it comes to relations with a country which is either seeking to join the common space or is a beneficiary of community support programmes. finally, in a context where a substantial part of the economy depends on transnational companies, there is also a call for the social responsibility of organisations.
in writing. - i support this report in that vocational education and training should be accessible, available and possible according to the age and status of people in the labour market and their income.
in writing. - the eu is going through a serious economic, financial and social crisis. the consequences of this crisis have been felt most acutely in the field of employment. the number of unemployed in the european union is currently 22.82 million. young people up to the age of 25 remain the most affected, with an unemployment rate of 21.3% in this age group. on the other hand, it is estimated that some 15.6 million new jobs in the eu will be created by 2020 for highly qualified people and, on the other hand, 12 million jobs will be eliminated for people with little or no qualifications. the europe 2020 strategy aims to respond to these new perspectives in the world of work. this report stresses the need to develop cooperation at european level in the field of education and vocational training in order to improve transparency and comparison between the different education systems. the report also stresses the importance of promoting the transposition and implementation of european legislation to facilitate the mobility of teachers and students and to simplify the procedures for the recognition of foreign professional qualifications. that is why i supported this report.
in writing. - the current dramatic situation in terms of unemployment levels, especially among young people, is twofold in several member states, and is thus one of europe's most pressing challenges. it is essential that member states adopt targeted policy strategies to tackle this problem, building on the europe 2020 targets to reduce the school drop-out rate to below 10% per year and to enable at least 40% of young people completing higher education to be addressed with concrete, creative and effective measures. i find, unfortunately, that the ambitions of strategy 2020 are visibly out of step with the reality of budgetary constraints, which have substantially cut funding for the main community programmes in the field of education. i welcome the measures taken by the commission to ensure greater permeability, transparency and comparability of the recognition process within and between training systems. it is also important that member states initiate a reform of their systems and strengthen the orientation of education and vocational training towards the real needs of the labour market.
in writing. − this report aims to strengthen cooperation measures between member states to promote mutually recognised, higher quality, labour market-oriented and more accessible vocational education and training. this report also reminds us of the need for a strategy for the future of education and, above all, for a guidance for the professional needs that europe will lack in the near future. in particular, the document warns of the need for greater interconnection within the european education and training system, a system in which transparency, mutual recognition of competences and skills is a de facto reality. it seems to me obvious that in an increasingly united europe, where mobility is a growing reality, mutual recognition of qualifications is absolutely essential. however, this requires the transposition of community legislation in these areas, as the report points out. in the face of this new european reality, education/training becomes the basis and the tool for a successful future. the promotion of mobility, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation is an objective need and should be encouraged by the eu, as stated in the report, which i agree with and which i voted in favour of.
in writing. − in a post-crisis europe, recovering and growing, the importance of vocational education and training plays a crucial role. it is imperative to give young europeans the tools they need to compete in a globalised world and to enter the labour market through their knowledge and skills. (we must not forget that, all over europe, the figures for youth unemployment are staggering.) but we must not ignore the fact that more training often does not equal more opportunities on the labour market. the number of young graduates, those with further training and those with postgraduate training who have no job and no prospect of getting one is increasing in the eu. training must be geared to market needs and must prepare young workers. this paradigm shift will, in my view, be fundamental to halting the growth of unemployment among young people and to guarantee them a future with more possibilities.

in writing. - we are faced with yet another tiresome repetition of the commission's usual rhetoric on the issues of lifelong learning and the promotion of mobility at eu level, which are considered the best guarantee for improving the employability and adaptability of workers. vocational training is seen here as a way of promoting entrepreneurship and responding to the need to create an environment where businesses can succeed, develop and grow, adding that to grow they need a reduced tax burden and predictability so that they can plan and make investments. it also considers that vocational training and lifelong learning should be more geared to the needs of the labour market, allowing for entry and mobility into the labour market. at a glance, the ideological mark of the report is clear: the problem of employment as an individual problem and not eminently social, with the individual (and not society) solving it, either by increasing his employability or by becoming an entrepreneur; a profit-friendly tax system and therefore a tax on work and consumption; education and training entirely at the service of the interests of capital. the rest is not investigated, and no solutions are sought.
in writing. − in this report we have a repetition of the usual rhetoric of the european commission in relation to the issues of lifelong learning and the promotion of mobility at eu level, considered the best guarantee against unemployment and the need to improve employability and adaptability of workers, in order to organise education and training provision. but the report's main emphasis is on the role of vocational training in promoting entrepreneurship and the need to create an environment where businesses can succeed, develop and grow, adding that to grow they need a reduced tax burden and predictability so they can plan and invest. it also considers that vocational training and lifelong learning should be more geared to the needs of the labour market, allowing for entry and mobility into the labour market. in other words, what the report does is to put education and training totally at the service of the interests of european capitalism. on the other hand, it ignores the social reasons for school dropouts, lack of access to higher education and youth unemployment, only to avoid the responsibility for neoliberal policies that promote the interests of economic and financial groups. we therefore consider this report unacceptable. it doesn't go into the causes, it doesn't look for solutions.

in writing. − impact assessments are a central tool in the legislative process. gathering concrete facts for policy decision-making and ensuring that all relevant strategic options are considered when addressing any specific problem is an imperative of rigour. impact studies should apply to all legislative proposals, have a clear methodology, and be carried out with complete independence and transparency. impact assessments shall also assess the option of inaction and the specific consequences for smes. despite improvements in this area, the impact assessments of the european commission and the european parliament can be further improved. this report, which has my support, calls for greater integration of the european parliament's committees, for detailed justification when the european commission does not carry out impact assessments, and finally challenges parliamentary committees to increase the use of impact assessments in order to improve the quality of their legislative action.
in writing. − for assertive and successful legislation, not only good political discussion and concerted efforts leading to cooperation and consensus are necessary, but also a sound technical basis to guide the legislators in assessing the context and consequences of the policies being dealt with. i therefore welcome the initiatives taken by the european institutions to ensure the quality and accuracy of impact assessments, which will in turn ensure their independence and transparency.
in writing. − the policy of the european union should have as one of its priority objectives the introduction of a transparent, clear, effective and high-quality regulatory environment. we have on many occasions criticised the shortcomings in the transposition and implementation of existing community legislation, which are largely the result of inadequate drafting of the legislative texts, and it is therefore the responsibility of the european legislative bodies to deal with this problem. impact assessments provide a systematic assessment of the likely effects of legislative action on health, fundamental rights, social, economic, environmental, etc., helping to reduce red tape and ensure the coherence of eu policies. i support this initiative which recognises the key role of impact assessments in supporting the decision-making process, which must be characterised by complete independence, transparency, follow a clear methodology, carry out a reasoned and objective analysis of potential effects and always be accompanied by a cost-benefit analysis. by contributing to informed and fully informed decision-making, which should lead to better quality of legislation, better transposition, enforcement and monitoring, and faster legislative processes.
in writing. − impact assessments (ias) are a central tool in the legislative process, as they give an account of the possible consequences of the application of a given legislation and therefore help to make a decision. independence and transparency are values which must be preserved and encouraged in any democracy, as they give citizens guarantees of objectivity in the assessment, proportionality in the decision and legality in the procedure. that is why i agree in general terms with parliament's proposals contained in this report.
in writing. - this report, by angelika niebler, deals with the question of how to 'ensure the independence of impact assessment'. impact assessments (ia) are fundamental to making the right decisions. without replacing the democratic decisionmaking process of the legislative authority, they are nevertheless the backbone of that process. i am voting in favour of this report because i share the rapporteur's view that impact studies are essential to carrying out our task as legislators. the more knowledge we have of a particular sector, the better our decision-making in relation to it. in addition, and despite the establishment of the impact assessment committee (iac) set up by the european commission and the positive results already achieved, i also think it is essential to create an autonomous impact assessment structure for the european parliament.
in writing. − impact assessments can be an important tool in the legislative process. this requires consideration of the economic, social, environmental and health consequences of the policy choices to be made and their impact on the fundamental rights of citizens throughout the policy cycle. the evaluation should be carried out not only ex ante but also ex post. the impact assessment process today is, however, fraught with many flaws, as the report acknowledges. often, the only attempt is to attribute a supposedly technical legitimacy and justification to measures which are the result of (conveniently concealed) political choices and assessments. there are also numerous questions concerning the methodology to be followed in each case: what or who will be measured the impacts on? what is the scope of the evaluation? what are the alternatives to consider? these decisions also usually depend on political choices and assessments. the commission has also been asked to provide a report on the impact of the new rules on the environment. transparency, openness, public consultation, participation and scrutiny of studies and their results are of decisive importance in ensuring, as far as possible, such independence and the quality of the study.
in writing. − impact assessments can be an important aid to better legislation if they study, throughout the policy cycle, all the economic, social, environmental and health consequences of the policy choices to be made, as well as their impact on the fundamental rights of citizens. but in the questions that are raised in impact studies, we have the criteria used in these impact assessments. we know that there are a number of criteria, not just cost-benefit. and even then, you have to know who's getting the costs and who's getting the benefits. ensuring the independence of impact studies is therefore important, but in practice it is a very difficult task given the multiplicity of variables and interests involved. there will be assessments and experts with more independent methodologies than others. but in reality, impact assessments often serve more to justify the decisions that are intended to be taken than to address, in fact, all the implications of the legislation that is intended to be adopted.
in writing. − impact assessments (ia) are very important in the legislative process and should be encouraged in the future. there are great advantages to ai. they alert the legislative authority to the consequences of its choices and contribute to better and more informed decision-making. they are thus an important contribution to legislation of excellence.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that impact assessments (ia) are a central instrument of the legislative process, which the european legislative authority should use more intensively in the future. the advantages of ai are obvious. ai informs the legislative authority of the possible consequences of its choices and helps it to make a decision. they can therefore be an important contribution to better lawmaking. however, ai is in no way a substitute for political discourse and the democratic decision-making process of the legislative authority, serving exclusively to prepare a political decision from a technical point of view. there has been progress in the quality of impact assessments carried out by the european commission, in particular due to the creation of the impact assessment committee (iac). however, on the basis of the report of the european court of auditors, i believe that the commission's impact assessments can be improved. i agree that greater involvement of the european parliament's committees in this work can be useful for a better quality impact assessment.
in writing. − the need to ensure the independence of impact assessments arises above all from their high profile in the political decision-making process. they cannot, as such, replace the decision whether or not to adopt a particular solution and can therefore have a decisive influence on the choice of a given political solution. it is therefore essential that measures be adopted to strengthen the guarantees of independence and transparency of impact assessments, thus helping to ensure that this instrument can fully play its role as an aid to the political decision-making process and as a guarantor of the quality and appropriateness of the work of the community institutions.
in writing. − impact assessments carried out in the european union are in the interest of all european citizens, as they contribute to improving the quality of legislation through independent analysis of the effects of potential and possible measures taken at european level. the rapporteur stresses the need to assess more effectively and efficiently the economic, social, environmental and public health consequences of the union's policy choices. impact assessments play a key role throughout the policy development cycle and are also a prerequisite for quality standards and the correct transposition and application of standards. i therefore support the proposals for criteria to be taken into account when carrying out impact studies put forward by this parliament. i would like to stress that these evaluations must be carried out as soon as possible in order to minimise any negative effects and to take account of the greatest possible number of institutional, economic and civil actors involved. however, they should not only be promoted before a legislative text (ex ante) but also after its adoption (ex post). impact assessments shall be independent and carried out in a transparent and objective manner. they should follow up new legislative proposals and follow a common system and methodology in the european parliament.
in writing. − i support this report, but consider that a possible optional scheme could be beneficial for consumers and smes if the commission provides concrete data indicating the need for further progress in order to ensure that the consultation carried out by the commission remains transparent.
in writing. - contracts are the basic link between business and consumers. the single market in the european union is based on a variety of contracts which are governed by different national laws. this divergence in contract law discourages companies, especially smes, from engaging in crossborder trade, thus preventing them from accessing the new opportunities and gains offered by the internal market. in addition, consumers are disadvantaged in terms of limited choice, high prices and lower quality due to weak cross-border competition. for example, only 8% of consumers shop online from another member state. this report, which i supported, argues for the need for an optional instrument (oi) for european contract law by means of a regulation. this will give consumers greater protection under european contract law and greater security when transacting across borders. for companies, particularly smes, it would be easier and less costly to conclude contracts under a common set of eu contracting rules.
in writing. − given the significant impact of contract law on economic transactions and, consequently, on the internal market, i welcome all the efforts made by the commission and the european parliament to harmonise its parameters within the eu and to adapt them to the single market. i agree with the report on this subject.
in writing. - the existence of a european contract law, which has been the subject of lengthy debate in the institutions, can bring a number of benefits to businesses, consumers and the functioning of the internal market itself. we are therefore not indifferent to the potential of a common set of general rules and principles applicable to contract law in terms of increasing cross-border transactions, regulating electronic commerce and improving consumer access to products. however, as the rapporteur has said, i believe that the option of an optional instrument for european contract law, which exists alongside national legislation but does not replace it, is relevant.
in writing. − this report, by diana wallis, looks at the strategic options for moving towards a european contract law for consumers and businesses. a correct choice, in terms of european contract law, can benefit the functioning of the internal market, smes and consumers. this has been a recurring theme in the european parliament (ep) since 1989, leading the commission to draw up an action plan in 2003. the commission has moved forward with a proposal for a directive on consumer rights, in 2008 it produced two progress reports, and now it has moved forward with a set of measures in the form of a green paper, to which this report aims to respond. i would like to say that i am very pleased that the commission has taken the initiative to present this report, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done.
in writing. the report seeks to use rhetoric to defend consumers and small and medium-sized enterprises. however, its contents pose dangers for both consumers and smes. the rapporteur's view is markedly neoliberal, as is clear from the emphasis on breaking down the barriers faced by those wishing to carry out crossborder transactions in the internal market, considering that the draft european contract law, together with other measures, is useful for the full realisation of the internal market. the liberalizations and deepening of the internal market that the eu has been producing show that it is mainly large companies that benefit the most. the current dynamics suggest that proposals for harmonising contracts (at this stage still optional) are being made with the same interests at the forefront. these reservations are justified by statements in the report, such as that the optional instrument must offer a very high level of consumer protection in order to compensate consumers for the protection they would normally enjoy under their national law. it should be stressed that the instrument proposed at community level, which is the same for all contracts at european level, is still very generic.
in writing. - it is a clearly neoliberal report, which is concerned with the interests of companies, and especially the largest ones, since in a fully liberalised internal market the powerful are the ones who gain the most, although there is always the pamphlet language of defence of small and mediumsized enterprises and consumers. but all this is aimed above all at embellishing the product to hide its real dangers from the voting citizens. that is why we did not vote in favour of the report. there is also the defence of an instrument at community level, albeit optional, the same for all contracts at european level, which is still very generic. here are some statements in the report: - supports measures to remove the range of barriers faced by those wishing to carry out crossborder transactions in the internal market and considers that the draft european contract law, together with other measures, is useful for the full realisation of the internal market; - i know . is convinced that both business-to-business and business-to-consumer contracts should be covered; stresses that the optional instrument must offer a very high level of consumer protection in order to compensate consumers for the protection they would normally enjoy under their national law; i would like to have more explanations on how this can be achieved.
in writing. − while it believes that there is still much to be done in the area of smes and consumer rights, this report is a first step in facilitating crossborder trade between smes.
in writing. − contract law determines and organises transactions within the internal market and therefore its potential to both hinder and facilitate such transactions is obvious. the right choice of the contract law path can make a significant contribution to improving the functioning of the internal market and unlocking its full potential for businesses, in particular smes, as well as consumers. it should be noted that parliament has, in its various resolutions on this subject, repeatedly recognised the benefits that an improved framework of contract law would have on the internal market, and has also welcomed the idea of a common reference framework and insisted on the close involvement of parliament itself and the interested parties.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the strategic options for moving towards a european contract law for consumers and businesses. contract law determines and organises transactions within the internal market and its potential to both prejudice and facilitate such transactions is therefore obvious. the right choice of the contract law path can make a significant contribution to improving the functioning of the internal market and unlocking its full potential for businesses, in particular smes, as well as consumers. i stress the need for a broad and balanced participation of the parties concerned. the current working method of the commission, with the participation of an expert group and a stakeholder group, already ensures the participation of the interested parties. however, while still at the consultation stage, it is important to ensure that this structure is maintained in the legislative process itself. stakeholder participation will be essential, in particular during this legislative process, the inclusive character and transparency of which should be ensured by all available means.
in writing. - one of the most pressing issues in community law is the harmonization of contract law. on the one hand, there seems to be a growing sense of the need for greater internal coherence, so that companies can benefit from the potential of the common market without fearing that in a given foreign law there are solutions which they did not expect or for which they were not prepared (this has been a real problem). but on the other hand, there is a certain resilience of the national states in sacrificing their normative solutions, often the product of centuries of doctrinal elaboration and widely known to their populations. in its green paper of 1 july 2010, the commission presented several regulatory models for a range of solutions, ranging from mere soft law to a european civil code. among the various options, parliament favours the creation of an optional instrument in the form of a regulation, which would primarily regulate cross-border transactions and which might also be suitable for regulating, albeit optional, internal contracts. i voted in favour of this because it seemed to me to be a reasonable solution.
in writing. - the completion of the internal market has the effect of increasing the number of potential consumers in the european union. however, there is still no harmonisation at european level of the rules on consumer and business contracts. this results in the continued existence of obstacles to the full completion of the internal market, resulting from the existence of divergent rules in national laws, and in a fragmentation of consumer law itself. the rapporteur's proposal is to examine the feasibility of an optional instrument in this area, which, formalised by a regulation and complemented by a toolbox, would ensure legal certainty and security. such an instrument would improve the functioning of the single market, benefit businesses and consumers and also bring advantages to the member states' own judicial systems. for the reasons i have just given, i voted in favour of the document and i support a proposal from the european commission to this effect, which should in future involve the european parliament itself as well as the economic and civil actors involved.
in writing. − i welcome this report as it includes a number of the s&d group's concerns in recognising the limitations of gdp and the need to include additional indicators to measure economic and social progress in the medium and long term. i also call for the development of clear and measurable indicators, taking into account climate change, biodiversity, resource efficiency and social inclusion, which can help towards a more inclusive, knowledge-based and low-carbon society.
in writing. - although gdp is a useful measure of production for the economic activity of markets, it does not take into account the sustainability of the development demonstrated, nor environmental, social, etc. aspects. i therefore welcome the initiative gdp and beyond measuring progress in a changing world, which aims to encourage and raise awareness of the use of other complementary indicators of gdp in evaluation and policy discussion. i believe that this measurement system, which is based on the corroboration of different parameters of study, will lead to policy decisions that are more suited to the needs of society and the economy in general.
in writing. - despite all the more or less lyrical constructions we can make, the truth is that it is by analysing the gross domestic product (gdp) that we can obtain a reliable picture of the state of development and progress of societies. this is why gdp is (and should continue to be) the main economic indicator to look at. however, it should be complemented, where relevant, by other indicators, which should be studied and introduced gradually.
in writing. − in 2007, the european parliament (ep), together with the european commission, the club of rome, the world wide fund for nature (www) and the oecd, organised a conference under the theme 'towards beyond gdp' where stakeholders argued for the need to develop other complementary indicators of gdp. this report, by anna rosbach, is part of a communication presented by the commission on 28 september 2009 entitled 'gdp and beyond: measuring progress in a changing world' and reflects this need to provide policymakers and all researchers with more comprehensive data. the gross domestic product (gdp) has been the most widely used measure of macroeconomic activity over the past few decades, and more recently has been used as an indicator of social development. in more recent times, several sociologists have argued that this is not the most accurate indicator because it does not take into account aspects such as environmental sustainability or social integration. i agree with the rapporteur's position and have therefore voted in favour of her report, as i believe that the proposal can and should be improved by introducing a more comprehensive and gradual strategy.
in writing. − the neoliberal policies and orientations developed by the eu have undermined social progress and inflicted severe blows on the peoples of europe. the worsening social inequalities in the eu countries, which are now reaching worrying levels, are a clear example of this. this is a fact which we must bear in mind when we look at indicators of development and progress, as in this report. gdp, which is often used as a basis for measuring these two factors - development and progress - is a numerical indicator with natural gaps. by considering only economic activity, wealth creation, and being useful in this respect in determining economic growth, it does not take into account such important parameters as the distribution of wealth, social inequalities, the quality of goods and services, non-commercial transactions or even externalities not accounted for by the market which are essential for measuring development and progress. in many situations, gdp can increase while the majority of citizens in a country become poorer, because gdp does not consider the level of inequality in a society. this makes it necessary to take into account other indicators that can fill these gaps, in order to make the measures of social progress as complete, credible and as close to reality as possible.
in writing. − economic divergences and social inequalities are increasing, caused by the eu's neoliberal policies and orientations, and by the increasingly unfair distribution of national income, both at the level of the european union and of individual states. the use of gdp as a basis for work and as a numerical indicator for measuring development and social progress is therefore becoming increasingly controversial. it is a numerical indicator with many gaps, as it considers only economic activity, leaving out important factors such as the distribution of wealth, social inequalities, the quality of goods and services, non-commercial transactions or even externalities not accounted for by the market. this means that in many situations, gdp can increase while the majority of citizens in a country become poorer, because gdp does not take into account the level of inequality in a society. in this sense, we can consider it acceptable to take into account other indicators that can fill in these gaps in order to make the measures of social progress as complete, credible and as close to reality as possible.

in writing. − the commission communication to the council and the european parliament on gdp and beyond - measuring progress in a changing world (com (2009) 433 final) recognises that gdp is a proxy indicator for overall societal development and progress in general, but does not measure environmental sustainability or social inclusion. in a world where people's quality of life is increasingly measured by factors other than economic, several international institutions, such as the un, the world bank and the oecd, are currently considering the definition of new indicators to measure and analyse economic and social progress. i therefore support this report because i believe it is important for the european union to adopt a systematic approach to measuring the full extent of social well-being, with a particular focus on economic, environmental and quality of life factors in the medium and long term. i believe that these indicators should take a strategic lead in shaping future cohesion policy, thus contributing to smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, in line with the principles enshrined in europe 2020.

in writing. the rapporteur said that the time had come to put an end to the loud declarations of intent without the appropriate allocation of financial resources to enable the declared objectives to be achieved in practice. well, this report is an exemplary demonstration of that exercise. by basically proposing to freeze the community budget until 2020 (with a residual 5% discount), they are thereby compromising many of the objectives set out in its 40 pages, and in particular the objective of economic and social cohesion. in the face of a serious economic and social crisis, aggravated by community policies, the budgets made possible by these financial perspectives will thus be unable to fulfil a redistributive function essential to the effective implementation of the principle of cohesion. we have made numerous proposals on the need to strengthen the community budget to support economic and social cohesion, accompanied by a reduction in the compulsory national contributions, reducing them to a maximum of 10% of the total amounts of the projects submitted, especially in the countries with the greatest financial difficulties. we have also stressed the importance of promoting investment in public services, supporting production, creating jobs with rights, eradicating poverty and combating social inequalities. the path proposed in this report is quite different. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. - despite some positive proposals, the report does not advocate a break and a change in the european union's policies and financial resources. that is why we voted against it. it is particularly serious that it does not give absolute priority to responding to the serious social problems created by the economic and social crisis, with a significant increase in the community budget to support economic and social cohesion, accompanied by a reduction in the obligation of national co-financing, reducing it to a maximum of 10% of the project submitted, especially in the countries with the greatest financial difficulties, which focuses on investment in public services, support for production, the creation of jobs with rights, the eradication of poverty, social inequalities and all kinds of discrimination, including gender. the promotion of peace, cooperation and development aid, and a sharp reduction in military and foreign representation expenditure are also essential. the report proposes a 5% increase in the current community budget, although it opposes the freezing of the eu budget after 2013, as advocated by some member states. but this suggestion of an increase means that the next multiannual financial framework (financial perspectives) 2014-2020 would represent only 1.11% of eu gni, compared to 1.06% foreseen for 2013.
in writing. − many member states are currently making difficult budgetary adjustments, so the defence of the eu budget must be very well justified. the eu budget must deliver the highest level of european added value (eva), be soundly managed and leverage public and private resources as much as possible. the eu's response to these challenges is the europe 2020 strategy. it is a strategy that should help europe recover from the crisis and emerge stronger through job creation and smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. i agree with the rapporteur that 'the europe 2020 strategy should be the political reference for the next mff and that it should reflect the ambitions of that strategy'. the priorities for the next multiannual financial framework should therefore be grouped around the following themes: knowledge for growth and jobs, natural resource management and sustainable development, cohesion for growth and jobs, citizenship and a global europe.
in writing. − the new multiannual financial framework is crucial for the full implementation of the 2020 strategy and, in general, for providing the conditions for sound development, which responds both to the problems faced by the different european citizens and to their expectations of improving their lives. in this context, i welcome the author of the report's proposal for a seven-year multiannual financial framework, in line with the 2020 strategy, subject to mid-term review in defence, at least: of the maintenance of the eu budget, with particular emphasis on the cap and cohesion policy; of greater flexibility, all the more necessary as the financial constraints are real, and also in favour of greater democratic accountability, so that the european funds are real levers for development projects with sustainable capacity. in this context, it is important that regions which have already left objective 1 should be able to undergo an intermediate phase which gives strength to the development they have already shown to be capable of, rather than being abruptly abandoned, jeopardising the progress achieved in the meantime.
in writing. − the eu's multiannual financial framework is an opportunity to make strategic choices for the future. in fact, at a time of deep contraction in the action of the states, the strengthening of the community budget represents an act of confidence in the common project and of strengthening action at supranational level. in fact, there are a number of challenges facing the states which can only be solved effectively at community level.
in writing. − europe 2020 is the european strategy to respond to the new global challenges facing the eu and its various member states, and it is important to structure the economic and financial conditions that will guide its applicability in the period 2014-2021. this report aims to contribute to the definition of the multiannual financial framework (mff) after 2013, by providing for an increase of 5 percentage points in the budgetary envelope compared to the current mff, the maintenance of the funds for cohesion and agriculture and a financial reinforcement of the areas of research, development and innovation, energy and transport. i am voting in favour of the report because i regard the strategic content as positive and, above all, because the budget is in line with the objectives set out in europe 2020. strengthening economic governance and the importance of cohesion policy are some of the areas i would like to emphasise in the pursuit of a smarter, more sustainable and inclusive europe. i think it is important to create an intermediate category for regions whose gdp per capita is between 75 and 90% of the eu's gdp, thus contributing to greater equity at regional level. however, i would like to stress that this new category should not prejudice the most disadvantaged regions in the allocation of community funds.

or, for example, in the venice commission. the issue of non-discrimination... mr szájer tells us that it is not true that discrimination against, for example, gender or sexual minorities is not of the fetus, or, for example, to the checks and balances of the hungarian republic itself. but then there is the discussion of the debate, and the debate on the legitimacy of this issue being raised here in parliament must also be fought very clearly. because, on the one hand, constitutions are not impervious. it must be said that where there is a violation of fundamental rights, the 500 million european citizens expect the european institutions to take action. whether that violation is by a law or by a constitution or by a regulation is irrelevant. where there is a violation of fundamental this. the fact that a constitution violates the spirit and the letter of the treaties, if that were the case, would also be violating the sovereignty of the other 26 countries that have agreed to be in a european union with that country which might violate the treaties. so it's a question of sovereignty for all of us. and i just want to take this opportunity to say one thing. the two-thirds majority, which is often called for here, and which, by the way, comes from 50% of the votes and not from two-thirds of the votes cast by hungarian citizens - that is two-thirds of the members, but only 50% of the votes - serves one purpose everywhere, namely that the constitution should be the subject of a broad social consensus. the hungarian authorities at this time used the two-thirds majority for exactly the opposite: to exclude the opposition and to make the constitution the subject of a great deal of dissent in society. you may be following the two-thirds rule to the letter, but you're violating its spirit. on behalf of the gue/ngl group, i would encourage you, mr stoyanov, to read the treaties of the union, the very rules of procedure of this house, which say that we, being elected by european citizens, must represent our own member states and the citizens, all 500 million citizens, of the european union. and we are mandated by these citizens to respect and enforce the fundamental treaties of the european union, which protect the rights of its citizens. it is very simple: both i and mr stoyanov have the right to speak on behalf of the 500 million european citizens as long as we are mandated to do so in this house, which is the home of the citizens.
the european union is an experiment made up of experiments: the euro zone, this parliament itself, the schengen area and various other instruments are experiments. the problem is that politicians are often much less humble than scientists. scientists are the first to recognize when an experiment didn't go as they hoped it would. in the case of the european arrest warrant (eaw), we now know that it has problems and raises doubts. it is to commissioner reding's credit that she has had the candor to say that yes, that there are problems and doubts with this mandate and that there are proportionality tests that must be passed when mandates are issued, which should not be applied automatically without a longer and more discriminating look from a judge. so the solution should not be to abolish the european arrest warrant, which is clearly useful. we want a rapist or a murderer not to be able to cross the border and be free. but the european arrest warrant must be complemented by effective defence instruments for the defendant, such as the presence of a lawyer and the right to translation, which baroness ludford has already dealt with in her report, but also and very crucially with the assessment of detention conditions in european prisons. it is not the same, and let us not be deluded or deluded, to be imprisoned in a prison in country a or in country b in europe. it is very important that these conditions be evaluated and that the european commission work very hard to evaluate the conditions of detention so that they are harmonised and so that a european arrest warrant can be applied with more confidence.
the european arrest warrant was established by a decision in 2002 and has so far, as the commission points out in a recent report, proved to be an effective instrument in the fight against crossborder crime, organised crime and terrorism. however, there are imperfections in the way the system works: there is a possibility that its reputation and effectiveness may be undermined by reports of its use for interrogation instead of prosecution and punishment and in cases of minor offences. it therefore appears appropriate and urgent that the council take appropriate measures to ensure that the disproportionate use of the european arrest warrant is curbed in practice. in addition, it is appropriate to ensure effective respect for procedural rights, that is to say that persons sought under a european arrest warrant have an effective right to legal assistance in both the issuing and executing states and that criminal justice standards and prison conditions in the european union do not create a situation of distrust between the judicial systems of the member states. only then can we speak of the effectiveness and success of this instrument at european level.
madam president, a few very brief notes on this case. the experience of the practical application of the environmental impact assessment procedure, despite the positive aspects it reveals, shows us that it can and should be improved. further attention should be paid to the analysis of the cumulative impacts of projects, whether of the same or different types. you look at the tree too often, you lose perspective on the forest. the dynamic and cumulative nature of man's actions on nature needs to be understood more fully. the post-evaluation phase should also be given further attention she's often neglected. it is important to assess the extent to which the expected impacts have materialised, the effectiveness of mitigation or compensation measures, if any, and the extent to which they have been implemented or not. public authorities in the field of the environment have a key role to play here and must be properly equipped to carry it out. finally, the transparency of the procedure, public participation and scrutiny are of decisive importance in order to ensure, as far as possible, the transparency, quality and independence of the study.

in writing. - as regards the european parliament's response to the situation in sudan following the 2011 referendum calling for independence for south sudan from 9 july, i believe that the motion for a resolution tabled by the epp group is the most appropriate one, as i believe that it takes a better approach to the political situation facing the country and to relations with other african countries.
in writing. the referendum in sudan sought to put an end to the widespread violence between the people of the north and the people of the south. the results of the referendum today make clear the will of the people of south sudan for independence, which has been repeatedly expressed for many years. my party has been following the issue, and in particular the darfur issue, for several legislatures, and was the promoter of the winning nomination of sudanese lawyer salih mahmoud osman for the 2007 sakharov prize. the award was intended to make the glaring scandal of genocide in that country more visible and to recognize the peaceful work of those who, against all odds, had not given up fighting for peace, solidarity and human rights. unfortunately, osman's award was not enough to impress upon the international community the desirable sense of urgency to address the repeated and serious human rights violations in sudan. i hope that both sides will be able to respect the agreement before and after the separation, build two peaceful countries, lift the people out of poverty and promote good neighbourliness. and the union can help to make that happen.
in writing. − the final results of the referendum on self-determination in south sudan on 9 january 2011 overwhelmingly confirmed the determination of the electorate to create an independent state. the referendum, the results of which were announced by the south sudan referendum commission and corroborated by the sudanese government, was considered by international and eu observers to have been fair. i therefore advocate respect for the results of the referendum as an expression of the democratic will of the people of south sudan and call on north and south sudan to actively engage in promoting democratic governance and establishing lasting peace, security and prosperity in both countries. i consider the provision of external aid to be very important and therefore welcome the council decision of 23 may 2011 to allocate eur 200 million for development cooperation with south sudan in order to contribute to the autonomy of local communities and to address the basic needs of the population and the lack of human resources and infrastructure.
in writing. - as we warned at the time, kosovo's independence set a serious precedent for imperialist intervention in state-building, artificially and in accordance with its geostrategic interests of access to and control of markets, natural resources and labour. the case of south sudan is in every respect similar to that of kosovo. a referendum was held, financed and promoted by various powers, with only the part of the country that wanted independence, as it should be, but without the rest of the country's population having a say. in addition to all this, the southern part of sudan contains large oil reserves which are essential for international capital. the current situation of renewed conflict in sudan and the region as a whole and the dispute over the definition of the border make it clear that the artificial creation of this country will not solve any of the existing problems or improve the living conditions of millions of sudanese, but will rather aggravate contradictions and conflicts. after the great imperialist powers have carved up the african continent in their own interests, all indications are that a process is under way in south sudan which will lead to more war and suffering for the already massacred african populations.
in writing. - the conflicts in sudan, particularly in the darfur region, have claimed many victims over the years, particularly among the most disadvantaged. we hope that the referendum will bring an end to the conflict and that it will definitely lead to a lasting peace process. the eu will have an important role in the future developments in the region and cannot relinquish its important role in pacifying the region.
in writing. the results of the referendum in sudan clearly indicate the will of the peoples of south sudan for independence, as they have been demanding for several years. the epp has followed the issue, and in particular that of darfur, through several legislatures, and was the promoter of the winning candidacy of the sudanese lawyer salih mahmoud osman for the 2007 sakharov prize. the referendum was aimed at ending the violence of the northern populations against those in the south of the country. it is hoped that a new chapter will be opened at this stage and that two peaceful countries will be built. the eu can and should play an active role in this regard, in particular by helping to lift people out of poverty and promoting good neighbourliness.
in writing. − between 9 and 15 january 2011, a majority of the south sudanese people voted in favour of the creation of an independent state. as is well known, this is an area of the world continually ravaged by conflicts which threaten the possibility of large sections of the population enjoying decent living conditions. in the light of these new developments, parliament called on the new authorities in south sudan (its independence will be declared on 9 july 2011) to make efforts to establish the essential foundations for the establishment of a democratic state based on the dignity of the person. the eu is also committed to the development of a common foreign and security policy. for these reasons i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. - i welcome all the efforts being made to strengthen and deepen good relations between the eu and other economic powers. in the case of the russia-eu relationship, i welcome the achievements already made in terms of a common space not only of economic cooperation but also of shared values. i believe that the motion for a resolution on the eu-russia summit tabled by the ppe group is the most appropriate one in the present context.
in writing. - the cross-eyes of europe and russia have always been marked by mutual admiration and simultaneous fear. on the european side, there was a general sense of amazement at the size of russia's territory, population and military power and the fear arising from its expansionist action. for russia, european technical and scientific progress has been emulated since the time of peter the great, but at the same time it has been feared as potentially dissolving the soul and the way of being russian, and as a threat to its territorial integrity. these trends have not abated, but rather have been exacerbated by the cold war. the road russia has taken towards a liberal-based pluralist democracy has seen ups and downs, but it is undeniable that it has been the same since the days of the iron curtain. however, it is useless to deny that much remains to be done in this respect, and that the european union and the russian federation share not only a common historical, cultural and religious heritage but also interests and challenges which coincide and which justify a rapprochement at the most diverse levels. the european union must continue to work to make this convergence possible and fruitful.
in writing. − russia is a permanent member of the un security council, sharing with the eu the responsibility for maintaining stability in the world. the challenges related to the middle east, libya, iran, terrorism, energy security, climate change and the financial crisis will be best addressed through cooperative relations with russia. however, three years after the conflict with georgia, russia still does not respect the agreements of 12 august and 8 september 2008 on the withdrawal of its forces from the occupied georgian provinces of south ossetia and abkhazia, and does not ensure free and full access of the european union monitoring mission to its territories. i therefore call for the eu and russia to intensify negotiations on a new partnership and cooperation agreement based on the mutual interdependence of the eu and russia. this agreement should be legally binding and comprehensive, and should cover all areas related to democracy, the rule of law, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, and the protection of the rights of minorities.
in writing. - as usual, the interests of the major european economic and financial groups are at the forefront of this resolution. it is in this context that we should read the pressures (also usual, on several other countries) on russia to join the world trade organization, to promote a level playing field for business communities on both sides and to promote trade liberalisation in the global economy by facilitating foreign investment and abandoning any protectionist measures. it is the undoing of the old, repetitive, neoliberal, meddling european union. in this case, however, in addition to access to investment and markets, the issue of access to and control of energy sources and flows, as well as other raw materials, particularly rare earths, for which a serious shortage problem has been raised in the eu, is a central concern. this calls for close cooperation on the supply of rare earths and raw materials, especially those considered critical. the security aspects, including the installation of the missile defence shield, should also be emphasised. it is recalled that romania, a member of the eu and nato, has already expressed its willingness to host this system - a threat to russia's security and to peace in europe.
in writing. the european parliament's majority is once again demonstrating its traditional neoliberal and meddling positions on relations between the european union and russia. the interests of economic and financial groups are at the forefront of the agenda, pressing russia to join the wto, to promote a level playing field for business communities on both sides and to promote trade liberalisation in the global economy, with russia facilitating foreign investment and abandoning any protectionist measures. access to and control of energy are therefore fundamental and therefore require access to markets, infrastructure and investment. there is also some desperation when russia is asked to cooperate closely on the supply of raw materials and rare earths, especially those considered critical. and then finally, there is the hypocrisy. russia is called upon to engage in a deeper comprehensive dialogue on security issues, including the deployment of the missile defence shield, when an eu and nato member state, romania, has already expressed a willingness to host a system that is a clear threat to russia's security and to peace throughout europe. the united states itself has not guaranteed that it will not.
in writing. − this resolution on the eu-russia summit provides for more ambitious trade relations, a new partnership and cooperation agreement and visa liberalisation, but moscow must give guarantees of improving the human rights situation in the country by ending politically motivated court decisions, lack of press freedom and the occupation of georgian provinces. at this time, we call on the eu and russia to use this summit to intensify negotiations on a new partnership and cooperation agreement and to resolve the last remaining issues concerning russia's accession to the wto. another important aspect to be taken into account is the dialogue on further visa liberalisation, recalling the commitment to the long-term abolition of visas for travel between the eu and russia.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution and stressed that russia will always be a very important partner of the european union, and that it is therefore necessary to create strategic cooperation, sharing not only economic and commercial interests but also the objective of close collaboration in europe and at international level. i hope that this cooperation will be based on the principles of respect, trust and solidarity.
in writing. − europe is a set of states that share a common matrix and this is a point to be taken into account when looking at eu-russia relations, relations between europe's most important political union and the largest european state. in short, an indispensable partner for the union, not only economically but also politically. the union must therefore strengthen its ties with its most powerful neighbour by advocating trade facilitation between the two states (which in itself leads to political rapprochement) and by strengthening the affirmation of the values which are part of its genetic code.
