in writing. - misleading advertising and unfair commercial practices undermine consumer confidence and thereby damage the internal market. it is therefore essential that european legislation protects consumers and businesses from such practices. as regards the frequent and harmful misleading practices in business directories, i welcome the revision of the applicable legislation to put an end to misleading practices by business directory publishers, in particular by creating a blacklist of misleading practices by business directories.
in writing. the resolution also calls for the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the european union's citizens are not misled by the media. unfortunately, the directive 2006/114/ec on misleading and comparative advertising is not only failing to deliver its intended results, but the victims are mainly the elderly, small and medium-sized enterprises and even charitable organisations. these are companies which are very aggressive in their tactics, which are unscrupulous predators whose actions must be stopped. as these practices cross borders, it is very difficult to bring those responsible to justice. in addition, there is no 'blacklist' of these fraudulent companies, which would help in prevention, and these practices continue to be verified with the knowledge of the national authorities. european law must protect the citizens of europe. we cannot allow these companies to move with impunity from one member state to another, and even outside the eu, taking advantage of the principle of free movement of persons and goods throughout the schengen area. it is a very timely proposal and deserves my full support. the victims are waiting for practical results and i hope that the commission will take the necessary measures to put an end to this situation.
in writing. - as mentioned in the resolution, the european parliament received more than 400 petitions concerning widespread deceptive commercial practices used by directory publishers affecting thousands of companies, mostly small businesses. these are practices that generally have a significant financial impact. in general, the deceptive commercial practices in question consist in attracting companies, as well as professionals and non-profit organisations, for free registration in a business directory. but then the signatories discover they've signed a contract with expenses. furthermore, directory publishers are often based in a different member state from their victims, making it difficult for victims to seek protection and/or justice from national authorities. the committee on petitions therefore regrets that directive 2006/114/ec on misleading and comparative advertising, which applies to business-to-business transactions, appears to be either insufficient to provide effective remedies or is inadequately applied by the member states. the european parliament, in the resolution now adopted, calls on the european commission to analyse the problem and seek a solution, which has earned our support.
in writing. − the internal market is undermined by misleading advertising and unfair commercial practices. we must therefore legislate to protect consumers and businesses from this kind of practice.
in writing. − this european parliament resolution of 9 june 2011 on misleading practices in business directories warns the commission to accelerate its activities in revising and improving the directive and other relevant legislation on this subject in order to end as soon as possible misleading practices used by business directory publishers, in particular by specifically blacklisting misleading useful practices used by business directories.
in writing. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat fraud and corruption, and calls for the eu to take action to combat fraud and corruption. on the one hand, because consumer confidence is essential for the proper functioning of the economy; on the other hand, and above all, because it is a practice that must be prohibited by law. this is a point which, because of its importance, has already merited community legislative intervention. however, in view of the results that are now known, it is necessary to call on the commission to monitor the application of directive 2006/114/ec and to examine its limitations with a view to its improvement.

the serious economic and social situation in several member states of the european union should merit very special attention at the next council meeting in june, a thorough reflection on its causes, the taking on of responsibility for the increasingly neo-liberal community policies, such as privatisation and devaluation of labour, which are causing more social inequalities, greater economic divergences, more unemployment, poverty and social exclusion. unfortunately, indifferent to the struggles of the workers and peoples, they propose to give a permanent character to the neo-liberal policies which have already caused serious crises in greece and ireland and which threaten portugal and other member states. what they want, after all, is to facilitate the way for greater profits for capital, for greater financial speculation, always at the expense of the same people as always: workers, micro, small and mediumsized enterprises, farmers, the populations affected by these reductions in investment and by austerity policies.

we in the socialist group want to make the cap fairer, more equitable and more appropriate to the times we are living in, when the questions of the legitimacy of aid to society and food security in the broadest sense are more important than ever. we have succeeded in including in this report our main concerns, such as the need to maintain a community cap with adequate financial resources - and i stress this point - we will not accept that financial resources are withdrawn to ensure the implementation of the common agricultural policy, we want a fairer distribution of support between member states and between farmers, the introduction of a new system that is decoupled from production, based on environmental and social criteria, that is, by giving value to employment, targeting the cap to those who are genuinely farmers and creating a specific mechanism for small farmers. i am sure that with the strengthened role of parliament, with the treaty of lisbon, we will be able to translate these objectives, which are for the moment only theoretical, into concrete actions.
this report does not address the challenges of the future that its title suggests, but above all it does not address the serious problems of the present, which is why we have tabled a number of amendments which we consider essential for a fundamental change in the current cap. i would like to stress here the defence of the instruments for regulating markets and the intervention mechanisms which guarantee fair prices for production, farmers and the right of each country to produce. among other examples, we propose the maintenance of the milk production quota system as an essential condition for the protection of producers in the most sensitive countries; we are in favour of maintaining the planting rights for vines and of maintaining aid for alcohol-by-mouth and crisis distillation. we propose the creation of a public agricultural insurance funded by community funds, which guarantees a minimum income to farmers in the event of a natural disaster. we have put forward proposals for a socially and environmentally sustainable agriculture, a vision incompatible with the unbridled professions of faith in the market and in competitiveness, as this report does.
the long process of work required for this important report, including the many commitments made, has made it a document, quite broad and balanced, of the various interests to which the cap has to respond. this report is a good guide for legislative proposals, and i congratulate its rapporteur. however, there are some proposals which concern me and which i shall follow with particular care as they develop. i am referring to the redistribution of aid, which i believe should be done uncompromisingly, only within the first pillar and on the basis of purely objective criteria, so that the sense of redistribution is not subverted by means of corrective criteria which will only tend to maintain the current situation. we need a fairer cap, properly budgeted and tailored to the demands made of it. i am also referring to the need to put the battered milk sector on the political agenda of the cap by adopting amendments nos 16, 12 and 5.
in writing. agriculture provides security of supply of affordable, quality food, essential protection of the environment and balanced use of land, and creates jobs, growth and wealth. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament. we have made a successful push to change the subsidies so that 80% of the subsidies do not continue to benefit the 20% of the largest farmers, and we have thus helped the small farmers. we are opening the door to a cap which is fairer between the eu countries, between farmers and different production lines, which respects the specific conditions of our regions, which is environmentally friendly and which promotes employment in rural areas. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i would stress this point, which is very important for the azores, given the strategic role played by the sector and the importance which quotas have had so far for milk producers, as no alternative measures to the milk quota system have yet been put forward.
in writing. this is a continuation report on the common agricultural policy, albeit with some contradictions. we therefore take a critical view and propose alternatives which effectively meet the need for agricultural production that guarantees the sovereignty and food security of each country, the problems of family farming and rural development, always taking into account the social importance of the land and those who work it, the specific characteristics of each country and social justice in the distribution of support by member state, by crops and by farmers. the commission has already made a number of proposals, including a clear and unequivocal defence of the system of production quotas, which are adjusted to each member state according to its food needs and which ensure the protection of farmers in countries such as portugal. we want to guarantee every country the right to produce, and we oppose the liberalization of the milk sector and the right to plant vines. we also want to maintain aid for alcohol-by-mouth and crisis distillation beyond 2012 and we advocate the existence of 'market regulation instruments and intervention mechanisms to guarantee fair production prices', thus countering the deregulatory trend of the previous cap reforms.

the rapporteur. - this is another moment of extraordinary work that has been done in the european parliament. i should like to thank corien, sylvie, carl, elisa and vicky, who have been with me as rapporteurs on this whole package of economic governance. i would also like to make a special mention of the various shadow rapporteurs who have helped us in our work and, finally, i would like to congratulate the council on the extraordinary work it has done on this subject, with particular reference to mr andrás kármán, who has been very much involved in this process, and to his commissioner, mr olli rehn, who has also played a valuable part in the whole process. my first word is a word of confidence, for the positive. this package of economic governance must show that europe is capable, that europe is capable of overcoming difficulties, that europe is capable of preventing future problems. that is why i have great confidence in what will happen in the coming days with regard to this legislation on economic governance. it is possible, in the stability and growth pact, which i was rapporteur for in the corrective part, to add the idea of growth to the idea of stability and budgetary discipline. it is possible to innovate with the macroeconomic imbalance procedure. it is possible to go beyond the logic of a simple sanctions mechanism, and that is why the adoption of this economic governance package will lead to more europe and a better europe. this economic governance package has brought us, for example, in relation to the corrective part of the stability and growth pact, a more intelligent application of the same pact: attention to the debt criterion, the introduction of an average for debt reduction, which is done in three years, creating the possibility of flexibility in compliance with the rules; this legislative package is not a response to the serious economic and social problems in many countries, which affect workers and populations and which have their fundamental origin in community policies of an increasingly neoliberal character and of greater concentration of financial and political power. the outcome of the negotiations, extending the requirements of the stability pact and strengthening sanctions, demonstrates the political consensus between the three institutions on the course and main guidelines of the european union, and is part of an unprecedented attack on the rights of national parliaments, which are conditioned by the neoliberal guidelines of the european union on their countries' budgets, aiming at austerity policies for workers and peoples, privatisation and reductions in public investment in essential sectors and services. after the negative results already known in greece, ireland and portugal of the struggles of their workers, it was time to go further and not to continue insisting on benefiting only economic and financial groups, especially the european powers. what these legislative diplomas now propose is to perpetuate these measures of interference, of subjugation of peoples and countries, transforming them into genuine protectorates or colonies, and deepening a path that can only lead to economic and social disaster and the implosion of the european union itself. that's why we're against it.

in writing. − this fund was set up in 2006 to provide additional support to workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns to enable them to re-enter the labour market, and was extended in 2009 to include workers made unemployed as a result of the economic and financial crisis. this is the third application to be examined under the 2011 budget and concerns eur 9.593.931 from the european globalisation adjustment fund for the reintegration into the labour market of 2 834 workers of general motors belgium and four of its antwerp suppliers. the commission considers that the application fulfils the eligibility requirements for the fund and recommends that the budgetary authority approve its mobilisation. it will make sure that it is mobilised thoroughly and quickly so as not to keep the workers who should actually benefit from the fund waiting.
in writing. - this report deals with the proposal for a decision of the european parliament (ep) and of the council on the mobilisation of the egf and falls within point 28 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the ep, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline and sound financial management. the egf was set up in 2006 to support workers who have lost their jobs as a result of structural changes in world trade patterns brought about by globalisation. on 20 december 2010, general motors belgium, a company in the automotive sector, submitted an application to the egf following the compulsory redundancies of 2 834 workers (main company and four suppliers). the current economic and financial crisis gives this egf a key role in mitigating the social impacts of the bankruptcy of many companies, often triggered by the aggressive economic policies of emerging markets, and this is the third application to be examined under the eu budget for 2011. i am pleased to note that the commission has taken the initiative to present a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work.
in writing. - requests to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund in the event of mass redundancies outside europe are being dealt with. in this case, more than eur 9 million was mobilised for belgium to assist some 2800 workers made redundant in the automotive sector. this is the third mobilisation to be examined under the 2011 budget. therefore, after deducting from the available appropriations the amount currently requested, an amount of eur 489 628 679 remains available until the end of 2011 of the 500 million provided for. although we support this mobilization because it is essential to support these workers, we reiterate our reservations and critical position with regard to this fund because we consider that it would be more important if measures were taken to prevent unemployment in order to avoid it. to do this, the neoliberal policies in force in this eu must be changed, as exemplified by the insistence on deregulation and liberalisation of international trade.
in writing. - while maintaining our critical stance on the european globalisation adjustment fund, because we believe that it would be more important if measures were taken to prevent unemployment in order to avoid it, we voted in favour of mobilising the fund to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of company restructuring or the liberalisation of international trade. in this case, more than eur 9 million was mobilised for belgium to assist some 2800 workers made redundant in the automotive sector. this is the third mobilisation to be examined under the 2011 budget. therefore, after deducting from the available appropriations the amount currently requested, an amount of eur 489 628 679 remains available until the end of 2011 of the 500 million provided for. it is symptomatic that, in a period of worsening social and financial crisis, only a little over 10 million of the funds provided have been used, which in itself shows the need to at least review the rules governing the fund.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. on 14 april 2011, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in belgium to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. this is the third application to be examined under the 2011 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 9 593 931 from the egf for belgium, based on 2 834 redundancies (all potential beneficiaries of assistance) in the main company general motors belgium and four of its suppliers. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the financial assistance mechanism is fully operational.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 established the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to support workers who lose their jobs as a result of structural changes in the global economy. with an allocation of eur 500 million for 2011, the commission considers that eur 9 593 391 should be made available to belgium to cope with redundancies at general motors belgium and its four supplier and manufacturing companies in the antwerp region. i believe that the egf should finance active measures to reintegrate the workers into the labour market, enabling them to acquire new skills and adapt them to the new working conditions that the 2 834 workers will have to face. i also believe that the european institutions should speed up the mobilisation of the egf in favour of belgium, by ensuring that the member state integrates workers made redundant as a result of globalisation into working life. i would also like to stress that the egf should not replace the legal and financial responsibilities of general motors, as it is a complementary support granted by the european union to alleviate the social difficulties that workers will face.

in writing. − the european parliament's rules of procedure, as amended in may 2009, now provide for a new procedure for joint meetings of parliamentary committees where a matter is not clearly the responsibility of a single committee. despite the positive outcome of this new rule at regimental level, the committee on constitutional affairs was given the task of clarifying and densifying the provision in question so that it would have a more easily appreciable operational content, in particular in the context of the ordinary legislative procedure. it is clear that the delimitation of the committees' powers has areas of overlap and difficulty to distinguish, so i believe that this clarification is positive and that the new wording proposed will allow for a more coherent use of rule 51.
in writing. - the present proposal for a report concerns certain amendments to be made to rule 51 of the rules of procedure of the european parliament (ep), following the setting up of a working party to review the rules of procedure and following a decision by the conference of presidents. on 6 may 2009, parliament revised its rules of procedure and introduced a new procedure for joint committee meetings in rule 51 to streamline procedures for approving matters beyond the remit of a single committee, so that only one report reflecting the position of all committees involved is presented to the ep plenary. the conference of committee chairmen's examination of a draft guideline for article 51 cooperation led to a request for consideration by the conference chair to the committee on constitutional affairs. this proposal clarifies the issues involved and refers the matter to the plenary for approval in the light of the rules of procedure in force. i therefore agree with the rapporteur's recommendation that the joint committees should be regarded as a committee responsible in the regulation.
in writing. − the conference of presidents in the previous legislature set up a working group on parliamentary reform, which was charged with reviewing the functioning of parliament and suggesting improvements. in this context, a new form of cooperation between committees was developed, established by the new article 51. the new form of cooperation between committees has raised doubts about its application, which have been referred to the committee on constitutional affairs. the committee on constitutional affairs believes that this is not a matter of mere interpretation but an important procedural matter which should be decided by a vote in plenary by the majority applicable to the rules of procedure, namely the majority of members of parliament. i agree with the version presented which makes the standard clearer and easier to use, and i voted in favour of its amendment.

in writing. − this report concerns the request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of the romanian mep adrian severin, following a case initiated by the national directorate for combating corruption on 21 march 2011. the case arose from information that severin had received €100,000 from the consultancy firm taylors jones public affairs in exchange for its support of an amendment to directive 94/91/ec on the time limit for the repayment of depositors in the event of bank failure. the company also promised him a paid position on its international advisory board. it was later found to be a fictitious company set up by the british newspaper sunday times whose behaviour is reprehensible. however, despite severin's argument that it was all a dummy company that deceived him, that no money was exchanged and the legislation was changed, romanian legislation severely punishes this kind of behaviour. in this connection, and in view of the recommendation of the committee on legal affairs recommending the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of adrian severin, i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. - the european parliament was asked to lift the parliamentary immunity of mep adrian severin following a criminal case in which he is accused of defamation under the romanian criminal code. there is no indication that the proceedings could be, on the part of the romanian judicial authorities, a case of fumus persecutionis, i.e. of sufficiently serious and precise suspicion that the action was brought with the purpose of harming the member politically. the committee on legal affairs, after considering the reasons of fact and law for and against the waiver of the member's immunity, recommends that the european parliament should waive the parliamentary immunity of adrian severin, considering, however, that until a final judgment is rendered, members are immune from any form of detention, imprisonment or any other measure preventing them from exercising the functions inherent in their mandate. on the basis of these arguments, i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − this fisheries protocol guarantees the possibility for several member states' fleets to fish in the seychelles eez. it includes five portuguese surface longliners. the renewal of this protocol is intended to support the sustainability of the member states' long-distance fishing fleets, a fleet segment which has been particularly affected by the crisis in the fisheries sector in recent years, an objective and concern which we naturally share. however, there are still some doubts, which we cannot fail to point out, and which are common to other fisheries partnership agreements, as to the effectiveness of the stated objectives of cooperation for the sustainable development of the sector in the third country concerned and as to the sustainability and control of the fishing effort. these are questions that need to be clarified in the future. we note that fishing opportunities have been halved and the cost of licences has increased by eur 40 000 for tuna seiners, despite the fact that the number of tuna seiners covered by the agreement has increased.
in writing. - this fisheries protocol guarantees the possibility of fishing in the seychelles eez by several member states' fleets, including five portuguese surface longliners. we agree with the renewal of this fisheries protocol, which is important to ensure the survival of the member states' long-distance fishing fleets, a segment of the fleet that has been particularly affected by the crisis in the fisheries sector in recent years. however, given that the agreement is valid for three years and that the fishing opportunities have therefore been halved, we are somewhat concerned about the increase in the cost of licences - by eur 40 000 - for tuna seiners, even though there has been an increase in the number of tuna seiners covered by the agreement. we also shared the rapporteur's concern about the problem of piracy in the indian ocean, which is increasingly affecting tuna fishing. for this reason, the partnership agreement provides for the possibility of applying a pro rata temporis payment to compensate for losses suffered by shipowners who are forced to leave the indian ocean if they feel that their safety is seriously threatened.

in writing. the principality of andorra is historically linked to the european union and has links with it in a wide range of areas. the customs union concluded in 1990 has increased these already strong and natural links. the proposal is designed to amend the community customs code and its implementing rules, while respecting customs security measures for goods exported to or imported from non-member countries. the proposal establishes a special regime between the union and andorra which at the same time allows trade between the two to flow normally without compromising the necessary security of the goods traded. to that end, they need to ensure equivalent levels of security in their respective areas of jurisdiction. i hope that the trade relations between the union and andorra will bear fruit and that the proposal will make a significant contribution to this objective. a final word to the rapporteur on his work.

in writing. the agreement under discussion in this report covers certain aspects of civil aviation safety and will replace the six existing bilateral agreements between the member states and canada, which include product certification. as the rapporteur expressly states, the intention to create a fully open aviation space between these two countries - a subject on which we have raised known reservations - does not fall within the scope of this agreement and should be the subject of a separate recommendation. the main objectives of the agreement are to minimise duplication of assessment, testing and controls, while ensuring that there are no significant regulatory differences, and to allow the eu and canada to rely on each other's certification systems. to this end, the requirements and regulatory procedures of both parties will progressively approximate. this agreement should generate savings for european and canadian aviation companies through simplified, faster and thus less costly product certification procedures and the mutual acceptance of certification results.

in writing. - the document in question, which was written by mr miroslav mikolášik, follows on from the commission's communication entitled 'cohesion policy: strategic report 2010 on the implementation of the 2007-2013 programmes', which is the first rigorous assessment of the implementation of the approximately 450 operational programmes adopted by the european commission. the european union's (eu) cohesion policy is part of a framework of european solidarity that encompasses the 27 member states and their 271 regions and aims to end the economic and social disparities within the eu. in view of the economic and financial crisis in europe, this report is of particular importance as it should be an instrument for reallocating and maximising the cohesion funds. in fact, and in view of the low implementation rates, it is necessary to create mechanisms to enable member states with more difficulties to use the funds allocated to them, otherwise they will be obliged to return these funds to the eu, which will distribute them among richer countries. i welcome the adoption of this report, which has my support, not only for the corrective measures it points to but also for the architecture of the future cohesion policy it suggests.
in writing. − the report acknowledges the accumulation of problems in cohesion policy, starting with the late conclusion of the negotiations on the multiannual financial framework and the legislative package and resulting in a delay in the implementation of national strategies and operational programmes. these factors are combined with the insufficiency of the amounts planned for the period 2007 to 2013, in particular in view of the enlargement of the european union, and the use of only 27,1% of the resources available in the current period, as well as the maintenance of national co-financing and the bureaucratic burden. this situation exposes some of the errors and shortcomings of cohesion policy, which we have always denounced. countries like portugal are moving further and further away from the promised economic and social development to approach the community average. national co-financing remains a factor hindering access to the funds, particularly for countries with weaker economies, which continue to see many millions of euros returned to the countries most benefited from the main eu policies, notably emu and the internal market, increasing rather than narrowing disparities between countries.
in writing. − this report recognises a number of problems in cohesion policy, starting with the late conclusion of the negotiations on the multiannual financial framework and the legislative package, resulting in a delay in the implementation of national strategies and operational programmes, the insufficiency of the amounts planned for the period 2007-2013, in particular in view of the enlargement of the european union and the use of only 27,1% of the resources available in the current period, as well as the maintenance of national co-financing at this time of crisis and the bureaucratic burden. this makes clear the errors and shortcomings of cohesion policy which we have always denounced. countries like portugal are moving further and further away from the promised economic and social development and closer to the community average. all this is compounded by the eu's main policies, notably emu, competition in the internal market and the liberalisation of international trade, among others.
in writing. − cohesion policy is a key pillar of eu policies and one of the engines for creating a one-speed europe, as it contributes to improving the socio-economic environment. member states are making progress towards achieving the objectives of cohesion policy, as evidenced by the national reports, albeit with some inherent heterogeneity at state and regional level. the results of this policy are not immediate, it is a long-term mechanism. the full picture of the 2007-2013 programming period will only be visible in 2015, two years after the second strategic report, as some countries have two more years to use all the allocated funding. i voted in favour of this report, which points out, among other things, that in certain areas the selection and effective implementation of projects are hampered by constraints which must be tackled. i would stress the late conclusion of the negotiations on the multiannual financial framework and the legislative package for this policy, which result in the late implementation of national strategies and operational programmes and the scarcity of public resources available for co-financing in the member states. it is imperative to address these issues if the objectives of the process are to be fully achieved.
in writing. − article 174 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides that the eu will develop and pursue its action to strengthen its economic, social and territorial cohesion, and has set the eu funds for the period 2007-2013 at eur 347 billion, corresponding to 35.7% of the overall eu budget. i am voting in favour of this report because it provides a credible analysis of the current situation with community funds by showing where €93.4 billion has been spent so far, suggests recommendations and areas for improvement, contributes to the resolution of the economic and financial crisis and highlights good practice and mutual learning at regional level. i would stress that the implementation of community funds is uneven across the member states and it is important for the ec to understand the difficulties that some countries have had in order to take corrective action that actively contributes to a greater uptake of community funds in line with the europe 2020 strategy. finally, i would like to congratulate the member states on the efforts they have made in drawing up the first national strategic reports, actively contributing to greater transparency, flexibility, effectiveness and accountability of cohesion policy funds.
in writing. - i welcome this report, which analyses the needs of urban areas, focusing mainly on two aspects: basic infrastructure and smart investment in infrastructure and services based on technological progress. i also agree with the call for strategic planning principles and the need for more flexible co-financing between the erdf and the esf.
in writing. - it is important to define a european urban policy which should contribute to the sustainable development of urban areas, taking into account the principle of subsidiarity. the european urban agenda includes not only the urban dimension of eu policies, notably cohesion policy, but also the intergovernmental strand of efforts at european level to coordinate member states' urban policies, implemented through informal ministerial meetings. it is important to strengthen the urban dimension in cohesion policy and to promote sustainable urban development, in particular by strengthening and developing instruments to implement the leipzig charter at all levels. at the same time, the dynamism of urban areas must be stimulated through effective and efficient synergies between the different european funding instruments, particularly with regard to research and innovation. it will therefore be necessary to ensure that urban areas in all regions of the eu, as centres of economic activity, innovation and employment, can benefit from the necessary and appropriate support to be able to face the enormous challenges they face, such as the trend towards sub-urbanisation, the concentration of poverty and unemployment, increasing congestion and pollution, etc.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the european urban agenda and its future cohesion policy, because it stresses the importance of networking cities, sharing best practice and adopting innovative solutions, strengthening the urban dimension of the european territorial cooperation objective and more effectively applying the partnership principle in cohesion policy with a view to more sustainable development of cities, particularly with regard to the modernisation of urban infrastructure and transport networks.
in writing. − one of the most important dimensions of cohesion policy is that which is specifically geared to cities, since it is predominantly urban areas that implement cohesion policy and that it is in them that much of the challenges to be addressed by the eu2020 strategy are concentrated. the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of information centres for the protection of the environment. it is also in large urban areas that the main centres of innovation, knowledge and science are located, as well as most of the productive activities that generate wealth and contribute to economic growth. in addition, urban areas also face the greatest challenges in terms of efficient management of infrastructure and transport, which have a direct impact on environmental and energy policies.
in writing. − the european union (eu) cohesion policy is part of a solidarity framework that encompasses the 27 member states and their 271 regions and aims to end the economic and social disparities within the eu. this report, by oldřich vlasák, is intended to follow up the previous one entitled the urban dimension of cohesion policy in the new programming period. the role of cities - home to some 80% of europe's population - as sources of wealth creation and poles of social and economic development is unquestionable. however, the problems affecting them (poverty and social exclusion, unemployment, housing, crime, drug use, etc.) are enormous and require increased attention. despite the creation of financial instruments developed by the european commission and the european investment bank such as jeremie, jaspers and jessica, as well as other structural funds, the results have fallen short of expectations. i therefore agree with the rapporteur's recommendations to draw up a comprehensive and integrated financial plan so that the funds are used for projects aimed at achieving the objectives set out in the eu 2020 strategy and not for actions that are limited to consuming those funds.
in writing. - the great contradiction of this report is that it places a high value on cities but forgets citizens. much emphasis is placed on strengthening the eu urban agenda, developing basic physical infrastructure and its contribution to the economic fabric, energy and environmental sustainability through investments based on technological progress, but people are secondary. cities and all their infrastructure are built by people. it is the people who live in them and make their public services in education, health and transport, commerce and industry and their cultural activities work. they should be at the heart of any urban policy. but they are largely the ones who are forgotten by eu policies. in our view, an urban agenda should give priority to a better distribution of the population in the territory of some countries, notably portugal, by alleviating the burden on cities by promoting the rural world and properly remunerated agricultural activity, distributing productive activity across their territory, promoting quality public services in rural areas and cities, combating unemployment and defending employment with rights, promoting wages and pensions and combating poverty.

in writing. − since 2009, the date of the first report entitled the urban dimension of cohesion policy in the new programming period, there have been new contributions and developments to this issue. this report aims to build on the previous one by highlighting several aspects of the urban dimension of cohesion policy which the committee on regional development identifies as crucial or problematic for the future cohesion policy, which should become a fully valid and effective policy for eu cities. i voted in favour because of the crucial importance of this subject for the development of small and mediumsized towns. i agree with the rapporteur's warning that the project-to-fund approach should be replaced by the funds-to-project approach. projects should not be designed to absorb the funds available, but to achieve the strategic objectives. experience shows that in many cases project ideas arise on the basis of the availability of funds rather than on the basis of real needs and strategic priorities. combating this must be one of the main challenges of development policies and also of cohesion policy.
in writing. - i consider the european urban agenda to be a policy of unquestionable importance, given that 70% of europe's population lives in cities and that they generate around 80% of the eu's gdp. the 2007-13 period sees €21.1 billion for urban development to be applied to the rehabilitation of industrial sites and polluted land, urban and rural regeneration, clean urban transport and housing. the european urban agenda is about developing the infrastructure and services of cities. cities today face varied and asymmetrical problems, forcing the implementation of differentiated integrated local development models. in this way, and as urban policy is integrated into the objectives of cohesion policy, it should serve as a link with rural areas to enhance inclusive development. cities must have a voice in solving their problems through multi-level governance and the use of the partnership principle. finally, i would stress that the development of integrated strategic planning must be complemented by flexible financial engineering so that national, regional and local authorities are free to implement their priorities.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the objective 3 report: future agenda for crossborder, transnational and interregional cooperation, as this is essential for the effectiveness of cohesion policy. to stress the importance of the creation of european territorial cooperation groups as a privileged instrument of territorial governance, which responds to the needs of structured cooperation in terms of finances, legal status and governance at various levels.
in writing. - 37.5% of the european population live in border areas, making territorial cooperation, with its three dimensions - cross-border, transnational and interregional - a key policy for the union, helping territories, regions and states to work better together in pursuit of their common objectives.
in writing. - this report, by marie-thérèse sanchez-schmid, deals with objective 3: a challenge for territorial cooperation the future agenda for crossborder and interregional cooperation. objective 3 - european territorial cooperation - can be seen as the poor relation of the structural funds. despite the population of the crossborder areas amounting to almost 200 million inhabitants, this objective is covered by only 2.52% of the cohesion funds. given that eu cohesion policy is part of a solidarity framework that encompasses the 27 member states and their 271 regions and aims to end the economic and social disparities within them, it is essential that the next multiannual financial framework (mff) includes an increase in the funds allocated to this objective, as these are regions with serious problems from the point of view of competitiveness but essential for the sustainability of the territory. i therefore agree with the rapporteur's proposal to strengthen the territorial cooperation objective by increasing the overall budget from 2.5% to 7% and to adopt measures to simplify the implementation of programmes and the creation of european territorial cooperation groups (etcs) which are essential for the functioning of crossborder governance systems.
in writing. − territorial cooperation has become one of the three pillars of the european union's cohesion policy, succeeding the interreg community initiative. subsequently, article 174 of the treaty made territorial cohesion one of the three strands of cohesion policy, alongside the economic and social strands. this is one of the european union's main priorities. the aim of this policy is to remove physical, administrative and regulatory barriers and to reduce the border effect between territories and regions so that they can face together common challenges, whether they are territorial (services, infrastructure, urban planning and spatial planning) or global (globalisation, climate change), or economic or societal. the report's main programmatic lines, namely the reinforcement of the objective of territorial cooperation through strategic territorial cooperation at all stages of planning and coordinated with strategy 2020, the adoption of a territorial approach for the remaining community policies, the encouragement of the creation of european groupings of territorial cooperation (egtcs), the simplification of the implementation of this policy and the focus on its transnational visibility, justify my vote in favour.
in writing. − since 1986, the objective of cohesion policy has been to strengthen economic and social cohesion between the various eu member states. however, the lisbon treaty and the new eu strategy entitled europe 2020 have defined a third dimension called territorial cohesion which promotes a functional approach to the integrated development of the 271 regions, considered as living spaces for citizens. i believe that territorial cohesion should help to remove the physical, administrative and regulatory barriers between european regions, promote harmonious european development and increased cooperation through joint projects between different regions but with similar development characteristics and objectives. i also stress that territorial strategies must be directly linked to the guidelines for the trans-european transport networks, the strategies for the integrated maritime policy and the europe 2020 strategy in order to build a smart, sustainable and inclusive european space. finally, i fully support the idea that an action plan for the outermost regions (orr) should be drawn up and that multisectoral principles should be established to promote the harmonious development of the ors and to help reduce the territorial disparities with other european regions.
in writing. − i strongly believe that an efficient strategic framework can ensure a common approach and capitalise on the synergies between all the funds supporting the objectives of cohesion policy as defined by the treaties, and thus better serve eu citizens and meet their expectations. this report is aimed at creating such synergies and i therefore approve it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on enhanced effectiveness between the erdf and other structural funds because i believe that the development of an effective strategic framework can ensure a common approach and capitalise on synergies between the various existing funds, with a view to achieving the objectives of cohesion policy as defined by the treaties and thus meeting the expectations of citizens.
in writing. - parliament has been insisting on the need to strengthen the effectiveness of the combined application of the erdf and the other structural funds and an integrated approach to sectoral policies. the need not to waste resources, which is becoming more and more felt in the time of serious crisis we are experiencing, recommends that we try to make the best use of the synergies resulting from the means made available by the structural funds and avoid wasting opportunities due to their excessive tightness. this effort to use the means at our disposal will aim to contribute to improving opportunities for sustainable growth and reducing disparities between regions and facilitating social inclusion and cohesion between regions. this effort will not succeed without a clear prioritization by the union and the member states to avoid the dispersion of funds and to strengthen what is really essential to pursue. the flexibility sought must be accompanied by strict monitoring of the implementation of the funds so that it is carried out with the utmost respect for the rules of rigour and transparency.
in writing. - this report, by georgios stavrakakis, looks at the current situation and the need to bring together future synergies in order to increase the effectiveness of the european regional development fund (erdf) and the other structural funds. for two decades, the structural funds have been invested in the most varied regions of europe and have made a decisive contribution to improving the quality of life for millions of europeans. it seemed to be an inexhaustible source from which the less favoured regions could satisfy their financing needs. the recent economic and financial crisis has brought us to our senses and shown us the consequences of a consumerism that is unrestrained and based on unsustainable investments. in fact, improving infrastructure does not always mean major development. a rigorous evaluation of all ongoing projects and a strategic reorientation of the funds still available in view of the achievement of the objectives set by the eu 2020 strategy in the context of the preparation of the next mff is therefore urgently needed. i support the recommendations in this report to build synergies by creating a strategic instrument covering all the structural funds and targeting innovation and technological development, supporting businesses, especially smes, and reducing administrative costs.
in writing. − the objective of this report is clear: to create a single strategic framework for the erdf and other structural funds, notably the eafrd and the eff, as from the next financial period after 2013, and to coordinate them with other instruments of the eu's external policies. the creation of a single strategic framework could result in the loss of specificities and the diversity of areas and sectors benefiting from it, paving the way for the restriction of the community budget and the reduction of the funds, as the major powers of the eu have advocated. this new framework aims to foster competition and strengthen the integration of eu policies to deliver the europe 2020 strategy, favouring large economic and financial groups and the concentration and centralisation of capital. for our part, we continue to advocate the development and complementarity of these funds to defend and promote production in each country, to combat unemployment and promote employment with rights, to create and distribute better the wealth created, to defend quality public services, to combat poverty, to defend small-scale coastal fishing, family farming and small and mediumsized farmers.
in writing. − this report advocates the creation of a single strategic framework for the erdf and other structural funds, notably the eafrd and the eff, as early as the next financial period after 2013, as well as their coordination with other instruments of the external dimension of eu policies. it should be borne in mind that the creation of a single strategic framework could lead to the loss of specificities and the diversity of areas and sectors benefiting from it, paving the way for the restriction of the community budget and the reduction of the funds, as has been advocated by the major powers of the eu. this new framework aims to foster competition and strengthen the integration of eu policies to achieve the europe 2020 strategy, favouring the same old things: the large economic and financial groups and the concentration and centralisation of capital. for our part, we continue to advocate the development and complementarity of these funds to defend and promote production in each country, exploiting their potential to combat unemployment and promote employment with rights, create and distribute better the wealth created, defend quality public services, combat poverty, defend small-scale coastal fishing, family farming and small and medium-sized farmers.
in writing. - the current economic situation should be seen as an opportunity to reformulate what can be done more efficiently, with increased legitimacy, and to fight tenaciously against any waste of time and resources. the need to consolidate public budgets forces us to be more innovative and to seek a greater impact of the available funding. this report, which i voted for, reflects on the present situation and the need for future synergies to improve effectiveness between funds. the coordination of these funds must be improved. the eu's cohesion policy instruments are managed under a common framework ranging from strategic guidelines to payments and reporting. however, coordination between cohesion policy instruments and others should be increased. i agree with the creation of an integrated planning and implementation system covering all policy areas. the virtue of integrated planning lies in the understanding that complex problems must be tackled simultaneously in a variety of ways. unemployment cannot be solved by training the unemployed alone, but also by policies to create jobs, to support smes or start-ups.
in writing. − the question of greater effectiveness and synergies between the various structural funds is of great importance in the context of the debate on future cohesion policy. the future cohesion policy must be simplified and more integrated. the future approach should therefore be based on a common strategic framework for the various structural funds in order to ensure a common perspective and optimise the synergies that can be created between the various funds. only with an integrated approach, focused on results and in line with the objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, will it be possible to speak of enhanced effectiveness between the various structural funds. as shadow rapporteur for the epp group, i believe that we must involve regional and local authorities in the development and implementation of partnerships and concentrate thematically on priorities and the financial resources to be allocated in the future. the regional dimension must be present and contribute to highlighting the european added value of cohesion policy. as regards financial instruments, the possibility of using financial engineering instruments should be strengthened, and provision should be made for member states and regions to use multi-fund programmes.
in writing. − on 29 september 2010, the commission presented a legislative package aimed at strengthening economic governance in the european union and the euro area. this reinforcement must be linked to the reinforcement of the democratic legitimacy of the decisions taken, i.e. with the closer and timely involvement of the interested parties, as well as of the national parliaments and the european parliament. this report, which i supported, argues that the corrective action plan should set out a set of specific policy measures that the member state concerned has implemented or intends to implement and should include the timetable for them. equally important is the possibility, as part of the corrective measures, for the european commission to be able to carry out enhanced surveillance missions in the member state concerned to monitor the implementation of the plan. finally, i would stress the power of the european parliament, either on its own initiative or at the request of a member state, to invite the president of the council, the commission and, where appropriate, the president of the eurogroup to appear before the competent parliamentary committee to discuss the decision declaring non-compliance.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report as i agree that when carrying out its economic reading of the scoreboard under the alert mechanism, the commission should pay particular attention to developments in the real economy, including economic growth, employment and unemployment performance, nominal and real convergence within and outside the euro area, productivity developments and their relevant drivers such as r&d and external/internal investment, as well as developments at sectoral level, including energy, which affect the performance of gdp and the current account.
in writing. − the current economic, financial and social crisis has shown that the economic governance model in force in the union has not worked: the supervisory framework has proved to be very weak and the rules of the stability and growth pact have not been respected. i therefore agree with the package of measures presented by the european commission on economic governance. i support the report by mrs elisa ferreira on the prevention and correction of macroeconomic imbalances. i congratulate the commission on the forecast scoreboard which has already produced good results in the areas of the internal market and the area of freedom, security and justice. i hope that the european parliament will be able to contribute in a qualified way to the definition of the indicators of the scoreboard by the commission. the number of indicators is expected to be quite high, but they should focus mainly on factors relevant to macroeconomic imbalances. i agree that it is possible to call for structural reforms in surplus countries, but more attention should be paid to deficit countries.
in writing. - it is very important to stress the importance of this regulation, which, being entirely new in the community legal framework, is absolutely innovative in its content and in what it is intended to do: identify and correct macroeconomic imbalances in the union. following the lessons of the recent crisis, this report is distinguished by its desire to ensure that, in the interests of a strong and balanced economic union, the monitoring and coordination of economic policies adopted in the various member states takes precedence. this report aims to create an alert mechanism for possible future imbalances that may occur in a given member state, allowing for their immediate and effective correction. finally, i would like to congratulate my compatriot elisa ferreira on her hard work and dedication, which was not always easy but clearly worthwhile.
in writing. − i believe that the commission should have a stronger and more independent role in the enhanced surveillance process with regard to member state specific assessments, monitoring, missions, and recommendations. i am in favour of the community method and therefore agree that the role of the council should be limited to the steps leading to the application of possible sanctions. the most important thing, however, is that we move towards economic governance with a strong preventive and corrective component so that these sanctions are avoided. the prevention and correction framework and the overall economic governance framework should promote growth and employment by strengthening the union's competitiveness and social stability. i therefore agree that the surveillance of member states' economic policies should be extended beyond budgetary surveillance to prevent excessive macroeconomic imbalances and vulnerabilities in the union. it is also important to analyse internal imbalances including private and public debt, its evolution and origin (internal or international) and the country's overdue payments, in particular from the public sector and large multinationals to small and medium-sized enterprises.
in writing. the report is part of a package of six legislative documents on so-called economic governance. the rapporteur and her group intend to distinguish it from the other five, but the truth is that it is a very revealing example of the contradictions that exist in this european union. in fact, it is not enough to identify macroeconomic imbalances in the member states if there are no community policies alternative to the present ones, based on solidarity and economic and social cohesion, to address these imbalances. the pious, well-intentioned statements on the defence of employment and labour and social rights are in profound contradiction to the defence of the maintenance of the stability pact (which they have already called stupid), including the strengthening of sanctions against the countries with the most vulnerable economies, victims of neoliberal policies, and the pact for the euro plus. the rapporteur and her group also insist on recognizing that the policies they have advocated and supported are the fundamental cause of the crisis, that the creation of the single currency, in the image of the deutsche mark, was based on wrong assumptions, which only served the interests of economic and financial groups in the stronger economies. if this continues, we will inevitably see a further deterioration of the economic, social and political situation.
in writing. - this report is part of the six-volume package on economic governance and reveals the contradictions in the european union. the truth is that it is not enough to identify macroeconomic imbalances in the member states if there are no alternative community policies of solidarity and economic and social cohesion to address such imbalances. it is not enough, therefore, to make declarations of good intentions on the defence of employment and labour and social rights if, instead of ending the stability pact and the euro pact and replacing them with a genuine pact for social progress and development, they prefer to broaden their demands and to strengthen sanctions against countries and peoples who are victims of neoliberal policies. until european leaders recognize that their policies are the root cause of the crises that persist, we shall be witnessing a deterioration of the economic, social and political situation, which will inevitably lead to further social tensions and new conflicts with unforeseeable consequences. what will happen if they do not recognize that the creation of the single currency, in the image of the deutsche mark, was based on wrong assumptions that only served the interests of strong economic and financial groups. and that this is the fundamental cause of the worsening of the crises... in writing. − on 29 september 2010, the commission presented a legislative package aimed at strengthening economic governance in the eu and the euro area. the package comprises six proposals: four deal with budgetary issues, including a reform of the stability and growth pact (sgp), while two new regulations aim to detect and address emerging macroeconomic imbalances in the eu and the euro area. this draft opinion concerns the proposal for a council regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1466/97 on the strengthening of the surveillance of budgetary positions and the surveillance and coordination of economic policies. it is agreed that the sgp, both in its preventive and corrective aspects, has failed and needs to be reformed. i agree with the amendments to the commission's original proposal which have won a large majority of support in the european parliament. i believe that it is important to take account of the experience gained during the years of the previous eec and, on the other hand, to take account of the increased democratization of economic governance by strengthening the role of the european parliament in the whole supervisory process. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - this is the only report which seeks to counter the dominant trend in the whole economic coordination package. my abstention underlines and enhances this aspect. the report by mrs ferreira deals with the prevention of major macroeconomic imbalances. in it, deficit and debt are no more important than trade surpluses and deficits, employment and unemployment, or the qualitative challenges that can ensure a sustainable growth strategy. this kind of comprehensive coordination, based on a panel of varied indicators, which identifies imbalances at an early stage, is sensible. what prevents me from voting in favour of this text is the fact that it is the poor relative of a coordination which continues to have its alpha and omega in deficit and debt.
in writing. − the stability of the euro area in particular and of europe as a whole requires the restructuring of prevention and surveillance instruments to correct macroeconomic imbalances. financial consolidation is key to correcting the mistakes of the past and allowing european economies to grow sustainably, not by relying on public and external debt, but by promoting employment and competitiveness. this report focuses on the panel of macroeconomic and structural statistical indicators, which allow comparisons between member states, reflecting structural and short-, medium- and long-term trends. the inclusion of new indicators and the establishment of lower and upper thresholds for them, which will be symmetrical where necessary, will allow them to act as alert levels to avoid the current financial rescues carried out by the commission and the imf. this new symmetrical smart system will trigger stricter supervision, in-depth assessment by the commission, the ep, the council and the ecb, and the development of recommendations on further reforms and corrective plans. at a crucial time for the european project, i consider it essential that all the european and national authorities be involved so that the necessary measures can be taken in advance.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis has exposed and increased the need for coordination and improved surveillance of economic policies in economic and monetary union (emu). these recent experiences have also revealed gaps and shortcomings in the current coordination system and in the existing supervisory procedures. the crisis has dramatically reversed the favourable conditions in which the economic and financial sector operated until 2007, with most member states having to undergo a process of consolidating their accounts in order to reduce public debt. for most countries, debt reduction is a key issue, given the negative effects it has on economic incentives and growth due to higher taxes and risk premia. this report advocates that the commission and the council should make a comprehensive and balanced assessment of all relevant factors, in particular their impact as aggravating or mitigating circumstances on the assessment of compliance with the deficit and/or debt criterion. the council will require the member state to meet its annual budgetary targets which will allow for a minimum annual improvement of 0.5% of gdp. i therefore support this report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because i agree that when the ratio of government debt to gross domestic product (gdp) exceeds the reference value, it is considered to be significantly declining and approaching the reference value in a satisfactory manner within the meaning of article 126 (2) (b) of the treaty if, in the preceding three years, the differential with respect to the reference value has been reduced by an average of one twentieth in the last three years as a reference value, on the basis of changes over the last three years for which data are available.
in writing. − the current economic, financial and social crisis has shown that the economic governance model in force in the union has not worked: the supervisory framework has proved to be very weak and the rules of the stability and growth pact have not been respected. i therefore agree with the package of measures presented by the european commission on economic governance. i support the excellent report by mr digo feio on the acceleration and clarification of the application of the excessive deficit procedure. i welcome the call for more speed in the process for the european commission to make its recommendations public. i agree with the proposal that the european parliament should have the right to invite the representatives of the member states and i regret that the council has not accepted it. i support the possibility that the commission may be allowed to carry out additional surveillance missions and that the ecb may be associated with such visits.
in writing. − the rules on budgetary discipline, compliance and enforcement should be strengthened, in particular by giving a much more relevant role to debt levels and developments and to sustainability in general. i therefore agree with an assessment of the sustainability of public finances, including the level of indebtedness, the debt profile (including duration) and its dynamics. in this context, private debt cannot be overlooked, as it can represent an implicit contingent liability for governments. the public and private debt control framework should support long-term growth, taking due account of the counter-cyclical role of fiscal policy and contributing to the improvement of investment prerequisites and the deepening of the internal market which is essential to ensure the proper functioning and strengthening of economic and monetary union. it is also important to set up a european monetary fund, managed in accordance with the union's rules and financed in particular by revenue from fines, in order to safeguard the financial stability of the whole euro area.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on implementing measures to correct excessive macroeconomic imbalances in the euro area, which is part of the legislative package to strengthen economic governance in the eu and the euro area. the commission's proposals on improving economic governance are of the utmost importance for the future of the eu and for economic growth, in particular in the euro area. the crucial importance of these measures has led the european parliament's rapporteurs to decide to examine the commission's proposals thoroughly as a package and to improve them in order to establish a solid and coherent framework for the coming decades. the rapporteurs took the commission's proposals as the starting point for their work. this is the first time that parliament has taken part in the council's decision-making process on the union's macroeconomic developments. the new powers conferred by the lisbon treaty bring with them new responsibilities and the council cannot take a final decision without the agreement of the european parliament on the whole package. this procedure is intended to ensure consistency and timely adoption of all the elements of the package. this has also been achieved by this report.
in writing. the report sets out a set of coercive measures to correct dangerous macroeconomic imbalances in the euro area. the range of instruments ranges from deposit-paying to the application of fines and, from this point of view, it fits perfectly into the punitive philosophy of the whole package, which i do not agree with. the inclusion of macroeconomic imbalances in the world of economic coordination is in itself a positive thing, but it does not remove the necessary consequences. for example, during the process of applying sanctions, there is no symmetry and interdependence between countries with trade surpluses and countries with excessive deficits. the penalties are all for those who are already in difficulties, even when they are the result of an overvalued euro against the dollar.

in writing. − this directive aims to simplify and complete the existing regulatory framework by merging into a single legislative instrument the four existing directives, which provide only for minimum harmonisation clauses and leave it to the discretion of the member states to adopt stricter rules, which has contributed to the existence of a huge fragmentation at community level and to high compliance costs for companies in cross-border transactions. a genuine internal market between businesses and consumers is needed, which can help to strike a fair balance between a high level of consumer protection and the competitiveness of businesses, but also ensure respect for the principle of subsidiarity. this will enable consumers to have access to competitive cross-border offers, benefiting from greater choice, better prices and clear advantages of the internal market, and also allowing them to have the greatest confidence in a high level of protection of their rights. at the same time, it will enable businesses to supply their goods and services without being subject to unnecessary legal obstacles. i agree that the ideal solution would be a total harmonisation approach as initially proposed by the commission and requested by various business circles, but unfortunately such an approach is not yet feasible at this stage... in writing. − consumer rights and their protection under community law are one of the main pillars of the functioning of the internal market. i believe that adequate consumer protection and safety is fundamental to the proper functioning of markets and trade, which is essential for competitiveness and growth. in this connection, it is essential to strike the necessary balance between a high level of consumer protection, particularly in terms of the information provided to consumers and the level of liability for damage caused to them, and the costs this will impose on businesses. as i said in the march vote, it is important to take account of the various national particularities and the protection offered, with due respect for the principle of subsidiarity. i therefore believe that this is an area where, on the one hand, maximum harmonization may be useful, but on the other hand, minimum harmonization may also be adopted depending on the type of contract, because it is more appropriate.
in writing. - this report is concerned with a proposal for a european parliament and council directive on consumer rights. the european union has always been concerned about the free movement of people and goods. however, this freedom sometimes raises questions which need to be clarified and, above all, prevented or avoided. in a globalised world where more and more purchases are made online, it is essential to adapt regulations to the new requirements of the markets in order to ensure the protection of the rights of consumers who are often not even aware of them. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report, which represents a major step forward in consumer protection, and i welcome the council's decision to restrict this directive to door-to-door and internet sales - a market which is growing rapidly but in which consumers still feel somewhat lost - and i commend the simplification measures adopted, in particular the possibility for consumers (not companies) to terminate a contract by telephone. in fact, the common market needs more precise and transparent rules, such as the clause on the obligation to provide information on internet transaction mechanisms.
in writing. - this is a new proposal for an agreement on the european consumer rights directive, which is the culmination of tough negotiations between the european parliament, the council and the commission. we are faced with a compromise on the rules designed to better protect consumers and to ensure clear common conditions for companies competing in the single market. the new proposal takes into account new rights, such as the existence of an eu-wide cooling-off period of 14 days from receipt of the products. in the event of return of goods, the price paid by the consumer must be refunded within 14 days of the withdrawal. if the seller does not inform the consumer of his right to return the goods, the buyer has one year to return them. in this new version, delivery must be made within 30 days. if this does not happen within this period, the buyer has the right to cancel the order and the seller is responsible for any loss or damage that occurs during transport and cannot charge any amount that is not included in the initial order. all costs added to the value of the order shall be borne by the seller. it is a globally positive proposal, which we support.
in writing. − this new proposal for an agreement on the european consumer rights directive is the culmination of tough negotiations between the european parliament, the council and the commission. it is a commitment to standards designed to better protect consumers and to ensure clear common conditions for companies competing in the single market. the following is to be noted concerning the new duties: - an eu-wide cooling-off period of 14 days from receipt of the products, during which the consumer making distance purchases may change his mind. in the event of return of goods, the price paid by the consumer must be refunded within 14 days of the withdrawal. if the seller fails to inform the consumer of his right to return the goods, the buyer has one year to return them; the delivery must be made within 30 days. if this does not happen within that period, the buyer is entitled to cancel the order; the seller is liable for any loss or damage occurring during transport and may not charge any amount that is not included in the original order. all costs added to the value of the order shall be borne by the seller.
