the rapporteur. - there are three basic issues i would like to stress at the beginning of this debate. first, the effectiveness of the legislation. once again, on such sensitive matters as those relating to schengen, the european parliament has been able to reach agreement at first reading. we worked well and fast. for those who do not believe in codecision, we have once again given a definitive answer. if the council were to take a unanimous decision, it would be delayed for a longer period. i thank the hungarian presidency for its efforts and its competent commitment. secondly, the strengthening of schengen. even with differing opinions on some matters, we have achieved a broad consensus in this parliament. because we are, in essence, in favour of strengthening schengen and we do not agree with attempts to weaken the free movement of persons. i thank the shadow rapporteurs for their cooperation and support. and thirdly, the community solution. although it initially had little support in the council, the creation of this agency corresponds to the preference expressed by this parliament, which has always fought for a european solution to the detriment of the intergovernmental one that still prevails in sis i. according to the commission's impact assessment, the creation of an agency is undoubtedly the best solution from a financial, operational and institutional point of view. i would ask commissioner barnier to convey to commissioner malmström our thanks for her timely initiative and cooperation. the regulation we are about to adopt responds positively to the concerns of this parliament. let me make seven points. firstly, new systems clash with the legislative instrument, and there is much talk of new systems in the area of freedom, security and justice. it was clearly safeguarded in the regulation that new systems could only be joined after they had been created by means of a specific legal instrument adopted in co-decision with the european parliament. secondly, no to interoperability between systems. it is expressly safeguarded that there may be no interoperability between the systems managed by the agency unless such possibility is expressly provided for in the legal instruments establishing each of those systems. thirdly, the location of the agency. the prerogatives of the european parliament were respected and the decision was taken in a codecision procedure between parliament and the council. headquarters in tallinn, technical site in strasbourg, the backup site in austria. the pressure from parliament has led to two letters from the french and estonian ministers confirming the investments that each of these countries will make in order to find the most cost-effective solution. fourthly, the communication infrastructure. we were able to reach a compromise: any possibility of unauthorized access is prohibited; it is mandatory that all data that circulates on the network is encrypted and it is guaranteed that the encryption key cannot be passed on to the responsibility of a private company outsourced, exactly the opposite of what happens today. we also regulated the members of the management board and voting rights, to ensure that member states only participate in the system to which they are bound. the united kingdom's participation was safeguarded and ireland decided not to be bound by this regulation. finally, madam president, various improvements have been made in terms of strengthening the role of the european parliament, increasing transparency and improving data protection.
the rapporteur. - madam president, i too would like to welcome commissioner malmström. before it came, i had the opportunity to remind you that if it proves once again that codecision is a powerful instrument, because if we were still with the old system and this decision did not have codecision but was adopted unanimously in the council, we would probably not have a decision because we would still be tied in the council waiting for a unanimity that we would never be able to get. i would like to say that i share the views expressed by mr marinescu. in fact, i would also have liked a board of directors with fewer members, but in these matters which have to do with schengen and are based on mutual trust, it is very important that all the member states participate and for that reason alone we have accepted a very large board of directors. but it really does not make sense that in all european agencies we have such large boards. monika benová and mikolášik raised the question of the participation of the member states. and the truth is that the united kingdom has decided to participate in this regulation, ireland has decided to stay out, but what has been guaranteed is that, firstly, the presidency of this agency can only be held by a member state which participates in all the systems which are managed by the agency, that is, member states which have a partial participation cannot be elected as president, and secondly, and i end with this, madam president, that only those member states which participate in each of the subjects have access to the information. and so i think that concerns are safeguarded. in conclusion, madam president, i would like to thank all the colleagues who have spoken to me in a very kind manner. i believe that we have all risen to the challenge and that parliament and the council, with the help of the commission, have once again demonstrated that we have been able, in record time, to reach a very successful first reading.
member of the commission. − madam president, let me try to answer all these questions, which are indeed very detailed. but this is a good moment to take stock of where we are. the negotiations with the us, australia and canada have now reached an advanced stage. the negotiations with australia have been concluded and the commission has recommended that the council sign and conclude the agreement and put it to parliament. the procedure for signing is pending in the council due to parliamentary scrutiny in some member states. the negotiations with the us are well advanced but still ongoing. the draft text has been made available to the council and to some members of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs. the negotiations with canada are also ongoing. there have been delays due to the parliamentary elections in canada. we hope to be able to present you with a draft text very soon but i cannot undertake to do so before the summer break. so important decisions will shortly be made on these three agreements. ms in ’t veld and certain others mentioned agreements concerning numerous countries, but the aim is to make a single joint multilateral agreement out of these three bilateral agreements. but that is for later, there are no negotiations whatsoever ongoing with any other country. let me start with a few remarks on necessity and proportionality and on profiling. the question of necessity and proportionality is something you face in many issues, including eu pnr. it is a very important question. this issue was analysed in depth in both our communication on pnr from last year and the impact assessment that accompanied the proposal for an eu pnr. the analysis essentially revealed three things: firstly, pnr is used by a growing number of countries globally to prevent and to bring to justice those guilty of serious crimes and terrorism. serious crimes and terrorism continue to cause very serious harm to victims, as well as to the economy and citizens’ sense of security. secondly, pnr can make a unique contribution because it helps identify people who are not known to be involved in criminal activities but whose travel patterns fit with those of drug smugglers or human traffickers. in other words, while simple passport data may not be enough to catch criminals already on the wanted list, pnr data makes it possible to identify a wider range of persons who are likely to pose a security risk. thirdly, there is evidence that pnr data has already been successful in preventing and fighting serious crimes and terrorism, both in member states and in third countries. data has been particularly important in identifying and dismantling criminal networks involving crimes such as drug-smuggling and human trafficking. my services have already met with you once to present evidence on the necessity of pnr and there will be a follow-up meeting tomorrow. the commission is therefore convinced that pnr is an important tool in fighting serious crime and terrorism, when it is complemented by strong data-protection guarantees and when the necessity and proportionality principles are respected. the issue of profiling was also raised. that has been discussed already and there is no exact definition of it in eu law. profiling is generally understood to be an automatic data processing technique where a profile is applied to an individual in order to take a decision that affects him or her. there are, therefore, three different uses of pnr: firstly, reactive use in specific investigations after the flight. secondly, real-time use prior to the flight, by checking pnr against pre-determined risk assessment criteria and against databases on wanted persons. thirdly, there is pro-active use – also known as trend analysis – to create or update risk assessment criteria. of these three uses of pnr data, only one – real-time use – might potentially be considered to be a form of profiling, in this case the checking of the pnr against pre-determined risk assessment criteria. to ensure that this use will not adversely affect individuals, the new eu-australia pnr agreement explicitly prohibits automated processing and always requires human involvement before adverse decisions are taken on the basis of pnr data. this prohibition was not present in the pnr agreement from 2007, so it is an important step forward. the commission is seeking to have the same provisions included in the us and canadian agreements. a similar provision is also included in the commission’s proposal for the directive on the european pnr. the commission’s approach to both the european pnr and pnr agreements with third countries is therefore in line with eu data protection legislation, which grants every individual the right not to be subject to a decision which produces legal effects concerning him or her, and which is based exclusively, or to a decisive extent, on automated processing of data on him or her. against this background, the commission is not convinced of the need to develop any new legal definition of profiling. on the eu-australia agreement, the commission’s view is that the new agreement respects the council’s negotiating mandate and the resolution of this house. we consider that it respects the principles of necessity and proportionality. we should bear in mind that the agreement has a well-defined and specific purpose limitation – a limited period of detention of all pnr. pnr will be masked-out a short time after the flight and stored anonymously. strict conditions apply on transfers of data to third countries and pnr must be transmitted by air carriers exclusively by the ‘push’ method. the question of proportionality should be viewed in the general context of the laws of the third country, in this case australia, and the security threat faced by that country. members have raised important questions on dispute resolution, suspension and termination. the procedures for terminating the agreement would be the same as those for concluding the agreement and therefore parliament’s role is fully assured. suspension of the agreement is regulated by article 218(9) of the treaty. there is no formal role for parliament. however, a parliamentary resolution calling for a suspension would certainly be a very important political consideration for whether the commission would desire to launch such a procedure. finally, the commission agrees with the european court of justice that the main purpose of pnr agreements is police and judicial cooperation, and not data protection. that was confirmed in 2005 by the european court of justice in the us pnr case. it was clearly stated that pnr agreements should be drawn up using the legal bases for police and judicial cooperation. on the us agreement, you asked whether there were any bilateral agreements between the us and member states on pnr. this issue was discussed in detail in this house in october 2010. the us signed a memorandum of understanding with several member states as part of the visa waiver programme. the memorandum of understanding was intended to commit the parties – the us and the specific member states – to enter into negotiations on passenger information, information on the screening of known or suspected terrorists, information to combat terrorism and serious crime and information on migration and border security matters. the memorandum of understanding was not intended to be in itself the legal basis for the exchange of data between that member state and the us. it merely expressed the intention of the two parties to have specific agreements to govern the exchange of data. only such an agreement would then be the legal basis for exchanging data. in order to implement the memorandum of understanding, the us and the relevant member states signed only two types of agreement, namely agreements on enhancing cooperation in preventing and combating serious crime and agreements on the exchange of screening information concerning known or suspected terrorists. following that debate, and in the context of the negotiations, we again examined the issue, and asked both the member states and the us whether there were any bilateral agreements between them on pnr. both sides replied categorically negatively. both the member states and the us assure us that the only agreement regulating pnr is the one that the us signed with the eu in 2007. no further agreement exists. secure flight data are not to be confused with pnr data. they differ both in nature and in function. they are much more limited in scope since secure flight data include only the name, date of birth and gender of passengers. such data are used by the us authorities exclusively to prevent individuals already known to pose a security risk – i.e. those on the us no-fly list – from boarding an aircraft. secure flight data is collected by air carriers on behalf of the us authorities and pnr data is collected by air carriers for their own commercial purposes. to reduce their economic burden, carriers generally choose to provide the required secure data with the pnr data to the us department of homeland security (dhs). on receipt, the secure flight data is retrieved from the pnr and stored separately for seven days and then deleted. another very important issue is ad hoc ‘pulls’ by the us authorities. last year’s joint review acknowledged that there was a problem with regard to both the number of ad hoc requests for pnr data and the fact that the dhs executed such requests by ‘pulling’ the data. it strongly called for improvements to this state of affairs and for the us authorities to step up their efforts to encourage air carriers to use the ‘push’ method of transmission only. the us has acknowledged that the high frequency of ‘pulls’ is problematic. the issue is being re-discussed in the context of negotiations with the us on the new pnr agreement. the commission’s aim is to ensure that data are transferred using the ‘push’ method, with recourse to ‘pulls’ only in strictly limited circumstances. finally, you asked about the opinion of our legal service. i can say that the commission is seeking improvements to the text on a small number of key issues. we have emphasised to the us that the support of both the council and the parliament is needed for the final outcome of the negotiations. on the issue of the transfer of data between the us and canada, this was, and continues to be, governed by the memorandum of understanding signed between those two countries. its purpose is the sharing of ‘look-out’ and advance passenger information data between canadian border service agencies and the united states customs and border protection to identify high-risk travellers and facilitate the flow of legitimate persons across the border. we have carefully assessed these agreements on a strictly confidential basis and we are convinced that they do not violate the pnr agreements with either country. i am sorry this was long but there were very many questions that i had to answer. i hope i have adequately answered the questions asked in this plenary.
on behalf of the green group in the european parliament i think that there is no excuse for lack of clarity here. we are facing a paradigm shift in research. citizens know that in the past they were investigated if they were suspected of a crime or had committed a crime. the thing about processing pmr data is that everyone is being investigated, including innocent people, and therefore, justified or not, proportionate or not, necessary or not, citizens need to be told clearly that they are being investigated, even when they are innocent. this cannot happen without a very clear debate with the citizens, particularly when their data is in the hands of third countries, as is the case. that is why we are discussing the agreement with the united states here today. most people would be okay with their data being used to stop a terrorist from blowing up the plane they're on. that's not the point. but what would people say if much of their data, including credit card and address information, was in the hands of a third country for 15 years, long after the plane had arrived at its destination? that is what is happening now with the agreement we have with the united states. and in 15 years, let's be clear, a lot of administrations change: an administration that says it wouldn't do data mining might actually do it. for that, the agreement would have to be perfectly clear, however, i believe that the agreement we have today leaves big holes, big windows for different uses. i wonder what the commission will do to close these big holes in the agreement we have now.

in writing. − in the framework of the solidarity which should govern relations between member states within the european union and the objectives of the eu solidarity fund, i supported the requests for assistance submitted by slovenia, croatia and the czech republic, for a total amount of eur 19 546 647. as a result of heavy rains in august and september last year, different regions of these countries suffered major damage to infrastructure, businesses, housing and agricultural property. these are situations of extraordinary and natural disasters, the effects of which must be overcome quickly in order to minimise the consequences for the living conditions of the affected populations and the economic stability of the region. in this connection, i would stress the need to ensure greater flexibility and speed in the procedures for implementing the solidarity fund.
in writing. − the report endorses the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund (eusf) to assist three countries - slovenia, the czech republic and croatia - which were affected in september 2010 by heavy rains followed by floods that caused heavy damage, in some cases forcing people to leave their homes and causing significant damage to public infrastructure, businesses, housing and agriculture. as the total losses are below the normal threshold for the mobilisation of the eusf, the request was examined on the basis of the so-called regional disaster criteria of exceptional nature, as provided for in the relevant regulation. we recall that a few months earlier, in may and june 2010, two of these countries - the czech republic and croatia - had already suffered identical disasters, which prompted the mobilisation of the eusf, and the requirements for classifying what happened as a major disaster were then met. naturally, in view of these disasters and their effects (on the territory, the economy and the people), we consider the mobilization of this support to be important and necessary and therefore we voted in favour of the report, while at the same time pointing out that much remains to be done in the field of disaster prevention, including the many proposals we have already made here and which the commission is slow to put into practice.

in writing. − the european commission has proposed to mobilise the european union solidarity fund for slovenia, croatia and the czech republic on the basis of point 26 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 on budgetary discipline and sound financial management. the agreement allows the mobilisation of the solidarity fund up to an annual ceiling of eur 1 billion. slovenia, croatia and the czech republic requested the mobilisation of that fund following natural disasters which have resulted in significant material damage. in these countries, in fact, a period of unusually heavy rainfall has caused floods, overflowing of rivers, with serious consequences and damage to the population. the european commission services verified that all applications fulfil the eligibility criteria set out in regulation (ec) no 2012/2002. in accordance with these requirements, the commission proposed the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund in the amount of eur 7 459 637 for slovenia, eur 1 175 071 for croatia and eur 10 911 939 for the czech republic, for a total of eur 19 546 647. on the basis of these facts i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − on 25 march, the commission presented in parallel amending budget no 2/2011 and a proposal for the mobilisation of the european solidarity fund following the floods and landslides in slovenia, croatia and the czech republic in august and september 2010, totalling eur 19.55 million. the scale of the damage caused and its impact on the populations concerned justify the mobilisation of the fund, but only delay its mobilisation.

in writing. - under the financial regulation, the commission may present draft amending budgets in the event of unavoidable, exceptional or unforeseen circumstances. following the report a7-0238/2011 detailing the mobilisation of the esf in favour of slovenia, croatia and the czech republic, it is necessary to approve an amendment to the union budget. the conditions for eligibility for assistance from the fund have been verified. the direct losses were calculated by the slovenian, czech and croatian authorities to be eur 19,5 million in total. in the case of slovenia, the direct losses exceed the normal threshold of 0,6% of gni for mobilisation of the eusf and the event can be considered as a major natural disaster. in the cases of the czech republic and croatia, where the direct losses do not exceed the normal threshold, the specific condition that a country affected by the same large-scale disaster as a neighbouring country may exceptionally benefit from the eusf was considered to be fulfilled. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which will enable slovenia, croatia and the czech republic to cope with the serious material damage caused by natural disasters.

in writing. - i welcome this report as it aims to support the maintenance of employment, in this particular case in denmark. this is a financial aid fund which will support some 825 workers with a total amount of eur 6.24 million.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the egf was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when we are faced with this serious crisis, with rising unemployment as one of its main consequences, the eu should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly in terms of support for people who have lost their jobs overnight. i have therefore supported the present report on the mobilisation of the egf for denmark to support the 825 workers made redundant by the machine and equipment manufacturer lm glasfiber.

in writing. - faced with the effects of the global economic and financial crisis on the european wind turbine market, with demand in europe falling sharply in favour of the asian option, lm glasfiber closed down its machinery and equipment manufacturing units in three municipalities in the region of south denmark (syddanmark) and started to develop its business through partnerships in china. as a result, 1 650 workers were made redundant at the beginning of 2010 at lm glasfiber. given the importance of the re-skilling of this workforce for the local and european productive fabric, i supported the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 6 247 415 from the european globalisation adjustment fund for programmes to support the reintegration of these dismissed workers into the labour market.
in writing. - another request for the mobilisation of the fund. these requests have been made in succession and thousands of workers have been made redundant in several member states since the instrument was introduced. this time, another request was made to denmark, which submitted a request for assistance in respect of 1650 redundancies at lm glasfiber, 825 of which were potential recipients of assistance. we are once again supporting this mobilisation, but we are once again insisting that we must intervene before this company is shut down again, in defence of production and employment. more than palliatives, a change of direction and policies is needed in this eu. the proposal we made during the debate on the 2011 budget for the creation of a european programme for employment and sustainable development, allocating 1% of eu gdp, to be supplemented by funds from the member states, with a view to real convergence, promoting the potential of each country, the sustainable use of its resources, and focusing on production and the creation of jobs with rights, is now becoming more urgent. the path the eu is taking is unfortunately quite different (and dangerous), leading only to more and more unemployment and recession.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid is now to be given to denmark, which has requested assistance in relation to 1 650 redundancies (of which 825 are potential beneficiaries of assistance) in the company lm glasfiber in nace rev. 2 division 28 (manufacture of machinery and equipment) in three municipalities in the region of southern denmark.

in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 established the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to support workers who lose their jobs as a result of structural changes in the global economy. lm glasfiber, based in the syddanmark region of denmark, faced serious difficulties due to the changing patterns of trade in wind turbines, the economic and financial crisis and the rapid decline in demand in the eu, as opposed to asia. therefore, lm glasfiber considered it appropriate to reduce the facilities in lunderskov and hammelev and to establish a strategic partnership with a chinese company. the commission proposes to allocate eur 6 247 415 to the machinery and equipment manufacturing company to provide financial support for the 1 650 workers made redundant, of whom 825 are potential beneficiaries of direct assistance. finally, i would like to stress that the egf should not replace the legal and financial responsibilities of lm glasfiber, that the financial support should reach the workers concerned as quickly as possible and that the ec should make its best efforts to speed up the process of activating the egf for the benefit of the member states.
in writing. − i welcome this report, as i recognise the need, already advocated by the european parliament in 2007, for a package of commitments for the creation of a second generation schengen information system. an agency is needed to ensure the operability and security of sis ii, vis and eurodac data, while also ensuring good economies of scale in the management of the three systems, both from the budgetary and human resources point of view.
in writing. − in june 2009, the european commission presented a set of two legislative initiatives with the aim of establishing an agency with responsibility for managing large-scale information systems within the area of freedom, security and justice. the creation of this agency responds to the request made by the european parliament in 2007 and is the best solution from a financial, operational and institutional point of view. this report, which i support, argues that the agency's objectives are purely technical and operational management and that it should not have access to data or the capacity to take policy decisions such as the creation of new systems or the possibility of interoperability between different systems. it also states that there should be no possibility of unauthorised access to the data, that all data circulating on the network should be encrypted and that the management of the crypto device can never be outsourced to a private company, as is the case today. finally, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr carlos coelho, on having been able to reach an agreement at first reading.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that the creation of this agency for the operational management of sis ii, vis and eurodac and other instruments to be created in the area of freedom, security and justice is undoubtedly the best option for the medium and long term functioning of the eu. i would also like to congratulate my colleague, mr carlos coelho, on his excellent report, the conclusions of which i am very pleased with. the agency will act as a platform for more effective information flow and therefore better results.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report by approving the creation of the european agency which will ensure the operational management of the schengen information system. this agency will contribute to improving the level of security in the eu's area of freedom, security and justice and will facilitate the sharing of information between authorities controlling the union's external borders.
in writing. - in principle, i believe that the creation of european agencies should be based on effective criteria of rationality and sound operational management. this is clearly one of those cases. its creation is of a nature which clearly justifies the appearance of such an organism. there is a real need, as the rapporteur, whom i welcome, says, to ensure the operational management of sis, vis and eurodac and parts of the communication infrastructure at the end of the transitional period and, possibly, of other large-scale information systems in the field of justice, freedom and security, subject to the adoption of separate legal instruments. this single managing authority will be able to help improve coordination between systems, enhance the european response capacity in highly sensitive matters, provide training for technicians and experts with a high level of knowledge on all these issues and, not least, make better use of resources. finally, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on the excellent work he has done.
in writing. − this report aims to ensure the establishment of an agency for the operational management of large-scale information systems in the area of freedom, security and justice, such as the second generation schengen information system (sis ii), the visa information system (vis) and the eurodac fingerprint comparison system, as well as parts of the communication infrastructure. it is an agency with purely technical and operational management objectives and tasks, without the capacity to take policy decisions, such as the creation of new systems or the interoperability between the various systems. this proposal, for which i congratulate the rapporteur, mr carlos coelho, whom i congratulate on having succeeded in reaching an agreement at first reading, strengthens the rules on data protection and the integrity and security of personal data, as well as the role of the european parliament in its democratic control.
in writing. - the aim of this report is to set up a european agency, based in tallinn, estonia, whose purpose will be to ensure the management of the schengen system. a database will be set up to store fingerprint records of asylum seekers and a visa information system will be set up. the possibility of creating other schemes in the schengen area is also mentioned. we are aware of our fundamental disagreements with the eu's approach to the areas covered in this report. the necessary preservation of rights, freedoms and guarantees, which are vital to the genuinely democratic functioning of states, is not, in our view, properly safeguarded. we reject the proliferation of databases and information on people in the name of supposed security. this is a dangerous path. on the other hand, in the current economic and social context, we do not think that the establishment of this agency is one of the eu's priorities. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. the report adopted today aims to set up a european agency, based in tallinn, estonia, to manage the schengen system through a database containing fingerprints of asylum seekers and the visa information system. the report also refers to the possibility of creating other systems in the schengen area. we are concerned about the proliferation of european agencies and, especially at a time of economic and social crisis, we believe that the creation of another agency for this purpose should not be one of the priorities of the european union. we also believe that it is essential to ensure the preservation of rights and freedoms which are vital for the genuinely democratic functioning of states. we reject the proliferation of databases and of information on individuals in the name of supposed security. we know this is a dangerous path. that is why we voted against it.
in writing. − the creation of a european agency to ensure the operational management of the schengen information system, the visa information system, a database of fingerprints of asylum seekers (eurodac) and other systems in the schengen area was approved by the european parliament today. the agency, based in tallinn, estonia, is expected to start its work in summer 2012. the purpose of this agency is to ensure secure, rapid and permanent communication (24 hours a day, 365 days a year) between the central services and all the member states that make up the various systems.
in writing. − the european commission presented in june 2009 a set of two legislative initiatives aimed at establishing an agency with responsibility for managing large-scale information systems within the framework of the area of freedom, security and justice. it was a proposal for a regulation on the matters covered by the first pillar in sis, vis and eurodac and a proposal for a decision on the matters covered by the third pillar in these three systems. however, with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, these initiatives lost their meaning and on 19 march 2010 the commission presented a new proposal which essentially corresponds to a revised version of the previous proposal for a regulation with a lisbon perspective and integrating the aspects relating to the 3rd pillar. i welcome the work of my colleague carlos coelho, who has tried in several articles to strengthen the role of the european parliament and to ensure greater transparency. in the same vein, it has sought to strengthen the rules on data protection and the integrity and security of personal data by strengthening the role of the european data protection supervisor. these are the facts which motivated my vote in favour.
in writing. − the creation of an agency for the operational management of large-scale information systems in the area of freedom, security and justice, with a view to the management of sis ii, vis and eurodac, aims to optimise the resources available, seeking to achieve economies of scale. in a matter of such a sensitive nature, it must be ensured that the agency is provided with the financial means necessary for its work, which to a large extent provide the desired autonomy, and that the member states are associated with its operational process by exercising a supervisory function. the european parliament's monitoring role must also be safeguarded, particularly as particularly sensitive issues such as the need to protect citizens' personal data are dealt with in these areas.
in writing. − the proposal aims to establish an agency responsible for the operational management of the existing second generation information systems in the area of freedom, justice and security, such as the schengen information system (sis ii), the visa information system (vis) and eurodac. these systems are currently operated by the european commission, but it is not its responsibility to operate computer systems on a larger scale. the legal instruments relating to sis ii and vis actually provide for the need to establish a management authority capable of ensuring the continuity and operational management of the systems and the organisation of the various data in the long term. in addition to these operational tasks, the agency, which is to operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, is also empowered to adopt security measures, draw up reports and provide training, as well as to publish and monitor information. i support the rapporteur in recalling that the agency cannot be given the power to make political decisions or decisions concerning the interoperability of systems. their subject matter and their responsibilities should relate only to the technical aspect of the operational management of the information systems.

in writing. − the eu treaties authorise the council, on a proposal from the commission and after consulting the european parliament, to adopt specific measures in favour of the outermost regions, taking account of the economic and social situation of these regions. in reality, the existence of permanent handicaps such as insularity, remoteness from the large markets, small size, difficult terrain and climate, economic dependence on a small number of products, seriously hampers the development of these regions and fully justifies the adoption of appropriate measures. this type of exemption makes perfect sense in helping these regions to cope more adequately with their economic challenges. we think, however, that it is appropriate for this type of exemption to become definitive and not have to be reassessed every ten years, leaving the peripheral regions in a situation of real economic insecurity.
in writing. - article 349 tfeu authorises the council, on a proposal from the commission and after consulting the european parliament, to adopt specific measures in favour of the outermost regions, taking account of their economic and social situation. in fact, the existence of permanent handicaps such as insularity, a well-known reality for the portuguese residents of the azores and madeira, combined with the remoteness from the large markets, the small size of the azores, the difficult terrain and climate, and the economic dependence on a small number of products, seriously hampers the development of these regions and fully justifies the adoption of appropriate measures. it is on this basis that france bases the so-called "octroi de mer" system, which has proved to be largely positive in relation to the objectives pursued, in particular the positive impact on the maintenance of employment. the commission proposal, accompanied by a proposal for a council decision, suggests that the scheme be extended to 50 products for guyana. the european parliament supports this proposal without amendments. in view of the specific characteristics of the economies of the outermost regions and in view of the fact that the granting of aid is in accordance with community law and is an economic stimulus, i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - the special situation of the outermost regions requires the adoption of specific measures in favour of the outermost regions which take due account of the economic and social situation of these regions. the constraints and permanent difficulties such as insularity, remoteness from markets and scarcity of land seriously hamper the development of these regions and justify measures which can help to reduce the effects of existing constraints. this possibility is enshrined in the treaty itself, which enshrines the special status of the outermost regions in article 349. it is on this basis that the decision on the measures for granting the right of withdrawal is based, in which france is authorised, in respect of its four overseas departments, until 1 july 2014 to provide for a differentiated system of charges for the tax on granting the right of withdrawal on certain products of these departments. i believe that special attention should be paid to the needs and difficulties of the outermost regions, and that this should be reflected in the adoption of specific and appropriate measures for all the outermost regions of the european union which contribute to promoting the development of these and other outermost regions and to better integrating them into the european internal market. i therefore voted in favour of the document in plenary.
in writing. − i welcome this report, which is the result of complex negotiation between all political groups, in that it emphasises the importance of the universal social inclusion obligations and calls on the commission to provide guidance on how best to adopt the revised universal services directive. i would also stress the importance of broadband access for all and the creation of a common european emergency number 112.
in writing. the concept of universal service was developed by the european institutions and defines a set of general interest requirements to which certain activities must conform. the obligations laid down are intended to ensure universal access for all to certain essential services of good quality at an affordable price. the present report, which i supported, aims to assess recent developments in the basic concept of universal service enshrined in the universal service directive in the context of universal broadband access. the report also focuses on the single emergency number 112, which was set up in 1991 in the context of the single market for the free movement of persons with the aim of ensuring single access to emergency services throughout the european union. it is therefore important to give visibility to the 112 emergency number, to improve the effectiveness of hotlines, in order to protect public health and to ensure effective civil protection. equally important is the commission's decision to carry out an in-depth study of the provision of internet services.
in writing. - i voted in favour because i consider universal service obligations (usos) to be important as a safety net for social inclusion. i support the broadband for all objectives of the digital agenda and am convinced that universal broadband access helps citizens and businesses to fully enjoy the benefits of the digital single market, including by improving social inclusion. i believe that the european emergency number 112 can save lives and increase the protection of eu citizens; and i believe that the commission should ensure that all sectors of society have access to this service, including people with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.
in writing. − universal service should provide all citizens, even in the most isolated and peripheral areas, with access to essential services that enable their participation in society, at affordable prices and without distorting competition, thus meeting the objectives of the digital agenda, with the expectation that by 2013 basic broadband coverage will be achieved for all citizens of the union, enabling them to fully enjoy the benefits of the digital single market. the creation in 1991 of the european emergency number 112 was of the utmost importance in allowing citizens to contact the emergency services on the same number, regardless of the member state in which they are located. the commission should also be able to assess the impact of the new rules on the free movement of persons, in particular the rules on the free movement of goods and services, the rules on the free movement of persons and the rules on the free movement of services. given that several recent disasters have demonstrated that early warning of citizens in the event of emergencies and of imminent or ongoing major disasters is necessary to reduce human suffering and loss of life, it is essential to improve the quality of implementation of this emergency support service, in particular in terms of information, accessibility, interoperability and response times.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the universal service and the 112 emergency number, because it provides for the development of a communication strategy to raise public awareness of the existence and use of the 112 number, as well as measures to improve the accessibility, quality and efficiency of this service.
in writing. - in a society such as the west, where the media and communications proliferate and the technology associated with them evolves at a rapid pace, it is clear that the lack of conditions for some sections of the population to use similar media and thus to access contact with others and the information they convey is a factor of social exclusion. the establishment of european targets for network coverage, in particular for broadband, requires coordination between the union and the member states and between the member states and the operators in order to achieve the desired universal coverage. i was not aware that the european emergency number was not sufficiently publicized, since in my country it is quite widespread, and i hope that this trend will be reversed, allowing more and more people to have access to it and to the emergency and rescue services which are made available through it.
in writing. − the european emergency number 112 was introduced in 1991 to complement national emergency numbers and make emergency services more accessible in all eu member states. however, according to a eurobarometer survey, only 26% of eu citizens currently spontaneously identify 112 as the appropriate telephone number to call the police, fire or emergency medical services anywhere in the european union. i understand that by 2020 that percentage should reach 80%. this is a service that can save lives and its universality is of fundamental importance for the protection of citizens, with particular emphasis on free movement within the european union. in order to ensure the greatest possible efficiency, better service to victims and to combat calls for false requests for help, i also advocate georeferencing calls by requiring mobile and fixed telecommunications operators to automatically ensure the identification and exact location of the persons making the calls. it is also important to promote an inclusive service, ensuring the technical conditions necessary to ensure an adequate response to people with disabilities including a deaf-mute , as well as responding to citizens of any nationality or foreign language.
in writing. − the report assesses the provision of the european emergency number 112 and analyses developments in relation to universal broadband access. the broadband for all objectives of the digital agenda are supported, considering that universal broadband access will improve social inclusion, create new opportunities for businesses and boost employment. the report also supports the emergency number 112. we consider universal services such as the european emergency number 112 to be important, and we have already taken initiatives in this parliament. to make it more effective, it needs to be more widely disseminated and of higher quality. according to the report itself, only 26% of the population is aware of this emergency number. as regards information technology, we are drawing attention to the approximately 100 million people in the eu who are at risk of poverty. it is not necessary to mention here the obvious difficulties in accessing the new technologies that these people will have. this is why concrete measures and actions are needed to enable everyone to have access, on an equal footing, to the emergency number, broadband and the new information technologies in general.
in writing. − this report aims to assess both the provision of the european emergency number 112 and developments in relation to universal broadband access. the rapporteur supports the broadband for all objectives of the digital agenda, considering that universal broadband access will improve social inclusion, create new opportunities for businesses and boost employment, just as it supports the emergency number and the universal service. we consider universal services such as the european emergency number 112 to be important. however, to make it more effective, more information and better quality are needed, which requires special measures, as only 26% of the population are aware of this emergency number. on the other hand, as we said in the plenary debate, all this must not also serve to increase social exclusion, since there are about 100 million people at risk of poverty, with difficulties in accessing the new technologies. it is necessary to take account of concrete measures and actions which will enable everyone to have access, on an equal footing, to the emergency number, broadband and the new information technologies in general.

in writing. the universal service directive was intended to define a set of universal services which, as the name suggests, should be provided to all citizens at a good price-benefit ratio. in the current context, it highlights the need for broadband as a tool for a networked economy at the service of european citizens. however, other instruments should not be overlooked and should be universally available: the commission's proposal is to provide a single european emergency number, 112, to help those who are most vulnerable for various reasons: a disease that makes them more vulnerable, an accidental problem, because they are in tourism. it is a global reading which deserves to be made, in the face of a europe at the service of the people.
in writing. - the importance of a single european emergency number, 112, with particular emphasis on its visibility and on raising awareness among citizens, is highlighted in the report. the efficiency of the emergency lines, the handling of calls and the quality of care after the call to 112 must be improved. the purpose of the adopted document was to assess the concept of universal service as it emerges from the universal service directive. member states should ensure a universal service in all technologies relating to broadband access. the european commission is called upon to ensure that 112 is effectively operational throughout the eu and accessible to all citizens. the number should be accessible to people with different types of disabilities and vulnerable groups by providing devices for users with hearing or visual impairments, text or sign language retransmission services or other special equipment. in this respect, i think it is appropriate to improve the reliability of information on the location of the appellant. it will be essential that the new european telecommunications rules require the updating of existing technologies for better automatic call location.
in writing. - i welcome this report, particularly the agreement reached on consumer rights in terms of access, quality and information and safeguarding the role of traditional trade. the most significant and valuable amendments to this report are undoubtedly those by the s&d group on improving working conditions, combating the shadow economy in the retail sector and implementing appropriate labour and social legislation to combat tax evasion and the informal economy, with the aim of maintaining employment levels and investing in the training of workers.
in writing. − the retail sector represents 20% of european smes, generates 4.2% of eu gdp and employs almost 20 million people. it is a key sector for the relaunch of the single market and for the pursuit of the europe 2020 targets. despite the progress made in this area, this report, which i supported, calls for measures to strengthen the retail market, namely: opening markets to businesses and eliminating the obstacles and difficulties that many businesses, especially smes, face; exploiting the full potential of electronic commerce by increasing business and consumer confidence; and improving the single euro payments area (sepa) system to develop a payment service accessible to all types of cards that increases transparency in transaction costs and eliminates unjustified interbank fees, ensuring faster bank transfers within the eu. finally, i would like to stress the european commission's idea of presenting a european retail action plan which sets out a strategy for addressing the outstanding issues, with recommendations at sectoral level.
in writing. − the retail market is undoubtedly a driver of growth, competitiveness and employment in europe and can make a decisive contribution to the pursuit of the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy. it is essential to build a more efficient, transparent and equitable retail market through an active contribution of retailers and suppliers themselves, to be complemented at community level by enhanced coordination between the different policies and by a comprehensive and long-term approach to this sector. we must tackle the remaining obstacles to the free movement of goods and services in the eu, namely the existence of more restrictive national rules, divergent interpretations and inadequate application of the rules, which ultimately limit the potential of the single market to serve european citizens and businesses. at the same time, the competition rules must be applied correctly, preventing abuse of a dominant position or unfair trading practices, and, if necessary, provide for access to more simplified, less time-consuming and more transparent infringement procedures. i support the excellent report by mrs corazza bildt and her call for an integrated european action plan for retail trade.
in writing. − the proper functioning of the internal market is essential for growth, competitiveness and employment. it is therefore important that all obstacles to its proper functioning be removed, especially at the level of the retail sector, which employs almost 20 million people, generates 4.2% of the union's gdp and represents 20% of european smes. the report identifies five priority areas for a more efficient retail market: (i) ensuring greater competitiveness, growth and employment; (ii) removing the remaining obstacles to the free movement of goods and services; (iii) opening up markets to consumers and businesses; (iv) taking stock of contractual and commercial practices between businesses; (v) enhancing efficiency and innovative practices. i believe that the removal of barriers and the effective completion of the internal market are urgently needed as a means of boosting growth and employment in a post-crisis europe.
in writing. the small and medium-sized enterprises sector, including the retail trade, is recognised as playing a decisive role in boosting the economy, with particular emphasis on promoting employment and the so-called middle class. retail trade is of paramount importance for economic and social cohesion, and i therefore support the call for an integrated european action plan for retail trade, with a view to defining a framework for action with concrete and pragmatic proposals to resolve the outstanding issues. i therefore commend the author of this report for her contribution to removing barriers to the free movement of goods and services, defending the interests of businesses and consumers and promoting their access to the market, increasing efficiency and sustainable consumption. in this way we are fostering competitiveness, growth and employment.
in writing. the report deals with a sector whose problems are all too obvious. retail trade, particularly in countries where the business fabric is dominated by micro and small family-type enterprises, is faced with the effects of the decline in the purchasing power of the general population, coupled with the overwhelming weight and unfair competition of the large retail sector. these are problems and difficulties which threaten the viability and future continuity of the sector, which plays, it should be remembered, a socially relevant role, particularly (but not only) outside the main urban areas. but the report does not address the root causes of this situation - a necessary condition for amending it. it ignores the effects of the deregulation and liberalisation of trade that the eu has been actively promoting, its effects on the proliferation of large supermarkets and the disproportionate increase in their power and influence, it does not address the consequences of liberalisation and privatisation, the reduction in the purchasing power of the population, the worsening of interest rates and the difficulties in accessing credit. the path is exactly the opposite: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. - this report is shrouded in many contradictions. it is true that the retail trade is under serious attack, especially in countries where it is carried on by micro and small family businesses and where, in some cases, the purchasing power of the population is declining, and especially in less urban areas where they play an important social role and where there are times of distress. but the report forgets the root cause of this situation and fails to properly criticize the liberalization of trade, the proliferation of large supermarkets, the consequences of liberalization and privatization, the decline in the purchasing power of the population, the worsening of interest rates and the credit difficulties. on the contrary, i did. the emphasis on the creation of the internal market is aggravating the difficulties of small retail businesses. that is why we did not vote in favour of this report.

in writing. the retail sector is perhaps the most visible aspect of the community action programme: not only because of its importance for the economy, but also because it represents the moment when trade brings together professionals and consumers, when the reality of the common space becomes tangible. however, this is an area which raises delicate problems which merit consideration: in this context, some member states have imposed obstacles indirectly, such as the introduction of particularly stringent packaging rules to the marketing of foreign products; the white marks have raised concerns among the holders of rights to the benchmark marks; on the other hand, some retailers (often integrated into distribution networks) have, by virtue of their strong bargaining power, crushed the margins of producers. these are cases which could jeopardize a free and competitive single market and one of the fundamental aims of the community project. the rapporteur has said that this is a point that must be on the agenda.

in writing. − this draft amending budget enters in the 2011 budget the surplus of eur 4 539 394 283 resulting from the implementation of the 2010 financial year, which reduces the overall contribution of the member states to the 2011 budget of the european union. i voted in favour of this draft amending budget because it complies with the provisions of article 15 of the financial regulation. i believe, however, that the european union must take the necessary measures so that in future the surplus amounts in the eu budget will no longer be credits for the contributing member states but will instead be an automatic increase in the budget for the following year, thus enabling the community to increase its capacity to intervene in support of the european project and socioeconomic cohesion.
in writing. − this draft amending budget is intended to enter the 2010 budget surplus in the 2011 budget, in accordance with article 15 of the financial regulation. the report considers that the part of the revenue calculated from interest on late payment and fines should not be considered as surplus and should therefore not be deducted from the member states' contributions and that these revenues [...] should be returned directly and reinvested in the eu budget, a position which the council has been critical of. however, parliament takes its word for it and approves the council's position without any amendments. the decision thus consists in reducing the 2010 surplus (eur 4.54 billion) in the member states' contributions to the 2011 budget accordingly. this means that the reductions in question will be much greater in countries with stronger economies than in countries with weaker economies. the example of germany (with a reduction of eur 923 million) compared with portugal (with a reduction of eur 59 million) only exacerbates the injustices in the distribution of these surpluses and calls into question the principle of the redistributive function of the community budget, which underlies any genuine cohesion policy.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the amending budget. in accordance with article 37 of the financial regulation, the commission may present preliminary draft amending budgets in the event of unavoidable, exceptional or unforeseen circumstances. in accordance with paragraph 3 of that article, the budgetary authority shall take its decisions in the light of urgency. in accordance with article 15 (3) of the financial regulation, the surplus or deficit for each financial year is to be entered as revenue or expenditure in the budget for the following financial year in an amending budget to be presented by the commission within 15 days of the provisional accounts being presented. draft amending budget no 3/2011 is intended to enter in the 2011 budget the surplus resulting from the implementation of the financial year 2010, amounting to eur 4 539 394 283. consequently, the overall contribution of the member states to the 2011 eu budget will be reduced accordingly. portugal shall contribute by minus eur 59 119 421.
in writing. - amending budget no 3/2011 relates to the surplus of eur 4.54 billion resulting from the 2010 financial year. it should be recalled that in 2010 there was already a surplus of 2.25 billion. it should be recalled that delays in implementation and the consequent payments of approved projects, interest earned on delays in project implementation and fines levied on member states for failure to apply or breach community rules contribute to the formation of the surplus. it should be noted that of the above-mentioned surplus, eur 1.8 billion correspond to fines and interest incurred in the delay in the implementation of projects. this surplus shall be calculated annually and deducted proportionally from the contributions of each member state to the union budget. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be allowed to apply the principle of proportionality to the payment of the surplus resulting from interest on late implementation of projects and fines levied on member states. the adoption of the amending budget is essential for the determination of the amount by which each member state is to contribute to the 2011 budget, otherwise there will be further delays in payments for projects that are being implemented or in the process of being implemented.

in writing. the draft amending budget voted today aims to enter the surplus of the previous year in the 2011 budget. the surplus of eur 4,54 billion is the result of exchange rate differences, revenue implementation and expenditure implementation. in accordance with the financial regulation, the commission may present preliminary draft amending budgets in the event of unavoidable, exceptional or unforeseen circumstances. the overall contribution of the member states to the 2011 budget will thus be reduced by eur 4,54 billion, as this amount, which corresponds to the 2010 surplus, will be returned to the member states. the proposal, which i voted for and which parliament is determined to promote and defend in the forthcoming negotiations on the annual and multiannual budgets, results in a reduction of 59 million euro in portugal's contribution to the community budget in this particular case.
in writing. − i welcome this report on the application of consumer protection legislation, and it should be noted that the main difference with the commission's initial proposal is the introduction of a review clause, according to which the commission has to carry out an assessment of the operational mechanisms and, in 2014, submit a legislative proposal with a more substantial revision of this regulation.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 2006/2004 aims to combat illegal crossborder trade which disrupts the proper functioning of the internal market and undermines consumer confidence. that regulation establishes a european-level network of public authorities responsible for the enforcement of consumer protection laws in the member states (cpc network). the regulation partially harmonises the investigatory and enforcement powers of the authorities by establishing mechanisms for the exchange of relevant information and the adoption of measures to put an end to infringements in cross-border situations. on the basis of recent developments in consumer protection legislation, this report, which has my support, deals with the proposal to amend and update the regulation. legislation that is not relevant in the field of consumer protection should be deleted and references to old legislation that is no longer in force should be updated.
in writing. − consumer rights and their protection in community law is one of the main pillars of the functioning of the internal market. while i believe that adequate consumer protection and safety is fundamental to the proper functioning of markets and trade, i also believe that such protection should be as uniform as possible in the union. at a time when many transactions and contracts are cross-border and online transactions are gaining new relevance, cooperation between the various public authorities responsible for enforcing consumer protection legislation should be as close as possible in order to ensure a higher level of protection and to increase trust.
in writing. − in the context of the internal market and the safeguarding of the interests of european citizens, the harmonisation and improvement of consumer protection mechanisms is of the utmost importance for the consolidation of european integration and for confidence in the economic and legislative system. in this context, i support this report, which updates and streamlines existing legislation in this area, in particular regulation (ec) no 2006/2004, which aims to combat illegal cross-border trade, establish a european network of public authorities responsible for enforcing consumer protection laws in the member states and harmonise the investigatory and enforcement powers of authorities to eliminate breaches in eu legislation that protects consumers' interests.
in writing. − the regulation aims to remove barriers to crossborder cooperation between public enforcement authorities to detect, investigate and bring to an end or ban infringements of eu consumer protection legislation. only in this way will it be possible to effectively tackle dishonest cross-border traders who disrupt the smooth functioning of the internal market and thus increase consumer confidence in accepting cross-border offers, so as to prevent sellers and suppliers from evading enforcement at the expense of compliant sellers and suppliers.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 2006/2004 on cooperation between national authorities responsible for the enforcement of consumer protection laws. the aim of this regulation is to remove barriers to crossborder cooperation between public enforcement authorities in order to detect, investigate and bring to an end or prohibit infringements within the eu of consumer interests. seven years after its entry into force, situations needing to be changed have been identified. however, there is still insufficient information on the functioning of the regulation and this information can only be obtained through an in-depth analysis. the commission is currently preparing the second report on the application of the regulation, which will be published later this year. according to the report, the commission also planned to carry out an external evaluation followed by a public consultation of stakeholders. i agree with the need, identified by the rapporteur, to include a review clause in the regulation. this clause obliges the commission to step up its efforts in this process and to accelerate the review process by submitting a new legislative proposal by the end of 2013.
in writing. - as the recognition of the economic freedoms of community citizens is a matter for the common space, the need to protect consumers from the abuses to which they are often subject quickly became apparent. in fact, their unjustified lack of protection would immediately lead to a breakdown in confidence in the virtualities of the common space. that is why this is one of the flags of community action. however, although a substantive framework is provided to regulate the position of consumers, it lacks mechanisms for the application of penalties. in this context, cooperation between the various national authorities responsible for enforcing consumer protection provisions is necessary, otherwise it will no longer be possible to hold those who act unlawfully accountable simply by crossing borders.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation because i agree that over-the-counter (otc) derivatives are not transparent, as they are privately negotiated contracts, for which information is normally available only to the contracting parties. they create a complex network of interdependencies which can make it difficult to identify the nature and level of risks involved. the financial crisis has shown that these characteristics increase uncertainty during periods of market stress and therefore pose risks to financial stability. i would therefore like to welcome the fact that this regulation establishes conditions for limiting such risks and for increasing the transparency of derivative contracts.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it presents a set of proposals that fill the current gaps in the regulatory framework for over-the-counter derivatives. the absence of legislation in this area has contributed to the financial crisis and its harmful consequences. the amendments adopted by parliament will help to improve the transparency and risk management of this market.
in writing. − this legislative proposal aims to fill the gap in the absence of community-wide regulation in the otc derivatives sector and aims to increase its transparency and reduce its risks. a set of requirements for derivative contracts, for the conditions for authorisation of central counterparties (ccps) and the criteria to be examined to ensure appropriate features for centralised clearing and for the reporting of otc derivative information to trade repositories where the aggregated information can be used, in particular, for systemic risk analysis and for the calculation of clearing, are now established. finally, i would like to call on the member states in the council to take a decision on this matter as soon as possible, so that this regulation can enter into force quickly in the community legal order.

in writing. − another revealing report on how the eu is dealing with the multifaceted crisis affecting the world, a crisis which has a recognised factor of disruption and risk in the hypertrophy of the financial sphere. here too, the aim is to regulate some of the financial market without going to the bottom of the problem. the eu financial sector uses derivatives because it is an area that is unregulated, unregulated and that develops without knowing the overall extent of the risks involved, knowing only that they are the basis of large speculative gains and therefore necessarily have the most serious systemic implications. financial market derivatives played a crucial role in triggering the financial crisis, as they were used for excessive speculation. this regulation proposes the supervision of the financial sector in europe with the aim of reducing the risks and severity of future financial crises, but without addressing the central issue: to put an end to this type of operation with this instrument. this central question, which was admitted at the outset of the financial crisis, is now being put aside, and the door to speculation and its effects is still open (even if it is now being tried to keep it closed).

in writing. − the financial products that financial institutions have created over the years have not been properly regulated, which has contributed to the severe financial crisis they have triggered in the past. the absence of a regulatory framework for otc derivatives contributed to the financial crisis and its ensuing consequences. in response to concerns about financial stability, the commission put forward a proposal to regulate this market in september last year. the amendments adopted by parliament today are aimed above all at improving the transparency and risk management of the otc derivatives market, so that the same mistakes with the serious consequences that we all know will not be repeated in the future.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation because i agree that reliable data will be needed to identify the relevant otc derivative categories that should be subject to the clearing obligation, the thresholds and the systemically important non-financial counterparties. therefore, for regulatory purposes, i agree that it is important to define a uniform reporting requirement for otc derivatives at union level. furthermore, i agree with the need to provide for a retrospective reporting obligation, as far as possible, for both financial and non-financial counterparties above the threshold, in order to provide comparable data to esma. if such retrospective disclosure is not feasible for any category of otc derivatives, i agree that an appropriate justification should be provided to the relevant trade repository. i also believe that effective, proportionate and dissuasive sanctions should be provided for in respect of compensation and reporting obligations. member states should apply those penalties in a manner that does not undermine the effectiveness of the rules. i agree that member states should ensure that the penalties imposed are publicly disclosed and that reports assessing the effectiveness of existing rules are published at regular intervals.
in writing. − otc derivatives are privately traded contracts for which information is normally available only to the contracting parties. its complex network of interdependencies makes it difficult to identify the nature and level of risks involved. the lack of regulation of these financial instruments has contributed to the financial crisis and its resulting economic and social consequences. the proposal aims to improve the transparency and risk management of otc derivatives by laying down rules on clearing and reporting obligations, albeit in a limited way. the compulsory notification of financial transactions is also an indispensable precondition for their future taxation. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − the current architecture of the european supervisory system integrates three authorities: the european banking authority, the european insurance and pensions authority and the european securities and markets authority. this is a model designed to avoid systemic risk by separating banking, insurance and securities supervision (a model also used in portugal: respectively, banco de portugal, instituto de seguros de portugal and cmvm, associated in the national board of financial supervisors). in this overall context of reconfiguration, it is important to regulate otc derivatives, i.e. over-the-counter derivatives. the central concern of community action at this point is to increase the transparency and monitoring of these actions and to avoid the creation of risks of financial instability. we are once again faced with a measure aimed at improving the mechanisms for preventing crisis situations.
in writing. − otc derivatives are not very transparent, as they are privately traded contracts, for which information is normally available only to the contracting parties. they create a complex network of interdependencies which can make it difficult to identify the nature and level of risks involved. i welcome the fact that this regulation establishes conditions for limiting such risks and for increasing the transparency of derivative contracts. effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties should be provided for in respect of the compensation and reporting obligations, which should be applied by member states in a manner that does not undermine the effectiveness of the rules. member states should also ensure that the penalties imposed are publicly disclosed and that reports assessing the effectiveness of the existing rules are published at regular intervals. in addition, it is also essential to protect the right to privacy of natural persons with regard to the processing of their personal data, in accordance with directive 95/46/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 24 october 1995 on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data.
