in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution by agreeing that financial conglomerates need to be identified across the union, insofar as they are exposed to group risks, on the basis of the common guidelines issued by the european supervisory authority (european banking authority - eba), the european supervisory authority (european insurance and occupational pensions authority - eiopa) and the european supervisory authority (european securities and markets authority - esma), following cooperation within the joint committee of the european supervisory authorities (joint committee). it is also important that the requirements for the waiver of the application of supplementary supervision are applied on a risk-based basis in accordance with those guidelines. this provision is particularly important in the case of larger conglomerates operating internationally.

in writing. the commission has proposed a number of measures to strengthen the complementary supervision of financial institutions in a financial conglomerate. they thus aim to identify and resolve some of the technical issues that needed an urgent response. in particular, i would like to stress the need for supervisors to be able to analyse mixed financial companies. it is necessary to ensure that the new european supervisory authorities issue general guidance on the supervision of financial conglomerates, it is essential to improve the transparency of supervisory activity, and it is crucial to adopt common criteria on the definition of mixed financial companies for inclusion in supplementary supervision. finally, i look forward to the wider and more detailed review by the commission of supplementary supervision.
in writing. − no sector, no actor, no product can be left out of effective regulation and intelligent supervision. this directive aims to strengthen financial stability. directive 2002/87/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 16 december 2002 on the supplementary supervision of credit institutions, insurance undertakings and investment firms in a financial conglomerate provides competent authorities in the financial sector with supplementary powers and tools for the supervision of groups composed of many regulated entities active in different sectors of the financial markets. thus, these groups (financial conglomerates) are exposed to risks related to the control of a group (group risks), which comprise contagion risks, where risks spread from one end of the group to another; risk concentration, where the same type of risk materializes in several parts of the group at the same time; the complexity of managing many different legal entities; potential conflicts of interest; and the challenge of allocating nominal capital to all its regulated entities, thus avoiding a multiple use of own funds. i agree that supplementary supervision should be applied to conglomerates in addition to supervision on an individual basis.
in writing. - this report is part of the body of legislation which has been discussed in this parliament with the stated aim of supervising the financial system, increasing transparency and, more specifically, reducing risks in derivatives markets and short selling and strengthening investor protection. as we have said, the measures already adopted and those now proposed do not provide the necessary response to the lack of regulation of the financial system. this does not mean that in some cases the existing situation cannot be improved. this is the case with this report on the supplementary supervision of financial entities in a financial conglomerate. in this case, for example, there is a concern on the part of the responsible body to carry out supervision on a consolidated basis, covering the parent company and all the entities in the banking group with regard to the requirements contained in the legislation for the sector. these are positive aspects, but they are not enough to solve all the problems that exist, and that is why we abstained in the final vote.

in writing. - the past has proved the difficulty of properly supervising financial entities forming part of a financial conglomerate. the complexity of these organisations and the extent of their activities make supervision difficult, which in turn can lead to serious problems when they go bankrupt. the commission's present proposal is intended to provide a rapid solution to a situation which has become more problematic during the financial crisis but which has been known for a long time. supervisors should be able to supervise mixed financial companies in the same way as they supervise financial companies (banking) and insurance holding companies (insurance). although the current directives do not seem to prohibit member states from adapting their legislation to exercise this power over mixed financial companies, european coordination is useful in making this exercise compulsory in order to avoid further problems in the future.

in writing. - i voted against the report on the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and the assessment of the risk of carbon leakage, because it contains insufficient proposals to respond to the challenges of climate change. i regret that parliament has not been more ambitious, since tackling climate change is good not only for the environment but also for the european economy and job creation.
in writing. − at a time when the debate on co2 emissions has become unavoidable and when maintaining the current energy dependence on oil and its derivatives is unsustainable, it is important that more environmentally friendly and equally reliable energy alternatives are found. it is also essential that europe finds, within the framework of the eu 2020 strategy, innovative ways to promote sustainable and greener growth. however, at a time of severe economic and financial crisis, not only are the political conditions not in place for increased public investment - which is necessary to increase the target of reducing emissions - but it is also unreasonable to expect that companies, already weakened by the economic situation, will be confronted with overly ambitious targets that impose additional operational difficulties on them. green growth without undermining competitiveness requires a sustainable and consistent energy policy, the proper functioning of the emission allowance market and the promotion of national projects that contribute to community objectives.
in writing. − in order to protect the quality of life of european citizens and the sustainability of the future of the economy, the european union must make every effort to go as far as possible in reducing greenhouse gas emissions. the eu must step up its commitment to a green economy, even against the resistance of world powers to accompany this priority cause. the threat posed to humanity by climate change is not diminishing, and the impacts of 2°c of warming are worse than previously thought. i support the challenge to the commission to come forward as soon as possible with proposals to increase europe's climate ambitions and reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 30% by 2020, provided that this is feasible and does not prevent or undermine the competitiveness of our businesses. i also believe that it is essential to focus on scientific research, technological innovation in decarbonised energy, energy efficiency and the creation of green jobs in order to increase the competitiveness of the european economy.
in writing. − this report points to a wound: the eu, claiming to be a leader in the fight against climate change, has set targets for reducing greenhouse gas emissions below the lower end of the range recommended by the united nations panel on climate change. this is a fact that the permanent shifting of blame onto other countries does not hide. if the eu is responsible for just over 10% of global emissions, as the report says, the truth is that its per capita emissions are about twice those of china or five times those of india, to name just two examples that are often cited. but the discussion of reduction targets is useless if it is dissociated from the means to achieve those targets. in this respect, it should be said that the dominant approach to the problem of climate change - which the report takes up - has been truncated in essential respects and, above all, skewed by so-called market solutions and the insistence on emissions trading. several examples disprove the virtuousness of market regulation. the same number of projects demonstrate the effectiveness of regulation and targeted investment, particularly in terms of environmental impact and protection. the same applies to the necessary transition to a low-carbon economy.

in writing. the european cohesion funds play a key role in maintaining the balance of the european area. projects supported by these funds at regional level contribute to pan-european objectives in areas such as economic growth, research, environmental protection, sustainable energy supply, social cohesion, and even cross-border development. this report is therefore of great relevance in view of the forward-looking analysis it proposes for the period after 2013. cohesion policies favour the principle of good governance at macro, micro and intergovernmental level, which i fully agree with. i believe that these instruments are crucial to reducing interregional disparities and that in an increasingly interconnected and interdependent europe, these disparities cannot take place. in this post-2013 improvement perspective, i stress the need to identify rigorously the priorities for european investment, as well as rigorous analysis of macro-regional strategies. i consider it imperative that the funds be managed in accordance with rigorous evaluation and constant financial control throughout the life of each project. a more balanced and developed european area requires a dynamic approach from european leaders to investment priorities and to european cohesion policy itself.
in writing. - the cohesion of the european union is increasingly being called into question in a variety of ways, with some even calling for its dissolution in the face of so many disintegrating pressures. i do not share this pessimism and i believe that if europe does not abandon its core values, it may be able to emerge from this crisis strengthened. but the task is extremely difficult and it puts a strain on one of the principles that contributed to its initial success: cohesion. without its promotion, each part of the union will tend to stick only to its own particular interests and lose the notion of solidarity and mutual help that is so necessary in a political and economic space that is desired in increasing integration. cohesion policy has reduced many of the asymmetries between the different regions of europe, but it is fair to acknowledge that disparities are still very large. if we abandon this solidarity dimension and lose the overall concept which must guide our structural policies, europe will lose an essential instrument for its construction and strengthening. i believe that cohesion policy can be based on promoting concrete results and providing the means to achieve them.
in writing. − with a view to consolidating the european construction and making its values and principles a reality, the need for a cohesion policy with adequate financial, technical and legislative resources is an absolute priority in defining the strategy for the future of the european union and in asserting it in the global context. in the face of the challenges currently posed by the economic, financial and social crisis, cohesion policy should be strengthened in order to ensure greater conditions for supporting and developing disadvantaged regions, which will be decisive in ensuring the effective implementation of the eu 2020 strategy and better ensuring the achievement of the objectives set out, in particular in terms of reducing school drop-out, increasing higher education qualifications, increasing the labour force and employment rates, reducing poverty and increasing local investment in environmental projects. it is important that cohesion policy is simple in its implementation and has the necessary flexibility. in addition, it is important that co-financing rates are increased for member states in financial difficulties so that the financial envelopes at their disposal are effectively used.
in writing. - this report starts from wrong premises, which then affects its whole development and some of its central ideas. the reality of the eu today, and particularly the difficulties faced by countries such as greece, ireland and portugal, clearly demonstrates the failure of the cohesion objectives, which have been enshrined in the treaties over the years. cohesion has not failed because of the crisis; the crisis - and the different impact it had in the various member states - is also an expression of the failure of cohesion. some of the points raised in the report are of great concern. on the one hand, a new intermediate category for objective 1 of cohesion - convergence - is called for for regions whose gdp per capita is between 75% and 90% of the eu average. the commission also proposes to strengthen objectives 2 (regional competitiveness and employment) and 3 (european territorial cooperation). as we have always said, the creation of new objectives or the strengthening of existing ones must necessarily be accompanied by an increase in the financial means to achieve them. the other objectives, in this case the convergence of the least developed regions (with a gdp per capita below 75% of the eu average), would be sacrificed.

in writing. - cohesion policy is a key policy for the future of the european union. cohesion policy is a structural policy which aims to help reduce the disparities between the levels of development of the various european regions and which should pay particular attention to the most disadvantaged regions and those with a special status, such as the outermost regions. the territorial dimension is one of the novelties of the lisbon treaty and henceforth, in particular in cohesion policy for the period 2014 to 2020, a more appropriate response must be found to contribute to the development of the regions. it is in this context that i voted in favour of the european commission's proposal to create an intermediate category of regions, including european regions whose gdp is between 75% and 90% of the european average, which would replace the current system of phasing in and phasing out, and which would not compromise the other categories of objectives 1, 2 and 3. i believe that cohesion policy exists for all european regions and i would argue that this should be the main priority of this policy in the next multiannual framework.

in writing. − budget support is now one of the most important forms of aid to developing countries, with commitments for budget support from the european commission amounting to €13 billion in 2003-09. while this mechanism makes up for the shortcomings of other types of support such as project/grant support, it also raises some doubts about its effectiveness, namely the existence of a direct link between the poverty reduction objective (and development policy within the meaning of the lisbon treaty) and these financial transfers to the treasuries of the beneficiary countries. in line with the demands always made by the ep, i believe it is imperative, from the outset, that this support be linked to respect for the rights and minimum standards of governance (which is not always the case), strict control by the commission of cases of misappropriation and waste of funds, transparency of public expenditure in the partner country, reduction of poverty in all its dimensions and the use of these resources in a progressive manner and in parallel with an effective political and strategic dialogue. i therefore support the creation of a multilateral system, involving national parliaments and civil society, to monitor budget support.
in writing. − this report analyses the future of eu budget support to developing countries, following the publication by the commission of a green paper on the same subject. the practical implementation of these policies and their budgetary support require european leaders to constantly monitor, evaluate and restructure them, if necessary. the report points to some shortcomings in these areas, stating that the mechanisms for monitoring by the commission in the scrutiny of the measures implemented or to be supported should be strengthened, also involving the national parliaments of the states to which the support is intended. the nature of these policies as a key instrument to support poverty eradication makes a large-scale involvement of civil society and national parliaments absolutely necessary. the political dialogue achieved should be about these issues, but also about the annual budget review. as we can see in the report, the 2006 oecd assessment showed that the impact of these policies in countries such as malawi, mozambique, nicaragua and uganda, among others, had a positive effect in terms of strengthening good governance, implementing national poverty reduction plans and improving accountability.
in writing. − the european union has a wealth of experience in the conduct of development aid processes and procedures. despite the added value of european support for the poorest countries, they must not only be recipients of aid but also partners and be held accountable as such. no matter how much money or other help is given to them, there will have to be a commitment on their part to transparency and good management. for such transparency to be effective and verifiable, it is essential to involve national parliaments and civil society in the debate on the management of aid received and to make this debate a central element of the annual political life of developing countries. the awareness that what should be for all is only for some, undermines social bonds and degrades the already fragile social capital of weaker societies. the union should not slow down its development aid effort but should introduce mechanisms, such as budget support, which enable european taxpayers and potential recipients in developing countries to know how it has been used, for what purpose and what the result has been.
in writing. − regardless of the time and the reason, any budgetary programme of investment or financial support must be preceded by rigor, transparency and a good assessment of its sustainability, along with guarantees of correct and efficient use and application of funds, in the interests of the beneficiaries. this is the direction in which the policy of support for developing countries should be directed. independent evaluations have shown that, on the whole, the programmes have benefited the beneficiary countries and their populations and that it will be advisable to continue them. however, they have reservations about the impact of the aid on poverty reduction and the consolidation of democracy in the beneficiary countries. on the other hand, these countries are largely independent of aid. i therefore support a clear definition of criteria, a strong focus on the endogenous development and regional integration of the beneficiary countries, and the clarification of the compensation for the contributing countries and institutions.
in writing. − the need to ensure the correct and transparent use of eu funds for budget support to developing countries is not in question. but we must not confuse technical questions - which we must place in the context of the necessary checks and audits, which should ideally be carried out by the developing countries themselves, for which they should have technical cooperation and training - with political options and assessments. the choices of developing countries in this last field should be respected, without impositions (explicit or veiled). the report is contradictory in this respect. on the one hand, it points out that budget support should not be used to serve the eu's particular economic and strategic interests - which deserves our full agreement. it is also clear that the eu should be aware of the added value of its enormous political weight and the potential importance of its action, and hence its leverage, so that its political influence is commensurate with the financial aid it provides. it also states that one of the eu's objectives is to encourage a social market economy, and that this principle also applies to development policy. these are among the most negative aspects of the report.

in writing. − the reduction of poverty and, in the long term, its eradication, is the primary objective of the european union's development policy. budget support is therefore a good instrument for providing such aid, but it is very important that it be used in parallel with effective political and strategic dialogue and with the imposition of conditions. only in this way can we ensure that the european union's foreign and security policy is directed towards the promotion of democracy and human rights, peace and security, which are essential prerequisites for sustainable development. more systematic efforts are also needed to give greater prominence to measures relating to climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction.
in writing. − budget support refers to the transfer of financial resources from an external funding body to the national treasury of a partner country, which has fulfilled the agreed payment conditions. the financial resources thus received shall then form part of the partner country's general resources and shall therefore be used in accordance with its public financial management system. this mechanism has been in existence since the marshall plan and became popular in the 1980s and 1990s when the world bank and various bilateral cooperatives began to provide budget support in the form of balance of payments aid. the nature of the aid mechanism requires the entities involved to seek ways of monitoring the effective application of these funds. in this context, the european parliament has made it politically imperative to grant aid only to countries which meet minimum standards of governance and respect for human rights. the impact of the aid granted is large and includes three portuguese-speaking countries, namely: cape verde, mozambique and guinea-bissau. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the european budget is one of the most important instruments for helping developing countries. the use of the fund for the reduction and eradication of poverty and the implementation of the millennium development goals (mdgs) should be guided by principles of transparency in its use. given that financial transfers are made directly to the treasuries of developing countries, respect for human rights and minimum standards of governance must be ensured. the creation of control systems involving parliaments and civil society can ensure greater effectiveness in the fight against transparency and corruption, without compromising the interests of the population. for these reasons, i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. - budget support (bsa) to developing third countries is one of the cornerstones of the common foreign policy. but it is not enough to simply provide financial aid to improve local institutions. indeed, according to the data available, it is difficult even to assess the impact of the current ao measures, since, for example, a certain feeling of dependence of the local states on the support granted is generated, which suggests that there is no structural progress. for example, there is a fear that the cut in aid will consequently imply a breakdown in the provision of basic services. the european parliament does not, however, dispute the goodness of such measures; the commission is committed to its good direction and demands that the criteria laid down for its provision be followed, based on objective analyses, so as to contribute to the consolidation of local structures which are oriented towards respect for the inviolability of the person. this suggests, at the very least, an active stance on the part of the union, acting as a political agent committed to the global political scene.
in writing. − the eu's role in development aid, the second largest donor in the world, takes many forms. budget support (bsa) is one of the methods and is carried out by transferring financial resources from an external body directly to the public accounts of a third country. the oa thus reinforces the concepts of ownership and enhanced partnership, since it imposes on the governments of third countries more responsibility for the commitments they have made and the strengthening of mutual cooperation to achieve the objectives of the policies and strategies they have put forward. this also allows for greater coordination between donor countries and greater harmonisation of procedures. the effectiveness of the oa in the development of the countries concerned is evident in several reports and assessments of the commission. however, it is necessary to clarify the eligibility criteria, which differ between beneficiary countries, to promote the participatory development of civil society in monitoring the expenditure and impact of this modality, and to strengthen coordination between member states' bilateral aid, between the eu and other international organisations. the transversal nature of the problems requires greater coherence between the various development support policies, adjusted on a case-by-case basis according to the specificities of the countries.

in writing. the prevailing view in this report is that the development of energy infrastructure is done within the framework of market economy paradigms. in this way it is part of the process of pursuing the third package of the internal energy market and is another step in that direction. its objective is to enable the free exchange of energy on all transmission interconnectors between countries and/or different tariff zones, i.e. the liberalisation of the energy market. we do not share this view and we oppose it head-on. without prejudice to necessary and desirable measures of cooperation in this field, the development of energy infrastructure should be the responsibility of each member state, taking into account its specific characteristics and needs and the interests of its population, its productive sectors and its economy. it should have a public framework, management and ownership as a means of ensuring a genuine public service of energy supply. the report, on the contrary, states that community public funds allocated to support infrastructure development projects will be channelled to projects of european interest, i.e. those which contribute to the completion of the internal energy market, increase integration, competition and market liquidity. a path that has already proved to be profoundly negative for a number of countries and their populations.
in writing. - we cannot accept the development of energy infrastructure on a market basis, which is another step in the continuation of the third package of the internal energy market, as the report says. its objective is to enable the free exchange of energy on all transmission interconnectors between countries and/or different tariff zones, i.e. the liberalisation of the energy market. the development of energy infrastructure should be the responsibility of each member state as public property contributing to a public energy supply service. but the report says that public funds from the community to support infrastructure development projects will be channelled to projects of european interest, i.e. those which contribute to the completion of the internal energy market ... increase integration, competition and market liquidity. the insistence on the policy of liberalization and the private energy market has already proved to be extremely negative, both in the increase in unemployment and the multiplication of technical problems, both in the price of energy for the consumer, both in its consequences for the increase in energy poverty, and in the increase in the escalation of energy dependence in which some member states are putting themselves. that is why we voted against the report.

in writing. - public services of universal access, regardless of the economic conditions of each individual, are an important social achievement, inseparable from the civilizational advances made in europe throughout the 20th century, the result of the social struggle of workers and peoples. they are an integral part of the course of progress that this struggle has opened in countless countries. when these public services are called into question today, it is really a matter of a regression of civilization. in the eu which started by changing their name to social services of general interest (ssigs) this is the way forward. we agree with most of the proposals put forward by the rapporteur. however, unacceptable points have been introduced in the report, relating to the privatisation and liberalisation of the gis, which we reject. this means that the final resolution has obvious contradictions, even if there are positive aspects and a progressive view in certain respects. but what is missing is the central issue we advocate for the concept of public services - public ownership and public management, with the democratic participation of users in these public services - in areas essential to the well-being of populations, namely health, education, communications, transport, energy, etc.

in writing. − one of the eu's main objectives is to constantly improve the living and working conditions and well-being of its people. this objective can only be achieved through the sustainable development of europe, based on balanced economic growth, a highly competitive social market economy geared to supporting small and medium-sized enterprises, aiming at full employment and social progress, protecting and improving the quality of the environment, combating social exclusion, discrimination and inequalities in access to health care and promoting social justice and protection, as well as equality between men and women, solidarity between generations and protection of the rights of the child. in order to achieve these ambitious objectives, social services of general interest are essential. therefore, only the provision of universal, accessible, portable and high-quality sgeis, in line with the commission's 2007 communication on services of general interest, can be considered as an essential pillar of the european social model and the basis for a good quality of life and for the achievement of the eu's economic, social and employment objectives.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the future of social services of general interest. social services of general interest cover compulsory and complementary social security schemes and universal services directly provided to the citizen, with a view to improving the quality of life for all. these services play a preventive and social inclusion and cohesion role and give effect to the fundamental social rights proclaimed in the european charter of fundamental rights and the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms. there is a broad european consensus that social services of general interest are essential for the well-being of our peoples and for an efficient economy and, although progress has been made in overcoming the difficulties created by the application of eu standards to the provision and development of social services of general interest, there is still no consensus within the commission and the council, or between these two institutions, on further practical measures to overcome the obstacles identified by stakeholders. this report seeks to identify measures to ensure that social objectives are achieved and are not undermined by the application of the single market rules.
in writing. − in recent years, relative confidence in the provision of social services of general interest (ssig) has eroded. the recent economic crisis has highlighted some of the structural weaknesses of the states, casting a general suspicion on their economic capacity to guarantee a wide range of social benefits to citizens. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the health of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a welcome step towards the creation of a european health insurance system. regardless of the solution found, there are data to be taken for granted: the gics are of substantial economic importance; the commission has also proposed that the member states should be required to provide information on the implementation of the community's environmental policy, and that the information should be requested not only from state authorities but also from associations, social enterprises and even private enterprises, and that the process of setting priorities in this area should be ensured by involving a number of non-state parent entities in order to find the most appropriate solutions to achieve the proposed objectives.
in writing. − social services of general interest (ssgis) are a fundamental pillar of the european social model, ensuring social, economic and territorial cohesion and at the same time making an important economic contribution in terms of employment, economic activity and the well-being of european citizens. the main objective of this report, in addition to promoting legal clarity and imposing flexibility, is to highlight the need to modernise the gis, with a focus on its accessibility, universality, equity, quality and effectiveness, with particular attention to the most disadvantaged groups. it should be noted that the sovereign crisis, by imposing cuts in the various member states, should not jeopardise the development of the gssi, in particular the social services supporting children and the elderly, education, health and essential network services, which function as a preventive driving force for social inclusion and poverty reduction. i support the principle of subsidiarity in this particular case, since it is the national, regional and local authorities who know the reality for the provision of the gss. however, i would stress that the eu must make efforts to modernise and adapt them to the dimension of the european social model, which itself needs to be re-thinked.

in writing. - i support this proposal, based on article 77 (2) tfeu (border issues), as it should be an added value as a legislative act of the union, in particular by ensuring the security of border guards, who are assisted by the right to check travel documents at the external borders. i agree with the rapporteur that the proposed text would respect the competence of the member states for the purpose of recognising travel documents. in accordance with the convention implementing the schengen agreement of 14 june 1985, decisions sch/com-ex (98) 56 and sch/com-ex (99) 14 relate to the creation of a manual on travel documents which entitle the holder to cross the external borders and on which visas may be affixed. however, these decisions date back to the period of intergovernmental schengen cooperation and need to be adapted to the current institutional and legal framework of the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i agree that, in accordance with the convention implementing the schengen agreement of 14 june 1985, decisions sch/com-ex (98) 56 and sch/com-ex (99) 14 relate to the creation of a manual on travel documents which entitle the holder to cross the external borders and on which bets can be made. however, these decisions date back to the period of intergovernmental schengen cooperation and need to be adapted to the current institutional and legal framework of the european union. since the purpose of the decision is to create legal certainty as regards the list of documents, this declaration proposes to clarify the consequences of the failure to notify the position of a member state within the prescribed period. this provision is consistent with the exclusive competence of the member states for the purpose of recognition of travel documents, as they will always have the right to notify their non-recognition of such documents.
in writing. − the travel document framework allows border control authorities to check whether a particular document is recognised for the purpose of crossing external borders and consular staff to check whether all member states applying the common visa policy recognise a particular document for the purpose of affixing the visa sticker. the current framework needs to be adapted to the new institutional and legal framework of the eu. the fact that member states are not obliged to indicate whether or not they recognise each of the documents listed creates legal uncertainty as the holders of those travel documents risk being refused entry or having a visa limited in territorial scope. harmonisation of the recognition of travel documents is not possible as it falls within the exclusive competence of the member states, but it is necessary to ensure that the list is kept up to date. i support the creation of a mechanism to ensure the constant updating of the list of travel documents issued by countries and the introduction of a centralised mechanism for the technical evaluation of these documents. at the same time, it should be ensured that all member states express their position on whether or not to recognise the listed travel documents.
in writing. - while the union does not want to be a strong europe, it is obviously necessary to guard against entry at its external borders and to provide that documents issued by third states are suitable to allow their nationals to enter the european area. the union should therefore list those who have such a capacity, and the member states will have to keep the list of those who have such a capacity up to date so that they can inform others of their acceptance or refusal, so that the border services can know about them and those seeking to enter the schengen area can know what documents they must carry. the decisions taken in this respect in the past need to be adapted to the present european institutional and legal framework. legal certainty, but also respect for border officials and all those who travel to our territory, requires such information.
in writing. − this report represents an effort by the european parliament to harmonise regulatory procedures and standards by the member states of the european union, with a view to adapting to the new institutional and legal framework of the eu. the list of travel documents allows border control authorities to verify whether a particular travel document is recognised for the purpose of crossing the external borders in accordance with the legislation in force and also allows consular staff to verify whether all member states recognise a particular travel document for the purpose of affixing the visa sticker. i believe that it is necessary to ensure the continuous updating of the list of travel documents by requiring member states to notify their position on whether or not to recognise these documents for the sake of simplification and efficiency. i would also stress the concern to ensure the safety of border guards and the fact that this decision does not affect the competence of the member states to recognise travel documents.
in writing. the report deals with a proposal for a decision on the list of travel documents which allow the crossing of external borders and on which visas may be issued and the establishment of a mechanism for drawing up this list. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the transport of dangerous goods by road. it is for the latter to confirm whether a particular document is recognised for cross-border purposes. we are faced with a proposal that is not without contradictions. on the one hand, it may facilitate the verification of a given travel document by the control authorities. but on the other hand, the proposal is centralising, it gives too many powers to the commission in this area, which can be done at the expense of the rights of the member states in respect of matters important to their sovereignty.
in writing. the report deals with a proposal for a decision on the list of travel documents which allow the crossing of external borders and on which visas may be issued and the establishment of a mechanism for drawing up this list. however, under the pretext of ensuring uniform conditions for the collection and updating of the list of travel documents, they want powers to be delegated to the commission. it is for the latter to confirm whether a particular document is recognised for cross-border purposes. so we are faced with a proposal with some contradictions. on the one hand, it may facilitate the verification of a given travel document by the control authorities. but on the other hand it gives too much power to the european commission in this area, which can be done at the expense of the rights of the member states in matters which are important for their sovereignty.
in writing. − the control of external borders is essential for the security of the eu, and we therefore consider that a strict definition of the list of travel documents allowing such control is necessary. this list should be common to all member states, despite their exclusive competence for the recognition of travel documents.
in writing. - i have approved this report on the proposal for a european parliament and council decision on the list of travel documents which allow the crossing of external borders and on which visas may be affixed and the establishment of a mechanism to draw up such a list. i welcome the rapporteur's well-structured report from the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs. the recognition of travel documents cannot be harmonised, as it falls within the exclusive competence of the member states. however, it is necessary to ensure that the list is kept up to date. i also support the creation of a mechanism to ensure the constant updating of the list of travel documents issued by countries and the introduction of a centralised mechanism for the technical evaluation of these documents. i believe that it should be ensured that all member states are able to express their position on whether or not to recognise the travel documents listed, since this falls within their exclusive competence.
in writing. - the rules on travel documents authorising their holders to cross external borders, laid down in the convention implementing the schengen agreement of 14 june 1985, need to be harmonised in the light of the new community legal framework. in this respect, the defence of legal certainty and security must take precedence: states must have at their disposal the means of ascertaining whether a document satisfies the requirements for crossing borders and whether a document is recognised in all member states. it is therefore reasonable to require a list of binding documents to take the form of a community legislative act. in a matter of such importance for the security of the common space, the first priority must be the application of the law.

in writing. the proposal for a directive, which is now undergoing its second reading, aims to facilitate the enforcement of penalties against motorists who, in a member state other than their own, have committed an offence of speeding, drunk driving, failure to use a seatbelt or disregard for a red traffic light. road safety and efforts to reduce the number of accidents and fatalities on the roads are extremely important issues, and many of these accidents are caused by a large proportion of the infringements that the directive identifies. however, reducing these numbers and promoting road safety is most effectively achieved through prevention, which is based on the concrete and differentiated reality in each country. while it is true that measures are needed to combat impunity in cases where the offender is in a member state other than the one in which he resides, excessive harmonisation of security measures at eu level, such as the harmonisation of traffic rules, monitoring procedures through the installation of monitoring and surveillance equipment, which offer little guarantee in terms of the protection of personal data, cannot be a panacea for all ills.
in writing. − the adoption of these new rules will make it easier to enforce penalties against motorists who have committed in another eu country an offence of speeding, driving while intoxicated or under the influence of drugs, failure to wear a seatbelt, unlawful use of a mobile phone, driving in a restricted lane, not wearing a safety helmet or disregarding a red light. the exchange of data between member states through the eucaris system (an intergovernmental network initially intended for cooperation against organised crime) and the obligation to inform drivers are reinforced in this new directive, which should be transposed into national legislation within two years. the directive aims to end impunity for motorists who commit road traffic offences in other eu member states.
in writing. − the 36% reduction in the number of fatalities between 2001 and 2009 in the european union fell short of the target set by the eu in 2001 following the publication of the green paper on european transport policy to reduce the number of fatalities to half the average recorded at that time. this directive aims to institutionalise the exchange of information between member states on vehicle registration plates, also allowing for the adjudication of serious road accidents throughout the union and ensuring equality before the law for citizens, irrespective of the member state in which they live. i believe that the roads in the union will be safer when the directive is implemented, and this is a very important first step towards increasing road safety. under the new system, the authorities of the country where the crime was committed will be able to send a letter to notify the offender of the type of offence and the applicable sanctions, as well as possible solutions and legal consequences of the act. the application of fines shall be determined in accordance with the rules of the member state where the offence was committed. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the white paper on european transport policy, presented in 2001, set the objective of halving the number of deaths from road accidents by 2010. the data, however, point to a 36% reduction, short of the target. however, some studies point to a disproportionate proportion of accidents caused by non-residents, caused mainly by speeding. this is due to the difficulty of applying the penalties associated with failure to comply with road rules. the rapporteur warns that this situation can be detrimental to residents of a member state, putting at risk the confidence of national citizens in the virtualities of the community. the european parliament has therefore set itself the task of seeking to strengthen the exchange of information between the various member states, not only in the exchange of data enabling the offender to be identified, but also in the application of penalties for non-compliance with road traffic rules.
in writing. − road safety on european roads is one of the union's major priorities. the ambitious target of reducing the number of road deaths by more than half by 2010 was not met. as portugal is the second country in the eu with the highest number of road deaths, i voted in favour of this report, stressing that more action is urgently needed to strengthen the penalties for non-resident drivers in the various member states. i regret that the ep's proposal was rejected at first reading and that this document focuses mainly on the exchange of data between member states by amending the legal basis which will simultaneously allow three states to opt out of this directive. the use of the eucaris system as a tool for managing data on the many offences should also be reconsidered, since its primary purpose is cooperation against organised crime and terrorism. the loss of life on europe's roads must be countered by concrete measures to hold offenders accountable. the next step should be to extend the scope of the infringements.

in writing. − our deep disagreement with the financial perspectives 2007-13, which represented a major cut in the eu budget, is well known. the lisbon strategy and foreign policy have been given priority over the structural and cohesion funds. it is now clearly unable to cope with the economic, social and environmental situation facing the eu, with increased inequalities and therefore also increased cohesion needs. with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, it was stipulated that the council would adopt the regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework after the approval of the european parliament and that the institutions would work together to find a solution with a view to adopting the mff. this new framework is the reason for the rapporteur's position of rejecting the draft council regulation which is nothing more than the regulation of the agreement concluded in 2006 on the grounds that parliament's new powers are not safeguarded. for our part, we reiterate that the mff must give the utmost priority to responding to the serious social problems created by the economic and social crisis, with a significant increase in the community budget to support economic and social cohesion.

in writing. − i welcome this report, agreeing with the rapporteur's view that, on the one hand, a review of the roadmap started in 2005 is welcome, but that, nevertheless, the need to maintain the tight tse measures and monitoring mechanisms is stressed. animal health and consumer protection must be kept as guiding principles for any future action.
in writing. − tses include serious diseases such as bovine spongiform encephalopathy (bse), which reached epidemic proportions in the eu in the mid-1990s due to the feeding of contaminated processed animal protein to cattle. this disease is transmissible to humans by the oral route, then taking the form of creutzfeld-jakob disease, which leads to deterioration of brain tissue and ultimately death. following the epidemic of the 1990s and the social alarm it caused, numerous measures were taken in the eu to control the spread of bse, which were successful and actually led to a decrease in the prevalence of the disease. the success of the measures taken should not lead us to slow down in the control and prevention of the disease, but rather to recognise the importance of these measures and to maintain them, even if they are adequately revised and adapted to the present situation.
in writing. - having regard to the need and importance of the primacy of food safety, i voted in favour of this report. in the context of the global economy and in view of the impact of contagion and epidemics, in particular as regards transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (tses) a family of diseases occurring in humans and animals and characterised by degeneration of brain tissue resulting in a spongiform appearance and eventually leading to death, as was the case with bovine spongiform encephalopathy, popularly known as mad cow disease it is necessary to maintain a strict and efficient control and surveillance regime for feed and food, which is able to reduce risks and ensure better conditions for the prevention of new diseases or outbreaks. it is in this context that we are seeing a sharp decline in the incidence of transmissible spongiform encephalopathies, and action must be taken to eradicate them.
in writing. - we all remember the social alarm caused in the mid-1990s by the epidemic proportions of bovine spongiform encephalopathy, a type of transmissible spongiform encephalopathy, which is also the human variant, creutzfeldt-jakob disease, in the eu. the proportion of the disease transmitted by an agent called prion, an abnormal form of protein has its proximate cause in the feeding of livestock contaminated processed animal protein. the report, based on commission proposals, takes the view that the prevalence of the disease has been substantially reduced (2167 cases in 2001 to 67 in 2009) as a result of the implementation of a set of legislative measures aimed at its eradication, and proposes an adaptation of the legislative provisions currently in force. the care and demands with which it does so seem to us justified and appropriate. we stress the importance of maintaining strict rules in the area of food prohibition. the root causes of this epidemic, as well as other food safety and public health problems, lie in the intensive production models that have been promoted in the eu, to the detriment of extensive production models that have consumer health, environmental safety and animal welfare at their core.

in writing. − transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (tses) are at the root of a number of diseases, including creutzfeldt-jakob disease, which affects humans. in order to combat the first epidemic of bse (the bovine variant of tse), the european parliament and the council adopted a series of control and prevention measures in 2001. at this stage, it is noted that the number of cases of this disease has decreased in recent years, reflecting the relative success of the measures taken. however, as the rapporteur rightly points out, as long as scientific knowledge does not allow us to guarantee that there is no danger of the preventive measures being withdrawn, the precautionary principle must prevail, given the risks to human health of a possible new outbreak.

in writing. − the issue of civil aviation safety has been at the top of the eu's priorities. several initiatives were adopted to create an integrated approach to aviation safety in order to achieve a high level of safety for citizens. body scanners are being seen as an additional tool for protection, with an increasing number of member states - finland, the netherlands, france, italy and the united kingdom - using body scanners to increase the detection capacity of prohibited objects, such as explosives, liquids or plastics, which cannot be detected by current metal detectors. i support the idea that there should be a common level of protection for citizens and that european regulations should be adopted, to be applied to member states opting for the use of this method of screening, containing common technical standards and operating conditions that ensure the minimum of risks inherent in the protection of personal data, the privacy and dignity of passengers and human health. passengers shall be provided with adequate information on all aspects of the use of scanners and be offered a realistic alternative to these controls. workers responsible for the use of scanners should be subject to appropriate training and a code of conduct.

in writing. - aviation safety is obviously a matter of the utmost importance, both for workers and for passengers. however, it seems to us necessary to guarantee this security without compromising the rights, freedoms and guarantees of individuals. the document adopted by the majority of this parliament, following the widespread panic about the terrorist escalation, aims to implement the body scanning method at european level. the report stresses its speed and effectiveness, and in a game of waist concerns, it tries to answer the fundamental question: that this method is a real attack on the dignity and privacy of passengers. moreover, although the report does not mention it, its effectiveness is disputed. however, the report does not omit all the risks associated with these devices. in advocating the use of scanners, it does not fail to recognise that cumulative exposure to doses of ionising radiation cannot be acceptable, as it increases the risk of skin cancer. it is equally unacceptable that this solution should still be defended. another worrying issue is the difficulty in guaranteeing passengers effective protection of their data and images generated by the scanners, a situation which could once again constitute a violation of dignity and privacy.

in writing. − demographic ageing is a challenge for society and for all generations in the european union. it is essential that european social models take account of their effects. i therefore voted in favour of the report on the european year of active ageing to be held in 2012. this initiative aims at creating a culture of active ageing throughout life in the european union based on a society for all ages. promoting active ageing means creating better opportunities for older citizens to play their role in the labour market, combating poverty, encouraging active participation in family life and society, promoting solidarity and cooperation between generations and encouraging ageing in dignity. active ageing also contributes to achieving a high level of employment in the european union and optimising opportunities for health and participation in society in order to improve the quality of life as people age.
in writing. - population ageing is one of the most important challenges that europe is facing and will face. increasing life expectancy and improving health conditions now allow people to live better and longer, increasing the proportion of the non-active population, while the birth rate, which has stagnated since the 1980s, does not allow the active population to replenish itself, creating difficulties for social security systems. eurostat projections foresee a decline of around 6.8% in the number of people of working age by 2030, with only two workers being able to afford a pension (currently the ratio is 4 to 1). this, as you can see, poses serious problems for the sustainability of the system. that is why, in the knowledge that people are getting older today, we need to find ways of ensuring active, independent and healthy ageing, by ensuring that people over 65 remain in the labour market or take on other forms of social intervention, whether in volunteering or in the family, thus freeing up public resources and constituting a real added value for societies.
in writing. − the ageing of the population is one of the major political challenges facing the european union. as 2012 is the european year for active ageing, urgent and concerted action is needed to affirm europe as a society for all ages and to put people at the centre of politics, society and the economy. in the context of the eu 2020 strategy, effective and concrete action by the european union and the member states is required, not least because there is already a high rate of unemployment among young people and the difficulty of financing pension schemes is already felt. if the current demographic trend is maintained, there will be a profound change in the structure of the population and the age pyramid within a few years. by 2050, the number of young people aged 0-14 will increase from 100 million to 66 million and the working age population will increase from 331 million to 268 million. in addition, the number of people aged over 80 will increase from 4.1% in 2005 to 11.4% in 2050. i am in favour of an integrated response based on the promotion of equity and solidarity between generations, on the link between pension systems, the budget, debt, as well as health care, rehabilitation, promotion of births, family protection and anti-discrimination policies.
in writing. − 2012 has been proclaimed by the european commission as the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations. a vague concept such as active ageing can encompass very different conceptions, as is evident from the contradictions presented in the report. on the one hand, it emphasises the need for better employment opportunities, the promotion of better health and safety conditions at work for older workers, more active family policies and addresses the issue of people with disabilities and chronic illnesses. on the other hand, there is a cross-cutting defence of the increase in the retirement age, adding that one of the effects of demographic ageing will be the change in european social models. the pressure on health, social and pension systems must therefore be reduced. we cannot support the theses which aim to align the retirement age with the average life expectancy (in its most fundamentalist versions), which constitutes an intolerable civilizational setback, contradictory even to the fight against unemployment. these tend to ignore factors such as the possibilities opened up by scientific and technological progress and its profound impacts on increasing labour productivity, and instead seek enhanced conditions for the exploitation of the labour force.
in writing. − the european commission intends to make 2012 the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations, using a vague concept of active ageing that can encompass many conceptions, including some against older people, as is evident in the contradictions in the report. on the one hand, it emphasises the need for better employment opportunities, better health and safety conditions at work for older workers, more cooperation between younger workers through training of young workers by older workers and volunteering so that older workers can share their skills, insisting on more active policies in the area of the family and raising the issue of people with disabilities and chronic diseases. on the other hand, there is a cross-cutting defence of increasing the retirement age, stressing that healthy ageing can contribute to older people participating more in the labour market, staying active in society for longer. it adds that one of the effects of demographic ageing will be to change european social models, aiming to reduce the pressure on health, social action and pension systems. we disagree with this view, which is to punish the elderly by prolonging their lives, which also harms the young and contributes to increasing unemployment.
in writing. − the ageing of the population is one of the most important challenges facing the european union, but it is also one of the greatest opportunities. for these reasons, the ageing of the population could be seen as a major challenge, not to say a risk, or it could offer new opportunities for european society, depending on how we prepare for it. one of the keys to overcoming this challenge is to ensure that people aged close to 60 and over remain longer in the labour market, continue to be active participants in society and remain healthy and independent for as long as possible. it is therefore a challenge for which european society must prepare itself, and if done well and well in advance, it could be an opportunity for europe to prosper more rapidly and with a greater degree of social cohesion between generations.

in writing. - the general ageing of the population is a phenomenon common to the european union, where considerable changes will be seen over the next 20 years. over the period 1995-2015, the 20-29 age group is estimated to lose 11 million people (-20%), while the 50-64 age group will increase by 16.5 million (+25%). i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that europe must take a growing interest in the active and healthy ageing of its citizens by defining programmatic actions to stimulate greater independence, accident prevention, rehabilitation after illness and the practice of sporting activities throughout europe. the european year for active ageing should also be an opportunity to establish greater intergenerational solidarity, as the exchange of knowledge between older people and young people will allow, on the one hand, to increase the skills and competences of future generations and, on the other hand, to enhance the life experience of older people. it should also be a year designed to make european businesses aware of the importance of developing new products and services that meet the special needs of this specific sector of the population.

in writing. - freedom of movement within the european union is one of the most remarkable features of the process of integration between the member states and one of the most emblematic of the good that this process has brought. the restriction of this freedom would be a setback to which our peoples would have difficulty getting used to again. however, it is undeniable that the freedom to move freely throughout the union and the end of internal border constraints have created problems for several member states, which are faced in many cases with illegal immigration. we must therefore seek balanced solutions to this problem without definitively calling into question a value so dear to europeans, which is essential for the maintenance of an area of genuine freedom, security and justice. it is also necessary to strengthen the capacity of member states to control external borders, to assess how they apply the schengen acquis and to seek to adopt best practices with a view to enhancing solidarity and information sharing, thereby enhancing its objectives, preventing abuses and preventing situations of border tension.

in writing. the scheme for the distribution of food to the most deprived, set up in 1987 under the cap, currently provides food aid to 13 million people in poverty in 19 member states and involves some 240 food banks and charities in the distribution chains. in the eu, 43 million people are at risk of food poverty, according to the commission's own estimates, a figure which will tend to increase due to the economic and financial crisis and the sharp rise in food prices. we must therefore try to avoid an immediate and drastic reduction in food aid as a result of the reduction in the funding of the programme from 500 million to 113 million euro. the interruption of this aid programme, without prior warning or preparation, has serious repercussions for the most vulnerable eu citizens. it is therefore necessary to find a way to continue the scheme of food distribution to the most deprived persons in 2012 and 2013 (the remaining years of the current funding period) and also in the new funding period 2014-2020.

in writing. − in 1999, the estimated number of victims of antipersonnel landmines was 18 000 people, and in 2009 it had fallen to approximately 4000, of whom 70% are civilians and one third are children. this is therefore a serious situation to which the international community cannot remain indifferent, especially when some states continue to use anti-personnel landmines, as is the case in burma and libya. according to the international community, and despite all the efforts made, there are still more than 90 countries affected by antipersonnel landmines, with afghanistan, colombia, pakistan, burma, cambodia and laos being the most severely affected. it is therefore urgent to continue the process of demining, in which the action of our american allies has been fundamental, both in sponsoring demining operations and in supporting programmes to assist victims, and to make every effort to ensure that governments abandon the use of anti-personnel landmines and accede to the anti-personnel mine ban treaty.
in writing. − in the context of defending the right to life and promoting peace, the fight against the eradication of mines and explosive devices for personal attack must be a priority action of the european union's external policy. despite the many positive advances that have been made in this area, we all recognise that there is still much work to be done. this is a problem that particularly affects victims in countries with high social and economic stress. given the specificities of these types of weapons in circulation and the lack of significant progress in explosives detection techniques and technologies, it is necessary to maintain financial support for this cause and to seek a more effective use of the resources available in mine action, in particular in the area of the recognition, detection, marking and removal of anti-personnel landmines and other explosive remnants of war, such as abandoned explosive ordnance, unexploded ordnance, cluster munition remnants and improvised explosive devices. i also support this report in calling for all countries to sign and comply with the ottawa convention on the prohibition of the use, stockpiling, production and transfer of antipersonnel mines and on their destruction.
in writing. - we know that the ottawa convention of 3 december 1997 on the prohibition of the use, stockpiling, production and transfer of antipersonnel mines and on their destruction, which entered into force on 1 march 1999, has been signed and ratified by 156 countries, including 25 eu member states. despite the efforts made in the fight against antipersonnel mines, 37 countries have not yet done so, including two in the european union, and we support the call for them to do so. on the other hand, as the report stresses, synergies must be found between the various dimensions of mine action, with particular emphasis on the humanitarian and development aspects and through the strengthening of local autonomy and participation in related projects, in order to better respond to the needs of the population directly affected. but we also cannot forget that this weapon, because it was cheaper, was used more by those who could not afford weapons of mass destruction, using more sophisticated technological means. the european union must be able to take action to prevent the spread of the disease and to prevent the spread of the disease.
in writing. - there is widespread support for the objective of a total ban and elimination of antipersonnel mines worldwide. i welcome the progress made in the field of mine action over the last decade. i share the concern expressed that efforts to this end need to be refocused and intensified to eliminate the threat of antipersonnel mines within a specific timeframe. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.

author. - madam president, recently at a meeting in jakarta, the representative of an indonesian human rights organization said: at the moment we have complete freedom of religion in indonesia, we can practice whatever religion we want, as long as it is not the ahmadiyya religion. there was a certain exaggeration in his statements because we know that other minorities are also at risk in indonesia, but this exaggeration was understandable because we were still in shock at the cikeusik massacre, in which three followers of this ahmadiyya religion, which considers itself muslim and which some fanatics do not want to be considered muslim, were killed. and here we have a serious problem: we know that most indonesians want peace and tolerance between religions and that's how they interpret the national principles of pancasila, but we also know that there is a minority that wants to speak for the whole of society and this is a very big challenge for the authorities. on the one hand, not to let a minority of fanatics try to take over the voice of society as a whole and, on the other hand, the government can clearly exercise a political repulsion towards such attempts and, from this point of view, i think it is very worrying that certain statements by the minister of religious affairs of indonesia have given the impression that the ahmadiyya religion is a religion that cannot declare itself muslim. i believe that if the indonesian government does not want the spirit of these fanatics to contaminate the rest of society, they must be very clear in their fight against intolerance and that is what we here in the european parliament are asking the indonesian authorities to do.
madam president, i lived in indonesia and i love indonesia. i know well the extraordinary progress that indonesia has made since the first free elections in 1999 in practising democracy and respect for human rights and civic and political freedoms. i believe that in europe we must appreciate – and i think we do in this resolution – how society in indonesia, now the third largest democracy and the largest muslim nation in the world, has firmly engraved in its fabric the values of diversity, pluralism, and tolerance, be it ethnic, linguistic, religious or political. it is that which makes indonesia strong and appealing and inspiring throughout the world. i would say like europe, the europe that i want. but in indonesia, as in europe, we see that extremists and fanatics are sowing bigotry, hatred and intolerance. this is shown in crimes like the ones against ahmadiyya followers or people in papua. in indonesia some of these extremists may be used by terrorist organisations or incite people to undermine the democratic system. this is one more reason why these extremists must be combated politically and ideologically and their crimes must receive exemplary punishment. i hope that the people in the indonesian government will read this resolution as an expression of concern for the victims and as a genuine expression of solidarity and encouragement for all those brave people in indonesian civil society – in government, in parliament, in the judiciary and in the media – that are fighting against these criminals and for the end of their impunity. i would like to recall a good friend who has been doing just that: suciwati, the widow of the great human rights campaigner munir who was murdered a couple of years ago. the perpetrators of his murder have not yet been fully brought to justice.

in writing. − the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union (frontex) was established in 2004 and became operational in 2005. the frontex agency shall enhance border security by ensuring coordination of the actions of the member states in the implementation of community measures relating to the management of the external borders. the abolition of internal borders has facilitated the free movement of citizens, which requires a coordinated approach to the security of the external borders, which must remain closed to cross-border crime as well as other illegal activities. it is therefore necessary to adopt and apply common rules and to strengthen cooperation between member states as regards external borders. the report, which i supported, therefore provides for the creation of european border guard teams to be deployed during joint operations, rapid interventions and pilot projects. i also stress the strengthening of frontex's fundamental rights obligations, the establishment of an effective mechanism to monitor respect for these rights in all its activities, the appointment of a fundamental rights officer and the creation of a consultative forum on this matter.

in writing. − this report is based on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament (ep) and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 2007/2004 establishing a european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union (frontex). on 14 june 1985 the schengen agreement was signed, which, by abolishing checks at the internal borders of the signatory countries and creating a common area, made possible the free movement of people (half a billion) and goods throughout the european union. the control of the eu's external borders has become a matter of common concern and requires integrated management. this freedom of movement, while being a positive factor for citizens of good faith, is also an opportunity for people who are not welcome in these states, such as refugees, terrorists, criminals, fugitives from justice, stateless persons, etc., to enter. i welcome and vote in favour of this report which aims to strengthen the agency, making it more efficient, increasing its visibility (by giving the name of european border guards to officials), binding member states to compliance with this regulation and subjecting it to more effective control by this parliament.
