in writing. − the frontex agency coordinates operational cooperation between member states in the field of external border management; supports member states in the training of national border guards, including the definition of common training standards; carries out risk analyses; monitors the development of relevant research on external border control and surveillance; supports member states in circumstances requiring enhanced operational and technical assistance at the external borders and provides member states with the necessary support in the framework of the organisation of joint return operations. the frontex agency shall enhance border security by ensuring coordination of the actions of the member states in the implementation of community measures relating to the management of the external borders. according to the revised regulation, frontex should promote solidarity between member states, particularly those that are subject to disproportionate specific pressures. eu countries, which have been contributing on a voluntary basis with staff and technical equipment to frontex, are now obliged to do so. the agency should, however, also be provided with the means to purchase or lease its own equipment. the review of the mandate of frontex aims to improve the functioning of the agency in the light of the experience gained since its creation in 2004.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 2007/2004 establishing a european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union (frontex). the abolition of internal borders, especially in the schengen area, the objective of a common area of freedom, security and justice of the eu, is counterbalanced by the fact that the external borders of the union are now a matter of common responsibility. in this context, it is imperative to strengthen its integrated management. it is indeed necessary to protect the external borders by keeping them closed to cross-border crime and other illegal activities. in this context, there is a need to strengthen and reformulate the powers of frontex. the amendments include strengthening the provisions on fundamental human rights; the creation of an eu border guard system; support for member states facing difficulties in their asylum systems; new powers in the implementation of voluntary repatriation operations; and the extension of the democratic control of the agency by giving the ep a greater role in monitoring the work of the agency, including its arrangements for working with third countries.
in writing. − the frontex agency, set up in 2004, is responsible for managing cooperation between the various member states on external borders. this is an area which, in view of the schengen area, requires very close cooperation, since the borders are twofold: while they delimit the territorial space of a state, they are also the boundary demarcation of a common space with 42 672 km of external borders, where about half a billion people move freely. it is with this fundamental idea in mind, that joint action by the states is necessary, that the amendment of the regulation establishing the frontex agency should be envisaged: the aim is to provide it with effective means of action to enable it to provide timely assistance to those states which need support as the first gateway to the european union. finally, it is also justified to strengthen relations between the frontex agency and other community agencies with common objectives, with a view to better rationalisation of resources and efficiency in action.
in writing. - the events on the island of lampedusa and the consequent closure of the borders by the french state have made it clear that frontex needs to be reformulated. integrated management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the eu member states is a guarantee of an area of freedom, security and justice for european citizens. the proposals submitted are intended to strengthen the role of frontex by giving it greater autonomy vis-à-vis the member states in terms of the human resources and instruments to be used. the creation of a european reserve guard system and the increase in the budget will provide the means to acquire their own equipment and to act in situations of immediate assistance, where the time limits for action and consent have also been reduced. another important element is the reinforced dimension of respect for human rights, through the creation of a consultative forum, and the new power in terms of processing of personal data, to combat cross-border crime and illegal migration. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that it is urgent to equip the eu with a migration policy, based on the principle of solidarity and responsibility and respecting international and community law, with particular attention to the most vulnerable people.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the amendment of council regulation (ec) no 428/2009 establishing a community regime for the control of exports, transfer, brokering and transit of dual-use items, which aims to oblige the commission and the member states to set up a secure system for the collection, transmission and storage of notifications and to oblige the commission to inform the european parliament of the operation of the system. i think it is important that the commission be required to report on the implementation and application of the regulation and to provide a full assessment of its impact.
in writing. − dual-use products and technologies are those which can be used for both civilian and military purposes. the community export control system is governed by a regulation, which contains an annex on controlled dual-use items. the current proposal introduces several new community general export authorisations designed to level the playing field for eu exporters and to facilitate exports in specific risk situations. i fully support the agreement reached in the tripartite consultation as a balanced document serving the interests of exporters while maintaining strong guarantees of transparency in the sensitive sector of dual use and technologies.
in writing. - dual-use products, goods which can be used for both civilian and military purposes, such as chemicals which can be used for fertilisers or to prepare bombs, computer technology but used to guide missiles, are today a highly sensitive matter. the control of exports of dual-use items and technologies at european level aims to ensure compliance with the international commitments of the eu and its member states on non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and conventional weapons. these include the ngs (nuclear suppliers group) against the proliferation of nuclear products and technologies or the australia group against the proliferation of chemical and biological products and technologies. this extremely important control, which makes it possible to prevent the proliferation of weapons through preventive measures enshrined in regulation (ec) no 428/2009 of 5 may 2009, effectively excludes any possibility of real action by the ep. i support this report because i think that the list of annex i products needs to be updated, but i would stress that in the context of future amendments to the regulation, parliament should have a greater say and a more prominent role in this matter.
in writing. − dual-use goods are all products, software and technology that can be used for civil or military purposes. the type of goods in question justifies particular care and attention to the way in which they are moved and used, as well as strict compliance with the international conventions applicable to them and the continuous updating of the list of products falling within that classification. in view of the recent changes in international export control regimes, the proposal in question aims precisely to update the list of dual-use items in accordance with regulation (ec) no 428/2009, which is why it deserves my support.
in writing. the report, drawn up by vital moreira, mep, proposes an amendment to council regulation (ec) no 428/2009 which established a community regime for the control of exports, transfer, brokering and transit of dual-use items. the export of dual-use items (listed in annex i) under the above regulation is subject to international control regimes such as the australia group (ag), the nuclear suppliers group (nsg), the missile technology control regime (mtcr) and the wassenaar arrangement (aw). the european parliament's role in this area has been very limited, so i am voting in favour of this report which recommends adopting the commission's proposal at first reading, as it meets the requirements of the lisbon treaty, requires the establishment of a secure system for the collection, transmission and storage of notifications by the commission and the member states, and requires parliament to be kept informed of the operation of the system - which is not the case at present - by means of the annual report to be presented by the dual-use coordination group.
in writing. − export controls on dual-use goods have been subject to measures at eu level. regulation (ec) no 428/2009 is the main community instrument for the control of exports, transfers, brokering and transit of dual-use items. international export control regimes are responsible for taking decisions that amend or update their control lists. these decisions are taken without the involvement of national parliaments, the ep or the eu. this regulation aims to change this situation by creating a common list of dual-use goods and technologies in the eu. the commission and the member states are obliged to inform the ep of any changes to this list. this ensures that commitments previously made by eu member states under international schemes are applied in a uniform and coordinated way across the eu. we believe that the member states should have the central role in drawing up the checklists - a view which conflicts with the centralisation of powers in the commission in this area, in particular through the dual-use coordination group, chaired by the commission, which decides which countries can trade dual-use goods with.
in writing. − export controls on dual-use goods have been subject to measures at eu level. regulation (ec) no 428/2009 is the main community instrument for the control of exports, transfers, brokering and transit of dual-use items. international export control regimes are responsible for taking decisions to amend or update their control lists, and these decisions are taken without the involvement of national parliaments, the ep and the european union. the amendment of annex i to that regulation included a common list of dual-use items and technologies. this ensures that commitments previously made by eu member states under international regimes are applied in a uniform and coordinated way across the eu. however, although we believe that greater democratic control and transparency are needed, we believe that it should be up to each member state to decide on its own checklists, and we therefore do not agree that the dual-use coordination group, chaired by the commission, should decide which countries can be traded with dual-use items, thus removing this competence from the member states.
in writing. − the report amending council regulation (ec) no 428/2009 establishes a community regime for the control of exports, transfers, brokering and transit of dual-use items. the commission and the member states now have a secure system for collecting, transmitting and storing notifications which reinforces compliance of exports of civilian goods, but with the risk of possible military use. until now, this registration has been optional and has largely depended on consensus decisions in international export control regimes such as the australian group (ag) for chemical and biological products, the nuclear suppliers group (nsg) for civil nuclear products, the missile technology control regime (mtcr) and the wassenaar arrangement (wa) for conventional weapons, dual-use goods and technologies.
in writing. − the treaty of lisbon clarifies the eu's competences in the field of international trade, thus providing a good opportunity to reaffirm the eu's role in this area, the european parliament's competences and responsibilities in the eu's institutional framework for decision-making. the community's dual-use regime should be organised in a more transparent and democratic way. the full participation of the european parliament, through the implementation of the obligations arising from the treaty of lisbon and the adoption of a joint interpretation by the european parliament and the european commission under the new framework agreement, will be crucial to achieving this objective.
in writing. - in the processes of control of exports, transfers, brokering and transit of dual-use goods, the ep currently has no real possibility of acting as an institution with a power of amendment. this should be the case, given the powers of the ep after the lisbon treaty and as a co-legislating body. in the light of future changes, it is necessary to ensure that the eu speaks with one voice and strong parliamentary support on all issues falling within the eu's exclusive competence. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the euro against counterfeiting is based on the principle of the protection of the euro against counterfeiting. the report also calls for the eu to be able to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action to combat terrorism. the powers of the ep, which are derived from the treaty of lisbon, should be gradually reflected in all community legislation. on the basis of this principle, i voted in favour of this report, which sets out a more transparent and democratic decision-making process involving the ep.
in writing. − the report amending council regulation (ec) no 428/2009 establishes a community regime for the control of exports, transfers, brokering and transit of dual-use items. the commission and the member states now have a secure system for collecting, transmitting and storing notifications which reinforces compliance of exports of civilian goods, but with the risk of possible military use. until now, this registration has been optional and has largely depended on consensus decisions in international export control regimes such as the australian group (ag) for chemical and biological products, the nuclear suppliers group (nsg) for civil nuclear products, the missile technology control regime (mtcr) and the wassenaar arrangement (wa) for conventional weapons, dual-use goods and technologies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution on the repeal of certain legal acts which have become obsolete because they have ceased to have effect over the last few decades, but which are still technically in force. for example, several measures associated with the accession of new member states provided for transitional measures to be applied immediately after their accession, but have since become obsolete.
in writing. - the obsolescence of all or part of certain legislative instruments is inevitable in any legal order. the transitional nature of certain acts, the verification of amending or rescission conditions, the expiry of programmes or the adoption of new legislation, among other things, may contribute to this. it is for the legislator to identify them and, where justified, to repeal them in order to facilitate the interpretation and application of the rules actually in force. the concrete irrelevance of obsolete acts may nevertheless cause unnecessary difficulties of interpretation and impede the implementation of the interinstitutional agreement on better law-making. as a lawyer by profession, i particularly understand the need for this repeal.
in writing. − the european union (eu) has changed its name over the course of its almost six decades of existence: european economic community (eec), european community (ec) and eu. as the name has changed, so too have many of the regulations and guidelines adopted become outdated, especially in view of the rapid scientific and technological developments of the last few decades. the report, drawn up by mr paolo de castro, mep, presents a proposal for a european parliament and council regulation repealing certain council acts in the field of the common agricultural policy which are considered to be obsolete (temporary acts which have lost their effects, transitional measures following the accession of new member states, linguistic and content errors, etc.). i therefore welcome this proposal which aims to clean up some outdated european standards and is in line with the interinstitutional agreement 2003c321/1 on better law-making.
in writing. - this report deals with the repeal of certain legal acts which have become obsolete as a result of regulations adopted over the last few decades which have ceased to have effect because of their temporary nature or because their content is contained in subsequent acts. several regulations at the cap level, such as community financing, premium schemes, restrictions and suspensions of aid, the establishment of the common agricultural policy, community compensation, common intervention prices, direct support measures for producers' incomes, and the improvement of community production, are now being repealed. having noted the direct implications that many of these now obsolete regulations have had in our country, it is necessary to recall that a large part of them has followed over time the deterioration of the agricultural sector in portugal, the accentuation of the country's agri-food production deficits and the increase in external dependence. this has created more difficulties for small and mediumsized farmers, without the necessary conditions for their adaptation, development and modernisation having been created. at a time when we are also experiencing a profound crisis in the rural world, it is regrettable that in some cases the commission has not acted otherwise, in particular by extending some regulations which are beneficial and necessary for the survival of production in some countries, such as portugal, in particular small and mediumsized farming, contrary to the general framework described.

in writing. − transparency of eu legislation is essential for greater democracy and equal access for all citizens. in order to eliminate legal maze and increase the clarity and security of european legislation, obsolete regulations should be repealed. the report repeals regulations relating to the common agricultural policy which were still formally in force, although they had become obsolete and no longer had any effect, in particular because they were temporary measures, their content had been taken up in subsequent acts or new measures had been introduced. it is absolutely necessary to remove from existing legislation those acts which no longer have any real effect, and i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - article 191 (2) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union states that the union's policy on the environment shall aim at achieving a high level of protection and that its action shall be based on the principles of precaution and preventive action. i am voting in favour of this proposal for a directive because i agree with the harmonization of the general principles for the evaluation of public and private projects in the field of the environment. i understand that projects can only be officially approved by the competent authorities after a prior assessment of their real effects. member states should also be free to set thresholds and criteria to exclude from the assessment projects which are not significant in terms of their environmental impact. in accordance with article 6 of the aarhus convention, i consider it extremely positive that citizens are involved in the decision-making process on projects with an environmental impact, increasing the involvement of local communities and their consequent accountability. however, it is important to establish rules and procedures for their active participation, and it is also important to define an environmental culture that reconciles the development of the regions with the protection of nature.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the public regulated service (prs) provided by the global satellite navigation system resulting from the galileo programme, because i consider that prs is one of the essential services provided by galileo which ensures and guarantees security even in severe crisis situations. the european satellite navigation programme galileo consists of five services in total: the open service, the commercial service, the security service, the search and rescue service and the regulated public service. this proposal concerns the regulated public service (prs), the use of which is reserved exclusively for users authorised by governments for sensitive applications such as critical infrastructure, transport, internal and external security and emergency services. i think it is important to establish common rules for the use, management and control of access to the prs. the mechanism proposed in this report, which is designed to ensure safety, provides the necessary harmony between, on the one hand, the definition of common minimum standards and the monitoring of compliance with the standards at eu level and, on the other hand, the decentralisation of the supervisory task of the member states.
in writing. − the galileo programme is of strategic importance for the independence of the union in terms of satellite navigation and location and dating services and will make a significant contribution to the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and to smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. the use and management of the regulated public service prs is a common responsibility of the member states in order to protect the security of the union and their own security. consequently, access to the prs should be strictly restricted to certain categories of users subject to permanent monitoring.
in writing. − the purpose of this proposal is to define the modalities under which states, the council, the commission, union agencies and international organisations can have access to the public regulated service (prs) provided by the global navigation satellite system (gnss) resulting from the galileo programme. the prs is a reserved service, to which the general public will not have access and whose use must be controlled for security reasons. the security objectives linked to the use of the prs are directly linked to the security of the union and its member states and have an impact on the union's external policy. it is therefore essential to supervise users by means such as the establishment of an authorization procedure, the use of cryptographic keys, the approval of receivers, etc. in addition, it is a service with some applications which may be very sensitive at political and strategic level. the prs requires the precise definition of the access arrangements in a legislative text, which is exactly what this proposal does.
in writing. the report, drawn up by mr norbert glante, mep, is concerned with a proposal for a european parliament and council decision on the modalities of access to the public regulated service (prs) provided by the global satellite radio navigation system resulting from the galileo programme. among the services provided by the european satellite navigation programme galileo is the public regulated service (prs). it is a service similar to traditional gps but with a tenfold level of accuracy. this service is available to the member states, the council, the commission and, under certain conditions, eu agencies, international organisations and third states. the commission proposal under consideration provides a detailed regulatory framework for access to the prs, management and user control, taking into account the need to ensure security in its operation for political and strategic reasons. given the specific nature of this service, i agree with the rapporteur's position that it is necessary to create a mechanism - a responsible prs authority - to prevent the breach of safety standards, i am voting in favour of this report and i am voting for it to be another instrument at the service of the european people and to contribute to improving their quality of life.

in writing. − the european satellite navigation programme galileo will offer a total of five services: the open service, the commercial service, the security service, the search and rescue service and the regulated public service. this proposal concerns the regulated public service (prs), the use of which is reserved exclusively for users authorised by governments for sensitive applications (such as critical infrastructure, transport, internal and external security and emergency services). this proposal introduces a detailed regulatory framework for the modalities of access to the prs and the management and control of users in order to ensure the security of the system and the protection of information. since certain applications of the service may be politically and strategically sensitive, and in order to ensure the high level of security required, it is important to act prudently in the development of this regulatory framework, in particular by introducing a common and harmonised process for user authorisation by participants. while the prs is expected to become operational in 2014, it is important to establish the necessary legal framework in advance so that member states and other actors have sufficient time to put in place the different control mechanisms and to comply with the required security standards.
in writing. − this report is based on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the modalities of access to the regulated public service provided by the global satellite radio navigation system resulting from the galileo programme. access to the regulated public service is reserved exclusively for users authorised by governments for sensitive applications (such as critical infrastructure, transport, internal and external security and emergency services). these applications require a high degree of accuracy and reliability, which is why the regulated public service uses strong and coded signals. the commission shall introduce a detailed regulatory framework for the modalities of access to the regulated public service and the management and control of users in order to ensure system security and information protection. the regulated public service is one of the essential services offered by galileo, which will be able to ensure continuity of service and ensure safety even in severe crisis situations. it is important to establish common rules for the use, management and control of access to the regulated public service. the report concludes that the proposed mechanism ensures the security of the system, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. − under the european satellite navigation programme galileo, the public regulated service (prs) will be made available for use by government-authorised entities for sensitive applications such as critical infrastructure, transport, internal and external security and emergency services. precisely because these are potentially politically and strategically sensitive applications and because breaches of security in the use of this service can have serious repercussions, it is important to establish common rules for the use, management and access control of the prs. that is the aim of the commission's present proposal, which i voted in favour of.
in writing. − the galileo programme, which plays a key role in the eu's independence from other satellite navigation systems, offers the possibility of five services. this report covers the regulated public service (rps) which is intended for specific applications (such as internal and external security, emergency services, critical infrastructure) for users authorised by member state governments. it provides a very detailed legal framework for the modalities of access to the rds and the management of users to ensure the security of the system and information. this regulation, which will only enter into force in 2014, lays down common minimum standards and security issues to be followed by the participants in the rdp, which may be, in addition to the member states, the council, the commission and, in particular cases, following international agreements, european agencies, third countries and international organisations. i would stress that it is important to define clearly the rules to be used in access and in the event of non-compliance, since the information from the rdp is naturally a matter of policy and strategy for the countries and can be used in emergency situations. the inclusion of the directive on data protection and privacy is another important point to highlight.

in writing. − for many centuries, tropical timber has been the object of the unbridled greed of those who seek to enrich themselves through the trafficking of this type of material, taking advantage of its quality and exoticism, without taking care to ensure the sustainability of the forest species they plunder. while biodiversity has been greatly reduced, the people of the countries from which these rare woods originate receive nothing from their trade and often see their livelihoods jeopardized by the activities of those who profit illegally from this trade. the european union could not ignore this problem and concluded the relevant international agreement in good time. i hope that you will persist in this global effort to put an end to the over-exploitation and illegal logging of these types of wood.
in writing. − this report, drawn up by vital moreira, mep, includes a recommendation on the 2006 international tropical timber agreement, taking into account the council decision on its signature on behalf of the european union. the oecd data show that the annual destruction of tropical forest areas is equivalent to the area of greece, which poses a threat to biodiversity and aggravates the risk of global warming. this has been the subject of discussion at various international meetings, leading to the signing of agreements and the creation of international bodies that try to implement a credible licensing system and prevent the illegal felling of trees, often centuries old, such as the international tropical timber organisation (itto). the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment from harmful substances.
in writing. − the delay in the adoption of this agreement is due to its non-approval in 2008 by the parliament, which now gives its approval in 2011 to accession to an international agreement dated 2006. this agreement was reached within the framework of the united nations conference on trade and development (unctad) and is intended to replace an earlier 1994 agreement (which remains in force until the entry into force of the 2006 agreement). we stress that all eu member states have expressed their intention to sign the 2006 agreement and to contribute appropriately to its implementation. the agreement aims to promote the sustainable management of tropical timber-producing forests by creating a framework for consultation, international cooperation and policy-making among all members with regard to all relevant aspects of the global timber economy. legitimate doubts are raised as to the compatibility of sustainable management with the promotion of the expansion and diversification of international trade in tropical timber, also mentioned in the agreement. for this reason, we share the view that the mid-term review of the current text should be used to put the protection of tropical forests and the restoration of degraded forest areas at its core.

in writing. − deforestation and forest degradation are the main causes of biodiversity loss. in turn, illegal logging is the main driver of deforestation, accounting for 20% to 40% of the world's industrial timber production. tropical timber is the most penalized for this type of activity and, as regards penalties, eu member states should lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of the provisions of this regulation and take all necessary measures to ensure their application. the penalties should be effective, proportionate and dissuasive and may take the form of fines proportionate to the environmental damage, the value of the timber and timber products concerned and the fiscal and economic losses resulting from the infringement, confiscation of the timber and timber products concerned or immediate suspension of the authorisation to carry out trading activities.
in writing. - according to oecd estimates, an area of forest equivalent to the size of greece is being destroyed annually, placing the irreplaceable biodiversity at risk of extinction and increasing the risk of global warming. although the first tropical timber agreement was concluded more than 20 years ago, illegal logging and over-exploitation continue to be widespread. almost half of all slaughter activities in regions such as the amazon, the congo basin, southeast asia and russia are illegal. the council and the commission endorse the international tropical timber organisation (itto), established by the 1983 international agreement, which they consider to be the answer to the most pressing issues facing the timber industry. the iatm will continue its work on issues such as deforestation and illegal logging, but it appears possible to make greater efforts to strengthen enforcement of forest law, as demonstrated by the additional measures adopted by the union. in this context, i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion by the european union of the 2006 international tropical timber agreement.
in writing. − every year, an area of forest equivalent to the area of greece is destroyed worldwide, posing a major threat to biodiversity, exacerbating global warming and accentuating social inequalities on the planet. this agreement replaces the 1994 agreement and allows for a credible licensing system, ensuring that only legal timber producers have access to the market. this and other measures in the agreement and other decisions of the european institutions are aimed at preventing the excessive exploitation and illegal logging which continue to be widely practised and which constitute a serious environmental and social problem. for these reasons i voted in favour of the recommendation. i cannot, however, fail to stress the importance of further measures for a truly sustainable management of forests, necessarily including fairer trade rules and trade relations.
in writing. − the 2006 international tropical timber agreement introduces a licensing system to condition market access to legally produced products only. it introduces a set of measures that meet the purpose of the joint action, recalling regulation (eu) no 995/2010 of the european parliament and of the council adopted on 20 october 2010. the protection of tropical forests is actually part of the wider problem of forest protection to which the eu is committed. this is another step towards combating illegal logging, which according to oecd figures has destroyed an area the size of greece every year.

in writing. − like other regions of the world, the south pacific ocean area did not have a convention on the conservation and management of its high seas fisheries resources. the union, through the commission, has participated in the negotiations to change this situation and has been a signatory to the convention since july 2010. despite the step taken by the european union and the importance of the subject matter underlying that international legal instrument, most of the states concerned seem reluctant to commit themselves definitively. the delay in ratifying the convention by important countries whose good practices and fishing tradition would suggest a different course of action weakens the agreement reached and calls into question its effective implementation. i hope that the situation will be reversed and that the convention can enter into force in order to ensure the sustainability and good management of fisheries resources in the south pacific. like the rapporteur, i believe that the union should be a party to most of these conventions, in order to ensure that its interests are respected, that the conservation of species is defended and that other actors adopt good practices.
in writing. − this recommendation, drawn up by ms carmen fraga estévez, is intended to address a proposal for a council decision on the approval, on behalf of the european union (eu), of the convention on the conservation and management of high seas fishery resources in the south pacific ocean. fisheries management in the south pacific is the responsibility of two international organisations: the inter-american tropical tuna commission (iattc) and the western and central pacific fisheries commission (wcpfc), which focuses on highly migratory species. to fill this gap and ensure the protection of biodiversity, the countries of the region (australia, chile and new zealand) are consulting on the creation of a south pacific regional fisheries management organisation (sprfmo). although catches by eu vessels are not significant, it is necessary for the parties to ratify the convention, which was signed on 26 july 2010 by the eu, as decided by the council on 24 july 2010. the aim of this proposal for a council decision is to approve it with a view to its ratification by the eu. i therefore vote in favour.

in writing. − all fishing in the south pacific has been managed through two regional fisheries management organisations (rfmo): the inter-american tropical tuna commission (iattc) and the western and central pacific fisheries commission (wcpfc). however, the aim of both is the management of highly migratory species, so in this vast area, fishing for other types of resources was not regulated. to fill this gap, and given that fishing is carried out both in the eez and in the high seas, the governments of australia, chile and new zealand decided to launch in 2006 a consultation process towards the establishment of the south pacific regional fisheries management organisation (sprfmo), with the aim of cooperating to address the management and conservation gaps of non-highly migratory species and to ensure the protection of biodiversity in the high seas of the south pacific. although the eu does not have a large fishing activity in this area, its presence obliges it, under the united nations convention on the law of the sea, to cooperate with other stakeholders in the management and conservation of the resources of this area, and the eu has therefore been involved in this process from the outset.
in writing. - fisheries in the south pacific have been managed by two rfmos: the iattc and the wcpfc, both with the aim of managing highly migratory species. the fishing for other types of resources was not regulated except in the eezs of coastal states. to fill this gap, and given that there is fishing activity both in the eezs and in the high seas, the governments of australia, chile and new zealand decided to launch an international consultation process towards the creation of the south pacific regional fisheries management organisation (sprfmo). the objective of this legislative act is to enable the eu to ratify the text of the convention signed in 2010 through the proposal for a council decision. the eu must be present at all rfmos to defend its priorities in terms of sustainable fisheries management and the defence of the interests of its fleet, and i believe that this document should be approved by this parliament.

in writing. − the agreement between the eu and the government of the federative republic of brazil on civil aviation security was signed on 14 july 2010 and, in accordance with article 218 (6) (a) tfeu, was awaiting the approval of the european parliament. the text of the agreement aims to facilitate trade in goods and services by limiting, as far as possible, the duplication of assessments, tests and controls to significant regulatory differences and by relying on the certification system of one party to verify compliance with the requirements of the other party. eu and brazilian companies will benefit significantly from the mutual acceptance of the certification results. the draft agreement also represents a net benefit for the european union by establishing the mutual acceptance of certification results for all member states. the increased role of parliament means that the negotiations on international agreements are monitored more closely. as the shadow rapporteur for this document, i think it is essential to stress the need to keep the european parliament regularly informed about the negotiations and to notify it of any reservations which could jeopardise its approval, without waiting for the conclusion of the negotiations.
in writing. − in july 2001, the council authorised the opening of negotiations with norway and iceland on mutual legal assistance and extradition agreements, with the aim of applying to iceland and norway the provisions of the 1996 eu convention on extradition. in 2002, after the eu agreed to replace extradition with a surrender procedure under the european arrest warrant, the mission's mandate was updated. in 2006 the council adopted a comprehensive approach to the agreement on delivery procedures, which is not yet formally concluded and to which the new procedure under article 218 tfeu will now apply, with the council only being able to conclude the agreement after the ep's approval. i supported the conclusion of this agreement which aims to improve the process of surrender between the member states to norway and iceland for the purposes of criminal proceedings or the enforcement of sentences. in other words, the provisions in force between eu member states are extended to these two countries, members of the schengen area.
in writing. − i support the conclusion of this agreement which aims to improve the process of surrender between the member states and norway and iceland for the purposes of criminal proceedings or the execution of a sentence. it should therefore ensure that the system of extradition between the contracting parties is based on a surrender mechanism following a detention order, which should be issued for offences punishable by the law of the issuing member state by a custodial sentence or detention order, which has a maximum duration of not less than 12 months or, where a sentence or detention order has been issued, by penalties of not less than four months' duration. in fact, this agreement is only extending to these two countries the provisions already in force between the member states, which i think is very positive, given the privileged relations that both countries, members of schengen, have with the eu. i fully share the concerns expressed by the rapporteur, mr rui tavares, about the possibility of a partial derogation from the principle of double criminalization.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation because i believe that the agreement will help to improve the process of surrender between the member states, norway and iceland for the purposes of criminal proceedings or the execution of a sentence. as norway and iceland already transpose much of european legislation, it was not appropriate to refuse their application to join provisions already in force between eu member states.
in writing. − the proposal for a council decision aims to conclude, on behalf of the european union, an agreement between the european union and norway on surrender procedures between the member states of the union and iceland and norway, which was already signed on 28 june 2006 but has not yet been formally concluded. the agreement is designed to improve the surrender procedure in cases of indictment or execution of a sentence, in accordance with the convention of 27 september 1996 on extradition. under the terms of the agreement, the contracting parties are to ensure that the extradition mechanism operates on the basis of a prior arrest warrant. since the agreement in question only applies to norway and iceland - at the request of those two countries - what was already in force between the member states of the union, there is no serious doubt as to its appropriateness.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the extradition procedure within the eu has been replaced by a surrender procedure under the european arrest warrant, and the european council has decided to extend this procedure to the schengen countries. the presidency of the council subsequently negotiated agreements on judicial cooperation in criminal matters and extradition proceedings with norway and iceland. in accordance with article 218 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), this agreement may be concluded only after its approval by the european parliament. in these terms, and considering that the agreement extends to the republic of iceland and the kingdom of norway only the provisions in force in the member states, i support the rapporteur's proposals.
in writing. − this agreement is very important as it aims to improve the process of surrender between the member states, norway and iceland for the purpose of criminal proceedings or the execution of a sentence, taking into account, as minimum requirements, the terms of the convention on extradition between eu member states of 27 september 1996. under the provisions of the agreement, the contracting parties shall ensure that the system of extradition is based on a surrender mechanism following the issuance of an arrest warrant.
in writing. the agreement, which is subject to parliament's approval, aims to improve the process of surrender between the member states and norway and iceland for the purposes of criminal proceedings or the execution of a sentence, taking into account, as minimum requirements, the terms of the convention on extradition between eu member states of 27 september 1996. under the provisions of the agreement, the contracting parties shall ensure that the system of extradition is based on a surrender mechanism following the issuance of an arrest warrant. a detention order may be issued for offences punishable by the law of the issuing member state by a custodial sentence or detention order of a maximum duration of not less than 12 months or, where a sentence or detention order has been issued, by a sentence of not less than four months. it is simply a question of extending to norway and iceland - at the request of these two countries - the provisions already in force between the member states. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − this agreement between the european union and the republic of iceland and the kingdom of norway aims to strengthen cooperation mechanisms in the field of criminal procedure and the enforcement of penalties. the legal framework is to extend the scope of provisions already in force in the law applicable to the single area. the main concern must therefore be to ensure the fundamental principles of criminal law, namely the effective guarantee of the prohibition of the principle ne bis in idem, according to which no one should be convicted twice for the same offence, and the protection of the fundamental rights of the accused.
in writing. − the commission proposal provides for the conclusion by the european union of an agreement on surrender procedures between the eu member states and iceland and norway, signed on 28 june 2006, but not yet formally concluded. the aim of this agreement is to improve the procedures for surrender for the purposes of criminal proceedings or the execution of a sentence, taking into account, as a minimum, the terms of the convention of 27 september 1996. by concluding the agreement, the contracting parties aim at an extradition system based on a surrender mechanism following an enforcement order. a warrant may be issued for an offence punishable by a custodial sentence or detention order for a maximum period of not less than 12 months or where a sentence or detention order for a period of not less than four months has been issued. the european parliament considers that, since the agreement is intended to extend the application of the existing rules in this field in the member states of the european union, iceland and norway, it should support its conclusion and has therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. − the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking was established by council regulation (ec) no 521/2008. fuel cell and hydrogen (pch) technologies are promising long-term energy options that can be used in all sectors of the economy, offering a wide range of benefits for energy security, transport, the environment and resource efficiency. they are expected to play a key role in the eu's transition to a low-carbon society and to help achieve the target of reducing greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions by more than 85% by 2050. despite the financial crisis, the eu's major competitors in this field (the united states, japan, south korea and china) continue to make great efforts to overcome these obstacles through rtd programmes, policy measures and marketing exercises. it is therefore essential that the eu continues to invest in this technology, which requires the revision of its original regulation, which we are now amending, as proposed by the commission.
in writing. the report, drawn up by mr herbert reul, mep, focuses on the proposal for a council regulation amending council regulation (ec) no 521/2008 on the establishment of the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking (pch), whose funding is shared between three institutions: the industrial grouping, the research grouping and the european commission. this venture is the result of a public-private partnership in the field of research at european level, based on article 187 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), which created the 'joint technology initiatives' (seventh framework programme). the application of this technology is unquestionable in a wide variety of areas, notably in information technology and transport, and has made considerable progress in recent years, contributing to the reduction of co2 emissions. the commission is currently developing a european strategic energy technology plan (set plan) to create a more sustainable energy system. i welcome this motion for a resolution, which puts the eu at the forefront of innovation, establishing itself as a competitive and dynamic knowledge economy, and i welcome the proposal to set up the european institute of technology.
in writing. - as regards amendments to a council regulation on the setting-up of the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking, i intend to vote in favour of the european parliament's legislative resolution for the following reasons: (a) the policy of promoting research in fuel and hydrogen cells was not having the desired effect and its weaknesses were identified, and it was necessary to improve it - this was the aim of the report; (b) it is commonly accepted that the study of alternatives to the oil economy is important, and that these alternatives are required to respond to economic, social and environmental crises. fuel cells and hydrogen are one of the promising possibilities that we should study. it is therefore desirable to continue the policy of supporting its study. however, i cannot help stressing that much remains to be done to achieve a more caring and environmentally friendly society.
in writing. − the fuel cells and hydrogen company is very important to meet the challenge of increasing the production of environmentally friendly energy. it's a company that's only been in operation for two years and it's aiming to be able to produce clean, low-cost energy. however, the recent crisis has led to a reduction in investment in this area, leading to a decline in activity. it is, however, very important that investment in this type of industry be reassessed if we are to achieve the objectives set for 2050.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a council regulation amending council regulation (ec) no 521/2008 on the establishment of the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking. the commission has submitted a proposal to the council for approval. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that the council should inform the ep if it wishes to depart from the text adopted by parliament. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the euro against counterfeiting is based on the principle that the euro should be used as a medium for exchange of information between member states.
in writing. − the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking was established by council regulation (ec) no 521/2008 of 30 may 2008. its three members - the industrial cluster, the research cluster and the european commission - share the funding of administrative and operational expenses. as a result of low funding rates and the financial and economic crisis affecting the industry in the field of these future technologies, the current level of participation in the joint undertaking shares is lower than initially expected. the aim of the european commission's proposal is to adapt the provisions of the regulation to these conditions so that there is no general loss of interest, both from the industry and the scientific community. the new text provides that the availability of funds equivalent to those of the eu will allow for the contribution of industry itself as well as that of other legal entities involved in the activities to be taken into account. fuel cell and hydrogen technologies are promising long-term energy options that can be used in all sectors of the economy, offering benefits for energy security and efficiency, transport, the environment. i therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. − the economic and financial crisis which is affecting the european union so deeply has led politicians, economists and journalists, among others, to look at the causes of this situation and at ways of avoiding similar situations. the european commission, aware of the seriousness of this situation, among other measures, has prepared a document entitled 'green paper' 'audit policy: the lessons of the crisis' and intends to make it a kind of warning and prevention manual. european citizens, who are suffering the consequences of the crisis, do not understand why those who had the obligation to warn of the ongoing financial slide (bank boards, regulators, supervisors and statutory auditors) did not do so. the economy and business need trust. this requires that auditors are independent and do not have other business with companies. we must end the oligopoly, open up the market, and drastically reduce the cost of auditors. i therefore agree with the report drawn up by mr antonio masip hidalgo and i hope that, in view of the measures that have been taken, europe will quickly emerge from the crisis in which it is immersed.
in writing. − the quality of audit processes is conditioned by the auditor's independence (or lack thereof). as the report points out, there is a possibility of conflicts of interest when audit firms provide different services to the same company. on the other hand, the high concentration of the market in four large audit firms may lead to an excessive increase in risk when it is known that there are several smaller firms. we recognise that a high quality audit system must be a key part of a good corporate governance framework. we therefore support the european parliament's call on the commission to present its proposals on corporate governance and auditing in a coherent manner, although we cannot help but note that many of the proposals in the report are merely palliative.

in writing. − demographic ageing is a challenge for society and for all generations in the european union. in this context, europe has the highest percentage of elderly women in the world. older women face discrimination in the labour market linked to sex and age, and greater vulnerability due to slower, shorter and/or interrupted career paths. these factors translate into a greater gender pay gap and create a differentiation in contributions to personal pension accounts, thus increasing the risk of poverty for older women. i therefore voted in favour of the report on the situation of women approaching retirement age, which calls on the european commission and the member states to take effective measures to combat this discrimination and to ensure that the principle of equality between men and women is respected in pension reform policies and equal pay.
in writing. − it is necessary and urgent to combat the increased risk of poverty in old age, with particular attention to be paid to the age group of women over 50, where there is a higher rate of poverty, unemployment, isolation and social exclusion. it is regrettable that the risk of poverty among older women has reached about 22%. indeed, the likelihood that women, for family reasons, will have shorter, interrupted or reduced part-time careers and will receive lower average wages than men will eventually create a differential in contributions to the pension system, thus increasing the risk of poverty. it is essential to promote policies to promote active ageing and specific measures in the pension sector to ensure that women have adequate resources when they retire. in fact, economic independence is an essential condition for any human being to be able to determine his own life and to have genuine possibilities of choice. more robust economic and social policies are needed, with the necessary mechanisms for adequately managing the ageing process and the inevitable changes in society.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it presents appropriate and effective measures to combat discrimination against women approaching retirement age. it is essential to amend the current european pension legislation to ensure that these schemes do not penalise women who are already disadvantaged in terms of benefits and contributions throughout their working lives.
in writing. - knowing that european society is ageing and knowing that the average life expectancy of women is higher than that of men, the truth is that we will have, increasingly, older women in our society to whom we must ensure adequate living conditions and a role which, in many cases, may still be active. i therefore consider it an important signal that 2012 is the 'european year for active ageing and solidarity between generations'. we must not forget that older women are more vulnerable to poverty and therefore need special attention. but more than solutions based on welfare or social status, i believe that these women must be assured of an active role in society. many are professionals with extensive experience that can be used to the benefit of younger ones. older women can take on key caring roles within the family, allowing young mothers to better balance family and work. they are invaluable assets and it is our task to encourage and protect them, creating a society of genuine solidarity between generations.
in writing. - we are currently experiencing problems that have never been equalized before. the increase in life expectancy, coupled with the drastic reduction in births in so-called developed countries, brings new social problems. the sustainability of social security financing systems is of course a matter for discussion. the report by edit bauer, in its examination of the situation of women approaching retirement age, draws attention to another gender equality problem which needs to be tackled, not just equalised, but also solved, in the context of the europe 2020 strategy, namely the fight against poverty and the promotion of employment. despite the fact that women outnumber men, the employment rate in the 55-64 age group in 2009 was 54.8% for men and 37.8% for women. it is therefore necessary to eliminate the causes of this discrimination, since studies indicate that women over the age of 60 are more exposed to the fragility of social exclusion, since their pensions are lower than those of men who have had a longer contributory career. i would therefore like to congratulate the rapporteur on her work, which i fully support.

in writing. − most active labour market policies promoting gender equality target adult women and men and often overlook the disadvantage of older women compared to men in the same age group. on the other hand, the gender pay gap, career breaks (maternity leave or caring leave), parttime work and low pay that characterize women's jobs lead to multiple discrimination in old age, when the ability to integrate into working life and pension rights are even more reduced. in this regard, it is necessary to develop a systematic and comprehensive approach to active labour market policies, including special measures on health and safety at the workplace, accompanied by a strategy explicitly integrating the principle of gender equality. i voted yes.
in writing. − the elderly constitute an important and growing category of the union's population. as europe's population ages, the sustainability of pensions is a major challenge in the face of low birth rates, a shrinking labour force and a growing number of pensioners who are in good health and reaching old age. older people are a huge cultural, social and professional resource. their ongoing contribution to society, in many cases unpaid, is often overlooked and their potential for greater participation and better contribution remains under-exploited. there is widespread concern that the older generation is becoming a burden on the younger working age population and that this could fuel intergenerational tensions. one of the keys to overcoming the challenge of demographic ageing and preserving solidarity between generations lies in ensuring that people stay longer in the labour market and remain healthy, active and self-employed for longer after retirement. solidarity between generations has long been a major concern of the european union, both in policy-making and in raising public awareness.
