in writing. − the objective of directive 2008/52/ec is to promote the resolution of disputes by consensus, encouraging the use of mediation, and ensuring a balanced relationship between mediation and judicial proceedings. in addition to predictability, the aim is to establish a framework which preserves the main advantage of mediation, flexibility, and member states are urged to take these requirements as a guide in drawing up national legislation for the implementation of this directive. the evaluation shows that most member states are not only complying with the directive but are also ahead of it. however, this report highlights the need for greater awareness and understanding of mediation, calling for more action in terms of education, increased awareness of mediation, the development of the use of mediation by businesses and the requirements for access to the mediator profession. it urges the national authorities to develop programmes to promote adequate knowledge of adr, with such actions targeting the main advantages of mediation, namely cost, success rate, time efficiency, and involving lawyers and businesses, in particular smes, as well as academics. i therefore gave my support to this report.
in writing. − one of the three pillars of the creation of an area of freedom, security and justice is the guarantee of better access to justice, with procedures that are fast, adequate and accessible to all. in this context, access to adequate dispute resolution procedures is essential for both individuals and businesses. this directive promotes the consensual resolution of disputes through mediation, introducing common principles which provide the parties with a predictable legislative framework, without compromising the main advantage of mediation, which is flexibility. most member states have overburdened judicial systems, where the out-of-court settlement of disputes in civil and commercial matters could contribute to a significant reduction in the volume of cases as well as in the average time taken to resolve them. it is important that member states carry out awareness raising activities to promote appropriate knowledge of this form of alternative dispute resolution, which offers practical tailor-made solutions in a faster and cheaper manner. i also support the need to establish common rules for access to the mediation profession in order to promote the highest quality of mediation and to ensure high standards of professional training and accreditation throughout the eu.
in writing. − mediation is an effective form of dispute resolution, capable of ensuring the protection of the legitimate rights and interests of the parties, in particular in civil proceedings, without recourse to the courts and to civil proceedings based on adversarial procedure. the report analyses the efforts made by the member states to transpose the directive into their national law and considers it important to analyse the impact of this legislation on legal practitioners and courts. i would remind you once again that in this as in other matters in the area of justice, while it is advantageous to have uniformity in the rules and the law applicable, since this gives legal certainty to citizens, the right of each state to go further in defining its own rules must continue to prevail.
in writing. − this report, by arlene mccarthy, mep, analyses the application of the mediation directive in the member states and its impact on mediation and monitoring by the courts. the purpose of this report is to assess how member states are implementing the mediation directive, in accordance with directive 2008/52/ec, to find out which member states have not yet transposed it, to know the problems arising from its application, etc. as an alternative to court justice, it is imperative that people are made aware of its advantages: greater speed and much lower costs, with success rates of around 80%. only the fact that it is unknown, particularly in crossborder cases, can justify the fact that it is no longer sought. i congratulate the rapporteur on her excellent report. mediation is an excellent alternative for resolving international disputes, especially family problems, which can and should be further developed, especially in times of crisis, by drawing on the contributions of the member states. the use of these extrajudicial means should be encouraged because it makes justice much quicker, it frees up the courts and saves taxpayers money.
in writing. − this report on the implementation of mediation by the member states demonstrates the importance of alternative means of conflict resolution, alongside the courts. we cannot ignore the fact that often the solutions found in mediation are the result of work done by the parties and are therefore likely to produce a better outcome which is accepted by both parties or which both parties consider to be a win-win, and which could never be obtained by a court decision. there is obviously still a long way to go in this area, particularly in the member states which have not yet implemented the directive. however, even for those who have already done so, there should be greater awareness of the use of mediation, particularly as regards access for smes. the report draws attention to the need to strengthen the guarantees for citizens who use this means of conflict resolution, particularly as regards the requirements for access to the profession of mediator.
in writing. − ensuring better access to justice is one of the key objectives of the european union's policy to create an area of freedom, security and justice. whereas the concept of access to justice should, in this context, include access to adequate dispute resolution procedures for individuals and businesses. the objective of directive 2008/52/ec is therefore to promote the consensus-based resolution of disputes, to encourage the use of mediation, and to ensure a balanced relationship between mediation and judicial proceedings. it is therefore necessary to facilitate access to mediation as a viable alternative to the traditional confrontational approach and to ensure that parties using mediation in the european union benefit from a predictable legislative framework. the directive introduces common principles to this end, dealing in particular with aspects of civil procedure.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the application of the mediation directive in the member states, its impact on mediation and monitoring by the courts. the rapporteur points out the need to encourage national authorities to develop programmes to promote appropriate knowledge of alternative dispute resolution, considering that such actions should target the main advantages of mediation, namely cost, success rate and time efficiency. i agree with the rapporteur and point to the portuguese example where the growth rate of alternative dispute resolution has been increasing since its implementation. this is an essential measure to free the traditional justice bodies from the large and complex cases which society is taking on to bring to them. i believe that the involvement of lawyers, businesses, and especially smes, and academics, is essential to the promotion of alternative dispute resolution.
in writing. − the commission proposal is part of a set of legislative initiatives which seek to bring the current european legal order into line with the provisions of the lisbon treaty, in particular those concerning delegated and implementing acts. the new procedures for delegating powers to the commission under the lisbon treaty imply a distinction between delegating and implementing acts. regulation no 378/2007 lays down detailed rules for the application of voluntary modulation. it is proposed that all the powers conferred on the commission by means of the regulation be implemented by means of implementing acts in order to ensure a uniform application of voluntary modulation of direct payments. the three institutions seem to support this interpretation, so i see no reason to oppose the technical solution advocated.
in writing. - this report, by britta reimers, is on a proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 378/2007 as regards the rules for voluntary modulation of direct payments under the common agricultural policy. in accordance with the treaty of lisbon, the powers conferred on the commission to adopt non-legislative acts of general scope which supplement or amend certain non-essential elements of a legislative act and on member states to adopt all measures of national law necessary to implement legally binding union acts are to be aligned by articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the commission proposal in question was examined in detail by the rapporteur and deserved her support, as she identified the areas where the conditions for implementing acts were met. in the light of the report and considering that this proposal concerns only amendments for the purpose of alignment, i therefore vote in favour of this proposal for a regulation.
in writing. − the clarification and simplification of the legal instruments now proposed reflect a strengthening of the european commission's power as a result of the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, to the detriment of the member states. but in this context, what is necessary to stress is the lack of a real modulation of direct aid, as well as of all public aid. what is required is the gradual adjustment of aid, by steps, according to the aid received per farmer/holding, as well as its capping. the money thus obtained could play an important role in defending and promoting the national production of each member state and in creating jobs, as well as in overcoming the food production problem that countries like portugal have, in promoting local/traditional markets, in the sustainable and productive occupation of the entire territory. small and mediumsized farmers and family farming are being stifled by rising energy prices, by rising production costs and by a producer price policy that favours large distribution companies at the expense of fair value and compensation for those who produce food. the situation they have reached calls for a break with the policy options which have framed the cap reforms.
in writing. - the entry into force of the lisbon treaty has led to the clarification and simplification of legal instruments, which have increased the power of the european commission to the detriment of the member states. but what is needed is the lack of real modulation of direct aid, as well as of all public aid. what is required is a gradual reduction in the aid, in stages, according to the aid received per farmer/holding, and a ceiling. the money thus obtained could play an important role in defending and promoting the national production of each member state and in creating jobs, as well as in overcoming the problem of food production that countries like portugal have, in promoting local/traditional markets, in the sustainable and productive occupation of the entire territory. we know how small and mediumsized farmers and family farming are being stifled by rising energy prices, by rising production costs and by a policy of producer prices which favours large distribution companies at the expense of fair value and compensation for those who produce food. the situation they have reached calls for a break with the policy options which have framed the cap reforms.
in writing. - the treaty of lisbon abolished the old comitology system based on the classic comitology procedures (consultation, management, regulation) and the regulatory procedure with scrutiny. this system is now replaced by a two-tier structure, consisting of delegated and implementing acts (the former including the right of veto of parliament) which allow the commission to exercise powers in implementation and enforcement. the existing legislative acquis must therefore be brought into line with this new legal reality. the proposal is limited to amendments for alignment purposes only, to the rules for voluntary modulation of direct payments under the common agricultural policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because, formally and as a consequence of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the powers conferred on the commission under regulation (ec) no 378/2007 should be aligned with articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. in practical terms, voluntary modulation is a mechanism which tends to create artificial imbalances in the various member states, since at the limit it will always be a question of the balance between the two pillars of the cap. i would remind you that portugal requested the use of voluntary modulation in 2008 to transfer funds from the first to the second pillar, and portugal is the member state of the european union with the best balance between the two pillars, showing well how this mechanism can be perverse if misused.
in writing. - the treaty of lisbon abolished the old comitology system and the system of implementing powers of the commission was based on the distinction between delegated and implementing acts. it has therefore become necessary to make adjustments to existing legislation in order to bring it into line with these new rules. this is precisely the aim of the present proposal for an amendment to regulation (ec) no 378/2007 on the rules for voluntary modulation of direct payments under the common agricultural policy, which i voted in favour of.
in writing. − the commission and the council are currently reviewing the legislative framework (the officially supported export credit agreement) with a view to its transposition into eu law. the aim is to give the export credit agencies (eca) of the member states more legal certainty. export credits are effective instruments to support union enterprises, capable of helping to create jobs and develop projects that might otherwise face financing difficulties. in view of the increasing number of applications received, i would recommend that the oecd convention be introduced rapidly by the member states. i agree with the econ committee's opinion that european supervision of export credits should be introduced as an exception when there is any distortion of competition in the internal market. the principle of subsidiarity should be maintained.
in writing. - this report concerns a proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the application of certain rules to the obtaining of export credits by companies which are recipients of official support. in fact, most member states have export credit agencies (eca) which play a key role in supporting european trade and business investment, reaching €468 billion in the period 2004-09. these supports are part of the agreement on subsidies and countervailing measures (ascm), also known as the arrangement, negotiated within the framework of the organisation for economic cooperation and development (oecd) countries, and represent public funding instruments to which the european union is committed. given that these agencies mainly support industrial activities with harmful effects on the environment, in particular due to the production of co2, and that, according to the world bank, the effects on poverty reduction are negligible, i agree with the rapporteur's position that the aces should contribute to the achievement of eu policies and objectives, and there is therefore no need to revise the oecd convention.
in writing. - the provision of credit to smes is an urgent need to enable them to maintain and create more jobs with rights, increase production and counteract the trend of closing down thousands of smes in countries in deep economic recession and with a dramatic social situation such as portugal. smes represent the majority of enterprises and employment in the eu. a credit policy, particularly of public institutions such as credit agencies, should favour smes. that doesn't happen. unfortunately, we find that the overwhelming majority of credit is granted to large transnational corporations, whose dominant position in the market is further strengthened at the expense of smes. that is the approach that this report sets out. of course, because it gives priority to exports and competitiveness when the priority at this time of crisis should be to strengthen the internal market of each country, particularly countries like portugal, and does not take into account their specificities and needs as an independent and sovereign country. the whole framework of the proposal is aimed at maintaining a framework of progressive liberalization of world trade which will accentuate the concentration and centralization of capital, further deepening the crisis of the system and the exploitation of peoples and countries.
in writing. - we know that lending to smes is an urgent need to enable them to maintain and create more jobs with rights, to increase production and to counteract the trend of closing them down, by the thousands, in countries in deep economic recession and with a dramatic social situation, such as portugal. smes represent the majority of enterprises and employment in the eu. a credit policy, particularly of public institutions such as credit agencies, should favour smes. that doesn't happen. what we unfortunately find is that the overwhelming majority of credit is going to large transnational corporations, whose dominant position in the market is further strengthened at the expense of smes. that is the approach that this report sets out. of course, because it favours exports and competitiveness, when the priority, at this time of crisis, should be to strengthen the internal market of each country, particularly countries like portugal. the whole framework of the proposal is aimed at maintaining a framework of progressive liberalization of world trade which will accentuate the concentration and centralization of capital, further deepening the crisis of the system and the exploitation of peoples and countries.
in writing. - export credit agencies (eca) facilitate legitimate trade where private capital markets cannot. they have a much higher risk-absorption capacity than private actors, since they do not have to pay taxes or realise benefits and therefore have a greater latitude than private banks to accuse losses on realised loans. the eca plays an important role in supporting trade and investment by european companies. however, in view of the public deficit situations existing in most eu member states, it seems of the utmost importance that its operations are financially sound. the support of these agencies to the economy is very important for the eu to successfully emerge from the crisis.
in writing. this report concerns the proposal for a council decision on the application of certain guidelines to officially supported export credits. most industrialized countries, including all eu member states and most emerging countries, have at least one export credit agency, which is usually an official or para-official segment of their governments. overall, export credit agencies represent the most important source of public financing of private sector projects worldwide. the financing of large industrial and infrastructure projects in developing countries is equivalent to several times the combined annual amount of all the multilateral development banks. the total amount of export credit guarantees granted in the period 2004-2009 by the export credit agencies of the eu member states was in the order of eur 468 billion. the rules to which these agencies are subject do not prevent a lack of transparency, in breach of the discipline established by the oecd convention. the current modus operandi is also conducive to bribery and corruption. i voted in favour of this report, which makes concrete proposals for greater transparency in the work of these bodies.
in writing. the rapporteur believes that the export credit agencies are the most important source of public funding for private sector projects, and that they operate mainly at national level. however, as regards the subject of the support, there is little data available, which results in undeniable lack of transparency. on the other hand, support is directed towards activities which conflict with the objectives of the union. union policy in this regard should be consistent with the objectives of the treaties and should seek to make the activities of export credit agencies compatible with community objectives. this is a path that cannot be ignored, given the high economic power of these entities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it argues that the eu needs to establish mutually beneficial partnerships that create win-win situations for resource-rich countries and for the eu itself. in addition to an africa-eu partnership, the union could also promote partnerships with countries in eastern europe, latin america or asia. china, in particular, is an obvious partner, as it produces most of the essential rare earth elements. so raw materials diplomacy is essential. at the same time, the eu could consider non-financial support for a raw materials holding company, involving numerous european companies in the procurement of raw materials. in addition to the oecd and the g8/g20, the commission should establish concrete cooperation with the usa and japan. ultimately, to be able to respond to the raw materials challenge, the eu needs a comprehensive and integrated strategy focusing on short and long-term measures that can be implemented at both domestic and international level, especially with regard to raw materials, in order to adequately address the triple challenge of ensuring future competitiveness, sustainability and security of supply.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on an effective strategy for europe in the field of raw materials, which must be fair and respect the right of developing countries to benefit from their own resources. it is also an opportunity for the eu to support its industry for greater recycling and efficiency.
in writing. − this report focuses mainly on issues such as access to strategic raw materials and resource efficiency, recycling and substitution of raw materials, including efficient waste management as a way to increase industrial competitiveness, sustainability and security of supply in europe. we all know how essential it is for european industry to maintain access to raw materials, and i would like to remind you of a point which is particularly important for my country, namely access to raw materials used in sugar refining, which is necessary if we are to avoid a repeat of the situation of shortages of supply which occurred in portugal at the end of last year. finally, at a time of crisis, when the tax burden on citizens is increasing in some parts of europe, i do not think that this is the time to ask the commission to carry out a study on the impact of a tax on water and land use.
in writing. - raw materials are fundamental to european industry, accounting for three quarters of exports and one third of employment in the european union. however, the use of raw materials, especially in times of crisis, requires us to give careful consideration to their use. the extraction of oil, particularly in countries considered to be developing, is considered a rather complicated problem, not only to avoid exploitation of these countries by the states considered to be rich, but above all for social and environmental reasons. the diplomacy of raw materials must therefore be a matter of constant concern to this parliament. given that the eu will see a 300% increase in raw material consumption by 2050, it is essential to adopt a comprehensive and integrated strategy that includes both short-term and long-term measures and that, while not neglecting innovation, also addresses recycling efficiency. i am therefore aware that access to raw materials is essential to the well-being of european citizens, and i therefore vote in favour of this report on an effective strategy for europe in the field of raw materials, which recommends that, wherever possible, these materials should be recovered and reused, but also that their extraction should be compatible with the environment, in order to minimise climate change.
in writing. the report highlights the concerns of an eu that is increasingly feeling the constraints of raw materials shortages. we are facing an increasingly acute confrontation between a system based on the irrational exploitation of natural resources and the natural limits of a generous, but finite, earth. as a result, the dispute over the existing reserves of some essential raw materials is intensifying and taking on violent forms, as is happening in north africa and the near and middle east. the sovereignty and interests of peoples and states are being disregarded and new and disturbing forms of colonialism are being put into practice, if necessary by means of war, as is happening in libya. another important aspect which the report does not adequately address concerns speculation in the commodities market. we have therefore put forward proposals to create all the conditions necessary to ensure that the physical market is not overshadowed by the financial market in derivatives, the volume of which has grown disproportionately over the years. in order to combat speculation, which can make raw materials inaccessible, it is not enough to talk about transparency in general, as is done in the report. we must go much further, including in the fight against speculative instruments and the derivatives market.
in writing. - as we said in the debate, it is essential to combat speculation in the commodities market and to create all the conditions to ensure that the physical market is not overshadowed by the financial market in derivatives, the volume of which has grown disproportionately over the years. but to protect it from speculation which can make raw materials inaccessible, it is not enough to talk about transparency in general. we must go much further, including in the fight against speculative instruments and the derivatives market. but it is also necessary that their exploitation be carried out in compliance with social and environmental rules, in addition to respect for the sovereignty and interests of the states and peoples where these resources exist, including in the development of cooperation with third producing countries, in particular africa, avoiding any new forms of colonialism. but as we know, the european union's positions in this field are increasingly imperialist in character, as is shown by all its intervention, particularly in libya. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. − europe faces challenges but also great opportunities in raw materials, as the eu has the opportunity to reap the benefits of the sudden increase in global demand for raw materials by improving their supply and efficiency, while meeting the needs of european industry and the sector in question. we believe that equitable access to raw materials at stable and predictable prices is of vital importance for the development potential, competitiveness, innovation and preservation of european industry, to the detriment of restrictions on access and supply, in particular of raw materials such as base metals and rare earth elements. similarly, high price volatility can hamper the competitiveness, eco-efficiency and innovation prospects of eu industry, especially smes. i believe that resource policy and resource diplomacy are of great importance to the eu not only in terms of industrial policy and international trade but also as a cross-cutting issue in different areas of internal policy as well as foreign and security policy.
in writing. - european industry is facing an increasingly difficult situation in the supply of raw materials. it is essential that the european union establishes mutually beneficial partnerships that create win-win situations for resource-rich countries and for the eu itself. the european union needs a comprehensive and integrated strategy focusing on short- and long-term measures that can be implemented at both domestic and international level, especially for key raw materials such as rare earth elements. at the heart of this strategy should be an industrial innovation strategy based on resource efficiency and recycling, the only measures that adequately address the triple challenge of ensuring future competitiveness, sustainability and security of supply. these are challenges facing not only the governments but all the entities involved, challenges that must be met with research and development (r & d) to replace them, to which the universities must be called upon to contribute, as the research pole that they are by nature.

in writing. − a sustainable, efficient and competitive european industrial policy, as expressed in the eu2020 strategy, requires a concerted policy on raw materials. this report focuses mainly on access to strategic raw materials, in particular rare earth elements, with a dimension on efficiency, reduction of resources used, recycling, reuse and waste management. the report also calls for the creation of a european innovation partnership for raw materials, which would include an internal and external dimension of raw materials' sustainability. at the internal level, it calls for greater cooperation between member states, while at the external level, it calls for partnerships with poor countries, with the brics, and with rich countries. regular listing of critical raw materials and an assessment of their risk, the establishment of a methodology to assess the current state and future developments of raw material efficiency, the creation of a legal framework to encourage and promote the recycling of raw materials are examples of the measures proposed in this report for more effective governance and coordination. finally, i would stress the importance of combating the volatility of agricultural prices in order to guarantee a fair price for all players in the sector and for consumers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the present and future management of fisheries in the black sea because it contains proposals which should make it possible to achieve tangible results in terms of protecting the livelihoods of fishermen and guaranteeing the economic development of coastal areas and protecting the ecological balance and fisheries resources.
in writing. − joint management of fisheries resources and coordination of efforts between the various actors in the fisheries sector are becoming increasingly important. unlike other areas of the world, the black sea has not benefited from this integrated management, which has been damaging the way in which the activity is developed in the region and threatens to put at risk both traditional ways of life and the survival of some of the species caught. the politically complex project of institutional coordination for the management of the sector, to be shared by all the riparian states, possibly by creating an autonomous regional fisheries management organization, seems to be of the greatest importance and could constitute an important stimulus so that, also in other matters, there can be similar coordination between the same countries.
in writing. - this report, by iliana malinova iotova, deals with the current and future management of fisheries in the black sea. concern for fisheries resources in the european union has been a constant in this european parliament, which has on several occasions debated the problems of the common fisheries policy. an integrated maritime policy requires control measures and investment. the situation is complicated in the black sea: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the fisheries sector. it is therefore necessary to set up a black sea fisheries management organisation to monitor this activity and to provide the basis for scientific research and the development of a regional database on fishing activity, in order to enhance the resource rather than deplete it. i therefore wholeheartedly support this report, which aims to establish a regulatory framework for solving this problem in the short term and within the eastern partnerships, which can be applied in other regions.
in writing. - the report has positive aspects in relation to the necessary definition of the medium-term development framework for fisheries in the black sea region. since there is no coordinated action in this region among all the fisheries actors, institutionalised coordination could ensure tangible results in terms of protecting fishermen's livelihoods, ensuring the economic development of coastal areas and protecting the ecological balance and fishery resources in the basin. this applies, of course, not only to the eu member states in the black sea region but also to the other four coastal states. however, we cannot agree with some of the proposals in the report, such as the call for the creation of a european coast guard function. we do not deny the need for increased cooperation in a number of areas covered in the report. however, we do not think that this is the appropriate framework for developing such cooperation. we also disagree with the excessive focus on the role that the european commission may play in defining the future framework for fisheries management in the region. this is part of a centralised approach to fisheries management, of which the current cfp is an example, which has shown its limits and problems to the full, in contrast to the necessary local management which we have always advocated.
in writing. − the black sea region is strategically important for the european union in view of its geographical location, which encompasses three eu member states (greece, romania and bulgaria) and several important partners, including russia and turkey. fisheries cooperation between the countries of the black sea region represents considerable progress in conservation management and effective dispute settlement in the black sea basin. the creation of a black sea regional fisheries management organisation is very important for the management of fisheries in the black sea. this body will allow the coexistence of fishing practices with the sole objective of recovering and preserving the fishery resources of the black sea. as eu members, bulgaria and romania are required to apply certain measures for the conservation of stocks in their waters. however, these measures cannot be fully effective without being applied also in the other black sea states. the creation of such an organisation will affirm the eu's commitment to the region in terms of sustainable fisheries development, as it will have long-term beneficial effects for all black sea states.
in writing. - the first objective of this report is to set out the medium- and long-term framework for the development of fisheries in the black sea region. an in-depth analysis of the fisheries situation in the black sea shows the need to find the most effective form of cooperation between all the countries in the region. the specific nature of the black sea's biodiversity also requires a common approach to the management of this unique basin. this requires institutionalised cooperation between these countries with regard to the conservation of stocks. through this initiative, the measures provided for in the eu's common fisheries policy will be implemented throughout the black sea basin. this argument is supported by scientific research, which shows that institutionalised cooperation is vital for the sustainable exploitation of marine biological resources in the context of sustainable development. it is important to stress that the creation of such an organisation will affirm the eu's commitment in the region in terms of sustainable fisheries development, as it will have long-term beneficial effects for all black sea states.
in writing. − the challenges posed by the management of the black sea must be addressed by the six states that share it, including two eu member states: romania and bulgaria. the various states concerned must in fact strengthen cooperation and dialogue in order to find joint solutions to ensure a stable, sustainable and adapted fisheries sector in the black sea basin, the protection of the ecological balance and fisheries resources in the region and a more effective fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
in writing. the environmental disaster in the gulf of mexico, the result of a colossal oil spill into the sea, has raised concerns about the risks, responsibilities and legislation governing oil exploration and extraction. the report to be voted on tomorrow reflects the eu's responsibility to ensure the protection of its coasts and its capacity to respond to such environmental disasters. i welcome the introduction of my suggestions, particularly as regards european coordination and the role of emsa. in terms of coordination at eu level and with neighbouring countries, there is a need to ensure best practice and harmonisation of the various approaches across the various regions of the eu, both at accident prevention and response level. i would like to highlight the role of the european maritime safety agency, based in lisbon, which provides technical support and assistance in the field of maritime safety and protection in the area of pollution caused by ships. the report proposes to extend the powers of the european maritime agency to include monitoring, information sharing and coordination of prevention and response.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the safety challenges of offshore oil and gas exploration because it is necessary to prevent the occurrence of accidents similar to those experienced off the coast of the usa, in particular by approving safety plans before operations start, including independent third party verification procedures. it is also important to ensure that the polluter pays principle applies to all damage to the marine environment and biodiversity and that oil and gas companies can be held liable for any environmental damage.
in writing. − in the eu, more than 90% of oil and 60% of gas are extracted from offshore operations, most of which take place in the north sea. it is essential that the union creates the conditions for the safest possible oil exploitation, knowing the importance of oil extraction to the countries that extract it and the dangers involved (as can be seen from the terrible consequences of oil spill accidents). to this end, it is important that there is adequate legislation, including basic safety standards for offshore oil and gas production, ensuring the safety of their extraction and supply in the eu. as a portuguese, i cannot help recalling the prestige disaster which deeply affected the galician coast, and i would like to draw attention to the fact that the measures now proposed should not be limited to oil exploration and extraction but also to its transport and supply, since oil tanker disasters are unfortunately more frequent than we would like and it is also important to review safety standards in order to reduce the likelihood of such disasters.
in writing. − this report focuses on the safety challenges of offshore oil and gas operations. the recent environmental disasters the gulf of mexico oil spill (one of the largest environmental disasters ever and the largest oil spill in us history) in april 2010 (bp) and the north sea oil spill in august 2011 (shell) have put the debate on the safety conditions in which oil and gas extraction companies operate on the agenda. we all recognise that the supply of oil and gas is fundamental to the quality of life of all citizens in general and of europeans in particular. however, safety measures for workers and construction standards must be guaranteed to prevent fuel leakage that could harm the environment. it is therefore essential that there is a simplified legal framework covering drilling operations and helping to solve the problems of environmental pollution. while i recognize that this is a rather complex matter, i welcome the presentation of this report, which i voted in favour of, as it safeguards the environmental aspects and the safety of workers in this activity, putting the public interest above the private interest.
in writing. - this report follows on from earlier debates in parliament on this same subject, in which the need for effective regulatory and control measures to prevent accidents similar to the gulf of mexico in the usa has been stressed. numerous accidents have already shown that offshore oil and gas activities and exploration cannot continue to be carried out with the central objective of maximising profits for the economic groups involved in such activities. this puts the safety of workers on the platforms and the people as well as natural ecosystems at risk. the report makes proposals which are generally positive, even if there are some contradictions in one case or another. it is essential to define very clear rules to protect the environment, the public interest, the workers involved and the neighbouring populations. it is also necessary and urgent to take the necessary measures to ensure compliance with them through effective supervision and control.
in writing. - the report seeks to stress the need for effective regulatory and control measures to prevent accidents similar to those which have already occurred, particularly in the usa. based on experience and the numerous accidents which have already shown that offshore oil and gas activities and exploitation cannot continue to be carried out with the main objective of maximising profits for the economic groups involved in such activities, at the expense of the safety of their workers and the population, a wide range of proposals are put forward which are generally positive, even if in some cases there are some contradictions. but it is essential that there be very clear rules in the defence of the environment, the public interest, the workers involved, the neighbouring populations. it is also necessary and urgent to take the necessary measures to ensure compliance with them through effective supervision and control.
in writing. − offshore sources account for more than 90% of oil and 60% of gas produced in the eu and norway. however, the numerous and serious accidents have shown that offshore exploitation cannot continue under the same rules and be dictated solely by the economic interests of private groups. the report calls on the commission to reduce the damage thresholds and to impose a strict liability regime. it also considers that operators should be required to prove that they have sufficient financial capacity to ensure that environmental damage caused by their activity, including those that may be caused by high impact and low probability incidents, is compensated. it stressed the risks of this activity to the health and safety of its workers and recommended continued regulation and an insurance scheme appropriate to the risks of workers. it also called for the treatment of workers within the same company to be avoided and for all workers in the offshore sector to be covered by the same rules. as the report is moving in this positive direction, i voted in favour of it. however, although it is not the subject of the report, i stress the need to rethink energy sources.
in writing. − this report emphasises the need to implement a package to monitor oil and gas exploration in eu seas in the national legislation of each member state. such measures are necessary to ensure that offshore oil and gas is properly exploited and that in these times of crisis this industry continues to prosper, without ever forgetting the continuation of the good fuel market, but also that the safety and well-being of citizens continue to prosper. i believe that the provisions of this report are of great importance in order to discuss in the member states the safety measures for offshore oil and gas exploration at all levels in order to avoid ecological disasters, since these do not respect the land or sea borders of any state. an independent body is therefore needed to monitor regularly the efficiency and the proper functioning of oil companies and the preventive measures taken by them. this report also addresses and clarifies issues related to the transport and exploitation of offshore oil and gas fields.
in writing. − national supplies of oil and natural gas make an important contribution to energy consumption and to the eu's energy security. in the eu, more than 90% of oil and 60% of gas is extracted from offshore operations. the activity is not evenly distributed across the eu and the vast majority of operations take place in the north sea. in the eu, only two member states account for approximately 80% of crude oil production, while norway produces more than all 27 eu member states combined. the challenges to safety in oil and gas exploration are great. although the allocation of operating licences is a matter for member states, it is essential to strive for high safety standards throughout the eu. in this respect, this report presents an important set of proposals to the member states on safety. the commission is also proposing that the european parliament should be given the right to vote on the proposals for the future of the european union.
in writing. - the adoption of safety measures for offshore oil and gas exploration is a priority in environmental protection. the risks involved in any extraction of these raw materials can and must be controlled in order to ensure not only the energy sustainability of europe but also the protection of environmental resources. the emphasis is on measures such as the exchange of information between the various actors, the creation of appropriate plans to deal with the risks involved, taking into account the intervention of workers particularly able to identify some dangers that might otherwise not be considered, and, by way of example, the introduction of accountability mechanisms that encourage the parties involved to ensure the safety of their premises (and also, when adopting a model of risk socialization, to ensure compliance with safety standards by other operators).
in writing. - articles 191 and 194 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union state that member states are responsible for determining the conditions for exploiting their energy resources and must act on the basis of preventive action to safeguard the environment and energy security. i am voting in favour of the report because i believe it contains suggestions for preventing accidents in a preventive manner. all phases of work, from the start of operations to decommissioning, must have a rigorous and structured safety, health and environmental plan to ensure the maintenance of the marine ecosystem. i would also like to stress that the procedures must follow a common set of eu criteria and that the farms must be subject to regular inspections by independent experts. it is important to ensure that inspection bodies are equipped with the most advanced risk monitoring methods and technologies. although a network of good practice already exists, i believe it is important to boost interregional forums, joint meetings between political authorities and exploiting companies and to encourage greater multilateral cooperation for a better sharing of knowledge. finally, i believe that workers should be involved in the definition of working conditions, and that a preventive culture in the field of health and safety at work should be promoted.
in writing. - there is a growing movement in europe towards women's participation in the labour market, which is also manifested in the world of small and medium-sized enterprises. although there are improvements compared to the past, the data show that the optimum level of gender equality in the area of entrepreneurship is not yet reached. women have more difficulty in starting up a business, either because of deep-rooted prejudices in society or because of the coordination of employment and family life, coupled with a severe economic and social situation in europe and the world. in this sense, i consider it extremely important to combat this status quo through policies to support women entrepreneurs, reducing the gender gap, creating vocational guidance and training structures at all levels, improving access to finance and social measures to allow free choice in conjunction with family life. i also welcome the creation of crossborder cooperation programmes to support women entrepreneurs, which will enable the exchange of experience, the rationalisation of resources and the sharing of best practice. only through strong and concerted policies can women participate in the world of entrepreneurship on a more equal footing.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it advocates information and training campaigns specifically for women, so that they can make better use of the funding opportunities available through european programmes. the conclusions of recent studies, which prove that women entrepreneurs are more prudent than men when it comes to taking economic and financial risks, should be taken into account in accessing finance.
in writing. the principle of equality is, alongside freedom, one of the pillars of democratic states governed by the rule of law. it is because i believe in the importance of the principle of equality that i understand that men and women deserve equal opportunities and should have equal conditions in the business world. europe needs entrepreneurs, whether men or women. but entrepreneurship is not a given. you create the conditions for yours first. for women, this is done by removing the remaining barriers - such as the negative impact of motherhood on career progression - rather than by regulatory imposition. i also do not think that this is the right place to bring up again the issue of quotas for women in management and business leadership, which was voted on by this parliament at the last part-session.
in writing. - this report, by marina yannakoudakis, focuses on women's entrepreneurship in small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). the role of smes as the economic engine of the european union (eu) - especially in times of crisis such as the present one - has been discussed on several occasions in this plenary. this report, however, draws our attention to another reality. the reality of female entrepreneurship. if times are hard enough on their own, they become even more troubling for those who struggle to thrive in a world hitherto dominated by men. this report, while recognising not only the value of women entrepreneurs in small and medium-sized enterprises but also their capacity for initiative and versatility in undertaking business tasks, particularly in administration, notes the existence of many obstacles which they have to overcome to achieve their objectives. i welcome the adoption of this report which not only recognises the role of women but also mentions their contribution to job creation and benefits to local economies. it also encourages member states to adopt good practices and guidelines to facilitate women's entrepreneurship, particularly in terms of facilitating access to finance.
in writing. - the term entrepreneurship has become widespread and commonplace. he's not innocent. entrepreneurship is a concept: the creation of one's own job; the idea that employment (or lack thereof) is not a social problem for which society and the state (its organized expression) must seek solutions, but a problem unique to the individual which the individual must, as he can and knows, solve. the gradual introduction of this concept is inseparable from the degradation of labour relations, social and labour rights, and the concrete and real destruction of jobs, particularly through the destruction of productive sectors, as is happening in portugal. the situation of women, who continue to live in many cases in a disadvantaged position, being victims of discrimination in their workplaces, is particularly worrying. the wage gap between the average wages of men and women in the european union is around 18%, a figure that is being aggravated by the crisis. this report misses many of these points, is full of contradictions, and that is why we did not support it. we recognize the importance of supporting smes, but we cannot ignore the growing reality of the so-called selfemployed, who are in fact a doorway to precarious employment.
in writing. - although the word entrepreneurship is being widely used, we cannot replace or disconnect from this concept, which also incorporates the idea of creating the workplace itself, from the current degradation of labour relations, given the deep and serious offensive that is being experienced, both at the level of social and labour rights and in the concrete and real destruction of jobs, in particular through the destruction of productive sectors, as is the case in portugal. the report therefore contains a number of contradictions, which is why we did not vote in favour of it. and while we recognize the importance of supporting micro, small and mediumsized enterprises, we think it is necessary to draw attention to the growing reality of the so-called selfemployed, who are in fact a door open to precarious employment relationships, with which the rights of those who work are intended to be destroyed. we are particularly concerned about the situation of women, who in many cases continue to be disadvantaged and are subject to discrimination at work at various levels, not to mention the wage gap between the average wages of men and women in the european union, which is around 18%, a figure which this crisis is likely to exacerbate.
in writing. − this own-initiative report makes a number of recommendations to promote member states' policies to support smes, taking into account the needs and the strategic role that women entrepreneurs can play. the report recommends that women's participation in the market be promoted through training programmes and project funding, tax benefits, exchange of good practice between countries and anti-discrimination policies in access to credit. it also aims to combat false selfemployment and to encourage the creation of programmes to help people, mainly women engaged in domestic work, carers or other services, who are neither employed nor selfemployed, to switch to the selfemployed scheme or to set up their own businesses. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. − in the business world, those who run their own businesses are often more committed and spend more time than their workers. in the case of women, the sacrifices may be even greater, for they may have to overcome discrimination in a traditionally male environment. many have to balance their own personal aspirations with their dedication to their family. despite all this, women have clearly demonstrated their capabilities in the workplace. recognising women's capabilities in the workplace and helping them through means such as an eu report to strengthen their situation are key. this will not only encourage women to enter the business world but also ensure that they move on an equal footing in an environment where there can be no room for sex discrimination.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on women entrepreneurs in small and medium-sized enterprises, which sets out a series of measures aimed at full gender parity. although in many sectors this is not a problem, active policies are needed for entrepreneurship. in this respect, i agree with the rapporteur who stresses the need to optimise access to financial and educational support, urging regional and local authorities to make better use of the funding opportunities available to women entrepreneurs through special grants, venture capital, social security arrangements and interest rate subsidies that allow fair and equitable access to finance, such as the european microfinance instrument progress, which offers micro-credit up to eur 25 000 to micro-enterprises and those wishing to start their own small business and who do not have access to traditional banking services, thus supporting the unemployed who do not have access to bank credit.

madam president, the number of homeless people and those living below the poverty line has been increasing steadily in recent years in several member states. the economic, financial and social crisis and the increase in unemployment have aggravated this problem, as everyone has already diagnosed. we also all agree that this phenomenon is the negation of important values of the european union: respect for human dignity and respect for fundamental rights. in my country, for example, which is subject to a strong austerity measure, the concept of homelessness, according to the national plan, includes people who come to ask for help to get a meal. and the number of people seeking help with eating has increased by more than 20 percent since 2008. the greatest increase is seen in the families and the needy, whose living situation has been altered by unemployment and also by bank debt. this is just one example of the seriousness of the situation. last year, the european parliament adopted a written declaration on a european union strategy for the homeless. in this declaration, parliament called for the european union to have a strategy, backed up by national and regional strategies, with the long-term objective of ending the situation of people sleeping on the streets and long-term homelessness. national strategies should focus on preventive measures, but also on concrete actions to improve the quality of services provided to the homeless and the availability of affordable housing. it is also clear that this european strategy must be compatible with the social housing policy of the member states. we have taken note of the commissioner's words and have noted the point he has made. i would like to conclude by urging the european commission to make a strong effort to coordinate the action of the member states and the regional authorities to combat this social injustice.

in writing. − the european union, recognising the very serious social consequences of the current economic and financial crisis, has set up the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to provide additional support to workers affected by structural changes in world trade. this report is based on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the egf, in accordance with point 28 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the european parliament, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline and sound financial management (application egf/2010/007 at/steiermark and niederösterreich, austria). in june 2011, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of austria to support the reintegration of workers made redundant as a result of the global crisis, following the abovementioned application submitted on 9 march 2010. this is the sixth application submitted under the eu budget for 2011, with a budget of eur 8 284 908, and aims to mitigate the social impact of the dismissal of 1 180 workers from 54 steel companies in the region of styria and lower austria. i approve this aid, hoping for a rapid recovery of the austrian metal industry.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the number of companies relocating is increasing, taking advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, with harmful effects for countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid is now to be granted to austria, which has submitted a request for assistance in respect of 1 180 redundancies (of which 356 are potential beneficiaries of assistance) in 54 enterprises in nace rev. 2 division 24 (basic metal industries) in the nuts ii regions of styria (at22) and lower austria (at12), austria.

in writing. - the application submitted by austria for assistance from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) concerns 1 180 redundancies (of which 356 are potential beneficiaries of assistance) in 54 enterprises operating in division 24 (basic metal industries) in the regions of styria and lower austria. according to the commission's assessment, this application fulfils all the eligibility criteria defined by law. regulation (ec) no 546/2009 of the european parliament and of the council of 18 june 2009 amending regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 establishing the european globalisation adjustment fund temporarily extended the scope of the egf to cover situations such as this one where, as a direct consequence of the global economic and financial crisis, at least 500 redundancies occur in a nine-month period, in particular in small and medium-sized enterprises, in a division at nace level 2, in a region or in two regions adjacent to nuts ii. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, in the hope that assistance for workers made redundant can be provided quickly and efficiently.
in writing. - this report supports the mobilisation of the egf in favour of austria to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. this is the seventh application examined under the 2011 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 1 221 128 from the egf for austria. it concerns 167 redundancies (74 of which were potential beneficiaries of aid) in the printed circuit board (pcb) manufacturing company at&s in the upper east styria region during the four-month reference period from 1 september to 31 december 2009. the application, egf/2010/008 at/at&s (austria), was submitted to the commission on 11 march 2010 and supplemented by additional information up to 22 february 2011. it was based on the intervention criterion in article 2 (c) of the egf regulation, which allows applicants to derogate from the requirements of article 2 (a) and (b) in small labour markets or in exceptional circumstances, provided that redundancies have a serious impact on employment and the local economy. in this case, the austrian authorities have specified that their application seeks a derogation from article 2 (a) which sets a limit of at least 500 redundancies in a four-month period.

in writing. the report is intended to respond to a request from the european commission to mobilise eur 610 000 from the fund to cover the commission's technical assistance expenditure. according to the commission, this amount is intended to cover the following activities: - control aims to collect data on applications received and financed, as well as on proposed and implemented measures, and will update and print the statistical picture of the egf. - information the egf website will be regularly updated and expanded, and translated into all the official eu languages. press briefings will be published and the egf annual report will be prepared, translated, printed and distributed. - creation of a knowledge base aims to establish a standardised system for egf applications and their processing, which will make it possible to simplify access to reports for different needs. - administrative and technical assistance the egf contact group of experts, which has 27 members, one from each member state, will hold two meetings. - exchange of best practice between member states. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval, and the council will be consulted on the matter.

in writing. − in the context of the european globalisation adjustment fund, the commission adopted on 22 june 2011 a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf, concerning the mobilisation of eur 610 000 to cover technical assistance expenditure of the commission. in accordance with article 8 (1) of the legal basis, 0,35% of the annual ceiling of the egf may be made available each year, on the initiative of the commission, for technical assistance expenditure. a maximum of eur 1,75 million may be used annually to cover the implementation needs of the fund indicated. the commission justifies the transfer of this amount on the basis of the need to cover the monitoring of applications received and financed, information activities (maintenance of the egf website and its translation into all official eu languages), the creation of a knowledge base, administrative and technical assistance, the exchange of best practices between member states and evaluation. in view of the favourable opinion of the letter from the committee on employment and social affairs and the approval of the committee on budgets, i have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 established the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to support workers who lose their jobs as a result of structural changes in the global economy. with a budget of eur 500 million in 2011, the egf has been an important instrument of support for workers in a wide range of member states, justifying the creation of networks that enhance the exchange of information and strategic synergies between the economic and social partners on this financing mechanism. article 8 of the egf regulation provides that a maximum of 0,35% of the annual amount may be made available each year to finance technical assistance activities, including the provision of information and technical guidance to member states in the egf analysis, evaluation and monitoring processes. i approve this report, noting that the ec has only requested the mobilisation of eur 610 000.00 out of the total amount of eur 1 750 000.00 provided for in the annual budget.

in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the effects of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. on 1 may 2009, the scope of the egf was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when we are faced with this serious crisis, of which the increase in unemployment is one of the main consequences, the eu should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs overnight. i have therefore supported the present report on the mobilisation of the egf in the netherlands to support workers made redundant in 26 printing and recording companies in the noord-holland and flevoland regions.
in writing. - having regard to the request for assistance submitted by the netherlands concerning 551 redundancies, all of them potential recipients of assistance, in 26 enterprises in nace rev. 2 division 18 (printing and reproduction of recorded media) in the two nuts ii regions of noord-holland (nl 32) and flevoland (nl 23), i voted in favour of the resolution, in that i agree with the european commission proposal, with the respective amendments introduced by the european parliament. i also agree that under article 6 of the egf regulation, it is necessary to ensure that the egf supports the individual reintegration of workers made redundant into working life. i would like to reiterate, however, that egf assistance should not replace actions which are the responsibility of firms by virtue of national legislation or collective agreements, nor measures to restructure firms or sectors. measures financed by the egf should aim at the creation of long-term jobs.
in writing. - several printing and recording industries in the netherlands have submitted requests for assistance. in the present case, 551 workers were made redundant in the regions of noord-holland and flevoland. in view of other resolutions adopted on the same date, this is not an isolated case. unfortunately, several industries in the same sector have had to lay off workers, creating social emergency situations which the egf is also trying to alleviate. in this case as in the previous ones, i hope that the mobilisation of the fund will make a real contribution to the reintegration of workers in difficulty and will promote the creation of more sustainable jobs.
in writing. - the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in accordance with point 28 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the european parliament (ep), the council and the commission on budgetary discipline and sound financial management (application egf/2010/030 nl/ noord-holland and flevoland division 18', netherlands). in june 2011, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of the netherlands to support the reintegration of workers made redundant as a result of the global crisis. this is the 12th application under the eu budget for 2011, submitted to the commission on 20 december 2010, for the mobilisation of eur 1 849 086, which is intended to mitigate the social impact of the 551 redundancies in 26 companies in the printing and reproduction of recorded media sector in the nut ii region, noord-holland (nl 32) and flevoland (nl 23). i am voting in favour of this proposal, which achieves the objectives which led the eu to set up this fund, and i hope that the economic fabric of the regions mentioned above will be restored quickly.
in writing. − the report concerns the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund, relating to an application from the netherlands which was approved by the european commission on 28 june 2011. this is the 12th application to be examined under the 2011 budget and is a new proposal in favour of the netherlands to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. this mobilisation corresponds to a total amount of eur 1 849 086 from the egf and concerns 551 redundancies, all potential beneficiaries of assistance, in 26 printing and recording companies. the application was submitted to the commission on 20 december 2010 and supplemented by additional information by 3 march 2011. it was based on the criteria laid down in the egf regulation, which make intervention conditional on the occurrence of at least 500 redundancies in enterprises in one region or in two contiguous nuts ii regions of a member state. as always, we felt it was more important to have an intervention before the closure of the companies. we voted in favour of the proposal to mobilise the vital support for the workers made redundant.

in writing. the proposal for a regulation (remit regulation on the integrity and transparency of energy markets) establishes a legal framework at eu level to prevent market abuse and manipulation in the energy (gas and electricity) sector. in view of the strategic importance of the energy market and the tendency to abuse it, the commission's proposal and its sectoral approach to prevent market abuse are welcome. the structure of the proposal and the mechanisms proposed for implementing the regulation are, as the rapporteur says, appropriate for regulating a market of increasing importance and which is intended to move towards the integration of national energy markets into a single european market.
in writing. - this report, by mr jorgo chatzimarkakis, focuses on a proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the integrity and transparency of energy markets. the energy market integrity and transparency regulation (remit) will apply to contracts for the production, supply and transport of natural gas and electricity and aims to prevent abuse in wholesale energy markets, thereby protecting consumers. the newly created agency for the cooperation of energy regulators (acre) will play a key role in monitoring these markets in partnership with the regulatory authorities of the member states and will report annually to the european commission. energy costs, both for individuals and for the business sector, represent a substantial share of expenditure. it is therefore necessary to avoid unfair practices that lead to price increases and undermine the confidence of potential investors. this is a proposal which deserves my support because it represents a significant step forward in defending the rights of consumers in one of the most important sectors of the world economy.
in writing. - first, they liberalized the energy sector. the consequences are well known: the formation of private monopolies, high prices, little attention to consumers, fabulous profits. the european parliament, which supported this option, now wants to pass new rules to prevent abuse in wholesale energy markets and, it is said, to protect consumers. the monitoring of these markets will be done at eu level to help member states prevent, detect and punish abusive practices, according to the commission proposal. they forget that they have contributed to this by facilitating privatizations and monopolistic concentration in the sector. by promoting deregulation processes in the name of the god of the market, with disastrous consequences (as attested to by several studies). this regulation on the integrity and transparency of energy markets (remit) will apply to trade in wholesale energy products, in particular to contracts and derivatives relating to the production, supply and transport of natural gas and electricity. they now say that energy must remain accessible to all, as it is a key sector for the economy. but they hide the fact that the liberalization they have promoted has led to serious problems and that energy poverty is a sad reality for consumers, smes have seen their production costs rise significantly, for which there are still no answers.

in writing. − this report assesses the commission's monitoring of the application of european union law in 2009. it focuses on the commission's key role as guardian of the treaties and its power and duty to bring actions against member states which fail to comply with obligations imposed on them by the treaty. the report calls on the commission to propose a procedural law in the form of a regulation under the new legal basis of article 298 tfeu in order to strengthen citizens' rights and ensure transparency. such a procedural right shall in no way limit the commission's discretion and shall be limited to ensuring that the commission, in the exercise of its power, respects the principles of an open, efficient and independent european administration as set out in article 298 tfeu and article 41 of the charter of fundamental rights of the eu.
in writing. − the ways in which community legislation is implemented, applied and enforced have long been a matter of concern to both european legislators and legal practitioners. their volume and complexity tend to increase while their intelligibility and applicability may be in question. to address these concerns, the lisbon treaty introduced a number of legal bases aimed at improving the way in which community law is legislated and applied. the resolution respects the commission's key role as the initiator of infringement proceedings against member states which fail to comply with the provisions of the treaty by focusing on its two phases: administrative and judicial. the commission's discretion in this type of procedure has been the subject of reflection by experts, with the rapporteur suggesting the need to adopt a procedural law which would not, however, limit it. this is just one of the problems in which legal and jurisdictional tension between the european institutions and the member states is evident and which reinforces the urgency of monitoring the adoption and application of community law and of seeking to improve both its formulation and its systematic coherence.
in writing. − this report, by eva lichtenberger, focuses on the 27th annual report on the monitoring of the application of european union law by the commission in 2009. the commission, as guardian of the treaties, is responsible for ensuring that they are complied with by the member states and is empowered to impose sanctions on those who fail to fulfil the obligations imposed on them by virtue of their signature. a more efficient europe implies the active participation of citizens, who must be made aware of the need to lodge complaints when treaties are not respected, particularly in the area of the environment, and of all violations of fundamental rights, in order to avoid harmful consequences for citizens. however, there should be more transparency in the handling of citizens' complaints by continuous information on the progress of the complaints. an ever stronger eu means that each member state, individually, and all of us in general, must take responsibility. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report and call on all member states to observe scrupulously the treaties to which they are parties. only then will we have more and better europe.

in writing. − transparency is one of the fundamental pillars of participatory democracy, complementing representative democracy, with access to documents and information being one of the ways of ensuring citizens' participation in the democratic process, as well as preventing and combating corruption. with the adoption of the treaty of lisbon, a new constitutional framework for institutional transparency in the eu was introduced, based on an open, effective and independent european administration, establishing a strong fundamental right of access to documents of the eu institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, so that decisions to refuse access to documents should be based on clearly and rigorously defined, reasonably explained and well-reasoned exceptions. this report argues that regulation (ec) no 1049/2001 should be revised in order to define and reduce the exceptions rigorously and to ensure that they do not undermine the transparency guaranteed by the treaties and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, and that this revision should strengthen the right of access to documents. it also advocates the need to strike an appropriate balance between transparency and data protection. i therefore support this report.
