in writing. - every five years, during the european commission's term of office, the college of commissioners of the european union's executive body is appointed. under the lisbon treaty, the number of commissioners corresponds to the number of member states - currently 27 - and is approved by the european parliament in two stages: first, on a proposal from the european council, elect the president of the commission; the council shall, after consulting the president, examine the applications proposed by the council. the procedure for ep approval is governed by annex xvii to the rules of procedure and comprises the following steps: examination of curricula vitae and declarations of financial interests, reply to a set of written questions, a three-hour public hearing, evaluation by parliamentary committees and evaluation by the conference of presidents. this report, drawn up by andrew duff, suggests a number of minor amendments to the rules of procedure with regard to hearings of commissioners-designate. i welcome the amendments to the rules of procedure which have been tabled, as they make a significant contribution to improving the quality of our commissioners, and they will be of great benefit to the citizens of europe.
in writing. - the rules of procedure laying down the current rules for commissioners' hearings seem to me to be adequate, but they do require some adjustments, which are provided for in this amendment. the adjustments are intended to provide greater transparency and to improve procedures. the proposed amendments are purely technical and will improve the way in which hearings are conducted, without introducing any substantive changes at political level. i would point out that a second and final hearing may be called if it becomes apparent during the first hearing that it is necessary to extend the examination of the commissioner-designate.
in writing. - this report on the amendment of rules 106 and 192 and annex xvii to the rules of procedure of the european parliament, concerning the hearings of commissioners-designate, reflects the strengthening of the powers of the european parliament in its rules of procedure following the treaty of lisbon. the european commission is the government of the union and the european parliament cannot fail to exercise its power of scrutiny when it comes to the composition of that government. i agree with the procedure proposed for submitting two joint questions to each of the commissioners-designate, drawn up by the conference of committee chairmen: the first on matters of general competence, european commitment and personal independence and the second on the management of the portfolio and cooperation with parliament, with the committee responsible responsible responsible for drawing up three other questions, and the right for each committee to draw up two questions in the case of joint committees. the proposal to allocate the greater part of the time to the political groups seems to me appropriate. for all these reasons, i voted in favour.

in writing. - throughout europe, people live on the streets in undignified conditions, exposed to the elements and the cruelty of the societies in which we live. the designation "homeless" euphemistically replaces the more crude terms "beggar" and "vagabond" that were once used to describe people who descended into similar states of destitution. rather than devise major european strategies to put an end to this scourge, i believe that global thinking must be accompanied by local action. and for this, no one is better than the social solidarity institutions, which are already active on the ground, really know the concrete people, are beyond statistics and can identify the best ways to guide them to a better life. without abandoning its programmes and studies and measures on this subject, the european union should seek to act wherever possible through the institutions already active on the ground.
in writing. − the existence of homelessness is not a new situation, having its origins in the current economic and financial crisis. they've always been there. we used to see them sleeping in subway stations, under bridges, in building entrances, in run-down buildings, etc. the present crisis has only exacerbated a situation which is deplorable in social terms and degrading in human terms. if a few decades ago they were people with drug addiction, alcoholism, bohemian beggars, today, with the worsening of economic and financial conditions, in particular the high interest rates that prevent many citizens from being able to meet their obligations to the banks, the paradigm has changed. we found young people, women, families! and in the face of this situation, the states remain passive. at most, they are driven from the city centers to the outskirts so as not to be seen by tourists or near the financial centers. we all have an obligation to protect the weak. member states, with the eu's assistance through the european social fund, have a duty to minimise this violation of the charter of fundamental human rights, which enshrines the end of homelessness. in these terms, i wholeheartedly support this motion for a resolution which seeks to implement a strategy for the homeless whose existence we should be ashamed of.

in writing. the resolution addresses the relevant problem of anthropogenic emissions of gases into the atmosphere, other than carbon dioxide, which are likely to interfere with the earth's climate. the almost exclusive focus on carbon dioxide has helped to obscure, both in public perception and at the level of policy initiative, the reality that other compounds can contribute to the so-called greenhouse effect. this attention is certainly instrumental in enabling so-called market solutions, such as the carbon market, and feeding the powerful interests that are emerging to dominate this business further. this resolution undoubtedly has this merit: to draw attention to the consequences of other pollutants and to the need to take measures to control them. methane (ch4), nitrous oxide (n2o), hydrofluorocarbons (hfcs), perfluorocarbons (pfcs), sulphur hexafluoride (sf6), halogenated hydrocarbons with a high global warming potential, black carbon (fuel) are some of these pollutants. the reference, however shy, to solutions other than market solutions (and their positive results) is equally important and should be valued. as well as the reference to the misuse of the kyoto protocol flexibility mechanisms such as the clean development mechanism (cdm). for these reasons we voted in favour of the resolution.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution in which parliament points out to the european commission, among other things, that rapid regulatory strategies are available to reduce the production and consumption of hydrochlorofluorocarbons and to reduce emissions of black carbon and of the gases which lead to the formation of tropospheric ozone. these strategies can be started within 2-3 years and, to a large extent, can be implemented within 5-10 years, which may produce the desired climate reaction within decades or sooner, in particular for some of the hydrofluorocarbons, at a public price of only 5 to 10 cents per tonne, whereas the carbon price currently exceeds 13 euros per tonne. the european parliament, faced with a race against time, urges the commission to inform it of any steps it may take to introduce new combat options into the process quickly so that lost time can be made up.
on behalf of the s&d group. we hope in this parliament that the conflict in libya is close to an end. the brave libyan people deserve that the suffering caused by 42 years of brutal dictatorship and six months of war will give way to a free and democratic country. to do that, gaddafi and his henchmen must be found and brought to justice. the european union, which has been present in benghazi since early may, was quick to raise its flag in tripoli as soon as the capital was liberated. it should also now swiftly unfreeze the libyan assets referred to, under the supervision of the security council, and seek to identify other financial resources diverted by the gaddafi regime so that they do not fuel the destabilisation of the country and to ensure their return to the libyan authorities. the high representative for foreign affairs and the european external action service must respond swiftly to libyan requests for assistance in the interim governance and transition to democracy, ensuring the necessary coordination between member states so that national agendas do not overlap with a coherent political strategy of the union itself. it is also to leave no doubt about the european union's respect for the sovereignty of the libyan people and to make possible the coordinating role of the united nations in coordinating the various international contributions to the process of economic and institutional reconstruction in libya. the immediate priority for promoting security and reconciliation in libya will certainly have to be the disarmament and social and professional reintegration of civilians who have been forced to take up arms. the european union can offer its experience and play a major role in the disarmament, demobilization and reintegration effort and thus in supporting security sector reform, as well as in preparing constitutional and electoral processes, building the justice system and institutional capacity building of civil society itself. the credibility of a libyan interim government will depend above all on its ability to fulfil its promises to build a democratic state that respects the human rights and fundamental freedoms of all citizens - libyans as well as foreigners - and in particular the migrants who suffered so much under gaddafi and who have continued to suffer until now, often being unjustly accused of being mercenaries in the service of gaddafi just because of the colour of their skin. we therefore welcome the recent declarations by the president of the national transitional council, jalil, in tripoli, announcing that libya will be a moderate muslim country, and we hope that this will mean that sharia, enshrined in a first constitutional declaration as the primary source of law, will be interpreted in such a way as to ensure full respect for the rule of law and human rights, especially for women and migrants. we hope in this parliament that the transitional government will lead the process of national reconciliation and, within this framework, ensure the participation of women and young people in all political and economic decision-making bodies. we europeans must learn the necessary lessons from our past in libya, as a bad example of policy, or rather, of the lack of foreign policy, through the collaboration of various european governments with the gaddafi regime, whether by in writing. - the resolution clearly shows the scale of the human tragedy in this part of africa. but by pointing out some of the immediate causes of hunger, it fails to identify fully and accurately the root causes and those responsible for this situation. this also limits the scope of some of the proposed solutions. the volatility of prices to which many countries have been exposed after the destruction of their fragile productive fabric (largely as a result of interventions by the imf and the world bank) is mainly due to financial speculation in food products. this is an area where speculators (investment funds, hedge funds, pension funds and big banks) have been concentrating as other speculative bubbles have been drying up or bursting. the only way to stop this speculation is to stop the instruments that enable it, in particular with some financial products such as otc derivatives. unfortunately, the measures taken by the eu in this area are far from being able to stop this sinister speculative machine and its inhuman consequences. the same applies to the proposals made in this resolution. to urge speculators to take social responsibility is like asking a fox to restrain itself once it is in the cage. that is why we abstained.
in writing. - we voted in favour of this resolution, but we insist that the hunger and despair in the horn of africa have their immediate causes, which we have always referred to: severe drought and internal conflicts. but they have, in addition, deep, often hidden causes, linked to colonialism and its new forms. we have seen foreign interference, the exploitation of natural resources and their population, debt and debt service at unbearable levels, speculation in the prices of raw materials and foodstuffs. in general, economic and social disaster gives way to civil wars, sometimes to the so-called failed state, to external military intervention. it was the us support for the ethiopian invasion of somalia, the saudi support for the islamist group, the recurring airstrikes, because somalia also has oil. humanitarian aid to the region is thus urgently needed, but without the interventionism of interested parties. the discourse of compassion and pity cannot hide the necessary understanding of these causes and the fair allocation of responsibilities.
in writing. - what is happening in east africa in the 21st century is unacceptable and shows that we all still have a lot to do to avoid this kind of human catastrophe. despite all the financial and human efforts the eu has made, they have not been enough to end hunger in the region. more eu support is therefore needed to mobilise the areas most affected by hunger in somalia and the horn of africa. priorities should be given to the provision of food aid, medical care, clean water and adequate sanitation. however, i believe that this effort must be accompanied by greater efficiency in order to avoid waste and illegal exploitation, which only harm the most deprived population, in particular children, women and the elderly.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution. all possible support must be given to the 13.3 million people in somalia, ethiopia, kenya, eritrea and djibouti who are in urgent need of food aid and are suffering from the worst famine in 60 years. the eu's solidarity cannot and should not be conditioned by economic constraints.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the eu's position and commitments ahead of the un high-level meeting on the prevention and control of noncommunicable diseases, as, according to the who, 86% of deaths in europe are caused by noncommunicable diseases and a significant proportion of these are preventable, the eu and the member states must strengthen primary prevention, research and early diagnosis in order to achieve the 25% reduction in mortality from preventable noncommunicable diseases by 2025 as proposed by the who.
in writing. − according to the world health organisation, 86% of deaths in europe are caused by non-communicable diseases, the most common being cardiovascular diseases, respiratory diseases such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, cancer and diabetes. while it cannot be said lightly that all these diseases are behavioral, the truth is that they are all associated with risk factors that are, such as smoking, unbalanced diet, abuse of salt, fats and alcohol, and lack of physical activity. it is up to the states - and the union can play an important role in this - to reduce, if not the prevalence, at least the mortality associated with these diseases. this must be done not only by prevention - combined with campaigns to promote healthier lifestyles - but also by a very serious commitment to the early diagnosis, detection and treatment of these diseases, factors which we know are essential to reducing their mortality.
in writing. the european parliament, in its resolution of 15 june on the situation in the democratic republic of the congo (drc), calls on the government of the drc to take all necessary measures to ensure that the drc is not subject to any form of sanctions. the human being seeks, throughout his years of existence, what we might call the quality of life. however, this quality of life can end in a silent death. we can say that some of the pleasures of life (improper diet, alcohol, and tobacco) can lead to death if not properly regulated. non-communicable diseases such as obesity, alcoholism and smoking - the causes of diabetes, cancer, cardiovascular disease, stroke, etc. - are responsible for about 85% of deaths in the eu and their treatment costs are estimated at many billions of euros. i therefore welcome the adoption of this proposal, which is aimed at generalizing measures already implemented in other countries and aimed at preventing and reducing these diseases, which, as we have said, are the main cause of death in europe.
in writing. − noncommunicable diseases i.e. cardiovascular disease (the number one cause of death in europe), cancer (the number two cause of death in europe), respiratory diseases and diabetes together account for 86% of deaths in europe, according to the world health organisation. this resolution, based on a realistic and enlightening picture of the situation, points to relevant solutions involving greater cooperation between member states in defining a strategy to combat these diseases, with primary prevention, research, early diagnosis and education as essential pillars. the need for greater cooperation in international fora is also stressed. although the resolution deserves our full support, a few words are necessary in relation to the current context in the eu with regard to public health services. the wise and correct words in the resolution cannot make us forget the brutal attack that is under way in many countries, including portugal, against the public health systems in all their various forms, as well as against the education and research systems. this attack also compromises in practice many of the efforts needed to combat these and other diseases. it is a pity that this aspect was not also mentioned in the resolution.

in writing. - the proposal for a resolution by mr herbert reul, on behalf of the committee on industry, research and energy, on the european union's policy approach to the itu world radiocommunications conference 2012 (wrc-12); the international telecommunication union (itu), the world's oldest international organisation founded in 1865, aims to standardise and regulate radio waves and international telecommunications. it is a specialized agency of the united nations (un) whose recommendations are recognized and accepted worldwide. in a digital society where information and communication technologies are evolving at breakneck speed, issues such as spectrum, wireless communications, data transmission speed, etc., are of enormous importance and can catalyse economic recovery. in fact, in no other field like this does it make sense to say that tomorrow begins now. i therefore welcome the adoption of this motion for a resolution, since an ambitious approach by the eu at the above conference is needed to create the conditions for the development of these cutting-edge technologies in all member states.
in writing. − at this important world radiocommunication conference it is up to each member state to define and defend its policy approaches. in a matter as important as this, which deals with radio, television, mobile, broadband and other transmissions, each member state of the european union will have its own strategic guidelines so that, in the spirit of the necessary cooperation, they can manage their spectrum better. in today's society, there is a constant contradiction. on the one hand, technological research and development have improved access to information and telecommunications, but on the other hand, as a result of the crisis and its economic and social consequences, increasing segments of the population have difficulty in accessing the most advanced radio communications technologies. this situation may be aggravated if they continue to undermine the public nature and universal access to radio spectrum, in particular through the creation of the single market in this area. so while we expect the european commission to provide technical and political support to member states in their bilateral and multilateral negotiations with third countries, and to cooperate with member states in the negotiation of international agreements, we do not agree that it should substitute itself for the member states by calling into question their interests in a strategic area.

the rapporteur. - i would like to begin by thanking everyone for their cooperation, the good cooperation that has been established during the preparation and drafting of this report. i would like to thank you above all for the fact that it was done at a particularly difficult time, the summer holidays, when everyone was available to help draw up commitments and for the fact that we are here today, in this debate, to discuss the content of the report. i would also like to thank the rapporteurs for the various opinions of the committees involved, for the contributions they were able to make and which were incorporated in the final report, and before i turn to the content of the report itself, i cannot help but express my great appreciation and gratitude to the two officials of the committee on industry, research and energy, susanne kiefer and oren gai, who worked with me during the month of august and i think they deserve more than recognition and a very special thank you. that said, it is timely that the commission has launched a common strategic framework for research and innovation funding for 2014-2020, which we have also had many opportunities to talk about with the commissioner and which i believe is a golden opportunity to reinforce the added value and strength of research and innovation in the european context. but also, as i have had the opportunity to say on several occasions, i understand that a common research and innovation funding framework is not made by the sum of its parts, because we know that often the whole is not equal to the sum of its parts. and so when we put the framework programme, the european institute of innovation and technology and the european competitiveness and innovation programme together and add the amounts that are associated we do not have a common strategy unless we think about what the objectives should be associated with this proposal. that is why i have tried to define the main objectives from the outset of the proposal. i think that the resources at our disposal are mainly used for three fundamental dimensions. firstly, capacity building: european researchers are the most valuable resource we have for research. the strengthening of these capacities, together with infrastructure, is one of the levels of investment we must embrace as a priority. secondly, and as a second objective, the potential and cooperation we have in the field of research. this is certainly one of the areas where we have been most successful, and it is important that we strengthen it, that we do not lose sight of areas which are fundamental and decisive for what is europe's wealth, such as the social sciences and basic research. without them we have no innovation, without them we do not know the societies on which we must intervene politically and that is why we cannot let them fall. and thirdly, innovation and the market oriented towards the common good. i believe that only by defining the objectives can we really have a common framework that serves everyone and can make research and innovation central and decisive areas at a time that is just as crucial as the one we are living in today: a situation of economic, social and financial crisis, in which we are on the way to an increasingly divergent europe. that is why i have voted to keep the structural funds separate from the european funds, because we have to make the road to cohesion, that is why it is important to ensure that there are decent working conditions for researchers in europe and that the measures to simplify research are implemented. i've been talking as an investigator for ten years. researchers cannot be guinea pigs for the bureaucratic systems we have created, they must be implemented. and that's also why it's very important that we not only look at excellence but really look at the path to excellence. in a divided europe, competition cannot be a race where those who have access to the first places at the finish line always win, and we know who they are, madam commissioner. it is therefore important to ensure that competition, as seen in the field of research and innovation, is healthy to have better conditions for all, but that it is in the direction of cohesion and convergence to make europe as a whole a zone of excellence in the same field.
on behalf of the ppe group. other i would like to begin by congratulating mrs marisa matias on her excellent work and the constructive collaboration she has established with the other political groups. the epp group is pleased to see its main proposals reflected in this report. these are: increasing the budget of the next research and innovation framework, coordinating it with the structural funds, including the concept of pathways to excellence, creating the conditions for greater involvement of industry and in particular smes, promoting the participation of young researchers and administrative and financial simplification. research and innovation are two fundamental pillars of economic development and job creation. it is therefore crucial to increase the share of funding allocated to research and innovation within the overall eu budget, by substantially increasing the framework programme and the percentage of the structural funds dedicated to this sector. the first objective of the framework programme is to promote excellence and this must continue, but it is equally important to create the conditions for the participation of small units, embryos of excellence such as small research groups and innovative companies. to this end, the report proposes the concept of pathways to excellence. the epp recognises the key role of the business community in job creation and economic development and welcomes the importance attached to smes in this report. unemployment among highly qualified young people is a scourge in several eu countries. the participation of young people in research projects will be highly beneficial. finally, there is an urgent need to simplify access to the research and development funds in order to create a culture of trust among all those involved in order to strengthen research and innovation in europe.

member of the commission. − madam president, i am very encouraged by the debate that has unfolded here. in answer to comments by mr rübig and others in relation to the budget, obviously i am in the hands of parliament and the council. certainly, from what i have heard this evening, i think that parliament will be a very strong ally in support of an increased budget. by way of conclusion, let me give you some flavour of how we think horizon 2020 should be organised. it will be structured around three distinct but mutually reinforcing blocks, in line with europe 2020 priorities. the first block, ‘excellence in the science base’, will strengthen the eu’s excellence in science. the second, ‘tackling societal challenges’, will respond directly to the challenges identified in europe 2020. the third block, ‘creating industrial leadership and competitive frameworks’, will support business, research and innovation. ms matias, i know these blocks do not correspond to the ‘three layers’ in your report, but i hope you will agree that the components are there and the objectives are the same. implementation will be simplified and standardised, with simplification covering both funding schemes and rules. key aspects will include a rationalised set of funding schemes, a single set of rules, earlier project start dates and further externalisation. the administrative burden on participants will be reduced through a radically simplified cost reimbursement approach. this will be based on the broadest possible acceptance of participants’ accounting practices and a greater use of lump sums and flat rates. the negotiation and selection phases will be shortened to allow projects to start earlier. simpler guidance and advisory services will be provided through both a single it portal and one-stop-shop support structures in the national language. there will be a clear differentiation between the objectives and modes of intervention of horizon 2020 and those of the cohesion policy funds, to ensure complementarities and synergies. horizon 2020 will allocate funds on the basis of excellence, regardless of geographical location. cohesion policy funds will focus on research and innovation capacity-building through pre-allocated envelopes for eligible regions. european regional development fund funding should support the development of smart specialisation strategies and should provide a ‘stairway to excellence’. based on these key principles, the commission will now develop its proposals for presentation by the end of this year. the proposals would have not been possible without your enriching report. all the issues that have been addressed this evening and have been addressed in the report will certainly be looked at very seriously and taken into account by myself and my services over the coming weeks.

madam president, the discussion of a strategic framework to help developing countries meet the challenges of food security, which is obviously necessary and welcome, is inseparable, as the rapporteur says in her report, from the discussion of the coherence between this objective, food security in developing countries, and the sectoral policies of the european union, such as agricultural, trade and energy policies, to name just three examples. and the truth is that there is today a blatant and manifest incoherence between these sectoral policies and this objective of food security. free trade, the promotion of intensive, export-oriented production models which threaten and destroy small and mediumsized farming and family farming, the use, the pressure to use fertile land for purposes other than food production and which compete with food production - all this threatens the food sovereignty of developing countries, which is inseparable from their food security. the greater a country's food dependence, the greater its food insecurity, the greater the difficulty in ensuring that its population is supplied with food in sufficient quantity and quality.
madam president, european schools have an important mission: to provide education in the mother tongue to pupils whose parents work outside their country of origin. that is why we are very concerned about attempts to implement measures which may undermine the mission and objectives of the european schools, under the pretext of cost rationalisation. we are talking about measures such as increasing the minimum number of students per class for optional subjects, vertical grouping of classes from two or more different years, or reducing support for students with learning difficulties. some of these measures may lead to situations which have in the past been considered by the european ombudsman to be unjustifiably discriminatory. we refuse to take any step back in this area. it is unacceptable that the principle of multilingualism should also be attacked in european schools and that the privileged status enjoyed in other areas by some of the languages of the european union should be extended here to the detriment of others.
madam president, disasters are a recurring theme in our parliamentary debate, which is natural, given that they are becoming more frequent and more devastating. i would therefore like to welcome the initiative of commissioner georgieva, because it seems to me very pertinent, and also congratulate the rapporteur, mrs gardini. we in the s&d group agree with the analysis of the effects of climate change on the increase in the number and severity of disasters and give priority to prevention policies. the lisbon treaty introduces provisions to strengthen the capacity to respond to disasters, making it more comprehensive, coordinated and efficient. we therefore welcome the proposal to create a european emergency response capacity and the proposal to develop a european emergency response centre. we also consider it of the utmost importance to maintain a permanent operational centre, operating 24 hours a day, in conjunction with the member states through focal points, which are also permanent. i would like to welcome the rapporteur's proposals, particularly in relation to pilot projects. the importance of the pilot project for a reserve of aircraft for fighting forest fires, for example, should be emphasized. its success justifies its continuation and consolidation. the lisbon treaty also introduced a solidarity clause, and i think solidarity is a dimension of disaster response that was important to reinforce in this report. and that is why we have tabled amendments to reinforce this aspect of solidarity.
madam president, commissioner, exactly one year ago, in september 2010, a large majority in this parliament approved a report, for which i was rapporteur, on a community approach to the prevention of natural and man-made disasters. it was noted that prevention, as the first and decisive phase of the disaster management cycle, should be given greater importance. prevention can prevent many disasters from occurring and significantly lessen the effects of others. the measures we proposed in that report included the creation of a financial framework for prevention, measures in the fields of forestry, fire prevention, protection and defence of the coast, the restoration and protection of water bodies, the creation of a public agricultural insurance scheme and the introduction of a minimum compensation scheme for farmers affected by disasters, the strengthening of early warning systems, and the revision of the solidarity fund regulation. a year later, it's easy to see that's pretty much all that's left to do. when discussing the other phases of the management cycle - preparation, response, recovery - it would be good to bear this in mind.

in writing. − this recommendation concerns an agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the palestinian authority of the west bank and the gaza strip, and aims to establish further liberalisation of trade in processed and unprocessed agricultural products, fish and fishery products, which amends the euro-mediterranean interim association agreement on trade and cooperation between the european community and the palestine liberation organisation (plo) for the benefit of the palestinian authority of the west bank and the gaza strip. the aim of this agreement, signed in april 2011, is to help develop the palestinian economy, which is in a very serious crisis due to poverty and unemployment, by exporting agricultural and fisheries products to the eu duty-free. despite the fact that the palestinian authority is the eu's smallest trading partner, i am voting in favour of this recommendation which aims to free exports from the palestinian territories from israeli customs controls and i hope that it will be the first step in building a palestinian state whose right to self-determination must be respected by the state of israel.
in writing. - the end of the israeli blockade of palestine and its people is essential for the development of the palestinian economy. this agreement, by proposing to increase exports of palestinian products to the eu and by facilitating imports from palestine, is, in the present framework, a contribution to achieving this objective. the scope of this contribution is, however, severely limited by the actual situation in the occupied territories today, which is characterized by a violent and persistent attack on the most basic rights of the palestinian people. amongst many other things, this brutal and illegal occupation creates numerous obstacles to palestinian exports and imports, in addition to daily barriers and limitations to the movement of people and goods. this is the problem that must be solved. the european union is therefore urging the palestinian authority to take immediate action to ensure that the palestinian authority is recognized as a full member of the un general assembly. the problem of economic relations between the eu and the state of israel still persists. that is to say, the problem of the eu's intolerable complacency and connivance in the face of the clear and repeated violations of human rights perpetrated by israel in the occupied territories - in defiance of the very provisions of the association agreement concerning human rights, which, as we have always said, are of little value.
in writing. - we voted in favour of this report because we believe that the approval of this agreement can help the development of the palestinian economy and the possibility for it to export products to the eu. however, what is important to stress is the urgent need to end the israeli blockade of palestine. the commission cannot ignore, by signing this agreement, the slow agony of the palestinian people with the occupation of their territories by israel. this brutal and illegal occupation creates numerous obstacles to palestinian exports and imports, in addition to the daily barriers and limitations to the movement of people and goods. although the commission has since 1998 ruled that no settlement in the occupied territories can be considered israeli territory, it is not fulfilling its obligations by imposing on the member states the obligation to monitor any irregularities in the origin of products. we therefore support the demand of the palestinian people, their right to recognition of the sovereign and independent state of palestine in the pre-1967 borders, with its capital in jerusalem.
in writing. − in 2005, under the rabat roadmap, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with a number of mediterranean countries, including the palestinian authority, in order to establish conditions for the liberalisation of trade in agricultural and fisheries products. more specifically, the agreement provides for duty-free (and mainly also quota-free) access for palestinian imports of agricultural products, processed agricultural products, fish and fishery products to the eu market. several products of the same nature originating in the eu will be exempt from duties (but not from quotas) to access the palestinian market, with some exceptions. however, the ultimate objective of the agreement is to help develop the palestinian economy and thus facilitate the possibility of exporting palestinian products to the eu. the future of the region depends on improved economic development. trade can also serve as a development mechanism that contributes to poverty reduction and political stability.

in writing. − i support this recommendation, as agreements in the field of civil aviation which have been governed by bilateral agreements should be replaced by a general agreement between the european union (including all member states) and third countries, in order to avoid discrimination with regard to free competition. the agreement is also of particular importance as it concerns mexico, an important partner in the european air carrier market, which in 2009 recorded approximately 2,5 million passengers and 90 000 tonnes of cargo.
in writing. − in 2002, the court of justice of the european union found that traditional designation clauses in bilateral air service agreements concluded by member states infringe union law. following the court decision, the european commission negotiated an agreement replacing certain provisions of the current 13 bilateral air services agreements concluded between the member states and the united mexican states. the horizontal agreement with mexico will restore a sound legal basis for eu-mexico relations in the aviation sector. mexico is an important market for eu carriers, which in 2009 recorded approximately 2.5 million passengers and 90 000 tonnes of cargo. given the importance and size of the eu-mexico aviation market, this report, which i supported, argues that a broader aviation agreement should be concluded, helping to strengthen eu-mexico aviation cooperation and to enhance opportunities and benefits for industry and consumers in both the eu and mexico.
in writing. − the court of justice of the european union has held that traditional designation clauses in bilateral air service agreements concluded by member states infringe union law in so far as they allow a third country to refuse, withdraw or suspend licences or authorisations granted to air carriers designated by a member state but whose capital is not substantially owned by that member state or by nationals of that member state and whose effective control is not exercised by them. these clauses constituted a clear discrimination, in breach of article 49 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which guarantees nationals of member states exercising their freedom of establishment the same treatment in the host member state as that accorded to nationals of that member state. this new agreement negotiated by the commission, in addition to correcting a discriminatory situation, obviously brings advantages in that it replaces provisions of 13 of the current bilateral agreements with a horizontal agreement that restores a sound legal basis for eu-mexico relations.
in writing. − ensuring aviation safety and harmonised rules for the various market players is the central objective of this agreement between the european community and the united mexican states on civil aviation safety ('the agreement'). the agreement will avoid duplication of procedures (whether testing, assessment or certification). it should also be noted that the mutual recognition rule (of joint inspections and investigations and of the exchange of safety data) allows efficiency gains for all actors. finally, the agreement guarantees all eu air carriers non-discriminatory access to routes between the eu member state party to the bilateral agreement and mexico. last but not least, the agreement will allow for significant savings not only for the aviation industries but also efficiency gains for the airlines themselves.
in writing. the report, drawn up by mrs silvia-adriana ţicău, concerns a proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of the agreement on certain aspects of air services between the european union and the united mexican states. the mexican market is important for eu carriers, with 2.5 million passengers and 90,000 tonnes of cargo in 2009. international relations in the field of aviation between member states and third countries were regulated by bilateral agreements until the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon on 1 december 2009, which requires the european parliament to approve air services agreements. although the agreement was signed on 15 december 2010, it needs the approval of the ep to be concluded. i welcome the establishment of another agreement aimed at providing all air carriers from the member states with non-discriminatory access to routes to mexico, which is an important step in strengthening eu-mexico relations in the aviation sector.
in writing. as we have said in previous agreements of the same scope, in the current concrete framework in which civil aviation activity is developing, this proposed agreement raises doubts as to its scope and possible consequences. in fact, avoiding discrimination between eu airlines by allegedly creating a level playing field for the various european airlines could help facilitate the monopolistic concentration in the sector (a process already under way). the reference to the prevalence of free competition (article 4) is inserted in this line, aimed at reducing the ability of member states to defend their flag carriers, in a sector which is, for various reasons, strategic for the safeguarding of national interests. although the possible implications for portugal are comparatively less than in the case of the previous, similar agreements already signed by brazil, the usa and canada, in coherence and for the same reasons as we have previously advanced, we did not support this report.

in writing. the european commission has negotiated an agreement which will replace the 13 existing bilateral agreements between eu member states and the united mexican states. this agreement, known as the horizontal agreement, like many others which have been negotiated and concluded by the european union with various international partners in the field of civil aviation, will serve as a common legal framework for the relations of the various member states of the european union with the united mexican states, constituting the first step towards strengthening their relations in this sector. the size and importance of the mexican aviation market to the european union justify moving towards a more comprehensive agreement that is capable of bringing benefits to the civil aviation industry and to consumers of both parties. the agreement also complements a number of agreements concluded with other states of the americas, such as those recently concluded with the united states, canada and brazil.

in writing. - this recommendation on the draft council decision aims at the conclusion of a new fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of cape verde, which sets out fishing opportunities and financial compensation. the protocol between the european community and cape verde in the field of fisheries, which had been in force for five years, expired on 31 august 2011. last december, a new protocol was negotiated, to be in force between 1 september 2011 and 31 august 2014. however, in accordance with the tfeu, the conclusion of the new protocol requires the consent of the european parliament. considering that this is a country that has long had privileged relations with the eu, including a special partnership established in 2007, and that has an intense link with the outermost regions of europe, the azores, madeira and the canary islands, i welcome the conclusion of this protocol, which will not only allow the fishing fleets of portugal, spain and france to continue fishing in cape verdean waters, but will also contribute to the sustainable economic growth of a country where financial resources are not abundant.
in writing. − this fisheries protocol guarantees the possibility for member states' fleets to fish off cape verde until 31 august 2014. the continental shelves of cape verde, due to the volcanic origin of its islands, are generally narrow, thus limiting the productivity of the fisheries sector. cape verde's fisheries resources are not considerable, but include commercially important migratory species such as tunas, along with small pelagic fish, some demersal fish and lobsters. overall employment in the fisheries and related activities subsectors of the public administration was around 10 400 jobs in 2008, around 5% of the total workforce. we support the concerns expressed by the rapporteur in asking the commission to provide parliament with all relevant documentation and information on the conclusions of the joint committee meetings, the multiannual sectoral programme and the results of the respective annual evaluations; to facilitate the participation of parliament representatives as observers in the joint committee meetings; and to submit to parliament, during the last year of application of the new protocol and before the opening of negotiations for its renewal, a full evaluation report on its implementation, without imposing unnecessary restrictions on access to this document.
in writing. − this report refers to the fisheries protocol which guarantees the possibility for member states' fleets to fish off cape verde until 31 august 2014. it is an important agreement for tuna fishing, where fishing licences for surface longliners for portugal have increased from 7 licences to 9. this agreement, as in other fisheries agreements with third countries, raises important questions, both as regards the economic viability of the long-distance fishing fleets of the european union countries and the real fishing opportunities granted under it, as well as the development of third countries and the development aid actually granted. the commercial nature of these agreements is maintained, although the partnership and development aspect is strengthened, as is the case with this agreement, the annual financial contribution of which has been increased to eur 435 000, eur 110 000 of which is intended to support the development of the fisheries sector policy of the republic of cape verde. hopefully, this will be enough to support the fishermen and the people of cape verde.

in writing. − the new protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of cape verde contributes, in the interest of both parties, to maintaining the continuity of fishing opportunities. the special partnership was established in 2007, taking into account the status of cape verde as a peripheral nation and the many things it has in common with the outermost regions of madeira and the azores. the geographical proximity and the affinity of the challenges faced contribute to an ever closer relationship, complementing the future atlantic dimension of the integrated maritime policy. in order to create a partnership framework for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy, the protocol provides for an annual contribution of eur 1 305 000. in addition, it would be desirable to foster synergies with various regional development programmes and to develop the agreement in a manner consistent with the eu's common fisheries policy and development policy. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.

in writing. - there are positive aspects to this report which we value. some of these correspond to relatively consensual but necessary guidelines, such as improving the efficiency of research and development (r & d) funding at regional, national and eu level. in view of the clear failure to meet the targets of a decade ago for r & d investment, a new horizon is now set to reach 3% of gdp invested in r & d: 2020. that is two decades after this goal was set. but it is foreseeable that unless there is a profound change in the wider political and macroeconomic framework, this objective will hardly be achieved even in 2020. many member states are far from this objective and, worse, are moving away from it rather than towards it. in the current crisis, research, education and innovation are key tools for economic recovery and job creation and for defining a model of sustainable and inclusive growth - commonplace in the discourse but necessary in practice, trampled underfoot by current policies. the rapporteur's call for attention to the situation of great precariousness faced by many scientific workers is pertinent. but the report does not avoid some contradictions, which reflect the majority in this parliament, such as the predominance attributed to the market.

in writing. − the european schools play a valuable role in their communities, as they act as promoters of multiculturalism and multilingualism and as models in the protection and promotion of the less widely used languages internationally. the economic crisis has had an impact on the funding of the european schools, and it is therefore necessary to rationalise the costs of these schools. however, this should not affect the education of the children. the budgetary constraints which schools will have to accept must be accompanied by a real increase in their autonomy in management. granting each european school a greater degree of budgetary autonomy, following an evaluation that ensures that this will be beneficial for the schools, can be an effective means of improving the management of the resources allocated to them.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that budget cuts must take account of the specific situation of european children and young people attending european schools. the savings cannot compromise the fundamental principles on which the system is based, namely the teaching of pupils' mother tongues, the education of vulnerable children, children with learning difficulties or children with special needs. the european schools are not elitist schools, but a necessity. its mission is to provide education in the mother tongue for pupils whose parents may be forced to change jobs or return to their country of origin.
in writing. - there are currently 14 european schools with 22 778 pupils, of whom 14 292 attend schools in brussels and luxembourg, corresponding to about 63% of the school population. as a parent of pupils who have attended european schools, i know how important they are, but i also know their problems. i admit that in the current economic context it is tempting to cut the budget for european schools, but as i have always maintained, any cut in the education of our children is a cut in our future ability to be competitive. so it's the wrong cut. i am in favour of european schools maintaining their multicultural matrix without losing sight of the real reason for which they were set up: to enable the children of displaced officials to have access to education in their mother tongue and in conditions as close as possible to those they would have in their country of origin.
in writing. - we used to hear that the best thing in the world is children. however, the responsibility for preparing their future is ours. it is therefore essential that we are aware that investing in education is investing in the future of our young people and in an increasingly globalised world. this report examines the european schools system, which has been in operation for more than 50 years. the first european school was founded in luxembourg in october 1953. at present, some 23 000 pupils attend these schools, 63% of whom (around 14 500) attend schools in brussels and luxembourg. the aim behind the creation of these schools was to ensure that the children of officials of the european institutions living abroad have access to education in their mother tongue. its system is sui generis, based on cooperation between the member states and the european union, and it values and promotes multiculturalism. given the significant demand for these schools, also due to eu enlargement, it is essential that they continue to fulfil the objectives for which they were set up. i therefore vote in favour of the report by mr cavada.
in writing. - the european schools (es) were the result of the intention to develop a school network to serve the children of officials of the european institutions who are subject to change of assignment or return to their country of origin by providing them with education in their mother tongue. the report contains positive aspects, which we value. examples are: the defence of the fundamental principles of the european schools, such as mother tongue teaching; the guarantee of equivalent educational conditions for children from all language communities; and the clear and unequivocal statement that the proposed cuts in the budgets of the european schools constitute a serious threat to the quality of education and the good functioning of the european schools, along with opposition to any budget cuts. this position is all the more relevant because, as we have already had occasion to denounce in the portuguese section of the european school of brussels ii (woluwe), measures are being prepared under the pretext of budgetary restrictions which endanger the quality of education, which is unacceptable. but the report also contains some contradictions, such as the defence of the use of so-called 'vehicular languages', and positions which are unfounded, which we do not support, such as the assertion that the current intergovernmental legal status of the ee has reached its limits and requires profound changes.

in writing. − the absorption of the structural and cohesion funds has been recognised as the main concern with regard to the implementation of the european union's cohesion policy since the late 1990s. many member states have had difficulty absorbing structural and cohesion funds from the eu budget, especially in the years immediately following accession. the rules on the structural and cohesion funds are complex and therefore difficult to comply with, leading to errors. thus, standards and processes should be simplified to achieve higher uptake rates, reduce errors and increase efficiency. at the same time, a balance needs to be struck between simplification and stability of rules and procedures. i think it is more appropriate to give greater attention to fraud rather than formal irregularities and to a more differentiated treatment of irregularities which allows some flexibility depending on the seriousness of the irregularity identified. a better balance should be struck between, on the one hand, the rules and procedures required to ensure the legality and regularity of eu expenditure and, on the other hand, making cohesion policy more performance-oriented and more cost-efficient.

in writing. the structural and cohesion funds are a privileged instrument for the balanced economic development of the community area. the analysis of the real impact of the use of the funds by the states, in order to assess their capacity to meet the purposes for which they were allocated, is a necessary condition for the development of a more effective future policy, with less waste of resources. the need to find faster and more effective decision-making procedures, to adapt the degree of control to the aid granted and, in this context, to combat genuine situations of fraud, is emphasised. these are points which the rapporteur has made very clearly, and i have therefore voted in favour of them.
in writing. − the absorption of the structural funds is a major concern in the implementation of cohesion policy, and an analysis of the difficulties encountered by the member states in the effective application of the funds is needed to draw lessons for the future. the regi committee, of which i am a member, has approved a set of proposals based on a diagnosis of the reasons behind the absorption problems, such as the initial problems at the start of the programming period, the financial problems resulting from the crisis, the new regulatory requirements and the organisational and control requirements, as well as the issue of insufficient qualification of human resources and the delays in information technology systems. the proposals put forward in the document adopted by parliament today stress the need to simplify rules and procedures and to focus on results-generating payments and a better balance between rules and procedures and a more performance-oriented and more efficient cohesion policy. they do not, however, forget the wide differences in absorption capacity between member states, suggesting the creation of a programme for the exchange of good practice and highlighting the importance of governance at various levels.

in writing. - the number of annual disasters has increased fivefold over the last 35 years. in europe alone, these disasters have killed almost 90 000 people, affected the lives of more than 29 million people and caused losses of €211 billion over the last 20 years. the lisbon treaty introduced new legal bases for civil protection and humanitarian aid with the aim of ensuring a rapid and effective response to disasters inside and outside europe. this report calls for greater efficiency at all stages of the european disaster management cycle, including prevention, preparedness, response and recovery, as well as optimising economic resources in times of austerity. it stressed the need to establish a genuine emergency response centre, which would operate at all times and in consultation with the member states, making decisions on the means to be mobilised in the event of a disaster, with a view to ensuring immediate and effective assistance to victims. it calls for better coordination between all actors to avoid overlapping and duplication of efforts. it also advocates simplifying the european civil protection mechanism. so i voted in favour.
in writing. - there has been a dramatic increase in the number and severity of natural and man-made disasters worldwide, i.e. forest fires, floods and landslides, earthquakes, industrial and nuclear accidents, terrorist attacks, etc. unfortunately, the eu and its member states are not immune to such disasters either. therefore, given the increasing pace of climate change and the increased likelihood of more frequent and more intense natural disasters, it is urgent to strengthen the eu's response capacity, inside and outside its borders, in order to improve its effectiveness, efficiency, coherence and visibility. a shift to a predictable system under the eu civil protection mechanism is needed, as well as the introduction of a system of monitoring, supervision and development in the framework of disaster assistance operations. it is important to develop a protection system based on the sharing and rationalisation of existing resources, avoiding duplication and overlapping of efforts, gaining in terms of coherence, effectiveness, speed of assistance and cost reduction. it is also urgent to make the necessary amendments to the regulation establishing the solidarity fund, which is characterised by rigid deadlines and procedures and contains assumptions which make it difficult and delay its mobilisation.

in writing. − this report, by elisabetta gardini, addresses the need to strengthen european capacity in disaster situations, especially in the field of civil protection and humanitarian aid. in recent times, we have seen a great increase in the number of disasters, such as those that have occurred in haiti and japan. in europe, we've had massive fires, the ash cloud from the icelandic volcano and landslides and floods due to heavy rains. in fact, in the last 20 years, the number of disasters has increased fivefold, claiming almost 100,000 lives. these are large-scale phenomena requiring effective and properly coordinated responses. the european union needs to take preventive action, such as tackling climate change, but also to play a coordinating role among all member states who have responsibility in this area so that we do not become entangled in a tangle of responsibilities that makes it difficult to respond quickly and effectively. i welcome the adoption of this report which focuses on the most vulnerable areas such as mountain, island and coastal areas, revealing a great human and financial concern, and i welcome the creation of a european civil protection force.
in writing. − preparedness, response and recovery are stages in the disaster management cycle where cooperation between states can and should exist. in view of the transboundary nature of disasters and the complexity, scale and cost of the material resources that need to be mobilised in the event of major disasters. such cooperation shall be based on solidarity and mutual assistance and may also include a sharing of resources. in any event, the sovereignty of states should be respected and there should be no duplication or overlap of chains of command which should be based in the competent national or regional authorities. the response to disasters cannot be a pretext for external interventionism, for the assertion of economic and geostrategic interests, or for military interventions and occupations, hidden under the guise of humanitarian interventions. there are already sad examples of this reality and, more than that, worrying signs that it may worsen in the future. the recent change in nato's so-called strategic concept, which illegitimately and unacceptably broadens the possibilities for intervention by this military (war) organisation, is worthy of note. we believe that the framework for disaster response proposed in this report does not safeguard all these aspects, which are essential to us.
in writing. - this report underestimates the importance of preventive policies, i.e. those which can prevent, in some cases, and minimise, in others, the effects of disasters. prevention is achieved through environmental, agricultural, energy, industrial, water and land-use planning and management policies. how many forest fires could have been avoided if the common agricultural policy had not contributed to the desertification of the countryside, to the reduction of our agriculture, our agro-agriculture and rural life? the eu must urgently provide more funding for de facto preventive policies and for prevention and alert measures. strengthening european response capacity must involve environmental protection, changes to common policies, environmental education and awareness, increased response capacity in individual states and planned cooperation between neighbouring states, including the existence of comprehensive risk charts and alert and response mechanisms. the idea of a special forest fire unit does not seem interesting or feasible. greater mutual help and cooperation is possible and desirable. when the usefulness of the european space policy and the global monitoring programme for the environment and safety is mentioned, there is a danger that, under the pretext of the environment, security concerns are overlooked.

in writing. - in view of the continued fragmentation of the euro cash transport market, national regulatory rules should be reviewed and simplified in order to allow for more efficient and faster circulation between the member states which have adopted the single currency. however, in addition to further simplification, the provisions in force in each member state concerning the transport of valuables must also be carefully considered. i believe that the agreement now reached allows for this balance, both in the choice of transport mode and in the public safety rules required and the social conditions achieved by the sector's officials.
in writing. − this report, by ms sophie auconie, is concerned with a proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on the professional crossborder road transport of euro banknotes and coins between euro area member states. the aim of this proposal is to facilitate the crossborder movement of euro cash between member states which have adopted this currency by defining clear and operational rules. the proposal for a regulation provides for five modes of transport for banknotes and two modes for transporting coins, from which each member state chooses the one best suited to its situation. the issue of the safety of this type of transport has not been forgotten, both for transport policemen and for the population, encouraging the use of the intelligent system of banknote neutralization as a deterrent to attacks on vehicles transporting value. i therefore vote in favour of this report and hope that it will help to facilitate the transport of valuables between member states, thus providing greater security for european citizens and their valuables.
in writing. the aim of this proposal for a european commission regulation is to facilitate the crossborder movement of euro cash, without prejudice to the different regulatory arrangements which member states may choose to apply to the movement of value. the rapporteur believes that this regulation will simplify the regulatory constraints in order to allow for a better circulation of euro coins and banknotes between the member states which have adopted the euro, also taking into account its contribution to stricter requirements in terms of public safety, both for transport controllers and for the general public. as the report states, the market for transporting euro cash remains very fragmented, despite the introduction of euro coins and banknotes dating back to 2002. the considerable heterogeneity of national rules in this field makes it very difficult for professional freight forwarders to provide crossborder services. it is appropriate to consider that the use of the intelligent banknote neutralisation system should be encouraged in the future as it helps to avoid the spiral of violence in attacks on vehicles transporting valuables.
in writing. − as the report says, the euro cash transport market remains very fragmented, despite the introduction of euro coins and banknotes dating back to 2002. the considerable heterogeneity of national rules in this field makes it very difficult for professional freight forwarders to provide crossborder services. the commission's proposal should facilitate the cross-border transport of euro cash, without, however, prejudicing the different regulatory arrangements which member states choose to apply to the transport of value. the purpose of this regulation is to simplify regulatory constraints in order to facilitate the circulation of euro coins and banknotes between member states which have adopted the euro, while also taking into account its contribution to stricter public safety requirements for both transport controllers and the public. the rapporteur therefore considers that the minimum experience required for a company to operate in the cross-border sector should be thorough, and stresses that the use of the intelligent system for neutralising banknotes should be encouraged in the future, as it avoids the spiral of violence that is seen in attacks on vehicles transporting valuables.

in writing. - according to the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the ep has to decide on proposals put forward by the commission on dual-use technology, i.e. goods that can be used for civilian or military goods. it is believed that by controlling such exports, the proliferation of weapons is being prevented. it is essential to reflect on how the european union can most effectively be an example in leading a movement against the proliferation of weapons, which is particularly important given its geopolitical and geoterritorial characteristics, especially after successive enlargements to the east.
in writing. - dual-use products, goods which can be used for both civilian and military purposes, such as chemicals which can be used for fertilisers or to prepare bombs, computer technology but used to guide missiles, are today a highly sensitive matter. the control of exports of dual-use items and technologies at european level aims to ensure compliance with the international commitments of the eu and its member states on non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and conventional weapons. the main function of these international export control regimes is to update the lists of products subject to controls. to date, these lists are almost automatically transposed into eu law, with little or no involvement of the european parliament. i welcome the adoption of a joint interpretation by the european parliament and the european commission under the new framework agreement, which will be crucial to making the community's dual-use regulation more transparent and democratic.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european parliament's amendments to regulation no 428/2009 make the eu's dual-use regime, i.e. goods that can be used for both civilian and military purposes, more democratic, transparent and secure. the amended regulation will also contribute to enhancing the union's image in international export control regimes, which are an important model for the development and practical application of eu legislation in this field.
in writing. − dual-use goods are all products, software and technology which can be used for civil or military purposes. as i have already said, the type of goods in question warrants particular attention and care to the way in which they are moved and used, as well as strict compliance with the international conventions applicable to them and the permanent updating of the list of products covered by that classification. the proposal aims to establish a community system of control of exports of such products and technologies, and therefore the emphasis must be on transparency and security, even if the products covered by the proposal to amend the regulation are destined for countries which do not present any particular danger.
in writing. - this report, by jörg leichtfried, is based on a proposal for a european parliament and council regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1334/2000 establishing a community regime for the control of exports of dual-use goods and technology, i.e. those which have a use both civilian and military. this is a very sensitive matter, because we are talking about products which could enable weapons of mass destruction to be manufactured, thus jeopardizing the safety of people and property. this process dates back to december 2008, when the commission presented to the council its first proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1334/2000 with a view to adding six new annexes. the amendments now introduced strengthen the security and control of exports of these dual-use items. i welcome the adoption of this report which is aimed at making the community's dual-use regimes more transparent and, for the safety of european citizens, at preventing their use by unauthorised persons and/or organisations.
in writing. − dual-use technological products are all those products (including software and technologies) which can be used for civilian or military purposes in parallel. the treaty of lisbon provides for the clarification of the eu's competences in the field of international trade, and is therefore a good opportunity to reaffirm the eu's role in this area and the role, competence and responsibility of the european parliament within the eu institutional framework for decision-making. the community's dual-use regime should be organised in a more transparent and democratic way; the full participation of the european parliament, through the implementation of the obligations arising from the treaty of lisbon and the adoption of a joint interpretation by the european parliament and the european commission under the new framework agreement, will be crucial to achieving this objective.
in writing. - this report concerns the community export control regime for dual-use goods and technology, i.e. goods which can be used for both civilian and military purposes. the community's dual-use regime should be organised in a more transparent and democratic way. indeed, the full participation of the european parliament, through the implementation of the obligations arising from the lisbon treaty and the adoption of a joint interpretation by the european parliament and the european commission under the new framework agreement, will be crucial to achieving this objective. in view of the fact that the european parliament's powers are being strengthened in the sense of greater scrutiny of export authorizations for these sensitive products, which may have secondary uses, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − dual-use products are characterised by the fact that they can be used for both civilian and military purposes. in this area, a network of controls is provided to control, as far as possible, the risks of use for illegal purposes. in this context, i would like to stress, together with the rapporteur, the need for the european parliament to take an active stance on the system of control of exports of dual-use goods and technologies, by strengthening the mechanisms of control, transparency and democratic legitimacy.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 428/2009 of 5 may 2009 introduced several significant changes in the control of exports, transfers, brokering and transit of dual-use goods and technology in the european union, i.e. in the control of goods that can be used for both civilian and military purposes. i agree with this report because it establishes effective control of exports of union products or their transit in the eu and is applied in a uniform manner, establishing a level playing field for all european exporters in accordance with the principles of international trade, thus avoiding unfair competition between eu exporters. the report aims to strengthen the competitiveness of the industry, simplify the current legal system and create its own rules and procedures, and it is important to stress the importance of establishing a secure and codified system for the exchange of information between member states. finally, i consider it essential to draw up triannual monitoring reports on this regulation, to carry out a thorough analysis of the impact of its application and to be able to make any suggestions for amendments that will improve the control of exports of dual-use goods and technologies.

in writing. − over the past few years, the european investment bank and the world bank have financed projects related to the water sector, notably the construction of dams in the least developed countries, such as laos and pakistan. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that water is a scarce resource essential for public health and that it is important to ensure that water resources are managed effectively and distributed equitably to the population. i am in favour of dams that help to improve the quality of life of the people, and that their impact on river flows and how they will affect the agricultural livelihoods of local communities should be assessed. in the future, efforts should be made to analyse the economic viability of major water projects and to take measures to optimise the distribution and use of water from existing infrastructure by multiple sectors of the economy. in this context, i believe that improving the quality of life of the people in the less developed regions should involve the definition of a comprehensive strategy for dams, the establishment of effective political dialogues and the use of warning systems capable of detecting natural causes such as floods, avalanches or tidal waves.
