in writing. - according to the fao, 925 million people suffer from hunger. this number is unacceptable in this day and age. if we are to achieve the millennium development goals in this area and eradicate hunger and improve food sovereignty, we need to establish synergies and put emphasis on a truly global global strategy in the field of food security. new threats such as price speculation, climate change, land degradation, biofuels, etc. have contributed to further exacerbating this situation. i welcome this communication from the commission and would like to stress at once the urgent need to increase the availability of food products, increase their nutritional value and combat price volatility, and to review at institutional level the european strategies for sustainable development (in particular the coordination of sectoral policies), increase the share of oda allocated to agriculture and respect the commitments made in this field within international organisations. the european union must recognise and defend the need for developing countries to ensure their food security and their right to be as self-sufficient as possible by promoting sustainable agriculture.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on helping developing countries to meet the challenges of food security, because poverty eradication and the achievement of the millennium development goals on fighting hunger and malnutrition should be a political priority for the eu and the member states, and measures to limit speculation in food and agricultural markets are needed.
in writing. − the food and agriculture organisation (fao) warned earlier this year of a possible increase in food prices in 2011, after they reached new all-time highs in 2010, following the rise during the 2008 food crisis. this increase in prices, which affects the whole world, particularly affects the developing countries. according to fao, the estimated number of hungry people was 925 million in 2010, and there are indications that this number may be increasing. it is a very serious situation and i believe that parliament should call for measures to mitigate it. but this is not the place to start the discussion on the future of the cap, let alone on the introduction of a financial transaction tax. as i have said on other occasions, i do not agree with this policy of systematically approving a proposal in reports which have nothing to do with the substance of the proposal itself, as is happening with the financial transaction tax.
in writing. − the first of the millennium development goals (mdgs) - to which the 189 member states of the united nations have committed themselves is to eradicate extreme poverty and hunger by 2015. to do that, they committed to halve the percentage of people who live on less than a dollar a day and to halve the percentage of the population who suffer from hunger. the achievement of this objective is being hampered by food insecurity, particularly in sub-saharan africa and developing countries. the united nations food and agriculture organization (fao) forecasts an increase in the number of hungry people in 2011, after a slight decline in 2010 due to the economic and financial crisis that has caused food prices to rise. added to this problem are climate change, biodiversity loss, soil degradation, pressures on water resources and biofuels. in view of this situation, the european union felt it necessary to review its approach to food safety. i welcome the adoption of this report, which includes principles of safeguarding the right to food in trade agreements between the eu and third countries.
in writing. - this report deals with a subject of great relevance. the rapporteur rightly points to the need for coherence - which is clearly lacking today - between the main eu policies (such as the cap and trade policy) and the objectives of this strategic framework. the emphasis on the role of small and family farming, women in rural areas, local production and consumption circuits, the necessary involvement of local and regional populations and authorities, and public investment in research into sustainable agro-ecological production systems is important. we also welcome the criticism of the current levels of official development assistance, particularly in the agricultural sector, and of the push for agrofuel cultivation. although not explicitly mentioned what would be important , the report does contain some basic principles associated with the concept of food sovereignty. as regards price volatility as a result of speculation in foodstuffs, the report could and should have gone further, notwithstanding some pertinent remarks, by stating that the only way to prevent such speculation is to put an end to the instruments which enable it, such as otc derivatives. finally, criticism of the epas is unfortunately lacking.
in writing. − in this report, which deals with a highly relevant subject, the rapporteur refers to the need for coherence between the main eu policies (such as the cap and trade policy) and the objectives of this strategic framework, highlighting the role of small and family farming, women in rural areas, local production and consumption circuits, the necessary involvement of local and regional populations and authorities, and also public investment in research into sustainable agro-ecological production systems. the current levels of official development assistance, particularly in the agricultural sector, and the push for agrofuel cultivation are also criticised. although not explicitly mentioned, the report does contain some basic principles associated with the concept of food sovereignty. as regards price volatility as a result of speculation in foodstuffs, the report could and should have gone further, notwithstanding some pertinent remarks, and in particular pointed out that the only way to prevent such speculation is to put an end to the instruments which make it possible, such as otc derivatives. the committee on budgets has also been criticised for its lack of a clear policy on the environment.

in writing. - my approval of this report was dictated by the dramatic situation in sub-saharan africa and the least developed countries in terms of food and the need for urgent intervention at this level. i have some reservations about more specific paragraphs in the report, particularly those relating to export subsidies, cap reform and the competitiveness of agriculture in developing countries. as regards a reduction in export subsidies, i believe that the eu should be more cautious, because although this is an important imperative, this type of measure must be in line with the principle of reciprocity by the other trading blocs in the context of the wto negotiations. i cannot fully agree with the rapporteur when she calls for a more thorough reform of the cap to enable developing countries to be more competitive. this statement deserves careful consideration and, above all, precise contextualisation, since there are several factors contributing to the distortion of trade, in addition to the cap. finally, as regards the competitiveness of developing countries, there are multiple variables at play and the lack of competitiveness cannot be attributed solely to subsidised agriculture in developed countries.
in writing. − the concept of food sovereignty instills the need to ensure that people have sufficient resources to cope with famine situations. this is one of the greatest challenges for economic development today. the recent price increases in food markets bear this out: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european parliament, including the provision of information on the activities of the european parliament and the commission. the timeliness of eu action to contribute to the food sovereignty of developing countries, with reference to the populations, is undeniable. in agreeing with this approach, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - more than 1 billion people in the world live under the burden of hunger, malnutrition and lack of a food security policy. this is due to a number of reasons, including the volatility and the steady increase in food prices since 2007. the report, which demonstrates the role of the eu and the member states in finding solutions to food security, aims to create a common programme of the european institutions and the member states to achieve the first millennium development goal. following the eu strategic framework on food and nutrition security presented by the commission in march 2010, the role of small-scale food production, which forms the basis of developing economies, should be emphasised. clear and specific support policies and programmes need to be adopted, which understand the diverse realities of developing countries. learning by doing is essential for the training of farmers and for the self-sufficiency of countries. in addition, a clear focus on research and innovation is needed to increase agricultural productivity. these concerns should be reflected in the agreements with developing countries, and in particular in the economic partnership agreements concluded with the acp countries.
in writing. the report deals with the unilateral declarations annexed to the council's minutes. i share the rapporteur's view that this matter deserves a political response rather than a change of rules. unilateral declarations have no legal value and sometimes do not even correspond to the results of the negotiations, and can thus undermine the coherence of legislative work. the ep should send a clear message to prevent such statements from coming up during second reading negotiations.
in writing. - notwithstanding the interest which they may have, unilateral statements entered in the minutes of council meetings do not have the capacity to interpret community law and are not binding on the other european institutions. as a co-legislator, parliament should be informed of the issuing of such declarations.
in writing. − the conference of committee chairs asked the committee on constitutional affairs to clarify the european parliament's position on the meaning and legal status of unilateral statements recorded in the minutes of council meetings which, in the context of the co-decision procedure, could compromise the legal force and will of parliament as co-legislator. the report we have just voted on, drawn up by mr trzaskowski, draws attention to certain inconsistencies in the council's rules of procedure, even in their most recent version, following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, in particular by subordinating the ep to the governments of the member states and to the national parliaments, which enjoy privileged access. in this respect, i agree with this report, that unilateral declarations should be avoided, that the european parliament should be duly informed by the council at all stages of the legislative process and that publication in the official journal of the european union should be avoided.

in writing. - while it is true that legal clarity is necessary in eu legislation, it is also true that such clarity cannot result from the limitation of the national sovereignty of a member state which considers that certain legislation may be prejudicial to its interests. this question is all the more important as a path of submission of the sovereignty of each country and each people over its present and its future and the realization of its aspirations and aspirations to the interests of the financial oligarchy of the great powers of the eu is consolidated. the eu's laws and guidelines, and their increasingly centralising and anti-democratic character, are clear to the big multinationals and the financial sector, who clearly benefit from them. for the working and popular classes, particularly in countries like portugal, what is clear is that their rights and social gains are being brutally reduced, while the great fortunes are increasing. and when they're not satisfied, they want more. only the organized struggle of the people can stop them.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which is based on a request from the conference of committee chairmen to the committee on constitutional affairs to clarify parliament's position on the meaning and legal status of unilateral statements recorded in the minutes of council meetings. several committee chairmen expressed concern at the proliferation of such declarations, particularly in the context of the codecision procedure, where they could compromise the legal force and scope of the acts adopted. it is concluded that unilateral statements by member states on legal acts should not be published in the official journal of the european union and that recourse to them should be avoided as far as possible. the council must keep parliament fully informed at all stages of the legislative process.
in writing. the legal value of unilateral statements entered in the minutes of council meetings must be determined by the framework given to the sources of community law. in this context, the primacy, from the interpretative point of view, must be that of the meaning to be attributed to the legislative text: the value of unilateral statements is purely a function of the elder, and cannot indicate the decisive meaning of the interpreted provision, nor allow the member states to change unilaterally the meaning of a common provision. i voted in favour of this because i agree with this view.
in writing. - i support this report because i generally support the views expressed, since they cover all the main aspects of external trade policy in goods and services, defence instruments, investment and intellectual property rights, and they present the idea of using trade as a tool for humanitarian assistance and development.
in writing. - external trade is a key element for the european economy. in 2000, the european union accounted for 25% of world gdp and it is estimated that by 2020 this figure will decrease to 18% of world gdp. the centre of gravity of the world economy is shifting to developing countries. some 36 million jobs in the european union - equivalent to 18% of jobs - are linked to external trade. by 2015, it is estimated that 90% of economic growth will be generated outside the european union, increasing dependence on external trade. this report advocates exports as an anchor for economic growth and job creation, arguing that the commission should make strengthening external trade a priority. it called on the commission to present as soon as possible a genuinely long-term strategy for external trade. in view of the foregoing, i support this report.
in writing. - a trade policy for europe will have to take account of the profound changes the world has undergone in recent years and to focus on the concrete benefits of the free market, without neglecting the political implications of its trade action, nor the dignity of the people involved in the production of goods and services and in trade on a world scale. it is essential that, in the present crisis, we have the courage to set ambitious goals and the political will to create the instruments necessary to achieve them. the commission is called upon to make this effort and to create the conditions for a competitive but supportive, ambitious but realistic trade policy.
in writing. - mr daniel caspary, author of this report on the need for a new trade policy for europe under the europe 2020 strategy, welcomes the communication from the committee on trade, growth and international affairs and the recognition that the eu's prosperity and growth depend on an optimised functioning of the international trade system. thanks to the world trade organization, there has been a great expansion of world trade in recent years. the european union, which accounted for 25% of global value added in 2000, is forecast to fall to 18% by 2020. in contrast, the emerging economies of china and india, which accounted for only 10% in 2000, will account for around 25% by 2020. these data force the eu to rethink its trade policy. the commission must analyse the causes of this situation very carefully and adopt measures to meet global challenges, in line with other european policies and in response to population growth. although it is a pessimistic but realistic document, i am voting in favour of this report and hope that the measures advocated to mitigate the consequences of the slowdown in european exports will be taken into account.

in writing. - i voted against two points in this important report on the union's external trade policy, with which i agree. the first point of disagreement concerns the use of exceptional trade preferences granted to third countries as a means of emergency aid in disaster situations. it happens that the eu has specific instruments for emergency aid and that trade preferences are clearly unsuitable for this purpose, because they take time to take effect, because they can hardly be focused to benefit those who need help most in these circumstances. secondly, while financial aid is charged to the eu budget, trade preferences will only affect countries that are harmed by imports facilitated by tariff exemptions or reductions, which are usually the least wealthy countries in the eu, as shown in the case of pakistan. i also voted against the reservations expressed in the report concerning the use of trade defence instruments (anti-dumping and anti-subsidy measures), which are essential means of fair trade action against unfair commercial practices by certain countries (china first) which thus seriously harm european companies on the european market itself.
in writing. − on 9 november 2010, the european commission presented its communication entitled 'trade, growth and international issues on the future trade strategy of the european union'. this communication aims to present the external aspects of the eu 2020 strategy and is primarily a continuation of the 2006 global europe strategy. i share the rapporteur's concern that this commission document offers good impetus for the coming months but does not represent a real strategy for the future. the report concludes that the commission should be urged to carry out an analysis and forecast which takes account of the current world economic situation and the current situation in the european union, as well as the likely future developments, and to draw up a long-term strategy which meets the needs of the european union and its citizens. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − this €43.9 million increase in the management of migration and refugee flows is intended to equip existing agencies and support instruments in this area with the necessary resources to be able to support the eu's multi-faceted response to the recent events in the southern mediterranean. the high migratory pressure in that region has led to the need to strengthen union actions under the external borders fund, the return fund and the refugee fund. support for the efforts of the member states most directly involved should be strengthened in order to relieve them of the considerable burden they bear, reflecting the fundamental principle of solidarity. the capacity of the frontex agency should also be improved, in particular to be able to carry out maritime surveillance activities in the mediterranean. i support this report which helps to clarify the contradictory positions of the council, which, on the one hand, in its reading of the draft eu budget for 2012, proposed a cut in the funds allocated to the management of migration and refugee flows and, on the other hand, approved the strengthening of several actions and programmes to be carried out by frontex, as well as other instruments and mechanisms in this area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i support the need to strengthen the european union's support for the management of migration and refugee flows. the natural increase in migration flows requires a multi-faceted eu response. in view of the political developments in the southern mediterranean countries, it is essential to increase the budgetary allocation of the frontex agency, the external borders fund, the european return fund and the european refugee fund.
in writing. - this amending budget proposal aims to respond to the flows of migrants and refugees following recent developments in north africa and is financed through reallocation and/or additional funds. in view of the exceptional situation facing the southern european states, i support this proposal.
in writing. − the budget of the european union for 2011 was finally adopted on 15 december 2010. throughout the first half of 2011, the eu witnessed political changes (arab spring) in several countries in the southern mediterranean where some peoples, with eu support, overthrew decades-old totalitarian regimes. these events have led to significant migratory flows towards other countries, particularly from southern europe. as no such exceptional expenditure had been foreseen, the commission presented draft amending budget no 4 on 17 june 2011, in accordance with article 314 tfeu, which was adopted by the council on 12 september 2011. the project provides for a €41.1 million increase (commitment and payment appropriations) for the following funds: external borders, european return and european refugee funds, to finance transnational actions in emergency situations, plus a €54 million increase for the frontex agency (maritime surveillance). because the eu must honour its commitments, especially when human rights are at stake, i welcome the adoption of this draft amending budget.
in writing. - the amending budget voted today represents a budgetary increase for the heading corresponding to the management of migration and refugee flows, reinforcing and/or extending maritime surveillance operations in the mediterranean, which are said to be necessary to cover the additional needs arising from the exceptional and unforeseen increase in migratory flows from north africa. a substantial part of the amount now mobilised is directed towards operational expenditure for frontex eur 30 million in commitments , the agency responsible for implementing the european union's repressive, security-based policy on immigration. a policy that hides the real causes of immigration. the report does not mention, but it should, that the exceptional and unforeseen increase in migratory flows from north africa is inseparable from the military aggressions of nato and several eu countries in the region, sowing war, destruction and chaos. at a time of deepening economic and social crisis in the eu, it is significant and symbolic that this increase in support for fortress europe comes from unused funds from the european economic recovery plan.

in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the egf was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when we are faced with this serious crisis, with rising unemployment as one of its main consequences, the eu should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly in terms of support for people who have lost their jobs overnight. i have therefore supported the present report concerning the mobilisation of eur 3 944 606 from the egf for denmark to support workers made redundant by six companies in division 28 manufacturing of machinery and equipment in the midtjylland region.
in writing. - in recent years, many european industries have experienced difficulties due to globalisation, aggravated by the economic and financial crisis that threatens many countries in the world. in the present case, six danish machinery and equipment manufacturing companies in the midtjylland region laid off 813 workers eligible for support from the european globalisation adjustment fund. i regret that these workers are also suffering from the impact of the recent paradigm shift in international trade and the present crisis, and i hope that the european economy can find a new path to prosperity.
in writing. − the european union, recognising the very serious social consequences of the current economic and financial crisis, has set up the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to provide additional support to workers affected by structural changes in world trade. this report concerns a proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of eur 3 944 606 from the egf to support the reintegration of danish workers made redundant as a result of the current economic and financial crisis. this application, the 14th to be examined under the eu budget 2011, was submitted by denmark on 11 may 2010 and concerns 813 redundancies in 6 enterprises in nace rev. 2 division 28 (manufacture of machinery and equipment) in the region of midtjylland (dk04) in denmark. as this is a specific budgetary instrument and the amount requested has a legal framework and is in line with the proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf for denmark, i am voting in favour of this proposal and hope that it will help to alleviate the economic difficulties of the people in that region and to revive the local economy.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid is now to be granted to denmark, which has submitted a request for assistance in relation to 813 redundancies (325 of which are potential beneficiaries of assistance) in six enterprises in nace rev. 2 division 28 (manufacture of machinery and equipment) in the nuts ii region of midtjylland (dk04).
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. on 11 july 2011, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of denmark to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. this is the 14th application to be examined under the 2011 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 3 944 606 from the egf in favour of 813 redundancies (325 of which are potential beneficiaries of assistance) in 6 enterprises in the nuts ii region of midtjylland, denmark, during the nine-month reference period from 6 june 2009 to 1 march 2010. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. − the application submitted by denmark for assistance from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) concerns 813 redundancies (325 of which are potential recipients of assistance) in six enterprises in nace rev. 2 division 28 manufacture of machinery and equipment in the nuts ii midtjylland region. according to the commission's assessment, this application fulfils all the eligibility criteria defined by law. regulation (ec) no 546/2009 of the european parliament and of the council of 18 june 2009 amending regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 establishing the european globalisation adjustment fund temporarily extended the scope of the egf to cover situations such as this one where, as a direct consequence of the global economic and financial crisis, 'at least 500 redundancies occur in a nine-month period, in particular in small and medium-sized enterprises, in a division at nace level 2, in one or two regions adjacent to nuts ii'. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, in the hope that assistance for workers made redundant can be provided quickly and efficiently.

in writing. - another request for the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund. once again, it is portugal. this request is intended to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant at rohde a total of 974 redundancies, with 680 potential beneficiaries of assistance. the total amount is eur 1 449 500. the story of this dismissal is, unfortunately, similar to so many others. the report mentions that the company was jointly acquired by square four and the merchant bank morgan stanley in an attempt to save rohde and its production share. according to the plan, the plant in portugal was to continue production. only, as in so many similar stories, meanwhile, the layoffs began. this was coupled with a decrease in orders from the german parent company, which affected the situation of rohde's factory in santa maria da feira, leading to the opening of bankruptcy proceedings in september 2009 which eventually led to the closure of the factory and the dismissal of the workers. once again, here is the denunciation of the unfair criteria of this fund and its regulation. for a similar number of workers, germany applies for and obtains the mobilisation of an amount about three times higher than that mobilised for portugal.
in writing. − the decision to mobilise the egf in portugal is intended to support the reintegration of redundant workers into the labour market, for a total amount of eur 1 449 500, involving 974 redundancies, with 680 potential beneficiaries of assistance. the application was submitted by the portuguese government to the european commission at the end of 2010. the document states that the company was acquired in an attempt to save rohde and that the plant in portugal should continue to be in production. however, redundancies began, coupled with a decrease in orders from the german parent company, which affected the situation of the rohde plant in santa maria da feira, leading to the opening of bankruptcy proceedings in september 2009 which eventually led to the closure of the plant and the dismissal of the workers. when we considered this proposal in the working party of the committee on employment, of which i am a member, i stressed the injustice of this mobilisation for portugal involving only eur 1.4 million, whereas the mobilisation for a similar situation in denmark involved eur 3.9 million and for germany some eur 4.4 million. although we all voted in favour of it in order not to harm the workers involved, we have once again pointed out the profoundly unfair criteria of this egf.
in writing. the european parliament has approved the mobilisation of €1.4 million to support workers made redundant by the footwear company rohde in santa maria da feira, a region with an unemployment rate above the national average. 974 workers, 87% of whom were women, were subject to collective redundancies following bankruptcy proceedings that were at least dubious. i voted in favour. the european globalisation adjustment fund does not prevent redundancies or bankruptcies, but it does allow for increased support for victims of collective redundancies. the approval of this support is an important counter-cyclical signal to the policies of eliminating social rights and facilitating dismissals. i regret, however, the slowness of the whole process. the support will eventually be unlocked 17 months after the first layoffs. i would also like to see more action in the area of education and training, as 78.5% of the workforce are low-skilled (not completed compulsory schooling).
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid is now to be granted to portugal, which requested assistance in relation to a case concerning 974 redundancies, 680 of which are potential beneficiaries of assistance, in an enterprise located mainly in the municipality of santa maria da feira, and which also affected the neighbouring municipality of ovar, both located respectively in two nuts ii regions: northern and central portugal.
in writing. − portugal submitted an application for the egf on 26 november last year following 974 redundancies at rohde sociedade industrial de calçado luso-alemã, lda., a footwear manufacturing company. of the 974 workers made redundant, 680 are potential beneficiaries of assistance (the portuguese authorities estimate that around 70% of the workers made redundant will participate in measures co-financed by the egf, while the rest will find another job, move abroad, retire or participate in other actions complementary to those co-financed by the egf). the assistance package will include recognition of skills, vocational training, grants for self-initiated training, training and assistance for business creation, support for self-employment and recruitment incentives. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this report which will promote the reintegration of these portuguese workers into the labour market.

in writing. - i welcome this report and strongly support the egf as an instrument of eu solidarity towards workers affected by the negative effects of globalisation and the current crisis.
in writing. - the accession of bulgaria and romania to the union entailed an enlargement of the customs union between the member states, so there was a need to negotiate compensatory adjustments with members of the international trade organisation who had rights over those countries. such adjustment is required if the adoption of the union's external tariff entails a decrease in the advantages for third states. this was the case for argentina, which, as the rapporteur argues, must now be compensated for this damage, since, as article xxiv (4) of gatt states: the establishment of a customs union or a free trade area must aim to facilitate trade between the constituent territories and not create obstacles to trade between other contracting parties with these territories.
in writing. - the draft council decision on the conclusion of an agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the republic of argentina pursuant to article xxiv:6 and article xxviii of the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt) 1994 relating to the modification of concessions in the schedules of the republic of bulgaria and romania in the context of their accession to the eu. the aim of this agreement, signed in april 2011, is to make a compensatory adjustment due to the increase in the consolidated duties and to comply with the requirements of the world trade organisation (wto). the products covered by the agreement are boned buffalo and beef from argentina and the increase in the erga omnes tariff quota for common wheat, barley for the brewing industry and maize. as argentina has been affected in its trade rights by the enlargement of the eu customs union to romania and bulgaria, i welcome the approval of this agreement and the re-establishment of argentine trade rights.
in writing. − as a consequence of accession to the european union, member states are obliged to harmonise their trade policies with community rules. this report is an example of this. in view of the agreements between the eu and different countries on customs and trade, the countries applying for eu membership have to amend the concessions provided for in their schedules. at the time of the accession of bulgaria and romania, the tariff concessions of these two countries to argentina were lower than those established at eu level. it is therefore argued that in order to comply with wto requirements and not to harm argentina, these two countries should open their markets to argentinian products. we consider that this constraint and obligation infringe the sovereign right of each country to decide its bilateral relations in international trade in accordance with its interests and the needs of its population. this change to the concessions in the bulgarian and romanian lists will not alter the volume of imports of argentinian products into the european union, so the impact on other countries, such as portugal, will be non-existent.

in writing. - article xxiv (4) of gatt stresses that the establishment of a customs union or a free trade area must be designed to facilitate trade between the constituent territories and not to create obstacles to trade between the other contracting parties and these territories. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report, because argentina has the right to see its trade rights restored, rights which were slightly affected by the enlargement of the eu customs union to romania and bulgaria. with such agreements, the eu demonstrates its respect for the rules of the multilateral trading system, hoping to contribute to a collective will to reach a global agreement in the doha round.
in writing. - argentina had suffered a slight deterioration in its trade rights as a result of the enlargement of the eu customs union to romania and bulgaria, and this accession had the effect of reducing argentina's customs duties. this agreement shows that the eu intends to respect the rules of the multilateral trading system, hoping in this way to contribute to a collective will to reach a global agreement in the doha round. the studies carried out and the dialogue with the interested parties have confirmed that this agreement does not harm the eu's agricultural interests, which is my main concern, as it merely restores the rights previously existing in argentina. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - the enlargement of the community to include bulgaria and romania has made it necessary to revise the external arrangements for customs arrangements concluded with third countries. under gatt (general agreement on tariffs and trade), the establishment of a customs union or a free trade area should aim to facilitate trade between the constituent territories and not create obstacles to trade between other contracting parties with these territories. the subject of the agreement in the form of letters between the european union and argentina is part of this renegotiation process, which aims to bring the range of rights of both contracting parties back into balance within the framework of the common tariff rules. the agreement covers boned beef and veal, boned buffalo meat and the increase in the tariff quota for common wheat, barley, barley for the brewing industry and maize. i voted in favour of this agreement because i agree with the subject matter.

in writing. − this report, by vicky ford, deals with a proposal for a directive on the requirements for budgetary frameworks in the member states of the european union. the proposal for a directive, which is part of a package of six legislative acts (six pack - five regulations and a directive) aimed at improving the eu's economic governance, was the subject of intensive negotiations between the council and the european parliament, which tabled more than 2000 amendment proposals, and was approved by the finance ministers of the eu member states, under the polish presidency of the council, on 16 september in wroclaw, poland. this directive must be applied faithfully and rigorously, as it will enable the european union to monitor and punish the member states. it cannot, as so often happens, have a purely cosmetic effect. it must be effective and oblige countries to provide appropriate statistical data which will enable a correct diagnosis of the financial situation of each member state. i welcome the adoption of this directive, which is a comprehensive and integrated solution to the crisis, introduces transparency criteria and sanctions for those who provide incorrect data and encourages budgetary accountability by setting minimum requirements for national budgets.
in writing. - we voted against this report, which concerns the proposal for a directive laying down the requirements for the budgetary frameworks of the member states, as it constitutes one of the most serious attacks on their sovereignty, a situation which will be even more serious for those in the euro area who are considered to be in excessive deficit and who, in addition to the permanent surveillance by the european commission, may be subject to sanctions. it is a directive which is part of the legislative package on so-called economic governance, which consists of six legislative titles, and which is a real attack on social and labour rights, and is also part of the european union's crusade against national independence and sovereignty, as is clear from the final agreement between the three institutions - the european parliament, the council and the european commission. the postponement of this vote only served to confirm what had already been decided. the results of the vote are an unprecedented attack on the rights of national parliaments and the constitution of the portuguese republic, whose members are bound by the european union's increasingly neoliberal guidelines on their country's budgets.
in writing. − incorrect and unrealistic macroeconomic and budgetary forecasts can significantly undermine the effectiveness of budgetary planning and thus compromise the commitment to budgetary discipline, whereas transparency and discussion of forecasting methodologies can significantly improve the quality of these forecasts. transparency is a key element in ensuring the use of realistic forecasts in the conduct of fiscal policies, which implies the publication not only of the official macroeconomic and budgetary forecast that is prepared for budgetary planning purposes, but also of the methodologies, assumptions and relevant parameters that have served as the basis for the preparation of those forecasts. in order to facilitate the preparation of the forecasts used in budgetary planning and to clarify the differences between the commission's and the member states' forecasts, each member state should have the opportunity to discuss annually with the commission the assumptions underlying the preparation of the macroeconomic and budgetary forecasts.
in writing. - although i abstained on some of the reports in the so-called economic governance package, i regard this legislative package as a remarkable step forward in the integration of the budgetary and economic policies of the member states, with a view to strengthening budgetary discipline and reducing macroeconomic imbalances and competitiveness asymmetries, which are conditions for the stability of the euro, economic recovery and the external competitiveness of the european economy. this legislative package corrects some of the main shortcomings in the architecture of the euro and monetary union that had been identified long ago. if this new regime had been introduced at the start of monetary union, it is very likely that the eu would have weathered the banking and then economic crisis of 2008 in a different way and could have been spared the current public debt crisis. if we cannot prevent the crisis, at least we can learn from it to prevent future crises. the adoption of this legislative package also sends a strong message of confidence to financial markets and economic operators in the guarantees of the stability of the euro. the adoption of this major reform is therefore welcome.
in writing. − the present draft opinion on the establishment of requirements for member states' budgetary frameworks was voted on as part of the legislative package to strengthen economic governance in the eu and the euro area. i voted in favour of this report because it follows up, in essence, the rapporteur's concerns, particularly as regards the amendments which have been made to the following key points: 1) the general objective of the proposal must relate to the promotion of a high level of employment, the guarantee of adequate social protection and the fight against social exclusion; (2) rules should be established to ensure improvements in national budgetary frameworks in the context of the european semester for policy coordination; (3) the requirements for national budgetary frameworks should ensure not only that the financial planning of the member states is based on realistic forecasts, but also that due attention is paid to the sustainability of their social protection systems, including health and pension systems; (4) finally, the requirements for national budgetary frameworks should also be designed to encourage member states to achieve the eu's employment and growth objectives.
in writing. − economic governance, as the adoption of policy measures aimed at achieving certain practical results, can only meet its objectives if there is reliable data on the situation of the member states. in other words, the success or failure of member states' economic intervention becomes all the more random the less reliable the data available. thus, the need for transparency and reliability of macroeconomic and budgetary forecasts by member states is a necessary condition for the success of economic governance measures. cooperation between the member states and the commission in this field, guided by the criterion of seeking data realism, is therefore necessary to facilitate effective policy action.

in writing. − the defence and guarantee of human rights are not only an integral part of the european cultural tradition, but also the starting point of the community's legislative structure. in this sense, the european union is committed, in all the fora in which it participates, to defending a political orientation based on and centred on the protection of human beings. that being the scope of this resolution, which focuses in particular on sexual orientation and gender identity, i voted in favour.
mr president, commissioner, minister, ladies and gentlemen, the debate we are having here should not have even existed. the most elementary common sense and a sense of solidarity should have solved the problem we are discussing here today. in the european area, which we consider to be the epitome of prosperity, freedom and justice, there are today, according to the european union's own estimates, more than 40 million people at risk of food poverty, that is, without access to a full meal every two days. in 2009, 440,000 tonnes of food were distributed to some 18 million people. no one doubts that the situation will be even worse in 2012. the worsening economic and financial crisis has thrown many people and families into unemployment, while social policies have been drastically curtailed. it is therefore incomprehensible and unacceptable that six member states have blocked the legal way out so that food aid funding could be maintained in 2012 at the level of previous years. i also welcome the commission's gesture, in the person of the commissioner, who has endeavoured to find the appropriate legal solution to the question raised by the european court. the council's attitude reveals a shocking social insensitivity which runs counter to all the values on which the european construction is based. i therefore strongly condemn the recent position of the council of agriculture ministers and call on the polish presidency and the heads of state and government to resolve this problem once and for all at their next meeting and to dismiss their agriculture ministers, restoring the image of solidarity and justice which is the mark of europe and which some ministers seem, unfortunately, to have forgotten.
mr president, we have already stressed here on several occasions the importance of maintaining a free food aid scheme for some 18 million people, as was the case in 2009. and, knowing that more than 43 million people are in extreme poverty and at risk of food poverty, including 20 million children, who also here in europe sometimes look for food in the garbage can that they do not have at home, it cannot be accepted that this programme is reduced from 500 million to only 113 million euros in 2012 and 2013. while poverty requires other measures of substance than austerity policies, which are only aggravating poverty and social exclusion, it is essential to take account of the european parliament's resolution of 4 july, including the promotion of an agreement on guaranteed minimum incomes based on 60% of the national average income of each member state. it is time for the commission to make a proposal on this subject here too.
twenty years later, we see that progress has been made, but we also know that there is still a long way to go to achieve the objectives set then. 1.4 billion people still live in poverty, and the main victims are women. there are 80 million people in europe at risk of poverty, so this resolution is important. the next summit should be used by the international community to address the challenges related to the three pillars of sustainable development. the commission and the council must take an ambitious and united stance in the negotiations with a view to achieving a strong political commitment to tackle the multiple challenges of poverty eradication, health, food, employment, gender equality and energy supply. the summit should also promote the transition to a green economy, promote renewable energy, energy efficiency, but also measures to ensure universal access to energy. the summit should renew commitments to promote access to clean water and healthy food, the protection of ecosystems and biodiversity, the efficient use of resources, sustainable forest management and the fight against deforestation. it is an important and urgent agenda to defend the planet and to give people answers and improve their quality of life.
despite progress over the two decades since the rio summit, many of the commitments made in terms of sustainable development have not yet been fulfilled. rio+20 is an opportunity to reaffirm our commitment to the transition to a green economy. this transition requires a radical transformation of the energy sector, including the promotion of renewable energy and energy efficiency. renewable energy and energy efficiency have the potential to mitigate climate change, contribute to social and economic development and improve security of supply. in this context, i would stress the importance of innovation and science and the need for scientific and technological cooperation and technology transfer to developing countries and the promotion of sustainable development. on the other hand, it is essential to support education and training programmes, particularly for young people in all countries. the promotion of new skills will help to create new jobs and reduce social injustices.
the earth summit held 20 years ago focused the attention, concerns and hopes of many millions of people around the world. twenty years later, between ups and downs, worries have grown. the environment does not exist separately from everything else: society and the economy. our biggest environmental problem today is the existence of a world-dominant economic and social system, which, in marx's words, either grows and accumulates, or dies. a system that is constantly confronted with the limits of a land that, being generous, is finite and whose balances and vital processes depend on sometimes very delicate balances. there's no point in trying to paint capitalism green. it's its inherent unsustainability that is going to be discussed in rio next year. it is the current trade, agricultural, energy, industrial, economic and financial policies that must be discussed and questioned.

the shameful situation in the refugee camps in tunisia has already been mentioned here, and we all share and i share a great deal of what has been said by my colleagues who have just spoken. i will not go into that in particular, but i will refer to another situation which is more neglected, namely that of citizens who have been taken in by families in tunisia. this is one of those situations that should make us even more ashamed because we notice: the european union is not in a position to show solidarity, and it is not in a process of transition to democracy, and it is not in a position to show solidarity, it is not in a position to receive. i think it is indeed shameful that we can count the number of refugees that have been taken in europe as a few hundred. many of these people, contrary to what has been said, no, they cannot return to their homes. and there were children who were enrolled in public schools, which has implications for infrastructure, has implications for what is the reception in these countries. and that is why, commissioner, i am very sensitive to your appeal and i am not saying this ironically, i am saying this seriously, but please, what about the commission? what about europe? what can you do? how does europe live so well with this double standard? we are so quick to repatriate and so slow to help, commissioner. it can't go on like this.
i am not saying that we should not be concerned about the future of the european union. the first is whether this fund, in the context of an ongoing economic and financial crisis and the very likely recession worldwide, should be extended until the end of 2013 or not. and my answer is, it should be prolonged. it must be prolonged because it does not in fact avoid the evils of globalised capitalism or the economic and financial crisis, but it does at least have the virtue of supporting its first victims, those who are victims of collective redundancies. and this is no small matter in a europe which looks much more at capital than it does at work. it's exactly because this is a redistributive fund that it's so important. it's because it offers a possibility to those who have far fewer opportunities. our conservative colleague thinks that we are instead supporting those who are not successful. because it's exactly because we're supporting those who don't succeed and giving them a second chance that this fund justifies its existence. but it is true that it must be changed. he should be retired. and from that point of view, i want to support the resolution adopted in the committee on employment because it reaffirms all the points that had already been adopted by this house a year ago and puts forward an extraordinarily important new one: the commission's proposal is that the funding of this fund should be in line with the co-financing rate of the structural funds. and this point had not been achieved. this fund cannot support redundancies in rich countries any more than it can support redundancies in countries which are suffering the most from recession and austerity policies.
mr president, the crisis in the european union has had serious consequences in all the member states and thousands of workers are affected by the redundancies caused by globalisation and the crisis. we cannot but express our solidarity with these workers who have lost their jobs and say that europe must help the member states to maintain an employment rate and to combat unemployment. a rapid reintegration of workers into the labour market is a priority objective. an example of the usefulness of this fund is my country, portugal, which has used it four times - although we are aware that access to this fund could be improved, especially in the countries most affected by the crisis. the existence of this globalisation adjustment fund has helped thousands of workers through vocational training measures, aid for the creation of new businesses and recruitment incentives. this proposal is positive because it will allow member states to call on this fund to support workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic and financial crisis. we support the extension of the deadline and believe that the member states most affected by the crisis should have greater and easier access to this fund to support globalisation and the crisis.
there are three questions which need to be clarified in this debate about the existence of this fund. the egf is only a palliative to the worsening unemployment caused by the european union's structural policies, which are undermining its industrial sector and making life easier for multinationals, which do not take any social responsibility. secondly, the egf uses funding criteria which are deeply unfair and lead to situations such as those we have had in this week's plenary session, where we approved egf mobilisations for a similar number of workers, allocating some eur 4.4 million to germany, some eur 3.8 million to denmark and only eur 1.4 million to portugal, which is the worst-off country. finally, the high co-financing rate required of the member states, of 35% of the overall amount provided for. to alleviate this situation, we hope that our proposal to reduce the share of state co-financing to only 5%, especially for countries with weak financial conditions such as portugal, will be accepted.

in writing. − this report, by pervenche berès, is concerned with a proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 establishing the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to support workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade, with a view to extending the exceptional period of this fund until 30 december 2013. in 2008, the eu, seeing a significant increase in the number of businesses closing and the resulting increase in thousands of unemployed, decided to temporarily amend the egf regulation, reducing the number of unemployed from 1000 to 500, extending the implementation period from 12 to 24 months, covering workers made redundant as a result of the economic and financial crisis and increasing the co-financing rate from 50% to 65%. the exceptional period - which started on 1 may 2009 - ends on 30 december 2011, as in 2008 it was expected that by this date the crisis would have been over. i welcome the adoption of this proposal extending the temporary derogation period, as unfortunately the prospect of an end to the economic and financial crisis remains a mirage.

in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 established the globalisation adjustment fund to support workers who have been subject to collective redundancies as a result of the relocation of their companies due to global competition. this scope was extended by regulation (ec) no 546/2009 of the european parliament and of the council of 18 june 2009, introducing an exception for redundancies resulting from the economic and financial crisis and an increase in the co-financing rate of the fund. that derogation expired on 30 december 2011. however, given that the causes of the crisis have not yet been addressed, i voted in favour of the proposal to amend the regulation to extend its application until 31 december 2013.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in 2006 to support and show solidarity with workers who have been made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns. the egf aims to facilitate the reintegration into employment of workers in areas, sectors and territories affected by economic disruption by co-financing active labour market measures. in view of the scale of the economic and financial crisis and the speed with which it has spread, the commission envisaged a revision of the egf regulation in the european economic recovery plan. in this context, a temporary derogation was created to extend the scope of the egf to cover workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic and financial crisis and to increase the level of egf co-financing from 50 to 65% for the period ending on 30 december 2011. with a sharp increase in the number of requests for assistance, the expected continuation of the effects of the crisis in the closure of businesses and the need for budgetary consolidation in the member states, the extension of the temporary derogation, for which i voted in favour in the european parliament's plenary session, is justified.

madam president, commissioner, this is a good report by mr casa. first of all, we must ask why vat should be revised in the european union. first of all, it must be made compatible with the single market. the more vat schemes and varieties, the less fluid the market will be. vat reform favours e-commerce, focuses competition on the value and price base of goods and services rather than on tax differences, combats fraud and ensures much-needed confidence, especially in cross-border transactions, improves the economy of smes and reduces administrative burdens. what other ancillary measures are already in place in the single market that can be combined with vat? firstly, a simple, clear and transparent digital support mechanism, measure 7 of the single market. measure 5 on services, the need to review legislation on standardisation and the implementation of the services directive. measure 9 which aims to remove tax obstacles and to explicitly review the vat system and the equalization of vat in online and face-to-face commerce that we all feel when we order books. the pressures for vat reform have two basic reasons. first, the economic crisis. more revenue is needed, including probably in some countries the reduction of labour contributions to promote economic development by passing this burden on to vat. secondly, the second major source of pressures is population ageing, demographic ageing and the trend of shifting from indirect to direct taxes, which is due to the reduction of the population base of incidence. the balance between direct and indirect taxation must be reconsidered, and we must reconcile subsidiarity with harmonization in these reforms. the range of variation in the standard vat rate needs to be narrowed so that we can all understand each other better. more transparency is needed in the definition of the reduced rate of vat and its scope, a clear and widely disseminated list of reduced rates. it is necessary to study exemption thresholds for smes, knowing full well that each exemption entails a train of small or large frauds. finally, i welcome the commission's recent proposal to create a european vat.

in writing. - i welcome this agreement as it allows all carriers in the european union to benefit from the right of establishment, thus avoiding discrimination on grounds of nationality between air carriers in the member states. the new agreement will give priority to eu competition rules over existing provisions in bilateral agreements.
in writing. − the court of justice of the european union has held that traditional designation clauses in bilateral air service agreements concluded by member states infringe union law in so far as they allow a third country to refuse, withdraw or suspend licences or authorisations granted to air carriers designated by a member state but whose capital is not substantially owned by that member state or by nationals of that member state and whose effective control is not exercised by them. those clauses constituted a manifest discrimination in breach of article 49 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which guarantees nationals of member states exercising their freedom of establishment the same treatment in the host member state as that accorded to nationals of that member state. this new agreement negotiated by the commission, in addition to correcting a discriminatory situation, obviously brings advantages in that it replaces provisions of 8 of the current bilateral agreements with a horizontal agreement which restores a sound legal basis for relations between the eu and the republic of cape verde.
in writing. − this agreement with the republic of cape verde represents a small step on the difficult path of the process of european construction which the eu and the member states have been continuously following over the last decades. in this case, and in the field of aviation, a further step is taken towards the full implementation of the common market, adding that in this case we are talking about its external aspect. i would stress both of these aspects and i am also pleased that this specific agreement has been concluded with cape verde, an african country with an official portuguese language, which as a portuguese mep is an additional factor of satisfaction.
in writing. − the eu-cape verde agreement on certain aspects of air services ('the agreement') replaces eight bilateral agreements of the same type and harmonises the common rules for air services across the union. the agreement will allow all european union carriers to benefit from the right of establishment and ensure that there is no discrimination against air carriers of member states on grounds of nationality. the agreement also lays down rules on fuel taxation and competition.
in writing. - the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and the republic of cape verde on certain aspects of air services. eight eu countries (portugal, belgium, germany, italy, the netherlands, romania, spain and the united kingdom) had bilateral agreements with cape verde, which is contrary to the spirit of the eu with regard to the standardisation of procedures, as ruled by the court of justice of the european communities. in accordance with the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations and the agreement was signed on 23 march 2011. on 17 may 2011, the council decided to submit the agreement to the european parliament for approval. i therefore voted in favour of the conclusion of this agreement between the eu and the republic of cape verde as it will allow european air carriers non-discriminatory access to routes between the member states and this african country, as well as clarifying the rules on the taxation of aviation fuel and competition.
in writing. - the proposal to conclude an agreement on certain aspects of air services between the eu and cape verde raises doubts and concerns as to the consequences that may result from this, given the current framework of liberalization and, consequently, of monopolistic concentration in the sector. the direct consequence of sacrosanct free competition is that member states are less able to defend their flag carriers. the path of market opening has obvious impacts on national airlines, in a sector which is strategic for safeguarding national interests. moreover, the agreement aims to replace, by a single union agreement, certain provisions on competition in bilateral agreements concluded by certain member states, including portugal, thus harmonising the set of requirements and competitive permissions which allow carriers to establish themselves in the territory of cape verde. it thus overrides the specificities of the bilateral agreements of each member state in this field. as in the previous cases of brazil, the usa, canada and the west african states, we did not vote in favour of this report.

in writing. − the air agreements which have been concluded by the eu with third countries, on the basis of article 49 tfeu, aim to eliminate the discriminatory basis on which certain european union air carriers are discriminated against in relation to freedom of establishment. in the case of this agreement with cape verde, the union intends to replace the eight existing bilateral agreements with a union-wide agreement, the so-called horizontal agreement. this agreement includes clauses on eu designation, on the right of establishment between air carriers of the member states, on a community framework for the taxation of energy products and on competition rules. the union has exclusive competence in this area, but i would reiterate that the european parliament should be consulted during the negotiation process, not just at the end of it. i welcome this report because i believe that both parties will gain economic advantages from the conclusion of the agreement, promoting mobility and accessibility between european countries and cape verde.

in writing. − the european investment bank (eib) can lend to projects not only in the member states of the european union but also in other countries. this report addresses the issue of eu budgetary guarantees to cover sovereign and political risks associated with lending and loan guarantee operations outside the eu. this is a matter for co-decision (parliament and council). on 21 april 2010, the commission presented to the parliament and the council a proposal for a decision granting an eu guarantee to the european investment bank against losses under loans and guarantees for projects outside the european union. at parliamentary committee level, a number of amendments were adopted at first reading, including commitments resulting from multiple informal contacts and opinions received from five other committees. on 27 january 2011, the committee on budgets (budg) adopted its recommendation to the plenary, incorporating an overall commitment amendment in the form of a consolidated text. this is an important step in that it safeguards and helps to make operational the possibility of granting loans, for example, for the development of projects in developing countries.

in writing. − since 2009, the european parliament and the european council have been deciding jointly on the external mandate of the european investment bank. it expires in october 2011. however, a commission proposal proposes to extend it until 2013. i am pleased to note that the negotiations between the various institutions have come to a positive conclusion, with a significant increase in the guarantees offered by the european union to the eib. let us hope that these funds will be used effectively and contribute to the solution of the crisis.
in writing. − the rapporteur considers that the text now presented broadly reflects parliament's first reading and is the result of intensive negotiations carried out from february to june 2011. it also considered that, overall, the extension of the eib's mandate would allow for better coordination in achieving eu objectives, allowing for substantially increased accountability and transparency and better use of the eu budgetary guarantee. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the aim of the commission proposal is to maintain the eu guarantee for the eib's external financing operations. at first reading, the european parliament's main objective was to increase the transparency of the eib's activities and to seek to integrate its activities into the eu's long-term objectives. among the points advanced at the time was that the commission's annual report should address the relationship between the support granted and the eu's external policy objectives, the implications of this action in terms of environmental and energy sustainability and the link between the funds made available through the eib and those of other donors. these amendments were accepted and the council took account of the observations of the european parliament. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. the european commission has published a report on the implementation of the european union's financial instruments. this was in response to the financial crisis and the intensification of the bank's support for the countries in which it operates. the proposal is to generate new recoverable capital by converting accumulated distributable reserves into share capital and will therefore not have an immediate impact on the eu budget. i am voting in favour of this report because i consider it to be an important measure to help reverse the current european economic and financial situation. the additional liquidity injection into the ebrd will objectively allow the bank to strengthen and develop its business. although the european parliament would have liked to go further, i am nevertheless pleased that the trilogue has agreed to submit a report by the end of the fourth review of capital resources, assessing the european public investment banking system and also examining the possibility of restructuring the banks concerned, as requested earlier by the european parliament.
in writing. − the board of governors of the ebrd decided to increase the capital in may 2010. the authorised capital of the bank will be increased by 50% from eur 20 billion to eur 30 billion. the purpose of this capital increase is to respond to the financial crisis and to step up the bank's support for those to whom it invests. as this is a non-controversial proposal and is intended to respond to a crisis situation, it cannot but deserve my vote in favour.
in writing. − in may 2010, the board of governors of the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) decided to increase its share capital by 50%, from eur 20 billion to eur 30 billion. it is the first eu financial institution to be set up to support europe's economic development following the break-up of the soviet union. the ebrd mainly supports the development of the local sector: small and medium-sized enterprises, private individuals, municipalities, regional cooperation, innovation, job creation, energy, green projects, etc. this report, by sharon bowles, is based on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the subscription by the european union of additional shares in the capital of the ebrd, in proportion to its current share of 3,031%. i agree with this subscription and welcome the eu's capital increase for the ebrd, an example of the eu's economic and shareholding capacity, and i hope that part of this capital will be used to support the development of the countries involved in the so-called arab spring.
in writing. − this proposal for a decision aims to allow the european union to subscribe to new feasible operations of the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) in the context of the capital increase decided by the board of governors of the ebrd in 2010. the decision shall also authorise the governor of the ebrd, representing the european union, to deposit the required instrument of subscription. in may the board of governors decided to increase the bank's capital by 50%, from eur 20 billion to eur 30 billion, in order to respond to the financial crisis and to step up the bank's support for the countries in which it operates. the capital increase consists of eur 1 billion of paid-in capital and eur 9 billion of capital realizable. as the committee on budgets points out, the proposal is to generate new capital by converting accumulated distributable reserves into share capital. the operation will therefore have no immediate consequences for the eu budget. the risk arises from the possibility of having to raise additional capital in the unlikely event of a significant negative development of the bank's investment portfolio.
