in writing. the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) was set up in 1990 to support the development of market economies from europe to central asia. the ebrd's share capital is currently held by the european union, the european investment bank and 61 countries. on 14 and 15 may 2010, the governors of the ebrd decided to adopt two resolutions to increase the bank's share capital by 50% from eur 20 billion to eur 30 billion. the issue of 100,000 shares will be proportional to the shareholding of the members in the bank, with the eu subscribing 3,031 new shares with an individual nominal value of eur 1,000. i agree with this report because the ebrd can increase its activity in the countries where it operates, ensure support for new markets, encourage increased cooperation with other european financial institutions and apply best prudential banking practices. i would also like to stress the importance of the adoption of mechanisms for monitoring the european banking system, of achieving the objectives set in the field of external relations and of allowing the eu to maintain the same number of votes in the ebrd.
in writing. − arms trafficking is one of the illegal activities that continue to threaten the internal security of the eu. this initiative addresses intra-community trade and transfers of firearms, their parts, essential components and ammunition and is part of the eu's policy to combat transnational crime, providing for the strengthening of the fight against illicit trafficking in firearms, including export controls and the tracing and reduction of the proliferation and spread of small arms worldwide. the united nations firearms protocol aims to promote, facilitate and strengthen cooperation among states to prevent, combat and eradicate the illicit manufacture of and trafficking in firearms and related items. given that only 13 member states have ratified the protocol so far, i think it will be important to adopt this initiative through the ordinary legislative procedure in order to allow article 10 of the protocol to apply to all member states. it will thus allow for the harmonization and simplification of procedures, while at the same time it should make the fight against illicit trafficking in firearms more effective by promoting and strengthening cooperation between states.
in writing. − this report promotes the fight against illicit trafficking in firearms and aims to apply article 10 of the un protocol against the illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms, their parts and components and ammunition, annexed to the united nations convention against transnational organized crime to all member states by promoting and strengthening cooperation. i would like to stress the general objective of this document, which is to harmonize and simplify procedures, and to combat effectively the illicit trafficking in firearms by promoting and strengthening cooperation between the member states. i voted for this report with satisfaction, because with the un protocol in force for the 27 the eu wins, the citizens win and world peace and security win.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the application of article 10 of the united nations firearms protocol, which lays down measures for the authorisation of exports, imports and transit of firearms, their parts, components and ammunition, as it contains important measures to combat illicit trafficking in firearms, provides for stricter control of legal transfers and strengthens cooperation between national authorities.
in writing. − the aim of this proposal is to transpose article 10 of the united nations protocol on firearms, their export, import and transit into european law, focusing on the issue of the export of firearms for civilian use. the general objective of harmonising and simplifying procedures is complemented by the objective of combating illicit trafficking in firearms effectively by promoting and strengthening cooperation between member states.
in writing. − this report, by mr salvatore iacolino, analyses the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council implementing article 10 of the united nations (un) protocol on firearms and establishing measures to authorise the export, import and transit of such weapons, their parts, components and ammunition. this proposal covers firearms for civilian use, in particular small calibre weapons and those used by hunters or sport shooters. the new proposal for a regulation transposes article 10 of the un protocol against the illicit manufacture of and trafficking in firearms into eu law. i support this proposal unconditionally, because all measures to combat illicit trafficking in firearms are welcome. let us remember what happened in sweden just recently with the slaughter of almost a hundred victims. it is also essential that all those involved in this trade feel that they are properly controlled so as to prevent the diversion of these weapons to the black markets. it's the safety of the citizens that's at stake.
in writing. - the purpose of this regulation is to transpose into community law article 10 of the un protocol against the illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms, their parts and components and ammunition (unfp). this protocol, which is the first binding agreement on small arms worldwide, was approved by the united nations general assembly in may 2001 and has been ratified by more than 80 un member states, including portugal. the regulation covers trade in and transfer of non-automatic weapons, their parts and ammunition for civilian use to third countries, including countries that have not ratified the unfp. this protocol sets out positive steps towards the fight against illicit trafficking in firearms at global level, focusing on the control of imports/exports and the transit of articles. unfp therefore considers that each state should establish or maintain an effective system of export and import licensing or authorization, as well as an effective system of measures relating to international transit.
in writing. - the purpose of this regulation is to transpose into community law the implementation of article 10 of the un protocol against the illicit manufacture of and trafficking in firearms, their parts and components and ammunition (unfp). this protocol, which is the first binding agreement on small arms worldwide, was approved by the united nations general assembly in may 2001 and has been ratified by more than 80 un member states, including portugal. the regulation covers trade in and transfer of non-automatic weapons, their parts and ammunition for civilian use to third countries, including countries that have not ratified the unfp. we consider that the unfp is making positive steps towards combating illicit trafficking in firearms at global level by focusing on import/export controls and the transit of items, noting that each state should establish or maintain an effective system of licensing or authorizing export and import, as well as an effective system of measures relating to international transit. but we do not follow the rapporteur in all his positions.
in writing. - new rules were adopted today to control the export of firearms for civilian use, such as small arms or those used by hunters or sport shooters. this legislation, already agreed with the eu council of ministers, establishes a system of export from member states to third countries, establishing a common system for the whole union. the aim is to strengthen the fight against illicit trafficking in firearms. the new regulation transposes article 10 of the un protocol against the illicit manufacture of and trafficking in firearms into eu law.
in writing. − this report introduces new rules to control the export of firearms for civilian use, such as small calibre weapons or those used by hunters or sport shooters. this new legislation, agreed with the eu council of ministers, establishes a regime for exports from member states to third countries, establishing a common union-wide system, with the aim of strengthening the fight against illicit trafficking in firearms by transposing article 10 of the un protocol against the illicit manufacture of and trafficking in firearms into the eu. european exporters will have to obtain an authorisation from a member state before they can export firearms, their parts or ammunition to countries outside the eu. an export authorization shall be granted only if the importing country agrees and if there is no objection from a transit country. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation introduced the system for the export of firearms from member states to third countries, pursuant to article 10 of the un protocol against the illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms, their parts and components and ammunition. i voted in favour of this proposal because it is a balanced proposal which contributes to safeguarding public safety while at the same time taking account of the socioeconomic implications of such a regulation.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation on the application of article 10 of the unfp protocol aims to incorporate it into european legislation. the aim is to apply a harmonised and simplified system for trade in firearms for civilian use within the eu. the unfp protocol provides for authorisation for the import, export and transit of the abovementioned articles to third countries, taking into account certain categories of users. this simplification of procedures is intended both to combat the illicit production and trafficking of arms as a threat to public security and to ensure the sustainability of the european industry itself. i think it is essential that the member states ratify the protocol, since it is an essential and complementary document to the united nations convention against transnational organized crime.

in writing. the exceptional trade measures applied to bosnia-herzegovina, serbia and kosovo are designed to revitalise the economies of the western balkans and to promote their political stabilisation. the shortcomings and tensions that continue to affect the countries of the region are still evident today, and therefore the special care and attention of the european union towards them and the encouragement not to abandon the already expressed intentions of one day being able to join the eu are fully justified. the termination of the measures in question would undermine the trade advantages of the above-mentioned states and would be a significant setback for their economies. i therefore welcome the extension of certain elements of regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 to allow for its extension until 31 december 2015 and for the implementation of adjustments resulting from the entry into force of the union's agreements with bosnia and herzegovina and serbia.
in writing. the report, drawn up by vital moreira, is on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 adopting exceptional trade measures in favour of countries and territories participating in or linked to the european union's stabilisation and association process. since 2000, the eu has exceptionally granted unlimited access to the european market, exempting almost all products originating in these countries from duties, in order to support internal reform processes and the implementation of democratic regimes. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is essential to extend until 31 december 2015 the trade preferences with the western balkan countries linked to the eu's stabilisation and association process (albania, bosnia and herzegovina, croatia, kosovo, macedonia, montenegro and serbia). these preferences give these countries significant economic advantages in their exports to the member states.
in writing. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's external borders are not encroached upon by the countries of the region. these preferences, initially provided for in council regulation (ec) no 2007/2000, subsequently codified by council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 of 30 november 2009, expired at the end of 2010. the rapporteur argues that the end of trade preferences could have very adverse consequences on the overall economic performance of all the western balkans, with the consequent negative repercussions on their internal reform and transition processes. these processes are, as is well known, part of the eu's enlargement strategy, which seeks to protect them in defence of the interests that govern the integration process itself - the same ones that benefit from it. the regulation provides for measures that the commission may adopt if imports of agricultural and fishery products cause serious disturbances in eu markets and their regulatory mechanisms. these are provisions which the commission can use at its discretion and which do not sufficiently protect the member states which consider themselves to be affected. the products concerned (some may be considered sensitive products) include: fish, meat and wine.

in writing. − with regulation (ec) no 2007/2000, the european union granted exceptional unlimited duty-free access to the eu market to almost all products originating in the countries and territories benefiting from the stabilisation and association process. the main objective of this measure is to revitalise the economies of the western balkans through privileged access to the eu market. the resulting economic development will promote political stability throughout the region. the benefits of this regulation shall expire on 31 december 2010. in view of the ongoing financial and economic crisis, it is necessary to extend these conditions until 31 december 2015 in order to ensure that the end of these privileged conditions does not lead to stagnation of the economies of these regions, which need good economic conditions to maintain stability and peace in this troubled region of the balkans.
in writing. − this report supports the extension of trade preferences with the western balkan countries until the end of 2015. the aim of the extension of this measure, which dates from 2000, is to maintain eu support for the revitalization of the western balkan economies through privileged access to the eu market. the end of the trade preferences would deprive the beneficiaries of an objective economic advantage in their trade with the eu. this could have very adverse consequences on the overall economic performance of all the western balkans, with the consequent negative repercussions on their internal reform and transition processes. moreover, their economic recovery could be seriously jeopardised. for these reasons i have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the western balkan countries, which benefit from the stabilisation and association process, have privileged access to the community market by virtue of the trade preferences introduced by regulation (ec) no 2007/2000, subsequently amended several times and codified in regulation (ec) no 1215/2009. according to that regulation, such trade preferences would only be granted until 31 december 2010. however, given the current financial situation, the consequences of not renewing them could be extremely serious for the economies of these countries. to this extent, i consider that the present amendment to regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 is fully justified, which, in addition to introducing certain adjustments made necessary following the entry into force of the bilateral agreements with bosnia and herzegovina and serbia, extends the application of these trade preferences until 31 december 2015.
in writing. − the eu granted, through regulation (ec) no 2007/2000, exceptional unlimited duty-free access to its market for almost all products originating in the countries and territories benefiting from the stabilisation and association process with the aim of revitalising their economies, which was, after several amendments, codified by council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009. those trade preferences are currently applied to bosnia and herzegovina, serbia and kosovo, while products originating in albania, the republic of croatia, the former yugoslav republic of macedonia or montenegro continue to be eligible under regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 for more favourable measures than the trade concessions established under the bilateral agreements. in so far as the interim and stabilisation and association agreements provide for trade concessions in favour of bosnia and herzegovina in respect of the products identified in the trade preferences, those concessions should be deleted from the regulation. however, the end of the trade preferences would deprive the beneficiaries of an economic advantage in their trade with the eu. the proposal voted on today therefore amends certain elements of the regulation to allow for its extension until the end of 2015 and to make certain adjustments following the entry into force of the agreements.

i thank mrs rühle for the excellent report she has prepared. the advantages of public procurement are certainly well known, but the obstacles are also clear: the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to take part in the negotiations on the future of the european union. the quality of prices/complexity of laws and procedures dichotomy is evident. it is essential to look at existing good practices, particularly in portugal, where e-procurement has worked well and has facilitated public procurement. effective european public procurement is a prime means of controlling government deficits and other growth. it should therefore have a stable and predictable legal framework, less bureaucratic procedures to attract smes and to uphold social and environmental values. that is why i welcome the intention that commissioner barnier has put forward here to review public procurement this year as one of the 12 priorities of the single market act.
i would like to begin by congratulating mrs rühle and all those who have worked with her. the question of electronic public procurement is important in the field of public procurement. unfortunately, the targets proposed by the european union (50% of electronic procurement in 2010) fell short, with an average of just under 5%. only a few countries, such as my own, portugal, have been successful in this area. the advantages of electronic public procurement are self-evident and are set out below: it allows the replacement of costly access procedures by simple consultation of the electronic platform, i.e. it reduces many costs for businesses, especially smes; the promotion of process parts via the internet and the ease of receiving them increases the number of suppliers, increasing competition and making it possible to buy better; makes the process of awarding public contracts easier and more flexible; simplifies access to public procurement in the european union, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises, thus facilitating the participation of these important economic drivers in the public procurement market. in this respect, we welcome and encourage the european commission to strengthen the mechanisms to make electronic public procurement an increasingly widespread reality.
we agree that public procurement should be based on principles such as maximising social welfare and protecting the environment. the purchase of goods and services by public authorities using public funds must meet the needs of citizens in each member state, and must do so while ensuring respect for criteria of economic, social and environmental sustainability, but the creation of a european public procurement market, under the concrete conditions in which the integration process is currently taking place, does not ensure, on the contrary, the attainment of these objectives. the main thing is to open the way for large economic groups to a market worth some 17% of the total gdp of the european union. the imbalances that exist today within the european union and the very serious situation facing the weakest economies justify that public procurement in these member states can be geared to national preference, stimulating domestic production, the activity of smes and shorter, socially and environmentally more sustainable supply chains, thus constituting an important instrument of economic recovery in the service of the essential growth and development, which allows overcoming deficits and blockages. here is our proposal and our challenge.
in recent weeks, the portuguese have lost 14% of their pensions, in recent years they have lost 30% of their pensions, a fifth of their salaries have had countless tax increases. now, what you didn't know is that this struggling country is making direct investment abroad, which has soared 134 percent in the last year and of which 80 percent is going to a single country, the netherlands, a country in the european union where 19 of the 20 largest portuguese companies have shell headquarters to avoid taxes. what this means, ladies and gentlemen, mr president, is that there are countries that are losing out on the crisis, but there are countries that are gaining out of the crisis, and this is bad for both of us because it prevents us from seeing the evidence, which may destroy us, that common budgetary targets without fiscal harmonization are pitting europeans against each other and could destroy the euro. in 1919, a european named john maynard keynes said that if the debate were based on prudent generosity and not stupid greed, europe's financial prospects would be much better. the decades that followed proved him right tragically, and we know that no one got away with it.
madam president, as in greece, so in portugal too the government is carrying out a serious offensive against labour rights and the social functions of the state. under the pretext of complying with the troika memorandum, the portuguese government has presented a state budget proposal which is a direct attack on workers' rights, public services and the social functions of the state: wage cuts, increased working time, devaluation of collective bargaining, higher taxes on goods and services of general consumption and reduction or closure of essential public services and supports in such important areas as health, education, social protection, transport and communications. all this heralds a serious economic and social disaster, and so there are the small and large struggles of the workers and the populations who deserve our solidarity, as in the past weekend in montemor-o-novo, in the alentejo, in the fight against the closure of the emergency service at night, or in lisbon, where more than 10 000 trade unionists and activists held a national plenary and a parade with great popular support. these struggles will continue in several other sectors, and a general strike is also planned for 24 november. hence our solidarity and appeal to all to do the same.

in writing. - having regard to the opinion of the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission, which concluded that the proposal in question was merely a codification of existing texts without any substantive changes, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - as the directive aims at codifying previous diplomas which are scattered (with advantages in terms of accessibility and familiarity with the legislation), without any changes being made in the material aspects, i voted in favour.
in writing. − in order to simplify and ensure clarity and transparency in european union law, this report on tyres for motor vehicles and their trailers and their installation on such vehicles meets the objective of codifying eu legislation. this report brings together the various acts on this subject in their entirety, preserving the content of the codified acts in their entirety. the technical requirements for motor vehicles and their trailers, as regards tyres, are thus aimed at approximating the laws of the member states for the purpose of the type-approval procedure. in this way, union law is made more accessible and understandable to european citizens, who can fully enjoy their rights.
in writing. − i support this report, considering that an area of freedom, security and justice, as enshrined in the treaties, must meet the needs of citizens and businesses, for example by creating clearer and simpler procedures, while improving access to justice, so as to adequately protect individual substantive rights and to regulate conflicts between the parties. i would stress that any approach to adr should go beyond consumer disputes to include civil and commercial transactions between companies, whether private or public, family disputes, defamation cases and other disputes of general interest or between parties with different legal status.
in writing. − alternative dispute resolution avoids the use of courts, helping consumers and traders to resolve disputes through the intervention of a third party, mediator or arbitrator, providing a quick and cost-effective alternative to legal action. this report calls on the commission, in cooperation with the member states, to carry out information campaigns to make consumers and businesses aware of the benefits of using them. it also suggested that the commission should set up a multilingual european portal on alternative dispute resolution on the internet, where consumers could find out how it works and their rights and obligations. finally, it underlines the crucial role they play in family disputes, as by reducing psychological damage they can help the parties to re-establish dialogue and thus help to ensure the protection of children. i therefore support this report.
in writing. − a genuine area of freedom, security and justice can only exist if the fundamental right of access to justice is properly safeguarded, in particular through clear, simple and accessible procedures. alternative dispute resolution (adr) seems to me to be likely to be a quick and cost-effective alternative to the current judicial practice. it is important to strengthen citizens' confidence in the internal market and in the enforcement of rights in international disputes by adopting the necessary legislative measures to ensure the uniform development of these systems throughout the eu. a balanced approach between the use and flexibility of adr systems on the one hand and the guarantee of the protection of consumers' rights and their access to fair, confidential, impartial, transparent, prompt and effective procedures on the other hand should therefore be safeguarded, which will undoubtedly bring benefits to the eu economy. it is also important to ensure regular monitoring and evaluation of adr entities by independent evaluators. in parallel, awareness-raising campaigns and pilot projects are being carried out to ensure that appropriate information is provided to businesses and consumers in general.
in writing. − those who know the courts of the member states are aware of the increasing difficulty they are having in ensuring the timely resolution of disputes brought before them. the complexity of procedural laws and the number of cases in court have overwhelmed judges, magistrates, lawyers and court officials who, despite their competence and dedication, find it impossible to address all disputes in a timely manner. many of these issues currently flooding the courts are not of particular legal complexity or economic importance and can be resolved through alternative dispute resolution methods that prove to be more effective and less complex. there are many examples of such facilities operating across the union. i do not think that we should try to impose models on the member states in relation to these mechanisms, but rather to provide them with information on the practices and experiences of each country so that they can improve their mechanisms.
in writing. − sustainable economic growth to end the economic and financial crisis facing the european union has been one of the commission's main objectives. in the work programme for 2011 and in the communication of 13 april 2011, the commission, responding to the request of the ep to present a legislative proposal by the end of 2011 on the use of alternative dispute resolution (adr) mechanisms in the eu, identified adr as one of the 12 levers for strengthening consumer confidence and capacity to act. this report on adr in civil, commercial and family matters contains a set of proposals aimed at making access to justice for european citizens through a conciliation process quicker, more accessible and cheaper. in addition to their cross-border nature, adrs should be executed online, as online purchases are growing exponentially. i welcome the possibility of extending adrs to smes. i welcome the adoption of this report and hope that very soon all member states will be able to transpose the adr framework directives into national legislation.
in writing. - the report on alternative dispute resolution in civil, commercial and family matters which was voted on today includes an analysis of alternative dispute resolution, particularly at cross-border level, which we consider to be positive, given the scarcity of information on forms of judicial intervention in this area. these alternative forms may enable the parties to avoid the lengthy and often costly appeals to the courts. these are forms of mediation and arbitration that in many cases are related to trade, consumer, environmental or family disputes. they can therefore have quick and cost-effective alternative processes and ways to resolve conflicts through the intervention of another element (mediator or arbitrator). given the way in which public authorities, including legal services and other bodies, play an important role in many countries in encouraging the settlement of disputes without recourse to judicial channels, we see this as a positive way forward.
in writing. - considering that alternative dispute resolution methods, which enable the parties to avoid traditional arbitration procedures, are likely to constitute a quick and cost-effective alternative to legal action, i voted in favour of this report. i support the commission's intention to encourage the use of alternative dispute resolution methods which are accessible, fast, effective and low-cost, with benefits for all parties when compared to current judicial practice.
in writing. - from the community's point of view, the proper functioning of the judicial institutions is indispensable for citizens' confidence in the single market. the eu's action has thus long sought to prevent the existence of highly differentiated legal systems from creating a gap in accountability which in essence contributes to increasing mistrust between citizens in the various member states. these difficulties have been exacerbated by the volume of cases which courts in all member states have been faced with. in short, in addition to the fact that we are faced with very different legal systems, the judicial machinery itself has been operating less and less efficiently. alternative dispute resolution means can play an important role in this context: in the present case, the court of first instance has not yet ruled on the question of the interpretation of article 2 of the sixth directive. i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe that these means of dispute settlement contribute to citizens' confidence in the justice system.
in writing. − the european parliament voted today on its report on alternative dispute resolution in civil, commercial and family matters, in response to the consultation launched by the european commission on this subject to examine the possibility of developing a harmonised legislative framework in these areas, while maintaining the existing frameworks. i believe that alternative dispute resolution is a possibility to be considered and that its potential has not yet been fully exploited. in addition, online transactions require effective and appropriate dispute resolution and therefore merit particular attention in the implementation of alternative modes. such alternative dispute resolution methods are less costly, faster and offer practical solutions and fewer formalities, making them more attractive to citizens. in particular, as regards consumer protection, such mechanisms are of great importance for the proper functioning of the european internal market, as they allow for the effective application of the rules and capture the confidence of consumers and businesses.

in writing. − this report concerns a commission proposal to postpone deadlines laid down in directive 2000/52/ec concerning compression ignition engines with a power of between 18 kw and 560 kw intended for installation on agricultural or forestry tractors. this directive sets emission limits for carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, hydrocarbons and particulate matter. the directive sets progressively lower limit values for the successive phases corresponding to the various dates set for the adaptation of the maximum emission levels for exhaust gases and particulate matter. the next stages established are stages iiib (starting on 1 january 2011) and iv (starting on 1 january 2014). in view of independent studies and the data compiled by the commission showing that more time is needed to allow manufacturers to develop systems that are in line with phase iv, i understand the need to postpone the start date of phases iiib and iv for tractors in categories t2, c2 and t4.1 by 3 years.
in writing. - this directive covers compression ignition engines with a power of between 18 kw and 560 kw, intended for installation on agricultural or forestry tractors. it aims to set emission limit values for carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxide, hydrocarbons and particulate matter, which were changed in 2005 without any specific impact assessment on the technical feasibility of this application. to achieve the level of compliance with these values, it is necessary to install after-treatment systems in the engine compartment which, due to their large size in comparison with the engine, cause technical problems and do not ensure the correct operational performance of the tractor. the commission considers that more time is needed to enable manufacturers to develop compliant systems and therefore proposes to postpone the obligation to comply with the requirements of stages iiib and iv for tractors of categories t2, c2 and t4 by 3 years. 1. the proposal is reasonable. the reduction of emissions of air pollutants for better air quality is certainly an important objective, which we are fighting for. measures to achieve this include research and technological development, but also incentives for the agricultural sector to exchange and acquire up-to-date low-emission technologies, particularly from small and medium-sized farmers.

in writing. − directive 2000/52/ec sets, in stages, the emission limits for carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxide, hydrocarbons and particulate matter from agricultural and/or forestry tractors. however, this tax should take account of the specificities of the different types of tractor. the requirements requested in phases iib and iv affect the size of the vehicle and therefore its operability. this report thus meets the need to postpone the implementation of these two phases for three years to allow time for a more in-depth assessment of the impacts of this directive as well as technological developments in this field. the clarity and coherence of european union law will allow for better legislative quality and efficiency in implementation when transposed by the member states, and at the same time for better understanding by european citizens.

in writing. − this report concerns a commission proposal to make directive 97/68/ec more flexible, setting maximum levels for emissions of carbon monoxide (co), hydrocarbons (hc), nitrogen oxides (nox) and particulate matter (pm) from engines of non-road mobile machinery. this report challenges the commission's view that manufacturers lose competitiveness if they comply with stricter environmental legislation. green innovation and low-emission technologies can only emerge with the help of a legislative framework to support them. only in this way will it be possible to achieve the eu 2020 objectives and enable the transition to a low-carbon society. it is essential to take steps forward, not backward. i agree with you that the global economic and financial crisis cannot be used as a reason for changing environmental standards. investments in environmentally friendly technologies are important for promoting growth, employment and health security in the future. i therefore take the view that this report takes account of environmental protection and safeguards, the development and competitiveness of industry, and is a balanced proposal which aims to mitigate as far as possible the impact of the current economic crisis on engine and machinery manufacturers.
in writing. the directive in question (97/68/ec) sets maximum emission levels for carbon monoxide (co), hydrocarbons (hc), nitrogen oxides (nox) and particulate matter (pm) for engines of non-road mobile machinery. this category includes various types of machinery, for example, for construction, agriculture and forestry, railway transport (locomotives and motor cars) and inland waterway vessels. it is noted that pm and nox emissions from this type of machinery represent respectively 7% and 16% of the total value. in order to ensure that the limits laid down in this directive are complied with in stages, a flexibility scheme has been introduced which allows manufacturers to replace engines gradually. according to the rapporteur, the engines in question are produced by only a small number of large companies. the european commission now proposes to extend the flexibility scheme, giving these companies more time to make the necessary replacements. the rapporteur was opposed to this outright, citing environmental and public health reasons, and proposed a much tighter regime. in the committee on the environment, it was possible to reach a consensus which, being more flexible than the rapporteur's initial proposal, is close to this one, restricting the margin of manoeuvre created by the european commission. we think it is a fair solution, and we have supported it.

in writing. − directive 97/68/ec set maximum emission levels for carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter from engines of non-road mobile machinery, resulting in a set of measures in union law aimed at the environmental protection and sustainability of the common space. in view of the technical adaptation effort involved in such a regulation, a system of flexibility was introduced, seeking to reconcile the objective of meeting the proposed targets with the need to provide a certain time-gap to allow firms to reshape their production processes. the european commission has, however, proposed an extension of the flexibility scheme, referring in particular to the difficulties facing industry as a result of the economic crisis. in the light of the rapporteur's report, i believe that the proposed model should not be abandoned, without prejudice to the possibility of extending the scope of the flexibility scheme in certain special cases. the general trend should be maintained, continuing the path towards reducing carbon emissions. on the other hand, it is a very appropriate way of rewarding companies which have invested in technological re-adaptation - reasons why i voted in favour.
in writing. - directive 97/68/ec is an important element in the field of the environment, since it sets maximum levels of emissions of carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, nitrogen oxides (nox) and particulate matter (pm) from engines of non-road mobile machinery. since nox and pm emissions are the main sources of air pollution, action is important in this sector. this directive was amended in 2004 to allow engine manufacturers a flexibility scheme in stages. manufacturers are thus allowed to place on the market a limited number of engines that meet the emission limits of the previous stage, 20% of the manufacturers' annual sales or a fixed number of machines, the latter for small producers. the report therefore seeks to approve the extension of the flexibility proposed by the commission. the 20% threshold is thus increased to 50% and the fixed number is also increased until december 2013. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that at this time of crisis, which is affecting the non-road mobile machinery industry, particularly the construction and agricultural sectors, we must support small and medium-sized producers. on the other hand, technological development has not accompanied this directive and we must therefore make provision for the necessary flexibilities.

in writing. - given that public procurement represents millions of euros annually, its economic importance cannot be called into question. for this reason, although there is a long tradition of community legislation on these same contracts, it will never be too late to call for better and more effective laws, ensuring full transparency of procedures, preventing all forms of corruption or manipulation of tenders for the benefit of a competitor, limiting to the maximum the number and value of contracts awarded without a competition or without negotiation, and guaranteeing effective competition in the internal market between competing undertakings, regardless of their country of origin. it should also be noted that in the field of electronic public procurement, portugal is a good example today, with all the gains that this represents in terms of simplification of procedures, efficiency and cost and time savings for both companies and public administrations, and transparency and accessibility.
in writing. − this report on the modernisation of public procurement policy comes as the 40th anniversary of the entry into force of the buildings directive, which was the first european legislation on public procurement. the advantages of implementing this legislation are indisputable in terms of transparency and lowering the price of contracted work, but we cannot say that all of these were positive aspects. in fact, transaction costs and outside counsel have gone up. in this time of crisis we need clear rules and transparency in the processes, qualification systems and electronic passes that make life easier for businesses, reduce costs and provide an incentive for modernisation. the objective of 50% of public procurement being carried out electronically by 2010 (with the exception of portugal) has been missed. it is not justified that companies should have to submit some 20 original documents for each call for tenders! efficiency needs to be increased through the use of the mail and the reinforcement of electronic templates. i therefore welcome this initiative to simplify, make more flexible and modernise public procurement policy and hope that it will benefit smes by reducing transaction costs and allowing them access to tenders which they do not currently have.
in writing. - this report cannot be dissociated from the concrete conditions under which the process of european integration is taking place, its nature, its matrix characteristics and objectives. the very discussion of this subject in the committee on the internal market, which is considered to be competent on the subject, is indicative of what is intended: to open the way, fundamentally, to the major european economic groups to a market worth about 17% of the eu's overall gdp - the public procurement market. everything else is not enough to conceal this intention. including all the rhetoric around social and environmental principles to be taken into account in public procurement. while it is true that public procurement must take full account of these principles of maximising social welfare and protecting the environment (when we talk about the use of public money, the pursuit of the common good must necessarily be a primary concern), it cannot be ignored, as we said in the plenary debate, that the perspective of commercial opening as stated in this report is not the best way of ensuring that these principles are observed. the suggestion and the challenge we put forward during the debate remain: to orient public procurement, particularly in the member states which are currently facing the greatest difficulties, towards national preference.
in writing. − public procurement must take account of principles such as maximising social welfare or protecting the environment, and so the purchase of goods and services by public authorities using public funds must respond effectively to the needs of the citizens of each member state, while ensuring that criteria of economic, social and environmental sustainability are respected. however, the creation and development of a european public procurement market, under the concrete conditions in which the integration process is currently taking place, does not ensure these objectives. the main aim of this initiative is to open the way for large european economic groups to a market worth some 17% of the eu's total gdp. however, given the current imbalances within the eu and the very serious situation facing the weakest economies, public procurement in these member states could be geared towards national preference, stimulating domestic production, the activities of smes and shorter supply chains - more socially and environmentally sustainable - thus becoming an important instrument of economic recovery, serving the essential growth and development, and allowing overcoming the deficits and bottlenecks that are facing today.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on modernisation in the field of public procurement. in fact, european public procurement legislation is celebrating its 40th anniversary this year. i believe that now is the right time to take stock and analyse where the successes and failures of european procurement policy lie. the new rules should be based on the original essence of the first degree: the guarantee of transparency, non-discrimination and certainty of competition.
in writing. - public procurement legislation is one of the areas where the intervention of union law is most limited and also one with the longest tradition, as this year marks the 40th anniversary of the first legislative intervention. this is an area where any effective intervention of union law can produce results that are advantageous to the economy. it benefits not only freedom of competition but also taxpayers in general, in that it makes transparency the central feature of the public procurement process. however, the highly technical nature of this field has increased so-called transaction costs, i.e. the costs that candidates have to bear in a public procurement process (e.g. in legal advice) to submit an application. the future of this legislation must therefore be simplified. in another respect, the path towards greater flexibility is justified: instead of the best price, the best solution prevails. i voted in favour of this view because i agree with it.

in writing. - i welcome this report in that, in order to gain a rigorous understanding of the current situation and of future developments in labour markets, the european commission's positive efforts towards effective implementation and support for worker mobility must be strengthened. this requires a further analysis of the infringement procedures addressed to non-compliant member states, of trends in occupational mobility in terms of competences, sectors and geographical areas, and the presentation of a comprehensive, multidisciplinary and long-term mobility strategy aimed at analysing and removing all existing legal, administrative and practical obstacles to the free movement of workers. given the current situation, the economic reasons for opening up labour markets have never been more pressing. i would like to stress that excessive protectionism in terms of labour mobility will lead to a growing separation between member states and a feeling of distrust which could affect the eu's performance as a global actor and could even weaken its competitive position. the time has come for the member states of europe to work and grow together.
in writing. − the right to live and work in another member state is one of the fundamental freedoms of the eu and is a basic element of european citizenship enshrined in the treaties. in fact, better transposition and implementation of the existing directives on the free movement of workers is needed, given that legal, administrative and practical obstacles remain to the full implementation of this fundamental freedom. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which stresses the need to promote information strategies on the rights of migrant workers and to simplify the administrative procedures relating to the exercise of the free movement of workers. better coordination between social protection systems is also needed to ensure that social rights acquired in advance are recognised. it is essential to strengthen the current legal framework for the recognition of academic and professional qualifications. the geographical mobility of young people should be promoted through learning mobility programmes and the teaching of foreign languages should be actively promoted. finally, i would stress the importance of the eures network in promoting the mobility of workers in the eu by providing information on job vacancies, information on vocational education and training opportunities and on living and working conditions.
in writing. - i believe that the restrictions in some member states on access to the labour markets for bulgarian and romanian citizens should be removed by the end of this year. i believe that these obstacles are counterproductive and discriminatory measures against european citizens. as long as there are no negative effects of labour mobility, there is no socioeconomic basis for maintaining barriers to entry into a new labour market. official data, including data from the european commission, show that eastern european workers have not generated unemployment or put pressure on social security systems. on the contrary, the flow of these workers has generated economic growth in the destination countries, estimated at about 1% of gdp. i voted in favour of this report because i regret the recent legislative proposals by some member states to weaken the rights of workers from the countries that joined the eu in 2004 and 2007, and i urge the commission to investigate whether these policies violate european law.
in writing. − eu citizens and their family members have the right to move and reside freely within the territory of the member states. living and working in another member state is a fundamental right of every european citizen, although statistics show that very few people currently enjoy it (2.3%). the mobility of workers is of an important socioeconomic nature both for the eu and for the member states, and also contributes positively to the pursuit of the employment objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy. there are still a number of obstacles and restrictions to the full exercise of this fundamental freedom which, by infringing this right, also end up hindering the recovery of eu economies and may have counterproductive effects such as the increase in illegal work and the exploitation of workers and an expansion of the shadow economy. support the promotion of occupational mobility, based on a comprehensive, multidisciplinary and long-term strategy that eliminates all existing legal, administrative and practical obstacles to the free movement of workers. i stress the need to develop a coherent, efficient and transparent policy, focusing on labour market needs and economic trends, to strengthen solidarity and responsibility-sharing between member states, and to define a clear legal regime on legal migration.
in writing. - the principle of free movement has been one of the great achievements of the european union as a union of states and peoples. it translates the ideas of freedom of movement for workers, establishment and provision of services between the different member states, which reinforce the notions of cooperation, solidarity and progress and are concepts which must therefore be deepened and continually improved. i believe that the free movement of european citizens, when motivated by employment issues, is a right which we have as european citizens. i therefore believe that policies should be designed to protect european citizens who choose to change. with well-implemented legislative frameworks for labour mobility, the citizen gains on the one hand, because of the facilitating conditions he finds, and on the other, the host country, because of the simplified integration into its national labour context. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report because of its relevance and the ideas it contains.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that certain member states should remove, by the end of this year, the restrictions on access to their labour markets for bulgarian and romanian citizens. these obstacles are counterproductive and constitute discriminatory measures against european citizens.
in writing. − mobility is increasingly a value to be taken into account in contemporary economies and, in particular, in an area where the free movement of people and goods is in force, such as the european union. despite this essential freedom, few europeans still enjoy it, practicing their professions in states other than their own. there are some known obstacles to the mobility of europeans which must be removed. the european union and the member states have a joint responsibility to seek to promote the mobility of workers and businesses in the european area and to remove the remaining obstacles. in the face of the crisis the union is currently going through, european workers and their families, as well as host countries, have much to gain if they are not burdened with administrative requirements and can instead enjoy freedom of movement, establishment and the exercise of their professions.
in writing. - with the enlargement of the european union to include the peoples of the east, many citizens from these countries have turned to the west in search of better living conditions, especially higher wages. however, some member states, fearing increased insecurity, have closed their borders to these european citizens. this own-initiative report by traian ungureanu focuses on the mobility of workers within the eu and is based on the principle agreed by all member states that the movement of people and goods is an inalienable right. any eu citizen has the right to seek work in the west. moreover, it is necessary to demystify the idea that the influx of these workers is negative, not only because they contribute to european integration, especially at a time when there is a shortage of labour in some sectors, but because they represent a 1% growth in the gdp of the host member state. i therefore vote in favour of this report which calls for an end to the legislative proposals which are damaging to the rights of eu citizens.
in writing. − this report advances a set of guidelines to encourage the mobility of workers across europe. the perspective with which it does so is not, however, neutral. this movement of labour is encouraged with a view to forcing the labour force of different countries to compete with each other, forcing their devaluation and levelling them below working conditions. it is not for nothing that the report, along with guidelines for mobility, makes a point of the need to strengthen the application of flexicurity. the report does not deal with such essential issues as collective bargaining and the question of wages in the countries of origin and of destination. the question of brain drain, which is likely to intensify with the deep crisis in the eu's weaker economies, is also not being properly addressed. mobility cannot therefore be seen as the most effective solution to the problem of unemployment - as this report does. the view underlying the whole report and the view of the use of the eu's approximately 25 million unemployed imposes on the remaining workers a further devaluation of the labour force, generalising precariousness, intermittent employment and structural unemployment.
in writing. - this report contains guidelines which seek not only to strengthen the conditions for the application of flexicurity but also to send a positive signal and encourage the distribution of workers throughout europe, always in defence of a position which is more in the interest of capitalism than of workers, who are placed in competition with each other. so what we have, in general, is social dumping and other harmful consequences of this unwanted migration. despite some positive measures, which are generally nothing more than palliative aid, the report never considers the problem of unemployment and migration as a result of the neoliberal system and policies followed, nor the question of collective bargaining and wages in the host countries. on the contrary, it classifies the mobility of workers as the most effective solution to the problem of unemployment. influenced by the europe 2020 strategy and its instruments, the old policies are justified and made viable with the known consequences: labour flexibility and deregulation and the primacy of deepening the internal market through the liberalization and privatization of even more economic sectors. the 25 million unemployed are being used to impose on the rest of the workforce a further devaluation of the labour force, generalising precariousness, intermittent employment and structural unemployment, a wrong path which this report seeks to deepen.
in writing. - this report deals with the promotion of worker mobility. i agree with the conclusions, particularly as regards the need to strengthen the positive efforts of the european commission towards effective implementation and support for worker mobility. given the current environment, the economic reasons for the opening up of labour markets have never been more obvious. excessive protectionism in terms of labour mobility will induce a growing separation between member states and a feeling of distrust that could affect the eu's performance as a global actor and could even weaken its position on a competitive scale. i agree with the rapporteur that it is time for the member states to work and grow together.
in writing. - the free movement of workers is one of the great flags of eu law. the experience gained in the member states since then shows that the initial fears that free movement would affect access to employment for nationals are unfounded. in fact, it has been seen as a key way of balancing supply and demand, in other words, as an added value for the functioning of the common market. in view of this finding that free movement brings value to the single market, it is necessary, on the one hand, to reduce the artificial barriers to it. on the one hand, it is justified to strengthen, a priori, the information available to community citizens about the state to which they intend to emigrate, and on the other hand, a posteriori, to ensure that the states of arrival put at the disposal of immigrants the appropriate instruments for successful integration. i voted in favour of this guideline.
in writing. the free movement of workers is one of the basic principles of the entire history of the european internal market. this principle has gradually evolved over the last 40 years and is now enshrined in article 45 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. in its communication on reaffirming the free movement of workers, the european commission refers to all nationals of the 27 member states who work in a member state other than their state of origin, including their family members. however, some categories such as posted workers, workers from third countries, selfemployed workers and volunteers are not included. the issue of labour migration in the european union is considered a potential factor for imbalances in national labour markets, as, although it is considered a right, it is possible for member states to maintain barriers to the free movement of workers on a temporary basis, with regard to the opening of their labour markets to nationals of the new member states. although overall the movement of workers is positive for the whole of the european union, it is essential that additional measures are taken such as adaptation to new languages, recognition of diplomas, better information and further administrative simplification.

in writing. − the services directive, adopted in 2006, remains a vital instrument for the establishment of a fully functioning single market for services. the mutual evaluation procedure provided for in article 39 of the services directive is new. the aim is to assess the state of the single market in services after the implementation of the directive. the report calls on the commission to ensure maximum transparency in this assessment and invites the commission to present its conclusions to parliament as soon as they are available. it called on the commission to raise awareness among all member states in order to ensure the full and correct transposition and application of the services directive at national level. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the provision of services to consumers. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - as is well known, services account for one fifth of total eu internal trade but more than two thirds of gdp and employment, with activities covered by the services directive accounting for 40% of eu gdp and employment. a single market for services is therefore fundamental to the success of any european policy aimed at boosting growth, jobs and innovation, and preserving european competitiveness in a global world. however, the mutual evaluation has shown that further action is needed by the commission if the european economy is to benefit fully from the potential of the single market for services. in this respect, the commission will give priority to working with individual member states to ensure the correct and complete transposition and implementation of the directive throughout the european area.
in writing. − this report, by małgorzata handzlik, focuses on the mutual evaluation process under the services directive. this directive, adopted in 2006, was aimed at improving the functioning of the single market for services. although we consider this directive to be one of the best in recent years, the truth is that after two years, few member states have implemented it. this is why this report is important and why we need to make progress, not only with measures to improve it on the basis of the evaluation carried out, but also with its extension to other policy areas. in fact, nine out of ten jobs in the european union are in the service sector and its implementation should be mandatory, although monitoring by the commission and the member states is required to ensure that it is properly applied and that the freedom to provide services provided for in article 16 is respected. i welcome the adoption of this report and hope that all member states will implement the services directive and the creation of efficient one-stop shops, as this is a key instrument in the functioning of a single market for services.
in writing. - the aim of this report is to take stock of the situation regarding the single market in services after the implementation of the services directive, putting pressure on the member states which have not yet done so to effectively transpose the directive. as in 2006, we strongly reject this directive and its transposition into national law. the transposition of this directive on the liberalization of services could have serious implications for several countries, particularly those with more fragile social situations, such as portugal. the aim is to advance the market in more and more areas of social life, by affecting sectors where the state has traditionally exercised its social function through public services. this is yet another attack on important achievements of civilization. liberalisation will increase unemployment, poverty and social inequalities, benefiting only large service companies and large economic groups, especially in the richest countries. we believe that each country should retain the sovereign right to decide on the public services it wants, on their public ownership, their way of functioning and organisation, the rights of their workers and users. this is a struggle which will continue in the face of the attempt to transpose this directive into national law.

in writing. − the services directive introduced a mutual evaluation process to ensure the results of its application. the purpose of this monitoring is to identify how the directive has been applied in the member states, particularly in the implementation of relatively vague concepts which give national legislators a margin of discretion. in the present case, this analysis was limited to certain requirements for the application of the legislative text. this model deserves positive appraisal, as it provides a means of cooperation between elements of the various states, allowing the sharing of good practices and the joint resolution of additional difficulties that may arise in the meantime. it should be noted, however, that the effectiveness of this instrument is to a large extent due to its application being restricted to a small number of elements, otherwise the bureaucratic burden on national administrations would increase disproportionately. in the light of the foregoing, i have voted in favour.
in writing. - the internal market is one of the major objectives of the european union and its functioning must therefore be constantly improved. on the basis of the results of the mutual evaluation of the services directive, it is intended to analyse the problems which still remain and to define the benefits which can and should still be derived from this directive. the main problems identified relate to the non-full implementation of some rules which could contribute to the better functioning of the internal market in services and which have been adopted in recent years. there are also difficulties arising from the possibility for member states to reserve some service activities to certain specific operators, which translates into 8000 regulated professions in one or more member states. further action is therefore needed to help to exploit better the full potential of the internal market in services. the commission will develop an impact assessment of the services directive and should continue to work towards effective and correct transposition of the standards into the national laws of the member states.

in writing. the economic and financial crisis the world is going through is a profound crisis of capitalism, which clearly demonstrates the contradictions of a system which sacrifices natural resources and the strength of human labour in the interests of the growing accumulation of profit. social injustices and inequality in the redistribution of wealth are the cause and consequence of years of neoliberal policies, with a narrow class matrix, always on the side of those who have the most and can do the most, against those who depend on their work for a living. this report never calls these assumptions into question. on the contrary, the solution he points to is a governance framework based on the same supranational institutions, without democratic legitimacy, which have embodied the essence of the neoliberal offensive launched against the peoples and their sovereignty. the formalisation of the g8/g20 and the strengthening of the role of the imf and the wto are part of a line of support for the imposition of neoliberal economic guidelines. the guidelines also cover the so-called recapitalisation of the banking sector, as it has been carried out. this crisis can only be resolved by breaking with the current system and replacing it with one that respects democracy, deepens social and labour rights and encourages cooperation based on social progress.
