in writing. − over the last few decades, economic growth has been observed on a global scale, with an increase in the purchasing power of citizens in the most developed countries. recently, europe and the us have been facing an economic and financial crisis resulting from unsustainable macroeconomic imbalances, requiring rapid and expeditious response. having agreed with the six-pack presented by the european parliament on economic governance, i am once again in favour of the suggestions in this report, which are to strengthen overall economic governance and reform the international monetary and financial system and its institutions. i also support a comprehensive understanding and common action by the member states in the areas of monetary policy, international trade and the sustainability of public finances, and the need to consolidate the opening of markets to the outside world and to strengthen financial regulation and banking supervision. finally, i believe that there should be greater cooperation between public and private authorities and a commitment to strong economic governance in the eu in order to avoid new crises in the years to come.
in writing. - i support this report because i believe that despite the crisis, social europe must not give up its social system. europe should give rewards and tax incentives to companies that offer childcare facilities and day care, which allow single mothers to work while their children are supervised and educated. in addition, companies should be given incentives to offer training courses to mothers on the complex situation of managing their motherhood and working status. the netherlands is an example of a similar practice that can be implemented by other member states, where childcare is free of charge for single mothers. flexible work opportunities such as part-time work, teleworking and online work should be offered at local, national and eu level to enable single mothers to reconcile private life with working life. single mothers should be given priority access to affordable housing. for each child in care, additional unemployment benefits should be allocated to single mothers. member states could follow the example of germany in implementing this measure, as germany has already increased unemployment benefits paid to single mothers with dependent children.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which underlines the need to respond to the problems faced by single mothers in the eu. single mothers, whether as a result of divorce, separation or never having been married, represent an increasingly important group. in the eu, 5% of women are single mothers and most are aged between 25 and 64. the living conditions of certain single mothers can have consequences for their children. these children, who live with fewer resources and less opportunities to access training, may later fall victim to social exclusion and poverty. single mothers are also more exposed to stress, as they perform tasks normally shared by both parents, have less access to medical care, and are more vulnerable. member states should therefore respond to this reality and adopt public policies to support the needs of these families. i would highlight some of the measures that could be implemented, such as the adoption of indirect subsidy policies, the guarantee of health care, the possibility of opting for flexible working hours, priority access to social housing and more childcare facilities. finally, the exchange of good practice with the nordic countries should be encouraged.
in writing. - single mothers represent a demographic group often overlooked and 5% of the female population in europe is currently made up of single mothers. it is urgent to look at the challenges faced by single mothers in the eu on a daily basis. in particular, it is concerned with work, the risks of poverty and social exclusion, and the difficult balance between family and professional life. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is important to improve single mothers' access to employment, housing, care, education, health and social security systems. i think that tax breaks for single-parent families and tax deductions for companies that recruit single parents should be designed.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that member states should continue to invest in policies that promote reconciliation between work and family life, reduce poverty and increase the economic independence of single mothers and parents. i believe that the authorities in the 27 member states and the european union should give the greatest possible support to single mothers, thus contributing to greater social cohesion and to combating child poverty, which should also be one of the eu's priorities.
in writing. - as a result of social developments, the fact is that single parents are becoming more and more frequent, and as the rapporteur rightly points out, single-parent families are not a homogeneous group but cover a huge range of family, financial and social situations. there are therefore all kinds of single mothers and single fathers who need non-discriminatory mechanisms to enable them to take full responsibility for motherhood/fatherhood without this representing a social or occupational penalty.
in writing. - barbara matera has given us an excellent report on the situation of many mothers in the european union. in fact, more and more women are finding themselves in this situation: single, divorced, or widowed, facing the task of raising children and managing a household alone, performing tasks that should be done by two. 5% of european women are single mothers who are at increased risk of poverty as a result of the current economic and financial crisis. the eu is aware of this problem and aware that the problem of single mothers is often linked to child poverty. it is committed to tackling this situation by making it a priority and implementing new initiatives that meet the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy on poverty reduction, employability and gender equality. there is an urgent need to create conditions for access to health care, tax incentives for businesses and opportunities for flexible working. i welcome the adoption of this report which encourages member states to put in place policies to support single-parent families, in particular support for education, health and social security systems, as well as policies to promote employment, housing and care services.
in writing. - this report addresses the situation of single mothers and some of the problems they face. these are inseparable from the current socioeconomic context, dominated by severe attacks on the dignity and living conditions of mothers, especially working mothers and children. as the rapporteur points out, single-parent families are at a higher risk of poverty. in 2006, about 32% of single-parent families in the european union were at risk of poverty, compared with 12% of two-parent families. this risk is growing significantly at a time of exponential unemployment, wage cuts, cuts in social support and increasing limitations on access to public services and social protection, which in some cases force some mothers to put their children in institutions because it is no longer possible to guarantee minimum living conditions. for these reasons, we consider that this report falls short of what is needed in terms of employment with rights, living wages, respect for the right to maternity and paternity in the context of labour legislation, the establishment and maintenance of public and publicly managed networks of childcare, nursery and school, free maternal and child health services and care.
in writing. - this report addresses the situation of single mothers, especially in the current socioeconomic context, which is aggravating the problems and attacks on the dignity and living conditions of mothers and children. single-parent families live in situations that imply a higher risk of poverty, as the report itself states: in 2006, about 32% of single-parent families in the european union were at risk of poverty, compared with 12% of two-parent families. this situation is aggravated by the exponential rise in unemployment, the fall in the value of wages, and cuts in social support and access to public services and social protection, which in some cases force some mothers to hand over their children to institutions because it is no longer possible to guarantee the minimum living conditions, whether access to essential goods to feed their children or housing for the family. we therefore consider that this report falls short of the necessary measures, and that there is an urgent need for the creation of jobs and decent wages, respect for the right to maternity (in particular as regards labour law), the establishment and maintenance of public and publicly managed networks of childcare centres, kindergartens and schools, and free maternal and child health services and care.
in writing. − the studies presented indicate that the negative effects felt throughout the european community as a result of the economic and financial crisis have hit women the hardest. this impact was even greater for the vast majority of single mothers in early career and aged 25 to 40. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this report on single mothers, which calls on member states to grant tax breaks to single-parent families and tax deductions to companies employing single parents. the report is not of course the subject of this report, but my main concern is the large families in which one or both parents are unemployed.
in writing. - the group of single mothers has often been left in the dark when drawing up public social support policies, to the detriment of the specific problems it raises. on the one hand, from the point of view of mothers, difficulties often arise in terms of access to employment and vocational training; on the other hand, on the part of children, a shorter period of family life is emphasized and, also, as a reflection, the decreased opportunities to continue their studies. this is an area which deserves the attention of policy-makers and where it is justified to open a dialogue in order to find solutions in an open manner to alleviate the current fragility. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - the reality of single mothers - single, divorced or widowed, aged 25-64 - represents 5% of the eu total, including all socio-professional categories. this is a specific group that is often neglected by public policies in the member states and socially stigmatised. the report calls on member states, together with the eu, to take concrete action in the areas of education, health, employment, social security and housing to reduce the associated risks of poverty, social exclusion and difficulties in reconciling family and working life. there is a need to adapt public policies to different family models and situations. according to 2006 data, 32 per cent of single-parent households in the eu25 are at risk of poverty, compared with 12 per cent of couples with children. this is associated with disruption of education and the acquisition of vocational skills, the lack of school infrastructure for children at affordable prices and with working hours compatible with working hours, and social stigmatisation in some european societies. i think it is urgent to work together and identify best practices between member states and at the same time create specific support measures for this vulnerable group.
in writing. − organized crime exploits globalisation, the abolition of the european union's frontiers and the legislative disparities between member states in order to obtain ever more substantial benefits while ensuring its impunity. organized crime operates on a transnational, crossborder basis and as such must be tackled in the same way. the lisbon treaty has opened up new opportunities and provided new instruments at eu level, both in terms of judicial and police cooperation and the bodies responsible for combating transnational organised crime, making it possible to establish common standards to combat crime more effectively. this report, which i supported, sets out proposals for action to improve the eu's legislative framework and relations with other international institutions such as unodc and interpol. particular emphasis is placed on the full application of the principle of mutual recognition of decisions in criminal matters, with a view to combating this type of organised crime, and on improving judicial cooperation both between member states and with third countries.
in writing. − the creation of a genuine european area of freedom, security and justice requires a balance between these three realities, since citizens will only be able to enjoy their rights and freedoms in an area where they are guaranteed a high level of security, in particular through measures to prevent and combat crime, coordination and cooperation between judicial and police authorities and mutual recognition of judicial decisions in criminal matters. it is indisputable that organised crime operates on a transnational basis, with implications ranging from drug trafficking, human trafficking, corruption and money laundering, and it is essential to combat it in the same way, where justice cannot be confined to cross-border barriers. i welcome this report which represents a significant political effort to strengthen the fight against organised crime by setting out the guidelines and proposals for action to improve the eu legislative framework, such as confiscation of the proceeds of crime, implementation of transparency measures for the management of public funds and the preparation of a new directive on common investigative techniques. it is also important to strengthen and improve the functioning of the european structures involved in this fight in various capacities, such as europol and eurojust, and to strengthen cooperation between these agencies and the member states.
in writing. - as the report now adopted states, organised crime, especially mafia-type crime, exploits globalisation, the abolition of frontiers within the european union and the legislative disparities between member states to its advantage in order to obtain ever more substantial benefits while ensuring its impunity. this is a serious situation and would in itself force the eu to think carefully. it was not to facilitate organized crime that we abolished our borders. it was not for this to flourish that we created a common space of freedom and security. i am sure that the commission will take parliament's proposals in the fight against organised crime into account and will shortly be putting forward a concrete proposal to that effect.
in writing. - organized crime in the european union has been increasing, both because of the economic and financial crisis and because of the disappearance of border controls. human trafficking and exploitation, international drug and arms trafficking, money laundering and financial crimes, corruption and embezzlement of public funds are some of the activities in which mafia organizations are engaged. the report, drawn up by sonia alfano, examines this practice, which is detrimental to the interests of european citizens and institutions, and sets out the guidelines which, in the context of a better eu legislative framework, parliament believes should be followed in order to stop the internationalisation of criminal organisations of the mafia type, in particular by strengthening and improving the functioning of the european structures involved in this fight, such as undc and interpol. given that the eu must make every effort to ensure that its territory is an area of freedom, with the free movement of persons and goods, but also an area of security, i fully agree with the measures presented in this report and hope that they will be implemented by the member states as soon as possible.
in writing. - the fight against organised crime is obviously a matter of the utmost importance. this fight must be decisive against the various forms of crime, in particular money laundering. it is therefore important not to belittle or minimize (or, worse, whitewash) certain forms of crime, particularly those which develop in the economic area. the increase in crime is not dissociated from the current socioeconomic situation in the european union, from the deep crisis of capitalism and its expressions in europe, and from its policies, whether in the financial or the social sphere - with the profound disregard for social and labour rights. at the same time as we are witnessing brutal violence against the people and workers, we are witnessing almost inaction in the fight against organized crime, the promotion of easy money and illegal schemes, such as drug trafficking, arms trafficking, human trafficking, etc. the report ignores these aspects. it is therefore necessary to emphasize the need to break with this policy, which is transversal in its effects and devastating in the most diverse areas, and which contains in itself the conditions for the development of organized crime in its various forms.
in writing. - we obviously consider the fight against crime to be a matter of the utmost importance. however, this fight must be effective in the various aspects of crime, particularly money laundering, which is undoubtedly one of the most obvious ways of blurring the line between legal and illegal. we therefore warn against the whitewashing of certain forms of crime, which are infiltrating the most diverse areas, particularly the economic one. the increase in crime is not dissociated from the current socioeconomic situation of the european union and its policies, whether in the financial area or in the disregard of social and labour rights. the devaluation of the importance of work and working people, with all the civilizational setbacks we are experiencing, is one of the incentives to crime, because, at the same time as we are witnessing brutal violence against people and workers, there is almost inaction in the fight against organized crime, the promotion of easy money and illegal schemes, such as drug trafficking, arms trafficking, human trafficking, etc. we therefore stress the need to break with this policy, which is transversal in its effects and devastating in the most diverse areas, despite our vote on this report.
in writing. − this initiative report has the aim of setting out parliament’s guidelines and proposals for countering organised crime at eu level. this is, of course, a very important aim and we can only support it. in the adopted text, concrete proposals are made for action to improve the eu legislative framework (including several specific measures to address the internationalisation of mafia-type criminal organisations), and to strengthen and improve the functioning of european structures that are involved in various ways in fighting organised crime, as well as relations with other international institutions such as the united nations office on drugs and crime. although we noted that sometimes the means suggested are either not clear enough from the legal point of view or, on the contrary, too detailed for eu level and for a non-legislative instrument, we very much support the fight against organised crime, as highlighted in the report, and for that reason we supported the work of the rapporteur and voted in favour.
in writing. − the consequences of organised crime have a profound impact on the commitments made by the european union to its citizens and, for this reason, the institutions must undertake a concrete political effort in the fight against organised crime in order to achieve concrete and important results. in this context, i voted in favour of this report, which sets out in detail the policies that the european union can adopt in the main areas of action of organised crime, in particular: trafficking in and exploitation of human beings, international drug trafficking, arms trafficking, money laundering and financial crime, corruption, the interpenetration and coexistence of organised crime, politics and public administration, the misappropriation of public funds (in particular european union funds) by organised crime, eco-mafia and environmental crime, computer crime, counterfeiting of products and related trafficking, extortion and usury.
in writing. - while the area of freedom is primarily at the service of the individual, it also provides a more favourable environment for the expansion of organised crime. indeed, with the common space comes the opportunity for unprecedented mobility, reinforcing the power of these organisations. the adoption of a common policy is therefore necessary. just as this problem has only gained the dimensions now known in the single market, so too only common action will be able to deal with it. i have voted in favour of this because i understand that efforts must be made in this direction.
in writing. - organized crime in the european union has many economic and social costs in the european single market. it is therefore essential to make the european union's action in this area effective, in accordance with the strategic priorities and tasks defined in the various existing strategic documents: the stockholm programme, the internal security strategy, the european pact to combat international drug trafficking, the eu action plan on drugs for 2009-2012, the council resolution on a strengthened strategy on customs cooperation and the council conclusions on the contribution of customs authorities to the implementation of the stockholm programme in the fight against cross-border organised crime. i support the european parliament's proposal, but i share the position of the ppe group, to which i belong, that there is no need for a special committee in the european parliament with powers in this area, particularly with regard to the spread of criminal organisations.
in writing. − i support this resolution, considering that the fourth high level forum (hlf-4) on aid effectiveness should set out future commitments for more effective development aid and contribute to the creation of a new architecture of international aid by the deadline for the achievement of the millennium development goals (mdgs) in 2015 and beyond. i would point out, however, that previous high-level conferences have failed to produce the necessary political pressure or a legally binding framework, and that the implementation of the paris declaration has not led to the expected reduction in the fragmentation of aid, and that there are still too many operations which are not very transparent, for example in terms of conditionality. i also believe that all forms of financing for development, including innovative financing mechanisms such as a possible tax on financial transactions or global funds for financing health or education, should incorporate and apply the principles of the paris declaration. i would remind you that effective aid also means allowing the poor countries to mobilise internal revenue.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that europe needs leadership and strong political commitments in busan in order to move forward with the aid effectiveness agenda. the objectives of the fourth high-level forum on aid effectiveness, to be held in busan at the end of november, are to reaffirm, deepen and reframe international commitments to make aid more effective, better functioning and development-enhancing. this is the only way to achieve the millennium development goals in 2015. i stress the need for the eu to take a strong stand in busan in order to reach a global consensus for an effective and truly inclusive partnership for the development of aid effectiveness.
in writing. − the fourth high level forum on aid effectiveness should define future commitments for more effective development aid. i think it is crucial that the european union takes an ambitious stance in busan and that it seriously commits itself to the commitments on aid effectiveness. of the thirteen goals set out in the paris declaration, only one has been achieved. it is important that donor and recipient countries take immediate action to meet their commitments. i would like to stress the importance of a differentiated approach to aid effectiveness, which takes account of both the level of development of the beneficiary countries and their specific needs. to this end, the involvement of local authorities and civil society organisations is vital, as is better coordination and harmonisation of donor country actions through simplified procedures and close cooperation with private donors.
in writing. − the evaluation of the effectiveness of official aid to developing countries should be periodically re-evaluated, as the development aid landscape is constantly changing, particularly at this historic juncture, when the question of the level of budgetary effort allowable for this type of external aid is posed to so many member states, as opposed to the need for effective and absolutely necessary development aid in so many countries or areas of the world. the current economic, financial and social instability, and the millennium development goals, which call for a new approach from donor countries, add to this. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that it adds rigor to the whole aid process through the measures it proposes. i would stress the measures for better coordination between donor countries or even greater involvement in monitoring aid by the national parliaments of the recipient countries which are, in my view, essential to ensure the success of the whole process.
in writing. − the european union is the world's largest donor and this status is often brought to its attention when its institutions and member states are confronted with the failure of the development policies they have supported. indeed, it has long been recognised that it is not enough to transfer money and goods to the states that need them most, but that it is necessary to monitor how they are used, to hold the institutions and governments responsible for their application accountable, to involve the civil society that benefits from aid and to prevent the diversion of funds and products for illicit purposes. the evaluation of the effectiveness of aid to developing countries is therefore a highly topical matter which deserves to be examined in detail and in a consistent manner. i hope that the union will continue to support developing countries and that they will be able to make the best use of the aid they receive, and that civil society and the parliaments of the recipient countries will be increasingly involved in monitoring the use of aid and deciding how it is actually put at the service of the people.
in writing. - this report, by mr cristian dan preda, focuses on the fourth high level forum (hlf-4) on the effectiveness of official development assistance (oda), which will take place from 29 november to 1 december in busan, south korea. the european union, as one of the main donors of funds to developing countries, should play its part in a way that is commensurate with its responsibilities. the commission is therefore proposing the introduction of a financial transaction tax, the need to put an end to tax havens and the acceleration of the fight against tax evasion. the revision of the labour code should also be carried out, which would save eur 6 million per year. it is a report which identifies the areas where help is most needed and which has the support of a significant majority of members of parliament. the expectations for this forum are high. i therefore vote in favour of this report in the hope that the measures proposed in it will enable a new framework to be set up to improve the quality of aid and contribute to the achievement of the millennium development goals by 2015.
in writing. - this report addresses the problem of the effectiveness of development aid (da), a matter related to the principles of the paris declaration and the accra programme of action. inevitably, it is also linked to the millennium development goals, which are slow to be achieved because of the obvious contradictions between words and action at the political level. as the report itself says, aid is not enough to end poverty. ad must act consistently on the causes of this poverty, by eliminating them, and not just on the symptoms. although frankly insufficient and incomplete, the report contains positive aspects such as the need to combat tax havens and tax evasion, as well as the reference to the creation of a financial transaction tax, which could channel resources to ad. we also stress the concerns about the decline in official development assistance and the fact that an increasing share of oda is coming from the so-called emerging countries. we do not follow up other points in the report, such as the attempt to blame the governments of developing countries in particular for the reduced appropriation of ad. the democratic appropriation of the ad requires genuine, consistent and effective aid which respects the needs of the peoples, their sovereignty and legitimate choices.

in writing. − this report on the fourth high level forum on aid effectiveness presents a set of proposals for the current redefinition of the aid effectiveness programme. the european parliament must be involved in this matter and must push for measures to make the union's aid more effective. in fact, the transparency of aid is essential to safeguard both its appropriation and its effectiveness. i agree with the need to never lose sight of the objective of aid quality and the promotion of an international development-oriented agenda.
in writing. − the fourth high-level forum on aid effectiveness (fan-4) aims primarily to draw up the strategy for the remaining period until the deadline for achieving the millennium development goals. in this context, it should be noted that the european union and its member countries spend more than half of the annual amount allocated to development aid, and are therefore in the lead. the european union should take this opportunity to act, within the framework of nafta-4, in order to respect its guiding principles: the commission's proposals are based on the following principles: efficiency, seeking to find ways of optimising resources for developing countries so that, instead of creating a situation of dependence, they are equipped with instruments enabling them to act autonomously after the end of aid; the promotion of cooperation between peoples, encouraging south-south aid; and, above all, respect for the rule of law, advocating the establishment of democratic models based on human rights. this is a line of action with which i identify and which therefore deserved my vote in favour.
in writing. - article 208 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union states that the primary objective of the union's aid policy is the reduction and, in the long term, the eradication of poverty. in implementing policies which may affect developing countries, the union shall take account of the objectives of development cooperation. it should be stressed that the european union and its 27 member states are the largest contributors to official development assistance (oda) and play a key role in enhancing the effectiveness of international aid. i agree with this report because i believe that countries should strengthen international cooperation, harmonize their actions and simplify their procedures. i also believe it is important to increase financial aid and involve the private sector in aid to the poorest countries in order to build an economy that is not dependent on external aid, to ensure sustainable development and to create wealth. finally, i believe that the fourth high-level forum on aid effectiveness (fan-4) should be able to build a new architecture for international aid by the deadline set for the achievement of the millennium development goals (mdgs), namely 2015.
madam president, it is a scandal that companies are closing down and multinationals are moving away, such as arcelor and nokia. these are the consequences of the capitalist policies of free competition, deregulation of the labour market, flexibility and flexicurity. it is these policies which allow large economic groups, after receiving substantial community support, to close down and send thousands of workers to unemployment, even with profits as high as arcelor mittal's. these are scandals that are multiplying in different member states, including portugal. it is time for the european commission to present initiatives to prevent this behaviour by multinationals and to defend european industry. it is time to intervene with public policies, including the nationalisation of sectors that are basic to production and employment. it is time to return to regulation, to recognition of the rights of workers. it is time for political power to take charge of the economy and not to let the economic and financial groups guide community policies.
the rapporteur. - i would like to thank my fellow shadow rapporteurs, with whom i have had a fruitful collaboration, and i would also like to thank the rapporteurs for the opinions of the four committees involved. their opinions are a valuable contribution to this report. we received 400 amendments and drew up 47 commitments, all of which were adopted. this shows the importance and interest of the subject of new skills and jobs. it is, after all, a question of preparing europe's human resources by anticipating the needs of the labour market in the next decade. the key strategy for the preparation of the report was to reformulate the common ideas to avoid repetition and to ensure the coherence of the report. i think that objective has been achieved. we all know that the crisis that is currently affecting us has highlighted the weaknesses of the european economic and social model and has reversed much of the progress made in the past. since the first effects of the crisis began to be felt on labour markets in 2008, europe has already lost more than 5 million jobs. today, nearly 23 million people are unemployed. youth unemployment is even more frightening: the youth unemployment rate is close to 21% and is more than double the general unemployment rate. in addition, unemployment rates vary across member states according to skill levels. this means that people with higher qualifications find jobs more easily. we also know that in the near future the needs for skills, competences and qualifications will increase across all types and levels of occupation. in this context, europe faces four challenges: first, job creation; second, the need to engage and remain competitive; third, the sustainability of social security systems; and finally, the difficulty of finding people with the right skills to fill job vacancies. this report thus has a twofold objective: first, to underline the need for rapid action to close the skills gap in europe; second, to better anticipate the skills needs of the labour market. to this end, several measures stand out: first, to ensure the availability of a skilled workforce, basic skills need to be improved, as well as skills in science, innovation, information and communication technologies and foreign languages. as i have already mentioned, skills needs should be identified early, over a horizon of at least 10 years. we now know the potential of a new sustainable economy, the green economy, and the need to invest in green skills. then there is the need to increase participation in lifelong learning, vocational retraining and the reduction of school drop-out rates. another important issue is the mutual recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications and the urgency of moving forward with this recognition. fourthly, we call attention to the link between educational establishments and the needs of the labour market. the traineeships must be of a quality and supervised by tutors so that they can lead to employment and to put an end to any abuse of the trainee status. particular emphasis is also placed on the role of the social partners and social dialogue. the report also proposes measures to promote demand and job creation. we have the future ahead of us and we have to create jobs. smes play a decisive role in this respect. the single market must also be strengthened to facilitate the free movement of workers and hence the need to coordinate social security systems so that workers can have their acquired rights guaranteed, in particular the portability of pensions. finally, the question of labour market flexibility: to improve the functioning of the labour market, flexicurity rules should be adapted to the socioeconomic contexts of each member state.
i would like to begin by trying to bring to this debate all the outrage and indignation that is being felt in many of our countries. it is the revolt of workers in precarious and low-paid work, of millions of women and young people who are being denied a job with rights and a living wage, and whose future is mortgaged to increasingly neo-liberal policies, which only seek higher earnings, higher profits, for the same people. unfortunately, this report does not go into the depths of these problems, it does not analyse the causes of the high unemployment, the real reasons for the loss of more than 3.5 million jobs over the last two years and the forecast loss of more than 2.5 million jobs in the coming years. it is simply blaming the crisis, without paying attention to the fact that the policies of the stability pact, free competition, liberalization and privatization, and flexible working conditions have contributed to creating and aggravating the crisis. so, despite one or another positive point, most of them are mere palliatives, simple aspirins for the cancer of the anti-labor and anti-social capitalist policies that are spreading in the european union. today there are thousands of highly qualified people who are unemployed. the most urgent thing is therefore to put an end to the closure of a series of companies, the relocation of multinationals, the destruction of industrial and agricultural sectors, the attack on public services and smes. the most urgent thing is therefore to put an end to the so-called austerity policies, the programmes of aggression against the workers and the peoples, as in greece and portugal. without that, we won't have a schedule for new skills and new jobs.

the rapporteur. - madam president, i would first like to thank all the members who have spoken in this lively debate. all colleagues have made very useful contributions and have contributed to a very constructive discussion on an agenda which is ambitious at a time when we are living through a serious crisis. in fact, this debate is taking place on the eve of a european council which will show whether or not there is political will to overcome the difficulties we are experiencing, whether there is political will to deepen our economic coordination and whether there is really a harmonized and united will to achieve the ambition on this agenda, namely: to have new jobs in the next decade, new jobs which will give young people who are currently unemployed and those who are in training hope on the labour market, hope on an inclusive labour market, which will give them an answer to their ambition of dignifying themselves through work, and also give them the opportunity to be in a permanent dynamism to keep up with the challenges of a globalised economy and with a dynamic that has no parallel in recent generations. so our ambition is really to have job creation, to have economic growth, to not only respond to those who are unemployed as a result of the crisis, but to those who are entering the labour market, and also to respond to the great challenges that are there with the green economy, with services in the health sector, with services in the transport sector, in the housing sector, which require from all of us a different vision, a smart vision and an inclusive vision of the labour market. thank you all so much.

in writing. - it is a source of pride that this month the first two european satellites have been launched into orbit, which will form part of what will be the galileo constellation by the end of the decade, with a total of 30 satellites at more than 23 000 km above the earth. the galileo satellites, which are entirely civilian in origin, will provide an alternative global positioning system which will enable europe to become independent of the american global positioning system (gps). i therefore support the conclusion of an agreement with the united states of america for the promotion, supply and use of both european satellite navigation systems.
in writing. - this recommendation, drawn up by herbert reul, concerns the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement for the promotion, supply and use of galileo and gps satellite navigation systems and related applications between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and the united states of america, of the other part. since the launch of gps in 2000, this sector has grown exponentially and is expected to represent a €230 billion market by 2025. the eu, a community attentive to this new technology, has developed a geostationary navigation system called egnos (european geostationary navigation overlay service), the precursor to the galileo system, which is expected to be operational in 2013 with a level of accuracy ten times that of gps. in view of the recommendation of the committee on industry, research and energy, i am voting in favour of the council's request for parliament to approve the agreement for the promotion, provision and use of galileo and gps satellite navigation systems and related applications between the european community and its member states, of the one part, and the united states of america, of the other part.
in writing. − this recommendation gives the green light to the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement for the promotion, provision and use of galileo and gps satellite navigation systems and related applications between the european community and its member states and the united states of america. many services, including more efficient road transport management, better search and rescue services, safer banking transactions and a more reliable supply of electricity, rely heavily on satellite navigation technologies. there are studies indicating that there are significant economic benefits for all parties involved. for these reasons i voted in favour of this recommendation.

in writing. - the european galileo project has a 100% european basis and is therefore seen by many as another reference element of european identity. the launch of the first two satellites on the 21st is just the beginning of a constellation of 30 satellites. this intelligent satellite navigation system will develop and improve numerous applications and services, including an intelligent transport system, search and rescue services, the security of financial transactions, and the supply of electricity. the independence of europe from the american gps was one of the initial objectives of the galileo project. but the work on interoperability and compatibility between the two has made it possible to sign this cooperation agreement. after four years of negotiations, users of both galileo and gps systems will be able to use both navigation systems with the same equipment. the importance of this project, still in its embryonic stage, shows that galileo has a market potential of 3 billion users and that its success will benefit the european market, in particular smes, and that it is estimated that it will generate, over 20 years, eur 90 billion and numerous public and social benefits.

in writing. - the process of community integration has left the tax systems of the member states almost entirely on the sidelines, where a strict notion of sovereignty - in this case, fiscal sovereignty - still prevails. however, this attitude of inertia has led to a veritable lex shopping (as the ecj, moreover, considers to be permissible for the formation of commercial companies), creating additional problems for the states. in the case of the tax system applicable to parent companies and affiliated companies, for example, the principle of double taxation often leads to the non-taxation of capital gains in the state in which the affiliated company is incorporated, to the benefit of the state of the parent company. this is problematic, since the location of the head office is chosen for reasons of tax competitiveness. the data is problematic: the eu corporate tax rate fell from 44% in 1980 to 35% in 1995. at present, it is 23.2%. it is therefore necessary to adopt a common policy to deal with this specific problem, where intervention by any one state alone would be bound to have little practical effect. for these reasons, i voted in favour.

allocated to this purpose under the european refugee fund. under current rules, member states are entitled to claim eur 4 000 for each resettled person belonging to one of the categories defined in the relevant decision. the main objective of the proposed amendments to the decision establishing the european refugee fund for the period 2008-2013 is to enable the establishment of common annual union priorities in the field of resettlement. this would mean that resettlement actions at union level would be better coordinated and concentrated. it is also important that the annual priorities would include certain specific categories which are partially listed in the current decision on the european refugee fund. for example, one of the categories of persons eligible for financial support from the european fund is those from a country or region covered by a regional protection programme. the regional protection programme was established in april 2010. it shall cover north african displaced persons eligible for funding under the current refugee fund. the same applies to particularly vulnerable groups, such as children and women at risk, and to people requiring special medical care. 7 member states: belgium, denmark, finland, ireland, the netherlands, portugal and sweden offered the office of the united nations high commissioner for refugees 408 places to resettle people from the north africa region. despite the fact that participation in resettlement activities is voluntary, the european parliament has suggested that further financial incentives be adopted to involve more member states by increasing the amounts of funding available. the amount requested is eur 6 000 per resettled person for a member state benefiting from the fund for the first time and eur 5 000 per resettled person for a member state which has benefited from the fund in the past. the council could support the above assumptions. however, the council cannot support the suggestion of the european parliament to apply the procedure for delegated acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu for the adoption of the annual union priorities on resettlement. the council's position is based on the explanations provided by the european commission concerning the timeframe imposed by the programming cycle linked to the operation of the general programme 'solidarity and management of migration flows'. the council supports the commission's view that the establishment of annual priorities in the field of resettlement is purely implementing in nature, as it concerns the application of the specific principles laid down in the decision on a specific situation. the council is seeking a solution to this issue, also taking into account the alternative approach presented in may this year, which would avoid the need for delegated acts. however, the polish presidency regrets that a mutually acceptable solution to this particular issue has not yet been found and that, as a result, the decision in question has not yet been adopted in its entirety. given that resettlement activities can be financed from the current refugee fund and given that there is only one year cycle left under the current programme, the polish presidency considers that it would be better to continue the discussion on the establishment of a joint union resettlement programme in the context of the next programming period.

in writing. − this report, by ms iliana malinova iotova, concerns the ombudsman's annual report for the year 2010. this is the first report drawn up by the european ombudsman, mr nikiforos diamandouros, after he took up his duties before the court of justice of the european union on 25 october 2010, following his re-election. the institution, chaired by nikiforos diamandouros, celebrated its 15th anniversary in september 2010 and, during its 15 years of existence, completed more than 3 800 inquiries and handled some 36 000 complaints relating to maladministration in the activities of the eu institutions, i.e. when a public body does not act in accordance with a rule or principle to which it is bound. one of the main complaints is the difficulty that citizens have in accessing eu documents. although the existence of confidential documentation is understood, the institutions cannot make life difficult for the citizen in this field. i welcome the adoption of this report, i hope that the ombudsman will be able to achieve the objectives set out in his new strategy for the 2009-2014 mandate and i hope that european citizens will be better informed about his role.
in writing. − the ombudsman's annual report enables me to check the work done in implementing his tasks and objectives. given that the ombudsman has the right to examine the substance of the commission's actions and findings when investigating complaints of infringements, it is important to check what is happening with the complaints lodged and to follow the progress of the case. for example, it can be checked whether the ombudsman's views are reasonable, well reasoned and fully and clearly explained to the complainants. it states that the ombudsman was able to help complainants in 70% of all cases handled in 2010 by opening an inquiry himself, transferring the complaint to a competent body at eu or national level, or giving advice to the complainant on where to go. the 2010 annual report pays particular attention to the new strategy that the ombudsman and his staff have formulated for his 2009-2014 mandate. the objectives are, inter alia, to hear stakeholders by obtaining information from complainants, to broaden and deepen contacts with the eu institutions, to identify best practices for achieving faster results by reducing the time needed to close investigations, and to develop simplified procedures to promote the swift resolution of complaints.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the annual report of the european ombudsman for 2010. the annual report for 2010 submitted to the european parliament gives special attention to the new strategy that the ombudsman and his staff have formulated for his 2009-2014 mandate. the objectives are not only to hear from stakeholders, to obtain information from complainants, to broaden and deepen contacts with the eu institutions and civil society, and to identify best practices, but also to achieve results more quickly by reducing the time needed to close investigations and to develop simplified procedures to promote the rapid resolution of complaints. i believe that these are worthy and necessary objectives for an institution which is often the last resort of the citizen to see his problem with the administration resolved.
in writing. - the ombudsman, whose statute is already enshrined in article 228 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, is a guarantee for community citizens in their relations with the european institutions (cf. article 43 tfeu). it is a public office with two central functions: on the one hand, it is a means of resolving disputes outside the formal control bodies, such as the courts. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the time when the ombudsman presents his annual report is always appropriate in this respect to withdraw references for the future. community policy should therefore continue to support its work by seeking to disseminate information on its activities and functions, since in countries with little tradition of having an ombudsman, such as portugal, citizens are often unaware of this instrument of appeal. it is also important to establish a climate of cooperation between the community institutions in order to maximise the contribution of the ombudsman. i have voted in favour of these points, as they are now being considered by the european parliament.
in writing. − the eu charter of fundamental rights recognises a set of personal, civic, political, economic and social rights of citizens and residents, incorporating them into community law. while article 41 sets out how citizens' affairs are to be dealt with, article 43 stresses the right to petition the ombudsman in cases of maladministration by various european institutions. i agree with this report because it shows that the eu has made an effort to reduce the average time to complete investigations, to continue to insist on the fundamental right of access to documents and to promote citizens' trust in the public service and the eu institutions. i would also like to congratulate the ombudsman on his strategy of focusing on the ongoing dialogue with complainants, civil society and other stakeholders, and on his efforts to identify best practices adopted by his colleagues in the european network of ombudsmen and to make procedures in the eu fairer and, above all, more transparent.

in writing. − the sexual abuse and sexual exploitation of children, including child pornography, constitute serious violations of fundamental rights, in particular the right of the child to protection and care necessary for his or her well-being, as set out in the united nations convention on the rights of the child and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. this report provides for stricter criminal sanctions against those who sexually abuse children or who access child pornography on the internet. it also obliges member states to remove websites containing child pornography. if this is not possible, they should block access to those pages. it criminalises the solicitation of children via the internet for sexual purposes and child sex tourism, whether the offence is committed on the territory of a member state or by a european citizen outside europe. it also provides that persons convicted of sexual offences may be temporarily or permanently prevented from engaging in any activities, at least professional, involving direct and regular contact with children. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - the sexual abuse and exploitation of children are horrendous crimes which must be prevented and combated. this report proposes to move forward with some instruments to do so, some of them sound and positive. however, alongside these, provisions are being introduced which give rise to our greatest reservations and concerns, such as those allowing access to certain internet sites and blocking them. we certainly agree that the circulation of child abuse and child pornography on the internet must be severely combated and stopped, but this can only be done effectively by removing the source of such material. the provisions in this report do not provide a complete and sufficient guarantee that blocking websites - the possibility of which is used for the first time in eu legislation, thus creating a precedent - will not pave the way for forms of censorship on the internet and in other areas. it should also be noted that the issue of sexual exploitation of minors cannot be dissociated from the social conditions in which these minors are found, as it is known that children from poor backgrounds and families face a higher risk of being the target of this type of crime. these causes must also be severely combated.

in writing. − the directive currently under discussion on the minimum rules on the conditions for third-country nationals or stateless persons to be eligible for international protection and the content of the protection granted is a recast of directive 2004/83/ec. it should be noted, however, that the degree of involvement of the european parliament in both cases varies. while its powers were initially purely advisory, the treaty of lisbon now allows it to act in co-decision on these matters. in a matter of the highest political importance, the need to ensure greater harmonisation of the action of the various member states in granting international protection is emphasised. it is also justified to adopt measures to ensure the integration of beneficiaries of protection into the community area, providing conditions for their access to the labour market from the outset. the role of the states as the primary actors in the granting of aid is also highlighted. i have seen these points reflected in the proposal which has been tabled and have therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. − the recast directive aims to establish a uniform basis for the treatment of cases of third-country nationals or stateless persons in need of protection as refugees or persons eligible for subsidiary protection, as regards the conditions to be fulfilled in order to qualify for international protection. this amendment is part of the eu's legislative work towards a common european asylum policy. the aim of the recast proposal is to adopt a common definition of the conditions for international protection and to ensure minimum levels of benefits common to the member states, in particular in terms of social security, access to employment and health, integration measures and residence permits. in addition, grounds relating to harassment have been broadened to include gender and gender identity and the care of unaccompanied minors. the ep also called for the commission to be given the right to adopt a new directive on the protection of workers from the risks arising from exposure to asbestos. solidarity, a core value of the eu, must not be reproduced only within the borders of the member states. i therefore consider the adoption of this report to be an important step towards creating a genuine european area of asylum and protection.

in writing. − this agreement should replace the 2008 interim agreement, applied only in 17 member states, which established a european legal framework on the conditions for the transfer of passenger name record (pnr) data by airlines to australian customs services. i support this agreement as it relates to the global approach to the transfer of eu pnr data to third countries. the criteria set out by the ep were satisfactory: the purpose is clearly and strictly limited, the transfer is carried out only through the push data export method, the possibility of using sensitive data is explicitly excluded, citizens are guaranteed the possibility of bringing administrative and judicial proceedings in australia, as well as guarantees in terms of access, rectification, deletion and security of their data. i agree with the rapporteur that we could have gone further and that there are still some concerns, but the great objective of ensuring that any transfer of data from the eu can only be done in full compliance with european data protection standards has been achieved! this agreement seems to be a success and i hope it will serve as an inspiration for the next agreement to be concluded with the united states.

in writing. − issues concerning the processing and transfer of personal data are always particularly complex, given the multiple human rights and security issues they raise. the attacks of 11 september 2001 have highlighted the weaknesses of airport security systems and have led to an understanding shared by the majority of democratic states and governments that there are indeed limitations to the right to privacy and the inviolability of personal data and that these are justified only in situations where the safety and life of others may be at stake. criticism of this majority view is well known from some quarters who seek to assert the primacy of individual privacy over collective security, but nevertheless their arguments do not seem to be of a persuasive nature to those who board airplanes and who, for the most part, do not mind sharing their personal data knowing that they are thereby limiting the capacity for action and impunity of terrorists. the agreement between the european union and australia seeks to strike a reasonable balance between the rights and interests at stake.

in writing. − the eu-australia agreement on the transfer of pnr (passenger name record data) data does not meet the guarantees requested by the ep in its previous resolutions. the commission has neither presented factual evidence supporting the claim that storage and processing of pnr for law enforcement purposes is necessary and proportionate, nor has it seriously explored less-intrusive alternatives. in particular, the agreement foresees an unjustified storage period of five and a half years, does not contain adequate safeguards to prevent discriminatory profiling and raises serious concerns regarding compatibility of the agreement with the charter of fundamental rights, as well as with the case law of the echr. furthermore, the commission has ignored parliament’s request to ask the eu agency for fundamental rights for an opinion on the fundamental rights dimension of the agreement. we stress our commitment to cooperating with australia and other third countries, but believe the blanket retention and processing of the pnr data of all passengers is incompatible with our vision of an open society. for this reason we voted against the report and supported the gue/ngl resolution seeking an opinion from the european court of justice on the legality of the agreement.

in writing. - australian legislation requires airlines to provide the local customs service with passenger identification data before arrival. this practice threatens the guarantees of data protection and has therefore led to the intervention of the community institutions. in this context, it seems that a negotiation between the two spaces cannot be avoided: in fact, in the absence of agreement, australian law tends to remain applicable. it is therefore desirable to find a balanced solution, assuming that any access to passenger data should be considered exceptional, and that its use and storage should be guided by the principles of necessity, appropriateness and proportionality in the strict sense. in this context, the european parliament must take a leading position in defending the fundamental rights of community citizens. as i see these concerns reflected in the recommendation on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and australia on the processing and transfer of passenger name record data, i voted in favour of approving the agreement.
in writing. − the australian customs service wanted to assess the risks of european passengers of international air carriers, based on their passenger identification register (pnr) data, and ran into a problem with european data protection legislation. at the council meeting of 30 june 2008, member states established a cooperation agreement with australia for the transfer of data by air carriers to the australian customs services. however, with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the ordinary legislative procedure, which requires the consent of the european parliament, has begun to apply to the negotiation of international agreements. in an increasingly globalised world, where the safety of citizens must be constantly ensured by the competent authorities, and given the good application of most of the criteria defined, i agree with this agreement between the eu and australia. i would also like to stress that the eu cannot prohibit third countries from collecting, storing and using pnr data, but can only define the conditions for the transfer of such data and whether it complies with its data protection rules.

in writing. - i support this motion for a resolution, considering that antimicrobial resistance is an important and largely unresolved issue which has become a public health threat in europe and the rest of the world, resulting in longer and more complicated treatments, a decrease in quality of life, a higher risk of death (annually 25 000 patients in the eu die from infections caused by resistant micro-organisms), increased healthcare costs and productivity losses of at least eur 1.5 billion per year. it is no accident that the world health organization has considered the theme of this year's world health day. i note with concern that antimicrobial resistance is a growing threat to public health in europe and the rest of the world, despite the measures taken at european and international level, and therefore call for an intensification of the fight against antimicrobial resistance in medicines for human use.
in writing. − antimicrobial resistance refers to the inability of certain antimicrobial agents (antibiotics, for example) to act effectively on organisms (bacteria, viruses and other micro-organisms) that were previously sensitive to them, because they have developed resistance. antimicrobial resistance has become a public health threat in europe (and the rest of the world), as it results in longer and more complicated treatments and increases the risk of failure to respond, with potentially fatal consequences (e.g. 25 000 people die every year in the eu from infections caused by resistant micro-organisms). this means that there is an urgent need for global action to ensure that antimicrobials are prescribed and used more prudently, that they are used only when they are really needed, and that the development and research of antimicrobials, together with the pharmaceutical industry, is encouraged as a way of treating patients infected with resistant micro-organisms.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on antimicrobial resistance, which threatens public health in europe and the rest of the world, because i believe that the commission should present without delay a legislative framework to combat antimicrobial resistance. it is necessary to use antimicrobials prudently, both in humans and animals, ensuring that they are used only when they are actually needed, and to investigate and develop new alternatives and antimicrobials.
in writing. - following questions for oral answer under rule 115 (5), a motion for a european parliament resolution on the problem of the threat to public health posed by antimicrobial resistance was tabled. most european citizens are unaware of the harmful consequences for public health of the indiscriminate use of antibiotics, both in humans and in animals. there are a number of scientific studies which warn of the public health risk of certain bacterial strains in food and in food-producing animals. the european institutions have drawn the attention of all those responsible to the prudent use of antimicrobial agents in human medicine, as they can destroy or inhibit the growth of bacteria, viruses and other microorganisms. given the interest and relevance of this subject antimicrobial resistance is a largely unresolved issue i welcome the presentation of this motion for a resolution which i hope will contribute to improving the quality of life of european citizens.
in writing. - the widespread use of antibiotics and the increase in resistance to antimicrobial agents are certainly a cause for concern. this is an important public health problem which this resolution warns of, and we have supported it, in that it calls for greater caution and vigilance and goes further with the need for more research to develop new alternatives and new antimicrobial agents. but more than developing new agents, it is important to understand and tackle the causes of the development of these resistances, which are also addressed in the resolution, and to address the widespread lack of information on this subject. we believe that it is important to inform and raise awareness among the public about the effects of antibiotics and their use, as stated in the resolution, but that effective investment is also needed in prevention and primary health care, which is now under severe attack and in an accelerated process of devaluation, with policies that have led to the divestment and the discharge of responsibility from the state by public health services. a fundamental change in agricultural and livestock production methods is also needed, by combating intensive production with a high incorporation of agrochemicals, including antimicrobials, which is responsible for the increase in the problems associated with antibiotic resistance. we regret the adoption of the amendments proposed by the ppe which weakened the resolution in this area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the threat to public health posed by antimicrobial resistance, recognising that this is a serious public health problem that needs to be addressed. however, i regret that the position taken by the rapporteur in paragraph 28 is excessive in its wording (too comprehensive and taxing), failing to make any distinction between the antibiotics currently used in the sector, failing to present alternatives to phasing out, and calling for the outright elimination of prophylactic antibiotics in livestock without regard to their negative impacts on european livestock farming. i voted against this paragraph.
in writing. − antimicrobial agents are designed to kill or prevent the growth of bacteria, viruses or other micro-organisms. in the process of the evolution of science, they have been translated into one of the great achievements for the reduction of pathologies and infections that, until the emergence of these techniques, had deadly effects. today, however, the problem of antimicrobial resistance arises, arising, among other reasons, from the overuse or misuse of medicines, both by humans and by animals. in contrast, the pharmaceutical industry, in opposition to a continuing activity of developing antibiotics, has developed a small number of antimicrobials. a holistic approach is therefore required, involving not only patient awareness policies but also the development of new techniques to combat the risks to public health and the adoption of an active surveillance policy by supervisory activities. for these reasons, which are set out in the motion for a resolution, i voted in favour.
in writing. − microbial resistance is a growing threat to public health in europe and the rest of the world, despite measures taken at european and international level. the fight against resistance to microbial agents in medicinal products for human use must therefore be intensified. microbial agents can destroy or inhibit the growth of bacteria, viruses and other micro-organisms and therefore play a considerable role in improving public health by helping to reduce the number of deaths caused by previously incurable or fatal diseases and infections. however, their use has led to the development of resistance, known as antimicrobial resistance, in certain micro-organisms previously sensitive to these microbial agents. the european commission should submit a proposal for a legislative framework in this area, promoting responsible use initiatives and supporting their dissemination and information. only by prudent use of microbial agents, increased control and surveillance of antimicrobial resistance and by encouraging research and development of alternatives can an approach to tackling this problem be promoted.

mr president, the general and continuing weakening of bee colonies is a worrying problem for which it has been difficult to find an effective and consistent solution. if we consider that this decline affects not only domestic bees but also the wild populations of various pollinator species, we can easily see the seriousness of its consequences for agriculture and the environment. in general terms, this problem cannot be dissociated from the current agricultural models, intensive agriculture, with the prevalence of monoculture, with a high and unsustainable incorporation of agrochemicals, pesticides, with the spread of genetically modified organisms, without due observance of the precautionary principle. without prejudice to measures which can and should be taken in the short term, such as banning certain types of products and providing adequate scientific and technical support to farmers, what is needed are substantive measures. measures that involve a change in existing production models and the policies that support them. the cap reform would therefore be an opportune moment to begin this necessary fundamental change.
mr president, while congratulating the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs on the good work they have done, i would like to stress one important point which, despite my efforts, remains missing. the need to guard against the harmful effects of using subspecies outside their natural range and to prevent the continuation of this practice, which began some 50 years ago and which has placed bees in conditions to which they were not adapted. in these cases, selection is based on certain characteristics, such as honey production, to the detriment of other aspects essential to their survival, such as defensive behaviour and swarming. there has also been the introduction of parasites and exotic diseases which sometimes led to the extinction of local subspecies. it is therefore important to prevent this practice, which is harmful to all, from continuing through proper training of beekeepers and appropriate regulation.
member of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank ms westphal for this report. this report represents a precious contribution for the european commission. as the report acknowledges, there are great differences in the demographic trends in europe which some regions are going to experience. therefore, a ‘one-size-fits-all’ approach will not work. cohesion policy already supports demographic change through actions such as active labour market policies, investment in entrepreneurship, modernisation of social and health sector infrastructures, kindergartens and housing, as well as support for the economic and social integration of immigrants and minorities. regional responses to demographic change should address the challenges through integrated approaches. the cohesion policy legislative package for the period 2014-2020, adopted by the commission on 6 october, will offer a framework to fund a wide variety of investments to tackle demographic change. in this regard, the commission has adopted a number of common provisions for the three funds included in the package: the european regional development fund, the european social fund, and the cohesion fund. the provisions related to the local development approach, integrated territorial investment and sustainable urban development, will allow further flexibility and additional possibilities for funding to address demographic change at regional and local level. active and healthy aging is critical for a sustainable european society. in order to face the demographic trend to a further aging population, the eu has to reduce the differences in terms of health and must contribute to improving access to health services. the commission is now drawing up a common strategic framework that will cover the three funds mentioned, plus the european agricultural fund for rural development and the european fisheries fund. the framework will translate the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy into key actions that will be supported by the different funds. it will address the multi-dimensional aspects of demographic change and will determine how the different funds can better collaborate in this field.

mr president, commissioner, this report by mr peter simon is a very balanced report. it uses economic services of general interest, within the framework of the common values of the union, as promoters of rights and of economic, social and territorial cohesion. there is certainly a legislative framework, but the framework is still very much in legal uncertainty and the principle of subsidiarity must be upheld. the report's many positive points are the clarification of the distinction between economic and non-economic activities, the reference to local and regional sgeis which do not affect competition in the internal market, the reference to project bonds, the de minimis rules for situations where sgeis operate on a limited local scale, and the status of sgei providers, which is sufficiently broad to include associations, foundations, community and voluntary organisations, ngos and social enterprises. finally, it is assumed that the definition of quality and efficiency of the sgeis should be linked to the principle of subsidiarity.

in writing. - this report is based on the proposal for a council decision on the accession of the european union to the athens convention relating to the carriage of passengers and their luggage by sea, 1974. the convention focuses on the safety of passenger ships and the rights of passengers. however, it was considered that the convention did not sufficiently regulate a number of important issues, such as the nature and extent of the liability of carriers and minimum insurance requirements. part of these issues were addressed through a protocol negotiated under the auspices of the international maritime organisation (imo) and adopted on 1 november 2002, amending the athens convention. however, the accession of the european union and its member states was not consensual and after 4 years of negotiations, a supplementary regulation on the liability of carriers of passengers by sea in the event of accidents with a view to the conclusion of the protocol and aiming to incorporate into community law most of the remaining substantive provisions was adopted in 2009 and is expected to apply until 2013. these steps have made accession to the convention possible. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
