in writing. the kingdom of spain, on behalf of the autonomous community of the canary islands, has requested the temporary suspension of the autonomous common customs tariff duties on imports of a number of industrial products into the canary islands in order to strengthen the competitiveness of local economic operators and thus ensure more stable employment in these outermost regions of the union. to ensure that imported products, whether raw materials, parts, components or capital goods, do not distort competition, these products will be subject to end-use controls ensuring their use by local enterprises on the islands. the capital goods will have to be used by local companies on the islands for a minimum of two years before they can be freely sold to other companies located elsewhere in the union territory. in addition, the raw materials, parts and components will have to be used for processing and industrial maintenance in the canary islands in order to benefit from the duty suspension. the effects of the proposed suspension will be limited to the regions concerned and will help to help smes and local farmers to invest and create jobs in this outermost region of the union in the current context of the economic crisis. for these reasons i voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. − the outermost regions of the european union face permanent constraints related to their remoteness, insularity, difficult terrain and climate, which result in a structural limitation to their economic and social situation, in accordance with article 349 tfeu. this specific status allows the treaty provisions to be adapted and, consequently, measures to be adopted at european level which take particular account of the needs of these regions. it is in this context that the report voted on today in the european parliament is aimed at temporarily suspending the autonomous common customs tariff duties on imports of a number of industrial products into the canary islands. such measures have also been adopted in other octs, such as madeira and the azores, and are intended to help strengthen the competitiveness of economic operators in these regions.

in writing. - i share the concerns of those who have serious doubts about nuclear energy: about its cost, about the fate of its radioactive waste and about the safety of its facilities (whether due to accidents of their own, to terrorist attacks or other criminal acts or to natural disasters such as those that occurred in fukushima, japan). i have an ambivalent view of mr březina's reports. i recognize that some of the lines of research may even be positive in that they focus on strengthening safety and protecting the population, but others are clearly intended to continue the efforts of an industry which is in several european states in the process of phasing out. that is why i decided to abstain in the final vote on both the reports on the implementation of the framework programme of the european atomic energy community for nuclear research and training (direct and indirect actions) and on the report on the proposal on the rules for the participation of undertakings, research centres and universities in indirect actions under this programme and for the dissemination of research results.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the european atomic energy community framework programme for nuclear research and training (indirect actions) because it is part of a legislative package which aims to continue support for research and development activities under the 7th euratom framework programme (2007-2011) by aligning it with the current eu multiannual financial framework until 2013.
in writing. - coordination in the field of atomic energy is one of the origins of the current process of european integration. from the very beginning of this process, it has been necessary to make a joint effort to seek to research and develop technology which would enable europe to keep pace with the development and use of this energy. nuclear energy is currently part of the energy mix of some member states of the european union, and the provision of adequate means for the ecsc to pursue its objectives could enable it to contribute to ensuring safer and cleaner nuclear energy for citizens, while maintaining its use. this resolution is one of the measures designed to achieve this, where appropriate by implementing the framework programme through indirect actions.
in writing. - this report, by jan březina, deals with the proposal for a council decision on the specific programme for the implementation of the framework programme of the european atomic energy community for nuclear research and training activities (2012-2013), to be implemented through indirect actions by the joint research centre. despite the disasters at chernobyl and, more recently, at fukushima, the nuclear question remains very topical, not only because of the need to accompany the dismantling of obsolete nuclear power stations and ensure the safety of waste management, but also, and fundamentally, because of a scientific and technological modernization issue, both in terms of energy production and medicine. over the past few years the european union has been making a decisive contribution to the advancement of research in this area by supporting various programmes and in particular the iter project, which is more than 50% funded by the eu. despite the economic and financial crisis, i believe that the eu must remain at the forefront of research in this area, so as not to lose its leadership and to call into question all the know-how acquired over the years. i therefore vote in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. - independently of the debate on the nuclear option for energy supply, which must be pursued, taking into account the limits, potential and dangers of this option, we consider that training and research in this area, which has many other applications besides the above, are necessary. the training of technicians and researchers specialised in this field and the existence of a body of research, monitoring and control infrastructures is a necessity for any country, whether or not nuclear is an energy option. the same applies to portugal, where the present government has plans to close down the nuclear technological institute, which have been rightly contested by technicians and researchers. as regards the content of the report, we are very concerned about some of its assumptions, particularly those which end up promoting nuclear energy. the way in which it does so is not in keeping with the debate which needs to be held in view of the well-known risks and consequences for people and the environment, as well as the recent accidents of alarming proportions.
in writing. − in times of crisis we need to ensure that the implementation of the framework programmes of the various eu bodies is well implemented. in the specific case of the european atomic energy community it is important that the funds are well used to safeguard potential safety risks as well as in research towards the discovery of cleaner atomic energy with less environmental risks.

in writing. − the euratom framework programme (euratom fp7) 2007-2011 consists of two specific programmes (one for indirect actions and the other for direct actions) and ends at the end of this year. the european commission has put forward a proposal dealing with indirect actions such as research into fusion and nuclear fission energy and radiation protection, with the intention of extending the programme specifically designed for this purpose for a further two years. i agree with the commission's present initiative because i believe it is important for the european union to take measures to continue the activities being developed and to start implementing the european strategic plan for energy technologies approved by the council in march 2008. finally, i believe that the new fp for 2012-13 should be simpler and less bureaucratic, with increased transparency and legal certainty in line with the european parliament's suggestions for the implementation of the research fps.
in writing. − i approve this report, noting the achievements of the s&d group. it is always worth stressing the importance of a europe which defends the welfare state in order to protect the weakest and which should not, by amending labour laws, jeopardise the rights of workers, particularly in insolvency proceedings.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on insolvency proceedings in the context of eu company law, as it aims to develop a useful discussion on the harmonisation of insolvency proceedings in the different eu countries. this harmonization, carried out at different levels, would be positive for europe, as it would make an important contribution to the strengthening of the single market and european integration.
in writing. - the recommendation follows a study carried out by this parliament in an attempt to identify specific areas of harmonisation between the various national insolvency laws. there is certainly a clear interest in exploiting the conclusions presented there, as well as in the proposals subsequently drawn up by the rapporteur. however, i would like to stress that although such harmonization will resolve possible conflicts in international insolvency law, it is not sufficient on its own. it therefore lacks a stronger community approach and coordination and an agreement between member states to enable more effective mechanisms for coordination of procedures.
in writing. - the current financial and economic crisis is forcing society at large to reflect on all the administrative and legal procedures involved in economic activity. one of the problems affecting modern societies is the functioning of the business fabric, which, when it grows, generates wealth and creates employment, and, when it falls, throws millions of workers into unemployment with the social consequences that we all know. one of the causes of unemployment is the failure of companies, often due to insolvency. at present, each member state has its own specific legislation on this matter, and therefore, in the spirit of the functioning of the single market, it is essential to harmonise insolvency proceedings at european union level. the recommendations in this report by klaus-heiner lehne, which will serve as guidelines for the commission, are based on a four-pronged approach: harmonisation (where possible), revision of the insolvency regulations (where possible improvement), improvement of trustee cooperation and cooperation in general, and the creation of an eu-wide insolvency register. because i believe that this report will help to improve the functioning of eu societies, i voted in favour.
in writing. the rapporteur makes some positive proposals. among these, we highlight the attention paid to workers, as evidenced by relevant statements such as the following: although labour law is the responsibility of the member states, it may be affected by insolvency law; in a context of increasing globalisation and, admittedly, economic crisis the question of insolvency must be examined from the perspective of labour law, as workers' rights should not be undermined in the event of insolvency by divergent definitions of employment and employed person in the member states; - considers it necessary to give greater priority to workers' claims over those of other creditors; the report is not without contradictions, however, notably the attempt to harmonize the conditions under which insolvency proceedings may be opened. moreover, the interests of small and mediumsized enterprises are not always safeguarded. while there are some positive points in opening up the processes, it will always be the most powerful who will benefit the most.
in writing. - there are several contradictions in this report, such as the attempt to harmonize the conditions under which insolvency proceedings may be opened. the rapporteur points out that there are positive aspects to the opening of the procedures, but the interests of smes will not always be safeguarded. in general, it's always the most powerful who will benefit from the process. there are positive aspects to this report, however. the attention paid to the workers is outstanding. this is the case, for example, with the following statements: it stresses that although labour law is the responsibility of the member states, it can be affected by insolvency law and that, in a context of increasing globalisation and, admittedly, of economic crisis , the issue of insolvency must be examined from the perspective of labour law, as workers' rights should not be undermined in the event of insolvency by divergences in the member states' definitions of employment and employed person. it considers it necessary to give greater priority to workers' claims over those of other creditors.
in writing. - the legislation on insolvency proceedings needs to be improved. in a climate of crisis, the number of insolvencies is increasing and it is necessary to speed up the procedures. on the other hand, there were gaps in the old legislation which need to be filled, in particular with regard to the insolvency of groups of companies. the insolvency regulation applies only to individual companies and there is no legislation at eu level applicable to the insolvency of groups of companies, despite the fact that groups are a very common form of business model in economic life. this omission has important negative consequences. it is necessary to be aware of the wide variety of different group structures and relationships between companies belonging to the same group and, consequently, also of the fact that the same solution cannot be applied to all types of groups, at least if we take into account the current situation of insolvency laws in force in the union. ideally, the insolvency of groups of companies should be administered by a single court which would apply its own insolvency law. this solution facilitates coordination and information transfer, saves costs, maximises the value of assets and facilitates recovery.
in writing. − on 23 march 2011, the committee on legal affairs held a seminar on the subject 'harmonisation of insolvency proceedings at eu level'. the aim was to identify areas in national insolvency legislation which could be harmonised. in preparation for the hearing, the committee on legal affairs commissioned a study on 'harmonisation of insolvency law at eu level'. the recommendations made in this report take into account the ideas put forward by the experts in that study and during the hearing and specified in detail in the documentation. this report thus contains recommendations to the commission on insolvency proceedings in the context of eu company law and sets out the actions to be taken in future legislative proceedings. as this is a process with constructive measures in an area where harmonization could bring more value, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the insolvency regime remains one of the areas of law in which the laws of the member states differ most. this is, however, an extremely important matter in which closer approximation of the laws of the various states is warranted: the way in which the insolvency proceedings are structured ultimately determines the satisfaction of the company's claims; on the other hand, it is also the last chance for a company to recover economically. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − when the insolvency regulation was adopted at european level in 2000, some important issues were not properly integrated and now need to be given special attention. the disparity between national legal systems on insolvency proceedings calls for harmonisation to allow for better restructuring of the various european companies, which should be reflected in the forthcoming legislative proposals. among the various items covered are harmonisation of the conditions for opening insolvency proceedings, a review of certain definitions in the regulation and its scope, improved promotion of cooperation between winding-up bodies and administrative bodies and the creation of a european-wide case register.
in writing. - i welcome this report, drawing attention to the fact that demographic change is a factor that must be taken into account in policy-making, with particular emphasis on the outermost regions and the most fragile regions supported by the convergence objective.
in writing. - demographic change is a reality in the european union. europe's population is ageing, with the oldest population and the slowest population growth rate in the world. demographic change is therefore considered the most important trend of the 21st century and will radically change the political, social and economic situation in europe. the report, which i supported, identifies the following priorities: better adaptation of the structural funds to the challenges of demographic change; avoiding the exodus of people and the social exclusion of the elderly; the need to combat unemployment among women and youth; and taking advantage of the knowledge and experience of the elderly. in order to achieve an adequate response to demographic change in europe, it is important that these changes can be measured in appropriate statistical terms and that there is better coordination between the responsible bodies at all levels and the exchange of best practice.
in writing. − europe's populations are ageing, life expectancy is increasing and demographic change is increasingly becoming a reality with social and economic impacts, both on social security and on migratory pressure. it will be important to address the challenges associated with the very different developments at regional level in order to counteract the displaced flow of young people to the cities at the expense of rural areas. otherwise, there will be an alarming 10% population decline in some 20 regions of the eu. demographic change has undoubtedly been affecting the elderly, children and families. therefore, countermeasures aimed at restructuring urban planning, particularly with regard to higher quality public transport, the granting of erdf funds with the intention of granting loans at lower interest rates so that beneficiaries can adapt houses according to the needs of the elderly, to an extended coverage of medical care and to a better use of the knowledge and experience of the elderly in counselling are indispensable to prevent population exodus and an exclusion of the elderly.
in writing. - the demographic structure of europe is changing radically. it's a fact. alongside an ageing population and lower birth rates worldwide, demographic changes in several regions of the european union bring new challenges which must be objectively considered in future eu cohesion policy. in some regions there is depopulation, in others considerable population inflows. i therefore consider it absolutely essential that an appropriate infrastructure policy be designed and implemented, one which is adapted to the needs of each area. the structural and cohesion funds play a central role here. it is therefore necessary to develop specific policies for rural areas suffering from depopulation on the one hand and specific policies for urban areas receiving significant population inflows on the other. the report gives good examples of what should be done. i voted in favour of it, and i believe that it provides relevant, objective, clear and easily understandable input to the discussion which has recently begun on the future of eu regional policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that gender equality policies can make an important contribution to tackling demographic change. in addition to measures to increase female employability, special attention should be given to incentives for employers to promote work-life balance.
in writing. - demographic change is evident in the european union, which is increasingly ageing and lacking the capacity to replace itself. this is a matter of concern to experts and policy-makers who cannot ignore the harmful consequences of the loss of vitality of their societies and who must instead look for ways of alleviating the problems arising from this and of adapting the social state to the new reality. while population ageing is not an evil in itself, but rather a reflection of how average life expectancy has increased, the low birth rate should merit our more vigorous attention in supporting the reconciliation of personal and family life and the adoption of family-friendly public policies.
in writing. - this report, by kerstin westphal, deals with a subject of major importance for the future of europe. we cannot, in fact, be indifferent to the demographic changes that have occurred, essentially, in the last three decades. the sharp fall in the birth rate, the increase in life expectancy, the depopulation of rural areas and migratory flows are some of the phenomena on which the european union must reflect and which it must address in the context of a future cohesion policy. since demographic change is 'the most important trend of the 21st century, which will radically change the political, social, societal and economic situation in europe', it is essential that the structural funds be directed towards mitigating the negative effects of this change: investments in rural areas to prevent exodus, urban infrastructure for reception, social support for the elderly, children and families, an increase in the female employment rate and a new policy for the integration of skilled immigrant workers. i therefore welcome the rapporteur's view that demographic change is not a problem but an opportunity to deal with the ageing of the european population, and i welcome the adoption of this report which takes a proactive view of demographic developments.
in writing. - demographic changes in europe are the expression, on the one hand, of civilizational advances such as the increase in average life expectancy, but also of worrying aspects such as the low birth rate, particularly worrying in some countries, such as portugal. the rapporteur, in view of these changes, intends to examine and explore the consequences of demographic change from the point of view of opportunities. as we said during the debate, we are concerned that this debate is often used, more or less covertly, to pave the way for the imposition of measures which call into question the fundamental rights and achievements of workers and peoples, such as social security systems; to impose the raising of the retirement age, the reduction of the value of pensions, the overcrowding and degradation of social infrastructures, the loss of rights to health care. all this has happened with the implementation of the so-called austerity measures. ensuring the existence and universality of quality public services, diversifying and strengthening them in the light of the new needs arising from demographic change, safeguarding their public character and changing the policies that have led to low birth rates are some of the conditions for demographic change not to represent a retreat from civilisation or to jeopardise economic and social cohesion.
in writing. - scientific and technical developments and the achievements of civilization in the last century have made possible a breakthrough which presents us with a whole new set of possibilities and challenges. but in the institutions of the european union this progress has been used as a pretext for imposing setbacks, that is, for calling into question the rights and achievements of workers and peoples, such as public and universal social security systems. many of the challenges have not been adequately addressed, whether in the context of cohesion policies, regional development, the fight against desertification or the strengthening and diversification of public services. this report addresses the important question of the use of the structural funds, namely the erdf and the european social fund, to address some of these challenges, particularly in the countries and regions most affected by ageing and depopulation. the increase in the rate of absorption of these community funds is all the more important as we know that many of these countries and regions are faced with unacceptable so-called austerity programmes, which squeeze investment levels to the point of poverty, preventing the full use of these funds by those who need them most and at the time when they are most needed.
in writing. − demographic change is a reality in the eu and how to manage this situation is one of the key tasks of the future. the european populations are ageing. europe has the oldest population and the lowest population growth rate in the world. in most member states, birth rates are below the replacement level of 2.1 children per woman (and will continue to decline in some cases) while life expectancy is increasing. demographic change will create new challenges in many regions of the eu. in this context, demographic trends will have to be analysed predominantly at the level of regions where very different trends are visible.
in writing. - i share the rapporteur's general conviction that difficulties are also opportunities for new forms of development. however, this is not always the case and demographic issues can be dramatic in a future without opportunities. i am referring specifically to the process of desertification of some of the azores islands. in particular, on the islands of graciosa, flores and s. jorge, the population is decreasing and with it economic, social, cultural and recreational activity and all hope of personal and collective development. in relation to these borderline situations, specific and effective policies and adequate funding are urgently needed, but are slow to emerge.

in writing. - i approve this report, stating that the socialists have fought and are fighting hard to put an end to speculation with an impact on the interest rates of sovereign debts in europe. the end of short selling and certain aspects of default swaps as policies in the field of european economic governance contribute to a more transparent global financial system.
in writing. − since the financial crisis, several member states have taken measures to suspend or prohibit short selling. however, the powers of national regulators to restrict or prohibit such sales still vary from one member state to another. this new regulation will create a harmonised framework for coordinated action at european level. this regulation prohibits or restricts such transactions and makes it more difficult to speculate on a country's sovereign debt. the new legislation aims to increase transparency and enable regulators to more easily detect risks in the debt market. the regulation will also make it impossible to buy credit default swaps (cds) for the sole purpose of speculating on a country's default, due to the negative impacts on the stability of sovereign debt markets that these instruments can cause. the european securities and markets authority (esma) will be at the heart of the monitoring and supervisory activities. the regulation also introduces enhanced information and notification requirements for national and european regulators to enable them to monitor markets and more easily detect risk accumulation. i therefore support this report.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. much of this speculation has been fuelled by the sale and resale of credit default swaps (cds), the price of which serves as an indicator of the level of risk of the respective sovereign debt. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules are applied in a uniform manner. these measures are designed to prevent anyone across the eu who does not hold sovereign debt from any eu country from buying these risk management products (rms) to speculate against their debt. finally, these proposals will also make it possible to achieve greater transparency in the short selling market (sale of securities which one does not own), with a view to better regulating an area which is also a source of much speculation.
in writing. - this report represents the culmination of an intensive process of negotiations between the two co-legislators and results, in my view, in a balanced position as regards the limit on sovereign debt speculation and the future of short selling. i would point out that the european union is thus the first region in the world to restrict the activity of short selling and default swaps and i welcome the option of limiting its activity as opposed to simply excluding it. i would also like to highlight the enhanced role given to the european securities and markets authority, which will allow for greater monitoring and supervision of the rules listed here and which accompanies the position of this parliament with regard to the european supervisory authorities. finally, i welcome the work carried out by the whole team of rapporteurs, which will bring about greater harmonization at european level of this type of activity.
in writing. - the current economic and financial crisis - as most experts say - has revealed the economic, social and political costs of a self-regulated financial system. the attention of experts is now focused on the search for a methodology that can identify the behaviour of the financial system that can provoke new crises. this report, by pascal canfin, deals with the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on short selling and certain aspects of default swaps, which were banned in some member states at the height of the financial crisis. bad debt can't be classified as good and no one can sell what they don't have. for the safety and smooth functioning of financial systems within the eu, it is essential that legislation harmonises the potential risks arising from short selling and default swaps. i welcome the adoption of this report which will bring more powers to european regulators, more transparency to financial markets and more security to all investors, who will now see reduced risks of losing their investments.
in writing. − as the report shows, at the height of the financial crisis in september 2008, the competent authorities in several eu member states and other countries, such as the us and japan, took emergency measures to restrict or prohibit short selling of some or all securities, with concerns that, in a period of considerable financial instability, short selling could exacerbate the vicious cycle of falling share prices, particularly of shares of financial institutions, in a way that could ultimately threaten their viability and create systemic risks. but within the european union, member states have taken differentiated measures in view of the absence of common regulatory measures. only now, two years later, are some measures being taken, although very insufficient, to harmonize the rules on short selling and certain aspects of credit default swaps (cds), requiring notification in duly typified cases, which may help to reduce some speculation, especially with sovereign debt. unfortunately, they will not come into force until 2012 and even after that date, the exceptions provided for still allow this practice in some cases.

in writing. statistics are an indispensable method and means of evaluation in virtually all areas of policy action and are extremely useful both in predicting certain events and in providing goods or services. these are also important for agricultural activity, since they enable us to know more precisely both the production and the production potential of certain areas and the whole framework of the respective market. updating, simplifying and optimising these statistics increases the possibilities of their use and takes some of the burden off them, allowing them to be carried out without undue constraints for the respondents.
in writing. statistics is an essential technique for the substantiation of most scientific work. if we have the best information on a given subject, we can make a more correct and informed decision. bureaucracy is a necessary evil which must be reduced to a minimum without affecting transparency or jeopardizing the achievement of the objectives set. in this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european statistics on permanent crops, mariya nedelcheva points out the advantages of this proposal, particularly in terms of reducing the administrative burden on respondents and simplifying procedures. i welcome the adoption of this report, which i voted in favour of, because i believe that the procedures for obtaining statistics are usually too bureaucratic and uniform for large and small farms, which often makes it difficult for the latter to operate.
in writing. − the aim of this report is to update the regulatory framework for european statistics on permanent crops, adapting them to the current needs of users and the market. the report improves on the european commission's initial proposal in some respects, notably by removing the possibility for the commission to amend the list of permanent crops (by delegated acts) without prior approval by parliament. the proposal for simplification is important, by reducing the administrative burden on respondents, which should initially involve smaller samples. the committee also expressed concern that the amendments would not impose an additional burden on the national competent authorities. it is not clear to us, however, that the changes now proposed to statistics will produce the necessary answers to the specific difficulties of small farmers and smallholders created by the current system of data collection. this is of course more relevant for countries such as portugal, where despite the strong concentration of ownership over the last few years (favoured by the cap), small and medium-sized ownership is still very prevalent, accounting for about four fifths of all farms. in view of the doubts and concerns raised, we supported the improvements proposed by parliament but did not support the final legislative proposal.
in writing. − the aim of this report is to update the regulatory framework for european statistics on permanent crops, adapting them to the current needs of users and the market. the report improves on the european commission's position in some respects, for example by removing the possibility for the commission to amend the list of permanent crops (by delegated acts) without parliament's approval. the proposal for simplification is also important, by reducing the administrative burden on respondents by introducing thresholds at farm and territorial level, which should initially involve smaller samples. it is not clear, however, that these statistics will produce the necessary answers to the concerns of small and mediumsized farmers, since they will be the technical support for decision-making in the fields of production and the european market. in countries with weaker economies and greater dependence on agri-food, such as portugal, the course of the last decades has been the decline of the agricultural sector, especially family farming, with the successive neoliberal reforms of the common agricultural policy. for all these reasons we supported the improvements proposed by the majority of the european parliament, but we did not support the final legislative proposal.
in writing. − the aim of this regulation is to update the existing regulatory framework for european statistics on permanent crops, adapting it to the current needs of users and the market. the aim of simplification should be emphasised and the efforts made by the commission to reduce the administrative burden on respondents should be commended. the aim is to use statistical data on permanent crops as a reliable basis for appropriate decision-making in the fields of production and the european market. it is however possible and desirable that the administrative burden can be reduced by modifying the data accuracy requirements to exclude all small holdings (less than 0,2 hectares)
in writing. − the aim of this report is to update the existing regulatory framework for european statistics on permanent crops, adapting it to the current needs of users and the market. the aim of simplification should be emphasised and the efforts made by the commission to reduce the administrative burden on respondents should be commended. the aim is to use statistical data on permanent crops as a reliable basis for appropriate decision-making in the fields of production and the european market. i agree with the rapporteur that there is a need to strike a better balance between the needs of users and the administrative burden of producing data. the rapporteur's proposal to reduce the administrative burden by amending the data accuracy requirements, excluding all small holdings (less than 0.2 hectares) from the scope and deleting the nuts 3 breakdown of some data on vineyards for purposes other than table grape production should be considered. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - the effectiveness of the application of community law depends to a large extent on its ability to adapt to the challenges that arise. to this end, it is necessary to have recourse periodically to procedures for reviewing the texts of the rules in order to determine in concrete terms which points can be improved. it is in this context that the commission's recent proposal to reduce the administrative burden on respondents for the purposes of european statistics on permanent crops is to be found. it is an initiative which deserves applause, since it contributes to the protection of citizens' confidence and to the simplicity of community legislation. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. − in may 2010, the european commission drew up a proposal for a regulation on european statistics on permanent crops, in which it advocates the need to update, simplify and optimise the existing regulatory framework for european statistics on permanent crops by replacing the two existing legal acts with a single one. i agree with the amendments to this regulation, as it is necessary to encourage greater cooperation between the authorities involved in the production and publication of european statistics, to consult a wide range of decision-makers, including experts with extensive knowledge of the subject, and to take into account best practices adopted at international level. i also consider it important that this regulation establishes a common framework for the systematic production of european statistics on permanent crops, facilitating greater integration and comparison at european level.

in writing. - i share the concerns of those who have serious doubts about nuclear energy: about its cost, about the fate of its radioactive waste and about the safety of its facilities (whether due to accidents of their own, to terrorist attacks or other criminal acts or to natural disasters such as those that occurred in fukushima, japan). i therefore have an ambivalent view of mr březina's reports. i recognize that some of the lines of research may even be positive in that they focus on strengthening safety and protecting the population, but others are clearly intended to continue the efforts of an industry which is in several european states in the process of phasing out. that is why i decided to abstain in the final vote on both the reports on the implementation of the framework programme of the european atomic energy community for nuclear research and training (direct and indirect actions) and on the report on the proposal on the rules for the participation of undertakings, research centres and universities in indirect actions under this programme and for the dissemination of research results.

in writing. - i approve this report, which is unanimous in most of the proposals. i note that, in line with the view of my group, the effective implementation of this directive would be greatly facilitated by the introduction of a european-wide professional portfolio.
in writing. − professional mobility is an essential element for economic development, sustainable economic recovery and the relaunch of the internal market. while citizens expect recognition of their professional qualifications to be easy and automatic, they are often disappointed. this report, which i supported, argues that the future revision of the vocational qualifications directive should be based on the following objectives: to simplify the procedures for the recognition of qualifications; to modernise the existing legislative framework; to strengthen trust and cooperation between member states. the european commission should also develop guidelines for the time limit for obtaining a decision from the competent authority on the recognition of qualifications. citizens should also be given the possibility to apply electronically for access to a regulated profession, thus reducing waiting times. finally, it should be stressed that the question of mobility should not be dissociated from the question of the transferability of social security rights and pension rights.
in writing. − there are still many barriers, directly or indirectly, which continue to hinder the free movement of people within the eu and the ability of citizens to fully benefit from the benefits of the single market, including the right to work or provide services in another member state. the right to recognition of academic qualifications and professional qualifications can only truly exist when national rules which tend to make it disproportionately difficult to exercise the right to skilled employment are eliminated. the evolution of markets itself calls for greater transparency, simplification and flexibility of the rules on the recognition of professional qualifications, where cross-border mobility should contribute to a more efficient functioning of labour markets and foster economic growth and competitiveness in the eu. i therefore support the need to modernise and improve this directive in order to ensure a clear legal framework, by strengthening the system of recognition of professional qualifications, by establishing measures for automatic recognition, by removing prejudices and formal obstacles to such recognition. while ensuring that the transposition and implementation of this directive is finally completed in all member states. i also welcome the use of more efficient and appropriate technologies to facilitate and speed up the recognition process.
in writing. - in the current economic and financial context, skilled managers often seek and exploit economic dynamics within the european area itself to their advantage. the free movement of persons, the freedom to provide services and the freedom of establishment are some of the basic pillars of the process of european integration. these are distinct principles and have been the subject of judgments by the ecj, as identified in the report. i therefore believe that the community legal framework governing internal labour migration should be improved, optimized, simplified and made clearer in order to fully respect the rights of european citizens and promote a more competitive internal market, as the rapporteur has advocated. the simplification of the process of recognition of qualifications, the full integration of professionals and the introduction of a professional portfolio for some professions to strengthen confidence in the system are procedures listed in the report and which i believe the union should apply. i am voting in favour of this report because it represents a further step forward in the process of european construction which is planned and under way and which we hope to see completed one day!
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider the free movement of skilled workers to be one of the fundamental benefits of european cooperation and a competitive internal market. cross-border mobility will contribute to more efficient functioning of labour markets and will favour economic growth and the eu's own competitiveness.
in writing. − in the current economic climate, the simplification and flexibility of all rules allowing greater mobility of professionals, especially in terms of the recognition of their qualifications, is an essential requirement for a sustainable economic recovery. in addition, the free movement of professionals is only truly possible if there are simple rules for the recognition of qualifications which do not act as a barrier to mobility. this is why we should welcome this report, which aims, among other things, to reduce the length of the procedures for the recognition of qualifications through the use of information technology and to update uniformly and regularly, and in line with scientific and technical developments, the minimum training conditions for professionals in the various sectors of activity.
in writing. - bureaucracy is a problem which has led the european parliament on several occasions to reflect and take measures to deal with it. the aim of a free and functioning single market often comes up against administrative procedures that are incomprehensible to many european citizens. this report, by emma mcclarkin, looks at the implementation of the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications (doctors, nurses, dentists, pharmacists, etc.) by many european citizens who would like to practise their profession in any member state of the european union but who are currently faced with the complexity and time-consuming nature of recognition procedures. this is therefore a priority issue, but it must take account of certain essential aspects, such as the language of the host state, the responsibility of the professional and the safety of citizens by means of a proactive alert in the event of a non-qualified professional. i welcome the adoption of this report which will help to improve the mobility within the eu of various professionals, which will not only help to reduce unemployment rates within the community but also fill many shortages of skilled human resources in some of the member states.
in writing. - the report has some positive aspects, although it is not without some contradictions. the current economic and social context, characterized by a deep crisis in several countries, such as portugal, is a factor of pressure on many workers, especially the youngest, to emigrate in search of work wherever it exists. mobility thus arises not as a desired option, determined by a choice between different possible alternatives, but as an exit towards which one is pushed by the absence of an alternative in the country of origin. it is of course important for those who want to work in a country other than their own to want their professional qualifications to be recognised. but there are issues that need to be taken into account, whether in relation to health professions, the historical and cultural component of the country concerned or the language itself. it is therefore necessary that the recognition of professional qualifications should not affect the rights of consumers and users of services. but above all, it is necessary to encourage and support the creation of jobs with rights in all member states so that people can actually work where they want, and are not forced to leave their country just because they do not have a job.
in writing. − the free movement of an increasing number of highly qualified workers is one of the fundamental benefits of european cooperation. i believe that all indirect obstacles to citizens' mobility in europe must be removed, without compromising labour rights and protection, and by striking a balance between mobility and the quality of vocational qualifications. the mobility of european workers has been particularly marked in the area of health and, given its immediate impact on public health, needs clear and transparent rules to ensure mobility and safety. this directive is in that direction, and i have therefore voted in favour. although it is not within the scope of this directive, i believe that the free movement of citizens within the union should be further developed, in particular by giving equal rights to citizens of all countries of the european union.
in writing. − the implementation of this directive is very important to facilitate doctors, engineers, dentists and all other professions the opportunity to work in another eu country. we have thus increased the flexibility of the labour market. this can only happen through the mutual recognition of professional qualifications and their rapid implementation, with due regard to the reliability and safety of their performance. accelerating the procedures for the recognition of professional qualifications would also help young europeans to believe that a professional experience is possible in any member state. in this context of crisis, all european professionals are looking forward to increased mobility to pursue their professions. one way of simplifying the overly bureaucratic procedures is the introduction of a voluntary occupational passport to be inserted immediately into the existing information system in the internal market, capable of connecting to public authorities throughout the eu.
in writing. − this report on the implementation of the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications calls on the commission not to fragment the process of modernising automatic recognition as proposed in the green paper and to ensure that any substantial changes to the directive are subject to parliament's scrutiny. i would stress in this report the call for greater mobility of graduates and for compliance with the judgment in morgenbesser, which held that member states should encourage paid supervised traineeships for graduates from other member states when they also offer the same possibility to their own nationals. professional experience acquired during supervised traineeships shall also be recognised in the home member state of the holder of the licence.
in writing. the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications has proved to be an important instrument for enhancing the mobility of workers between the different member states and ensuring that supply and demand match in the european labour market. in the context of the evaluation of the results achieved in the meantime, the need is emphasized not to create additional difficulties for the mobility of workers, without prejudice to the recognition that measures should be taken to prevent mobility from jeopardizing the safety and health of consumers. this will be the case, for example, of health professionals who, having been prevented from exercising their activity in one member state, move to another country, thus avoiding being held liable. in general, the integration process must continue, not only by promoting the mobility of workers but also by creating coordinated mechanisms to combat fraud. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. − mobility within the eu's borders is one of the four freedoms of the eu and a sine qua non for the completion of the single market. the recognition of qualifications, which is necessary to boost the mobility of highly qualified people and workers, should be a process that is not bureaucratic. this directive distinguishes between the freedom to provide services and the freedom of establishment, in accordance with the criteria established by the court of justice: duration, frequency, regularity and continuity of the provision of services. the automatic recognition process has been hugely successful, whereas the recognition process under the general system, based on professional experience, is excessively time-consuming and complex and therefore incompatible with the free movement of citizens. the creation of a proactive alert system is also essential to prevent professionals who are suspended or prevented from exercising their profession from doing so in another member state. the eu's competitiveness is based on its know-how, so the process of simplifying the recognition of professional qualifications and diplomas is urgently needed to tackle the obstacles to economic growth in the european area. the creation of an information portal will inform european citizens of their rights.

in writing. − the inconsistency in vat rules applicable to products sold in physical cultural content in electronic form has long been a matter of concern to the eu. this new strategy is welcome and in line with the evolution of european consumers, who are increasingly buying cultural content (music, newspapers, magazines, books, etc.) via the internet. given that member states may apply reduced vat to cultural goods by physical means in order to promote access to these products, it does not seem to me right that the same products, because they are sold online, should be treated differently. we are therefore talking about an aspect of the vat directive which is completely obsolete in the face of new consumer trends. it is therefore important that this point be revised so that there is no different vat just because the same products are sold through different distribution channels. this development, together with the copyright reform, will facilitate the free circulation of audiovisual content online, thus contributing to the creation of a true digital internal market.
