in writing. - i am voting in favour of this report because it sets out balanced measures to better control online gambling. the most important thing in this area is to punish and detect illegal operators, and in this respect it is crucial to keep up to date on a subject like this, which is constantly expanding.
in writing. − there is a significant supply and demand for online gambling in the eu, and the economic importance of this sector is growing. online gambling is the fastest growing segment of the gambling market, accounting for around 10% of the overall annual revenues of this market. the challenges posed by the coexistence of different regulatory models have led to the development of important so-called illegal online grey markets in all member states. this market should be open and sufficient incentives should be created for firms to offer a legal offer, the best model being licensing, provided it is based on the principle of non-discriminatory competition. an open and regulated online gambling market presupposes an independent and strong national regulatory body. given the cross-border nature of the internet, strong cooperation between national regulatory authorities is indispensable and institutionalised cooperation is necessary, based on the internal market information system. equally important is the establishment of minimum rules for the protection of minors, the fight against gambling addiction and the fight against money laundering and other forms of gambling-related crime. i therefore support this report.
in writing. − with the increase in internet use, the increasing prevalence of betting on online gaming services and the fragmentation (or lack thereof) of legislation at eu level, action on this activity at community level is necessary to control a fast-growing market with about 85% of its activity unregulated. the internet is by its very nature a platform for cross-border connectivity. given the nature of the phenomenon, it is necessary to take regulatory measures to control this activity and to make it profitable in the context of the european internal market. in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, which has already been confirmed by a decision of the ecj, gambling has been excluded from the services directive, so that member states can continue to regulate their markets, provided that such regulations are consistent with the objectives pursued, for example, in combating gambling addiction. i am voting in favour of this own-initiative report because i believe that there is a need to set up an institutionalized cooperation network, coordinated by the commission and based on the internal market information system, in order to share information in a rapid, efficient and effective way in the european area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that member states should continue to decide on the regulatory systems they wish to apply in their respective territories in line with the case law of the cjeu, which is based on the principle of subsidiarity and takes account of public policy requirements and different national cultures and traditions. i believe, however, that the eu has an important role to play in this area, in particular by strengthening cooperation between the regulatory authorities of the member states, where the fight against illegal gambling on the internet is of paramount importance.
in writing. − the online gambling market is growing steadily, representing today some 10% of all gambling in europe and a turnover of over eur 10 billion. however, this is a market which remains largely unregulated, with all the dangers this poses to consumers. at present, of the 14 823 online gambling sites in europe, more than 85% operate without any licence. this is therefore an area which lacks attention and self-regulation. however, in line with what is advocated by the vast majority of states, the competences in the field of gambling should remain with the member states, and the eu may establish guidelines and directives in compliance with the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. the report by jürgen creutzmann deals with online gambling in the european internal market. the widespread availability of the internet has brought new problems for governments and their controllers. one of the fastest growing markets on the internet or similar distribution channels (mobile phones or interactive television platforms) is the online gambling market, which currently represents around 10% of all gambling in europe. if there are member states where these games are properly controlled, as in france, there are others where there is no regulation or control whatsoever, which, in addition to representing a significant loss of revenue, allows indiscriminate access to these platforms, in particular by minors who end up becoming addicted. because the internet is a cross-border medium, legislative harmonisation is urgently needed not only for the sake of fairness (unfair competition against licensed online operators by illegal operators), but also to control the black market and prevent the tax evasion of millions of euros that could, and should, be spent on public works or social programmes. i therefore voted in favour and hope that the member states will quickly implement the measures now adopted.
in writing. - the development of common community rules on this subject of online games is very problematic, given their specific nature and the social risks involved. it is important to take into account the cultural aspects and traditions which differentiate the member states in this field. in some of them, public entities control this sector of games of chance and luck, with their revenues channelled to social intervention, important in supporting the most deprived populations. this is the case in portugal. these specificities should be recognised and maintained, ensuring that this area is always a matter for member states to decide, taking into account the principle of subsidiarity and sovereignty. we are also concerned about the already serious problem of gambling addiction, which could worsen if access to gambling is made easier, particularly for young people. even with the care that is mentioned in the report, there is no guarantee that access to drugs will not become easier and that the problems of addiction will not multiply, especially among young people.
in writing. - the development of community positions on this issue of online games is very problematic, given their specific nature and the social risks involved. of course, because it can serve to increase the already serious problem of gambling addiction by making it easier to access, especially for young people. even with the care that is mentioned in the report, there is no guarantee that access to it will not become easier and that the problems of addiction will not multiply, especially among young people. in particular, account must also be taken of the different cultures and traditions of the member states, particularly those where there are public entities that control this sector of games of chance, earmarking their revenues for the fundamental social intervention to support the most deprived populations, as in the case of portugal. this must be maintained and protected, ensuring that this area is always a matter for the member states to decide, taking into account the principle of subsidiarity and sovereignty.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it aims to achieve two fundamental objectives when it comes to gambling: the protection of minors and the prevention of addiction. the report calls for the regulation of online gambling to be ensured through the issuing of gambling licences, which also allows the fight against illegal gambling. more than enough reasons to vote for it.
in writing. - the online gambling market is growing steadily. according to current figures, around 10% of all gambling in europe takes place on the internet or through similar distribution channels such as mobile phones or interactive television platforms, with a growing trend and a market volume of over eur 10 billion. the face-to-face and online gambling markets are characterised by a wide range of products: on the one hand, classic lottery and lottery games, but also sports betting, poker, bingo and horse and greyhound racing betting, as well as the mutual betting process. the internet is naturally a cross-border medium. so online gambling does not stop at borders. the current fragmentation of the european market in this area is becoming more and more apparent, as supply is constantly increasing and the number of players is increasing. in several member states there are total bans or bans subject to authorisation, but others have a completely open and liberalised market.
in writing. - this report on online gambling in the internal market comes at a time when the online gambling market is booming. according to current figures, around 10% of all gambling in europe takes place on the internet or through similar distribution channels, with an increasing trend and a market volume of over eur 10 billion. in view of the many cases of sports betting fraud which have called into question the integrity of sport, it is in the direct interest of all stakeholders, namely sports associations, fans, gambling operators and players, that the integrity of sport is ensured and betting fraud is prevented. i voted in favour of the concerns of the sector in portugal, defending the rapporteur's initial proposals which better defended the fight against illegal gambling and the dangers it poses. the surgical amendments proposed further reduce consumer protection, make the world of financial transactions more opaque and prevent effective combating of crime and fraud (specifically money laundering), so i voted against these amendments.
in writing. - the online gambling market has experienced strong growth over the last decade. it is estimated that it already represents 10% of the market. however, the ease of access by consumers, regardless of their age and where they access, leads to an increase in situations of gambling addiction on the one hand and of difficulty for states to control the exercise of these activities on the other. this justifies a joint eu approach guided by the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. - this own-initiative report is the european parliament's position on the european commission's green paper on online gambling in the european internal market. the development of the internet and the increase in the supply of online gambling services require particular attention, which the commission is trying to promote in its proposal by means of a number of issues: better definition and organisation of these services, consumer protection, prevention of fraud and money laundering and the guarantee of secure online payment systems. however, according to the position of the court of justice of the eu, the organisation of online games is a competence of the member states, and there should, however, be strong cooperation between the various national authorities due to the cross-border nature of these games. it should also be noted, as a regulatory principle, that online gambling operators may only provide services or apply for licences in member states if they do not act unlawfully in another member state.
in writing. - i approve this report. it is important to stimulate and develop this important sector, which is the source of income for some 600 000 european citizens. i note that as an economic and social activity it plays a key role in the sustainable development of rural areas, generates employment and provides an important service to the ecosystem through pollination, which contributes to the improvement of biodiversity by maintaining the genetic diversity of plants.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on bee health and challenges for the beekeeping sector, for it contains proposals to increase the funding available for the beekeeping sector, support research and development of new veterinary medicines specifically for bee diseases and promote the enforcement of legislation on pesticides. it should be underlined that beekeeping is a crucial sector for society, given its contribution to biodiversity, the sustainability of agriculture and food security.
in writing. − beekeeping is a very old form of food gathering by humans and has a very long tradition on the european continent. the need to protect this sector and to develop studies to ensure the good health of bees, which are facing increasing threats, is clear. despite the fact that this sector is most closely linked to honey production, the impact of bee action on nature goes far beyond honey production, with many plant species dependent on bee pollination. bees are therefore an essential element for the preservation of ecosystems as we know them and should deserve particular attention from veterinary authorities and be considered in the context of european agricultural policy.
in writing. − most eu citizens are unaware of the role bees play in preserving ecosystems and, consequently, the survival of the human species. einstein said that if there were no bees, life on the planet would end in four years. this report, by mr csaba sándor tabajdi, focuses on the problems facing the beekeeping sector, particularly as regards bee health, and the challenges facing the sector. as well as providing an income for over 600 000 eu citizens, beekeeping, an integral part of european agriculture, not only contributes to the preservation of biodiversity but is also vital to agricultural activity due to pollination. unfortunately, this is a poor sector because of the lack of support from the pharmaceutical industry. on the other hand, the lobby of plant protection products is against the removal of active substances harmful to bees in these products. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report and hope that these measures will soon be adopted by all the member states and implemented by farmers and, in particular, beekeepers.
in writing. the report addresses a problem whose persistence, without a consistent solution to stop it being found to date, is a matter of serious concern: the general and continuing weakening of bee colonies and the decline of natural pollinator populations. while we are certain that some of the specific proposals in the report may be important, especially in the short term, we do not think that the approach taken and the philosophy behind it are the most correct. in particular, the report does not touch on a fundamental issue which is inseparable from this problem, namely the need to change existing production models and the policies - such as the cap - which support them. that is why we supported the alternative resolution, which unfortunately was not adopted. the resolution makes a strong criticism of intensive farming models based on a high incorporation of pesticides and proposes alternative sustainable production methods that respect and promote biodiversity, with concrete proposals to achieve them. it is not, however, without contradictions, particularly with regard to gmos and the manifest reversal of the precautionary principle, since the moratorium on cultivation should be prior to the studies and not subsequent, as is wrongly advocated.
in writing. − this report calls for increased support for research and development of veterinary medicines to combat the current pathogens affecting bees in the eu, especially the varroa destructor mite. but the report does come up against some contradictions. the commission should also be able to take account of the fact that the commission has already adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of animals used for scientific purposes. but the report also stresses the need to provide incentives to the pharmaceutical industry for the development of new medicines to combat bee diseases. however, we agree to insist on more financial resources for beekeeping, by strengthening support for the beekeeping sector under the cap after 2013, and by ensuring the continuation and strengthening of existing support programmes. it is also good to insist on the creation of a safety net or a common insurance system for beekeeping in order to mitigate the impact of crisis situations on beekeepers or to support training programmes for beekeepers on disease prevention and control.
in writing. - 84% of plant species and 76% of food production in europe depend on bee pollination. the report recognises that pesticides and genetically modified organisms are adversely affecting these populations. monoculture is responsible for the disappearance of the honeybees. however, it calls for more control and studies of the effects of pesticides and monoculture, but maintains the paradigm of industrial intensive agriculture. it merely calls for training on the use of plant protection products beneficial to bees. the gmo case is more serious. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services by road. the report calls for incentives for the pharmaceutical industry. i disagree. supporting producers to adopt new production methods and supporting the fight against identified causes is necessary, but not creating a new pharmaceutical business to ensure the perpetuation of bad practices and the creation of new risks. i welcome the ban on the import of exotic bombus sp. and the harmonization of labels and the increased traceability of honey. i think it is essential for parliament to identify the causes of the problems, and this report does that. but it is taking too few steps towards resolving these causes, which is why i abstained.
in writing. − bee mortality is a serious problem that must be tackled, as if it is not addressed it will have a 'profound negative impact on agriculture, production and food security'. it is therefore necessary for the commission to increase support for research into the prevention and control of diseases affecting bees and for the allocation of more resources to beekeeping under the cap after 2013. increased support for research and development of veterinary medicines to combat the current pathogens affecting bees in the eu, in particular the varroa destructor mite, is essential. some 76% of food production in the eu depends on bee pollination. this number gives us a sense of the seriousness of the problem for agriculture, for food production and security, for biodiversity, for environmental sustainability and for ecosystems. more flexible rules should be laid down for the authorisation and making available of veterinary products for bees, including medicinal products of natural origin and other medicinal products which are not harmful to insect health.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the portuguese case is of particular importance in this context, since portugal is part of the group of member states with professional beekeeping. it should be noted that the importance of this sector is not only due to its economic dimension, despite all the relevant factors - some 600 000 community citizens depend on it directly or indirectly - but also to its environmental impact, since bees play a central role in the ecological balance. a holistic approach is therefore warranted to address the difficulties facing the sector, such as the recent increases in bee mortality, the presence of toxic agents that have impaired the health of the hives and the increasing average age of beekeepers, which are putting the sector's survival at risk. by making these concerns my own, i voted in favour.
in writing. the european parliament's committee on agriculture proposes a series of measures to help meet the challenges facing the beekeeping sector in recent years, which have contributed to the decline in products derived from bee activity. it calls for further studies to understand the factors that have led to the disappearance of a large number of bees whose activity is an integral part of european agriculture and contributes to the balance of ecosystems and biodiversity.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this directive which provides for the reform of eu state aid rules applicable to services of general economic interest. these services are crucial for the individual, but they also play a vital role in the well-being of society as a whole. the amendments proposed in this reform focused mainly on clarifying the application of state aid rules, taking into account their enormous diversity, in particular clarifying the relationship between the internal market and the provision of public services, ensuring that the principle of subsidiarity is applied in the definition, organisation and financing of these services. it was also stressed that any legal instrument should have to ensure satisfactory legal certainty.
in writing. - the importance of services of general economic interest in promoting fundamental rights and social, economic and territorial cohesion is undeniable. they thus contribute to combating social inequalities and promoting sustainable development, as well as to improving the economic performance and competitiveness of member states. they should undoubtedly play an important role in the europe 2020 strategy in pursuing the growth objectives, particularly in the areas of employment, training and social inclusion. in order to serve citizens properly, these services should be characterised by a high level of quality, safety and affordability, equal treatment and the promotion of universal access and user rights. despite the improvements introduced by the altmark package in 2005, there is still a need to make the legal instruments clearer, simpler, more proportionate and more effective in order to ensure a minimum satisfactory level of legal certainty. i welcome the commission's plans to review the state aid rules applicable to services of general economic interest in order to enhance the contribution that these services can make to the recovery of the eu economy as a whole and the promotion of sustainable economic growth.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report, as it calls for greater simplification, clarity and proportionality in the application of community rules on services of general economic interest (sgei). this report responds to the need to create a more effective legal framework in support of these services. the measures advocated will also help to dispel uncertainties about what should be considered a legitimate defence of the sgeis or an unjustified breach of the european treaties.
in writing. − compensation granted by the state or public authorities to undertakings entrusted with the operation of services of general economic interest is subject, in accordance with article 106 tfeu, to the provisions on state aid. in the context of the reform of eu state aid rules, it is necessary to ensure that competition rules do not preclude appropriate compensation for undertakings entrusted with the provision of services of general economic interest, and to take account of the importance of the services provided for the promotion of fundamental rights; for social, economic and territorial cohesion; for combating inequalities in society and for promoting sustainable development.
in writing. − the quality of life of european citizens a maxim found in all the treaties implies the existence of fully functioning services of general interest. these are basic services that we only become aware of when something goes wrong, such as a strike in the solid waste collection services, a breakdown in a high-voltage line that causes a blackout, or a rupture in a water supply pipe that prevents us from taking a shower in the morning. the report by peter simon focuses on the reform of the european union (eu) rules on state aid for economic services of general interest (sgeis). undeniable in their social function and in promoting economic and territorial cohesion, they also promote the europe 2020 strategy in the fields of employment, training and social integration. as such, we cannot expect them to be profitable services, but to benefit from state support. however, in view of the current economic and financial crisis, it is imperative to improve the rules for the granting of such aid. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report, which establishes a new legal framework for support for sgeis, based on the principles of simplification, regulatory clarity and proportionality.
in writing. - the report contains undoubtedly positive aspects, including several considerations which run counter to the dominant neoliberal view in this parliament, which views public services as business areas, in a mercantilist perspective. some of the positions expressed have long been held by us, but are often rejected by the majority, including the main political groups (including the social democrats). for example: the position that public services should be of high quality and universal; the strengthening of investment in the modernisation of infrastructure in various areas; the opposition to the commission's imposition of the liberalisation of public services in third countries in free trade agreements (in the various names they may take: association agreements, economic partnership agreements, etc.); the provision of compensation amounts for all public services of general economic interest which member states consider to meet essential social needs, as well as the maintenance of unlimited exemption in favour of hospitals and social housing. however, the report insists on the division between services of general interest and services of general economic interest, which we disagree with. the fact is that many of these services are subject to competition rules and the possibilities for state intervention in defence of the common good and the pursuit of national interests are severely limited. that is why we abstained.
in writing. the report also calls for the establishment of a european network of national authorities responsible for the protection of the environment. examples of such cases are the positions we support, but which are not always supported by the majority of the ep, namely: that public services should be of high quality and universal, increased investment in the modernisation of infrastructure in various areas, the request that the commission not impose the liberalisation of public services in third countries, and that it ensure compensation amounts for all public services of general economic interest which member states consider to meet essential social needs, as well as the maintenance of unlimited exemption in favour of hospitals and social housing. but unfortunately it insists on the division between services of general interest and services of general economic interest, which in itself weakens the scope of the report. it provides for state aid only for these services as compensation granted by the state or public authorities to undertakings entrusted with the provision of services of general economic interest, subjecting them in many cases to the rules of competition. that is why we abstained.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the reform it advocates is to allow the economic services of general interest (seig) to be subject to clearer and simpler rules on state funding. i believe, however, that much remains to be done in this area and that the report does not fully meet all the needs identified. i believe that the road to universal and quality imps cannot be made without public funding and that we must therefore establish strict and fair funding rules. as it is a step towards a more just and supportive society, it deserves my vote.
in writing. − services of general interest play a decisive role for individual citizens and are also of paramount importance for the prosperity of society as a whole. the range of services is wide, and in the european union it is up to national, regional or local authorities to define what can be considered a service of general interest, i.e. what service should be offered in the general interest. however, these services have one common feature: services which the state or public authorities consider to be of particular importance for all citizens but which could not be provided without state intervention or could not be provided to a sufficient extent. the state intervention aims to ensure that all citizens have access to the services in question and that a supply of quality services at prices that are affordable to all citizens is possible. the provision of services of general interest also contributes to the successful implementation of the europe 2020 growth strategy, particularly in the fields of employment, training and social inclusion. particular importance is attached to social services of general interest, which play an important role in the defence of fundamental rights and make a crucial contribution to equal opportunities.
in writing. − this report deals with the reform of eu state aid rules for services which the state or public authorities consider to be of particular importance to all citizens and which could not be provided without state intervention. the state intervention aims to ensure that all citizens have access to the services in question and that a supply of quality services at prices that are affordable to all citizens is possible. the objectives of the reform the commission is pursuing are to bring greater clarity to the application of state aid rules to services of general economic interest and to ensure a differentiated and proportionate response to the different types of services of general economic interest. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - services of general economic interest are, in a sense, a reflection of the community economic model. while the aim is to ensure the universal provision of a given range of essential services, the aim is to assign their operation to private operators in order to achieve a higher degree of efficiency. however, given their obligation to provide services on a universal basis, private entities are entitled to compensatory allowances to cover the non-profit-making aspect of the activity. a proposal to revise the system of such compensation was submitted to the european parliament for its consideration. in this connection, i believe that, in addition to ensuring transparency in the application of the rules for awarding compensation, there is also a need to speed up the procedure, so that it is efficient. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − services of general economic interest (sgei) play a fundamental role in society and are of paramount importance to citizens. the state intervenes to ensure quick and efficient access to the services in question, with the aim of providing them at affordable and high quality. i agree with the report which aims to bring greater clarity in the application of state aid rules to sgeis, to increase overall legal clarity, to avoid bringing cases before the court of justice of the european union and to provide public services with greater operational efficiency. i would also like to stress that the sgeis are an important part of the common values of the european union, promoting fundamental rights and social, economic and territorial cohesion, and that it is crucial to adopt measures to simplify the application of state aid rules in the context of a more diversified approach.
in writing. the european parliament has also called for the commission to be given the task of drawing up a report on the situation in the eu. the objective of reducing the number of poor people by some 20 million by 2020 should remain a top priority and the necessary budgetary resources should be allocated to this end.
in writing. − the phenomenon of poverty is multifaceted and its combating should be the subject of tailor-made policies, depending on the age group to which it is addressed and the objective needs of each person or group of people, which should be based on the universal principles enshrined in the european convention on human rights, because poverty and social exclusion are not compatible with the european social model that we are so proud to defend. it is important that action is taken at community level not only in terms of prevention and awareness-raising but also through greater coordination, through measures to effectively combat poverty and social exclusion and, of course, through micro-financing of specific policies implemented by the different member states, provided that they are in line with the objectives set by the europe 2020 strategy. this mission is made all the more evident by the eu's repeated commitment to eradicating poverty, social exclusion and territorial cohesion. i generally agree with the content of the report, and i therefore voted in favour of it, mainly because of the commitments made by the rapporteur after hearing the other political groups, in particular the ppe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that although the fight against poverty and social exclusion is essentially the responsibility of national governments, the union should play a more prominent role in raising awareness, coordinating and financing. this platform, which is part of a strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, will play a major role in reducing poverty, optimising european funds and improving the effectiveness of social protection systems.
in writing. - the current economic and financial crisis raises fears of a worsening of poverty and exclusion across europe. unfortunately, the ambitious objectives set by the lisbon strategy have proved difficult to achieve. in view of the multiple and large scale of the problems, greater european coordination is needed in this area in order to lift 20 million people out of poverty, as the europe 2020 strategy aims to do. the european union must not lose sight of the fact that it exists for the people, and that any initiatives it takes to combat poverty and social exclusion must not lose sight of the dignity of every human being, nor confuse the establishment of large bureaucratic structures with the effective help to those who need it most. if the multidisciplinary nature of the problem calls for a multidisciplinary response, the sensitivity of the programme calls for the fundamental rights of every human being to be kept in mind, bearing in mind the financial difficulties faced by the member states and the realism which this limitation imposes.
in writing. − the europe 2020 strategy sets the objective of reducing the number of people in precarious situations by 20 million by 2020. one of the seven flagship measures of this strategy is the european platform against poverty and social exclusion, whose framework for social and territorial cohesion was presented by the commission on 16 december 2010, as the european year against poverty and social exclusion was about to close. this report, by frédéric daerden, looks at the european platform against poverty and social exclusion and argues that solidarity between states and citizens must be a priority for the european union. the economic and financial crisis since 2008 has hampered economic growth and, consequently, job creation, one of the pillars of the fight against poverty and social exclusion. the eu should encourage member states to ease austerity policies through new investment, both public and private. i welcome the adoption of this report and hope that it will contribute to significantly reducing the number of 80 million european citizens at risk of poverty, including 20 million children.
in writing. - we regret that our proposals, which denounced the causes of poverty and proposed the alternatives needed to eradicate it, were not adopted, in particular the following: condemns the so-called austerity policies and programmes which are aggravating poverty and social exclusion; insists on the need for a fundamental change in community policies in the economic, financial and social fields which are at the root of current poverty, in particular the stability and growth pact, the euro plus pact, liberalisation and privatisation of essential public services; calls for the rejection of the jep and the euro plus pact and insists on their replacement by a pact for social progress and development which gives priority to employment with rights, social inclusion and poverty eradication; considers that the poverty affecting people who already have a job does not reflect fair working conditions and calls for efforts to be concentrated on changing this situation so that remuneration in general and minimum wages in particular, and regardless of whether they are defined by law or by collective agreements, can ensure a decent standard of living.
in writing. - this report comes at a time when we are witnessing the escalation of poverty in europe. more than 116 million people are at risk of poverty in the european union and some 42 million people live in situations of extreme deprivation. social protection standards are needed and the establishment of a roadmap for the european union and the member states is crucial in this serious socioeconomic context. however, if we are to effectively eradicate poverty, we must put an end to austerity policies and focus on job creation. i therefore abstained.
in writing. the european union, one of the richest regions in the world, has more than 80 million people at risk of poverty, including 20 million children and 8% of the working population. this situation is unacceptable in the light of the european values of justice and solidarity enshrined in the treaties. however, poverty and social exclusion have increased in recent years, despite the union's commitments to reduce them. the 2008 crisis and its aftermath have further exacerbated this problem, putting pressure on the most vulnerable populations. while the fight against poverty and social exclusion is primarily the responsibility of national governments, the union can nevertheless play an important role in raising awareness, coordinating and financing. to ensure sustainable and inclusive growth, it is essential to integrate the most vulnerable categories of people at the heart of the european project, given that poverty reduction is a driving force for future growth.
in writing. − poverty and social exclusion have increased in recent years, despite the european union's commitments to reduce them. the 2008 crisis and its aftermath have further exacerbated this problem, putting pressure on the most vulnerable populations. while the fight against poverty and social exclusion is primarily the responsibility of national governments, the union can nevertheless play an important role in raising awareness, coordinating and financing. to this end, and to ensure sustainable and inclusive growth, it is essential to integrate the most vulnerable categories of people at the heart of the european project, given that poverty reduction is a driving force for future growth. listening to the people on the ground was the concern that guided the preparation of this report, to which the actors involved have made a significant contribution by presenting proposals aimed at eradicating the scourge of poverty and social exclusion. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − poverty and social exclusion represent major obstacles to the integrated development of the various communities. a society with great social asymmetries is, in fact, prone to suffer situations of enormous instability, with clear losses ultimately for the citizens. unfortunately, even today, almost 20% of european citizens live below the so-called poverty line. it is therefore justified for the community institutions to adopt policies to help member states to deal with the social imbalances that are felt, so as to reduce and ideally eradicate the remaining poverty situations (which, in aggregate, cover 80 million community citizens). that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. − the eu has dedicated 2010 to the issue of poverty and social exclusion, in order to show the commitment of the institutions to eradicating poverty, as expressed in the lisbon strategy and the eu 2020 initiative, the european platform against poverty and social exclusion. this platform will enable member states to take a multi-dimensional approach with a framework to achieve the objectives and to reduce by 20 million the number of people in precarious situations by 2020. the eu has more than 80 million people at risk of poverty, including 20 million children and 8% of the working population. the multiplier effects of this problem call for an integrated but at the same time individualised response, since poverty and social exclusion are expressed in different ways. i think it is important to use the open method of coordination in order to regularise the monitoring in the member states of the objectives achieved in this fight and to allow the sharing of good practice. another point i would like to make is the emergence of so-called hidden poverty, which affects the middle class in european countries.

mr president, let's be honest with each other. we've been on a drug for three years to get out of this crisis, and it's getting worse by the day. instead of a cure, we've created two fatal vicious circles. the first between banks and states. in europe today, it is easier to discuss the bankruptcy of a state than that of a large bank, but it is still expected that banks should finance states and states should bail out their banks. this spiral has to be broken. the commission must move forward with european legislation to protect taxpayers from banking crises. but it is also vital to protect the debt of states from the attacks of speculators. and for that it is urgent, and already too late, to prepare coordinated sovereign debt issues, called eurobonds or stability bonds, and guarantee them through robust instruments of a community and non-intergovernmental nature. in short, we must also review the involvement of the european central bank. but the second vicious circle results from the argument that some states are rich because they are virtuous, while others are poor because they have sinned. this narrative is politically explosive and technically wrong. it ignores the essential fact that a single market and a single currency, constructed by political choice and among inequalities, necessarily exacerbate the imbalances in competitiveness between the centre and the periphery. and this is what needs to be attacked in economic governance. no, mr rompuy, by sanctions which promote the crushing of wages and incomes, with one country controlling another. firstly, through involvement, commissioner, of both the surplus and the deficit countries, so as to bring productivity together through investment, education and science. the sanctions have only generated unemployment, disillusionment and a recessionary wave from which we cannot escape.

in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the egf was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when we are faced with this serious crisis, with rising unemployment as one of its main consequences, the eu should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly in terms of support for people who have lost their jobs overnight. i therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 12 689 838 from the egf for ireland to support workers made redundant by 1 482 firms in division 41 (building) in the border, midlands and western and southern and eastern regions.
in writing. - given the various repercussions that ireland has been experiencing due to its fragile exposure to the us mortgage credit financial crisis and structural changes in world trade patterns, i considered it important to support this report which will provide vital temporary and one-off assistance to unemployed workers. i also believe that the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for ireland, totalling eur 12 689 838, will be used to this end. this support for the reintegration of workers made redundant as a result of globalisation and the global economic and financial crisis into the labour market in ireland is essential to safeguard the 3,205 redundancies that occurred in 1,482 companies in division 41. of the package of measures proposed by the commission, i would like to highlight two of the most important: career guidance, in that individual counselling sessions will be organised for unemployed workers to give them guidance on the steps to be taken in returning to work, and second-level vocational education and training programmes and income support, which will be designed to provide an increasingly important updating of skills in a context of increasing competitiveness in a more globalised world.

in writing. − the application submitted by ireland for egf assistance concerns 4866 redundancies (of which 3205 are potential beneficiaries of assistance) which occurred in 1482 enterprises in nace rev. 2 division 41 (building), in the nuts ii regions of border, midlands and western (ie01) and southern and eastern (ie02), during the nine months of the reference period from 1 july 2009 to 31 march 2010. this is a request related to the mortgage credit crisis which has seriously affected irish banks and has also had an impact on the construction sector. according to the commission's assessment, this application fulfils all the eligibility criteria defined by law. the egf regulation provides for the egf to be mobilised in situations such as this one where, as a direct consequence of the global economic and financial crisis, 'at least 500 redundancies occur in a nine-month period, in particular in small and medium-sized enterprises, in a division of nace level 2, in a region or in two regions adjacent to nuts level ii'. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, in the hope that assistance for workers made redundant can be provided quickly and efficiently.

in writing. − the application submitted by ireland for egf assistance concerns 842 redundancies (of which 554 are potential beneficiaries of assistance) which occurred in 230 enterprises in nace rev. 2 division 71 (architecture and engineering activities; technical testing and analysis activities) in the nuts ii regions of border, midlands and western (ie01) and southern and eastern (ie02) during the reference period 1 july 2009 to 31 march 2010. this is a request related to the mortgage credit crisis which has seriously affected irish banks and has also had an impact on the construction sector. according to the commission's assessment, this application fulfils all the eligibility criteria defined by law. the egf regulation provides for the egf to be mobilised in situations such as this one where, as a direct consequence of the global economic and financial crisis, 'at least 500 redundancies occur in a nine-month period, in particular in small and medium-sized enterprises, in a division of nace level 2, in a region or in two regions adjacent to nuts level ii'. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, in the hope that assistance for workers made redundant can be provided quickly and efficiently.
