in writing. - i approve this report. i welcome the fact that the acp has succeeded in establishing itself as a key player in north-south cooperation. however, more attention should be paid to the concrete results on the ground, to the work of the acp-eu jpa and to the consistency between its resolutions and those of the european parliament.
in writing. − the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly (jpa) represents a global partnership, unique in the world, which has been developing at both institutional and content level and which now encompasses areas such as aid, economic cooperation, human rights, trade relations between the eu and the six acp regions and political dialogue. in my view, this is the richness that makes acp-eu cooperation a unique model for this kind of development partnership. i therefore welcome the fact that the ppp continued to provide a framework for an open and in-depth dialogue between the eu and the acp countries in 2010, which culminated in two meetings last year (tenerife and kinshasa), while i regret the absence of the eu council at the latter. i stress the importance of the ppp to keep up pressure on eu member states to take action to meet their commitments to achieve the millennium development goals, to involve national parliaments more closely in national and regional strategy papers and in the implementation of the edf, and to take action to tackle poverty, climate change and strict respect for all aspects of human rights.
in writing. − the acp-eu parliamentary assembly is an important forum for debate, reflection and decision-making between parliamentarians from the two regions who, in the framework of the cotonou agreement, can strengthen relations and better understand each other's realities, as well as promote the exchange of experience and the adoption of best practices. in this context, the involvement of national parliaments and their public opinion is crucial if what is decided is to have a concrete impact on the lives of citizens and can positively influence local political debate. i regret that the portuguese language, spoken by no less than seven countries in the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly, has not yet been properly recognised for its importance and consequently has not been granted the same facilities for translation and interpretation and timely access to documents as english and french. this discrimination is unacceptable and has persisted on the basis of unconvincing budgetary arguments. the damage they cause to the people of portuguese-speaking countries is infinitely greater than any gains that such obstinacy has allowed.
in writing. - since its inception, the european union has enjoyed privileged relations with the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries in the field of development cooperation, particularly at political, economic and social levels. relations between the eu and the acp countries are currently governed by the cotonou agreement signed in 2000. this report, by filip kaczmarek, takes stock of the activities of the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly, which met twice in 2010, in tenerife (spain) and kinshasa (people's republic of congo), and adopted nine resolutions and a declaration on the second revision of the cotunu agreement. the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly has a decisive role to play in strengthening the north-south dialogue, and it is therefore essential that the european parliament should look at how it works, so that we can achieve our objectives, both as regards the reconstruction of post-conflict countries and the functioning of democracy, especially in countries receiving international aid. i therefore vote in favour of this report, welcome the measures referred to and welcome the commission's intention to cooperate in the implementation of the cotonou partnership agreement.
in writing. − this report takes stock of the work of the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly (jpa) throughout 2010. in this report, some of the most positive aspects of the functioning of this house are identified, as well as its virtues. we also support the call for greater attention to be paid to the work of the ppp and the results achieved. the active role of acp national parliaments is also of central importance. however, we felt that some of the issues raised needed further consideration. we did so during the debate in the plenary on such important issues as the economic partnership agreements, land grabbing and the burden of external debt and its servicing. we also disagree with some of the points in the resolution, for example when it calls for the european parliament's (ep) resolutions to be consistent with those of the app. in our opinion, one of the riches of the app lies precisely in the fact that it is often at odds with the dominant positions in the ep on many issues. this helps to highlight (and to expose) the limitations and contradictions (and often the ulterior motives!) of the european union's cooperation and development policy.
in writing. - this report analyses the activities of the acp-eu parliamentary assembly. as a non-member of this house, i welcome this information, although i do not agree with all the information contained therein. we are concerned about the conclusion of the so-called economic partnership agreements and the european commission's insistence on free trade. the rapporteur rightly says that more attention should be paid to the results of the work of the acp-eu parliamentary assembly. and from this work it is possible to see the repeated resistance - fair, legitimate and entirely understandable - that the acp countries have shown to the epas. as they are designed, they may be very profitable for some european multinationals, but they will be disastrous for these countries. finally, a reference to the economic and financial crisis and its effects on the acp countries, which are calling for the abolition of this enormous burden. it is a debt that has been paid off many times and yet is growing. to put an end once and for all to an unacceptable plundering of wealth and to help these countries in an effective way to find a sovereign and independent path of development and social progress, it is urgent to cancel this debt.
in writing. − the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly (jpa) has been gaining in importance within the framework of the global partnerships, as they have been developing in various fields, notably at institutional and content level, and now encompass matters such as aid, economic cooperation, human rights, trade relations between the eu and the six acp regions and political dialogue. it is this diversity of positions that makes acp-eu cooperation a unique model in this kind of development partnership. it is, however, important that the jpa maintains pressure on eu member states to take action to deliver on the commitments they have made to the millennium development goals, namely greater involvement of national parliaments in national and regional strategy papers and edf implementation, as well as measures to combat poverty and climate change and to ensure strict respect for human rights in all aspects.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the work of the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly in 2010. i would like to stress in this report the positive vote that parliament gives to the increasingly parliamentary nature and therefore the policy of the joint parliamentary assembly. the increasingly active role of the members of the jpa and the improved quality of its debates should also be highlighted, which has helped to ensure the vital importance of the jpa for the acp-eu partnership.
in writing. − the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly met twice in 2010, in tenerife and in kinshasa. the three standing committees met four times: the commission also adopted a communication on the implementation of the european year of the environment, which was published in the official journal of the european communities on 1 january. the work carried out included the adoption of resolutions on haiti, south sudan, the results of the elections in côte d'ivoire and the situation in the sara-sabel region. fact-finding and election observation missions were also organised. the evaluation of the work of 2010 shows that the app now plays a valuable role in south-north relations, providing a good forum for dialogue between the countries of the two hemispheres.
in writing. − during 2010, the joint parliamentary assembly met twice: from 6 to 9 june in tenerife, spain, and from 30 november to 3 december in kinshasa, democratic republic of congo. these meetings resulted in nine resolutions and a declaration on the second revision of the cotonou partnership agreement. in addition to these meetings, a regional meeting was also held in mahé, seychelles. in 2010, the importance of cooperation and partnership between the european union and the acp countries was reaffirmed in order to promote an in-depth, open and democratic dialogue on the cotonou agreements and on the economic partnership agreements with the six acp regions. i stress the importance of implementing the regional and national strategy papers for cooperation with the european union until 2013 and i therefore call on the joint parliamentary assembly to make progress towards contributing to the objectives of the millennium development goals, stressing the crucial importance of adopting clear, effective and transparent legislation within the framework of the commitments undertaken.
in writing. - i approve this report, as a solid basis for the implementation of the european heritage label must be ensured. this initiative will be of fundamental importance for the promotion of the history of our continent and our culture, as well as an important instrument for future generations, even from an educational point of view. i should like to stress the natural wealth of the outermost regions, such as the azores, which will certainly be included in the list of sites to be awarded this label.
in writing. - the mark of european heritage is spread over the whole of the area which has been successively influenced by greek, roman and judeo-christian influences, decomposed in its jewish and christian, catholic, orthodox and protestant sensibilities and, in some cases, also touched by arab and ottoman influence. the european brand is precisely the built and unbuilt heritage that marks the diversity of civilizations which, like layers of the same ground, underlie what the cultures of the member states are today. in order to speak of a european trademark with a property, it will be necessary not to overlook the role of each state in the formation and formatting of that same trademark and to resist the temptation to seek only references which are consensual, but which overlook the quintessential multicultural reality which permeates all of the so-called high european culture. i welcome the decision to value europe's heritage. i hope that this appreciation of europe's heritage will not be discriminatory and that it will not seek to rewrite history.
in writing. - this report, by chrysoula paliadeli, is a recommendation for a second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting the decision of the european parliament and of the council to develop eu action on the european heritage label. the commission proposal, presented on 9 march 2010, aimed to strengthen the sense of belonging to the european union among european citizens by enhancing their history, heritage and intercultural dialogue. in fact, we're part of the same continent and share a common history. so this brand is something we should celebrate and be proud of in these times of economic recession. this mark is an essential achievement of european unity and a way of making young europeans feel proud to belong to the old continent. i welcome this initiative, which promotes our heritage and culture through an educational dimension, and which is another important step towards overcoming the financial crisis by boosting the growth of european tourism in its cultural dimension, and i hope that it will be a great success throughout europe.
in writing. - the position we expressed at the first reading of this report is maintained at the second reading. the warnings issued then are now being reiterated by us. there is no such thing as a single european cultural heritage. culture, like all historical phenomena, is not made up of any homogeneous and common identity. on the contrary, it is an expression of antagonisms, conflicts and contexts of cultural domination. we also question the meaning of the designation of european union heritage, which is based on the mere location of the heritage elements in question, when we know that europe's heritage is indebted to many cultures and could be claimed equally by the islamic world, the mediterranean cultures or the cultures of the peoples subject to european colonialism. the rapporteur hopes that by building a symbolic cultural dimension in the eu, the feeling of belonging to the european union will be strengthened by european citizens. but it ignores the growing clash between the interests and legitimate aspirations of the citizens of this eu. it ignores the terrible consequences of eu policies in many areas, including culture. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect.
in writing. the report also calls for the creation of a european cultural area, which would be a key element in the development of the european union. well, the truth is, there are different cultures. we are talking specifically about the imf-eu programmes, so-called financial assistance programmes, which are in fact genuine programmes of aggression against democratic values, social and labour rights and also culture. it is the estate left to abandonment; are the poverty budgets; the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force. the point is to develop efforts to legitimize an integration whose orientation is increasingly contrary to the interests and legitimate aspirations of citizens, starting with the creation of a symbolic cultural dimension. this initiative is thus inseparable from the intense ideological struggle naturally inherent in the very lively social struggle which is raging throughout the eu. but heritage is a sensitive domain, because it is inseparable from history. we hope that this is not another door that opens to the disturbing and degrading processes of rewriting history that we have seen in recent years in various countries.
in writing. - the european heritage brand is diverse, encompassing greek, roman and judeo-christian influences and, in some cases, the arab and ottoman brand. the european brand represents the heritage that encompasses all the different cultures of the member states in their most varied forms. the value of europe's heritage is of the utmost importance.
in writing. − the purpose of this report is to adopt the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting the decision of the european parliament and of the council establishing a european union action on the european heritage label. i defended the merits of this project when the european parliament voted on the decision at first reading. having noted that the amendments proposed by the council incorporated, in whole or in part, the vast majority of the amendments tabled by the european parliament at first reading, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the commission's initiative to create the european heritage label aims to strengthen european identity by distinguishing certain sites for their significance in the conception of a common cultural space. the council's first reading position, which accepted most of the amendments proposed by the ep, was therefore submitted to parliament for its consideration.
in writing. - the withdrawal of citizens from the european project, as well as nationalist and populist demonstrations, show that action is needed at european level to create identity links with european integration. the idea of a european identity is complementary to the national identities of the 27 member states. the commission's action aims to identify landmarks which are part of the history of european integration. this initiative, which is voluntary and undertaken at the request of the european parliament, is to take place every two years, with the member states pre-selecting the sites, and the final selection being made at european level. i am voting in favour of this report and i support the idea that the european parliament should take an active part in the selection process. i support such initiatives, which aim to bring the european institutions closer to the european citizens, especially in a time of growing scepticism and total disbelief.
in writing. - i support this report, as the reform of the first railway package is of crucial importance, in particular on issues such as the financing of railway infrastructure, the services associated with these structures, the role of the bodies regulating road transport services and the independence of infrastructure management.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the single european railway area because it contains proposals to clarify and improve legislation in the field of rail transport, so as to make it more attractive as a means of transport for passengers and goods and thus contribute to the development of more sustainable transport systems in the eu.
in writing. - the decline of rail transport has been evident in some member states. this raises fears about its viability and encourages reflection on how to establish a single european railway area that can reverse this declining trend and promote a means of transport for people and goods that is faster, safer and less polluting than those that use fossil fuels. member states should closely monitor the implementation of this european railway area and promote the use of this means of transport internally, as well as enhance connectivity between railway lines in the various member states. a europe with a single railway area will tend to be more environmentally friendly and better supplied with goods and services.
in writing. - in recent years, with the exception of high-speed lines in some eu countries, all other rail projects have been relegated to the background in terms of investment, which has resulted in a significant increase in road traffic and improvement of the respective routes. this report, by debora serracchiani, focuses on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive establishing a single european railway area. we all know the discomfort of arriving at a border and having to change trains because the track is different. in fact, few trains cross borders. this is a market for transport, both of passengers and goods, with enormous growth potential, as it is cheaper and faster than road transport and has major environmental advantages. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report, i welcome the measures proposed to remove the administrative barriers which impede the development of this market at european level, and i hope that very soon we will be able to enjoy a single railway area within the eu.
in writing. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer. once again, the false idea is being insisted upon (which experience in several countries has been flatly refuting) that more markets and competition lead to better services. this directive will have serious consequences for the population, which will have fewer, poorer and more expensive services; for workers, with the intensification of the exploitation of the labour force at european level; for security, which is dangerously compromised, subjected to free competition; and for national interests, relegated to the background in a strategic sector, overridden by the interests of multinationals. there are particularly serious, even disturbing, aspects of the proposal presented today. for example, that safety criteria in rail transport are subject to the rules of competition in the single market. this is the result of the obligation on the national safety authorities to submit to the opinion of a regulatory body which assesses the conformity of the safety rules laid down with the competition rules. it is also a statement of the values and principles which inspire the majority in this parliament.
in writing. the reform of the railway package, approved by a majority of meps including portuguese psd, ps, cds meps , poses a serious threat to national public rail services, making it difficult to provide a quality public transport service with safety and affordability for the population. this directive will deepen the serious consequences for people, for workers in the sector and for national economies, which have resulted from the liberalization and privatization of the railway sector, carried out in several countries, insisting on the false idea (which experience has been refuting) that more market and competition lead to better services. the most serious aspects of this directive include: the total separation of infrastructure management and railway operations, which liberalises the railway sector, privatising the areas that generate profit and leaving to the state the areas where large amounts of funding are needed; the construction and maintenance of infrastructure. the proposed fragmentation is tailored to the multinationals in the sector, which are taking over rail transport and colonizing the markets for associated services in several countries. the example of the german multinational db, which controls more than 60% of the freight sector (where liberalisation first advanced) at european level, is a good illustration of this.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it aims to further privatisation of rail services. the separation of related activities advocated in the report invariably leads to the transfer of revenue-generating activities to the private sector and the retention in the public sector of loss-making activities. the european rail network needs coordination, integration and investment if it is to become the most efficient medium- and long-distance freight transport mode again. this report will not allow that future, and i have therefore voted against it.
in writing. − unfortunately, rail transport has been experiencing a decline in use in some member states. this should be of concern to us, because it is a means of transporting people and goods that is fast, safe and less polluting than those that use fossil fuels. the establishment of a single european railway area can therefore help to reverse this trend. a europe with a single railway area will tend to be more environmentally friendly and better supplied with goods and services.
in writing. − the first railway package adopted in 2001 was the first serious attempt to end the decline of rail transport and to reform the european regulatory framework. the aim was to ensure the integration of the sector and to enhance its attractiveness compared to other modes of transport. the aim of this report is to present a new framework for increasing the modal share of the railway sector by profoundly reviewing the legislation. as the current system has already shown its shortcomings, the rules will have to be strengthened and harmonised and new elements added to make rail more attractive as a mode of transport for both passengers and goods. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − despite its potential as an environmentally sustainable means of transport, rail has not succeeded in establishing itself as the preferred means of transport for people and goods. in the latter field, between 1996 and 2008, they lost market share to road transport. policies are therefore needed to revitalise these modes of transport, to reduce the obstacles to international transport, where artificial barriers to free movement still exist, and to encourage new entrants to the market. to this end, it is necessary to separate the entities which are engaged in the railway structures of the service operating companies, so that all are on an equal footing, avoiding the abuse of a dominant position by the operators with the greatest economic weight. i voted in favour of this reform of the regulatory framework for the railway sector, which will contribute to the creation of a genuine european transport network with significant advantages in terms of quality of service, job creation, safety and environmental sustainability.
in writing. − the creation of a single european railway area, as expressed in the objectives of the 2011 transport white paper, requires harmonisation of national regulations, which will greatly increase the competitiveness of this sector in relation to other modes of transport. the implementation of the first railway package did not achieve the objectives proposed and the lack of clarity of the text itself gave rise to different interpretations and, consequently, to infringement proceedings against the member states. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. the report focuses on the liberalisation of the national passenger market, the strengthening of the independence and powers of national regulatory bodies, the internalisation of external costs, financing issues, working conditions and safety rules. the creation of a european regulatory body will be the next step. furthermore, the commission will present, by the end of 2012, two legislative proposals on the vertical separation of the infrastructure manager from the service provider and the opening up of the railway market to make it more transparent, fair and non-discriminatory, avoiding distortions in the sector.
in writing. − i approve this resolution, reinforcing the message that it calls on the european union to confirm publicly and unequivocally its strong commitment to the kyoto protocol and to take all necessary measures to avoid any change to the commitment periods under the kyoto protocol. i therefore support the call for the european union to make an open declaration before durban that it is prepared to continue with the second commitment period under the kyoto protocol. maintaining measures to combat global warming is important for future generations and it is essential to implement environmentally sustainable policies, as is the case in the azores, a world example in areas such as the use of renewable energy.
in writing. − it is important that the european union maintains its leading role in the fight against climate change. the durban conference should result in concrete proposals for agreement on the second period of the kyoto protocol and on negotiations under the united nations convention on climate change. at the level of the convention negotiations, the cancún agreement on technology transfer, capacity building and forests must be implemented and the cdm for the least developed countries must be redesigned. for the second period of compliance with the kyoto protocol, europe must agree on the following conditions: the existence of a timetable for a legally binding agreement that includes the largest economies, a new separation between industrialized and developing countries, and the adoption of a sectoral approach for energy-intensive industrial sectors as a solution to carbon leakage.
in writing. - i support this resolution in its entirety. i would like to stress two points which i consider to be of the greatest importance for the durban conference. i agree with the urgency that the eu attaches to a new agreement between member states for a post-2012 protocol. it is essential to secure a comprehensive, international, fair, ambitious and legally binding agreement in order to secure the targets of reducing emissions (by 26%) by 2020 on the basis of 1990 levels and limiting the increase in the global average temperature beyond 2°c. equally important is a restructuring of the financial architecture of the protocol, the current one providing only 5% of what is estimated to be the capital needed by developing countries in the coming decades. otherwise we may find an unwanted reluctance on their part to join a new agreement. the eu therefore needs to press and pressure member states to create new mechanisms that make new and additional funds available, such as a financial transactions tax, a green tax, a shipping/air transport tax, among others. i admit that this requires rethinking the whole tax package so as not to place an undue burden on people and businesses in times of recession.
in writing. − it is essential that the eu develops a strategy to tackle climate change, making a serious commitment to sustainable development, seeking to reduce its carbon emissions, without jeopardising productive activities, particularly industries. any policy on climate change, especially in the context of the economic and financial crisis, must seek economic efficiency and sustainability, by putting innovation and research at the service of new techniques and new solutions that are more environmentally friendly and equally efficient and competitive. the focus should be on more efficient use of natural resources and strong investment in research and cleaner technologies to maintain european competitiveness and enable job creation in a green growth environment.
in writing. the european union is also committed to the principle of subsidiarity, which is the basis for the european union's action in the field of climate change. the natural disasters of 2011 and the melting of the ice caps prove the need for us to be very attentive to these situations and to take action at the global level. because it is people who have to respond to climate change and not the other way around, we have to limit the average temperature increase to two degrees and make the year 2012 the peak year for greenhouse gases. it is not enough to adopt good measures, they must be implemented! i therefore welcome the significant presence of eu representatives at this conference to give effect to the recommendations now adopted and welcome the fact that the eu is committed to complying with the kyoto protocol and to reducing co2 emissions to levels above the 20% target for 2020.
in writing. - this resolution, like its predecessors (cop-15 and cop-16), contains positive aspects. in general terms, the importance of reducing ghg emissions and the need to meet the targets set in the un framework are highlighted. but, like the previous ones, this resolution also fails to define the means to achieve these goals and to analyse why, conference after conference, the goals are not met: the solution to this environmental problem will not be found within the framework of the irrational economic and social system that has generated it. the failure to recognise and debate this premise, the insistence on the capitalist approach to this problem, of which market instruments such as carbon trading are a prominent feature, does not allow for optimism about the effective resolution of the problem. the problem is, moreover, expressed in far more diverse and complex terms than those used in the resolution concerning the progressive and inexorable shortage of raw materials on which many areas of activity in contemporary societies depend to a very large extent. moreover, what is profoundly heterogeneous (the different member states) in terms of their specific situation, in the framework of the principle of common but differentiated responsibility, continues to be regarded as a homogeneous entity (the eu).
in writing. - we know that the depletion of natural resources at a rate that is absolutely disproportionate to the needs of the world's population, air and water pollution, the effects of war, the destruction of forests and intensive agriculture are all concrete effects of industrial activity and factors that reduce the quality of life of the general population. even more serious is the distribution of costs and benefits effected by capitalism, where the territories most affected by the intensive exploitation of nature are precisely those occupied by the most impoverished populations and most deprived of the enjoyment of the benefits of the development of technology and industrial production. the report has positive aspects in that it stresses the importance of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and the need to meet the targets set. however, it fails to analyse the essential reasons why, conference after conference, these are not being met. the solution to the environmental problem will not be found within the framework of the irrational economic and social system that has created it. the failure to recognise and debate this premise, the insistence on a capitalist approach to this problem, of which market instruments such as carbon trading are a prominent feature, does not allow for optimism in solving the environmental problem.
in writing. the resolution sets as a general objective a legally binding international agreement consistent with the principle of common but differentiated responsibility. the resolution states that, irrespective of the outcome of international negotiations, it is in the eu's interest to set a climate protection target of more than 20%, as this would have the effect of simultaneously creating green jobs, growth and security. aiming for a reduction in the eu that is higher than the eu's own target is of the utmost importance. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the establishment of a green climate fund to support the transition to low-carbon and climate-resilient development in developing countries is also called for. i also welcome the position to include aviation and transport in the durban agreement. for the reasons stated, i voted in favour. i must, however, make clear my opposition to carbon trading mechanisms and i regret that intellectual property rights are given more weight than the fight against climate change.
in writing. − the european parliament must be firm in its defence of the kyoto protocol and the reduction of co2 emissions in the period after 2012. the adoption of this resolution at the climate change conference in durban, south africa, from 28 november to 9 december, brings with it greater responsibilities for the eu to go further in reducing co2 by 20% by 2020, which could help to stimulate the european economy. concrete measures are needed to close the gigatonnes gap (i.e. the difference) between current levels of ambition and the levels required to keep global warming below 2°c.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution on the durban climate change conference (cop 17), which sets out the european parliament's concerns and calls on the parties to ensure that a fair, ambitious and legally binding post-2012 comprehensive international agreement is reached, based on the international system based on the rules of the kyoto protocol, consistent with the 2°c target and the peak of national and global greenhouse gas emissions in the shortest possible time.
in writing. − the next conference on climate change, to be held in durban from 28 november to 9 december 2011 (17th conference of the parties), is another opportunity to adopt a new political strategy to address the climate change facing the planet. in this context, there are a number of points which the european union must consider to be unassailable: to take the lead in adopting measures to ensure the environmental sustainability of the economy, to push for a decision-making process based on respect for the principle of majority voting, to strengthen support for research into environmentally less polluting technologies and to support the resulting structural adjustment of the economy. i voted in favour of this guideline because i agree with it.
in writing. − in 2009, the european commission published the white paper entitled 'climate change adaptation: towards a european framework for action' aimed at reducing the european union's vulnerability to the impact of climate change, presenting an overall strategy, concrete objectives and metrics, as well as potential funding instruments. i am voting in favour of this resolution because i consider it important to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and to take measures to deal with the impacts of climate change. i believe it is urgent that the european union sets itself more ambitious targets than the 20% reduction set for 2020 and introduces new measures to reduce emissions from aviation and shipping, which were not included in the kyoto protocol. finally, i believe that the european institutions must undertake a global strategy to reduce land and sea temperatures, to change the volume and patterns of precipitation, to control the rise in the average sea level and to avoid the risks of coastal erosion and natural disasters associated with weather phenomena.
in writing. - i approve this report. firstly, i welcome the renewed commitment by the member states to honour their commitments to provide 0.7% of their gni in aid. i note, however, that in 2010 the european union fell short of its own target for oda for that year by some eur 15 billion. on the other hand, i agree with the council that oda alone will not be enough to eradicate poverty globally. the european union's development policy should aim at removing structural obstacles to the objective of poverty eradication and be consistent across the various policy areas, such as agriculture, trade, investment, tax havens, access to raw materials or climate change. without a reinforced level of commitment, it will not be easy to achieve the millennium development goals in 2015, particularly the one that calls for the eradication of extreme poverty.
in writing. − the eu and its member states are by far the world's largest donors of official development assistance, despite the increasing pressure on national budgets as a result of the financial and economic crisis affecting the world. however, i share the rapporteur's concerns that in the past year eu member states have only contributed 0.43% of their gni to official development assistance (oda), despite the commitment to collectively devote 0.7% of their gni to oda by 2015 and an intermediate target of 0.56% in 2010. not only for the eu's credibility, but also for the concrete situation of the poorest (particularly hard as a result of the economic and financial crisis for which they are not responsible), it is urgent that the eu fulfils its development commitments and, instead of reducing its development aid budgets, takes urgent action to secure the commitments made, looks at new innovative financing mechanisms and is able to ensure greater coherence between the union's trade and development policies.
in writing. the european union's commitment to development is one of the main hallmarks of an integration process which is not to be closed in on itself. despite the difficulties experienced by several member states, which have led to a reduction in the aid provided by several of them, i would like the union to continue its efforts to cooperate with the people and the states which have the least. however, i also believe that this aid should be subject to greater transparency and that it should be channelled to the populations who really need it and scrutinized, not only by the donors but also by the public and the parliaments of the countries receiving aid. i disagree with the rapporteur on the possibility of introducing a financial transaction tax to finance member states and boost development aid. i believe that the generalization of this measure needs further study and that its potential negative consequences warrant particular caution in its adoption.
in writing. - the motion for a resolution on the european union's responsibility for financing development follows the questions with oral questions to the council and the commission put by mrs michèle striffler, pursuant to rule 115 of the rules of procedure, on behalf of the committee on development. the current global economic and financial crisis is particularly damaging to developing countries, and the eu needs to meet the millennium development goals of devoting 0.7% of gross national income to helping the poorest countries by 2015. official development assistance plays a key role in the survival of many peoples, with the eu's contribution accounting for more than half of total aid. the eu must therefore not only ensure that this aid is implemented in a transparent and effective manner, taking account of the real needs of these countries, but also increase the resources available in the next financial framework. given that the credibility of the eu cannot be called into question, i am voting in favour of this motion for a resolution, knowing that with the measures adopted, the eu will fulfil its promises to support developing countries under the mdgs.
in writing. − the eu and its member states are the world's largest donors of official development assistance, despite the budgetary constraints member states are subject to as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. despite all the difficulties, the eu needs to deliver on its development commitments and, instead of reducing its development aid budgets, take urgent action to secure the commitments it has made, look at new innovative financing mechanisms and be able to ensure greater coherence between the union's trade and development policies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution of 16 november 2011 on the report on eu accountability for development finance. in this resolution, parliament welcomes the commission communication on the abovementioned report as a very useful exercise in transparency and peer review. it also welcomes the fact that the report calls on european union donors to intensify political dialogue on development cooperation with emerging economies and also encourages member states to support triangular and south-south development cooperation initiatives, considering that there is no longer any justification for aid in the form of grants to states with abundant monetary reserves.

in writing. − overall, the eu and its member states are the world's largest donors of official development assistance (oda), despite the economic and social crisis facing countries. however, in the past year, the member states and the union have not fulfilled their commitments under the millennium development goals. that is why we must do more and better. i welcome the commitment of the member states to provide 0.7% of their gni in aid from 2015 onwards, at a time of social upheaval in european societies themselves. however, we must go beyond direct funding. we must commit ourselves to coherent policies in the fields of agriculture, trade, investment, access to raw materials and the fight against climate change, with development prospects for the world's poorest countries. in addition, we must establish other sources of financing, in particular through the eib, microfinance and a financial transaction tax, part of which is intended for development aid. private sector support for development should also be strengthened, as solidarity with the poorest should not be achieved through public policies alone. we must at the same time ask the receiving countries for accountability and transparency.

madam president, commissioner, the integrated maritime policy advocates a coordinated approach to the management and governance of the oceans, seas and coasts, in a global and coherent perspective of all european policies relating to the sea. taking a global perspective and an integrated approach implies the interaction of european maritime policies and calls for better governance through greater involvement in european decision-making. the success and relevance of this policy has been demonstrated over the last few years by the various initiatives financed in the form of preparatory actions and pilot projects. the integrated maritime policy should therefore continue to benefit from adequate funding during the next years of the current financial programming period. in this respect, i advocate adequate funding until 2013 not only to consolidate previous projects but also to establish a stable framework for the objectives of this programme. issues of policy, governance, sustainability and maritime surveillance are, for obvious reasons, issues of particular interest to some regions of the european union, such as the outermost regions. the octs are regions which, with the exception of french guiana, are small islands and depend on a small number of economic activities, and in which activities related to the sea and fishing are particularly important. the outermost regions also contribute to the european union's status as the world's largest exclusive economic zone. the outermost regions account for more than half of the european union's exclusive economic zone, some 15 million out of 25 million km2, and together with coastal regions, they are key to the economic growth of the european union and its member states. a programme such as the one under the integrated maritime policy should benefit these regions by giving priority to transnational coordination of maritime policies and relevant international cooperation. it is therefore necessary to ensure continuous and sufficient funding, not only for the next two years, but also and above all for the next financial framework, starting in 2014.
madam president, i cannot but take this opportunity, when we are talking about an integrated maritime policy, to underline the enormous potential that the atlantic and island dimension holds for the european union. the atlantic, as europe's western maritime frontier, also links it to the americas, north and south america and africa, giving europe a strategic dimension which is indispensable in the architecture of a future-oriented maritime policy. and it is with a view to the future that the integrated maritime policy, in addition to promoting the coordination of maritime activities, must put the potential of the atlantic in its three-dimensional dimension, based on science and technology, at the forefront of its priorities. the research of the mid-atlantic ridge, deep sea and seabed is a new frontier with potential in biotechnology and mineral resources and is of inestimable value to the knowledge economy. the union should therefore take advantage of the privileged position of the azores and the excellence of its oceanographic department to set up the deep sea observatory there.
madam president, the nature and specific features of the marine environment, the enormous diversity and increasing activity which is taking place in it today, and the need to regulate these activities by resolving potential conflicts in a socially and environmentally sustainable way, make it advisable to develop an integrated maritime policy to this end. the objectives, guiding principles and means of this policy will not, of course, be indifferent. we have serious reservations, and even disagreements, about the way the integrated maritime policy is being defined. the commission's proposal is based on a federalist approach to the imp, which disregards the sovereignty and powers of the member states over their territorial waters and exclusive economic zones and links it to the european union's foreign policy objectives. on the contrary, a maritime policy based on cooperation between member states, which naturally recognises the transboundary nature of the sea but respects the sovereignty and competences of states, promotes synergies, adds value and promotes the sustainable use and conservation of marine resources - this imp could undoubtedly have positive impacts.

in writing. - this report, by mr georgios koumoutsakos, concerns a proposal for a european parliament and council regulation establishing a programme to support the further development of the integrated maritime policy (imp). in 2007, the commission, advocating an integrated approach to ocean, sea and coastal management, presented the green paper on msy and the communication 'an integrated maritime policy for the european union' which formed the basis of european policy in this area. in the following years (2008-2010) the european parliament adopted a number of resolutions in this context and a number of initiatives were funded through preparatory actions and pilot projects. despite the financial crisis, it is essential that the eu continues to finance this imp in accordance with the marine and water framework directives. in addition, member states should pool synergies in order to share information and collaborate, taking into account the sustainable use and protection of marine and coastal resources. in this context, i am voting in favour of this report, which follows parliament's support on 21 october 2010 for the commission's intention to finance pmi with an amount of eur 50 million over the next two years.
in writing. − the integrated maritime policy (imp), as it has been put forward by the commission and defended by the majority of this parliament, is marked by a federalist, mercantilist and geo-strategic view of the use of the eezs of the member states. the report states that the strategic objectives of the imo include integrated maritime governance at all levels and it is well known that, from border control to the liberalisation of maritime transport, to security issues and the european coast guard, this policy has objectives with which we cannot agree. this report is about regulating a programme of support for the deepening of the mip, and at this stage its content does not reflect the dangerous negative aspects highlighted. however, these cannot be disregarded. the aim at this stage is to make it possible to finance studies on aspects such as the protection and preservation of the marine environment, or to support the formulation of policies relating to the sea or coastal areas, in particular in the fields of economic development, employment, environmental protection, research, maritime safety, energy and the development of green marine technologies. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect.
in writing. − the nature and specificities of the marine environment, the enormous diversity of activities taking place in it today (and the trend is increasing) and the need to regulate these activities by addressing potential conflicts in a socially and environmentally sustainable way, call for the development of an integrated maritime policy to this end. the objectives, guiding principles and means of this policy will not, of course, be indifferent. we have serious reservations and disagreements about the way the eu's integrated maritime policy is being defined. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to apply the principle of subsidiarity to the management of the fisheries sector. on the contrary, a maritime policy based on cooperation between member states, respecting their sovereignty and competences, promoting synergies, adding value and promoting the sustainable use and conservation of marine resources could undoubtedly have positive impacts.
in writing. - the approval of this eur 40 million for the deepening of the maritime policy is very important for the achievement of the objectives already defined. the eu's integrated maritime policy, established in 2007, advocates an integrated approach to the management and governance of oceans, seas, coastal areas, islands and outermost regions, and promotes the interaction of all eu policies related to the maritime domain, such as transport, fisheries, tourism, environmental protection and biodiversity. this regulation provides for a programme to provide a stable framework for the financing of a set of projects and initiatives from 2011 to 2013, the year in which the current financial perspectives (the eu's multiannual financial framework) end.
in writing. − the integrated maritime policy for the management and governance of oceans, seas and coasts allows all european policies related to the sea to be aggregated, thus promoting the adoption of comprehensive strategies. in a matter of such wide scope, a policy-refinement support programme must set clear objectives, establish transparent funding rules and involve all community actors in the decision-making process - even more so when the proposed funding amounts to eur 50 million for the period 2011-2013. in general, this is a worthwhile strategy, which takes the sea as a source of economic and environmental wealth and as a field that requires specific responses. i voted in favour of this measure.
in writing. − an integrated european maritime policy means an approach to the management and governance of the oceans, seas and coasts in the eu that takes into account a greater interaction between all sea-related policies at european level. a number of initiatives have already been carried out through preparatory actions and pilot projects with a maximum duration of two or three years. the purpose of the european parliament's proposal is to establish the programme in a stable framework capable of supporting it from 2011 to 2013. the agreement reached safeguards the european parliament's concerns about maintaining the programme with adequate funding, which guarantees eur 50 million for the current programming period.

in writing. − the open and neutral nature of the internet has been a driver for greater competitiveness, economic growth and innovation, resulting in extraordinary levels of development of online applications, content and services. in this context, the 2009 eu telecoms regulatory framework safeguards the principles of net neutrality and openness of the internet and promotes the ability of consumers to access and distribute information without discrimination as to the content, applications and services of their choice. unfortunately, some abusive business practices in traffic management, such as blocking access to skype, can call into question this principle of net neutrality. in this context, it is essential to uphold the minimum conditions necessary for internet neutrality, such as effective competition in electronic communications, transparency in traffic management and quality of service, as well as the ease for consumers to switch to a new provider that best meets their needs and preferences. in order to ensure that the internet can continue to provide high quality services in a framework which promotes and respects fundamental rights, i voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. we welcome the adoption of the following points of this resolution: - urges all member states not to adopt, sign or subsequently ratify a protocol under the convention on certain conventional weapons (ccw) allowing the use of cluster munitions which are prohibited under the ccw; - calls on all eu member states and candidate countries not party to the jcc to accede to it as a matter of urgency, and urges the signatory states to ratify the jcc as soon as possible; - calls on all eu member states that are not yet parties to the ccm but wish to reduce the humanitarian impact of cluster munitions to adopt strong and transparent measures pending their accession, including the adoption of a moratorium on the use, production and transfer of cluster munitions, and to start, as a matter of urgency, the destruction of stockpiles of cluster munitions; - calls on all eu member states that have signed the jcc to take every opportunity to encourage all states - including eu candidate countries that are not parties to the jcc - to accede to the convention as soon as possible.
in writing. - cluster munitions pose a serious risk to the civilian population due to their extensive lethal trail. in post-conflict situations, the use of such munitions has caused many serious injuries and deaths among the civilian population, as unexploded munitions are often found by children and other innocent people unaware of the danger. the support of the majority of eu member states for parliamentary initiatives and the work of civil society organisations was instrumental in the successful conclusion of the oslo process, which led to the entry into force of the convention on cluster munitions (cmf), whereas 22 eu member states are states parties to the cmf and 15 eu member states have not signed or ratified the cmf. the fmc prohibits states parties from using, developing, producing or otherwise acquiring, storing, retaining or transferring to another, directly or indirectly, and from aiding, abetting or inducing another to engage in an activity prohibited to a state party under the convention. we are therefore on the right track for the elimination of cluster munitions.

in writing. - i approve this resolution, recalling the oecd principles on taxation of electronic commerce adopted at the 1998 ottawa conference. according to these principles, rules on consumption taxes, such as vat, should imply that taxation is to take place in the territory where consumption takes place. in accordance with the provisions of directive 2008/8/ec, the oecd principles will apply in the european union as from 1 january 2015. i believe that a revision of vat legislation, by giving more flexibility to member states in the area of reduced vat rates, should go hand in hand with the application of the principles enshrined in directive 2008/8/ec. however, i would stress that in order to allow all member states to benefit equally from the digital single market, the principle of taxation in the member state of the customer should be implemented as soon as possible.

in writing. - i fully support this resolution, which, following the report on the modernisation of vat, presents another innovative initiative in the field of taxation. in particular, it concerns the paradigmatic case which still exists in the book industry, namely the difference between the vat rates applicable to the supply of books in physical format and those applicable to books in digital format. the latter do not currently benefit from the same reduced vat rates as the former, and a negative differentiation between the former and the latter still exists, which leads to a distortion of competition between the latter, with all the ensuing consequences. moreover, this negative differentiation does not occur on the other side of the atlantic, creating a real obstacle to european industry in this sector, making it impossible for it to grow.
in writing. the resolution calls for the creation of a digital single market where cultural, journalistic and creative content will be distributed. there are several contradictions in its general sense. in order to develop this market as widely and rapidly as possible, the commission proposes that these goods and services of cultural content, supplied by electronic means, should be subject to a temporary reduction in vat. we are in favour of the principle of subsidiarity, and therefore believe that the commission should not invade the competence of the member states, including in matters of indirect taxation, particularly as regards the setting of vat rates. this is what is happening through the so-called financial assistance programmes, which are in fact genuine aggression programmes, under the auspices of the imf and the eu, launched in countries such as portugal. there are now many direct and/or indirect pressures to generalize and perpetuate this interference, under the pretext, how often, of the so-called fiscal harmonizations, of which so much is said without touching on the content: harmonized by whom, in what form and in whose interest? each member state should be able to decide on the application of vat rates. moreover, this reduced vat rate should not be a temporary measure but a definitive one for such content.

in writing. - the inconsistency in the vat rules applicable to products sold in physical, electronic form is a matter of longstanding concern to the eu. given that member states may apply reduced vat to cultural goods by physical means in order to promote access to these products, it does not seem to me right that the same products, because they are sold online, should be treated differently. we are therefore talking about an aspect of the vat directive which is completely obsolete in the face of new consumer trends. it is therefore important that this point be revised so that there is no different vat just because the same products are sold through different distribution channels. this development, together with the copyright reform, will facilitate the free circulation of audiovisual content online, thus contributing to the creation and stimulation of a genuine digital internal market.

in writing. − equal treatment for men and women is a cause i have always embraced and continue to defend. we all have the same rights, but we cannot forget the differences that exist, particularly for women in terms of maternity protection and reconciling work and family life. the ep is a testament to equality between men and women, as there are many women in this house who stand out for the quality of their work, which is why i reiterate that i see no need for the implementation of any artificial mechanism to achieve this equality. competence is always having the last word.
in writing. - article 8 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union states that in all its actions, the union shall aim to eliminate inequalities and to promote equality between men and women. gender mainstreaming is thus one of the eu's principles, and there should be no discrimination between men and women in the conduct of the union's activities. this report aims to show that the ep must do more to integrate gender and that all its policies must reflect the needs, aspirations and experiences of all members of society. the femm committee takes a number of initiatives for the implementation and development of the gender perspective, including through the process of mainstreaming the gender perspective in amendments and the appointment of a gender perspective member in each committee. this makes it possible to monitor the way gender is taken into account in the legislative process of the parliament.
in writing. − illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing is a serious and growing problem worldwide that undermines conservation and stock management efforts in all types of capture fisheries, leads to the loss of economic and social opportunities in both the short and medium term, and has negative repercussions on food security and environmental protection. the european union has a special responsibility in combating iuu fishing, as it is the world's largest fish market and one of the major fishing powers. the objective of this regulation should therefore be to prevent, deter and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. the report makes the following recommendations to achieve this objective: to increase the capacity to investigate criminal activities at sea; to increase the transparency and traceability of fisheries in order to enable the detection of criminal activities and reduce the proceeds thereof; to monitor or, preferably, prohibit the sale of used vessels to companies of unidentifiable shipowners; to improve the monitoring of the activities of fishing vessels and their interaction with merchant ships. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - unfortunately, illegal fishing exists and has very negative and harmful effects on the formal economy at the global level, as well as on the sustainable preservation of our natural resources. the nature of the phenomenon of unreported fishing makes it impossible to estimate precisely the volume of catches and their economic value. however, it is estimated that the percentage is at least 15% of the total catches. in view of this, and because we all want to continue to eat wild fish in the future, it seems to me essential that the union, as the world's largest fish market and one of the world's largest fishing powers, should be an example for the rest of the world to follow. it is therefore imperative to ensure that fishing rights are subject to objective criteria of transparency of ownership of operations and catches. it is also essential that member states which do not comply with their obligations lose their fishing rights. there's still a lot to do. the report takes account of this. i therefore believe that it is possible to combat (organized or sporadic) crime in the fishing sector and to promote the formal, transparent and sustainable development of this activity through greater cooperation between the member states and at european level.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'fighting illegal fishing worldwide - the role of the eu', because illegal fishing can only be effectively tackled by strengthening international cooperation. the eu should make every effort to mobilise the international community to develop legal instruments, including in the world trade organisation, to prevent and punish illegal fishing, which accounts for some 15% of global annual catches, or an estimated 11 to 26 million tonnes of fish per year.
in writing. - illegal fishing is a phenomenon that threatens all the efforts made by the international community and the european union in particular to balance a strong and dynamic fishing industry with the necessary replenishment of fisheries resources. although it is not possible to have precise figures because of the illegal nature of fishing, recent studies have estimated that 11 to 26 million tonnes of fish are caught each year, and that 11 million would represent 15% of total marine catches. as portugal is a maritime and fishing country, it is very important to me that the eu takes all measures to protect fisheries and to prevent illegal fishing which harms everyone, and in particular the communities which are engaged in fishing as their main source of income.
in writing. - in essence, the report takes an approach which we believe is correct to the problem of illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. the role of multilateral organisations such as the un and fao in combating this practice, which is highly damaging to marine ecosystems, and the role of regional fisheries management organisations seem appropriate. in addition to the environmental consequences, this is a practice that also has extremely harmful economic and social consequences, in some cases with prolongations and links to organized crime. without prejudice to aspects which would merit further clarification, with regard to the fight against iuu fishing within the eu, an area in which we will certainly have some differences with the rapporteur's position, we value several of the proposals presented in the report, some of them innovative (for example, with regard to the marketing states and others). but we cannot but point out that the amendments proposed by the ppe, and approved, on the creation of a european coastguard with surveillance, inspection and combating what they consider to be future threats at sea such as terrorism and piracy are profoundly negative. these are regrettable amendments which clearly go beyond the scope of the report and destroy the consensus which had been reached in committee.
in writing. - fishing is a global activity, as is its illegal component. illegal, unregulated and unreported fishing causes significant damage to a common heritage of humanity, which includes the oceans and their vast, albeit finite, resources. it is estimated that at least 15% of the total catch volume is accounted for, although in reality it may be much higher. the conservation of this heritage is unequivocally a common task and responsibility of humanity. for this reason, it is a priority to consider combating illegal fishing within the framework of international cooperation established between multilateral organisations such as the fao. the fao agreement on measures to be implemented by port states, the united nations fish stocks agreement, the fao agreement to promote compliance and the united nations convention on the law of the sea thus gain particular prominence. but we disagree with the creation of the european coast guard proposed by the epp. these are amendments which clearly go beyond the scope of the report and the debate which took place during its preparation. the commission has also proposed a number of amendments which are far from consensual, unlike the majority of the other measures proposed in the report, some of which are innovative.
in writing. − the fight against illegal fishing is of great importance as it represents one of the most serious threats to ocean biodiversity and a source of unfair competition for fishermen who respect the rules in force. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat illegal fishing, including by strengthening inspections at sea, blocking access to markets for these products and imposing sanctions on countries that fail to comply. the volume of catches from illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing has been estimated at between 11 and 26 million tonnes per year, equivalent to at least 15% of global catches, making sustainable management of the world's marine resources economically, socially and environmentally unfeasible. the fight against iuu fishing requires, in order to be effective, international cooperation and a comprehensive exchange of information on fishing vessels, their activities and catches.
in writing. the vast majority of the surface of the oceans (two thirds) is not under the jurisdiction of states. to this extent, problems such as global fisheries require integrated responses from the various states, since, in isolation, they have no capacity to react. in this context, the european union should play a leading role by providing itself with the necessary instruments to combat illegal fishing and by strengthening cooperation with international organisations capable of carrying out control and surveillance activities with a broad supporting base. the existence of a fair competitive market depends on fisheries regulation, but also, and above all, on the very sustainability of certain fish species and the balance of the ecosystem. i voted in favour of this measure.
in writing. - the issue of illegal fishing is one of the european union's major concerns in the fisheries policy. despite the difficulty of determining the volume of illegal fishing, it is estimated to be between 11 and 26 million tonnes per year. the european union has a particular responsibility in this area, as it is one of the world's major fishing powers and the largest market. the european parliament has therefore supported a number of proposals concerning initiatives in international organisations, the strengthening of transparency and the eu's role in this area, as well as cooperation between member states and the fight against organised crime in order to help improve the problem of illegal fishing.

the crisis in the euro area, including its expression in sovereign debt, has structural and other more cyclical causes. the first concerns the way in which the uneven development of capitalism, which is characteristic of the eu, is expressed; the asymmetric interdependence, which relegates the peripheral countries, with weaker economies, to a subordinate and unfavourable position in the process of the international division of labour. in this process, their production systems are dismantled and, as a result, they increase external dependence, miscellaneous deficits and external debt. the second concerns the conditions created for financial speculators, as other speculative bubbles were drying up or bursting, to focus on sovereign debt. the free movement of capital, tax havens, derivative financial products and the speculative practices associated with them, the absence of taxation of financial transactions, the role assigned to rating agencies - all this creates the framework which allows speculation on sovereign debts to make its way. summit after summit, debate after debate, these causes remain untouched. this is the fundamental question that has been avoided in this debate by both the commission and the majority of this parliament. worse, they take steps to deepen some of these causes.

the rapporteur. - first of all, let me thank all those who have worked with me on the budgets of parliament and the other institutions. i thank the political groups and the shadow rapporteurs for their work, i thank them for the excellent cooperation, the excellent work, the result and the work we have done with the commission and the council presidency. i would also like to stress the excellent cooperation and work we have had with parliament's bureau, the support of the secretariat of the committee on budgets. i would like to highlight the cooperation of the epp staff and, in particular, the excellent technical work of the adviser, nicole witts. i also note the rigorous work that all the institutions have done in their administrative budgets, despite the costs of croatia's accession, the entry of 18 new members, the existence of new institutions, the consolidation of others, such as the european external action service, the new tasks and competences. despite all this, the updating of the administrative and operating budgets of all the institutions of the european union is only 1.3%. in the face of inflation and new commitments, this has only been possible through strict, efficient management and structural changes. for 2012, the administrative budget of the institutions has a negative growth. i welcome the results of the conciliation meeting on friday, 18 november, on the budgets of the european parliament and the other institutions. the council approved the european parliament's proposal in its entirety on the administrative and operating expenditure of all the european institutions, recognising the rigour and fairness of our proposal. the rigorous work, the austerity and the balance between budget cuts on the one hand and the minimum necessary for the proper functioning of each institution on the other have paid off. there's one thing you should always remember. all administrative and operating expenditure of all the institutions of the european union corresponds to less than 6% of the budget of the european union. this means that more than 94% of the union budget is for investment. it should also be remembered that the budget of the european union, although it represents only 1% of the union's gross domestic product, has a major leverage effect, an added value, allowing for coordinated solidarity. that is why this budget should be strengthened, especially in times of crisis like this. i therefore welcome the increase in funds for economic growth, training, research and youth, and i also express the council's concern and concern: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
the 2012 draft budget will not meet the needs. my opinion differs from commissioner lewandowski's. in research, ecological sustainability, territorial cohesion and social solidarity, this budget has no power to compensate for or correct the national austerity policies that are being pursued across europe. this is a budget which does not recognise europe's return to recession, unemployment and widespread insecurity among the younger generations. a budget of less than 1% of gdp, really less than in 2011, is a minimal budget for a minimal europe. it's business as usual. to mitigate this evidence, the proposal decided to add or increase the divergence between commitments and payments. in other words, it covers up a bad budget with a bad budgetary practice. alternatively, negative investment priorities could have been defined more clearly, freeing up resources for positive ones, but in this budget, expenditure on security and military research is being increased, frontex is being strengthened, funds are being increased for the large multinationals, export support is being maintained which is ruinous for the developing countries. i conclude by saying that schizophrenia has taken over. we all talk about more and better europe, but in the end we always decide on less europe.
the negotiating process with the council has brought us the expected result: what was already short, very short, has been cut again. the usual ritual will follow: self-styled europeans of various shades, who here clap their hands at the chest saying that a strong budget is important for growth and development, are preparing, without blushing, to vote in favour of this proposal. a final proposal that is less than 1% of the community's gross income and that will represent a decrease in the community budget in real terms compared to the previous year. at the same time as tightening the noose on instruments such as the stability pact, which freeze or even deepen inequalities between member states, they reduce to almost nothing the redistributive function of the budget, which would be essential to reduce these inequalities. all this is greatly aggravated by the interventions in the countries which are victims of the imf and the european union programmes. more than dead letter in the treaties, the claimed cohesion is thus increasingly a big lie. it is also against this great lie that a current of protest and struggle is growing outside europe.
