in writing. the report, drawn up by tadeusz zwiefka, concerns the request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of the greek mep georgios toussas, following the letter from the judge of the court of first instance of piraeus, athens, greece. the prosecutor's office accuses the mep of having embezzled more than €147,000, along with eight other people, as manager of the merchant navy seamen's pension fund. georgios toussas, at his hearing before the committee on legal affairs, claimed that this accusation took the form of political persecution, which was not confirmed by the said committee. in view of the recommendation of the committee on legal affairs and whilst all the accused are considered innocent until the sentence has been passed, i am voting in favour of this proposal to waive the parliamentary immunity of georgios toussas, as it is essential for the credibility of the ep that there is no corporatism whatsoever among us.
in writing. - the defence of the independence of the mandate of a member of the european parliament is the competence of the european parliament and this independence cannot be called into question. in the present case, the court of first instance of piraeus, section 7, requested the waiver of the immunity of georgios toussas, member of the european parliament, in order to allow him to open criminal proceedings initiated following instructions issued by the public prosecutor's office of the court of first instance of piraeus, concerning an alleged breach of trust involving damages exceeding eur 147 000 (article 390 of the greek criminal code and article 1 of law 1608/1950) as well as a judicial inquiry (articles 246, 248 and 250 of the greek code of criminal procedure). the judge intends to summon georgios toussas to testify as a defendant in this case and to respond to the above-mentioned charge, pursuant to articles 270, 271 and 273 of the greek code of criminal procedure. it is therefore advisable to recommend that parliamentary immunity be waived in this case, hence my vote.
in writing. - the european parliament was asked to waive the parliamentary immunity of mr georgios toussas. the committee on legal affairs and citizens' rights has taken a position on the matter and unanimously adopted a report in which it decided to waive parliamentary immunity. indeed, it was considered that there was no basis for the allegation of fumus persecutionis in the present case.
in writing. − the request for the waiver of parliamentary immunity was requested by the greek court of first instance in order to initiate a judicial procedure concerning the alleged breach of confidence, with evidence of fraud. this type of procedure is in accordance with the rules laid down in the rules of procedure of the european parliament. the member stated in the committee on legal affairs that this case was a political persecution, a fact for which the committee found no evidence. that is why, in the light of this report, i am in favour of the waiver of parliamentary immunity.

in writing. the report, drawn up by bernhard rapkay, deals with the request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of italian mep luigi de magistris. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. bagnoliafutura spa accuses the member of parliament of posting on its website statements blaming it for delays and waste of public funds, for inaction and inefficiency, and for engaging in an activity which it classifies as a combination of politics and delinquency. lugi de magistris defended himself by arguing that he had disseminated information relating to a written question to the european commission concerning irregularities found by the commission and the alleged waste of public funds. the facts of the case show that the information published by luigi de magistris has a direct and obvious link with the performance of his duties as a member of the european parliament and, having regard to article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union, i am voting in favour of the defence of luigi de magistris's privileges and immunities.
in writing. - the defence of the independence of the mandate of a member of the european parliament is the competence of the european parliament and this independence cannot be called into question. the request by luigi de magistris concerns a summons against him before the court of naples on behalf of bagnolifutura spa, a company established in naples with activities in the fields of soil design and decontamination, relating to press releases which he has authored and which are published on his website. the notices in question were published on the website of luigi de magistris at a time when he was a member of the european parliament following the 2009 european elections. those press releases by luigi de magistris disclosed information relating to a supplementary written question to the european commission, in which he requested additional information on irregularities found by the commission in may 2009 in the field of public procurement. since luigi de magistris also requested additional information on the alleged waste of public funds in the naples area, where the activities of the company bagnolifutura are carried out, by publishing those press releases, luigi de magistris was acting in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament. i hereby agree to uphold the privileges and immunities of luigi de magistris.
in writing. - the european parliament was asked to waive the parliamentary immunity of luigi de magistris. the committee on legal affairs and citizens' rights has taken a position on the matter and unanimously adopted a report in which it decided not to waive parliamentary immunity. it was considered that mr de magistris was in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament when he made the statements which gave rise to the criminal proceedings. the attempt to prevent members of the european parliament from expressing their views on matters of public interest by instituting legal proceedings is not acceptable in a democratic society. i voted in favour of defending the freedom of expression of members in the exercise of their duties and defending the interest of the european parliament as an institution.

in writing. − council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 did not define the financial assistance granted by member states to beneficiaries as being reimbursable or non-reimbursable. in order to clarify the doubts regarding the eligibility of certain types of support, in august 2011 the european commission (ec) presented the proposal amending council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 as regards repayable assistance and financial engineering, clarifying the eligibility of repayable assistance and defining the information obligations in the field of financial instruments. this report will enable member states to grant support to the various entities on the type of repayable aid, allowing the structural funds to be used several times throughout the programming period. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 as regards repayable assistance and financial engineering, because i agree with the general objective of the proposal and believe that most of its elements are beyond doubt. i also agree that legal clarity and certainty on repayable aid and financial engineering instruments should be safeguarded.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i think it is a good thing that, in the current crisis, some additional flexibility is being introduced in the use of the structural funds. in this sense, i believe that the commission's proposal is a step in the right direction in allowing some of these funds to be used to co-finance repayable aid.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1260/1999 defines the different types of assistance that may be provided by way of structural fund contributions. the proposal we are adopting today seeks to amend this regulation to incorporate into its text a widely established practice of co-financing repayable aid with the structural funds. it also confirmed that the provisions on large projects, revenue-generating projects and the sustainability of operations do not apply to financial engineering instruments. this is a clarifying proposal which improves legal certainty and security.
in writing. - colleague danuta maria hübner has presented us with a report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 as regards repayable assistance and financial engineering. good administrative and financial practices, when they promote results at the level of excellence, should lead to the adoption of innovative methodologies and reforming regulations which, although adopted with the best of intentions, do not always meet the objectives for which they were created. the commission proposal under examination aims to clarify, following the opinions of the european court of auditors, the legality of a practice introduced in the 2000-06 programming period under regulation (ec) no 1260/1999 but in breach of regulation (ec) no 1083/2006. it is therefore imperative that the new regulation should include, among the financial engineering instruments, the repayable aid which proved extremely positive in the previous community framework.
in writing. - this report deals with the amendment of a regulation which does not provide for whether aid from the structural funds can be reimbursed or not. this amendment introduces the concept of a repayable grant, as a direct financial contribution by way of a donation, which may be fully or partially reimbursable and interest-free. this makes it possible for the structural funds to finance operational expenditure, including through contributions to repayable grants, and clarifies that such grants, which are reimbursable to the body granting the support, or to another competent public authority in the member state, must be kept in a separate account and reused for the same purposes or in line with the objectives of the operational programme. the commission proposal also lays down the obligations to provide information and to provide appropriate follow-up in the field of financial engineering instruments. the rapporteur proposes, as seems appropriate, to accept the general objectives of the commission proposal, although restricting the additional information obligations of the member states.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1260/1999 defines the different types of assistance that may be provided by way of structural fund contributions. member states introduced these arrangements in the 2000-2006 programming period by creating specific funds and granting aid reimbursable by other instruments. on the contrary, council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 does not define aid as repayable or non-repayable. the repayable aid is apparently not covered by that regulation. however, member states continued to use this type of aid, thanks to the good experience of the previous programming period. the commission itself approved programming documents containing descriptions of the schemes in question. it is therefore necessary to provide in regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 that the structural funds may co-finance repayable aid. the aim is therefore to make an established practice legally possible.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's position adopted at first reading on 1 december 2011 with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the previous legislation on repayable assistance, financial engineering and certain provisions on declaration of expenditure. i did so because the general objective of the proposal is correct and most of its elements are beyond doubt.
in writing. − the proposal, which aims to amend council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 as regards repayable assistance and financial engineering, aims to clarify that the structural funds can co-finance repayable assistance. this is a practice which has been followed by european legal practitioners and this amendment is justified in that it is positive for customary law and therefore offers advantages in terms of the familiarity of union law. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 does not define the financial assistance granted by member states to beneficiaries as being reimbursable or non-reimbursable, and there are doubts as to the eligibility of some types of support to be granted. this is all the more important when, in the current programming period, several member states have continued to use the non-repayable financial aid modality. in august 2011, the european commission (ec) presented the proposal amending council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 as regards repayable assistance and financial engineering, clarifying the eligibility of repayable assistance and defining information obligations in the field of financial instruments. i agree with this report, because i think it is good that the member states give support to the most diverse entities on the type of reimbursable aid, and can thus take advantage of the structural funds several times throughout the programming period.
in writing. − i approve this report and all necessary and exceptional measures to support member states in difficulty in coping with the current financial crisis. the crisis is now spreading to all the member states and is reaching levels that were unimaginable until very recently. we need policies to stimulate investment that leads to growth and employment, without which we will never be able to control sovereign debt. however, in the present situation of lack of liquidity in the banks and public finances of the member states involved, only the european funds can promote such investment. but with weakened public finances, the absorption capacity of funds is reduced, so the reduction now introduced in national co-financing needs will make a valuable contribution to improving the socio-economic and financial situations in these countries.
in writing. − in august 2011, the european commission (ec) presented the proposal to amend council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 as regards certain provisions relating to the financial management of certain member states affected or threatened by serious difficulties in financial stability, namely greece, hungary, ireland, latvia, portugal and romania. eur 629 million will be made available to portugal, which represents an advance on the financial amount of cohesion policy for the period 2007-13. the increase of 10 percentage points in the co-financing rate will benefit portugal as this increase will help inject money into the national economy, help the business fabric, especially smes, and contribute to job creation. i therefore support this report.
in writing. − in the current economic and financial crisis, it is important to ensure the proper implementation of cohesion policy programmes as an instrument for injecting funds into the economy. however, the implementation of the programmes is a problem, especially for the member states most affected by the crisis and which have received financial assistance under the emff. i welcome the commission's proposal to make payments to these countries while they are still benefiting from the support mechanisms, without changing the total allocation of cohesion policy for the period 2007-13. this will provide additional financial resources to member states at this critical juncture and facilitate the continued implementation of programmes on the ground.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis and the economic recession that the world and europe are experiencing have led to a deterioration of financial, economic and social conditions in several member states, including portugal, leading to a reduction in the financial resources available for financing public investments. i welcome the european commission's proposal to provide additional financial assistance through cohesion policy to member states which are currently facing serious difficulties in managing their deficits, such as my own country, thus allowing the continuation of the implementation of programmes which were threatened by the economic situation. i share the rapporteur's view that the retroactivity of these measures to increase the co-financing rate by 10 points is of strategic importance, and i think that the agreement reached is balanced, since it sets time limits and eligibility criteria which are without prejudice to the future multiannual financial framework. i am convinced that this amendment to regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 will be of key help to the member states most affected by the crisis, relieving the pressure on their national budgets and laying the foundations for a genuine cohesion policy among eu member states.
in writing. − member states that have undergone stabilisation/financial assistance programmes are currently facing major difficulties in financing their public investments. the enormous fiscal consolidation effort they are subject to and the lack of liquidity in their economies threaten to stop a significant body of public investment with strong community support. if the eu were to allow this to happen, not only would these countries not receive some of the community support to which they are entitled, but it would also make it more difficult for their economies to recover. i therefore voted in favour of the report because i regard the proposal to increase community co-financing as very positive.
in writing. − at a time when positive signals from the european institutions are needed to stem the financial crisis, it is important to approve the proposal to amend council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 (general regulation) to provide additional financial resources to eu member states facing serious financial difficulties. this amendment allows the co-financing rates for eu funds for portugal, greece, ireland, romania, latvia and hungary to be increased to cover 95% of the total costs of projects that strengthen competitiveness, growth and employment.
in writing. - i welcome the european parliament's approval of this proposal, which allows for the interim payments under the structural funds and the cohesion fund to be increased by 10 percentage points above the actual co-financing rate for each priority axis in the case of member states facing serious difficulties in financial stability and having requested to benefit from this measure. the member states eligible for this measure are euro area countries that have received financial assistance under a european financial stabilisation mechanism (efsm) programme and non-euro area countries that have received financial assistance under the european balance of payments facility. this provision shall therefore apply retroactively to portugal, ireland, greece and portugal with effect from the day on which financial assistance has been granted to them in accordance with article 77 (2). it shall also apply to hungary, latvia and romania from 1 january 2010. cohesion policy funds can thus be 95% european co-financed. the overwhelming majority of the european parliament voted in favour of this report. i hope the council will do the same.
in writing. - the national effort required, together with the restrictions on public investment imposed under the pretext of the stability pact, has long compromised the full use of community funds by the economically weaker countries which would need them most. the imf-eu programmes have significantly aggravated this picture, pushing investment - public and private - to historically low levels. the commission's proposal to increase community co-financing (erdf and esf) for the countries facing the greatest difficulties, with a corresponding reduction in national effort, has thus long been felt to be a necessity and unfortunately comes too late. but it should be noted that this proposal does not increase - as it should - the budget available to each of the countries in difficulty. on the contrary, the practical result, due to the reduction in national effort, will be a reduction in the overall value of investment planned in the areas concerned: social areas and regional development. the growth and development prospects opened up by the investments made will therefore be further reduced. the objective of cohesion is thus compromised. the commission must therefore consider the possibility of actually increasing the community funds available to these countries. in addition to the abolition of the irrational criteria of the stability pact, freeing up the necessary public investment.

in writing. - the present report, by danuta maria hübner, concerns the proposal for a council decision amending decision 2002/546/ec as regards its period of application which expired on 31 december 2011. the abovementioned decision, which falls within the framework of article 349 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), provides for special measures to support the eu's outermost regions in order to help them overcome economic disadvantages resulting from their geographical situation. the canary islands are among the regions considered to be the outermost regions. the global economic and financial crisis had a serious impact on tourism in the canary islands and caused a significant increase in unemployment in the region, which rose from 17,3% in 2008 to 26,2% in 2009, prompting the spanish government to request the european commission to extend the period of application of decision 2002/546/ec by two years. in this context, i am voting in favour of extending the period of application of decision 2002/546/ec to local products from the canary islands for a further two years, i.e. until 31 december 2013, the date on which the guidelines on national regional aid for 2007-2013 expire.
in writing. − the eu's outermost regions are affected by a number of structural factors affecting their social and economic situation and development, such as remoteness, insularity, small size, difficult topography and climate, and economic dependence on a small number of products. for this reason, these regions should be given special attention. among other things, special conditions for the application of sectoral legislation and policies should be defined. this applies, of course, to all the outermost regions, including the azores and madeira, although the measures approved here only concern the canary islands. council decision 2002/546/ec authorises spain to apply, until 31 december 2011, exemptions or reductions from the tax known as aiem to a list of products manufactured locally in the canary islands. the aim is now, at the request of the spanish government, to extend the period of application of these measures. the commission and the rapporteur propose that spain's request be granted, which deserves our agreement. in addition to the protection of local production in the outermost regions, measures are needed to protect national production, particularly in member states with weaker economies, as in the case of portugal. we have already made proposals to that effect.

in writing. − in the current economic context, the role of the european central bank is hotly debated, as with price stability as its primary objective and, consequently, financial stability and adequate liquidity in markets, much can still be done to help the eu's economic recovery. in addition to the ecb's increasingly active role in crisis management, notably in the summer of 2011, the report envisages a number of scenarios to be explored by the eu, such as the creation of a european finance minister, the creation of a european treasury, a european monetary fund, increased ecb intervention alongside the commission and the imf in the countries involved, among other proposals currently under discussion in the eu. this report therefore goes beyond a mere analysis of the ecb's role and activity throughout 2010 and makes concrete proposals.
in writing. − the european central bank, established on 1 june 1998, is the european union institution responsible for the monetary policy of the economic and monetary union. its main objectives are to preserve the purchasing power of the euro and to ensure price stability in its area. the importance of the euro is unquestionable, and without it the global financial crisis would have been much worse for most european countries. we have only recently seen how their intervention can calm the markets. in view of the crisis the eu is going through, it is more than ever essential to have a strong and stable euro if the single market and the movement of people and goods is to be a success. in fact, it was not the euro that failed. what has failed is the governance of the euro area, especially the failure to comply with the stability and growth pact. i believe that the ecb has maintained a balanced and constructive stance, making appropriate use of the mechanisms at its disposal, in particular the issuance of money, seeking to keep markets stable and exercising supervision at the macro level. i therefore voted in favour of the ecb's annual report for 2010.
in writing. - what we have been denouncing for a long time has become very clear this year: the ecb's false independence. as speculators focused on the sovereign debt of the states, charging quick interest on their necessary financing, the ecb financed the banks at interest rates several times lower than those which the banks later charged to the states. with this genuine mechanism of extortion, thus fuelled by the ecb, the banks, especially the big banks of the great powers, have won, but the states, especially those with weaker economies, and the people have lost. this mechanism is now complemented by the purchase of debt on the secondary market, thus alleviating the exposure of the same banks to debt securities of countries in difficulty (potentially toxic assets). this is how the banks' backs are kept warm, encouraging the extortion of states and peoples to continue. all this requires a fundamental change in the ecb's statutes, guidelines and false autonomy, guaranteeing the equal presence of the states in its management, in order to ensure effective political control by its member states. the report ignores all this and endorses the role and the intervention that the ecb has been developing. that is why we voted against it.

in writing. − the presentation of the european central bank's annual report 2010 recalls the difficult problems that the european union has been facing for some months now. the rapporteur points out with undeniable relevance the successes that have been achieved despite recent events. in fact, monetary union seems to have been the basis for the success of the single market, providing the conditions for a comprehensive system of free intermediation in trade. it also allowed the introduction of mechanisms for correcting and monitoring the public accounts of the member states, albeit weak ones, which seems to be the source of the current disturbances. however, despite the control instruments provided, there is a lack of a central governance mechanism, which led to the ecb's intervention. it is noted, for example, that since its introduction, there have been dozens of violations of the stability and growth pact, including by france and germany. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution, taking into account what is most fundamental about it: a genuine common budgetary policy.

in writing. - early school leaving is a complex phenomenon and represents a major challenge for europe. the europe 2020 strategy has set as one of its priority objectives the reduction of school drop-out by 10% by 2020. school failure cannot be assessed in isolation, as it is intrinsically linked to phenomena such as poverty, migration and family situation and has social and economic implications that have been shown to be extremely serious. this report proposes a set of major measures and initiatives to reduce this phenomenon, it being estimated that reducing the number of young people leaving school early in europe by 1% would create over half a million qualified young people every year. in this respect, it is crucial that the present approach is student-centred, with a view to offering wider choice, promoting mobility between different aspects of education, improving pupil/teacher ratios and reintegrating young people who have left school. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that these measures can help to combat early school leaving.

in writing. the report, drawn up by gay mitchel, is one of four texts adopted in a somewhat controversial conciliation procedure on codecision between the european parliament and the council. the joint text approved by the conciliation committee for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1905/2006 establishes a financing instrument for development cooperation (dci). in a tight financial framework such as the one we are in due to the economic and financial crisis, the development cooperation appropriations are not the ideal way to support more countries, more students and implement measures to combat poverty and social exclusion. i welcome the adoption of this report, which i voted in favour of, as it is essential that we continue to work towards eradicating poverty, in line with the millennium development goals (mdgs) and the europe 2020 strategy. it is also important that these funds motivate people to respect human rights, to comply with the rules set by the international labour organisation (ilo) and to contribute to the reduction of co2 by combating climate change.
in writing. the conciliation procedure resulted in parliament's backing down from the council's positions. the report is critical of the council's position, but accepts it in the name of compromise, on the condition that this procedure does not constitute a precedent for the future. we do not dismiss this debate on delegated acts, which has been dragging on since the beginning of the discussion of this report. but more than this is at stake in the discussion on the development cooperation instrument (dci). in particular, because financial instruments are inseparable from the policy objectives they serve, there is a need to reflect more deeply on a fundamental question: the guiding principle of eu development cooperation and aid policy. and here we have to take account not only of quantitative aspects, such as the amount of funding - which takes time to meet the commitments made - but also, and this is no less important, of qualitative aspects. the commission has tried to impose free trade agreements (the so-called epas) on developing countries, despite their many resistance, and has even made part of present and future aid conditional, explicitly or implicitly, on such agreements, in an unacceptable act of blackmail.

in writing. the proposal aims to make compulsory the collection of data by type of goods for road transport statistics by standardising the type of information collected and processed in the 27 member states. i am convinced that the commission is right to take the initiative in this matter.
in writing. − the objectivity of statistics as a branch of applied mathematics gives it a special status both in the field of scientific research and in public and private organisations. no government can do without a body responsible for statistical studies. the eu itself has the statistical office of the european communities (eurostat). in an ever-expanding area where the road is playing a decisive role in the transport of goods, reliable data are essential to inform all studies in this area, which are only possible with statistics. this report, by brian simpson, concerns the recasting of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on statistical surveys of the carriage of goods by road in the eu. in view of the opinion of the consultative group of the legal services of the ep, the council and the commission that this proposal does not involve any substantive changes, but merely codifies existing acts, i am voting in favour.
in writing. - in its proposal to recast the regulation on statistical surveys of road freight transport, the commission intends to extend its delegated powers. the rapporteur rightly considers that the scope of the proposed delegation of power is too broad. it is therefore proposed to restrict this scope, with the concern, of course, that the financial burden imposed on respondents and member states will also be restricted. this regulation ensures that community provisions are clear and easy to understand, particularly as regards statistical data on vehicles, journeys and goods. member states shall transmit to eurostat on a quarterly basis the individual data, duly verified, corresponding to the variables mentioned. the proposed approach is identical to the approach for the recently approved statistical information on tourism, which seems appropriate to us. the usefulness of having reliable statistics to support the formulation of sectoral public policies is thus balanced by the absence of overburdening the respondents.

in writing. − the kaliningrad region of the russian federation became an enclave within the european union following the enlargement of the eu in 2004, and since then all its links with neighbouring countries have been considerably restricted. in recent years, there have been several initiatives in the eu that have facilitated the movement of kaliningrad residents. however, taking into account the specific geographical situation of kaliningrad, these initiatives have proven insufficient in responding to the marginalization of kaliningrad and its residents. i welcome the european commission's proposal to amend the regulation on small border traffic in response to an exceptional situation.
in writing. − the kaliningrad region is characterised by a very specific geographical situation, as it became the only enclave in the eu after the 2004 enlargement, being entirely surrounded by two eu member states. it is therefore of fundamental importance in terms of cooperation and exchange in the baltic sea area, and it is important to ensure that the eu's borders do not serve as an obstacle to economic, regional, social and cultural cooperation with these neighbouring countries. while there is a 2007 eu-russia agreement on visa facilitation, the small border movement regulation provides for greater facilities that are more in line with the specific needs of regular, or even daily, movement of people living in a border area. i consider this proposal to be essential from the point of view of crossborder cooperation developed under the european neighbourhood policy, which will undoubtedly contribute to promoting the strategic partnership between the eu and russia and to improving neighbourly relations between the two. it should be noted, however, that this was a unique solution to the exceptional situation in the kaliningrad region and that it is by no means a precedent.
in writing. - the present kaliningrad region - part of what was formerly east prussia - is a russian enclave within the european union. in order to avoid the isolation of its population, it is proposed to facilitate the movement of its inhabitants by derogating from certain rules contained in the schengen borders code - amending regulation (ec) no 1931/2006 to that effect - and their access to the neighbouring polish regions. the peculiar situation of that russian region seems to justify the exceptional nature of these measures and to favour dialogue with one of the union's most important partners, so i give my consent to their adoption.
in writing. − one of the greatest successes in european history was the schengen agreement, which, by abolishing internal borders, facilitated the movement of people within the territories of the signatory states and promoted trade and tourism. this freedom of movement, however, entails great responsibilities for the states and requires them to coordinate their activities. the success of this agreement is such that some countries which have not joined the european union have signed it. in order to regulate the control of persons crossing the external borders, a regulation called the schengen borders code (sbc) has been adopted. the small kaliningrad province of the russian federation is surrounded by two member states and has been the only eu enclave since the 2004 enlargement, and should therefore be included as a small crossborder traffic area in the sfs, which will favour the strategic partnership between the eu and the russian federation. i therefore vote in favour of the report by mr kyriacos triantaphyllides on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1931/2006 by welcoming the inclusion of the kaliningrad region and some polish administrative districts of the border area in the schengen agreement.
in writing. − the kaliningrad region, an enclave of the russian federation on the baltic sea coast, has all its land borders with eu countries (poland and lithuania) following enlargement in 2004. there has since been a considerable curtailment of all its ties with neighbouring countries. the eu has taken initiatives in recent years to facilitate the movement of kaliningrad residents, such as the facilitated transit document and the facilitated rail transit document. these initiatives have simplified travel between kaliningrad and mainland russia. an agreement between the ec and the russian federation on visa facilitation was also concluded in 2007, which facilitates the issuance of short-stay visas to all russian nationals travelling to the schengen area countries. however, taking into account the specific geographical situation of kaliningrad, these initiatives have proven insufficient in responding to the marginalization of kaliningrad and its residents. therefore, both poland and the russian federation requested amendments to the regulation on small border traffic, taking into account the specific situation of the kaliningrad region. this report thus seeks to provide an answer - which we believe is appropriate and positive - to a problem which persists.

in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1391/2006 of the european parliament and of the council, which lays down rules for short-distance border traffic at the external borders of the member states, allows for a derogation from the rules on border control for neighbouring states, and in these exceptional cases, visa, proof of sufficient means of subsistence and proof of the purpose of entry are not required. this derogation from the regulation is based on the concern to ensure good relations between peoples, without breaking the links (economic, social and cultural) between the different communities, which have a secular tradition. this is the case of the kaliningrad region (german: königsberg), which was part of the soviet union between 1945 and 1992 and since then of the russian federation, and which has a natural border with the baltic sea and a territorial border with poland and lithuania. it is also justified to extend the size of the border zone to a total of 50 km (against a rule of 30 km), in order to avoid a breakdown of a regime which is intended to be single by several artificial zones. i therefore voted in favour, hoping that the agreement would help to facilitate relations between the two areas, which had been made more difficult by the enlargement of 2004.

in writing. - it is very important that members of the european parliament exercise their mandates in full independence and transparency. it is therefore welcome that a code of conduct has been adopted which aims to safeguard independence, transparency and avoid conflicts of interest, as is the case in many other sectors of activity, including in several professions which have their own codes of ethics which require healthy self-regulation.
in writing. the report, drawn up by mr carlo casini, deals with amendments to the rules of procedure of the european parliament concerning the code of conduct for members of the european parliament on financial interests and conflicts of interest. the current economic and financial crisis, which many citizens attribute to the wrong decisions of politicians, has placed this profession under very close public scrutiny, which is not unknown to new information technologies, such as wikileaks with the disclosure of confidential information. it is more important than ever that rules on transparency be established in relation to the financial interests of those holding public office. in the case of meps, under article 232 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, it is for the ep to lay down the rules relating to the interests of its members. i am aware that it is not enough to be caesar's wife, you have to look like one, and i am voting in favour of the proposed amendments to the current rules.
in writing. the report essentially considers that the new code of conduct will increase the transparency required for the performance of the duties of elected members of the european parliament. meps will have to submit a declaration of financial interests containing a range of information, including their professional activities in the three years prior to taking up their duties in the ep, among other things. this report follows a number of scandals involving members of the current parliament, some of whom have since resigned. hence the concerns now referred to. we naturally agree with the prohibition on accepting or receiving 'any direct or indirect financial advantage or any other form of reward in return for exercising influence or voting on legislation, motions for resolutions, written statements or questions tabled in parliament or in one of its committees'. the code states that members may not enter into 'any agreement which leads them to act or vote in the interest of a third party, whether natural or legal, which could jeopardise the freedom to vote'. it will be important to assess and monitor its effectiveness.
in writing. - it is stated that the new code of conduct is mainly aimed at increasing transparency. meps will have to submit a declaration of financial interests containing a range of information, including professional activities in the three years before taking up their seats in the ep, participation in committees or boards of directors of companies during the same period, etc. occasional paid outside activities, including writing, lecturing or consulting, will also have to be declared if the remuneration exceeds eur 5 000 per year. we know that this report comes after a number of scandals involving some members who have left the ep. hence the concerns now referred to. for example, the code states that meps may not enter into 'any agreement which leads them to act or vote in the interest of a third party, whether natural or legal, which could compromise the freedom to vote'. they may also not accept or receive 'any direct or indirect financial advantage or any other consideration in return for the exercise of influence or a vote on legislation, motions for resolutions, written statements or questions tabled in parliament or in one of its committees'. we'll see how effective it is.
in writing. - the recent events involving some meps and leading to the resignation of some of them have forced the european parliament to adopt some amendments to the code of conduct for its members. these aim to enhance transparency in the exercise of the mandate and the freedom to vote. the amendments also provide for penalties for breaches of the rules laid down, which may include suspension or withdrawal of the ep's mandate. there are principles which should not be forgotten in the conduct of those elected to the european parliament when they exercise the functions for which they were elected by the citizens of their country: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. hence my vote.

in writing. − the code of conduct for members of the european parliament on financial interests and conflicts of interest aims to provide the community legal order with instruments to ensure the transparency of decision-making processes, and to prevent situations of abuse of power. in order to make these rules operational, however, amendments to the rules of procedure of the european parliament are necessary. that is the purpose of this proposal, which is why i voted in favour of it.

in writing. − according to estimates by the united nations and the world health organisation (who), there are about 2.2 million people living with the human immunodeficiency virus (hiv), with an increase in diagnosed and reported cases both at european level (with an alarming growth in eastern europe) and worldwide. another alarming fact is that, according to the european center for disease prevention and control, about 30 percent of those infected do not know that they are infected. the fight against aids must have a global and transdisciplinary response and commitment, in which preventive measures and strategies are the key to reducing the number of infected. the information, quality of services and goods needed to protect against transmission and promote safe behaviour are essential for effective control. against this background, it is necessary for member states and each european region to have a strategy adapted to their reality, with a focus on universal access to prevention, testing, counselling and treatment, thus avoiding stigmatisation and discrimination of hiv carriers. as the 15-24 age group is an increasingly vulnerable target, public policies need to be targeted at this group.

in writing. the report under review focuses on the european parliament's recommendations to the council, the commission and the eeas concerning the negotiations on the association agreement between the european union and ukraine. the eu's european neighbourhood policy provides for the gradual opening up of certain european union programmes to the participation of neighbouring countries with the aim of promoting reforms, modernisation and often democratisation. ukrainian political and state leaders have repeatedly expressed ukraine's intention to join the eu in the medium term, despite the condemnation of this parliament on 11 october for the trial and conviction of former prime minister yulia tymoshenko. ukraine, in addition to having carried out a set of public administration reforms, has been actively involved in the creation and work of the euronest parliamentary assembly - a platform for cooperation between the ep and the national parliaments of the eu's eastern neighbourhood. the new generation of ukrainians has strong pro-european ambitions. i therefore vote in favour of this report in the hope that it will contribute to the democratisation and consolidation of the rule of law in ukraine.
in writing. - ukraine, because of its geostrategic importance and natural resources (including energy), has been a preferred target for the european union. the proposals in the report are not unusual in the economic sense. nor is it strange that the principles which the eu itself claims to uphold, namely the separation of powers, impartiality or transparency and the independence of the judiciary from the political power, are being disregarded, as is the attempt to influence the proceedings brought by the ukrainian judicial institutions against yulia tymoshenko. we reject all the external interference that this report promotes, in the continuation of other political guidelines that do not take into account the interests of the ukrainian people or the peoples of the eu countries, but rather of the economic and financial monopolies, of which the proposal for the creation of a free trade area is another example.
in writing. − ukraine is of great geo-strategic importance to the eu as a regional player with a high level of influence in neighbouring countries. the association agreement commits ukraine to applying a large part of the community acquis. ukraine's efforts to consolidate internal political stability, to create an environment characterised by strong political pluralism, democratic freedoms and respect for the rule of law, and to further internal reforms are facilitating the development of the country's european perspective. however, recent political developments, in particular the use of judicial means for political combat, show that there is still a long way to go to speed up the process for future eu accession, namely the fulfilment of all the conditions required by the rule of law.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution, in which i stress the call for intensified cooperation on youth and student exchanges and the development of scholarship programmes, allowing ukrainians to become familiar with the european union and its member states and vice versa.
in writing. - with the recent enlargements of the european union, ukraine is now at the doorstep of the common space. it is a state which occupies a geostrategically important area not only as a possible trading partner but above all as a guarantor of peace and security in a region where the rule of law is not yet established. in this context, recent concerns about ensuring a fair criminal trial (in the case of the detention of yulia tymoshenko) are recalled. however, these elements should not contribute to increasing mistrust between the two areas, but above all to encouraging community action in support of ukraine, based on mutual recognition between the two areas. the eu can assert itself in this context as a genuine regional power in respect for human rights and in defence of the rule of law. i therefore look back at the resolution and vote in favour of it.
in writing. − the instrumentalisation of judicial institutions for partisan and political purposes which has been taking place in ukraine reveals that there are still obstacles to the promotion of the fundamental rights and guarantees of ukrainian citizens. the events of the past month call into question one of the eu's fundamental values: the rule of law and freedom of thought and of the press. this association agreement, which also includes a deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta), is a document that opens a new door to eu agreements with third countries, as it presupposes a very high degree of integration, through the incorporation of the community acquis. such agreements, which should serve as an example for the countries of the neighbourhood policy, leave open the possibility of future accession. the reform policy pursued by ukraine focuses on institutional, economic and social areas. the strategic importance of ukraine for the eu is undeniable. however, we must avoid playing a double game, forgetting the founding principles of the eu, which are the basis of all european policies. i think it is important to get the commitment of the ukrainian authorities to restore the rule of law.
in writing. - i welcome this report as a message that to achieve a modern system of customs arrangements, we must strengthen the eu's competitiveness, while promoting security, market surveillance, consumer protection and our financial interests.
in writing. − support an efficient customs union, as the free movement of goods is one of the cornerstones of the european integration process, economic development and growth in the internal market. i am aware that customs play a crucial role in ensuring safety, protecting consumers and the environment, ensuring the full collection of revenue, strengthening the fight against fraud and corruption and ensuring respect for intellectual property rights, and i hereby express my support for their modernisation.
in writing. − the modernisation of customs systems plays a key role in ensuring security, protecting intellectual property rights, fighting fraud and updating and adapting systems to evolving technology. this is a bold and innovative report. the modernised customs code (mcc), adopted in 2008, plays a key role in simplifying customs procedures and harmonising eu customs rules, thereby helping economic operators to carry out their activities more effectively and customs authorities to do their job more efficiently. however, the cam is not yet applicable as the it systems have not yet been implemented and/or developed. consequently, the progress made to date is indicative of a failure to meet the deadline for implementation (set at 24 june 2013). i agree, however, that it is appropriate to delay the implementation of the cap, especially since the vast majority of member states and trade representatives support this option. it is also important to ensure cooperation between customs authorities and, subsequently, between customs authorities and economic operators, as well as with government authorities. i accept that it may be necessary to set up a european customs agency for this purpose.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the modernisation of customs regimes, as it contains proposals which will contribute to greater product safety and consumer protection, as well as to strengthening the eu's competitiveness.
in writing. - the role of customs in europe's economic competitiveness is of the utmost importance, as they not only guarantee citizens' safety, but also protect consumers and intellectual property rights, collect revenue and help to fight fraud and corruption. in order to fulfil these functions to the full, they need to be modernised. however, all indications are that the deadline for implementing the rules contained in the modernised customs code will not be respected by all member states. this code will make it possible to introduce an electronic customs system, a single-contact system and a centralised service. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that there is a need for greater cooperation between the various customs services, allowing for an improvement in their activities of excellence and the rapid implementation of the modernised customs code.
in writing. the european union's objective of creating a single market in which barriers between member states are removed and only external borders with respect to external countries are maintained requires the adoption of exceptional measures in order not to jeopardise european economic competitiveness, which is essential for the revitalization of the internal market. the report by matteo salvini, which i voted for, deals with the modernisation of customs regimes and stresses the role played by customs in securing and protecting property rights, protecting authors and fighting fraud. in order to simplify customs procedures and harmonise customs rules, the modernised customs code (mcc) was adopted in 2008 and has a deadline of 24 june 2013 for application. however, several member states contested this deadline because of the delay in implementing the computer systems necessary for its operation. it is therefore urgent to solve this problem in the light of the added value of the cap, namely coordination between all member states, facilitation of business activity by economic operators and better control by the tax administration. it will also facilitate the movement of legitimate goods and product safety.
in writing. − the report considers that a smooth, simple and functional customs system is essential to facilitate the mobility of goods and trade in the internal market, especially for smes. we agree that the modernisation of the eu's customs strategy and instruments must have a budget that allows for a functional, efficient and simplified customs procedure policy. but we have some reservations about the vision inspired by the rapporteur, since, taken to its ultimate consequences, it does not always take into account the interests and basic national productions, as in agriculture and other food areas. moreover, it does not always take account of the interests of smes themselves, which are exposed to competition from much larger companies eager to increase their share of the existing market and of new markets. in summary, member states should therefore make the resources correspond to the customs procedures and procedures appropriate in each case. in particular, the development of computer systems is essential for the much needed modernization of customs. customs must therefore put particular emphasis on using the limited resources available in the field of risk management, ensuring the protection and security of the market and society, and border protection at the eu's external borders.
in writing. the report considers that a smooth, simple and functional customs system is essential to facilitate the mobility of goods and trade in the internal market, especially for smes. it is a concept which we do not support globally, since it does not always take into account the interests and basic national productions, as in agriculture and other food areas. but we agree that the modernisation of the customs strategy and the customs instruments of the european union should have a budget which allows for a policy of functional, efficient and simplified customs procedures. member states should match resources to the ever-increasing responsibilities of customs and the allocation of adequate financial resources, in accordance with budgetary frameworks, to customs procedures and processes, particularly the development of computerised systems, is essential for the achievement of much-needed customs modernisation. customs must therefore put particular emphasis on using the limited resources available in the field of risk management, ensuring the protection and security of the market and society and border protection at the external borders of the european union. that is why we abstained.
in writing. - european economic competitiveness is of crucial importance, particularly for the revitalisation of the internal market. customs have a key role to play in this context in increasing competitiveness. simplifying existing legislation and promoting electronic systems are essential to boosting economic growth by making customs modern and active. the creation of a european customs agency to deal with customs matters is also worth mentioning, thus facilitating cooperation between the entities concerned and ensuring security and accountability in the context of the flow of transparent information.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution, which stresses the importance of ensuring that legitimate customs controls carried out by third countries are not misused in certain circumstances to create de facto new non-tariff barriers to goods from the european union. in the present economic context, in particular, these artificial barriers must be combated.
in writing. - by introducing a system of control of products entering the common market, customs are, on the one hand, a means of ensuring the safety of goods moving within the european area, but, on the other, a barrier to the free movement of goods. legislation must therefore be balanced between these two opposite concerns: to defend the competitiveness of the european area, without, however, calling into question the central concerns of community action. the modernised customs code, introduced in 2008, was designed to achieve this by introducing control mechanisms marked by procedural simplification. however, its potential has not yet been fully realised and some additional activities still need to be developed with a view to its full implementation. finally, this is an area where the highest level of cooperation between the administrative authorities of the various member states is required in order to ensure the uniform application of union law. these are points which i found in the resolution before the european parliament, and which i therefore voted in favour of.
in writing. − the competitiveness of the european union is of great importance, especially at the present time when there is a prospect of revitalizing the european single market. in this context, customs regimes play a significant role, in particular through the simplification of customs legislation and the promotion of its electronic and digital component. however, if the customs systems of the member states are to make a real contribution to improving european competitiveness, modernisation, increased cooperation, greater action and responsibility must be accompanied by guarantees of safety and efficiency.

the external dimension of the cfp in general, and the partnership agreements with third countries in particular, are an essential part of the cfp. and the eu-morocco agreement is one of the most important for the southern european fleet, coming at a political moment when it is important not to close doors. the partnership agreements make it possible for the community fleet to be present in the external fishing grounds traditionally frequented by the european union and which are indispensable for obtaining important fishery products which contribute to ensuring europe's food supply. at the same time, they also play a major role in the economies of third countries and their social development. however, it is required that the european union's action at international level be consistent with the principles and objectives of the cfp, in particular the sustainability and preservation of marine ecosystems. in this context, the new sustainable fisheries agreement between the european union and morocco should be guided by sustainable management of fisheries resources through a transparency clause ensuring that exploitation of resources by community vessels in third country waters is limited to resources that they cannot or do not intend to capture. the new eu-morocco agreement should therefore have a credible scientific basis and an effective method of monitoring and monitoring its implementation, safeguarding the interest of the community fleet, ecosystems and local populations, which should also benefit from the agreement. in this respect, and in general terms, i cannot but regret that the high standards of action proposed by the european union, respect for local populations and safeguarding their fishing heritage, are not common to other fleets which sometimes operate in the same waters, which, incidentally, will happen in a wild way if the european fleet withdraws.

in writing. − the european union has set up the european union solidarity fund (eusf) to show solidarity with the people of regions affected by disasters. the solidarity fund is mainly used in cases of major natural disasters with serious repercussions on the living conditions of citizens, the natural environment or the economy of one or more regions of a member state or of a country applying for accession to the european union. in exceptional circumstances, the eusf may also be mobilised for disasters considered to be regional in nature, where a region is struck by a disaster causing damage affecting the majority of its population and having a serious and lasting impact on its living conditions and economic stability. spain and italy submitted applications to mobilise the fund. spain for damage caused by the earthquake in the region of murcia and italy for flooding in the veneto. both applications comply with the eligibility criteria of regulation (ec) no 2012/2002, and i therefore voted in favour of this report on the mobilisation of eur 21 070 950 for spain and eur 16 908 925 for italy.

in writing. - i support this report, considering that the introduction of minimum standards is a step in the direction of fundamental rights. it is important that suspects and accused persons are informed of their rights, because if they are not, we are calling into question one of the fundamental principles of the rule of law which states that suspects or accused persons should be presumed innocent until proven guilty in court. in order for this procedure to be uniform throughout the european union, there must therefore be common rules and enhanced cooperation between national and european institutions so that all citizens of the european union enjoy the same rights.
in writing. − the proposal for a directive on the right to information in criminal proceedings, presented by the european commission in july 2010, aims to establish a set of common minimum standards on the right to information in criminal proceedings applicable throughout the european union. that is, it is intended to assert the right of suspects and accused persons to be informed of their rights. this information must be given in plain and accessible language, either orally or in writing, and in a language which they understand. the report amends the european commission's proposal to ensure that the directive covers all cases of restriction of a person's liberty, regardless of the member states' treatment of the proceedings by which the suspect was deprived of liberty. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal to affirm the right of suspects and accused persons to be informed of their rights, as it is suggested that the information be provided in simple and accessible language for all to understand. the introduction of the proposed standards will ensure a better enforcement of the fundamental rights of eu citizens and will also contribute to overcoming the difficulties experienced in the recognition of criminal decisions caused by the lack of trust between judicial authorities.
in writing. − to address the impasse in the council since 2004, it was decided at the jha council of 30 november 2009 to initiate a phased approach in which procedural rights in criminal proceedings should be dealt with in stages, and a roadmap was adopted listing six measures as the basis for future action. the first measure, adopted last year, is the right to translation and interpretation. this initiative is the second of these measures and consists of the right to information in criminal proceedings, setting out minimum standards to be applied in relation to the information to be provided to suspects or accused persons (regardless of their legal status, citizenship or nationality) of having committed a criminal offence, regarding their rights and the charge against them. such information shall be provided in simple and accessible language and in a language which the individual concerned understands. knowing your rights is a first step towards ensuring that they are respected, as failure to do so not only undermines the fairness of criminal proceedings but is also likely to lead to miscarriages of justice. i therefore voted in favour of the compromise reached and hope that the member states will proceed swiftly with its implementation, particularly by drawing up the charter of rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it sets out common eu-wide minimum rules on the right to information in criminal proceedings. this new directive ensures that anyone who is in a situation of detention or prosecution has access to a bill of rights which will inform them of their procedural rights in plain language and in a language they understand. these measures are crucial to building trust in the european area of justice, as more and more european citizens travel within the eu.
in writing. - we all know that criminal justice, in order to function effectively, must specifically provide for the rights of suspects and/or accused persons, in order to guarantee them an adequate possibility of defence through appropriate legal and judicial means. in this context, it is essential to guarantee suspects and/or accused persons the right to be informed, in a language they understand, of their rights and duties, the content of the charge against them, the right of access to the file and everything that is relevant to the file to which they are party. this is the only way to ensure an effective defence, a cornerstone of the rule of law and modern criminal procedure.
in writing. − the european union, as an area of free movement of persons and goods, must convey an image of security and a community of values such as freedom, democracy and respect for the rule of law, which is the hallmark of the eu. this report, by birgit sippel, focuses on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the right of european citizens to information when involved in criminal proceedings in a member state other than their own. often the accused (e.g. tourists) do not know the language or the criminal law of that country and they live very complicated and distressing situations. the directive gives them the right to be informed of their rights before the proceedings are opened, including an interpreter and a lawyer, and to have access to the grounds of the accusation. i therefore express my support for this proposal for a directive, which has received the unanimous support of all the political groups, and i am voting for the member states to transpose it into national legislation as soon as possible, as this is a measure which will bring greater security and confidence to all european citizens.
in writing. - this report contains aspects which we value, relating to the right to information in criminal proceedings, in particular in relation to the right to interpretation and translation, the right to be informed of the accusation and to access to the file. we would point out that these provisions are enshrined in the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms (echr) and should therefore be complied with and respected by the member states which are parties to the echr. as such, unfortunately, it is not the case, and this report is intended to be an attempt to strengthen mutual confidence. this is part of a wider process, aimed at so-called harmonisation, in this case at the judicial and criminal level. we know how often many of these repeated attempts at harmonization by the eu end up failing to protect and safeguard the rights and interests of the people, and even ignoring the good practices and examples of some of the member states. so we shall see how this process develops.
in writing. - this report contains points which we consider important concerning the right to information in criminal proceedings, in particular the right to interpretation and translation, the right to be informed of the charges and to access the file. these points, while positive, not only because they are enshrined in the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms (echr), but because they are basic rights of persons, should be fulfilled and respected by the member states, which are parties to the echr. as this is not the case, this attempt to strengthen mutual trust is being pursued, which is part of a wider process of so-called harmonization, in this case at the judicial and criminal level. these recurrent attempts at harmonisation by the eu are in most cases not made to defend the rights of peoples and often ignore good practice and examples from the member states. we'll see how this process plays out.
in writing. − the difficulty felt in implementing the principle of mutual recognition of criminal decisions is essentially due to the lack of common minimum standards in the field of criminal procedure in order to guarantee and ensure the effective enforcement of fundamental rights. i therefore welcome the establishment of a set of common minimum standards on the right to information in criminal proceedings applicable throughout the european union, in particular the right of suspects and accused persons to be informed of their procedural rights. as criminal procedural law is the seismograph of existing fundamental and constitutional rules, it is imperative that it be strengthened as a basic principle of the rule of law.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe that the introduction of common minimum standards in the field of criminal procedure will ensure a better enforcement of the fundamental rights of eu citizens and will at the same time help to overcome the difficulties experienced in implementing the principle of mutual recognition of criminal decisions due to a lack of trust between judicial authorities.
in writing. the high degree of economic integration in the european area has not been matched by the same degree of approximation in legal areas more closely linked to the idea of state sovereignty. the term is used to refer to criminal law (in the broad sense) or, more specifically, to criminal procedure law. however, it is certain that the area of freedom, by promoting the free movement of persons, has also broken with the isolationist paradigm of the various criminal legal systems. the reality of crime is, at least in some areas, european, not reflected in the curtains offered by geographical borders. in this context, it is appropriate to begin to take the first steps towards approximating the laws of the various member states: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the right to information in criminal proceedings. in the light of the foregoing, the aim is to incorporate into the community acquis some of the fundamental elements which are at the core of the idea of due process: the right of the defendant to be informed of his rights, the right to be informed of the charges against him and the right of access to the file. i therefore voted in favour, stressing that the portuguese procedural model, which is based on the accusatory principle, already recognises these guarantees.
in writing. − under these new rules, suspects of a criminal offence will have to be informed of their rights in a language they understand. this will allow eu member states to ensure that all detainees or persons subject to a european arrest warrant are issued with a bill of rights covering their basic rights during criminal proceedings. i voted in favour of this initiative, which i consider to be fundamental to strengthening the area of security and justice in the european union.

in writing. − the court of auditors is an independent audit institution which checks the legality and regularity of the european union's revenue and expenditure and the sound financial management of its operations. in this spirit, the appointment of the individuals who make up the committee must be governed by criteria of competence and independence. the court of auditors has thus been appointed by the council on the initiative of a number of eminent persons from various eu countries. all of them submitted their cvs, answered a written questionnaire and were heard by the committee on budgetary control. most of them presented sufficient arguments to justify their appointment to the court of auditors to perform their duties there in a competent and independent manner. i therefore voted in favour of the name karel pinxten.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the appointment of mr pinxten as a member of the court of auditors. all the information submitted, which has informed my decision, indicates that the criteria laid down in article 286 (1) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, in particular the guarantees of independence, have been met, and i therefore welcome the appointment of mr pinxten as a member of the court of auditors.
in writing. - the court of auditors, which is designated by the treaty on european union as the eu institution (cf. article 13 (1) teu), is responsible for monitoring the use of european public funds. in this respect, and like similar institutions at national level, it is necessary to ensure a high level of technical competence and to guarantee the independence of the members of the institution (see, in this respect, article 286 (1) tfeu). in that regard, the appropriate moment for the review of the suitability of the members of the court of auditors to perform their duties is the moment of their appointment, and in the light of the information gathered, karel pinxten, nominated by the council, fulfils all the conditions necessary to be appointed as a member. i therefore voted in favour of the nomination, aware that the work of this institution is central to ensuring the quality of european political action.
in writing. − section 7 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union establishes the court of auditors as one of the european institutions. created in 1975, its objectives are to monitor the accounts and improve the financial management of the european union (eu). the court of auditors may carry out audits of any person or organisation responsible for the management of eu funds, and its findings are presented in writing in the form of reports, which are sent to the commission and the governments of the eu countries. the member states shall submit a proposal to the council, which, after consulting the european parliament, shall adopt the list of members of the court of justice. i am voting in favour of the appointment of karel pinxten because he fulfils the conditions laid down in article 1 of article 286 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union.
