in writing. - chapter 1, section 7 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union establishes the court of auditors as one of the european institutions. created in 1975, its aims are to control the accounts and improve the financial management of the european union (eu). the court of auditors may carry out audits of any person or organisation responsible for the management of eu funds, and its findings are presented in writing in the form of reports, which are sent to the commission and the governments of the eu countries. member states shall submit a proposal to the council which, after consulting the european parliament, shall adopt the list of members of the court of auditors. i am voting in favour of the appointment of hans gustaf wessberg, as he fulfils the conditions laid down in article 1 of article 286 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union.
in writing. - i approve this report. the main amendment proposed by the ep at first reading is the introduction of the instrument allowing for the issuing of a european protection order and a european criminal record order. i should like to stress the benefits of this amendment, as it will help to strengthen the rights of victims in the european union and will lead to the recognition by the council of important measures of protection in civil matters. this revision of the first reading agreement is essential to improve the legal framework of the european union and is a contribution to the strengthening of european democracy.
in writing. − all member states have measures to protect victims of crime. however, these measures cease when these people cross the country's borders. with the adoption of this report, which i supported, a victim of crime who is granted protection in an eu country will be able to continue to be protected if he decides to move to another member state. the new european protection order will be available, for example, to victims of domestic violence, harassment, kidnapping, persecution or attempted murder. in addition to the protection of the victim, a european protection order may also be applied for for the family members of victims, where they are covered by a protection measure at national level.
in writing. −i voted in favour of this directive, as it represents an important step towards building a just europe. the text adopted allows for the application for a european protection decision (epd) extending to other eu countries the protection granted to a national of a member state under national criminal law, with the issuing and sending of the decision to the other member state being the responsibility of the member state of origin. this directive applies only to protection measures adopted in criminal matters. however, taking into account the differences between the legal systems of the different member states, the country to which the citizen moves may apply other types of measures (criminal, administrative or civil) in order to promote the same level of protection as previously received. a european protection decision may also be requested to safeguard the family of the beneficiary of a ppd.
in writing. − based on a joint initiative of 12 member states, this european protection decision is undoubtedly an important instrument to facilitate and strengthen the protection afforded to victims or potential victims of crime in the eu. it is important to ensure that in the eusr, where eu citizens have the right to move and reside freely within the territory of the member states, the exercise of that right does not end up entailing a loss of their security. the initiative focuses on crimes likely to endanger the life, physical, psychological or sexual integrity of the victim, as well as his or her personal freedom, where the protection measures offered by one member state must be maintained and continued in any other member state to which the person moves. i am glad that a political agreement has been reached and that this second reading can be concluded. i also support the only proposed amendment which seeks to clarify its scope, as it is necessary to take into account that this directive focuses on protection measures adopted in criminal matters, as there are different legal traditions in the member states in this area, and to take into account the new context created by the presentation of the legislative package on the rights of victims in the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation because i believe that a victim of crime who enjoys a protection measure in an eu country should continue to be protected if he decides to move to another member state. these rules, which were approved by the european parliament, are of great importance, particularly in cases where protection is granted to victims of domestic violence, harassment, abduction, persecution or attempted murder.
in writing. - as i said when voting on this proposal at first reading, the legal protection of victims of crime is fundamental to the construction of an area of freedom, security and justice. that is why i am voting in favour of the agreement now before us, which seeks to improve the current legal framework in the following respects: (i) improvement of the conditions on which the revocation of the european protection decision is based; (ii) continuity of legal defence; (iii) reduction of the grounds for non-recognition or rejection of the european protection decision; (iv) the time limits for the decision to take effect; and (v) specification of the victim's travelling situation.
in writing. − this report is a first step towards ensuring that a crime victim who enjoys a protection measure in an eu country will continue to be protected if he or she moves to another member state. this european protection decision will cover, for example, victims of domestic violence, harassment, abduction, persecution or attempted murder. although much of the protection measures are aimed at women victims of domestic violence, the new rules will cover any victim (regardless of gender), taking into account the specificities of each type of crime committed. the directive shall apply to measures designed to protect a victim or a potential victim from the criminal acts of another person which may in any way endanger the life of that person or his physical, psychological or sexual integrity and to prevent further criminal acts or reduce the consequences of previous criminal acts. although it seems to us, in the context described, fair and necessary to ensure this principle, we stress that all this needs regulations (which do not yet exist) in order to be able to have practical effects.
in writing. − a first step has been taken so that a victim of crime who enjoys a protection measure in one eu country can continue to be protected if he or she decides to move to another member state. the new european protection decision will be available, for example, to victims of domestic violence, harassment, kidnapping, persecution or attempted murder. this european protection decision aims to ensure that protection afforded to a person in one member state is maintained and continued in any other member state to which that person moves or has moved. although much of the protection measures are aimed at women victims of domestic violence, the new rules will cover any victim (regardless of gender), taking into account the specificities of each type of crime committed. the directive shall apply to measures designed to protect a victim or a potential victim from the criminal acts of another person which may in any way endanger the life of that person or his physical, psychological or sexual integrity and to prevent further criminal acts or reduce the consequences of previous criminal acts. but all this still needs new regulations to be made practical.
in writing. − the adoption of the european parliament and council directive on the european protection order is an important step towards a freer, fairer and safer europe, as enshrined in the treaty. from now on, a victim of crime who is granted protection in one member state will also be protected if he or she decides to reside or remain in another eu country. where there is a risk of a crime being committed against a person which could endanger his or her life, physical or psychological integrity and dignity, personal liberty or sexual integrity, the member state must adopt a protection measure, under criminal law, which ensures the protection of that person in the country concerned.
in writing. − this draft directive on the european protection order was the result of an initiative by 12 member states. this directive aims to specify the measures which allow the state to continue to protect a person against a criminal act by another person which may endanger his or her life, physical or psychological integrity, dignity, personal freedom or sexual integrity. the ultimate objective is to prevent new criminal acts, reduce the consequences of previous criminal acts and improve the protection of victims. the main change compared with the european parliament's position at first reading concerns the scope of the instrument which has been partially redefined, providing for a closer link between the possibility of issuing a european protection order and criminal conduct. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - for a long time, at least in countries with an inquisitorial tradition, criminal proceedings have focused on the relationship between the public authorities and the criminal, with the prevailing view that the legal problem raised concerned above all (or only) the violation of assets fundamental to the community, that is, that it was a public legal issue. this guidance, however, although it can offer the guiding matrix of criminal policy, obscures the role of the victim: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. it is in this context that the legislative process for the adoption of a european decision on the protection of victims of crime is being carried out, with the aim of providing the legal systems of the various states with instruments which will enable them, in addition to satisfying the public objectives of criminal proceedings, to protect victims from committing new criminal offences. i am therefore voting in favour of the european parliament's position, with the minor amendments that have been introduced in the meantime.
in writing. − a victim of crime who enjoys a protection measure in an eu country can continue to be protected if she decides to move to another member state, under new rules approved by the european parliament. protection will be available, for example, to victims of domestic violence, harassment, kidnapping, persecution or attempted murder. protection measures exist in all eu member states, but they cease to have effect when someone crosses the country's borders. this european protection order aims to ensure that the protection afforded to a person in one member state is maintained and continued in any other member state to which the person moves or has moved.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering it essential that this single procedure should become a reality as soon as possible, since it strengthens the right of citizens to participate in the european common market and reinforces the principle of free movement of persons within the european union. with the increasing movement between member states of people working and living in a member state other than their country of origin, there is an increasing need for a de-bureaucratization of procedures in order to make unhindered use of a freedom acquired in the treaties of the european union, making it easier for citizens to enjoy their rights fully.
in writing. − the european union (eu) must ensure equal treatment for third-country nationals legally resident in the territory of the member states. its integration policy should aim to ensure rights and obligations comparable to those of citizens of the european union. as regards legal migration, the eu should develop migration policies that fully respect the competences of the member states, with the aim of helping them to meet current and future labour needs, contributing to the sustainable development of all countries. the aim is to establish a single residence and work permit procedure for legal immigrants and to give them a common set of rights throughout the eu. the aim is to simplify procedures so that national authorities can issue a single residence and work permit to legal migrants and grant them a set of rights equivalent to workers in the member states in which they reside, for example in terms of working conditions, including pay and dismissal, freedom of association and trade union membership, recognition of diplomas, social security, access to public services, etc. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - i hereby express my appreciation for the report on the procedure for granting a single authorisation for third-country nationals to reside and work in the territory of a member state. a common set of rights for third-country workers legally resident in a member state is also proposed.
in writing. - i congratulate the rapporteur, ms véronique mathieu, on her excellent work, which has enabled agreement to be reached at second reading on this important dossier, which represents a significant step towards a european policy on economic migration and is also the first report on legal migration to be adopted under codecision. the adoption of this single application procedure leading to a combined residence and work permit should help to simplify and harmonise the rules currently in place in the member states. it will help to improve the speed (the decision should be taken within 4 months from the date on which the application was made) and the efficiency of the current procedures, which will bring clear benefits for applicants who intend to immigrate to the territory of the member states, but also for employers themselves. it reflects the need to make the current immigration policy more flexible so as to contribute to the development and economic performance of the union, while at the same time allowing for greater control over the legality of the residence and employment of these migrants. they are also guaranteed rights and obligations (access to education and training, social benefits, working conditions) similar to those of eu citizens.

in writing. - after many difficulties, today we have approved the council's position on the creation of a single application procedure for work and residence permits and the definition of a common set of rights for all third country nationals legally residing and working in the eu. this implies common rules for all member states, which aims to put an end to the current differences between the various member states' regimes and to make the process of legalising workers faster, more uniform and more transparent throughout the union. if, on the one hand, legal labour migration, especially skilled labour, helps to combat illegal work and can help the competitiveness of the economy and help to overcome existing shortcomings, on the other hand we must not forget that in a period of crisis and economic vulnerability, when unemployment is increasing, labour migration policy must be flexible, but it must also be sustainable and reasonable.
in writing. − this recommendation for second reading, drawn up by veronique mathieu, is aimed at adopting the european parliament and council directive on the single application procedure for residence and work permits and the recognition of a set of rights for third-country nationals legally resident in a member state. the ageing of the european population, with the exception of eastern europe, has led to labour shortages in some sectors, especially in the primary sector, which have been minimised by immigration from east and north africa. in some member states, their productivity represents 2% of gdp. it is therefore the most elementary justice to make their lives easier by means of a single application for residence and work and to grant them rights equivalent to those of national workers as regards working conditions, social security and access to public services. i welcome the adoption of this directive, which i voted in favour of, because it brings greater equality of treatment to all eu workers, thus recognising the contribution they make to the economic growth of the member states in which they work.

in writing. − the proposal for a directive on the single residence and work permit was launched in 2007 by the european commission and reached the ep in march 2011, after the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. the aim of this proposal, at second reading, is to facilitate and simplify the safeguarding of the rights of migrant workers. thus, third-country workers legally present in the territory of a member state should enjoy rights similar to those of national workers, in particular as regards social security, access to public services, health and education and the same working conditions. i am voting in favour of this proposal, since workers from third countries are contributing in the same way to the economy of eu countries. they should therefore have the same rights and guarantees as european citizens. the eu must avoid discrimination against immigrants as much as possible, as it adopts programmes and measures that boost the migration of people from third countries to the european area.

in writing. - after several months of deadlock, we voted today, at second reading, on the proposal on accounting obligations for micro-entities. i repeat what i said in the first reading vote in march 2010: companies that are totally different cannot be treated equally. small and large companies cannot be treated equally. this proposal is aimed at defending small and mediumsized enterprises by proposing simpler and less costly measures which will naturally lead to the possibility of more jobs and more growth. these are key measures to combat the crisis and to support smes. finally, i would like to pay a special tribute to klaus lehne, as shadow rapporteur for the econ committee, where i debated the reasonableness of accounting measures for smes.
in writing. - this recommendation for second reading, by klaus-heiner lehne, is aimed at adopting the european parliament and council directive amending directive 78/660/eec on the annual accounts of certain types of companies, as regards micro-entities, i.e. a subgroup of micro-enterprises, the majority of whose business activity is at local level. this is a definition not included in commission recommendation 2003/361/ec, which defines micro, medium and small enterprises, but which is required for accounting operational reasons. like other companies, micro-entities are obliged to publish their accounts annually, which represents a significant burden in view of their turnover. however, member states may exempt micro-entities from this publication, subject to certain conditions. the objective of this directive is therefore to facilitate the entrepreneurial activity of micro-entities by reducing the administrative burden. given the importance of these companies to local economies and their contribution to national gdp, i welcome the proposals to change the amounts up to which exemptions can be granted (balance sheet: from eur 250 000 to eur 350 000; turnover: from eur 500 000 to eur 700 000) and i vote in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. − the preparation and publication of annual accounts can be a heavy burden for certain micro-entities. this report recognises this and therefore advocates an exemption of micro entities from the general publication requirements. it is intended that member states should be allowed to exempt micro-entities from the general publication requirements, provided that balance sheet information is duly submitted for deposit in accordance with national law to at least one designated competent authority and that the information is transmitted to the commercial register. in this context, member states may exempt from some of the obligations laid down in this directive undertakings which, at the balance sheet date, do not exceed the limits of two of the following three criteria: balance sheet total, eur 350 thousand; net turnover, eur 700 thousand; average number of employees during the year, 10. while recognising the importance of relieving micro and small enterprises of some of the constraints they face, particularly at this time of deep recession and crisis (and there are many of these constraints and many more), this proposal, which in some respects departs from the original proposal of the european commission, gives rise to some reservations.
in writing. − this report on the annual accounts as regards micro-entities seeks to allow member states to exempt micro-entities from the general publication requirements, provided that balance sheet information is duly submitted (for filing purposes) in accordance with national legislation to at least one designated competent authority and that the information is transmitted to the trade register. member states may, in accordance with paragraphs 2 and 3, exempt from some of the obligations laid down in this directive undertakings which, at the balance sheet date, do not exceed the limits of two of the following three criteria for micro-entities (balance sheet total: eur 350 000).
in writing. − the possibility for member states to grant certain schemes to some micro-entities is a very important issue and simplifies and improves the existing regulatory framework in order to limit the reporting obligations for eu micro-entities arising from accounting requirements. in this crisis scenario, it is important to create more agile mechanisms that reduce administrative costs. i therefore support this second reading.

in writing. - the community legislator, in dealing with company law, must take account of the extreme heterogeneity of the world of commercial companies. if we take the portuguese situation as a reference, we soon find that the same accountability requirements are not (as a rule) imposed on a limited company (gmbh in germany, sarl in france) or a public limited company. in fact, each of the company types is designed to meet different economic needs, and it is therefore justified that the company regime is not identical. the introduction of a special scheme for the publication of annual accounts by micro-entities, which is currently in the process of being legislated, is therefore to be commended. in this context, i voted in favour of the minor amendments tabled by the european parliament at second reading to the proposal put forward by the council.

in writing. − as a result of the current economic, financial and social crisis affecting europe, some member states are facing budgetary constraints which could lead to non-compliance with commitments made under co-financed community programmes, risking the loss of community support under the eafrd. this report approves the increase in the cofinancing rates of the rural development funds for portugal, greece, ireland, romania and latvia, with the european union's contribution being able to cover 95% of the total costs of projects in this field. these measures will be in force until the end of 2013. the aim is to help these countries' economic recovery by allowing them to launch programmes which had not been implemented until now because of a lack of national funding. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - the economic and financial constraints facing some member states of the union raise a number of questions as regards the commitments made in the context of the co-financing of community programmes under the structural and cohesion funds, the eafrd and the european fisheries fund. in the specific case of the eafrd, the risk of losing community support is increased when there is no clear evidence of effective national participation. in this context, the commission has proposed a temporary increase (2011/2012) of this co-financing for portugal, ireland, greece, latvia and romania (currently), which is supported by parliament, whose rapporteur has only introduced 6 amendments to make the procedures faster. as i said earlier, i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − at a time when positive signals from the european institutions are needed to stem the financial crisis, it is important to approve the proposal to amend council regulation (ec) no 1698/2006 to provide additional financial resources to eu member states facing serious financial difficulties. this amendment allows the co-financing rates for eu funds for portugal, greece, ireland, romania and latvia to be increased, and this contribution can cover 95% of the total costs of projects in the field of rural economy, which means that community funds are not lost due to the unavailability of own financing.
in writing. − this report deals with the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1698/2005 as regards certain rules relating to financial management for certain member states whose financial stability is seriously threatened, such as portugal, greece and ireland. the budgetary constraints faced by these countries may prevent them from investing the amounts allocated to them under the co-financed community programmes (structural and cohesion funds, eafrd and european fisheries fund) because they do not have the amount corresponding to the national component. this would force the member states concerned to repay these amounts to the eu, further aggravating their weak economy. the proposal aims to temporarily increase the maximum eu co-financing rate for member states' programmes supported under the european financial stabilisation mechanism (efsm). i welcome this proposal, which i voted in favour of, and i welcome the measures adopted, since they discriminate positively against the member states most affected by the economic and financial crisis and which are making great social sacrifices in order to rebuild their economies.
in writing. - this proposal for a regulation recognises the negative effects of the serious crisis affecting some member states, such as portugal, on the use of funds from co-financed community programmes (such as the structural and cohesion funds and the eafrd). the restrictions on public investment imposed under the pretext of the irrational stability pact had the same effect before. we have long advocated an increase in community co-financing rates for these member states, which are having difficulty using community funds at a time when they are most needed because of the amounts of co-financing required. the commission is now proposing, with regrettable delay, an increase in community participation. for the convergence and outermost regions in particular, the community co-financing will increase to 95%, while for the other regions it will be 85%, until the end of 2013. but this commission proposal does not increase the budget available to each of the countries in difficulty, as was required, so the practical result, due to the reduction in the national effort, will be a reduction in the overall amount of investment planned. the commission must therefore consider an effective increase in the community funds available to these countries, in addition to the abolition of the unreasonable criteria of the stability pact, thus freeing up the necessary public investment.
in writing. - it is important that this proposal for a regulation, which recognises the negative effects of the serious crisis affecting some member states, such as portugal, on the use of funds from co-financed community programmes (such as the structural and cohesion funds and the eafrd), should finally be adopted. the restrictions on public investment imposed under the pretext of the irrational stability pact had the same effect before. we have long advocated an increase in community co-financing rates for member states which have difficulties in using community funds at a time when they are needed the most because of the amounts of co-financing required. this means an increase in the community co-financing to 95%, in particular for the convergence objective and the outermost regions, while for the remaining regions it will be 85% by the end of 2013. but this commission proposal does not increase the budget available to each of the countries in difficulty, as was required, so the practical result, due to the reduction in the national effort, will be a reduction in the overall amount of investment planned. the commission must therefore consider an effective increase in the community funds available to these countries, in addition to the abolition of the unreasonable criteria of the stability pact, thus freeing up the necessary public investment.
in writing. − the adoption of this report will have the consequence of temporarily increasing the maximum rate of union co-financing for member state programmes supported under the emff and the balance of payments support facility for non-euro area member states. since, as a result of the financial and budgetary crisis, some member states are facing budgetary constraints which could prevent them from meeting their commitments under co-financed community programmes, risking the loss of community support under the eafrd, this proposal will allow (for those member states requesting such an increase) to reduce the amount of their national funds needed in the financial years 2011 and 2012. it will therefore make the funds planned available to the rural economy and contribute to a general economic recovery in those member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report which proposes to temporarily increase the maximum rate of union co-financing for member states' programmes supported under the emff (council regulation (eu) no 407/2010, currently greece, ireland and portugal) and the balance of payments support mechanism for member states outside the euro area (council regulation (ec) no 332/2002, currently latvia and romania). portugal will thus be able, in the context of the current budgetary constraints, to honour its commitments under co-financed community programmes (structural and cohesion funds, eafrd and european fisheries fund). however, it should be noted that this early availability of community funding does not exclude a high risk of the inability to receive/reduction of applications for new projects before the end of the financial period in 2013, leading to a slowdown in investment in rural economies.
in writing. − the current crisis facing the union has made it possible to improve the community's mechanisms for preventing systemic risks and reacting to situations of economic and financial fragility. on the one hand, this has allowed the attention of community policy-makers to be focused on the need to adopt structural instruments which, in the future, will allow a more rapid response to the various problems that may arise; on the other hand, it led to the adoption of measures which, in the short term, could mitigate the effects of the economic and financial crisis. the proposal to increase the rate of community cofinancing in the context of the structural and cohesion funds, the eafrd and the european fisheries fund for the benefit of countries covered by the emff (european financial stability mechanism) or, outside the euro area, beneficiaries of balance of payments support, is part of this framework. this is a proposal which i voted in favour of, in the hope that it will speed up the process of economic recovery in portugal.
in writing. − due to the global economic and financial crisis, some eu member states are facing serious budgetary constraints which could make it impossible to meet the commitments made under the european fund for rural development (efrd). this is the case for portugal, greece, ireland, romania and latvia. in order to contribute to an efficient economic recovery in these member states, the european commission took the initiative of increasing the co-financing rate by 10 percentage points to cover 95% of the total costs of projects under the structural funds. i agree with this initiative because i believe that it will not involve changes in the funding of cohesion policy, but rather an advance on the funds allocated to the member states. the countries concerned will not therefore have to allocate a large amount of money to the co-financing of community projects, and it will be easier to boost initiatives already approved at the time of application and to take advantage of new actions.
in writing. - i welcome this report because it provides a clear analysis of the tariff barriers and policies which currently exist in trade between the member states of the european union. on the other hand, i think it is important to try to remove existing barriers to european businessmen who have difficulty exporting to eu trading partners who impose serious barriers to european imports. it is necessary to respect that tariff setting also depends in part on national and regional options, for example at the level of gmos, but in general we can send the message that enhanced cooperation between the world's largest trading partners will allow the economy of all the players to be revived. finally, it is important to pay particular attention to the needs of developing countries.
in writing. the commission is also proposing that the european parliament and the council should be given the opportunity to present their views on the future of the european union. in the 15 pages of your report, which i recommend to anyone interested in international trade issues (in particular with regard to its legislative framework in recent years), i would just like to stress the need to eliminate non-tariff barriers to trade and investment as one of the main objectives of the union's trade policy under strategy 2020. of the many corrective and preventive measures proposed, i would like to highlight only one: the commission's study of an early warning mechanism to detect non-tariff barriers and the strengthening of its current analytical instruments for a better qualitative assessment of them. from what i have said above, it is easy to see that i voted in favour of the report and i congratulate robert sturdy on the excellent work he has done.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i think it is a good report, promoting, among other things, the fight against unfair competition, the removal of unjustified non-tariff barriers, the strengthening of respect for intellectual property rights, the protection of eu consumers and, in particular, the protection of the environment inside and outside the eu.
in writing. - free trade and the abandonment of protectionism are defining elements of the european project as it exists. the european construction is based on freedom of movement within its borders, but also on freedom of trade and investment with third countries. this is the right model, and i'm not asking for your review. but as the french president warned in marseille last week, we cannot impose quality standards on our producers and manufacturers which are not then met by the products we import. we cannot be the most open space and not see that our openness to imports and foreign investment is reciprocally accepted in other important markets where europeans want to enter. finally, free trade agreements, while important and desirable, must be reciprocal, otherwise we condemn the european economy to a slow death throes.
in writing. − this report focuses on the barriers to trade and investment in the european union, which hamper competitiveness, economic growth and, consequently, wealth and job creation. as rapporteur robert sturdy points out, open and fair trade is the best way to ensure and maintain a level playing field for european companies competing globally. the issue of barriers to trade and investment has been addressed at several levels: the transatlantic council decided to strengthen cooperation between the united states of america and the eu (principles on trade in information and communication technology services ict); the commission has also made progress in the automotive sector and a high-level conference is expected. all this shows that the removal of trade barriers is a priority for the eu. while i agree with the openness advocated in the report - which is why i voted in favour of it - i also believe that a mechanism should be set up within the world trade organisation (wto) to speed up the removal of non-tariff barriers, that is to say, of trade-restrictive regulatory measures which restrict imports, in a peaceful but effective manner.
in writing. - the rapporteur is a staunch advocate of free trade and, to that extent, this view is what ultimately prevails in the report. a view that is in line with the dominant positions in parliament, uniting the right with the social democrats. we consider the contents of the report unacceptable. we are faced with yet another unbridled apology for the liberalization and deregulation of international trade. recognising that among the so-called barriers to trade there are practices, regulations and procedures which are justified by elementary reasons of public interest, they want to restrict these barriers as much as possible by advocating a restrictive conception of the public interest. they want to force several countries to lift their non-tariff barriers in the name of free movement of eu products against the favouritism towards state-owned enterprises. the liberalization of world trade has disastrous consequences for many sectors of economic activity. it destroys productive capacity and jobs, affects the ability to create and distribute wealth, increases external dependence, and leads to chronic and growing imbalances in trade balances, in short, economic and social backwardness. the defence of each country's right to produce in a sustainable way is a requirement for the future. in the name of a new economic, social, energy and environmental rationality, which the neoliberal model not only does not guarantee, but makes impossible.
in writing. - this is a report which is fundamentally aimed at defending free trade, which is in line with the dominant positions in parliament, uniting the right and the social democrats, but which we reject. we are faced with yet another unbridled apology for the liberalization and deregulation of international trade without taking into account the different degrees of development of countries, or even the right of each country to produce in a sustainable way. while recognising that among the so-called barriers to trade there are practices, regulations and procedures which are justified by elementary reasons of public interest, they want to restrict these barriers as much as possible by advocating a restrictive conception of the public interest. they want to force several countries to lift their non-tariff barriers in the name of free movement of eu products against the favouritism towards state-owned enterprises. the liberalization of world trade has disastrous consequences for many sectors of economic activity. as we know, it destroys productive capacity and jobs, affects the ability to create and distribute wealth, increases external dependence, and leads to chronic and growing trade imbalances. in short, it is an economic and social backwardness.
in writing. − as non-tariff barriers, which are a growing obstacle to free access to partner countries' markets, include a range of trade restrictive measures other than import duties which restrict imports, it is important that the commission proactively act to remove or at least reduce the restrictive impact of such non-tariff barriers so that the export capacity of european companies is not affected and thus a level playing field is ensured and maintained for european companies competing in a global market.
in writing. − the most sensible measure to strike the right balance between the trading partners is the existence of an open market, but balanced by certain exceptions that protect certain sensitive sectors of each partner's economy to allow it to gradually adjust and prepare for global competition before it is actually opened up. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that this legislation is in line with this objective.
in writing. the european union is committed to a twofold economic order based on trade liberalization: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's trade policy is not distorted by the introduction of new technologies. whatever the basic position adopted in this respect, it is certain that, within certain limits, a system of free intermediation in trade results in what has been termed a positive sum game: in other words, both states, or groups of states, who sacrifice a more protectionist orientation, end up profiting more together than individually. in this context, the reduction of non-tariff barriers, i.e. of sub-reptile ways of introducing restrictions on international trade, such as export subsidies, anti-dumping duties, exchange rate manipulations, etc., i.e. of barriers which do not follow the formal route of introducing a customs tariff, is justified. in the light of the above, political action to abolish these instruments gradually is justified, without prejudice to the fact that they are reserved mainly for the most fragile sectors of the economy, as exceptional schemes. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − the multilateral trading system is seen as the most appropriate framework for regulating and promoting open and fair trade and ensuring the development of global trade rules that are fair and equitable between countries. however, european companies are having serious difficulties in establishing themselves in some markets, notably china, brazil and argentina, where restrictive measures are in place on trade in european products. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that non-tariff barriers to european countries must be removed or reduced, international regulatory cooperation must be improved, foreign direct investment in the european economy in key markets must be stimulated and a stable and attractive environment must be created for european investors abroad. finally, i believe that the european commission should make every effort to draw up a complete and up-to-date inventory of the main barriers facing european businesses.

political reforms in third countries. but when it comes to our taxpayers' money, we should give more to those who are doing the most to bring us closer to the values we believe in. this principle means that the faster a country progresses in its internal reforms, the more support it will receive from the european union. the principle of more for more is therefore correct, fair and consistent. this means, of course, that we also anticipate the possibility of cases or countries where we will have less for less. the neighbourhood policy is now based on the defence of the pursuit of common values and the commitment to democracy, human rights, the rule of law and good governance. but this quest implies a greater responsibility. our partners are called upon to take more responsibility in the process, and so we advocate the principles of greater differentiation, greater conditionality and more for more. by taking a bottom-up approach to our partners and tailor-made policies, we are minorities, environmental protection and resource efficiency. the serious economic and social problems facing our neighbours also need to be addressed immediately. it is clear that without our in writing. - i approve this report. a new paradigm of support for european producers and processors is needed, promoting a better use of what is produced in the european union, which will be able to generate direct revenues for producers and processors. for example, about 80% of the orange juice consumed in the european union comes from the united states and brazil. this is not justified, because we have excellent citrus fruit, we are able to produce locally and on a european scale high quality fruit juices, and it is necessary to boost production here too.
in writing. − this report is the second amendment to council directive 2001/112/ec of 20 december 2001 on fruit juices and certain similar products intended for human consumption. new rules are thus established on the composition, use of reserve names, manufacturing specifications and labelling of fruit juices in the european union. these new rules reflect new international standards on authorised ingredients, such as those concerning the addition of sugar, which is no longer authorised in fruit juices. the new rules, which apply to all products marketed in the eu, even those imported from third countries, stipulate that only those products which have not been added with other juices may be sold as orange juice. in the case of juices produced from two or more fruit species, the name should be supplemented by an indication of the fruit used, in descending order of the volume of the fruit juices incorporated. these measures should be reinforced by specific information campaigns enabling consumers to know exactly what product they are buying. i have therefore supported this report.
in writing. - this draft legislative resolution, which seeks to amend directive 2001/112/ec, is essentially a technical proposal to clarify and simplify the european legislative framework for the production and labelling of fruit juices intended for human consumption in the european union. i agree with the compromise reached by the trialogue and reflected in the amendments proposed by the rapporteur, and i therefore voted in favour of this report, which has now been adopted at first reading.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on fruit juices and certain similar products intended for human consumption because it includes rules on the composition and labelling of these products which will ensure clearer information for consumers, particularly as regards the indication of added sugar, which is particularly important for people with diabetes.
in writing. - fruit juices account for 10% of all non-alcoholic beverages consumed in europe. of these, only a small percentage is produced locally, with 82% imported from brazil. it is important to boost european fruit juice production in order to support our processing industries and our producers. in addition, it is essential to ensure that consumers are provided with the information they need to know exactly what kind of juices they are consuming, so that they can make an informed and conscious choice.
in writing. the commission proposal aims to amend for the second time council directive 2001/112/ec of 20 december 2001 on fruit juices and certain similar products intended for human consumption. fruit juices produced in the european union are high quality products, manufactured according to sustainability standards, and contribute to a healthy and balanced diet. it is therefore essential to ensure the quality of all products marketed within the union. the report advocates the proximity product, which should not be transported over long distances because of the resulting co2 emission, which is manufactured under social and labour conditions compatible with eu legislation and based on the principles of food safety established in the eu, without wanting to call into question any kind of import policy. i think that consumer information is essential, because there is a danger of misleading the consumer, particularly with regard to the withdrawal of the non-added sugar statement without first providing the consumer with an effective clarification. i agree with the rapporteur that industry needs to be given time to communicate and inform the consumer.
in writing. - we supported this report, which aims to clarify concepts relating to nomenclature, flavouring and to improve consumer information on the subject. it is therefore proposed to prohibit the use of potentially misleading or misleading names, such as natural fruit juice, which mislead the consumer into thinking that the juice is obtained directly from fruit, when in some cases the juices are obtained from concentrates. this is because there are difficulties at present in distinguishing, for example, between juices and nectars, and because the presence or absence of sugars is important for the consumer to make choices according to his specific needs and desires. for these reasons, information campaigns on different categories of juices are welcome. there are, however, concerns, also expressed in the report, notably about the delegation of powers to the european commission, particularly with regard to the review of authorised ingredients. this was the area which caused the greatest difficulty during the negotiations with the council and which should not be changed by means of delegated acts for that reason too. the proposal for a directive provides for an 18-month period for adaptation to the new legislation, which allows industry to make the necessary changes.
in writing. the report aims to clarify concepts relating to nomenclature, flavouring and to improve consumer information on this subject in the area of fruit juices and certain similar products intended for human consumption. it is therefore proposed to prohibit the use of potentially misleading or misleading names, such as natural fruit juice, which mislead the consumer into thinking that the juice is obtained directly from fruit, when in some cases the juices are obtained from concentrates. there are difficulties when it comes to distinguishing, for example, juices from nectars and the presence or absence of sugars. to enable consumers to make choices according to their specific needs and desires, information campaigns on different categories of juices are welcome. there are, however, concerns, also expressed in the report, notably about the delegation of powers to the european commission, particularly with regard to the review of authorised ingredients. this was the area which caused the greatest difficulty during the negotiations with the council and which, for that reason too, should not be changed by means of delegated acts. the proposal for a directive provides for an 18-month period for adaptation to the new legislation, which allows industry to make the necessary changes, and we therefore supported the report.
in writing. the ep's approval of new rules to ensure clearer information for consumers will lead to a better distinction between fruit juices and nectars for consumers. since the fruit juices and other similar products sector is a significant industry in the european union, the revised rules on the composition and labelling of these products, the inadmissibility of certain practices and the indication of added sugar will ensure a high level of quality for all products marketed in the union. with the corresponding benefit for the constant improvement of the internal market.
in writing. the commission proposal aims to amend for the second time council directive 2001/112/ec of 20 december 2001 on fruit juices and certain similar products intended for human consumption, laying down rules on the composition, use of reserved names, manufacturing specifications and labelling of these products, in order to ensure their free movement within the european union. the european parliament has advocated that the criteria set out in this directive should apply under the same conditions to products manufactured in the union and to imported products. i have voted in favour of this report because i support this same position.
in writing. - in the fruit juice market, about 82% of the products consumed in the european union are produced outside the community. the main reason is that fruit juice production in the european union is based on surplus production and not on fruit which is deliberately grown for juice production. the european production cycle thus ends up optimising available resources and avoiding the need for long transport journeys to put goods into circulation in the common market. these points, at a time when the european union is renewing its commitment to ecological sustainability, should be taken into account in the regulation of the fruit juice market. it is the fundamental concerns of the report before the european parliament which, within the limits set, seem to me to be legitimate and have led to the vote in favour.
in writing. the fruit juice market accounts for 10% of non-alcoholic beverage consumption and it is clear that further measures are needed to protect consumers' interests and to provide them with the fullest information available on the market. since a large proportion of the fruit used in fruit juices is produced outside the european union, it is imperative that the same standards be applied to all producers, avoiding situations of fraud and unfair competition. i therefore vote in favour of this report, as i believe that it is necessary to standardize the rules on the ingredients used and their composition, to classify products by category and to define common practices for manufacturing companies. i also think it is important to adopt clearer criteria to distinguish between the different types of beverages available on the market, in particular between juices and nectars, so that consumers can choose those that are most appropriate for their health and well-being.
in writing. - i approve this report. if we take into account the environmental impact of phosphate in european waters, it is urgent to drastically reduce the introduction of phosphate products and derivatives into european waters, which thus reduce their quality year by year. there are alternatives to the use of derivatives of this component, and i would stress the need for greater environmental awareness on the part of detergent manufacturers, as well as on the part of european citizens themselves, in the choice of products they use.
in writing. − phosphates alter the natural cycle of water systems such as rivers, lakes and streams. in europe, the baltic sea and the danube basin are the most affected by the increased use of phosphorus, particularly from detergents for washing machines and dishwashers (mll). with an increasing incidence of this chemical element in the composition of waters, rapidly developing plants (such as algae) tend to proliferate in an infesting way on other living organisms, depriving them of oxygen, and can produce toxins, killing fish and plants and degrading the quality of water - eutrophication. unlike laundry detergents, there are as yet no phosphate-free formulations as an alternative to mll detergents. by setting a date for the commission to set a limit on the phosphorus content of milk products, we can see more investment in innovation to speed up the transition to formulae without this compound. at the same time, the commission will allow sufficient time in advance to reduce the negative impact on manufacturers and will also harmonise, by means of a regulation, the different standards at national level. i therefore support the report by mr bill newton dunn on the use of phosphates and other phosphorates in detergents.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the use of phosphates and other phosphorus compounds in household laundry detergents, as it includes rules which will allow phosphates to be removed not only from laundry detergents but also from dishwashing detergents, which will be very positive for the protection of water quality and the environment in the eu.
in writing. the european union is known for the high level of detail in its legislation applicable to the most varied areas of production. this regulation is often intended to protect consumers and sometimes the environment and natural resources, as is the case with this regulation on the use of phosphates in household detergents. while i agree that such protection is desirable, i would say again that imposing restrictions on the manufacturers of household detergents as regards the use of phosphates will only make sense if those same rules prevent the entry into the eu of imported detergents which violate those same rules. we cannot demand more and more from our producers and industries without imposing equivalent rules on imported products.
in writing. the current commission proposal for a regulation aims to reduce the amount of phosphorus used in detergents for household washing machines. phosphates reach water systems, rivers, streams and lakes, causing eutrophication, that is, an overgrowth of algae that deprives other living organisms of oxygen and can produce toxins, killing fish, plants and other species and degrading the quality of the water itself. alternatives to the use of phosphates in detergents exist, especially in the case of household laundry detergents, where there is a trend towards phosphateless formulations. however, there are still technologies that use phosphate (which contains phosphorus but in much smaller quantities), preventing a total ban on phosphorus at this time. it is nevertheless important to set deadlines and limits for the maximum amounts of phosphorus which will make it possible to combat the eutrophication of water systems, rivers, streams and lakes. the commission has opted for a regulation rather than a directive in order to better harmonise the different standards at national level. the harmonisation of diverging national rules on the content of phosphates and other phosphate compounds improves the free movement of detergents for laundry and household use in the internal market.
in writing. − this report focuses on the problem of excess phosphate and phosphate compounds from household detergents, which, when they end up in waterways, rivers and seas, cause the phenomenon of eutrophication, i.e. the excessive growth of algae and other rapidly developing plants, which causes a sharp decrease in dissolved oxygen in the water, causing the death of aquatic life in these areas and significantly affecting biodiversity, with serious consequences for water quality and public health. the report sets maximum levels for the presence of phosphorus in household detergents for laundry and dishwashers at 0,5 g per dose in both cases with effect from 1 january 2013 and 2015 respectively. however, industrial and institutional detergents are excluded from this regulation. given the possibility of minimising the impact of this element on the environment and the fact that detergents for domestic use with a very low phosphorus concentration and with an effective action already exist, this regulation makes a positive contribution to a better environment, better living conditions and public health.
in writing. - the problem of excess phosphate and phosphorus compounds from household detergents which, when they end up in watercourses, rivers and seas, cause the phenomenon of eutrophication, i.e. the excessive growth of algae and other rapidly developing plants, which causes a sharp decrease in dissolved oxygen in the water, causing the death of aquatic life in these areas, significantly affecting biodiversity, with serious consequences for water quality and public health. this report sets maximum levels for the presence of phosphorus in household laundry detergents and dishwasher detergents at 0,5 g per dose in both cases with effect from 1 january 2013 and 2015 respectively. however, industrial and institutional detergents are excluded from this regulation. given the possibility of minimising the impact of this element on the environment and the fact that detergents for domestic use with a very low phosphorus concentration and with an effective action already exist, this regulation makes a positive contribution to a better environment, better living conditions and public health.
in writing. − this proposal, approved by the european parliament, aims to reduce the amount of phosphorus used in detergents for washing clothes and dishes throughout the eu. this will make detergents for washing and dishes more environmentally friendly, which is extremely important to ensure the protection of the environment, in particular the aquatic environment, and the proper functioning of the internal market for these products.
in writing. − this report approves new rules to reduce the amount of phosphorus used in detergents for washing clothes and dishes across the eu. the aim is to ensure the protection of the environment, in particular the aquatic environment, and the proper functioning of the internal market for these products. in southern europe, water is harder and detergents generally contain more phosphates. according to the commission, portugal is one of the countries that would benefit most from the switch to phosphate-free detergents. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − phosphates affect watercourses and systems, promoting the rapid development of algae and other plants, leading to their eutrophication and consequently the death of several native species due to reduced oxygen availability and/or the possible production of toxins. detergents contribute significantly to the introduction of phosphate into the aquatic environment and alternatives to the use of phosphates in detergents are currently available. this report greatly limits the amount of phosphates in detergents for laundry and household use. a study is also requested to investigate the feasibility and potential impact of a ban on phosphates in industrial and institutional detergents. these measures give greater protection to rivers, lakes, marine habitats and the whole ecosystem and all wildlife, and i voted in favour of them.
in writing. the rapporteur's main concern is to ensure that the commission's proposals are implemented in a way that is compatible with the common market. some european water resources are now overrun by algae and other organisms which eventually saturate the means available for the survival of fish and plants sharing the same resources. the commission proposal for a regulation therefore aims to reduce the permissible percentage of phosphates in this type of detergent. this is a proposal which, on the surface, seems to deserve applause, in that it seems to offer, at a small cost, great environmental benefits. i therefore voted in favour, but i must stress two points: firstly, the need for a study to assess the economic impact of this measure and the time needed for industry to adapt to the new rules, and secondly, the need to adopt a technical solution that can meet the needs of consumers. in this context, and to use a point made by the rapporteur, i would point out that in southern europe, because the waters are harder, the use of phosphates is more necessary for efficient washing.
in writing. the commission proposal aims to reduce the amount of phosphorus used in detergents for household washing machines and to better harmonise the different standards at national level. phosphates reach water systems and to clean europe's water it is desirable to reduce the amount of phosphorus reaching the waters on our continent. the largest use of phosphates in the eu is in fertilisers, but there is also another source of phosphates at the household level: dishwasher detergents, used in detergents to combat water hardness and allow effective cleaning, also performing other functions that enhance cleaning capacity. however, water hardness varies from region to region, which translates into different phosphate formulas between member states. it is important to lay down rules on the reduction of phosphate but also to allow for the impact in different member states and the various conditions to be taken into account in order to achieve the intended purposes.

in writing. - we welcome the rejection of the extension of this agreement. as we have always said, the agreement which the commission now proposed to extend is unacceptable. as it is an agreement between the eu and morocco, it is unacceptable that it provides for the exploitation of a natural resource in western sahara, a territory illegally occupied by morocco since 1975. morocco's sovereignty over the territory of western sahara has never been recognized by any country, until today. with this agreement - contrary both to international law and to the various un resolutions on this issue - the eu implicitly recognised it. this was therefore the only solution compatible with international law. the commission must take it very seriously. your attitude was deplorable throughout the entire process. it should be noted that parliament will be able to exercise its right of consent only two months before the expiry of the deadline for the end of this extension (which in practice began in february). the difficult situation is now created by the absence of a legal agreement covering the fishing activities that have taken place in the last ten months in that area. the commission is now obliged to correct the serious problems identified with this agreement, which we have long been denouncing, in possible future agreements.
in writing. - we welcome the rejection of the extension of the eu-morocco fisheries agreement. the rejection of the agreement shows that it is not viable from an economic point of view (it is one of the most expensive fisheries agreements the eu has with a third country) or from an ecological point of view, given the dangerous state of conservation of several stocks. however, the most serious issue we consider in this agreement is the implicit recognition of morocco's sovereignty over western sahara, its waters and fisheries resources. since 1975, with the opinion of the international court of justice, until today, morocco's sovereignty over the territory of western sahara has never been recognized. the eu-morocco fisheries agreement is illegal and violates all relevant un general assembly resolutions and international law. we therefore believe that any future protocol to be negotiated by the european commission must correct the serious problems identified with the previous and current protocols.

in writing. − the external dimension of the cfp, and more specifically the partnership agreements with third countries, not only make it possible for the european fleet to be present in traditionally frequented external fisheries, but are also indispensable for obtaining important fishery products which contribute to ensuring the eu's food supply and play a major role in the economies of third countries. in the particular case of this agreement, the extension of the protocol is essential for the community fleets fishing there, particularly the portuguese fleet. it should be noted that there are portuguese vessels that have been operating in moroccan waters for many years, in particular under the fisheries agreement between the european union and that country which was in force from 1988 until 1999, when portugal was deprived of operating in moroccan waters, which led to the killing of several dozen vessels, with irreversible economic and social consequences for several of the portuguese fishing communities. in order to prevent such situations from recurring, and in view of the objectives of the external aspects of the cfp, i am voting in favour of this report.

in writing. − this recommendation aims to extend for a further year the protocol on the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and morocco. the protocol, signed in may 2006, sets out the fishing opportunities for eu vessels, taking into account the available surplus and, at the same time, the financial compensation on utilisation, the second highest rate in the eu, and support for the sustainable development of the sector. despite the many divergent issues regarding the outcomes/consequences of this agreement, particularly with regard to cost-effectiveness, species sustainability, environmental issues and the western sahara issue, i think it will be important to extend the agreement for another three months and, at the same time, to start negotiations on a new protocol to the fisheries agreement that addresses the shortcomings described above.

in writing. - due to its privileged location in north africa, the kingdom of morocco has a vast exclusive maritime area which has been coveted by various fishing fleets, including european ones, throughout the ages. this quasi-territorial continuity has fostered the establishment of privileged economic relations between the european union and the kingdom of morocco, making it the largest beneficiary of eu funds under the european neighbourhood policy and enshrining europe as the main destination for its exports. unfortunately, parliament has just ruled out the possibility of extending the partnership agreement with morocco. however, we cannot go on for long without a new agreement, otherwise the european fishing fleets operating in moroccan waters will go bankrupt and moroccan development aid will be cancelled. i therefore call for a new negotiation to be launched with a view to concluding a new agreement between the eu and morocco. i therefore urge the commission to draw up as soon as possible a new economic, ecological and socially sustainable agreement with morocco, not only to continue to support the moroccan populations so in need of support, but also to allow the fishing fleets licensed for that region to resume their activities.
in writing. - first of all, we believe that a future fisheries agreement between the eu and morocco must be in accordance with international law, which is not the case with the one that expired this year and which parliament has agreed, just today, not to give its consent to extend. this was one of the reasons why this happened. since 1975, with the opinion of the international court of justice, until today, morocco's sovereignty over the territory of western sahara has never been recognized. morocco, which has been occupying this territory illegally ever since, has therefore no sovereign right under international law over the natural resources of the territory, in particular its fisheries resources. it is therefore regrettable that the resolution adopted by the major political groups - the epp, s&d and liberals - simply ignores this issue when it comes to discussing a future agreement. we therefore regret the rejection of both our resolution and the two amendments we tabled, which sought to defend the inalienable sovereign rights of the people of western sahara over the natural resources on their territory. it is imperative that the legitimate representatives of the sarawi people be heard on any agreement involving the exploitation of natural resources from their territory.

in writing. the motion for a resolution tabled today, expressing its disapproval of the proposal for a protocol between the european union and the kingdom of morocco setting out the fishing opportunities and financial compensation provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the kingdom of morocco, is based on the idea that morocco, which does not have sovereignty over the territorial waters adjacent to western sahara, would not have the legitimacy to conclude the agreement. i think that, however, and regardless of the position taken on the substance, this is a wider issue and should be considered in another context, taking the problem in its entirety at the outset. i therefore voted against the motion.
in writing. - i welcome this report which confirms that member states are increasingly cutting back on defence and security, as a result of the current economic crisis. it is important that this situation does not promote a european inability to act on the international stage, particularly to pursue its peace missions. at this time, more than ever, the solution to improving the effectiveness of the defence sector lies in close cooperation between the various member states, european institutions and international organisations.

in writing. - like other sectors, defence has not escaped successive cuts prompted by the financial crisis affecting the european union. however, it must be said that this is not a sector like any other and that divestment from it can have serious consequences for the security and defence of the member states. at a time when the united states of america, the main guarantor of peace and democracy in the world since the second world war, is seeking to redefine its strategic positioning at global level and is making it increasingly clear that it must be able to count on the involvement of its partners in missions affecting the security of all, to reduce european investment in defence means exposing europe to less and worse military capability. in fact, it is becoming increasingly clear that if the union is not to stop the road to irrelevance, it must take its share of the burden-sharing of the western-based democracies. to say so is not to promote waste and certainly not war. europe cannot be indifferent to a rule that is often centuries old: se vis pacem, para bellum.
in writing. the economic and financial crisis facing all member states in general is forcing a rethinking of the priorities of a government which, while not forgetting the need for economic growth, should take measures of social and environmental protection which do not compromise the future. as the european union is an enlarging community of states (27+1), the principle of subsidiarity is fully applied and can represent a significant saving of human and financial resources. the european security and defence policy (esdp) is made up of several areas. in order to reduce costs without losing efficiency, we must identify the most effective projects, such as surveillance, maritime surveillance, control of the use of certain weapons, etc. i welcome the adoption of this report by mr krysztof lisek on the consequences of the austerity imposed by the crisis in the defence sector, which i voted in favour of, and which, while not neglecting the maintenance of the missions in which the eu is involved, such as monitoring in georgia, the horn of africa, protection of humanitarian aid, prevention of ship hijacking, etc., calls for an understanding between all member states and better coordination with other organisations and powers, such as nato and the usa.

in writing. - there are many reasons why we voted against this report. its central objective is the implementation of a militaristic agenda and the relaunching of the arms race which, in the wake of the crisis, is preparing new and dangerous developments for the peoples and countries of europe and the world. he advocates a qualitative leap in the militarisation of the eu, which is increasingly subordinated to nato and its agenda of global domination. it aims to implement and develop the tools created by the lisbon treaty, in particular the increase of eu military spending within nato and the assignment of a policy planning role to the european defence agency. it aims to implement enhanced cooperation and a kind of european semester which defines the priorities to be implemented by each country, or by groups of countries, in a framework which is not one of defending the sovereignty, territorial integrity and independence of countries, but of their specialisation for the reinforcement of eu interventionism in the world. at a time when social expenditure is being drastically cut, robbing workers and peoples of important rights and gains, the guidelines proposed here aim to finance the military-industrial complex, either directly through support and arms purchases or indirectly through research funding from european funds.
in writing. − it is worrying to observe the trend towards cuts in defence budgets in most eu member states as a result of the financial, economic and debt crisis. in addition to having a negative effect on its military capabilities, these cuts may also reduce the eu's ability to fully assume its responsibilities for peacekeeping, conflict prevention and strengthening international security. a reinforced european defence capability will increase the strategic autonomy of the european union and make an important contribution to collective security in the context of nato and other partnerships. the european commission should therefore carry out an assessment of the impact of these budget cuts on the development of capabilities in support of the european security and defence policy.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution mainly because i agree with the request made by the european parliament to allocate a more appropriate budget to the european union satellite centre. in fact, the centre operates on a modest budget and has demonstrated its efficiency and added value in a number of security and defence operations. the growing demand for satellite imagery and the importance it has shown in recent events in north africa are worth recalling. in view of its civil-military use, i agree with the proposal for this centre to be financed from the eu budget.
in writing. - despite the large number of states that make up the european union, the community defence system still has a number of weaknesses. the reasons for this are many: in addition to the most basic reference to the budgetary weaknesses of the various member states, there is a lack of coordination between the defence policy of the various member states. in fact, policy coordination between the various member states would allow for a better optimisation of resources, making it possible to create a genuine european defence force, based on the complementarity between the armed forces of the various states. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's energy policy is not undermined by the threat of nuclear power stations being shut down. i believe that defence policy is one of the greatest challenges facing the european union, without which political sovereignty itself seems to be (effectively) in jeopardy.

in writing. − although terrorism is not a recent phenomenon, it has taken on new forms in recent decades and terrorist networks have become more complex in terms of structure, means and funding, making the terrorist threat more complex and with more devastating consequences. terrorism is a constantly evolving phenomenon which must be combated in an appropriate manner, focusing on four essential aspects: prevent, protect, prosecute and respond. therefore, counter-terrorism policies, both at eu and member state level, must also be able to keep pace with these developments, but always in full respect of fundamental rights. there is a need for a coherent approach at eu and member state level to initiatives taken in the field of internal security, including terrorism and organised crime, in order to identify any remaining gaps and overlaps or duplications of counter-terrorism actions and instruments. terrorism is a phenomenon that can affect the security of the entire union, and it is the duty of the union and its institutions to combat it and to ensure that the values on which our free, open and democratic societies are based are respected, and that they contribute to the possibility for every citizen to live in safety and without fear.
