in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the eu, its member states and partner countries must adopt a strategy to combat international terrorism in full respect of the rule of law and fundamental rights. the european union's external action in this field should have as its primary objective prevention by promoting dialogue, tolerance and understanding between different cultures, civilizations and religions.
in writing. - this year marks the 10th anniversary of the terrible attacks of 11 september 2001 in the united states. never before, as on that day, had the world realized the global, borderless, and absolute threat that was terrorism. then came the attacks in madrid and london, which brought terror within our borders with a violence never before known on european soil. ten years later, terrorism is one of the greatest threats to the life of contemporary societies and therefore deserves not only the utmost repudiation but also the greatest possible combined efforts to eradicate it. it is now clear that the states are not capable of dealing with an increasingly global threat and that this threat can only be mitigated if they join forces and share information efficiently and quickly, and if they coordinate effectively in terms of resources and personnel.
in writing. - modern societies with a high degree of comfort and sophistication should be synonymous with safety. but what we have seen in this first decade of the 21st century is that technology has been used to carry out what we can consider the most serious and violent terrorist attack of all time: the attacks of september 11 in the united states. but europe was not left unscathed! in 2004, madrid, in 2005, london! i was in the same place. not to mention norway this summer and belgium during this plenary session. this is not to mention religious terrorism, especially in islamic countries, as happened in egypt. the feeling of insecurity on the part of citizens is great and no one can guarantee that they are safe from a terrorist attack. it is a huge threat to international stability and requires a global response, because it is a scourge that knows no borders. international cooperation in the form of a good intelligence network and an effective police, judicial, political and sometimes military system can help to weaken terrorist activity. i welcome the adoption of this report which harmonizes the european security strategy and the internal security strategy in the fight against terrorism.
in writing. - the so-called fight against terrorism has been used over the past decade as a pretext to justify a security drift which has opened the way to unacceptable restrictions on the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens. this escalation is supported theoretically and ideologically by the false dichotomy between security and freedom and the deliberate confusion between security and defence. the consequences of this fight against terrorism are well known: invasion and occupation of sovereign countries, hundreds of thousands of dead, millions of refugees, the creation of concentration camps and a worldwide network of secret prisons, or even the adoption of legislation restricting and providing for the suspension of fundamental democratic rights. these abuses, which the eu has sometimes condoned, are an integral part of the fight against terrorism. this report, like the resolution that was finally adopted, is part of that vision. we strongly reject it, as it does not make any contribution to the fight against real terrorism and the transnational crime associated with it. on the contrary, it poses real dangers to the security and fundamental freedoms of citizens in the various member states. the resolution adopted also whitewashes the past ten years of the fight against terrorism, by ignoring the causes that fuel terrorism and omitting state terrorism.
in writing. ten years after the crime against the american people, the attacks of september 11, reality shows how imperialism has exploited it, unleashing a paranoia of security that has served to perpetuate the false dichotomy between security and freedom, with the very serious consequences known to us: invasion and occupation of sovereign countries, hundreds of thousands of deaths, millions of refugees, the creation of concentration camps and a worldwide network of secret prisons, or even the adoption of legislation restricting and providing for the suspension of democratic rights. these abuses, many of which are the shared responsibility of the eu or at least its connivance, are an integral part of the strategy of a supposed fight against terrorism which we reject (and this report is part of that strategy), because they do not add any value in the fight against real terrorism and the transnational crime associated with it. on the contrary, it does involve real dangers to the security and fundamental freedoms of citizens in the various member states. in addition, this report whitewashes the ten years of the so-called fight against terrorism, by ignoring the causes that fuel terrorism and omitting state terrorism. that is why we voted against this report.
in writing. - i voted against this report, supporting the position of the epp, because i think it has the wrong approach to fighting terrorism. the rapporteur sees a number of ideological considerations in the text with which i cannot agree. only the substantial changes to the text proposed by the epp amendments would make it possible to improve the regulation in such a way that it would merit my support.
in writing. − this own-initiative report entitled 'eu counter-terrorism policy: key achievements and future challenges' calls on the commission to map out a comprehensive and detailed map of all counter-terrorism policies in europe, with particular focus on eu legislation and how it has been transposed and implemented at union level. i think that is one of the important measures and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i would have preferred voting and approving the in ’t veld report adopted in the committee on civil liberties last july, which had stronger wording. unfortunately we have been forced to express our vote first on an alternative motion for resolution (amr) that looked to be the only possible positive compromise. the amr nevertheless proposes a strict evaluation of the eu counter-terrorism policies; it insists on strengthening civil liberties, providing clear guidelines as to how to ensure counter-terrorism policies are proportional, necessary and efficient and bound by an objective and transparent evaluation process, and stresses that prevention, investigation and prosecution should be based on the judicial and police cooperation coupled with full parliamentary scrutiny and completion of the road map for uniform procedural guarantees: i.e. the only answer to terrorism can be more rule of law and democracy. for these reasons, i have voted in favour of the amr despite the reference to the definition of ‘terrorism’ as it is formulated in the framework decision 2002/475/jha, which we have always opposed as a group and that has been introduced against our will. the substantially positive elements of the amr undoubtedly outweighed the few negative references.
in writing. - terrorism is one of the major challenges facing the modern rule of law, having clearly broken with the classical paradigm of sovereignty. with the terrorist attacks of 2001, it became clear that there are global, or at least transnational, threats that can only be tackled together. this is the basis on which this phenomenon should be understood: the european states should devise a common policy to deal with this phenomenon. should not sacrifice their fundamental axiological framework of respect for the rights of persons and any measure adopted should pass the proportionality test; on the other hand, the policy approach to terrorism should not only be reactive (or ex post) but also preventive (or ex ante). finally, it is emphasized that measures adopted, at least at community level, should be subject to the scrutiny of the european parliament, even if only superficially.
in writing. - the last ten years have been marked by the war on terrorism, following the attacks of 11 september 2001. although these events took place on american soil, the preparation for them took place partly in europe and other attacks have occurred on european soil in the meantime. the eu is a potential target and the concern for the safety of its citizens is prominent. the report on the eu's counter-terrorism policy, which was tabled in plenary today, welcomes the commission's communication and its four areas for the future: preventing terrorist acts, protecting people and infrastructure, pursuing terrorist movements and responding to post-attack situations. following the position of the epp group, to which i belong, i voted against the overall amendment proposed to the document and which replaced it.

judicial cooperation in criminal matters in order to establish a genuine european judicial area, promote rapid and effective legal aid, respecting fundamental guarantees of defence, procedural guarantees and general principles on human rights. judicial cooperation in criminal matters should be guided by trust between member states based on the principle of mutual recognition of judgments and judicial decisions. we know that the conditions of detention and the management of prisons remain the responsibility of the member states, as the presidency of the council has reminded us, but there can be no mutual trust without respect for fundamental rights and without an effort to approximate the rights of suspects and accused persons and procedural rights in criminal proceedings. there are still huge differences between member states in terms of detention conditions. in some member states, these conditions are below the acceptable level, endangering not only judicial cooperation in criminal matters at the level of the european union, but also raising concerns in terms of the protection of fundamental rights and the possible violation of the charter of fundamental rights. there are significant differences in terms of prison overcrowding, inadequate prison structures, high numbers of detainees in remand, as well as the average length of time spent in remand. these situations undermine mutual trust, as vice-president kallas has already pointed out, and they raise problems in the implementation of the decision taken on the european arrest warrant. there have been several refusals to surrender detainees on the basis of the european arrest warrant by several member states. we want to call on the european commission to establish common minimum standards. i hope that the commission will be able to present an initiative taking into account the results of the public consultation triggered by the green paper referred to by commissioner kallas and i call on the member states, through the presidency of the council, to take urgent action to ensure that the fundamental rights of prisoners, in particular the rights of vulnerable persons, are respected and protected and to support the application of minimum standards of detention common to the whole of the european union.
the european arrest warrant and the conditions of detention in prisons are certainly a reminder to many european citizens of other situations that are also taking place in the european union. basically it's this mania that we have of doing things by halves: unifying where it's easy and then not harmonizing where it's hard. i am in favour of the advantages and i see the value of a european arrest warrant. i think it might be important for the victims, it might be important for justice to be done. but on the other hand, we cannot, and we have said this many times in this house, and the commission knows this very well, we cannot go on for much longer without, on the side of detention conditions, or the procedural conditions in general with which suspects and accused persons of a crime are treated, we cannot go forward with the european arrest warrant without, on the other hand, filling in these gaps that exist at the level of the european union. the european commission is now well aware of them. it has drawn up a green paper on the difference, the enormous variety of conditions of detention in the european union. we are now asking what the commission will do to harmonize these conditions, because without this it will always be very difficult for us, together with our citizens, to explain the purpose of a european arrest warrant and why some suspects are in conditions which are sometimes painful, degrading and inhuman in some of the countries of the union which have truly deplorable conditions of detention.

in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the egf was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when we are faced with this serious crisis, with rising unemployment as one of the main consequences, the eu should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i have therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 24 493 525 from the egf for france to support workers made redundant by renault s.a.s. and seven of its suppliers.
in writing. - although i regret the events which led to this procedure by renault and seven of its suppliers, i was pleased to see this mobilisation of the egf, amounting to some eur 24.5 million, following two votes in the committee on budgets, the first of which rejected the application. this first rejection was supported by the socialists in the s&d group and the parliamentary groups of the ecr and the nra. the socialist members in particular have used this procedure as a weapon against the french government. it seems to me that it is not at all right to make a political joke about the unemployment of a few thousand workers. in addition, the precedent of using the egf for purposes other than its specific purpose seems to me to be quite objectionable. i now hope that this sum will be mobilised as soon as possible, as requested by the rapporteur.
in writing. - renault, the flagship company in the european automotive sector, laid off 4,445 workers. the company's problems have also affected seven of its suppliers, who are now in serious difficulties. this makes even more evident the worrying situation that the european economy is going through and how it affects businesses and households. i hope that the european car industry can regain its former role on the world stage and that its leading brands can survive the crisis that affects us all. i hope that the mobilisation of the fund can be approved so that workers who can benefit from it can be reached quickly and that this additional aid can help them to re-enter the labour market.
in writing. − in july 2011, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf), set up in 2006 to support workers made redundant as a result of globalisation, for the benefit of france. this is the 13th application for 2011 and provides for the mobilisation of eur 24 493 525 to alleviate the social impact of the redundancies of 4445 workers in seven companies in the automotive sector (application egf/2009/019 fr/renault-france). the complexity of implementing the fund and its low maximum rate of co-financing (65%) have led to a very low level of resources being used, with only 14% (eur 370 million) of the total available amount being used in five years. i welcome the adoption of this proposal for a decision, which i voted in favour of, and i urge the commission and the council to submit to this parliament a proposal to increase the maximum rate of egf co-financing from 65% to 95% for member states in the financial assistance process, such as portugal and greece, as recently approved by the ep for the cohesion funds and the eafrd.
in writing. - my vote, in this case renault, was mainly a vote of protest against the action of the epp, which prevented the vote on an amendment by the liberal group demanding that the rights of renault workers should not be called into question by recent decisions of the french government. it should also be recalled that renault made profits of millions of euros and that the french state is one of the shareholders of this company. but as i said in the plenary, in the renault case, we must first of all express our solidarity with the approximately 5000 workers who have been made redundant. on the other hand, we regret the confusion created by france in the egf application process, its lack of dialogue with the representatives of its workers and its lack of transparency as regards the progress of the process, as has been pointed out by several french meps, including those from our group. we maintain our position of solidarity with the workers and support the mobilisation of this fund whenever there is transparency in the process, despite the criticisms we also continue to make of its regulation.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu member states and this aid is now to be granted to france, which has submitted a request for assistance in relation to a case of 4,445 redundancies, of which 3,582 were potential beneficiaries, in renault s.a.s. and seven of its automotive suppliers.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. on 11 july 2011, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of france in order to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. this is the 13th application to be examined under the 2011 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 24 493 525 from the egf for france, based on the redundancies of 4445 out of 3,582 requiring assistance, in the french company renault and in seven of its suppliers, during the four-month reference period from 1 april 2009 to 31 july 2009. since all the necessary conditions for the activation of this financial assistance mechanism have been met, i have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i abstained from voting on the mobilisation of the egf in the renault case. training for workers has already been carried out and financed by the french state and by renault itself. in this case, it was a matter of reimbursing the french state and renault, which should not have been done. renault declared profits of eur 1,2 billion in the first half of 2011, continues to insist on its plans to reduce staff and replaces permanent contracts with precarious contracts. worse, it does all this with the complicity of the french state, at the expense of european taxpayers' money. on the other hand, this fund has been attacked by some of the member states which have benefited most from it, including germany, the netherlands, sweden, denmark and the united kingdom. the egf is one of the few union instruments to help workers reintegrate in the context of the current socioeconomic and financial crisis, by providing training programmes tailored to each worker. allowing the use of this fund to be misused so that large european multinationals can carry out restructuring without regard to the social costs of such restructuring is another way of putting an end to this fund.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 established the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to support workers who lose their jobs as a result of structural changes in the global economy. following the redundancies of 3,582 workers at renault and seven of its suppliers in the french regions of île-de-france (53%), haute-normandie (29,5%) and nord-pas-de-calais (12,5%), france requested the mobilisation of the egf in order to obtain european funding to support the employment situation of the workers concerned. i agree with the requested amount of eur 24 493 525, which will be channelled to provide individual, one-off and temporary support to workers made redundant as a result of the effects of globalisation and the economic and financial crisis. finally, i believe that the european institutions should make every effort to improve the procedural and budgetary arrangements for the egf, by making the fund available quickly and efficiently to workers.
in writing. - i approve this report. firstly, because the treaty of lisbon requires the commission to do everything possible to make the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the european union operate more transparently. i also think that we should take this opportunity to try to make this regulation the only legal framework for public access to all documents handled by the eu institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, without forgetting that the end users are the citizens. it is our duty and obligation to make access as easy as possible from the user's point of view. in addition, it is necessary to take this opportunity to try to arrange the different provisions in a more coherent and reasonable way so that the institutions can work together to define common standards and guidelines for the treatment of the different types of documents.
in writing. − the openness provided by the lisbon treaty should be used to convey to citizens the message that the eu institutions, bodies and agencies are ready to raise the union's transparency to the level required by the new treaty. only with greater transparency of european legislation and decision-making mechanisms will we be able to bring the eu closer to its citizens, reinforcing the democratic legitimacy of the political system. the adoption of this regulation will make public access to documents handled by the eu institutions, bodies and agencies easier, giving the opportunity to order the different existing provisions in a more coherent and reasonable way, with a view to making the european decision-making process more understandable. unfortunately, no agreement has yet been reached, with differences ranging from the definition of documents, to the extent of exceptions to access to documents, to the protection of personal data and the handling of classified documents. however, this institutional impasse gives a very negative image of the eu and its institutions, and i therefore call on both co-legislators to show signs of greater openness and commitment to the benefit of citizens and to safeguard their fundamental right to access documents and to participate in the political process.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because it promotes greater transparency in the legislative and administrative process of the institutions.
in writing. − the openness of the european institutions and the clarity of their procedures ensure that civil society and public opinion in the member states are not only informed but are an integral and informed part of their decision-making process. despite the relative distance between the populations, enhanced by the troubled and not always clear and uncritical process that led to the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the european institutions must persist and make a real effort to make as many documents as possible available in a timely manner, thus helping to reduce that gap. i cannot, however, but regret that the necessary improvement in the legal framework for access to documents has been used to disregard, in a populist way, the real need for confidentiality of certain procedures, documents and information. so in an agreement of the whole parliamentary left which excluded the epp, a view is enshrined which goes far beyond the normal public access to the documents of the institutions, with which i cannot agree.
in writing. - we can say that transparency is the essence of democracy and that it should be at its service. the european union (eu), as an example of how democracy works, felt the need to show citizens that it had nothing to hide and so ten years ago it adopted its first transparency regulation. the report by mr michael cashman deals with the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament, the council and the commission on public access to eu institutions' documents. access to information and documents from public bodies - even if it can sometimes be embarrassing - is a fundamental right of citizens and should be treated as such. however, a certain degree of confidentiality is necessary in certain matters, both for personal and copyright reasons and to prevent misuse by those who may have privileged access to certain information. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that there should be transparency in all decisions of public bodies, provided that the exceptions are safeguarded, as they appear to be: documents classified as confidential and those relating to private life under the statute for members and officials.
in writing. − citizens should be guaranteed access to all documents handled by the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the european union as easily as possible from the user's point of view. information and knowledge of what is dealt with and decided in these instances can be quite important so that people know who decided and what decided on the areas that will invariably have a direct implication on their lives. this report, although it still has a lot of room for improvement, is a positive step towards increasing the transparency of the eu institutions. that is why we voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted against this report because i think it goes too far in terms of legislative transparency. i cannot agree that relevant and confidential documents can be made available on the internet without any control. public access to european parliament, council and commission documents is important but should not be generalised, and there should be a right of reservation where sensitive documentation is concerned and in such cases its unrestricted access should be assessed.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the objectives of increasing the transparency of the regulation, without making it too specific and difficult to apply, and of improving the practices of the institutions by drawing on past experience. public access to european parliament, council and commission documents can be a means of ensuring transparency in european decision-making.
in writing. − this report seeks greater transparency in public access to documents of all the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the european union, as expressed in article 255 of the treaty of lisbon. however, this proposal goes beyond its initial objective and regulates undue matters. in addition to violating existing interinstitutional agreements and competition procedures, it also affects personal information and information considered to be sensitive. the general definition of the concept of a document also includes preparatory, confidential and classified documents and the negotiating initiatives themselves, in particular informal trilogues. what will happen is that citizens will have access to negotiations and procedures that may call into question the final conclusions due to public influence. for these reasons, i am voting against this report, because transparency and access to eu documents must not override the protection of privacy, data protection and the protection of trade secrets and sensitive information in judicial and competition terms.

in writing. − the emsa was set up in 2003 in response to the erika oil tanker disaster and the environmental contingencies it created. since then, its mission has been focused on disaster prevention at sea and maritime safety. it now intends to extend its activities to 'create a european maritime area without barriers' by making it possible to transport goods and passengers by sea between member states without any more formalities than those applied to road transport. i believe that this task is essential in the economic climate europe is currently experiencing, since the sea can create important business and trade opportunities which can and must be encouraged.
in writing. − the european maritime safety agency (emsa) was established by regulation (ec) no 1406/2002 of the european parliament (ep) and of the council to respond to the problem created by the sinking of the oil tanker erika on 12 december 1999, which released 15,000 tonnes of fuel oil and polluted 450 km of the coast of brittany. the mission of the agency is to provide technical assistance and support for maritime protection in situations of pollution caused by ships, and therefore it plays a crucial role in the protection of the marine environment. both ocean protection and the creation of pollution control or control mechanisms must be seen on a global scale in order to save resources and streamline procedures. in the light of the experience of the emsa, it is necessary to extend its powers and to provide it with the means to strengthen the fight against pollution and piracy, as well as the support and surveillance of fishing and transport vessels. i welcome the adoption of this proposal which will extend the powers of the emsa, thereby contributing to our enjoyment of a healthier, more protected and more capable aquatic environment for the survival of future generations.
in writing. − as a purported response to the erika oil tanker accident, the european maritime safety agency was set up in 2003. based on legitimate environmental concerns, this agency imposes itself on a large scale on national authorities and jurisdictions, imbued with the federalist and centralist spirit of the eu, trampling on the sovereignty of member states in their maritime strategies, especially those with important exclusive economic zones, such as portugal, the eu country with the largest maritime area. we are very concerned about the insistence on the creation of the so-called european coast guard, because of its security, control and surveillance character, aspects of the sovereignty of the member states which, through the national authorities, ensure this control, surveillance and exploitation of their eezs. the report calls for the creation of a 'european maritime area without barriers' with a 'european integrated maritime policy', a 'european coastguard', satellite surveillance at european level and automatic identification systems. in the end, the initial, legitimate environmental concerns are dissolved into exaggerated supranational instruments and policies, usurping responsibilities and powers which belong only to each member state, including its strategies and policies of cooperation with the other countries of the union and third countries.
in writing. − the erika (1999) and prestige (2002) shipwrecks prompted the european union to strengthen maritime safety through a number of legislative measures. it is in this context that the european maritime safety agency was set up to assist the commission and the member states in matters of maritime safety, the protection of maritime transport and the prevention of pollution caused by ships. i voted in favour of the text proposed to amend the regulation establishing the european maritime safety agency. the amendments will allow for greater efficiency gains and lower costs, taking an important step towards an ambitious european maritime policy and developing rapid response tools to prevent damage caused by maritime disasters that can have very serious environmental and economic consequences.

in writing. − included in the economic governance package is the new mechanism for detecting and correcting potential macroeconomic imbalances in the european union and in particular in the euro area. also included in the economic governance package is a statement by the european commission in which it commits itself to monitoring and accompanying both deficit and surplus countries in the same way. indeed, as the european parliament argued when it adopted the package, it is important to monitor the situation in all member states equally because the interconnection is so close that possible deviations in certain member states may originate from measures implemented in another member state. a union-wide macroeconomic framework is therefore essential to enable problems to be correctly identified and solutions to be applied. finally, given the importance of this new mechanism, parliament called on the commission to develop the scoreboard further and to make some indicators more explicit, in order to ensure transparent implementation.
in writing. − the current economic and financial crisis has forced the eu to analyse national accounts in detail to identify the source of macroeconomic imbalances. on 16 november 2011, regulation (eu) no 1176/2011 of the european parliament and of the council aiming to prevent and correct possible budgetary irregularities was adopted as part of a set of rules on economic governance. this motion for a resolution follows the question for an oral answer under rule 115 (5) of the rules of procedure and is based on the document drawn up by the commission services entitled 'assessment panel on the monitoring of macroeconomic imbalances: initial draft'. in order to prevent further financial slippages in some member states, which could lead to a new crisis, and in the six-pack proposals as a whole, there will be macroeconomic surveillance with a focus on countries with current account deficits or surpluses. i therefore vote in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that there must be rigour in the management of public money so that the markets, especially the financial markets, can regain the lost confidence and so that the eu can finally take the lead in terms of economic growth and job creation towards the objectives set out in the eu 2020 strategy.
in writing. − the newly established supervisory mechanism aims to prevent and correct excessive macroeconomic imbalances in the european union and in particular in the euro area. in accordance with regulation (eu) no 1176/2011, the new mechanism also aims at a sustained convergence of the behaviour of the economies of the member states and a closer coordination of economic policies. therefore, and in view of the current economic situation, it is essential that the macroeconomic surveillance framework is operational as soon as possible. i believe that the potential indirect effects of member states' and the union's policies should be identified and discussed at an early stage (e.g. at the time of the annual growth survey) and, in any case, both before and after the adoption of convergence/stability programmes.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that it contributes to the improvement of the quality and safety of european transport by promoting coherent and concrete targets to achieve these objectives. i would also stress the importance attached to environmental issues through the decarbonisation of this sector and through a clear commitment to research and the development of intelligent management systems for all modes of transport.
in writing. the report under review, by mathieu grosh, is based on the european commission's white paper, adopted in march 2001, entitled roadmap for a single european transport area towards a competitive and resource-efficient transport system. we all know that mobility is essential for the functioning of societies, in particular for a competitive economy and for the freedom of citizens. over the last few years, road transport has been given priority over rail. now, in the context of the europe 2020 strategy, we must take into account fundamental aspects such as road safety in order to reduce the number of deaths and injuries, environmental protection (with a halving of co2 emissions), green energy sources and economic sustainability. we are talking about over ten million jobs and about 5% of gdp. as i am in favour of the creation of a single european transport area, i voted in favour of this report and hope that the implementation of the new instruments will improve all transport, particularly in the peripheral regions of the eu, and give a new impetus to the transeuropean network and rail proposals.
in writing. - the liberalization of the transport sector and the consequent privatisation of everything that generates profit under the (never verified) assumptions of improved service quality, better prices and more jobs has, on the contrary, led to losses for users, workers and national economies. this european transport policy may serve the interests of certain economic and multinational groups seeking a transport network to suit their needs. the german multinational db, which now controls more than 60% of the rail freight sector, is an illustrative example. but it will certainly not serve the interests of workers and the population, of smes, who see transport costs rising and quality declining as the liberalization advocated here progresses. the roadmap for the single european transport area is developing around the creation of a european internal transport market through the opening up of networks and markets, including the so-called single european sky and the european emission allowance trading. in this context, the most urgent calls for the commission to certify the absence of social dumping, the deterioration of the quality of services and of monopolies and oligopolies are of no avail. we obviously voted against this report.
in writing. - once again, the proposal to liberalize the transport sector has come to fruition. the resulting privatization of everything that generates profit, under the (never verified) assumptions of improved quality of service, better prices and more jobs, has, on the contrary, led to losses for users, workers and national economies. this european transport policy may serve the interests of certain economic and multinational groups seeking a transport network to suit their needs. the german multinational db, which now controls more than 60% of the rail freight sector, is an illustrative example. but it will certainly not serve the interests of workers and the general public, nor of smes, which see transport costs rise and quality fall as the liberalization advocated here progresses. the roadmap for the single european transport area is developing around the creation of a european internal transport market through the opening up of networks and markets, including the so-called single european sky and the european emission allowance trading. in this context, the most urgent calls for the commission to certify the absence of social dumping, the deterioration of the quality of services and of monopolies and oligopolies are of no avail. we voted against this report.
in writing. − transport is of great importance to eu citizens, who benefit from the european transport area, as it allows them to move in all situations of life and thus enjoy the freedom of movement in europe both at home and at work. in addition, passenger and freight transport provides jobs for many eu citizens and contributes to the completion of the european internal market. this is why calls for proposals to facilitate the creation of a truly integrated european transport market are of particular importance.
in writing. − transport is an important factor for cities and regions because it not only ensures the connection between them but also contributes to consolidating the position of the european union as a place of research and innovation and is therefore a fundamental element of the development of the eu and its regions, with a direct influence on the social cohesion of the regions. the creation of a single european transport area, as the objective of the future european transport policy, is therefore intrinsically linked to regional, environmental, economic, social and employment policy. due to this link, the transport sector can make an important contribution to the europe 2020 strategy. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the transport white paper, horizon 2050, sets out a strategic policy for all modes of transport under two premises: sustainability and efficiency. the achievement of the objectives set shall be reviewed annually in order to understand in advance possible shortcomings and to adapt the measures to the reality of each member state. the transport sector is an area which interacts with all european policies. the completion of the single market and the free movement of people and goods will only be fully achieved if there is a network of transport infrastructure and services. however, the strategy to be followed should take account of the different realities of the member states and of the european regions themselves. the choice of transport modes must therefore take account of the particular features of each region. the outermost regions, given their geographical and morphological characteristics, are far from the european internal market. the focus on maritime transport and regional airports is central to their full integration. the instruments of the transeuropean networks must also be coordinated with the regional policy funds in order to make it possible to develop the key infrastructures for increasing the competitiveness of european regions and reducing existing disparities.
in writing. - i approve this report, stressing that poor detention conditions or the risk that they do not meet the minimum standards required by the european prison rules approved by the council of europe may constitute an obstacle to the transfer of prisoners. in a developed europe that respects human rights, we cannot allow this to happen, and to prevent this from happening, the member states must restructure, modernise and improve the quality of their prisons and the conditions of the police officers working there, in particular through training.
in writing. − judicial cooperation in criminal matters should be guided by mutual trust between member states based on the principle of mutual recognition of judgments and judicial decisions. while conditions of detention and the management of prisons remain the primary responsibility of the member states, mutual trust can only be maintained if standards of fundamental rights standards are respected and efforts are made to approximate the rights of suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings. there are huge differences between member states in terms of detention conditions (overcrowded prisons, high numbers of detainees in pre-trial detention, inhuman and degrading treatment, number of deaths and suicides, etc.). in some cases, they are even below the acceptable threshold, putting at risk not only judicial cooperation in criminal matters at eu level, but also raising concerns in terms of the protection of fundamental rights. this has a negative impact on mutual trust between member states, leading to the reluctance or even refusal by the judicial authority of one member state to enforce a decision taken in another member state. i hope that the commission will soon come forward with an initiative on the establishment of common minimum standards and i call on the member states to take urgent action to ensure that the fundamental rights of prisoners are respected.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motions for resolutions in so far as the poor conditions of detention in many member states make it urgent for the eu to define a set of fundamental rights for detainees as well as common criteria to limit the abuse of preventive detention and provide alternatives to it.
in writing. − a political community which makes democracy, freedom and human rights its core values cannot fail to seek to ascertain the conditions in which those who have potentially committed crimes are detained and to assess whether they live up to the standards of humanity it has set. the rapporteur listed several reasons for concern: prison overcrowding, the increase in the prison population, the increase in foreign prisoners, the high number of detainees in pre-trial detention, prisoners suffering from mental and psychological disorders and the number of deaths and suicides in prisons. i share them and i hope that the member states can respond to them with concrete measures that will effectively reduce them. despite these circumstances, it must be said that the member states of the european union have some of the best legal systems and prison systems in the world. the dissatisfaction with the status quo and the public expression of it is proof of this and of the transparency with which this matter is dealt with internally. the serious problems we are facing and the specific abuses we are lamenting and condemning should not prevent us from saying that the european union is a model for most countries to follow also in terms of conditions of detention.
in writing. − conditions of detention in the european union (eu) vary from one member state (eu) to another, and in some of them these conditions violate the eu charter of fundamental rights (cdf), namely article 1: the dignity of the human being is inviolable. it must be respected and protected. these violations are due to prison overcrowding, abuse of pretrial detention, the increase in the number of foreign detainees, detainees suffering from mental and psychological disorders and the number of deaths and suicides in prisons. this motion for a resolution follows a number of questions with requests for oral answers from members of various groups, pursuant to rule 115 (5), and is based on the commission green paper entitled 'strengthening mutual trust in the european judicial area - green paper on the application of eu criminal law in the field of detention'. the absence of a european dimension in prisons means that improved conditions of detention, family visits, imprisonment and rehabilitation of minors, etc., are needed. i therefore vote in favour of this motion for a resolution, because i hope it will help to improve conditions of detention in the member states with full respect for the fundamental rights of persons in detention.
in writing. - we know that the social reintegration of prisoners is an essential task of the state, and this will be all the more effective the better conditions of dignity are guaranteed for them, whether in terms of logistics, training or the conditions of hygiene, health and safety themselves. we consider that ensuring these conditions is fundamental to the reintegration of people into society and we draw attention to the fact (not mentioned in the report) that only a public management of the prison system can guarantee this, as opposed to private management which, as is clear in the cases of the usa and israel (for example), puts the interest of profit, and even political, above the interest of the people. the green paper on the application of eu criminal law in the field of detention, presented by the commission in june, sets out an alarming picture of prison overcrowding, the increase in foreign detainees, the high number of detainees in pre-trial detention, detainees suffering from mental and psychological disorders and the number of deaths and suicides. however, conditions of detention must be in conformity with human dignity and the rights of suspects or accused persons must be guaranteed, including the right not to be subjected to inhuman or degrading treatment.
in writing. − the european union's main objective is to create an area of freedom, security and justice, while respecting, in accordance with article 6 teu, human rights and fundamental freedoms. the necessary approximation of the rights of suspects and accused persons and of procedural rights in criminal proceedings, which is a fundamental aspect of ensuring mutual trust between the member states in the area of freedom, security and justice, does not exhaust the objective pursued by the union. decent conditions of detention and access to pre-reintegration facilities should be created to ensure that the fundamental rights of prisoners, in particular the rights of vulnerable persons, are respected and protected.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution on conditions of detention in the eu, which sets out its concerns and stresses the importance of ensuring respect for fundamental rights, in particular the rights of defence and access to a lawyer, and of ensuring that the rights of suspects or accused persons are respected, including the right not to be subjected to inhuman or degrading treatment. in this context, the importance of the commission's proposal on the right of access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings and the right of communication after detention is recalled.
in writing. the european parliament, in its resolution of 15 june on the situation in the european union, calls on the member states to ensure that the fundamental rights of prisoners, in particular the rights of the most vulnerable, are respected and protected. the document considers that there should be a common minimum standard for detention conditions in the european union that should be applied in all member states. parliament also welcomes the european commission's communication of 14 june 2011 entitled 'strengthening mutual trust in the european judicial area - green paper on the application of eu criminal law in the field of detention'.
in writing. - i support this report because we cannot turn a blind eye to the large-scale use of child labour in this country. the international organizations have recognized the continuing disregard for human rights in that country. if the european union is to be a bulwark in the defence of fair trade and human rights, it must of course make any kind of partnership agreement with uzbekistan unfeasible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the european union should not ignore, in its trade relations and in particular in the cotton sector, the continued use of child labour in uzbekistan. in this sense, i believe that the eu can and should use its trade relations and cooperation protocols to make a genuine and universal defence of human rights.
in writing. - the reports of widespread child labour in uzbekistan, particularly in the cotton harvest, are worrying. this constitutes a violation of the rights of the children involved and of the international labour rules to which that country is a party. european industries, including textiles, cannot compete with those who violate the most basic rules in this way. i support the decision of parliament to consider giving its consent only if the uzbek authorities allow ilo observers access to monitor the situation closely and unhindered and confirm that tangible reforms have been put in place. i agree with the suspension of privileged relations with uzbekistan if the ilo proves the widespread nature of these practices and the union evaluates the possibility of creating an effective traceability mechanism for goods produced through the use of forced child labour.
in writing. the report under review focuses on the partnership and cooperation agreement (acp) between the european union and uzbekistan on bilateral trade in textile products. the current acp-eu agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of uzbekistan, of the other part, does not include trade in textile products which were covered by a bilateral agreement which expired in 2005. a protocol to the partnership and cooperation agreement is currently being finalised, which aims to include bilateral trade in textile products. when establishing agreements and partnerships, the eu has included binding clauses on respect for democracy, the principles of international law and human rights (article 2 of the acp-uzbekistan agreement). as the eu is the main importer of uzbekistan's cotton (up to 23%) it is essential that it uses all means to bring this country on the path of democracy and to abandon inhumane practices such as the exploitation of child labour. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution and hope that the children of uzbekistan will soon be able to devote themselves exclusively to their studies and will no longer be forced to work in the cotton fields.
in writing. the aim of this report is to approve the protocol amending the partnership and cooperation agreement on textiles. the rapporteur, however, raises obstacles to the conclusion of this agreement because of issues relating to human rights, democratisation and the rule of law. we consider unacceptable the demands of the european union to the uzbek government to carry out market-oriented reforms in the uzbek agricultural sector; to propose eu assistance in the long-term transition towards privatisation and liberalisation of the sector, seeking to interfere in the internal affairs of a country and openly taking sides with the forces that safeguard the interests of eu economic groups. we also follow the concerns about the issue of forced labour and forced labour among children. we believe that the international labour organization, with the authorization of the government of uzbekistan, should be responsible for investigating this situation and helping to achieve the goal of eradicating child and forced labour. the central question here is to defend the independence and sovereignty of this country and the will expressed by its people.
in writing. - there is every interest in making this agreement a reality. however, we must not forget that serious human rights violations and the use of child labour still exist in uzbekistan. i therefore agree with the position of the european parliament, which will only consider giving its approval to this agreement if the uzbek authorities allow access to the observers of the ilo (international labour organisation) so that they can monitor the situation closely and unhindered and confirm that tangible reforms have been put in place, bringing substantial results and capable of demonstrating that the practice of forced labour and child labour is indeed being eradicated at national, regional and local level.
in writing. the european parliament has also called for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu's security forces are fully involved in the fight against terrorism. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. - the report seeks to include in the ec-uzbekistan partnership and cooperation agreement a protocol on textile products and thus to bring the most favoured nation clause as established by the wto and the abolition of quantitative restrictions within this framework. however, and in view of the numerous allegations by ngos and international organisations of child labour in cotton production, parliament should only give its consent if the uzbek authorities allow monitoring of these allegations by the world labour organisation. i therefore vote in favour of this draft interim report on the textiles protocol, and i look forward to the commission opening a dialogue with the authorities, taking account of human rights in the common commercial policy.
in writing. − it is noted that more and more citizens move and live in a member state other than their state of origin, but there are still barriers to the free movement of persons, in particular with the transitory restrictions at the borders of the member states. if we want a union of solidarity and respect for free movement, this must not appear possible.
in writing. − in the current economic climate, the simplification and flexibility of all rules allowing greater mobility of professionals is an essential requirement for a sustainable economic recovery. moreover, the free movement of workers within the eu is one of the fundamental freedoms enshrined in our founding treaties. without it, the european union will no longer be what we want it to be: a single market in which there is effective free movement.
in writing. the joint motion for a resolution, tabled by several parliamentary groups, arises because some member states, due to political pressure, have placed restrictions on the entry of workers from romania and bulgaria, contrary to the maxim that the european union is an area of free movement of people and goods. the right to live and work in any member state is one of the fundamental freedoms of the eu, which also recognises the right to non-discrimination on grounds of nationality and to equal treatment. the member states must remove all barriers by the end of this year, because there is no economic justification for them. on the contrary, the member states with the highest numbers of romanians and bulgarians had an increase in gdp. their economies have grown and there is no evidence that they have been a burden on social security and health services, thus helping to bring the crisis to an end. i am voting in favour of this resolution because we are all european citizens with the same rights and duties and it makes no sense to create mechanisms to control and/or restrict the free movement of workers, particularly bulgarians and romanians, without a clear and transparent socioeconomic justification for a serious disruption of the labour market.
in writing. - it is not enough to say that freedom of movement for workers is a basic principle of the european union. we must ensure that equal rights are guaranteed for all, that the european union's guidelines and economic policies create the jobs needed for all and that the necessary economic and social mechanisms are guaranteed to avoid any kind of social dumping. it is therefore time to end the restrictions on access to the respective labour markets for romanian and bulgarian citizens, as in many cases these restrictions can serve as a cover for bogus self-employment and undeclared and irregular work, which undermines the rights of all workers in the host countries and of the citizens of bulgaria and romania. we know that the promotion of neoliberal policies is aggravating unemployment, precarious and low-paid work, undeclared work, where social dumping proliferates, the exploitation of workers intensifies and the culture of xenophobia and racism is created. we insist on policies of economic and social progress, on the firm fight against the most diverse forms of discrimination, on the defence of equal rights and opportunities, and on respect for the dignity of workers.
in writing. − the free movement of workers represents a positive socioeconomic example, both for the eu and for the member states. it is a framework for european integration, boosting economic development, social cohesion, individual promotion at professional level, countering the negative effects of the economic crisis and making europe a stronger economic power, ready to face the challenges of global change. in addition, globalisation, new working patterns and demographic changes require a higher degree of mobility among workers. however, serious disturbances in certain labour markets should be assessed in line with the criteria and methodology defined by the commission, so as not to create distortions and significant impacts.
in writing. − this resolution calls on member states wishing to maintain restrictions on access to their labour market for romanian and bulgarian workers to provide, in a clear and transparent manner, a comprehensive justification, in line with the criteria and methodology defined by the commission and substantiated by convincing arguments and data, including all socioeconomic indicators, that have led to the conclusion that geographical mobility is causing a serious disturbance in their labour market. i voted in favour of this resolution, making sure that restrictions must be exceptional and duly justified.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that in four years of implementation of the eu strategy for asia, satisfactory results have been achieved. the eu has launched important initiatives and programmes to support the priorities set out in its initial document, and i would highlight those which focused on good governance, the rule of law, human rights and democratisation; education and training; economic development, trade and investment; transport and energy; environmental sustainability and water management; tackling threats and responding to common challenges; intercultural dialogue. there has been a lot of activity, member states have a direct stake in implementing the eu strategy, european banks (eib, ebrd) are currently active in the region. however, i would like to draw attention to the fact that since 2007, major changes have taken place around the world: in the context of the global economic and social crisis, arab revolutions follow one another and the international coalition begins to withdraw from afghanistan with no certainty about the outcome of the war after ten years of military intervention. the european union must therefore remain vigilant and strengthen its link with asia.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because it aims to strengthen cooperation between the eu and central asia by promoting better management of the region's water and energy resources, as well as the defence of human rights, the rule of law and regional security.
in writing. - the central asian region has historically been in the geostrategic orbit of russia/soviet union and traces of this coexistence and influence are still visible today. in addition to russia, china and the united states have strategic interests in central asia, seeking to secure control of energy sources and raw materials. the european union too is trying to assert itself, but it must be admitted that it is not as attractive to local authorities as the other powers mentioned, nor has it been able to present a fully coherent policy for the region, thanks to its internal diversity. the union has sought to reverse this state of affairs through the use of partnership and cooperation agreements, but despite the significant progress made, it is safe to say that there is a lot of misunderstanding and little contact between the european union and central asia. with its own external action service, the european union should try to fill this information gap about the european union and try to use the soft power it has to promote change in those countries, particularly in terms of democracy, human rights, the rule of law, free and fair competition and the opening of markets.
in writing. - this report, by nicole kiil-nielsen, looks at the state of play of the implementation of the european union strategy for central asia. this is a very important region for the eu's foreign policy, which, if it moves away, will hand over the geo-strategic dominance to russia and china. despite problems such as high levels of poverty and drug production - often associated with human rights violations - it is a region rich in natural resources and can diversify export routes, making it essential to strengthen trade. the eu should therefore review its strategy towards these central asian countries in the light of the report's conclusions, in particular by supporting projects and initiatives that promote the defence of universal values and human rights. its experience in interregional cooperation gives it a facilitating and mediating role between the five countries concerned and could help to stimulate economic growth and combat unemployment. i welcome the adoption of this report which places particular care in the choice of institutions to support so that eu funds are not channelled to pro-governmental or human rights organisations.
in writing. − as central asia is of well-known but often underestimated strategic importance to europe, the eu should reflect on central asia policy, assess the results achieved to date and suggest new approaches to adapt action to a region faced with numerous threats that may have repercussions in europe. i therefore think that the eu should rigorously reassess its strategy and strengthen its involvement, focusing on the objectives and actions that are most likely to contribute to addressing the most pressing challenges: human rights and the rule of law, water and energy, and regional security.
in writing. − the development of an eu strategy for central asia in 2007 was a recognition and commitment to a comprehensive and structured approach that has borne positive fruit. the eu rapporteur's perspective is to rigorously reassess the eu strategy and to strengthen its participation, focusing on the objectives and actions most likely to contribute to addressing the most pressing challenges, which he considers to be human rights and the rule of law, water and energy, and regional security. i have voted in favour of this report because i consider the strategy presented to be balanced.
in writing. − the eu strategy for the new partnership for the central asian region was established in 2007, demonstrating the importance of this geographical area in the global context. the cooperation priorities underpinning this partnership are consistent with those established with other third countries, in particular in the fields of human rights, the rule of law, good governance and democracy, education, economic development, trade and investment, energy and transport, the environment, intercultural dialogue and common challenges and threats. this report aims to highlight once again the importance of the main challenges of this partnership by strengthening the participation of ngos and civil society in order to establish new funding channels. assistance shall be conditional on progress as presented in the annual reports. i am in favour of adopting this document and the oral amendment tabled for the establishment of an eu interparliamentary forum with the national parliaments of central asia.

in writing. − i approve this report which provides a comprehensive analysis of the implementation of the 2007-2012 strategy on health and safety at work. it is essential to ensure a high level of health and safety at work, to prevent risks in order to reduce the rate of work-related accidents and diseases, and to consider the positive impact of good management of health and safety at work, both at national and european levels and at company level. i have no doubt that proper prevention of workers promotes well-being, quality of work and productivity. i would like to point out a growing phenomenon which is also having an impact in this area: subcontracting and temporary work, which often involve strained and sometimes illegal working relationships, making it more difficult to identify responsibility for health and safety provisions at work. finally, i would like to stress the need to pay more attention to the growing impact of chronic work-related health problems such as musculoskeletal injuries (msds) and psychosocial risks.
in writing. - i naturally agree with the need to protect workers from all risks to their safety and health at work. there is already a broad consensus in europe and other developed countries and an adequate legislative framework. fortunately, we are a long way from the blackboard that charles dickens painted in the 19th century of working conditions in britain. without calling into question this (already established) protection, it is worth considering whether this is the time to ask for more protection for workers. the truth is that we are going through one of the most difficult economic crises and that unemployment is rising all over europe. perhaps this is the time to create more jobs to boost the european economy and not to create more rules and more duties for employers, lest this ultimately only harm the workers we want to protect.
in writing. - the economic and financial crisis must not be used to neglect health and safety at work. there are thousands of people dying at enormous cost to individuals, businesses and social security. we must prevent occupational diseases, both physical and mental. this text focuses on the mid-term evaluation report of the european strategy for health and safety at work 2007-2014. according to this report, 168 000 european union citizens die every year as a result of accidents at work or occupational diseases, and 7 million are injured. this is a matter which requires a new approach to reduce the risks of accidents and occupational diseases, which would save a significant amount and improve productivity and quality of life. the potential risks of new diseases due to new technologies and new substances such as nanomaterials should be considered in the legislation in force, as well as the stress caused by work. it is also essential that workers feel free to report all situations which could lead to an accident and not feel constrained to keep silent. so i voted in favour.
in writing. the report adopted today criticises the mid-term review of the community strategy on health and safety at work. it also considers that the review did not provide any substantive information on the situation of the member states in relation to the eu strategy. it also stresses that the vast majority of member states have not yet set targets for occupational diseases, health problems and work-related diseases and for risk factors in occupational or high-risk sectors, as required by the community strategy. the report focuses on positive aspects, which we support, such as the advocacy of preventive action, preparedness in occupational safety and health and also the full protection of temporary, parttime and most vulnerable workers. it also seeks to focus more on stress and psychosocial risk factors. it emphasises gender-discriminated statistics and gender-specific risk assessment. it called for greater involvement of workers in the design, monitoring and implementation of prevention policies, insisted on a stronger link with reach, advocated a ban on asbestos and recalled the ilo recommendation on risk prevention inspectors and labour inspectors. for these reasons, we voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of a mid-term evaluation of the european strategy for health and safety at work. in addition to the right to health being a fundamental right, all workers benefit from the legal guarantee of working conditions that respect their health, safety and dignity, and are also alert to the positive impact of good management of health and safety at work at both national and european level and at company level.
in writing. - i voted in favour of agreeing to the strategy of involving all workers in prevention policies. i believe that it is important, in order to provide adequate answers, to identify the categories of workers at risk as well as those who are not covered, and to take measures to ensure that all workers are covered by prevention policies and effectively benefit from the respect of their fundamental right to health.
in writing. - european legislation on health and safety at work is already quite complete, meeting the treaty and the charter of fundamental rights. however, according to this report, there is still work to be done, particularly with regard to psychosocial conditions. at the same time, there is a call on the member states to apply the directives already adopted, so that harmonisation is ever wider. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of the virus and to ensure that the virus is contained in the body. health and safety at work should not be seen as another burden for companies, but rather as a way of increasing well-being at work by providing increased productivity.

(s&d). – mr president, i will never forget the self-burned women whom i visited in herat in 2008 and the tales i heard of the women who filled the jails of afghanistan, escaping oppressive families and a police and judicial system that badly discriminates against them. i have no doubt that much has improved since the liberation from the rule of the taliban, but i know that we are facing tremendous risks with the negotiations with the taliban. it is imperative that the eu demands that women be at the negotiating table and demands that the afghani authorities be held accountable for afghanistan’s international obligations. there is a vibrant society in pakistan, but it is not enough to have a woman in a position of power, namely as foreign minister. it is incredible and outrageous that discriminatory uncivilised laws prevail against women, from hudood, to marriage laws, blasphemy and so on. it is imperative, as we have requested in this resolution, that we demand accountability for the human rights clause that is inserted in the eu-pakistan cooperation agreement.
mr president, afghanistan and pakistan are cases where the worst trends in international geopolitics, the politics of great empires and great powers, are combined with the worst local trends. and then when these countries no longer serve their temporary purpose for the big international politics, you let these countries fall and then the worst tribal, atavistic tendencies of these countries come back up. that's what happened in afghanistan. in afghanistan, the united states has now discovered, here a few years ago, that there is no military solution to afghanistan. of course there is no military solution to afghanistan. we have known for decades - if not centuries or millennia - that there is no military solution to afghanistan. however, they are preparing to make a transitional government, including the taliban, which will roll back, by and large, all kinds of practices, in this case anti-women, which are already traditional in this country, such as the practice of the baad, the sale of women, or the gang rapes to clean the honor of certain families. yes, we voted in favour of these resolutions, but we demand that the european union be aware of these developments, particularly when it implements its agreements with these countries.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to finance the necessary measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to finance the necessary measures. in a year, no one could have imagined what could have happened in the arab world and what we have seen unfold before our eyes. the text we have in this urgent debate on the case of mr zacharia bouguira, who protested against the police after witnessing a moment of police brutality, is a bit more than that. we walked a lot in one year. that's why tunisians call their revolution not the jasmine revolution, but the revolution of dignity, because in one year we went from someone who had no other way of expressing himself in the face of police brutality or in the face of police humiliation than to immolate himself by fire to someone who wants dignity in his country's politics. the dignity of the citizen who complains and a treatment i say by the authorities. we must think beyond the narrow framework of this parliamentary urgency. it should make us think that we have in tunisia probably the best example of the new wave of arab democracy and that we, on this side of the mediterranean, where we have crisis in the southern mediterranean countries, are not taking advantage of the demographic dynamics, the economic dynamics, the political dynamics that come from these countries. what we want is to close the borders and not to admit refugees. i think the urgency we must have is an urgency to rethink our european policy in the first place. and i leave you with this challenge.
mr president, i had the great privilege of being an international observer to the first free elections in tunisia recently. i was very moved two days ago to see the great human rights defender, moncef marzuki, being sworn in as president of the republic. i know that tunisia has all the conditions to succeed on its path to democracy, but i also know that this episode of zacharia bouguira and the 13 young moroccan victims of abuse illustrates that this is a long journey that requires great perseverance and support. support from the european union, in particular, for the reform of the security sector system, judicial, police, magistrates, judges, officials of the ministry of the interior and justice. the european union can make a difference in supporting the reforms that are needed and in that sense it will also be very helpful if tunisia considers establishing a human rights council as called for in this resolution.
